The action for nullity may no longer be brought either by the spouses or by the relatives whose consent was required, whenever the marriage has been approved expressly or tacitly by those whose consent was necessary, or when two years have elapsed without complaint on their part, since they became aware of the marriage. The action for nullity may not be brought by the spouse either, when two years have elapsed without complaint on his part, since he reached the competent age to consent by himself to the marriage.

###### Article 194

Any marriage contracted in contravention of the provisions contained in Articles 163, 164, 165, 173, 174 and 175 may be challenged, within a period of thirty years from its celebration, either by the spouses themselves, or by all those who have an interest, or by the public prosecutor.  
Nevertheless, a marriage contracted by spouses who had not yet reached the required age, or one of whom had not reached that age, may no longer be challenged:

1° when six months have elapsed since that spouse or the spouses reached the competent age;  

2° when the woman who had not reached that age conceived before the expiry of six months.  

The father, mother, ascendants and family who consented to the contracted marriage are not entitled to request its nullity.

###### Article 195

In all cases where, in accordance with Article 194, the action for nullity may be brought by all those who have an interest therein, it may not be brought by collateral relatives, or by children born of another marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, but only when they have a vested and actual interest therein.

###### Article 196

The spouse to whose detriment a second marriage has been contracted may request its nullity, even during the lifetime of the spouse who was bound to him or her.

###### Article 197

If the new spouses contest the nullity of the first marriage, the validity or nullity of that marriage must be determined beforehand.

###### Article 198

The Public Prosecutor, in all cases to which Article 194 applies, may and must request the nullity of the marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, and have them ordered to separate.

###### Article 199

A marriage that has been celebrated in fraud of the law may be annulled at the request of the spouse who acted in good faith or of the Public Prosecutor's office, brought within one year of the marriage.

###### Article 200

Any marriage that has not been contracted publicly, and that has not been celebrated before the competent public officer, may be challenged, within thirty years from its celebration, by the spouses themselves, by the fathers and mothers, by the ascendants, and by all those who have a vested and current interest therein, as well as by the Public Prosecutor's office.  
The period is reduced to fifteen years when there has been possession of status as spouses during that period and a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register is produced.

###### Article 201

If the marriage has not been preceded by the required publication or if the dispensations permitted by law have not been obtained or if the prescribed intervals between publications and celebrations have not been observed, the public officer and the contracting parties, or those under whose authority they acted, are liable to a fine of 20,000 FD to 50,000 FD.

###### Article 202

The penalties pronounced by the preceding article shall be incurred by the persons designated therein, for any contravention of the rules prescribed by Article 177, even if such contraventions are not deemed sufficient to result in the nullity of the marriage being pronounced.

###### Article 203

No one may claim the title of spouse and the civil effects of marriage, unless he or she produces a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register, except in the cases provided for by Article 77, under the title Of Civil Status Records.

###### Article 204

Possession of status cannot dispense the alleged spouses who invoke it respectively, from producing the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer.  

On the other hand, subsequent publicity cures prior or concomitant clandestinity to the marriage when possession of status as spouses exists.

###### Article 205

When there is possession of status, and the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer is produced, the spouses are respectively not entitled to request the nullity of that certificate.

###### Article 206

If nevertheless, in the cases of Articles 203 and 204, there exist children born of two individuals who have lived publicly as husband and wife, and who are both deceased, the legitimacy of the children cannot be contested on the sole ground of failure to produce the certificate of celebration, whenever such legitimacy is proved by possession of status that is not contradicted by the birth certificate.

###### Article 207

When proof of a lawful celebration of the marriage is established by the result of criminal proceedings, the registration of the judgment in the civil status registers ensures to the marriage, from the day of its celebration, all civil effects, both with regard to the spouses and with regard to the children born of that marriage.

###### Article 208

If the spouses or one of them died without having discovered the fraud, the criminal action may be brought by all those who have an interest in having the marriage declared valid, and by the Public Prosecutor.  
The court ruling on the criminal matter must, in order to enter a conviction, recognize that the incriminated act had the result of suppressing the proof of a marriage actually celebrated.

###### Article 209

If the public officer is deceased at the time of the discovery of the fraud, the action shall be brought in civil proceedings against his or her heirs by the Public Prosecutor, in the presence of the interested parties and upon their denunciation.

###### Article 210

A marriage that has been declared null nevertheless produces its effects with regard to the spouses, when it was contracted in good faith.  
If good faith exists only on the part of one of the spouses, the marriage produces its effects only in favor of that spouse.

###### Article 211

It also produces its effects with regard to the children, even if neither of the spouses acted in good faith.  
The exercise of parental authority is determined as in matters of divorce.

#### Chapitre V. Des obligations qui naissent du mariage Article 212

The spouses contract together, by the mere fact of marriage, the obligation to feed, maintain and educate their children.

###### Article 213

Children owe maintenance to their fathers and mothers or other ascendants who are in need.

###### Article 214

Sons-in-law and daughters-in-law likewise owe, and in the same circumstances, maintenance to their father-in-law and mother-in-law, but this obligation ceases when the spouse who produced the affinity and the children born of his or her union with the other spouse are deceased.

###### Article 215

The obligations resulting from these provisions are reciprocal.  

Nevertheless, when the creditor has himself or herself seriously failed in his or her obligations towards the debtor, the judge may discharge the latter from all or part of the maintenance debt.

###### Article 216

Maintenance is granted only in proportion to the need of the person claiming it, and to the fortune of the person who owes it.  
The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, even of its own motion, and according to the circumstances of the case, attach to the maintenance allowance a variation clause permitted by the laws in force.

###### Article 217

When the person who provides or the person who receives maintenance is placed in a state such that one can no longer give it or the other no longer needs it in whole or in part, discharge or reduction may be requested.

###### Article 218

If the person who must provide maintenance proves that he or she cannot pay the maintenance allowance, the Civil Chamber may, with full knowledge of the facts, order that he or she shall receive into his or her dwelling, and shall feed and maintain the person to whom he or she owes maintenance.

###### Article 219

The Civil Chamber shall also determine whether the father or mother who offers to receive, feed and maintain in his or her dwelling, the child to whom he or she owes maintenance, shall in that case be dispensed from paying the maintenance allowance.

#### Chapitre VI. Des devoirs et des droits respectifs des époux Article 220

The spouses owe each other mutual fidelity, support, assistance.  

Each of the spouses may bear, for use, the name of the other spouse, by substitution or addition to his or her own name in the order he or she chooses.  

If one of the spouses complains of any act causing him or her prejudice on the part of the other spouse without being able to provide proof thereof, and if the judge cannot determine the responsible spouse, he or she must appoint two persons to whom he or she gives the task of reconciling the spouses. After having studied the situation, the conciliators must, to the extent possible, reconcile the spouses and, in all cases report on their mission to the judge.

###### Article 221

The spouses jointly ensure the moral and material direction of the family. They provide for the education of the children and prepare their future.

###### Article 222

If the matrimonial agreements do not regulate the contribution of the spouses to the expenses of the marriage, they contribute thereto in proportion to their respective means.  

If one of the spouses does not fulfill his or her obligations, he or she may be compelled thereto by the other in the forms provided for in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 223

Spouses mutually undertake to live together.

The family residence is at the place they choose by mutual agreement.

Neither spouse may, without the other, dispose of the rights by which the family home is secured, nor of the household furnishings with which it is equipped. The spouse who has not given consent to the act may apply for its annulment: the action for nullity is open to that spouse within one year from the day on which he or she became aware of the act, but may never be brought more than one year after the matrimonial regime has been dissolved.

###### Article 224

Each spouse has full legal capacity; but his or her rights and powers may be limited by the effect of the matrimonial regime and the provisions of this chapter.

###### Article 225

A spouse may be authorized by the court to execute alone an act for which the cooperation or consent of his or her spouse would be necessary, if the latter is unable to express his or her will or if his or her refusal is not justified by the interest of the family.  
The act executed under the conditions set by the court authorization is enforceable against the spouse whose cooperation or consent was lacking, without resulting in any personal obligation on his or her part.

###### Article 226

A spouse may give a mandate to the other to represent him or her in the exercise of the powers conferred upon him or her by the matrimonial regime.

###### Article 227

If one of the spouses is unable to express his or her will, the other may be authorized by the court to represent him or her, in a general manner, or for certain particular acts, in the exercise of the powers resulting from the matrimonial regime. The conditions and extent of this representation are determined by the judge.  
In the absence of legal power, mandate or court authorization, acts performed by one spouse in representation of the other have effect, with regard to the latter, according to the rules of management of affairs.

###### Article 228

Each spouse has the power to enter into contracts alone for the purpose of maintaining the household or educating the children: any debt thus contracted by one binds the other jointly and severally.  
Joint and several liability does not apply, however, for manifestly excessive expenses, having regard to the household's standard of living, the usefulness or uselessness of the transaction, and the good or bad faith of the third party contracting.  
It also does not apply to obligations arising from instalment purchases if they have not been concluded with the consent of both spouses.

###### Article 229

If one of the spouses seriously fails in his or her duties and thereby jeopardizes the interests of the family, the President of the Court of First Instance may order all urgent measures required by those interests.

He may in particular prohibit that spouse from making, without the consent of the other, acts of disposition over his or her own property or over community property, whether movable or immovable. He may also prohibit the removal of movables, except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or the other of the spouses.

The duration of the measures provided for in this article must be determined. It may not, including any extension, exceed three years.

###### Article 230

If the order prohibits acts of disposition over property whose alienation is subject to publication, it must be published at the instance of the applicant spouse. This publication ceases to have effect at the expiration of the period determined by the order, unless the interested party obtains in the meantime a modifying order, which shall be published in the same manner.  
If the order prohibits disposing of or removing corporeal movables, it is served by the applicant on his or her spouse, and has the effect of making the latter a responsible custodian of the movables under the same conditions as a person whose property has been seized.  
When the spouse brings the order to the knowledge of a third party, that third party, if he or she nevertheless contracts with the other spouse, is in bad faith.

###### Article 231

All acts performed in violation of the order are voidable, at the request of the applicant spouse, if they were executed with a third party in bad faith, or even, in the case of property whose alienation is subject to publication, if they simply post-date the publication provided for in the preceding article.  
The action for nullity is open to the applicant spouse for two years from the day on which he or she became aware of the act, but may never be brought, if the act is subject to publication, more than two years after its publication.

###### Article 232

Each spouse may open, without the consent of the other, any deposit account and any securities account in his or her own name.  
The depositing spouse is deemed, with regard to the depositary, to have free disposal of the funds and securities on deposit.

###### Article 233

If one of the spouses appears alone to perform an act of administration, enjoyment or disposition over movable property that he or she holds individually, he or she is deemed, with regard to third parties in good faith, to have the power to perform that act alone.  
This provision does not apply to household furnishings referred to in Article 223, paragraph 3, nor to corporeal movables whose nature creates a presumption of ownership by the other spouse in accordance with Article 1651.

###### Article 234

Each spouse has the right to pursue a profession without the consent of his or her spouse, and may always, for the needs of that profession, alienate and encumber alone his or her personal property in full ownership.

Each spouse administers, encumbers and alienates alone his or her personal property. The origin and composition of personal property are established both with regard to third parties and to the spouse, according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Article 235

Each spouse receives his or her earnings and salary and may dispose of them freely after discharging the burdens of the marriage.

###### Article 236

Creditors to whom a spouse has become obligated may pursue their claims against his or her personal property, even if the obligation was not contracted by him or her in the exercise of his or her profession.

###### Article 237

The provisions of this chapter, in all respects where they do not reserve the application of matrimonial agreements, are applicable, by the sole effect of marriage, whatever the matrimonial regime of the spouses.

#### Chapitre VII. De la dissolution du mariage Article 238

Marriage is dissolved:

1° By the death of one of the spouses;

2° By legally pronounced divorce.

#### Chapitre VIII. Des seconds mariages Article 239

A woman may not contract a new marriage until three hundred full days have elapsed since the dissolution of the previous marriage. A woman may, however, before the expiration of this period of widowhood, contract marriage with her former spouse. The period is extended to four months and ten full days from the death of the husband, for a widow, and from the judgment referred to in Article 158 of this code, for the spouse of a missing person.

This period ends in the event of childbirth after the dissolution of the marriage. It also ends if the woman produces a medical certificate attesting that she is not pregnant.  
The President of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the marriage is to be celebrated may, by order made on simple application, shorten the period provided for in this article when it is evident from the circumstances that, for three hundred days, the previous husband has not cohabited with his wife. The application is communicated to the public prosecutor. In the event of rejection of the application, an appeal may be lodged.

### Titre VII : Du divorce

#### Chapitre I. Des cas de divorce Article 240

Divorce may be pronounced in the case of:	either mutual consent;	or definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond;	or fault.

##### Section I: Divorce by mutual consent

###### § 1. Divorce upon joint application of the spouses Article 241

When the spouses jointly apply for divorce, they are not required to disclose the cause; they need only submit for the judge's approval a draft agreement settling the consequences thereof.  
The application may be presented either by the parties themselves, or by their respective lawyers, or by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.  
Divorce by mutual consent may not be applied for during the first six months of marriage.

###### Article 242

The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers, if one or both spouses have chosen one.  
If the spouses persist in their intention to divorce, the judge informs them that their application must be renewed after a reflection period of one month.  
In the absence of renewal within three months following the expiration of this reflection period, the joint application shall lapse.

###### Article 243

The judge approves the agreement and pronounces the divorce if he has acquired the conviction that the will of each of the spouses is genuine and that their consent is free and informed.  
The judge may refuse approval and not pronounce the divorce if he finds that the agreement insufficiently protects the interests of the children or of one of the spouses.

###### § 2. Accepted divorce Article 244

Divorce may be applied for by either spouse or by both when they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage without consideration of the facts at the origin thereof.  

This acceptance is not subject to retraction. Once it has been validly given, it can no longer be called into question, even by the exercise of a means of appeal.

###### Article 245

If he has acquired the conviction that each of the spouses has given his or her agreement freely, the judge pronounces the divorce and rules on its consequences.

##### Section II: Divorce for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond Article 246

Divorce may be applied for by one of the spouses when the conjugal bond is definitively broken down.

###### Article 247

The definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond results from the cessation of the community of life between the spouses, when they have been living separately for two years at the time of the divorce summons.  
Notwithstanding these provisions, divorce is pronounced for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond in the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 251, as soon as the application presented on this ground is made by way of counterclaim.

##### Section III: Divorce for fault Article 248

Divorce may be applied for by one of the spouses when facts constituting a serious or repeated violation of the duties and obligations of marriage are attributable to his or her spouse and make the continuation of life together intolerable.

###### Article 249

In the event of reconciliation of the spouses occurring since the alleged facts, those facts can no longer be invoked as a cause for divorce. If this should nevertheless be the case, the judge would be obliged to declare the application inadmissible.  
A new application may however be made by reason of facts occurring or discovered since the reconciliation, the old facts then being able to be recalled in support of this new application.  
The maintenance or temporary resumption of life together are not considered as a reconciliation if they result only from necessity, from an effort at conciliation, or from the needs of the children's education.

###### Article 250

The faults of the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce do not prevent examination of his or her application; they may, however, remove from the facts he or she reproaches his or her spouse the character of seriousness which would have made them a cause for divorce.  
These faults may also be invoked by the other spouse in support of a counterclaim for divorce. If both applications are granted, the divorce is pronounced on shared fault.  

Even in the absence of a counterclaim, the divorce may be pronounced on the shared fault of both spouses if the proceedings reveal faults attributable to both.

###### Article 251

If an application for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond and an application for fault are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the application for fault.  
In this case, if he rejects the application for divorce for fault, the judge rules without delay on the application for divorce for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond.

##### Section IV: Modifications of the ground of an application for divorce

###### Article 252

The spouses may, at any stage of the proceedings, ask the judge to record their agreement to have divorce pronounced by mutual consent by presenting him with an agreement settling the consequences thereof.

###### Article 253

The spouses may also, at any stage of the proceedings, when divorce has been applied for on the ground of definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, ask the judge to record their agreement to have divorce pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage.

###### Article 254

If, in proceedings instituted for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the defendant applies by way of counterclaim for divorce for fault, the plaintiff may invoke the faults of his or her spouse to modify the ground of his or her application.

#### Chapter II

Divorce proceedings Section I: General provisions

###### Article 255

The proceedings on the cause, the consequences of the divorce and the provisional measures are not public.

###### Article 256

In the case of divorce for fault, and at the request of the spouses, the court may limit itself to recording in the grounds of the judgment that there exist facts constituting a cause for divorce, without having to state the faults and grievances of the parties.

###### Article 257

If an application for divorce must be made in the name of an adult under guardianship, it is presented by the guardian with the authorization of the family council, after the opinion of the attending physician.  
The adult under curatorship exercises the action himself with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 258

If the spouse against whom the application is made is under guardianship, the action is exercised against the guardian; if he is under curatorship, he defends himself, with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 259

A special guardian or curator is appointed when the guardianship or curatorship had been entrusted to the spouse of the incapacitated person.

###### Article 260

If one of the spouses is placed under judicial protection, the application for divorce may not be examined until after organization of the guardianship or appointment of a special curator.

###### Article 261

When one of the spouses is placed under one of the protection regimes provided for in Chapter II Legal protection measures for adults of Title XII Majority and adults protected by law(

###### art. 565

and following), no application for divorce by mutual consent may be presented.

##### Section II: Procedure applicable to divorce by mutual consent

###### Article 262

The application for divorce is presented by the parties themselves or their lawyers. The spouses may be represented by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.  
This application takes the form of an initial petition to which is annexed an agreement containing the provisional measures that the spouses will observe during the course of the proceedings, as well as a draft final agreement intended to settle the consequences of the divorce.  
The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers if they have chosen one.

###### Article 263

When the conditions provided for in Article 243 are met, the judge approves the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce and, by the same decision, pronounces it.


This excerpt sits under: REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI > BOOK I: PERSONS > Title VII: Divorce > Chapter I. Cases of divorce Article 240

###### Article 264

In case of refusal to approve the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce, the judge may nevertheless approve the provisional measures contemplated by the parties pursuant to Article 262, paragraph 2, and take any measure provided for in Articles 272 and 273, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes res judicata, ensuring in particular that these measures are in conformity with the interest of the child or children.  
A new agreement settling the consequences of the divorce may then be presented by the spouses within a maximum period of three months.

###### Article 265

In the absence of presentation of a new agreement within the time limit set in the preceding article or if the judge refuses approval once again, the application for divorce shall lapse.

##### Section III : De la procédure applicable aux autres cas de divorce

###### § 1. De la requête initiale Article 266

The spouse who files an application for divorce presents, himself or herself or through a lawyer, an application to the judge, without indicating the grounds for divorce.

###### § 2. De la conciliation Article 267

The judge shall mandatorily organize a conciliation hearing. In case of failure, the conciliation attempt may be renewed and attempted at any time during the divorce proceedings which may be initiated by a spouse in accordance with Article 276.  

The judge invites the spouses to consider renouncing the divorce and, if he or she observes their intention to pursue the proceedings, the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses both on the principle of the divorce and on its consequences.

###### Article 268

When the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses, he or she must meet personally with each of them separately before bringing them together in his or her presence.  
The lawyers are then called upon to attend and participate in the meeting.  

In the case where the spouse who has not filed the application does not appear at the hearing or is unable to express his or her will, the judge meets with the other spouse and invites him or her to reflect.

###### Article 269

The conciliation attempt may be suspended and resumed without formality, allowing the spouses time for reflection within a limit of eight days.  
If a longer period appears useful, the judge may decide to suspend the proceedings and resort to a new conciliation attempt within six months at most. He or she orders, if necessary, the necessary provisional measures.

###### Article 270

When the judge observes that the applicant maintains his or her application, he or she encourages the spouses to settle the consequences of the divorce amicably.  
He or she asks them to present for the trial hearing a draft settlement of the effects of the divorce.  

To this end, he or she may take any provisional measure within the meaning of Articles 272 and 273 of this Code, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes res judicata, ensuring in particular that these measures are in conformity with the interest of the child or children.

###### Article 271

What has been said or written on the occasion of a conciliation attempt, in whatever form it may have taken place, may never be invoked for or against a spouse or a third party in the continuation of the proceedings.

###### § 3. Des mesures provisoires Article 272

Upon the appearance of the spouses in the case referred to in Article 244, or upon the order of non-conciliation in other cases, the judge prescribes the measures that are necessary to ensure the existence of the spouses and children until the date on which the judgment becomes res judicata.

###### Article 273

The judge may in particular:
1° Propose to the spouses a mediation measure and, after having obtained their agreement, appoint a mediator to proceed with it;  
2° Enjoin the spouses to meet with a mediator who will inform them about the purpose and conduct of mediation;  
3° Rule on the modalities of the separate residence of the spouses;  
4° Allocate to one of them the enjoyment of the dwelling and furniture of the household, or share this enjoyment between them, specifying whether it is free of charge or not and, where applicable, recording the spouses' agreement on the amount of an occupancy indemnity; failing that, fix this amount;  
5° Order the return of clothing and personal objects and, in case of dispute over the ownership of these goods, decide provisionally on their allocation;  
6° Fix the maintenance allowance and the provision for costs of proceedings that one of the spouses must pay to his or her spouse, designate which spouse or spouses must ensure the provisional settlement of all or part of the debts;  
7° Grant to one of the spouses advances to be credited against his or her rights in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime if the situation makes it necessary;  
8° Rule on the allocation of the enjoyment or management of common or undivided property other than those referred to in 4°, subject to the rights of each of the spouses in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime
;  

9° Appoint any qualified professional with a view to drawing up an estimated inventory or making proposals regarding the settlement of the pecuniary interests of the spouses;  
10° Appoint a notary with a view to preparing a draft liquidation of the matrimonial regime and formation of lots to be divided.

###### Article 274

If there are minor children, the judge shall rule on their custody, as well as on the right of visitation and accommodation. He or she shall fix the contribution due, for their maintenance and education, by the spouse who does not have custody.  
Parental authority is exercised by the spouse to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other.

###### Article 275

The judge may take, from the initial application, emergency measures.  

He or she may, in this capacity, authorize the applicant spouse to reside separately, if necessary with his or her minor children; the judge may then and where applicable, determine, with the agreement of the spouses and failing that by decision, the financial arrangements between spouses in order to facilitate this separate residence.  

The judge may also, for the guarantee of the rights of a spouse, order all conservatory measures such as the affixing of seals on common property. The provisions of Article 240 and the other safeguards established by the matrimonial regime remain however applicable.

###### § 4. Del'introduction de l'instance en divorce Article 276

After the order of non-conciliation, a spouse may initiate proceedings or file a counterclaim for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for final breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault.  
However, when at the conciliation hearing the spouses have declared that they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage and the pronouncement of divorce on the basis of Article 244, proceedings may only be initiated on that same basis.

###### Article 277

On pain of inadmissibility, the application initiating proceedings must include a proposal for settlement of the pecuniary and patrimonial interests of the spouses.

###### Article 278

When he or she definitively rejects the application for divorce, the judge may rule on the contribution to the charges of the marriage, the residence of the family and the modalities of the exercise of parental authority.

###### § 5. Des preuves Article 279

The facts invoked as causes of divorce or as defenses to an application may be established by any mode of proof, including admission. However, descendants may never be heard on the grievances invoked by the spouses.

###### Article 280

A spouse may not submit to the proceedings an element of proof that he or she obtained by violence or fraud.

###### Article 281

Reports drawn up at the request of a spouse outside judicial proceedings are excluded from the proceedings if there has been a violation of domicile or unlawful infringement of the privacy of private life.

###### Article 282

Spouses must communicate to each other and to the judge as well as to the experts appointed by him, all useful information and documents to determine benefits and pensions and liquidate the matrimonial regime.  
The judge may have all useful investigations carried out with debtors or those who hold assets on behalf of the spouses without professional secrecy being invoked. Any contravention of the judge's order shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance, and punished by a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 FD.

#### Chapter III: Consequences of divorce

##### Section I: The date on which the effects of divorce occur Article 283

The decision pronouncing the divorce dissolves the marriage on the date on which it acquires the force of res judicata.

###### Article 284

To contract a new marriage, the woman must observe the period of three hundred days as provided for in Article 250.  
If the spouses have been authorized to reside separately during the proceedings, this period begins to run from the day of the decision authorizing separate residence or approving, in case of joint application, the temporary agreement entered into for this purpose.  
The woman may remarry without delay when the divorce has been pronounced in the cases provided for in Articles 246 and 247.

###### Article 285

The period referred to in the preceding article ends if a birth takes place after the decision authorizing or approving separate residence or, failing that, after the date on which the divorce judgment has acquired the force of res judicata.  
If the husband dies before the divorce judgment has acquired the force of res judicata, the period runs from the day following the day on which the death is officially recorded.

###### Article 286

The divorce judgment is enforceable against third parties, with regard to the property of the spouses, from the day on which the formalities of marginal notation prescribed by the rules of civil status have been completed.

###### Article 287

The agreement or divorce judgment takes effect in the relations between the spouses, with regard to their property: when it is pronounced by mutual consent in accordance with Article 263, on the date of approval of the agreement settling all the consequences of the divorce, unless the latter provides otherwise; when it is pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for definitive impairment of the conjugal bond or for fault, on the date of the non-conciliation order.  

One of the spouses may request that the effect of the judgment be brought forward to the date when, through the fault of the other, their cohabitation and collaboration ceased.

###### Article 288

Any obligation contracted by one of the spouses chargeable to the community, any alienation of common property made by one of them within the limits of their powers, subsequent to the initial application, shall be declared null and void, if it is proved that there has been fraud against the rights of the other spouse.

##### Section II: Consequences of divorce for the spouses

###### § 1. General provisions Article 289

If the divorced spouses wish to contract another union between themselves, a new celebration of the marriage is necessary.

###### Article 290

Following the divorce, each of the spouses loses the use of the name of their spouse.  

One of the spouses may nevertheless retain the use of the name of the other, either with the latter's agreement, or with the authorization of the judge, if they justify a particular interest for themselves or for the children.

###### Article 291

Divorce has no effect on matrimonial benefits that take effect during the marriage and on gifts of present property whatever their form.  
Divorce automatically revokes matrimonial benefits that only take effect upon dissolution of the matrimonial regime or upon the death of one of the spouses and dispositions upon death, granted by one spouse to their spouse by marriage contract or during the union, unless the spouse who granted them expresses a contrary intention. This intention is recorded in the agreement signed by the spouses and approved by the judge, or by the judge at the time of pronouncing the divorce; in these cases, the benefit or disposition maintained are irrevocable.  

However, if the marriage contract so provides, the spouses may always take back the property they have contributed to the community.

###### Article 292

Divorce has no effect on the rights that either spouse derives from the law or from agreements entered into with third parties.

###### Article 293

The spouses may, during divorce proceedings, enter into any agreements for the liquidation and partition of their matrimonial regime.  
When the liquidation concerns property subject to land registration, the agreement must be made by notarial deed.

###### § 2

Consequences specific to divorces other than by mutual consent Article 294

Without prejudice to the application of Article 297, damages may be awarded to a spouse in compensation for consequences of particular gravity that they suffer as a result of the dissolution of the marriage:
1° either when they were defendant in a divorce pronounced for definitive impairment of the conjugal bond and they had not themselves filed any application for divorce;  
2° or when the divorce is pronounced on the exclusive fault of their spouse. This application may only be made in connection with the divorce action.

###### Article 295

In the absence of a conventional settlement by the spouses, the judge rules on their applications for maintenance in joint ownership, preferential allocation and advance on share of community or undivided property.  
The judge rules on applications for liquidation and partition of property interests, under the conditions set out in Articles L.624-5 to L.624-11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, if it is justified by any means of the disagreements remaining between the parties, in particular by producing: a joint declaration of acceptance of a judicial partition, indicating the points of disagreement between the spouses; the draft prepared by the notary appointed on the basis of 10° of Article 273.  

The judge may, even of their own motion, rule on the determination of the matrimonial regime applicable to the spouses.

###### Article 296

The spouses may, during the proceedings, submit to the judge for approval agreements settling all or part of the consequences of the divorce.  
The judge, after having verified that the interests of each of the spouses and of the children are preserved, shall approve the agreements by pronouncing the divorce.

###### § 3. Compensatory benefits Article 297

Divorce terminates the duty of support between spouses.  

One of the spouses may be required to pay the other a benefit intended to compensate, as far as possible, for the disparity that the breakdown of the marriage creates in the respective living conditions.  
However, the judge may refuse to grant such a benefit if equity so requires, either in consideration of the criteria provided for in Article 298, or when the divorce is pronounced on the exclusive fault of the spouse who requests the benefit of this benefit, having regard to the particular circumstances of the breakdown.

###### Article 298

The compensatory allowance is determined according to the needs of the spouse to whom it is paid and the resources of the other, taking into account the situation at the time of the divorce and its foreseeable future evolution.  
For this purpose, the judge takes into consideration, in particular: the duration of the marriage; the age and state of health of the spouses; their qualifications and professional situations; the consequences of professional choices made by one of the spouses during the common life for the education of the children and the time that will still need to be devoted to it or to promote the career of their spouse to the detriment of their own;  
	the estimated or foreseeable assets of the spouses, both in capital and income, after the liquidation of the matrimonial regime; their existing and foreseeable rights; their respective situations with regard to retirement pensions, having estimated, as far as possible, the reduction in retirement rights that may have been caused, for the spouse entitled to the compensatory allowance, by the circumstances referred to in the sixth paragraph.

###### Article 299

In the context of determining a compensatory allowance, by the judge or by the parties, or on the occasion of a request for revision, the parties provide the judge with a declaration certifying on their honour the accuracy of their resources, income, assets and living conditions.

###### Article 300

The compensatory allowance has a lump-sum character. It cannot be revised even in the event of an unforeseen change in the resources or needs of the parties, unless the absence of revision would have consequences of exceptional gravity for one of the spouses.

###### Article 301

When the composition of the assets of the spouse liable for the compensatory allowance permits, it takes the form of a capital sum whose amount is determined by the judge.

###### Article 302

The judge decides on the terms according to which the allocation or assignment of capital assets will be executed:
1° Payment of a sum of money;  
2° Abandonment of property in kind, movable or immovable, but for the usufruct only, the judgment operating as a forced transfer in favour of the creditor;  

3° Deposit of income-producing securities with a third party responsible for paying the income to the spouse entitled to the allowance until the fixed term.  
The divorce judgment may be made conditional upon the actual payment of the capital or the provision of the guarantees provided for in Article 306.

###### Article 303

If the spouse liable for the compensatory allowance does not have immediate liquid assets, he or she may be authorised, subject to the guarantees provided for in Article 306, to constitute the capital in three annual instalments.  
In the absence of capital or if it is insufficient, the compensatory allowance takes the form of an annuity.

###### Article 304

When the compensatory allowance takes the form of an annuity, this annuity is granted for a period equal to or less than the life of the creditor spouse.  
The annuity is indexed; the index is determined as in matters of maintenance.  
The amount of the annuity before indexation is fixed uniformly for its entire duration or may vary by successive periods according to the probable evolution of resources and needs.

###### Article 305

Upon the death of the debtor spouse, the burden of the annuity passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 306

Independently of the legal or judicial mortgage, the judge may require the debtor spouse to provide a personal or real security to guarantee the annuity.

###### Article 307

In the event of a joint application, the spouses determine the amount and terms of the compensatory allowance in the agreement they submit for approval by the judge.  
The judge, however, refuses to approve the agreement if it inequitably determines the rights and obligations of the spouses.

###### Article 308

The approved agreement has the same enforceable force as a judicial decision.  

It can only be modified by a new agreement between the spouses, also subject to approval.  
The spouses nevertheless have the option of providing in their agreement that each of them may, in the event of an unforeseen change in their resources and needs, request the judge to revise the compensatory allowance.

###### Article 309

The transfers and abandonments provided for in this paragraph are considered as participating in the matrimonial regime. They are not treated as gifts.

###### Article 310

The spouse through whose exclusive fault the divorce is pronounced is not entitled to any compensatory allowance.  

However, he or she may obtain compensation on an exceptional basis if, taking into account the duration of the common life and the collaboration provided to the other spouse's profession, it appears manifestly contrary to equity to refuse him or her any pecuniary compensation following the divorce.

###### § 4. Du devoir de secours après le divorce Article 311

When the divorce is pronounced for breakdown of common life, the spouse who initiated the divorce remains fully bound by the duty of support.  

In the case of Article 247, the duty of support covers everything necessary for the medical treatment of the sick spouse.

###### Article 312

The fulfilment of the duty of support takes the form of maintenance. This may always be revised according to the resources and needs of each of the spouses.

###### Article 313

Maintenance automatically ceases to be due if the spouse who is the creditor thereof enters into a new marriage.  
It is terminated if the creditor lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.

###### Article 314

Upon the death of the debtor spouse, the burden of the maintenance passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 315

When the composition of the assets of the debtor spouse is suitable, the maintenance is replaced, in whole or in part, by the provision of a capital sum, according to the rules of Articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309.  
If this capital becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the creditor spouse, the latter may request a supplement in the form of maintenance.

###### § 5. Du logement Article 316

If the premises serving as housing for the family belong in ownership or personally to one of the spouses, the judge may grant a lease thereof to the other spouse:
1° When the custody of one or more children has been entrusted to the latter;  
2° When the divorce has been pronounced at the request of the owner spouse, for breakdown of common life.  

In the case provided for in 1° above, the judge determines the duration of the lease and may renew it until the youngest of the children reaches the age of majority.  
In the case provided for in 2°, the lease may not be granted for a period exceeding nine years, but may be extended by a new decision. It terminates automatically in the event of remarriage of the person to whom it was granted. It is terminated if the latter lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.  
In all cases, the judge may terminate the lease if new circumstances justify it.

##### Section III : Des conséquences du divorce pour les enfants Article 317

Divorce leaves intact the rights and duties of the father and mother towards their children, subject to the rules that follow.

###### Article 318

According to the interests of minor children, their custody is entrusted to one or the other of the spouses.  
On an exceptional basis and if the interests of the children so require, this custody may be entrusted: 1° either to another person chosen preferably from among their relatives;  
2° or, if this proves impossible, to an educational establishment or a recognised association in this field.

###### Article 319

Before ruling on the custody of children, provisional or final, and on visitation rights, the judge may assign any qualified person to conduct a social investigation. The purpose of this investigation is to gather information on the material and moral situation of the family, on the conditions in which the children live and are educated, and on the measures to be taken in their interest.  
If one of the spouses contests the conclusions of the social investigation, he or she may request a counter-investigation. The social investigation may not be used in the debate on the grounds for divorce.

###### Article 320

The spouse to whom custody of the children has not been entrusted retains the right to supervise their maintenance and education. He or she contributes to it in proportion to his or her resources.  

A right of visitation and accommodation may only be refused for serious reasons.  
He or she may be charged with administering, under judicial supervision, all or part of the children's patrimony, by way of derogation from articles 480 and 518 paragraph 2, if the interest of proper administration of that patrimony so requires.

###### Article 321

The judge rules on the attribution of custody and on the modalities of the exercise of parental authority, at the request of one of the spouses, a family member or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 322

The judge takes into account:
1° Agreements reached between the spouses;  
2° Information that has been gathered in the investigation and counter-investigation provided for in article 319;  
3° Feelings expressed by minor children when their hearing has appeared necessary and does not entail any disadvantages for them.

###### Article 323

Decisions relating to the exercise of parental authority may be modified or supplemented at any time by the judge, at the request of a spouse, a family member or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 324

In the case of divorce by joint application, the provisions of the agreement approved by the judge relating to the exercise of parental authority may be revised, for serious reasons, at the request of one of the spouses or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 325

The contribution to the maintenance and education of children provided for in article 320 takes the form of maintenance payments made to the person who has custody of them.  
The modalities and guarantees of this maintenance payment are fixed by the judgment or, in the case of divorce by joint application, by the agreement of the spouses approved by the judge.

###### Article 326

When the composition of the debtor's assets so permits, the maintenance payment may be replaced, in whole or in part, according to the rules of articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309, by the payment of a sum of money into the hands of an accredited body charged with granting the child in return an indexed annuity, the abandonment of property in usufruct or the allocation of income-producing property.

###### Article 327

If the capital thus constituted becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the children, the person who has custody may request the allocation of a supplement in the form of maintenance payments.

###### Article 328

The parent who assumes primary responsibility for adult children who cannot themselves provide for their needs may request his or her spouse to pay a contribution to their maintenance and education.

#### Chapitre IV : De la séparation de corps

##### Section I : Des cas et de la procédure de la séparation de corps

###### Article 329

Legal separation may be pronounced at the request of one of the spouses in the same cases and under the same conditions as divorce.

###### Article 330

The spouse against whom an application for divorce is presented may file a counterclaim for legal separation. However, when the main application for divorce is based on the definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the counterclaim may only seek divorce.  
The spouse against whom an application for legal separation is presented may file a counterclaim for divorce.

###### Article 331

When an application for divorce and an application for legal separation are concurrently presented, the judge examines the application for divorce first. He or she pronounces it as soon as the conditions are met. Failing that, he or she rules on the application for legal separation.  
However, when these applications are based on fault, the judge examines them simultaneously and, if he or she grants them, pronounces divorce with shared fault in respect of both spouses.

###### Article 332

The rules contained in article 250 as well as in chapter II above are applicable to the procedure for legal separation.

##### Section II : Des conséquences de la séparation de corps Article 333

Legal separation does not dissolve the marriage but it terminates the duty of cohabitation.

###### Article 334

Legal separation allows each of the spouses who was using the other's name to retain that use for the future. However, the judgment of legal separation, or a subsequent judgment, may prohibit a spouse from retaining the use of his or her spouse's name.

###### Article 335

In the event of the death of one of the spouses legally separated, the other spouse retains the rights that the law grants to the surviving spouse. When legal separation is pronounced by mutual consent, the spouses may include in their agreement a waiver of the succession rights conferred upon them by articles 858 et seq. and 872 et seq. of this code.

###### Article 336

Legal separation always entails separation of property.  

With regard to property, the date on which legal separation produces its effects is determined in accordance with the provisions of articles 286 to 288.

###### Article 337

Legal separation leaves the duty of support subsisting; the judgment pronouncing it or a subsequent judgment fixes the maintenance payment that is due to the spouse in need.  

This payment is awarded without consideration of fault. The debtor spouse may nevertheless invoke, where applicable, the provisions of article 215, paragraph 2.  

This payment is subject to the rules of maintenance obligations; the provisions of article 315 are however applicable to it.

###### Article 338

Subject to the provisions of this section, the consequences of legal separation are governed by the same rules as the consequences of divorce set out in chapter III above.

##### Section III : De la fin de la séparation de corps Article 339

The voluntary resumption of life together terminates legal separation.  

To be enforceable against third parties, this must either be recorded by notarial deed or be the subject of a declaration to the civil registrar. Mention of it is made in the margin of the marriage certificate.  
Separation of property subsists unless the spouses adopt a new matrimonial regime following the rules of article 1642.

###### Article 340

At the request of one of the spouses, the judgment of legal separation is converted by operation of law into a judgment of divorce when the legal separation has lasted three years.

###### Article 341

In all cases of legal separation, it may be converted into divorce by a joint application.  
When legal separation has been pronounced on joint application, it may only be converted into divorce by a new joint application.

###### Article 342

As a result of the conversion, the ground for legal separation becomes the ground for divorce; the attribution of fault is not modified.  
The judge fixes the consequences of the divorce. Benefits and payments between spouses are determined according to the rules specific to divorce.

###### Article 343

The wife may contract a new marriage as soon as the conversion decision has become res judicata.

#### Chapter V

On the conflict of laws relating to divorce and legal separation Article 344
Divorce and legal separation are governed by Djiboutian law: when both spouses are of Djiboutian nationality; when both spouses have their domicile on Djiboutian territory; when no foreign law recognizes jurisdiction, while the Djiboutian courts have jurisdiction to hear the divorce or legal separation.

### Title VIII: On filiation

Chapter I: Provisions common to legitimate filiation and natural filiation Section I: On presumptions relating to filiation

###### Article 345

The law presumes that the child was conceived during the period extending from the three hundredth to the one hundred eightieth day, inclusively, before the date of birth.  
Conception is presumed to have occurred at any moment during this period, according to what is required in the interest of the child.  

Proof to the contrary is admissible to rebut these presumptions.

###### Article 346

Possession of status is established by a sufficient combination of facts that indicate the relationship of filiation and kinship between an individual and the family to which he is said to belong.  
Possession of status must be continuous.

###### Article 347

The principal of these facts are: that the individual has always borne the name of those from whom he is said to descend; that they have treated him as their child, and that he has treated them as his father and mother; that they have, in that capacity, provided for his education, maintenance and establishment; that he is recognized as such, in society and by the family; that the public authority considers him as such.

###### Article 348

The parents or the child may request from the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or from the judge designated for that purpose that there be issued to them, under the conditions provided for in articles 106 and 107 of this code, a certificate of notoriety establishing proof of possession of status until proof to the contrary; this without prejudice to all other means of proof to which they could resort to establish its existence in court, if it were to be contested.

##### Section II: On actions relating to filiation Article 349

No action is received regarding the filiation of a child who was not born viable.

###### Article 350

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction to hear actions relating to filiation under the civil code. The Personal Status Court of First Instance has jurisdiction to hear disputes relating to personal status matters of persons governed by the family code.

###### Article 351

In case of an offense affecting the filiation of an individual, the criminal action may only be decided after the judgment that has become res judicata on the question of filiation.

###### Article 352

Whenever they are not confined by law within shorter terms, actions relating to filiation are prescribed by thirty years from the day on which the individual would have been deprived of the status he claims, or began to enjoy the status that is contested.

###### Article 353

The action that belonged to an individual regarding his filiation may only be exercised by his heirs in cases where that individual died as a minor or within five years after his majority or emancipation.  
His heirs may also pursue the action that he had already initiated, unless there has been a withdrawal or lapse of proceedings.

###### Article 354

Actions relating to filiation may not be the subject of waiver.

###### Article 355

Judgments rendered in matters of filiation are opposable to any person, even to those who were not parties to the proceedings; but persons who were not parties to the proceedings have the right to file third-party opposition against said judgments.  
Judges may of their own motion order that all interested parties whom they consider should be bound by the judgment be joined to the case.

###### Article 356

Similarly when, in one of the actions opened by articles 418 and 436 below, a plea of inadmissibility or a defense is raised based on the fact that the mother had, during the legal period of conception, relations with a third party, the judge may order that the latter be called to the case.

###### Article 357

The courts settle conflicts of filiation for which the law has not established another principle, by determining by all means of proof the most plausible filiation.  
In the absence of sufficient elements of conviction, they have regard to possession of status.

###### Article 358

In the case where they are led to dismiss the claim of the party who was, in fact, taking care of the education of the minor child, the courts may, nevertheless, taking into account the interest of the child, grant that party a right of visitation.

##### Section III

On the conflict of laws relating to the establishment of filiation Article 359
Filiation is governed by the personal law of the mother on the day of the child's birth; if the mother is not known, by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 360

However, if the legitimate child and his father and mother, the natural child and one of his father or mother have in Djibouti their habitual residence, common or separate, possession of status produces all the consequences that flow from it according to Djiboutian law, this even in the case where the other elements of filiation could have depended on a foreign law.

###### Article 361

Marriage entails legitimation when, on the day the union was celebrated, this consequence is admitted, either by the law governing the effects of marriage, or by the personal law of one of the spouses, or by the personal law of the child.  

Legitimation by judicial authority is governed, at the choice of the applicant, either by the personal law of the latter, or by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 362

Voluntary recognition of paternity or maternity is valid if it was made in conformity with either the personal law of its author, or the personal law of the child.

###### Article 363

The action for maintenance is governed, at the choice of the child, either by the law of his habitual residence, or by the law of the habitual residence of the debtor.

#### Chapter II: On legitimate filiation

##### Section I: On the presumption of paternity Article 364

The child conceived or born during marriage has the husband as father.  

Nevertheless, the latter may disavow the child in court, if he establishes facts proper to demonstrate that he cannot be the father.

###### Article 365

In case of judgment or even application, either for divorce or for legal separation, the presumption of paternity does not apply to the child born more than three hundred days after the order authorizing the spouses to reside separately, and less than one hundred eighty days since the final rejection of the application or since the reconciliation.  
The presumption of paternity nevertheless recovers, by operation of law, its force:
1° If the child, with respect to the spouses, has possession of status as a legitimate child and if he does not have a paternal filiation already established with respect to a third party.  
2° If, upon application brought by each of the spouses before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance during the minority of the child, proof is provided that the husband is indeed the father of the child. This action is also open to the child during the ten years following his majority.

###### Article 366

The presumption of paternity is set aside when the child, registered without indication of the husband's name, has possession of status only with respect to the mother.

###### Article 367

When the presumption of paternity is set aside under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the child's filiation is established with respect to the mother as if there had been a disavowal admitted in court.  
Either spouse may request that the effects of the presumption of paternity be restored, by proving that, during the legal period of conception, a factual reunion took place between them, which makes the husband's paternity plausible.

###### Article 368

A child born before the one hundred and eightieth day of the marriage is legitimate and deemed to have been so from conception.  

The husband, however, may disavow the child according to the rules of Article 312.  

He may even disavow the child on the sole proof of the date of delivery, unless he knew of the pregnancy before the marriage, or unless he behaved as the father after the birth.

###### Article 369

The presumption of paternity is not applicable to a child born more than three hundred days after the dissolution of the marriage, nor, in case of declared absence of the husband, to one who is born to a married woman more than one year after the absence or death of her husband or the date of divorce.

###### Article 370

The husband must bring the action for disavowal within six months of the birth, when he is present at the place.  
If he was not present at the place, within six months of his return.  

And within six months following the discovery of the fraud, if the birth of the child had been concealed from him.

###### Article 371

If the husband died before bringing the action, but while still within the time limit to do so, his heirs shall have standing to contest the legitimacy of the child.  
Their action, however, shall cease to be admissible when six months have elapsed from the time when the child took possession of the alleged paternal property, or from the time when they were disturbed by him in their own possession.

###### Article 372

Any extrajudicial act containing disavowal on the part of the husband or contestation of legitimacy on the part of the heirs, shall be deemed null and void if it is not followed by a court action within six months.

###### Article 373

The action for disavowal is brought, in the presence of the mother, against a guardian ad hoc, appointed to the child by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or by the judge designated for that purpose.

###### Article 374

Even in the absence of disavowal, the mother may contest the husband's paternity, but only for the purposes of legitimation, when she has, after dissolution of the marriage, remarried the true father of the child.

###### Article 375

On pain of inadmissibility, the action, brought against the husband or his heirs, is joined to a request for legitimation made in the terms of Article 390 below.  
It must be brought by the mother and her new spouse within six months of their marriage and before the child has reached the age of seven years.

###### Article 376

Both claims are decided by a single judgment, which may grant the contestation of paternity only if the legitimation is admitted.

##### Section II: Proof of legitimate filiation Article 377

The filiation of legitimate children is proved by birth certificates recorded in the civil status registers.

###### Article 378

In the absence of such title, possession of the status of legitimate child is sufficient.

###### Article 379

There is possession of the status of legitimate child only insofar as it connects the child indivisibly to both father and mother.

###### Article 380

No one may claim a status contrary to that given by his birth certificate and possession consistent with that certificate.  
And reciprocally, no one may contest the status of one who has possession consistent with his birth certificate.

###### Article 381

However, if it is alleged that there has been a false representation of a child, or substitution, even involuntary, either before or after the drafting of the birth certificate, proof thereof shall be admissible and may be made by all means.

###### Article 382

In the absence of title and possession of status, or if the child was registered either under false names or without indication of the mother's name, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses.  
Proof by witnesses may not, however, be admitted unless there exists either a commencement of proof in writing, or presumptions or indications serious enough to determine its admission.

###### Article 383

Commencement of proof in writing results from family documents, registers and domestic papers, as well as from all other public or private writings emanating from a party involved in the dispute or who would have an interest therein if alive.

###### Article 384

Contrary proof may be made by all means capable of establishing that the claimant is not the child of the mother he claims to have, or even, maternity being proved, that he is not the child of the mother's husband.  
If the husband was not made a party to the status claim proceedings, he may contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the judgment having become res judicata granting the child's claim.

###### Article 385

Without waiting for a status claim to be brought by the child, the husband may, by all means, contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the birth.

###### Article 386

After the husband's death, his heirs shall likewise have the right to contest his paternity either preventively if the husband was still within the time limit to do so, or in defense to a status claim action.

###### Article 387

The spouses, separately or jointly, may, by providing the proof provided for in Article 382 above, claim a child as being theirs; but if the child already has another established filiation, they must first demonstrate its inaccuracy, assuming that one is in one of the cases where the law authorizes such demonstration.

##### Section III: Legitimation Article 388

Legitimation is the act by which a lawfully married couple confers upon a natural child the status of legitimate child.  

Legitimation may benefit all natural children, as soon as, either by voluntary recognition or by judgment, their filiation has been legally established.  

Legitimation takes place either by marriage of the parents or by authority of justice.

###### § 1. Legitimation by marriage Article 389

All children born out of wedlock are legitimated by operation of law by the subsequent marriage of their father and mother.  

If their filiation was not already established, these children are the subject of recognition at the time of the celebration of the marriage. In this case, the civil status officer who performs the celebration records the recognition and legitimation in a separate act.

###### Article 390

When the filiation of a natural child has been established with respect to his father and mother or one of them only after their marriage, legitimation may take place only by virtue of a judgment.  
This judgment must establish that the child has had, since the celebration of the marriage, possession of the status of common child.

###### Article 391

Every legitimation is noted in the margin of the birth certificate of the legitimated child.  
This notation may be requested by any interested party. In the case of Article 389, the civil status officer provides for it himself, if he has had knowledge of the existence of the children.

###### Article 392

Legitimation may take place after the death of the child, if he left descendants; it then benefits them.

###### Article 393

Legitimation confers upon the legitimated child the rights and duties of a legitimate child. It takes effect on the date of the marriage.

###### § 2. Legitimation by judicial authority

###### Article 394

If it appears that marriage is impossible between the two parents, the benefit of legitimation may still be conferred on the child by judicial authority provided that the child has, with respect to the parent who requests it, the possession of status of natural child.

###### Article 395

The application for legitimation is made by one of the two parents or by both jointly before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 396

If one of the child's parents was, at the time of conception, bound by a marriage that has not been dissolved, his or her application is admissible only with the consent of his or her spouse.

###### Article 397

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and, after having received or solicited, as the case may be, the observations of the child himself or herself, of the other parent when he or she is not a party to the application, as well as of the applicant's spouse, it pronounces, if it deems it justified, the legitimation.

###### Article 398

Legitimation by judicial authority takes effect on the date of the decision that pronounces it definitively.

If it took place at the request of only one of the parents, it has no effect with respect to the other; it does not entail modification of the child's name, except by contrary decision of the Civil Chamber.

###### Article 399

If legitimation by judicial authority has been pronounced with respect to both parents, the child takes the father's name; if he or she is a minor, his or her custody is decided by the Civil Chamber, as in matters of divorce.

###### Article 400

The provisions of articles 391 to 393, paragraph 1 are applicable to legitimation by judicial authority.

#### Chapter III: Natural filiation

##### Section I

Effects of natural filiation and its modes of establishment in general Article 401
Every natural child falls under the regime of the civil code whenever his or her parents have expressed their will to subject this child to this regime at the time of the declaration of his or her birth to the civil status officer.
The parent who, alone, makes the declaration is deemed to act in agreement with the other for this purpose. The one who has not made the declaration has one month, from the declaration made to the civil status officer to contest its meaning. In case of disagreement between the two parents, the regime of the family code shall then be applicable to the child.
If the parents of this child give birth to one or more other common children, these shall be subject to the choice made for the first common child.

###### Article 402

The natural child has in principle the same rights and the same duties as the legitimate child in his or her relations with his or her father and mother.

He or she enters into the family of his or her author.

###### Article 403

The natural child acquires the name of that one of his or her two parents with respect to whom his or her filiation is established first; the name of his or her father, if the filiation is established simultaneously with respect to both.

###### Article 404

Even in the case where his or her filiation was established only second with respect to the father, the natural child may take the latter's name by substitution, if, during his or her minority, his or her two parents make the joint declaration before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose.

If the child is more than fifteen years old, his or her personal consent is necessary.

###### Article 405

In all other cases, the change of name of the natural child must be requested from the Court of First Instance.
The action is available during the child's minority and in the two years following either his or her majority or a modification made to his or her status.

###### Article 406

The substitution of name extends by operation of law to the minor children of the person concerned. It extends to adult children only with their consent.

###### Article 407

In the absence of established paternal filiation, the mother's husband may confer, by substitution, his own name on the child by a declaration that he will make jointly with the mother, under the conditions provided for in article 404 above.
The child may however request to resume the name he or she bore previously by a request that he or she will submit to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within two years following his or her majority.

###### Article 408

The rules for attribution of name provided for in the preceding articles do not prejudice the effects of possession of status.

###### Article 409

In the case provided for in the third paragraph of article 401 above, the natural child may be raised at the conjugal domicile only with the consent of the spouse of his or her author.

###### Article 410

Natural filiation is legally established, either by voluntary recognition, or by judicial declaration, following an action in search of paternity or maternity.
Natural filiation may also be legally established by the necessary effect of a judgment, in particular following an action in disavowal or in contestation of legitimacy.

###### Article 411

Any recognition is null, any request in search is inadmissible, when the child has a legitimate filiation already established by possession of status.

###### Article 412

If there exists between the father and mother of the natural child one of the impediments to marriage provided for by articles 173 and 174 by reason of kinship, the filiation being already established with respect to one, it is prohibited to establish the filiation with respect to the other.

##### Section II: Recognition of natural children Article 413

The recognition of a natural child shall be made by authentic act, when it has not been made in the birth certificate.

###### Article 414

The recognition by the father, without the indication and avowal of the mother, has effect only with respect to the father.

###### Article 415

The birth certificate bearing the indication of the mother is valid as recognition, when it is corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 416

As long as it has not been contested in court, a recognition renders inadmissible the establishment of another natural filiation that would contradict it.

###### Article 417

The recognition may be contested by all persons who have an interest therein, even by its author.
The action is also available to the public prosecutor, if indications drawn from the acts themselves render the declared filiation implausible.

When there exists a possession of status consistent with the recognition and which has lasted at least ten years since the latter, no contestation is admissible any longer, except on the part of the other parent, of the child himself or herself or of those who claim to be the true parents.

##### Section III: Actions in search of paternity and maternity Article 418
