In the absence of title and possession of status, the search for maternity is admitted. The mother may however, at the time of childbirth, request that the secrecy of her admission and her identity be preserved.
The child who exercises the action is required to prove that he or she is the one of whom the alleged mother gave birth.

He or she may prove it by establishing that he or she has, with respect to the latter, the possession of status of natural child. Failing that, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses, if there exist either serious presumptions or indications, or a beginning of proof in writing, within the meaning of article 383.

###### Article 419

Paternity outside marriage may be judicially declared in the presence of constant facts that render the filiation plausible.

###### Article 420

The right of action belongs only to the child.  
The parent, even if a minor, with respect to whom filiation is established has, during the child's minority, sole capacity to bring an action to establish maternity or paternity.  

If no filiation link is established or if that parent is deceased or unable to express their will, the action is brought by the guardian in accordance with the provisions of Article 542, paragraph 2.

###### Article 421

The action to establish paternity is brought against the alleged parent or against their heirs. In the absence of heirs or if they have renounced the succession, it is directed against the State. Heirs who have renounced are called to the proceedings to assert their rights.

###### Article 422

The action must, on pain of forfeiture, be brought within two years following the birth.  

However, when the alleged father and the mother lived during the legal period of conception in a state of cohabitation, implying, in the absence of a shared life, stable and continuous relations, or when the alleged father has provided for or participated in the maintenance, education or establishment of the child in the capacity of father, the action may be brought until the expiration of two years following the cessation, either of the cohabitation, or of the acts of participation in the maintenance and education of the child.  

If it has not been brought during the child's minority, the child may still bring it during the two years following their majority.

###### Article 423

When it grants the action, the court may, at the mother's request, order the father to reimburse her for all or part of her maternity and maintenance expenses during the three months preceding and the three months following the birth, without prejudice to the damages to which she might be entitled by application of Article 1391.

###### Article 424

The court rules, if appropriate, on the attribution of the name and on the exercise of parental authority, in accordance with Articles 405 and 486.

###### Article 425

In rejecting the claim, the judges may, nevertheless, award maintenance to the child, if relations between the mother and the defendant have been demonstrated under the conditions provided for in Articles 426 and following.

##### Section IV: Action for maintenance Article 426

Any natural child whose paternal filiation is not legally established may claim maintenance from the person who had relations with their mother during the legal period of conception.  

The action is admissible even if the father or the mother was at the time of conception bound by the ties of marriage with another person, or if there existed between them one of the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 173 to 176 of this code.

###### Article 427

The action for maintenance may also be brought by the child of a married woman, if their status as a legitimate child is not corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 428

Maintenance is determined, in the form of a pension, according to the needs of the child, the resources of the debtor, and the family situation of the latter.  

The pension may be due beyond the child's majority, if they are still in need, unless that state is attributable to their fault.

###### Article 429

When Article 356 above applies, the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, in the absence of other elements of decision, has the power to impose compensation intended to ensure the maintenance and education of the child on the defendants, if faults are established against them, or if commitments have been made previously by them.  
The President determines the period within which the compensation must be paid to the child's legal representative; in case of failure to pay within the indicated period, the creditor may seize that judge by simple petition with a view to accompanying the judgment with a penalty payment which shall, in this case, be immediately final.  

The provisions governing maintenance are, for the rest, applicable to this compensation.

###### Article 430

The defendant may dismiss the claim by proving that they could not be the father of the child.

###### Article 431

The burden of maintenance is transmitted to the debtor's succession within the limits of Articles 216 to 219.

###### Article 432

Articles 420 to 423 above are applicable to the action for maintenance.

###### Article 433

The judgment awarding maintenance creates between the debtor and the beneficiary, as well as, where applicable, between each of them and the relatives or spouse of the other, the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 161 to 164 of this code.

###### Article 434

The res judicata on the action for maintenance raises no bar to a subsequent action to establish paternity.  
The award of maintenance shall cease to have effect if the paternal filiation of the child is subsequently established with respect to someone other than the debtor.

### Title IX: Adoptive filiation

Chapter I: Full adoption

##### Section I: Conditions required for full adoption Article 435

Adoption, under the regime established by the Civil Code, may be requested after five years of marriage by two spouses not legally separated.

###### Article 436

If the adopter is married and not legally separated, the consent of their spouse is necessary unless that spouse is unable to express their will.

###### Article 437

The adopters must be fifteen years older than the children they propose to adopt. If the latter are the children of their spouse, the required age difference is only ten years.  

However, the court may, if there are just grounds, grant the adoption when the age difference is less than those provided for in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 438

Adoption is permitted only in favor of children under fifteen years of age, received into the home of the adopter or adopters for at least six months.  
However, if the child is over fifteen years of age and was received before reaching that age by persons who did not meet the legal conditions to adopt or if they were the subject of a simple adoption before reaching that age, full adoption may be requested, if the conditions are met, throughout the child's minority.  

If they are over thirteen years of age, the adoptee must personally consent to their full adoption.

###### Article 439

No one may be adopted by several persons except by two spouses.  

However, a new adoption may be granted either after the death of the adopter, or of both adopters, or even after the death of one of the two adopters, if the application is presented by the new spouse of the survivor of them.

###### Article 440

May be adopted:
1° Children for whom the father and mother or the family council have validly consented to the adoption;  
2° Children who have been legally entrusted to a duly registered association for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defense or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognized by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.  
3° Children declared abandoned under the conditions provided for in Article 448.

###### Article 441

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to their father and mother, both must consent to the adoption.  
If one of the two is dead or unable to express their will, if they have lost their parental authority rights, the consent of the other suffices.

###### Article 442

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to only one of his or her parents, that parent gives consent to the adoption.

###### Article 443

When the father and mother of the child are deceased, unable to express their will or have lost their parental authority rights, consent is given by the family council, after obtaining the opinion of the person who, in fact, takes care of the child.

The same applies when the filiation of the child is not established.

###### Article 444

Consent to adoption is given before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose of the domicile or residence of the person who consents, or before a Djiboutian or foreign notary, or before Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. It may also be received by an association duly registered for at least five years as of the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defense or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognized by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.  
Consent to adoption may be withdrawn within three months. The withdrawal must be made by any means allowing confirmation of its receipt by the person or service that had received the consent to adoption. The return of the child to his or her parents upon request, even verbal, also constitutes proof of withdrawal.  

If at the expiration of the three-month period, the consent has not been withdrawn, the parents may still request the return of the child provided that the child has not been placed with a view to adoption. If the person who has taken the child in refuses to return him or her, the parents may apply to the court, which assesses, taking into account the interest of the child, whether it is appropriate to order the return. The return renders the consent to adoption null and void.

###### Article 445

The father and mother or the family council may consent to the adoption of the child while leaving the choice of the adoptive parent to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorized adoption agency that would provisionally take in the child.

###### Article 446

Except in the case where there is a relationship of kinship or affinity up to and including the sixth degree between the adoptive parent and the adopted person, consent to the adoption of children under two years of age is valid only if the child has been effectively handed over to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorized adoption agency.

###### Article 447

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may grant the adoption if it considers abusive the refusal of consent opposed by the legitimate and natural parents or by only one of them, when they have shown no interest in the child at the risk of compromising his or her health or morality.  
The same applies in case of abusive refusal of consent by the family council.

###### Article 448

A child taken in by a private individual, a private agency or an association as designated in Article 444, whose parents have manifestly shown no interest during the year preceding the filing of the application for declaration of abandonment, may be declared abandoned by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.  
Parents who have not maintained with the child the relations necessary to maintain emotional ties are considered to have manifestly shown no interest in their child.  
The simple withdrawal of consent to adoption, the request for news or the expressed but unfulfilled intention to take back the child, is not a sufficient mark of interest to automatically justify the rejection of an application for declaration of abandonment.  

Abandonment is not declared if, during the period provided for in the first paragraph of this article, a member of the family has requested to assume responsibility for the child and if this request is deemed to be in the interest of the child.  

When it declares the child abandoned, the court delegates by the same decision the parental authority rights over the child to an association as designated in Article 444 or to the private individual guardian of the child.  

Third-party opposition is admissible only in case of fraud, deceit or error as to the identity of the child.

##### Section II

Placement with a view to full adoption and judgment of full adoption Article 449
Placement with a view to adoption is carried out by the effective delivery to the prospective adoptive parents of a child for whom consent to adoption has been validly and definitively given, or of a child declared abandoned by judicial decision.  

When the filiation of the child is not established, there may be no placement with a view to adoption during a period of three months from the taking in of the child.  
Placement may not take place when the parents have requested the return of the child as long as no decision has been made on the merits of this request at the application of the most diligent party.

###### Article 450

Placement with a view to adoption prevents any return of the child to his or her family of origin. It precludes any declaration of filiation and any acknowledgment.  
If the placement with a view to adoption ceases or if the court has refused to grant the adoption, the effects of this placement are retroactively resolved.

###### Article 451

Adoption is granted at the request of the adoptive parent by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, which verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and whether the adoption is in the interest of the child.  
In the case where the adoptive parent has descendants, the court further verifies whether the adoption is not likely to compromise family life.  

If the adoptive parent dies after having lawfully taken in the child with a view to his or her adoption, the application may be filed in his or her name by the surviving spouse or one of the heirs of the adoptive parent.  

The judgment granting the adoption is not reasoned.

###### Article 452

Third-party opposition to the adoption judgment is admissible only in case of fraud or deceit attributable to the adoptive parents.

###### Article 453

Within fifteen days of the date on which it becomes final, the decision granting full adoption is transcribed in the civil status registers of the place of birth of the adopted person, at the request of the Public Prosecutor.  

The transcription states the day, time and place of birth, the sex of the child as well as his or her given names, as they result from the adoption judgment, the given names, surnames, date and place of birth, profession and domicile of the adoptive parent or parents. It contains no indication relating to the actual filiation of the child.  

The transcription serves as a birth certificate for the adopted person.  

The original birth certificate and, where applicable, the birth certificate established pursuant to Article 89 are, at the initiative of the Public Prosecutor, marked with the notation "adoption" and considered null and void.

##### Section III: Effects of full adoption Article 454

Adoption produces its effects from the day of filing of the application for adoption.

###### Article 455

Adoption confers on the child a filiation that replaces his or her filiation of origin: the adopted person ceases to belong to his or her family by blood, subject to the prohibitions on marriage referred to in Articles 161 to 164.  
However, the adoption of the child of the spouse allows his or her filiation of origin to subsist with respect to that spouse and his or her family. It produces, for the rest, the effects of an adoption by two spouses.

###### Article 456

Adoption confers upon the child the name of the adopter and, in the case of adoption by two spouses, the name of the husband.

Upon the request of the adopter or adopters, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may modify the given names of the child.

If the adopter is a married woman, the Civil Chamber may, in the adoption judgment, deduce from the consent of the adopter's husband that the latter's name shall be conferred upon the adoptee; if the husband is deceased or unable to express his will, the court shall assess sovereignly after having consulted the husband's heirs or his closest successors.

###### Article 457

The adoptee has, in the family of the adopter, the same rights and the same obligations as a legitimate child.

###### Article 458

Adoption is irrevocable.

#### Chapter II: Simple Adoption

##### Section I: Required Conditions and Judgment Article 459

Simple adoption is permitted regardless of the age of the adoptee.

If the adoptee is over fifteen years of age, he must personally consent to the adoption.

###### Article 460

The provisions of Articles 435 to 437, 439 to 448, 451, 452, 454 and 456, last paragraph, are applicable to simple adoption.

###### Article 461

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes res judicata, the decision pronouncing simple adoption is noted or transcribed on the civil status registers at the request of the Public Prosecutor.

##### Section II: Effects of Simple Adoption Article 462

Simple adoption confers the name of the adopter upon the adoptee by adding it to the latter's name. The court may however decide that the adoptee shall bear only the name of the adopter.

###### Article 463

The adoptee remains in his family of origin and retains all his rights therein, in particular his inheritance rights.

The prohibitions on marriage provided for in Articles 173 to 176 of this code apply between the adoptee and his family of origin.

###### Article 464

The adopter alone is vested with regard to the adoptee with all the rights of parental authority, including that of consenting to the marriage of the adoptee, unless he is the spouse of the father or mother of the adoptee; in that case, the adopter has parental authority concurrently with his spouse, but the latter retains the exercise thereof.
The rights of parental authority are exercised by the adopter or adopters under the same conditions as with regard to a legitimate child.
The rules of legal administration and guardianship of a legitimate child apply to the adoptee.

###### Article 465

The relationship resulting from adoption extends to the legitimate children of the adoptee.

Marriage is prohibited:
1° Between the adopter, the adoptee and his descendants;
2° Between the adoptee and the spouse of the adopter; reciprocally between the adopter and the spouse of the adoptee; 3° Between the adoptive children of the same individual;
4° Between the adoptee and the children of the adopter.

Nevertheless, the prohibitions on marriage set forth in 3° and 4° above may be lifted by dispensation of the President of the Republic, if there are serious causes.

The prohibition on marriage set forth in 2° above may be lifted under the same conditions when the person who created the affinity is deceased.

###### Article 466

The adoptee owes maintenance to the adopter if he is in need and, reciprocally, the adopter owes maintenance to the adoptee.
The obligation to provide maintenance continues to exist between the adoptee and his father and mother. However, the father and mother of the adoptee are only required to provide him with maintenance if he cannot obtain it from the adopter.

###### Article 467

The adoptee and his legitimate descendants have in the family of the adopter the same succession rights as a legitimate child without however acquiring the status of forced heir with regard to the ascendants of the adopter.

###### Article 468

If the adoptee dies without descendants, the property given by the adopter or received in his succession returns to the adopter or to his descendants, if they still exist in kind at the time of the adoptee's death, subject to contributing to the debts and subject to rights acquired by third parties. The property that the adoptee had received gratuitously from his father and mother likewise returns to the latter or to their descendants.
The remainder of the adoptee's property is divided in half between the family of origin and the family of the adopter, without prejudice to the rights of the spouse over the entire succession.

###### Article 469

Adoption retains all its effects, notwithstanding the subsequent establishment of a filiation link.

###### Article 470

If serious grounds are established, adoption may be revoked, at the request of the adopter or the adoptee.
The request for revocation made by the adopter is only admissible if the adoptee is over fifteen years of age.
When the adoptee is a minor, the father and mother by blood or, in their absence, a member of the family of origin up to and including the fourth degree, may also request revocation.

###### Article 471

The judgment revoking adoption must be reasoned.
The operative part of the judgment is noted in the margin of the birth certificate or the transcription of the adoption judgment, under the conditions provided for in Article 461.

###### Article 472

Revocation terminates for the future all the effects of adoption.

### Title X: Parental Authority

Chapter I: Parental Authority in Relation to the Person of the Child

###### Article 473

The child, at any age, owes honor and respect to his father and mother.

###### Article 474

He remains under their authority until his majority or emancipation.

###### Article 475

Authority belongs to the father and mother to protect the child in his safety, his health and his morality. They have with regard to him the right and duty of custody, supervision and education.

###### Article 476

The child may not, without permission of the father and mother, leave the family home and he may not be removed from it except in cases of necessity determined by law.

###### Article 477

The father and mother may not, except for serious reasons, obstruct the personal relations of the child with his grandparents. In the absence of agreement between the parties, the modalities of these relations are settled by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.
In consideration of exceptional situations, the Civil Chamber may grant a right of correspondence or visitation to other persons, whether related or not.

##### Section I: Exercise of Parental Authority Article 478

During marriage, the father and mother jointly exercise their authority.

###### Article 479

If the father and mother cannot agree on what the interest of the child requires, the practice that they may have previously followed on similar occasions shall serve as a rule for them.
In the absence of such a practice or in case of dispute over its existence or its validity, the more diligent spouse may refer the matter to the President of the Court of First Instance or the judge he delegates for this purpose, who shall rule after having attempted to reconcile the parties.

###### Article 480

With regard to third parties in good faith, each of the spouses is deemed to act with the agreement of the other, when he alone performs a usual act of parental authority in relation to the person of the child.

###### Article 481

Loses the exercise of parental authority or is temporarily deprived of it that one of the father and mother who is in one of the following cases:
1° If he is unable to express his will, by reason of his incapacity, his absence, his remoteness or any other cause;  
2° If he has consented to a delegation of his rights according to the rules established in section III of this chapter; 3° If he has been convicted under one of the various counts of family abandonment, as long as he has not resumed his obligations for a period of at least six months;  
4° If a judgment of forfeiture or withdrawal has been pronounced against him, for those of his rights which have been withdrawn from him.

###### Article 482

If one of the father and mother dies or is in one of the cases enumerated by the preceding article, the exercise of parental authority is devolved in full to the other.

###### Article 483

If the father and mother are divorced or legally separated, parental authority is exercised by the one of them to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other.  
When custody has been entrusted to a third party, the other attributes of parental authority continue to be exercised by the father and mother. But the court, in designating a third party as provisional guardian, may decide that he must request the opening of a guardianship.  

When ruling, the judge always does so taking into consideration the best interests of the child.

###### Article 484

Divorce or legal separation does not prevent the devolution provided for in article 482, even when the one of the father and mother who remains able to exercise parental authority had been deprived of custody by effect of the judgment pronounced against him.  
Nevertheless, the Civil Chamber which had ruled last on custody may always be seized by the family or by the public prosecutor, in order to designate a third party as guardian of the child, with or without opening of a guardianship, as stated in the preceding article.  
In exceptional circumstances, the Civil Chamber which rules on custody of the child after divorce or legal separation may decide, even during the lifetime of the spouses, that it will not pass to the survivor in case of death of the custodial spouse. It may, in this case, designate the person to whom custody will be provisionally devolved.

###### Article 485

If there no longer remains either father or mother able to exercise parental authority, there shall be grounds for opening a guardianship.

###### Article 486

Concerning the natural child, parental authority is exercised by the one of the father and mother who has voluntarily acknowledged him, if he has been acknowledged by only one of them.  
If both have acknowledged him, parental authority is exercised in full by the mother. The court may, nevertheless, at the request of either one or the other, or of the public prosecutor, decide that it will be exercised either by the father alone, or by the father and mother jointly, to whom articles 478 to 480 will then be applicable, as if the child were a legitimate child.

##### Section II: Educational Assistance Article 487

If the health, safety or morality of an unemancipated minor is in danger, or if the conditions of his education are seriously compromised, educational assistance measures may be ordered by the court at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor. The judge may seize the matter on his own motion in exceptional circumstances.  

These educational assistance measures may be ordered at the same time for several children subject to the same parental authority.  

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, or the judge he delegates for this purpose, has jurisdiction, subject to appeal, for everything concerning educational assistance.  

The president or the delegated judge must always endeavor to obtain the family's agreement to the measure envisaged.

###### Article 489

Whenever possible, the minor must be maintained in his current environment. In this case, the judge designates either a qualified person or an association as designated in article 444, giving the designated person or association the mission of providing aid and advice to the family, in order to overcome the material or moral difficulties it encounters. This person or association is responsible for monitoring the child's development and reporting to the judge periodically.  
The president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may also make the child's maintenance in his environment subject to particular obligations, such as that of regularly attending an educational establishment, or of engaging in a professional activity.

###### Article 490

If it is necessary to remove the child from his current environment, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may decide to entrust him:
1° To the one of the father and mother who did not have custody;  
2° To another member of the family or to a trustworthy third party; 3° To an association as designated in article 444.  
However, when a petition for divorce has been filed or a divorce judgment rendered between the father and mother, these measures may be taken only if a new fact likely to cause danger to the minor has been revealed subsequent to the decision ruling on custody of the child. They may not prevent the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge from deciding, by application of article 302, to whom the child must be entrusted. The same rules are applicable to legal separation.

###### Article 491

In the cases specified in 1° and 2° of the preceding article, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may instruct a qualified person, an association as designated in article 444, or an observation, education or re-education service in an open environment, to provide aid and advice to the guardian as well as to the family and to monitor the child's development.  
In all cases, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may accompany the handing over of the child with the same modalities as under article 489, paragraph 2. He may also decide that he will be given periodic reports on the child's situation.

###### Article 492

On a provisional basis but subject to appeal, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may, during the proceedings, take one of the measures provided for in articles 490 and 491.  
In case of urgency, the public prosecutor of the place where the minor was found has the same power, subject to seizing within eight days the president of the Civil Chamber, who will maintain, modify or withdraw the measure.

###### Article 493

Decisions taken in matters of educational assistance may be, at any time, modified or withdrawn by the judge who rendered them either on his own motion, or at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor.  

The father and mother whose child has given rise to an educational assistance measure retain their parental authority over him and exercise all the attributes thereof which are not incompatible with the application of the measure. They may not emancipate the child without authorization from the children's judge, as long as the educational assistance measure is being applied.  
If it has been necessary to place the child outside his parents' home, they retain a right of correspondence and a right of visitation. The judge sets the modalities thereof and may, if the child's interest so requires, decide that the exercise of these rights, or of one of them, will be provisionally suspended.

###### Article 495

The costs of maintenance and education of the child who has been the subject of an educational assistance measure continue to be the responsibility of his father and mother as well as the ascendants from whom maintenance may be claimed, except for the power of the judge to discharge them in whole or in part.

##### Section III: Delegation of Parental Authority Article 496

No renunciation, no transfer relating to parental authority, may have effect, except by virtue of a judgment and in the cases determined below.

###### Article 497

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, when called upon to rule on the custody or education of a minor child, have regard to the agreements that the father and mother may have freely concluded between themselves on this subject, unless one of them justifies serious grounds that would authorize him to revoke his consent.

###### Article 498

The father and mother, together or separately, or the guardian authorized by the family council, may, when they have entrusted the minor child of sixteen years to a trustworthy individual or to an establishment approved for this purpose, or an association as designated in Article 444, renounce in whole or in part the exercise of their authority.  
In this case, delegation, total or partial, of parental authority shall result from the judgment that will be rendered by the Civil Chamber on the joint application of the delegators and the delegatee.  

The same delegation may be decided, on the sole application of the delegatee, when the parents have lost interest in the child for more than one year.

###### Article 499

The delegation of parental authority may also take place when the minor of sixteen years has been taken in without the intervention of the father and mother or the guardian. But it is necessary, in this case, that the individual, establishment or association, after having taken in the child, has made a declaration thereof to the administrative authority of the place.  
This declaration is made within eight days. The administrative authority, within the month that follows, gives notice thereof to the father and mother or to the guardian. The notification thus made to them opens a new period of three months at the expiration of which, failing by them to claim the child, they are presumed to renounce exercising their authority over him.  

The individual, establishment or association that has taken in the child may then present an application to the Civil Chamber for the purpose of having parental authority delegated to it totally or partially.

###### Article 500

The delegation may, in all cases, come to an end or be transferred by a new judgment, if new circumstances are justified.  

In the case where the restitution of the child is granted to the father and mother, the Civil Chamber shall charge them, if they are not indigent, with the reimbursement of all or part of the maintenance costs.  
When the application for restitution has been rejected, it may not be renewed until six months from the day on which the decision of rejection became final.

###### Article 501

The right to consent to the adoption of the minor is never delegated.

##### Section IV

Forfeiture and Partial Withdrawal of Parental Authority Article 502
May be deprived of parental authority by an express provision of the criminal judgment the father and mother who are convicted, either as perpetrators, co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offense committed against the person of their child, or as co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offense committed by their child.  

This forfeiture is applicable to ascendants other than the father and mother for the share of parental authority that may fall to them over their descendants.

###### Article 503

May be deprived of parental authority, outside of any criminal conviction, the father and mother who, either by ill-treatment, or by harmful examples of habitual drunkenness, notorious misconduct or delinquency, or by a lack of care or a lack of direction, manifestly endanger the safety, health or morality of the child.  
May likewise be deprived thereof, when an educational assistance measure had been taken with regard to the child, the father and mother who, for more than two years, have voluntarily abstained from exercising the rights and fulfilling the duties left to them by Article 494.  
The action for forfeiture is brought before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, either by the public prosecutor, or by a member of the family or the guardian of the child.

###### Article 504

The forfeiture pronounced by virtue of one of the two preceding articles applies by operation of law to all attributes, both patrimonial and personal, relating to parental authority; in the absence of other determination, it extends to all minor children already born at the time of the judgment.  
It entails, for the child, exemption from the maintenance obligation, by way of derogation from Articles 212 to 214, except contrary provision in the judgment of forfeiture.

###### Article 505

The judgment may, instead of total forfeiture, limit itself to pronouncing a partial withdrawal of rights, limited to the attributes it specifies. It may also decide that the forfeiture or withdrawal shall have effect only with regard to certain of the children already born.

###### Article 506

In pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal of the right of custody, the court seized must, if the other parent is deceased or if he has lost the exercise of parental authority, either designate a third party who shall provisionally assume the custody of the child subject to his requesting the organization of guardianship, or entrust the child to an association as designated in Article 444.  

The court seized may take the same measures when parental authority is devolved to one of the parents by the effect of the forfeiture pronounced against the other.

###### Article 507

The father and mother who have been the subject of a forfeiture or a withdrawal of rights for one of the causes provided for in Articles 502 and 503, may, by application, obtain from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, by justifying new circumstances, that there be restored to them, in whole or in part, the rights of which they had been deprived.  
The application for restitution may not be made until six months from the day on which the judgment pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal became final; in case of rejection, this application may not be renewed until after a new period of one year. No application shall be admissible when, before the filing of the application, the child has been placed with a view to adoption.  

If restitution is granted, the public prosecutor shall request, where appropriate, educational assistance measures.

#### Chapter II: Parental Authority in Relation to the Property of the Child Article 508

The father and mother have, subject to the distinctions that follow, the administration and enjoyment of the property of their child.

###### Article 509

Legal administration is exercised in accordance with the provisions of Articles 518 and following of this code.

###### Article 510

The right of enjoyment ceases:
1° As soon as the child has completed sixteen years, or even earlier when he contracts marriage;  
2° By the causes that terminate parental authority, or even more specifically by those that terminate legal administration;  
3° By the causes that entail the extinction of any usufruct.

###### Article 511

The charges of this enjoyment are:
1° Those to which usufructuaries are generally bound;  
2° The food, maintenance and education of the child, according to his fortune;  
3° The debts burdening the succession received by the child insofar as they should have been paid from the income.

###### Article 512

This enjoyment shall not take place for the benefit of the surviving spouse who has failed to make an inventory, authentic or under private signature, of the property accruing to the minor.

###### Article 513

Legal enjoyment does not extend to property that the child may acquire through his or her work, nor to property given or bequeathed to him or her on the express condition that the father and mother shall not enjoy it.

### Titre XI : De la minorité, de la tutelle et de l'émancipation

###### Article 514

In this title, whenever reference is made to the judge, it means the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he or she has designated.

Chapitre Ier: De la minorité Article 515
The minor is the individual of either sex who has not yet reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 516

In any proceedings concerning him or her, the minor capable of discernment may, without prejudice to provisions requiring his or her intervention or consent, be heard by the judge or, where his or her interest so requires, by the person designated by the judge for that purpose.
This hearing is a matter of right when the minor so requests. When the minor refuses to be heard, the judge assesses the merits of this refusal. He or she may be heard alone, with a lawyer or a person of his or her choice.

###### Article 517

The legal administrator represents the minor in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes minors to act themselves.

#### Chapitre II : De l'administration légale Article 518

Legal administration belongs to the parents.
If parental authority is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is a legal administrator. In other cases, legal administration belongs to the parent who exercises parental authority.

###### Article 519

When legal administration is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is deemed, with respect to third parties, to have received from the other the power to perform alone acts of administration relating to the minor's property.
The list of acts that are regarded as acts of administration is defined by presidential decree.

###### Article 520

When the interests of the sole legal administrator or, as the case may be, of both legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the latter request the appointment of an ad hoc administrator by the judge. In the absence of diligence by the legal administrators, the judge may proceed with this appointment at the request of the public prosecutor, the minor himself or herself or of his or her own motion.
When the interests of one of the two legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the judge may authorize the other legal administrator to represent the child for one or more specified acts.

###### Article 521

Property given or bequeathed to the minor on condition that it be administered by a third party is not subject to legal administration.

The third-party administrator has the powers conferred upon him or her by the gift, the will or, failing that, those of a legal administrator.

When the third-party administrator refuses this function or is legally unable to exercise it, the judge designates an ad hoc administrator to replace him or her.

###### Article 522

The legal administrator is required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in managing the minor's property, solely in the minor's interest.

###### Article 523

The legal administrator is liable for any damage resulting from any fault he or she commits in managing the minor's property.
If legal administration is exercised jointly, both parents are jointly and severally liable.

The action for liability is barred after five years from the interested party's majority or emancipation.

#### Chapitre III : De la tutelle

##### Section I : Des cas d'ouverture et de fin de la tutelle Article 524

Tutorship opens when both the father and mother are deceased or are deprived of the exercise of parental authority.
It also opens with respect to a child whose filiation is not legally established.

###### Article 525

In the case of legal administration, the judge may, at any time and for serious cause, either of his or her own motion or at the request of relatives or in-laws or the public prosecutor, decide to open tutorship after having heard or summoned, except in urgent cases, the legal administrator. The latter may not perform any act of disposition from the day he or she is informed of the application until the final judgment except in urgent cases.
If tutorship is opened, the judge convenes the family council, which may either appoint the legal administrator as tutor or designate another tutor.

###### Article 526

If a child comes to be recognized by one of his or her two parents after the opening of tutorship, the judge may, at the request of that parent, decide to substitute legal administration for tutorship.

###### Article 527

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 526, tutorship ends upon the emancipation of the minor or upon his or her majority. It also ends in the event of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata or in the event of the death of the interested party.

##### Section II : De l'organisation et du fonctionnement de la tutelle

###### § 1. Des charges tutélaires

###### Article 528

Tutorship, protection owed to the child, is a public duty. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 529

The following may not exercise the various duties of tutorship:
1° Unemancipated minors, except if they are the father or mother of the minor under tutorship
2° Adults who benefit from a legal protection measure provided for by this code; 3° Persons from whom parental authority has been withdrawn;
4° Persons who have been prohibited from exercising tutorship duties by court decision.

###### Article 530

Any tutorship duty may be withdrawn by reason of the unfitness, negligence, misconduct or fraud of the person to whom it has been entrusted. The same applies when a dispute or conflict of interest prevents the holder of the duty from exercising it in the interest of the minor.
Any person to whom a tutorship duty has been entrusted may be replaced in the event of a significant change in his or her situation or in that of the minor.

###### Article 531

The family council rules on impediments, withdrawals and replacements concerning the tutor.
The judge rules on those concerning the other members of the family council.

A tutorship duty may be withdrawn, by the person who entrusted it, only after its holder has been heard or summoned.
The judge may, if he or she considers that there is urgency, prescribe provisional measures in the interest of the minor.

###### § 2. Du conseil de famille Article 532

Even in the presence of a testamentary tutor and except in case of vacancy, tutorship is organized with a family council.

###### Article 533

The judge designates the members of the family council for the duration of the tutorship.

The family council is composed of at least four members, including the tutor. The judge is not included in this number.
Relatives and in-laws of the minor's father and mother as well as any person, residing in Djibouti or abroad, who shows an interest in him or her may be members of the family council.

The members of the family council are chosen in consideration of the interest of the minor and according to their aptitude, the habitual relations they maintained with his or her father or mother, the emotional ties they have with him or her as well as their availability.

The judge must avoid, as far as possible, leaving either of the two branches, paternal or maternal, without representation.

###### Article 534

The family council is chaired by the judge. Its deliberations are adopted by vote of its members.

However, the tutor does not vote.

In the event of a tie, the judge's vote is decisive.

###### Article 535

The family council shall determine the general conditions for the maintenance and education of the minor, having regard to the wishes that the father and mother may have expressed.  
It shall assess the allowances that may be granted to the tutor.  

It shall make decisions and give the tutor the necessary authorisations for the management of the minor's property in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII of this Code.

###### Article 536

The deliberations of the family council are null and void when they have been obtained by deceit or fraud or when substantial formalities have been omitted.  
The action for nullity may be brought by the tutor, the other members of the family council and the Public Prosecutor within two years of the deliberation, and by the minor who has reached majority or been emancipated within two years of his majority or emancipation. The limitation period does not run if there has been deceit or fraud as long as the fact which is the origin thereof has not been discovered.  

Acts performed pursuant to an annulled deliberation shall be annulled upon simple request by any of the persons entitled to act under the preceding paragraph. However, the period runs from the act and not from the deliberation.

###### § 3. Of the tutor Article 537

The individual right to choose a tutor, whether or not related to the minor, belongs only to the last surviving of the father and mother if he or she has retained, on the day of his or her death, the exercise of parental authority.  
This designation may only be made in the form of a will or a special declaration before a notary.  
It is binding on the family council unless the interest of the minor requires that it be set aside. In that case, the family council shall decide to refer the matter to the judge, who shall assess it.  

The tutor designated by the father or mother is not obliged to accept the tutorship.

###### Article 538

If there is no testamentary tutor, or if the person designated in that capacity ceases his functions or refuses the tutorship, the family council shall designate a tutor for the minor.

###### Article 539

The family council may, in consideration of the situation of the minor, the aptitudes of the interested parties and the composition of the estate to be administered, designate several tutors to exercise the protective measure jointly. Each tutor is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a tutor would not need any authorisation.  
The family council may decide that the exercise of the tutorship shall be divided between a tutor responsible for the person of the minor and a tutor responsible for the management of his property. Unless otherwise decided by the family council, these tutors are independent of each other, and are not responsible to each other. However, they shall inform each other of the decisions they make

###### Article 540

The tutor is designated for the duration of the tutorship.

###### Article 541

Tutorship is a personal charge.  

It is not transmitted to the heirs of the tutor.

###### Article 542

The tutor shall take care of the person of the minor and represent him in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorises the minor to act himself.  
The tutor shall represent the minor in legal proceedings. However, he may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert non-patrimonial rights except after authorisation or upon injunction of the family council. The family council may also enjoin the tutor to withdraw from the proceedings or action, or to settle.  

The tutor shall manage the property of the minor and account for his management in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### § 4. Of the vacancy of the tutorship Article 543

The President of the Court of First Instance and the Public Prosecutor shall exercise general supervision over the tutorships within their jurisdiction.  

Tutors and other tutelary bodies are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.  
The judge may issue injunctions against them and impose a civil fine of 50,000 to 200,000 FD on those who have not complied.

###### § 5. Of liability Article 544

All bodies of the tutorship are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.  

Where the fault causing the damage was committed in the organisation and operation of the tutorship by the judges or the clerk, the action for liability is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 545

The action for liability is barred after five years from the majority of the interested party, even if the management continued beyond that time, or from the end of the measure if it ceases earlier.

#### Chapter IV: Of emancipation Article 546

The minor is emancipated by operation of law by marriage.

###### Article 547

The minor, even if not married, may be emancipated when he has reached the age of sixteen years.  

After hearing the minor, this emancipation shall be pronounced, if there are just grounds, by the judge, at the request of the father and mother or one of them.  
When the request is made by only one of the parents, the judge shall decide after hearing the other parent unless the latter is unable to express his will.

###### Article 548

The minor left without father or mother may be emancipated at the request of the family council, convened by the tutor or by the court at the request of a member of the family council or of the minor himself. Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 547 are then applicable.

###### Article 549

The account of the administration, if any, or of the tutorship shall be rendered to the emancipated minor in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### Article 550

The emancipated minor is capable, like an adult, of all acts of civil life.  

He must nevertheless, in order to marry or give himself in adoption, observe the same rules as if he were not emancipated.

###### Article 551

The emancipated minor ceases to be under the authority of his father and mother.  
They are not liable by operation of law, in their sole capacity as father or mother, for damage he may cause to others after his emancipation.

###### Article 552

The emancipated minor may not be a merchant.

### Title XII: Of majority and adults protected by law

Chapter I: General provisions Article 553
Majority is fixed at eighteen years completed; at that age, everyone is capable of exercising the rights of which he has enjoyment.

##### Section I: Of provisions independent of protective measures Article 554

To make a valid act, one must be of sound mind. It is for those who bring an action for nullity on this ground to prove the existence of a mental disorder at the time of the act.

###### Article 555

During his lifetime, the action for nullity belongs only to the interested party.  

After his death, acts done by him, other than inter vivos donations and wills, may be challenged by his heirs, for unsoundness of mind, only in the following cases:

1° If the act bears in itself proof of a mental disorder;  
2° If it was made while the interested party was placed under safeguard of justice;  
3° If an action was brought before his death for the purpose of opening a curatorship or tutorship or for the purpose of family habilitation.  
The action for nullity is available within a period of five years, to the interested party from the cessation of his condition and, after his death, to the heirs, from the day of death.

###### Article 556

A person who has caused damage to another while under the influence of a mental disorder is nonetheless obliged to make reparation.

##### Section II: Provisions common to protected adults Article 557

Adults receive protection of their person and their property that their condition or situation makes necessary according to the procedures provided for in this title.  
This protection is established and ensured in respect of individual freedoms, fundamental rights and the dignity of the person.  
Its purpose is the interest of the protected person. It promotes, as far as possible, the autonomy of that person. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 558

The President of the Court of First Instance and the Public Prosecutor exercise general supervision of protection measures within their jurisdiction. They may visit or have visited the protected persons and those who are the subject of an application for protection, whatever the measure pronounced or sought.  
The persons responsible for the protection are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.

###### Article 559

The President of the Court of First Instance may issue injunctions against persons responsible for the protection and impose a civil fine of 10,000 FD to 100,000 FD on those who have not complied.  
He may also remove them from their mission in case of a characterized failure in the exercise thereof, after having heard them or summoned them.

###### Article 560

Without prejudice to the application of the rules of management of affairs, the death of the protected person terminates the mission of the person responsible for the protection.

###### Article 561

Persons exercise judicial protection measures free of charge.  
However, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may authorize, according to the importance of the property managed or the difficulty of exercising the measure, the payment of an allowance to the person responsible for the protection. He shall fix the amount thereof. This allowance is borne by the protected person.

###### Article 562

All organs of the judicial protection measure are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.  

However, when the person designated as organ of judicial protection exercises his mission free of charge, he incurs liability, for acts accomplished with his assistance, only in case of fraud or gross negligence.

###### Article 563

When the fault causing the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the protection measure by the judge or the clerk, the action for liability brought by the protected person or person who has been protected or by his heirs is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 564

The action for liability is barred after five years from the end of the protection measure even though the management may have continued beyond.  
However, when the curatorship has ceased by the opening of a guardianship measure, the period runs only from the expiration of the latter.

#### Chapter II

Judicial protection measures for adults Section I: General provisions

###### Article 565

Any person unable to provide for his interests alone by reason of an impairment, medically established, either of his mental faculties or of his bodily faculties such as to prevent the expression of his will, may benefit from a judicial protection measure provided for in this chapter.  
Unless otherwise provided, the measure is intended for the protection of both the person and the property interests thereof. It may however be expressly limited to one of these two missions.

###### Article 566

The dwelling of the protected person and the furniture with which it is furnished, whether it is a principal or secondary residence, are kept at the disposal of that person as long as possible.  
The power to administer the property mentioned in the first paragraph permits only precarious enjoyment agreements which cease, notwithstanding any provisions or stipulations to the contrary, upon the return of the protected person to his dwelling.  

If it becomes necessary or if it is in the interest of the protected person that the rights relating to his dwelling or his furniture be disposed of by alienation, termination or conclusion of a lease, the act is authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, by the President of the Court of First Instance, without prejudice to the formalities that the nature of the property may require. If the act has the purpose of accommodating the interested party in an establishment, the prior opinion of a physician, not exercising a function or occupying a position in that establishment, is required. In all cases, souvenirs, objects of a personal nature, those indispensable to disabled persons or intended for the care of sick persons are kept at the disposal of the interested party, where appropriate by the care of the establishment in which he is accommodated.

###### Article 567

The person responsible for the protection measure may not proceed either with the modification of accounts or passbooks opened in the name of the protected person, or with the opening of another account or passbook with a bank or any other organization that may legally receive funds from the public. The family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may however authorize it if the interest of the protected person so requires.  

A special account is opened in the name of the protected person with a local bank by the person responsible for the protection if the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance deems it necessary.  
When the protected person holds no account or passbook, the person responsible for the protection measure opens one for him.  

Banking operations of collection, payment and asset management carried out in the name and on behalf of the protected person are carried out exclusively by means of accounts opened in the name of that person; the fruits, products and capital gains generated by the funds and securities belonging to the protected person accrue exclusively to him.  
If the protected person has been subject to a prohibition on issuing checks, the person responsible for the protection measure may nevertheless, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, operate under his signature the accounts of which the protected person is the holder and have all the usual means of payment.

##### Section II: Provisions common to judicial measures Article 568

The protection measure may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application either of the rules of common law of representation, or of those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protection measure.  

The measure is proportionate and individualized according to the degree of impairment of the personal faculties of the interested party.

###### Article 569

The judicial protection measure may be opened for an emancipated minor as for an adult.  

For an unemancipated minor, the application may be filed and judged in the last year of his minority. The judicial protection measure takes effect, however, only from the day of his majority.

###### Article 570

The application to open the measure may be submitted to the judge by the person who needs to be protected or, as the case may be, by his or her spouse, or by a relative or in-law, a person maintaining close and stable ties with the adult, or the person exercising legal protection over him or her.  
It may also be submitted by the Public Prosecutor either on his own initiative or at the request of a third party.

###### Article 571

The application must be accompanied, on pain of inadmissibility, by a detailed certificate drawn up by a doctor chosen from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This doctor may seek the opinion of the treating physician of the person who needs to be protected.

###### Article 572

The judge rules after the person has been heard or summoned. The person concerned may be accompanied by a lawyer or, subject to the judge's agreement, by any other person of his or her choice.  
However, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with the hearing of the person concerned if such hearing is likely to harm his or her health or if he or she is unable to express his or her will.

##### Section III : De la sauvegarde de justice Article 573

The judge may place under safeguard of justice the person who, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, needs temporary legal protection or to be represented for the performance of certain specified acts.  

This measure may also be ordered by the judge, seized of curatorship or guardianship proceedings, for the duration of the proceedings.

###### Article 574

The person placed under safeguard of justice retains the exercise of his or her rights. However, he or she may not, on pain of nullity, perform an act for which a special agent has been appointed pursuant to Article 576.  
The acts he or she has performed and the commitments he or she has entered into during the duration of the measure may be annulled for simple lesion or reduced in case of excess. The courts take into account in particular the usefulness or uselessness of the transaction, the size or composition of the protected person's estate and the good or bad faith of those with whom he or she has contracted.  

The action for nullity or reduction belongs only to the protected person and, after his or her death, to his or her heirs. It is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him or her to exercise it.

###### Article 575

The mandate by which the protected person has entrusted another person with the administration of his or her property continues to produce its effects during the safeguard of justice unless it is revoked or suspended by the President of the Court of First Instance; the agent being heard or summoned.  
In the absence of a mandate, the rules of management of affairs are applicable.  

Those who have standing to apply for the opening of a curatorship or guardianship are required to perform the conservatory acts essential to the preservation of the protected person's estate as soon as they become aware both of their urgency and of the opening of the safeguard measure. The same provisions apply to the person or establishment that accommodates the person placed under safeguard.

###### Article 576

If there is a need to act outside the cases defined in Article 570, any interested party may give notice thereof to the judge.  

The judge may appoint a special agent for the purpose of performing one or more specified acts, even acts of disposition, made necessary by the management of the protected person's estate.  
The special agent is required to account for the performance of his or her mandate to the protected person and to the judge under the conditions provided for in Articles 639 to 644.

###### Article 577

The special agent may also be entrusted with a mission to protect the person in accordance with Articles 595 to 600.

###### Article 578

On pain of lapse, the safeguard of justice measure may not exceed one year, renewable once under the conditions set out in the fourth paragraph of Article 581.  
The judge may, at any time, order its lifting if the need for temporary protection ceases.  

In the absence of lifting, the safeguard of justice ends upon expiration of the period or after the performance of the acts for which it was ordered. It also ends with the opening of a curatorship or guardianship measure from the day on which the new legal protection measure takes effect.

##### Section IV : De la curatelle et de la tutelle Article 579

The person who, without being unable to act himself or herself, needs, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, to be assisted or supervised continuously in important acts of civil life may be placed under curatorship.  
Curatorship is ordered only if it is established that safeguard of justice cannot provide sufficient protection.  

The person who, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, must be represented continuously in acts of civil life, may be placed under guardianship.  
Guardianship is ordered only if it is established that neither safeguard of justice nor curatorship can provide sufficient protection.

###### Sous-section 1 : De la durée de la mesure Article 580

The President of the Court of First Instance sets the duration of the measure, which may not exceed five years.  

The judge who orders a guardianship measure may, by specially reasoned decision and on the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list of judicial experts in accordance with Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure finding that the impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not appear manifestly likely to improve according to established scientific knowledge, set a longer duration, not exceeding ten years.

###### Article 581

The judge may renew the measure for the same duration.  

However, when the impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not appear manifestly likely to improve according to established scientific knowledge, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, renew the measure for a longer duration that he or she determines, not exceeding twenty years.  
The judge may, at any time, terminate the measure, modify it or substitute another measure provided for in this title, after obtaining the opinion of the person responsible for the protection measure.  
He or she rules on his or her own initiative or at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 570, on the basis of a medical certificate and under the conditions provided for in Article 572. However, he or she may only strengthen the protection regime of the person concerned if he or she is seized of a request to that effect satisfying Articles 570 and 571.

###### Article 582

The measure ends, in the absence of renewal, upon expiration of the set period, in case of a judgment of lifting that has become res judicata or in case of death of the person concerned.  
The judge may also terminate it when the protected person resides outside the national territory, if such absence prevents the monitoring and supervision of the measure.

###### Sous-section 2 : De la publicité de la mesure Article 583

Judgments ordering the opening, modification or lifting of curatorship or guardianship are enforceable against third parties only two months after the mention thereof has been entered in the margin of the birth certificate of the protected person according to the procedures provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure.  

However, even in the absence of this mention, they are enforceable against third parties who have personal knowledge thereof.

###### Sous-section 3 : Des organes de protection Article 584

Curatelary and tutelary duties are subject to the conditions provided for tutelary duties of minors by articles 529 to 531. However, the powers conferred by article 531 on the family council are exercised by the judge in the absence of constitution of that body.

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries, may not exercise a curatelary or tutelary duty with regard to their patients.  
The fiduciary designated by the fiduciary contract may not exercise a curatelary or tutelary duty with regard to the settlor.

###### § 1. Du curateur et du tuteur Article 585

A curator or a tutor is designated for the protected person under the conditions provided for in this paragraph and subject to the powers conferred on the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 586

The curator or the tutor is designated by the judge.

The judge may, in consideration of the situation of the protected person, the aptitudes of the interested parties and the consistency of the patrimony to be administered, designate several curators or several tutors to exercise jointly the protection measure. Each curator or tutor is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a tutor would not need any authorization.  
The judge may divide the protection measure between a curator or a tutor responsible for the protection of the person and a curator or a tutor responsible for patrimonial management.  
Unless the judge has decided otherwise, the persons designated in application of the preceding paragraph are independent of one another, and are not responsible to one another. They inform each other, however, of the decisions they make.

###### Article 587

The designation by a person of one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or tutor in the event that he or she is placed under curatorship or tutorship is binding on the judge, unless the designated person refuses the mission or is unable to exercise it, or unless the interest of the protected person requires that he or she be excluded. In case of difficulty, the judge decides.  
The same applies when the parents or the last surviving of the father and mother, not subject to a measure of curatorship or tutorship, who exercise parental authority over their minor child or assume the material and emotional care of their adult child designate one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or tutor from the day when they themselves die or can no longer continue to take care of the interested party.

###### Article 588

In the absence of designation made in application of article 587, the judge appoints, as curator or tutor, the spouse of the protected person, unless common life has ceased between them or another cause prevents entrusting him or her with the measure.  
In the absence of appointment made in application of the preceding paragraph and subject to the last reservation mentioned therein, the judge designates a relative, a person related by marriage or a person residing with the protected adult or maintaining close and stable ties with him or her.

The judge takes into consideration the feelings expressed by the latter, his or her usual relationships, the interest shown in him or her and any recommendations of his or her relatives and persons related by marriage as well as of his or her entourage.

###### Article 589

When no family member or close person can assume the curatorship or tutorship, the judge designates a judicial representative for the protection of adults. This representative may not refuse to perform urgent acts required by the interest of the protected person, in particular indispensable conservatory acts for the preservation of his or her patrimony.

###### Article 590

If the interest of the person accommodated or cared for in a health establishment justifies it, the judge may designate, as curator or tutor, a person or a service agent of the establishment registered on the list of judicial representatives for the protection of adults.  
The mission entrusted to the representative extends to the protection of the person, unless otherwise decided by the judge.

###### Article 591

No one is required to retain the curatorship or tutorship of a person beyond five years, with the exception of the spouse, the children of the interested party and judicial representatives for the protection of adults.

###### § 2. Du curateur ad hoc et du tuteur ad hoc

###### Article 592

The curator or the tutor whose interests are, on the occasion of an act or a series of acts, in opposition to those of the protected person or who cannot provide him or her with assistance or act on his or her behalf due to the limitations of his or her mission, has appointed by the judge or by the family council if it has been constituted a curator or a tutor ad hoc, that is to say a curator or a tutor for the act or series of acts concerned.  
This appointment may also be made at the request of the Public Prosecutor, any interested party or ex officio.

###### § 3. Du conseil de famille des majeurs en tutelle Article 593

The judge may organize the tutorship with a family council if the necessities of the protection of the person or the consistency of his or her patrimony justify it and if the composition of his or her family and entourage permits it.  
The judge designates the members of the family council in consideration of the feelings expressed by the protected person, his or her usual relationships, the interest shown in him or her and any recommendations of his or her relatives and persons related by marriage as well as of his or her entourage.

The family council designates the tutor, and, where applicable, the tutor ad hoc in accordance with articles 584 to 591.  
The rules prescribed for the family council of minors apply, with the exception of those provided for in article 532, in the fourth paragraph of article 533 and in the first paragraph of article 535. For the application of the third paragraph of article 536, the time limit runs, when the action is brought by the protected adult, from the day when the protection measure ends.

###### Article 594

The judge may authorize the family council to meet and deliberate outside his or her presence, when the latter has designated a judicial representative for the protection of adults as tutor. The family council then designates a president and a secretary from among its members, excluding the tutor.  
The president of the family council transmits to the judge in advance the agenda of each meeting.

The decisions made by the family council take effect only in the absence of opposition filed by the judge, under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.  
The president exercises the missions conferred on the judge for the convening, meeting and deliberation of the family council. The judge may, however, at any time, convene a meeting of the family council under his or her presidency.

###### Sous-section 4

Des effets de la curatelle et de la tutelle quant à la protection de la personne Article 595
The protected person receives from the person responsible for his or her protection, according to methods adapted to his or her condition and without prejudice to the information that third parties are required to provide to him or her by virtue of the law, all

information on his or her personal situation, on the acts that the person responsible for his or her protection wishes to carry out, their usefulness, their degree of urgency, their effects and the consequences of a refusal on his or her part.


This excerpt sits under: RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI > LIVRE I : DES PERSONNES > Titre XII : De la majorité et des majeurs protégés par la loi > Chapitre II > Section IV : De la curatelle et de la tutelle Article 579

###### Article 596

Subject to the specific provisions provided by law, the performance of acts whose nature implies strictly personal consent may never give rise to assistance or representation of the protected person.

The following are deemed strictly personal: the declaration of birth of a child, recognition thereof, acts of parental authority relating to the person of a child, the declaration of choice or change of a child's name and consent given to one's own adoption or to that of one's child.

###### Article 597

Except in the cases provided for in Article 596, the protected person alone makes decisions relating to his or her person to the extent that his or her condition permits.
