When spouses are subject to the dotal regime, the husband may give immovable dotal property on emphyteutic lease with the consent of the wife and judicial authorization.  

Concerning premises for residential use, lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with tenants continue automatically with the owner of the building until the end of each of the lease contracts as signed with the tenants.

###### Article 756

Proof of the emphyteusis contract is established in accordance with the rules of this code regarding leases.

###### Article 757

In the absence of contrary agreements, it is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 758

The lessee may not request reduction of the rent on grounds of partial loss of the land, nor on grounds of sterility or deprivation of any harvest following fortuitous events.

###### Article 759

In the absence of payment for two consecutive years, the lessor is authorized, after a summons that has remained without effect, to have the resolution of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.  
Resolution may also be requested by the lessor in case of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deteriorations on the land.  
Nevertheless, the courts may grant a delay according to the circumstances.

###### Article 760

The lessee may not free himself from the rent, nor evade the performance of the conditions of the emphyteutic lease by abandoning the land.

###### Article 761

The lessee may not make any change in the land that diminishes its value.  

If the lessee has made improvements or constructions that increase the value of the land, he may not destroy them, nor claim any compensation in this regard.

###### Article 762

The lessee is liable for all contributions and charges on the property.  

With regard to constructions existing at the time of the lease and those that will have been erected in performance of the agreement, he is liable for repairs of all kinds; but he is not obliged to rebuild buildings, if he proves that they were destroyed by fortuitous event, by force majeure, or that they perished by defect of construction prior to the lease.  

He is liable for fire, in accordance with Article 1394, paragraphs 2 and 3, of this code.

###### Article 763

The emphyteuta may acquire active easements for the benefit of the land, and encumber it, by title, with passive easements for a time that will not exceed the duration of the lease and subject to notifying the owner.

###### Article 764

The emphyteuta benefits from the right of accession during the duration of the emphyteusis.

###### Article 765

In case of expropriation for public utility, the lessor must make known the right of the emphyteuta, in accordance with the legal provisions in force. Separate compensations are granted to the lessor and to the lessee.

###### Article 766

The lessee alone has the hunting and fishing rights and exercises with regard to mines, mineral deposits, quarries and peat bogs all the rights of the usufructuary.

###### Article 767

The constitutive instrument of emphyteusis is subject only to the registration and transcription fees established for rental leases of limited duration.  
Transfers of all kinds having as their object either the right of the lessor or the right of the lessee are subject to the legal provisions concerning transfers of ownership of immovable property. The fee is assessed on the market value determined by an estimated declaration of the parties.

#### Chapter V: Of the Right of Superficies Article 768

A land may be the object of a division aimed at conferring on a third party ownership of a part of this land situated above or below a conventionally fixed limit. The ownership of the top is called superficiary ownership or right of superficies, that of the bottom subsoil ownership.  

Thus, the right of superficies consists, for the holder of this right, in the fact of possessing constructions, works or plantations on land belonging to another. For the holder of the ownership right on the soil, the right of superficies is a renunciation of accession.  

The holder of the right of superficies may encumber with easements the properties that are the object of his right, but only within the limit imposed for the exercise of this right.

###### Article 769

A land may also be the object of a spatial division creating volumes. To each volume corresponds a full right of ownership.  
A descriptive statement of division must obligatorily be executed by notarial deed.

### Title IV: Servitudes or Land Services

###### Article 770

A servitude is a charge that encumbers a property for the use and benefit of a property belonging to another owner.  
It establishes neither preeminence of one property over the other nor personal obligations for the benefit or charge of the owners, but only relationships between the servient property and the dominant property and the services attached to them.  

It derives either from the natural situation of the places, or from obligations imposed by law, or from agreements between the owners.  
Chapter I: Servitudes Arising from the Situation of Places Article 771
Lower properties are subject towards those that are higher to receive waters that flow naturally from them without the hand of man having contributed thereto.  

The lower owner may not raise a dike that prevents this flow.  

The upper owner may not do anything that aggravates the servitude of the lower property.

###### Article 772

Every owner has the right to use and dispose of rainwater that falls on his property.  

If the use of this water or the direction given to it aggravates the natural servitude of flow established by Article 771, compensation is owed to the owner of the lower property.  
The same provision applies to spring waters arising on a property.  

When, through borings or underground works, an owner causes waters to spring up in his property, the owners of lower properties must receive them; but they are entitled to compensation in case of damage resulting from their flow.  

Houses, courtyards, gardens, parks and enclosures adjoining dwellings may not be subjected to any aggravation of the servitude of flow in the cases provided for by the preceding paragraphs.  
Disputes to which the establishment and exercise of the servitudes provided for by these paragraphs may give rise and the settlement, if applicable, of compensation owed to the owners of lower properties are brought, in first instance, before the judge of the district court of the canton who, in ruling, must reconcile the interests of agriculture and industry with the respect owed to property.  

If an expert assessment is necessary, only one expert may be appointed.

###### Article 773

He who has a spring in his property may always use the waters at his will within the limits and for the needs of his property.  
The owner of a spring may no longer use it to the prejudice of the owners of lower properties who, for more than thirty years, have made and completed, on the property where the spring rises, apparent and permanent works intended to use the waters or to facilitate their passage into their property.  
Nor may he use it in such a way as to deprive the inhabitants of a commune, village or hamlet of the water necessary to them; but if the inhabitants have not acquired or prescribed the use thereof, the owner may claim compensation, which is determined by experts.  

If, from the exit of the property where they spring up, the spring waters form a watercourse offering the character of public and running waters, the owner may not divert them from their natural course to the prejudice of lower users.

###### Article 774

Every owner may compel his neighbor to mark the boundaries of their contiguous properties.  

Boundary marking is the operation that allows the recognition and fixing, in a contradictory and definitive manner, of the separating limits of private properties belonging or intended to belong to different owners.  
Boundary marking is carried out by common agreement of the parties and, failing that, by a decision of the judge seized by one of them or, within the framework of the property registration procedure, by the sworn surveyor of the Cadastre section who has been designated by the Registrar to proceed with the boundary marking of the property to be registered.  

Boundary marking is done at common expense.

###### Article 775

The action for boundary marking is perpetual

###### Article 776

Every owner may enclose his property, subject to the exception relating to the right of passage set forth in Articles 794 and following.

#### Chapter II: Servitudes Established by Law Article 777

Servitudes established by law are governed by the rules that institute them.

##### Section I: Party Walls Article 778

A party wall is a right of undivided ownership over a wall, a fence or a ditch.

###### Article 779

A wall, a fence or a ditch may only be constructed straddling the separating line of two contiguous properties by common agreement of the owners of said properties.  
The one of the two who has not consented to this construction may not, in the urbanized zones of the country, require the demolition of the wall. He acquires by operation of law and free of charge the party wall status thereof.

###### Article 780

Existing walls, fences or ditches, constructed at the separating boundary or on the line separating two properties, are presumed to be party walls, unless there is a title or contrary factual element.

###### Article 781

Unless there is a title to the contrary: a wall is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the property towards which its top is inclined in whole or on the side of which there are architectural elements attesting to the initial will of the builders of the wall; a ditch is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the property on the side of which the earth spoil is located; a fence is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the enclosed property if only one of the properties is enclosed.

###### Article 782

The expenses of repair and reconstruction of a party wall, fence or ditch are divided between the owners in proportion to the rights of each, unless the expenses were made necessary by the act of one of them. The latter must then bear the entire charge.  
However, any owner of a party wall, fence or ditch may avoid these expenses by abandoning his right of party wall status, unless the wall supports a building belonging to him or the ditch serves for the drainage of waters from his property.

###### Article 783

Each of the owners may support his construction on the party wall.

###### Article 784

Any co-owner may raise the party wall; but he must pay alone the expense related both to the raising and to future maintenance repairs above the current height of the common fence.  

If the party wall is not in a condition to support the raising, the one who nevertheless intends to raise it must have the wall entirely rebuilt at his expense, and any excess thickness that may be necessary must be taken from his side.  
The neighbor who has not contributed to the raising may acquire the party wall status thereof by paying half of the expense it cost and the value of half of the land provided for the excess thickness, if there is any.
The expense that the raising cost is estimated at the date of acquisition, taking into account the condition in which the raised part of the wall is found.

###### Article 785

Any owner adjoining a wall has the option of making it a party wall in whole or in part, by reimbursing to the master of the wall half of the current value of the wall and half of the value of the land supporting the wall or the part of the wall.  

This option does not apply to other modes of enclosure nor to ditches.

###### Article 786

No owner may carry out works affecting or potentially affecting the structure of the party wall, fence or ditch without the consent of the other or, failing that, the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 787

The fruits and products of a party wall hedge belong to the owners in equal shares.

The co-owner of a party wall hedge may destroy it up to the boundary of his property, provided he builds a wall on that boundary. The same rule applies to the co-owner of a party wall ditch that serves only as an enclosure.

Trees located in the party wall hedge are party wall property like the hedge. Each owner may require the uprooting or pruning of a party wall tree as soon as it is isolated and does not form part of the enclosure.

##### Section II: Distances to be observed between neighbouring properties Article 788

A person who builds on his property is obliged to observe the distance prescribed by particular regulations and customs according to the works in question.

###### Article 789

Similarly, the planting of vegetation is governed by administrative regulations or by constant and recognized customs. In the absence thereof and subject to particular provisions on urban planning, it is only permitted to have trees, shrubs and bushes near the boundary of the neighbouring property at a distance of two metres from the dividing line between the two properties for plantations whose height exceeds two metres, and at a distance of half a metre for other plantations.

###### Article 790

The neighbour may require that trees, shrubs and bushes planted at a lesser distance or whose branches extend over his property be uprooted or reduced to the legal height or distance. He may also cut himself what overhangs his property, provided that this does not cause the vegetation in question to perish, failing which he shall be liable.
If it is the roots, brambles or twigs that extend over his property, he has the right to cut them himself at the boundary of the dividing line. This right is imprescriptible.

The fruits that fall naturally from these branches belong to him.

###### Article 791

Openings or arrangements that allow a view towards the neighbour's property, such as a window, a balcony or a platform, are jours.
Openings or arrangements that allow air or light to pass through, but do not allow a view towards the neighbour's property, such as a translucent brick, are vues.
Jours and vues constitute external arrangements within the meaning of the provisions relating to easements. Consequently: no opening, neither jour nor vue, is authorized when the wall is party wall property, unless all the owners agree; only jours are authorized when the wall is private property and it is established at the dividing boundary of the neighbouring property; when the wall built by the owner of a property at a distance from the dividing line between the properties, any direct view must be 1.90 metres from that boundary; and any oblique view must be 0.60 metres from that same boundary. This distance is calculated from the centre of the opening to the dividing boundary of the properties.

###### Article 792

The distance rules provided for in the preceding article do not apply to openings that give onto a space forming part of the public domain, nor when particular provisions on urban planning provide for other rules.
They do not apply either when the proposed opening gives onto a property subject to an easement preventing construction, such as a right of way easement, established in favour of the person who wishes to open the view, provided that the distance between the proposed opening and the boundary of exercise of the easement in the neighbouring property is located at least three metres away.

##### Section III: Roof drainage Article 793

Every owner must construct his roofs in such a way that rainwater flows onto his property or onto the public highway; he may not cause it to flow onto his neighbour's property.

##### Section IV: Right of way Article 794

The owner whose properties are landlocked may claim a sufficient right of way over the properties of his neighbours, subject to compensation proportionate to the damage he may cause, unless the state of being landlocked was voluntarily created.
A property is landlocked if it has no access to the public highway, or only insufficient access, to allow its normal use or agricultural, industrial or commercial exploitation.

###### Article 795

The right of way must normally be taken from the side where the route is shortest from the landlocked property to the public highway, unless another route is less damaging in which case that route must be preferred.

###### Article 796

If the landlocked state results from the division of a property following a sale, an exchange, a partition or any other contract, the right of way may only be claimed over the land that was the subject of those acts.

However, in the case where a sufficient right of way could not be established over the divided properties, Article 794 would be applicable.

###### Article 797

The action for compensation, in the case provided for in Article 794, is subject to prescription, and the right of way may be continued, even though the action for compensation is no longer admissible.
The maintenance of the right of way is the responsibility of the owner of the dominant property, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 798

In the event of cessation of the landlocked state and regardless of the manner in which the location and mode of the easement were determined, the owner of the servient property may, at any time, invoke the extinction of the easement.
In the absence of an amicable agreement, this disappearance is established by a court decision.

#### Chapter III: Easements established by human act

##### Section I

Various types of easements that may be established on property Article 799
Easements are either continuous or discontinuous.

Continuous easements are those whose use is or may be continual without requiring the actual act of man: such are water conduits, drains, views and others of this kind.
Discontinuous easements are those that require the actual act of man to be exercised: such are rights of way, drawing water, grazing and other similar rights.

###### Article 800

Easements are apparent or non-apparent.

Apparent easements are those that are announced by external works, such as a door, a window, an aqueduct.
Non-apparent easements are those that have no external sign of their existence, such as, for example, the prohibition to build on a property, or to build only to a specified height.

##### Section II: How easements are established Article 801

Easements that do not result from the configuration of the land or that are imposed by law can only be acquired by title.
By way of exception, continuous and apparent easements may be established by destination of the father of the family:

There is destination of the father of the family when, in the absence of a stipulation to the contrary in the deed of division, it is proved that the two properties currently divided belonged to the same owner, and that the external works or arrangements from which the easement results were carried out by him before the division of the property and maintained since.

###### Article 802

If the owner of two properties between which there exists an apparent sign of an easement disposes of one of the properties without the contract containing any agreement relating to the easement, it continues to exist actively or passively in favour of the alienated property or on the alienated property.

###### Article 803

When an easement is established, one is deemed to grant everything necessary to use it.

Thus the easement to draw water from another's fountain necessarily carries with it the right of way.

##### Section III

Rights of the owner of the property to which the easement is owed Article 804
The person to whom an easement is owed has the right to carry out all works necessary to use it and to preserve it.

###### Article 805

These works are at his expense, and not at the expense of the owner of the servient land, unless the title establishing the servitude provides otherwise.

###### Article 806

Even in the case where the owner of the servient land is charged by the title to carry out at his expense the works necessary for the use or preservation of the servitude, he may always free himself from the charge by abandoning the servient land to the owner of the land to which the servitude is owed.

###### Article 807

If the land for which the servitude was established comes to be divided, the servitude remains owed for each portion, without however the condition of the servient land being aggravated.  
Thus, for example, if it concerns a right of way, all the co-owners shall be obliged to exercise it by the same place.

###### Article 808

The owner of the land subject to the servitude may do nothing that tends to diminish its use, or to render it more inconvenient.  
Thus, he may not change the state of the premises, nor transfer the exercise of the servitude to a place different from that where it was originally assigned.  

But however, if this original assignment had become more onerous to the owner of the servient land, or if it prevented him from making advantageous repairs thereto, he could offer to the owner of the other land a place equally convenient for the exercise of his rights, and the latter could not refuse it.

###### Article 809

On his side, he who has a right of servitude may only use it according to his title, without being able to make, either in the land which owes the servitude, or in the land to which it is owed, any change which aggravates the condition of the former.

##### Section IV : Comment les servitudes s'éteignent Article 810

Servitudes cease when things are in such a state that they can no longer be used.  

They revive if things are restored in such a manner that they can be used.

###### Article 811

Every servitude is extinguished when the land to which it is owed, and that which owes it, are united in the same hand.

###### Article 812

The servitude is extinguished by non-use for thirty years, unless it is registered in the Land Register.  

The period begins to run from the day on which the holder of the dominant land ceased to enjoy it, in the case of discontinuous servitudes, and from the day on which an act contrary to the servitude was done, in the case of continuous servitudes.

###### Article 813

If the land in favour of which the servitude is established belongs to several persons in indivision, the enjoyment by one prevents extinctive prescription with regard to all.  
If, among the co-owners, there is one against whom prescription could not run, such as a minor, he shall have preserved the right of all the others.

## LIVRE III. DES DIFFERENTES MANIERES DONT ON ACQUIERT LA PROPRIETE

Dispositions générales

###### Article 814

Ownership of property is acquired and transferred by succession, by inter vivos or testamentary donation, by the effect of obligations, by accession or incorporation, by occupation, by delivery, by prescription, or any other mode of acquisition provided by law.  

Titre Ier: Des successions
Chapitre Ier: De l'ouverture des successions et de la saisine des héritiers Article 815
Successions open, upon death, at the last domicile of the deceased.  

They are devolved, when the deceased has not disposed of his property by liberalities or will, according to the present provisions of the civil code whenever the spouses have opted for the regime of the civil code at the time of their marriage or an unmarried person has expressed his or her wish to that effect to the civil registrar. Liberalities and wills are authorized to the extent compatible with the reserved portion.  

The provisions of this title apply to the succession of a person subject to bankruptcy proceedings, subject to the special provisions provided in this area.

###### Article 816

Agreements which have the object of creating rights or renouncing rights over all or part of a succession not yet open or of property dependent thereon produce effect only in the cases where they are authorized by law.

###### Article 817

The law regulates the order of succession among the different heirs and the surviving spouse.  

Universal legatees and donees are seised under the conditions provided in Title II, Des donations entre vifs et des testaments, of this book.  
In their absence, the succession is acquired by the State.

###### Article 818

The heirs and the surviving spouse are seised by operation of law of the property, rights and actions of the deceased, under the obligation to discharge all the charges of the succession.  
The State must have itself sent into possession.

###### Article 819

The provisions of this title, in particular those which concern indivision and partition, apply as appropriate to universal or residuary legatees and donees, when not derogated from by a particular rule.

#### Chapitre II

Des qualités requises pour succéder - De la preuve de la qualité d'héritier

##### Section I : Des qualités requises pour succéder Article 820

To succeed, it is necessary to exist at the instant of the opening of the succession or, having already been conceived, to be born viable.  
A person whose absence is presumed within the meaning of articles 142 et seq. may succeed.

###### Article 821

When several persons who had a vocation to succeed one another perish in the same event, the order of deaths is established by all means.  
Persons who die without it being possible to establish which survived the other are deemed to have died at the same instant, if at least one of them is called to the succession of the other.  
The succession of each of them is then devolved to the persons who would have been called to receive it in their absence.

###### Article 822

The following are unworthy to succeed, and, as such, excluded from successions:
1° A person who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily caused or attempted to cause the death of the deceased;  
2° A person who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily inflicted blows or violence having resulted in the death of the deceased, without intention to cause it;  
3° A person who is convicted of having voluntarily refrained from preventing the commission of an offence against the bodily integrity of the deceased and from which death resulted, when he could have done so without risk to himself or to third parties;  
4° A person who, in criminal proceedings, has brought against the deceased an accusation or testimony found to be false or defamatory;  

5° An heir of full age who, having learned of the murder of the deceased, did not report it to the authorities. However, the failure to report may not be invoked against the ascendants and descendants of the murderer, nor against his relatives in the same degree, nor against his husband or wife, nor against his brothers or sisters, nor against his uncles and aunts, nor against nephews and nieces.

###### Article 823

When by reason of their death, the public prosecution could not be pursued to its conclusion against the persons who committed the acts mentioned in 1° and 2°, they may nevertheless be declared unworthy by the court upon application of any heir and, in the absence thereof, of the public prosecutor. The application must be made within six months of the death.

###### Article 824

When the deceased, subsequent to the facts which constitute the cause of unworthiness, had knowledge thereof and expressly specified, in testamentary form, that he intended to maintain the heir in his rights or made him a universal or residuary liberality, this successor affected by a cause of unworthiness is not excluded from the succession.

###### Article 825

The heir excluded from the succession on grounds of unworthiness is required to return all fruits and all revenues of which he has had enjoyment since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 826

The children of the unworthy person are not excluded by the fault of their ancestor, whether they come to the succession in their own right, or by the effect of representation; but the unworthy person may not, in any case, claim, over the property of this succession, the usufruct that the law grants to fathers and mothers over the property of their children.

##### Section II : De la preuve de la qualité d'héritier Article 827

Proof of the status of heir is established by all means.  
This does not derogate from customs concerning the issuance of certificates of ownership or inheritance by judicial or administrative authorities.

###### Article 828

Proof of the status of heir may result from a certificate of notoriety drawn up by a notary, at the request of one or more beneficiaries.  
The certificate of notoriety must refer to the death certificate of the person whose succession is open and mention the supporting documents that could be produced, such as civil status records and, where applicable, documents concerning the existence of testamentary liberalities that may have an impact on succession devolution.  

It contains the affirmation, signed by the beneficiary or beneficiaries who are the authors of the request, that they have entitlement, alone or with others whom they designate, to collect all or part of the succession of the deceased.  

Any person whose statements would appear useful may be called to the act.  
Mention is made of the existence of the certificate of notoriety in the margin of the death certificate.

###### Article 829

The certificate of notoriety thus established is evidence until proof to the contrary.  

The person who relies on it is presumed to have inheritance rights in the proportion indicated therein, and the heirs designated in the certificate of notoriety or their common agent are deemed, with regard to third parties holding property of the succession, to have free disposal of such property and, if it concerns funds, free disposal thereof in the proportion indicated in the act.  
The certificate of notoriety does not, by itself, entail acceptance of the succession.

###### Article 830

Any person who, knowingly and in bad faith, relies on an inaccurate certificate of notoriety, incurs the sanctions provided for in Article 888, without prejudice to damages.

#### Chapitre III : De l'ordre des successions Article 831

Successions devolve to the relatives and to the surviving spouse entitled to succeed of the deceased, in the order and according to the rules determined hereinafter.  
The surviving spouse entitled to succeed is the surviving spouse who is not divorced.

##### Section I : Des droits des parents en l'absence de conjoint successible

###### § 1. Dispositions générales Article 832

The law does not distinguish according to the modes of establishment of filiation in regulating succession.  

The rights resulting from adoptive filiation are regulated in Title IX of this code, relating to adoption according to the Civil Code.

###### Article 833

In the absence of a surviving spouse entitled to succeed, relatives are called to succeed as follows: 1° Children and their descendants;  
2° Father and mother; brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter; 3° Ascendants other than father and mother;  
4° Collaterals other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter. Each of these four categories constitutes an order of heirs which excludes the following ones.

###### Article 834

Children or their descendants succeed to their father and mother or other ascendants, without distinction of sex or primogeniture, even if they are born of different unions.

###### Article 835

When the deceased leaves neither issue, nor brother, nor sister, nor descendants of the latter, his father and mother succeed to him, each for one half.

###### Article 836

When the father and mother died before the deceased and the latter leaves no issue, the brothers and sisters of the deceased or their descendants succeed to him, to the exclusion of other relatives, ascendants or collaterals.

###### Article 837

When the father and mother survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, but has brothers and sisters or descendants of the latter, the succession devolves, for one quarter, to each of the father and mother and, for the remaining half, to the brothers and sisters or to their descendants.  

When only one of the father and mother survives, the succession devolves for one quarter to that person and for three quarters to the brothers and sisters or to their descendants.

###### Article 838

When only the father or the mother survives and the deceased has neither issue nor brother nor sister nor descendant of the latter, but leaves one or more ascendants of the other branch than that of his surviving father or mother, the succession devolves for one half to the father or to the mother and for one half to the ascendants of the other branch.

###### Article 839

When the father and mother or one of them survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, they may in all cases exercise a right of return, up to the shares fixed in the first paragraph of Article 837, over the property that the deceased had received from them by donation.  
The value of the portion of property subject to the right of return is imputed as a priority against the succession rights of the father and mother.  

When the right of return cannot be exercised in kind, it is executed in value, within the limit of the succession assets.

###### Article 840

In the absence of heirs of the first two orders, the succession devolves to ascendants other than father and mother.

###### Article 841

In the absence of heirs of the first three orders, the succession devolves to the collateral relatives of the deceased other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter.

###### § 2. Des degrés et des branches Article 842

Proximity of relationship is established by the number of generations; each generation is called a degree.

###### Article 843

The sequence of degrees forms the line. The sequence of degrees between persons who descend one from the other is called the direct line, and the sequence of degrees between persons who do not descend from one another but who descend from a common ancestor is called the collateral line.  
The direct line is distinguished into direct descending line and direct ascending line. The first is that which links the head with those who descend from him; the second is that which links a person with those from whom he descends.

###### Article 844

In the direct line, there are as many degrees as there are generations between the persons. Thus, the child is, with regard to the father and mother, in the first degree; the grandson or granddaughter in the second; and reciprocally from the father and mother with regard to the child and from the grandparents with regard to the grandson or granddaughter; and so on.  
In the collateral line, degrees are counted by generation, from one of the relatives up to but not including the common ancestor, and from the latter to the other relative. Thus, brothers and sisters are in the

second degree; uncle or aunt and nephew or niece are in the third degree; first cousins in the fourth degree; and so on.

###### Article 845

In each order, the closest heir excludes the heir more remote in degree. At equal degree, heirs succeed in equal portions and per capita.  
All subject to what will be said hereinafter concerning division by branches and representation.

###### Article 846

Collateral relatives belonging to the order of heirs mentioned in 4° of Article 833 do not succeed beyond the sixth degree.

###### Article 847

Relationship is divided into two branches, according to whether it proceeds from the father or the mother.  
When the succession devolves to ascendants, it is divided by half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 848

In each branch, the ascendant who is in the closest degree succeeds, to the exclusion of all others.  
Ascendants in the same degree succeed per capita.  

In the absence of an ascendant in one branch, the ascendants of the other branch receive the entire succession.

###### Article 849

When the succession devolves to collaterals other than brothers and sisters or their descendants, it is divided in half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 850

In each branch, the collateral who is in the closest degree succeeds, to the exclusion of all others.  
Collaterals in the same degree succeed per capita.  
In the absence of a collateral in one branch, the collaterals of the other branch receive the entire succession.

###### § 3. De la représentation Article 851

Representation is a legal fiction, the effect of which is to call the representatives to the succession, in the place, in the degree and in the rights of the person represented.

###### Article 852

Representation takes place indefinitely in the direct descending line.  

It is admitted in all cases, whether the children of the deceased compete with the descendants of a predeceased child, or whether all the children of the deceased having died before him, the descendants of said children find themselves among themselves in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 853

Representation does not take place in favor of ascendants; the closest, in each of the two lines, always excludes the more remote.

###### Article 854

In the collateral line, representation is admitted in favor of the children and descendants of brothers or sisters of the deceased, whether they come to his succession concurrently with uncles or aunts, or whether all the brothers and sisters of the deceased having predeceased, the succession is devolved to their descendants in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 855

In all cases where representation is admitted, the partition is carried out by stirpes, as if the person represented were coming to the succession: if the same stirps has produced several branches, the subdivision is also made by stirpes in each branch. Within a stirps or a subdivision of a stirps, the partition is made per capita.

###### Article 856

One does not represent living persons, but only those who are dead; one may represent a person whose succession one has renounced.  
One represents renunciants only in successions devolved in the direct or collateral line.  
The children of the renunciant conceived before the opening of the succession from which the renunciant was excluded bring back to the succession of the latter the property which they inherited in his place and stead, if they come in competition with other children conceived after the opening of the succession. The bringing back is made according to the provisions set forth in articles 994 et seq. of this code.  

Unless the donor wills otherwise, in case of representation of a renunciant, the donations made to the latter are imputed, where applicable, on the reserved portion that should have gone to him had he not renounced.  

The law does not distinguish, for the exercise of representation, between legitimate filiation and natural filiation.

###### Article 857

Representation is admitted in favor of the children and descendants of the unworthy person, even though the latter is alive at the opening of the succession.  
The provisions set forth in the second paragraph of article 856 are applicable to the children of the unworthy person during his lifetime.

##### Section II : Des droits du conjoint survivant

###### § 1. De la nature des droits, de leur montant et de leur exercice Article 858

The successor spouse is called to the succession, either alone or in competition with the relatives of the deceased.

###### Article 859

If the predeceased spouse leaves children or descendants, the surviving spouse receives, at his choice, the usufruct of all the existing property or the ownership of one quarter of the property when all the children are issue of both spouses and the ownership of one quarter in the presence of one or more children who are not issue of both spouses.

###### Article 860

If, in the absence of children or descendants, the deceased leaves his father and mother, the surviving spouse receives half of the property. The other half is devolved one quarter to the father and one quarter to the mother.  

When the father or the mother has predeceased, the share that would have gone to him or her passes to the surviving spouse.

###### Article 861

In the absence of children or descendants of the deceased and of his father and mother, the surviving spouse receives the entire succession.

###### Article 862

By way of derogation from article 861, in case of predecease of the father and mother, the property that the deceased had received from his ascendants by succession or donation and which is found in kind in the succession is, in the absence of descendants, devolved for half to the brothers and sisters of the deceased or to their descendants, themselves descendants of the predeceased parent or parents at the origin of the transmission.

###### Article 863

When the surviving spouse receives all or three quarters of the property, the ascendants of the deceased, other than the father and mother, who are in need benefit from a claim for maintenance against the succession of the predeceased.  
The time limit to claim it is one year from the death or from the moment when the heirs cease to provide the benefits they previously furnished to the ascendants. The time limit is extended, in case of joint ownership, until the completion of the partition.  
The pension is taken from the succession. It is borne by all the heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all the particular legatees, proportionally to their emolument.  

However, if the deceased expressly declared that a certain legacy shall be satisfied in preference to the others, article 1080 shall apply.

###### Article 864

When the spouse has the choice of ownership or usufruct, his rights are non-transferable as long as he has not exercised his option.

###### Article 865

The spouse's option between usufruct and ownership is proved by any means.  

Any heir may invite the spouse in writing to exercise his option. Failing to have taken a position in writing within three months, the spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct.  

The spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct if he dies without having taken a position.

###### Article 866

The calculation of the right in full ownership of the spouse provided for in articles 859 and 860 shall be carried out on a mass made up of all the property existing at the death of his spouse to which shall be fictitiously reunited those of which he would have disposed, either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, in favor of successors, without dispensation from bringing back.  
The spouse may exercise his right only on the property of which the predeceased will not have disposed either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, and without prejudice to the rights of reserve or to the rights of return.

###### Article 867

The liberalities received from the deceased by the surviving spouse are imputed on the rights of the latter in the succession. When the liberalities thus received are less than the rights defined in articles 859 and 860,

the surviving spouse may claim the complement, without ever receiving a portion of the property greater than the available portion defined in article 1228.

###### § 2. De la conversion de l'usufruit Article 868

Any usufruct belonging to the spouse on the property of the predeceased, whether it results from the law, a will or a donation of property to come, gives rise to a faculty of conversion into a life annuity, at the request of one of the bare owner heirs or of the successor spouse himself.  

The faculty of conversion is not susceptible to renunciation. The coheirs cannot be deprived of it by the will of the predeceased.

###### Article 869

In the absence of agreement between the parties, the request for conversion is submitted to the judge. The request for conversion may be brought until the final partition.  
If the judge grants the request for conversion, the judge determines the amount of the annuity, the security that the debtor coheirs must provide, as well as the type of indexation appropriate to maintain the initial equivalence of the annuity to the usufruct.  
However, the judge cannot order, against the will of the spouse, the conversion of the usufruct relating to the dwelling that he or she occupies as a principal residence, as well as the furniture furnishing it.

###### Article 870

By agreement between the heirs and the spouse, the conversion of the spouse's usufruct into capital may be carried out.

###### Article 871

The conversion of the usufruct is included in the partition operations. It does not produce retroactive effect, unless otherwise stipulated by the parties.

###### § 3

Temporary right to housing and life right to housing Article 872
If, at the time of death, the successor spouse effectively occupies, as a principal residence, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or falling entirely within the estate, he or she has by right, for one year, the free enjoyment of this dwelling, as well as the furniture, included in the estate, that furnishes it.  

If his or her housing was provided by means of a rental lease or a dwelling belonging in undivided part to the deceased, the rent or occupancy compensation shall be reimbursed to him or her by the estate during the year, as and when paid.  
The rights provided for in this article are deemed direct effects of marriage and not succession rights. This article is a matter of public policy.

###### Article 873

In addition, unless otherwise intended by the deceased expressed in the conditions of Article 1127, the successor spouse who effectively occupied, at the time of death, as a principal residence, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or falling entirely within the estate, has on this dwelling and on the furniture included in the estate that furnishes it, until his or her death, a right of habitation and a right of use.  

When the dwelling is subject to a rental lease, the successor spouse, if he or she effectively occupied the premises as a principal residence at the time of death, benefits from the right of use on the furniture included in the estate furnishing it.  
The deprivation of these rights of habitation and use expressed by the deceased in the conditions mentioned in the first paragraph has no impact on the usufruct rights that the spouse receives by virtue of law or a liberality, which continue to obey their own rules.  

These rights of habitation and use are exercised under the conditions provided for in Articles 745 paragraph 3, 747 and 748.  

The spouse, the other heirs or one of them may require that an inventory of the movables and a statement of the immovable subject to the rights of use and habitation be drawn up.  
By way of derogation from Article 745, paragraph 3, when the situation of the spouse is such that the dwelling burdened with the right of habitation is no longer adapted to his or her needs, the spouse or his or her representative may lease it for use other than commercial or agricultural in order to generate the resources necessary for new accommodation conditions.

###### Article 874

The value of the rights of habitation and use is imputed to the value of the succession rights received by the spouse.  
If the value of the rights of habitation and use is less than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse may take the balance from the existing property.  

If the value of the rights of habitation and use is greater than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse is not required to compensate the estate for the excess.

###### Article 875

The spouse has one year from the death to express his or her intention to benefit from these rights of habitation and use.  
The successor spouse and the heirs may, by agreement, convert the rights of habitation and use into a life annuity or into capital.  

If among the successors who are parties to the agreement there is a minor or a protected adult, the agreement must be authorized by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### § 4. Right to pension Article 876

The estate of the predeceased spouse owes a pension to the successor spouse who is in need. The time limit to claim it is one year from the death or from the moment when the heirs cease to pay the benefits they previously provided to the spouse. The time limit is extended, in case of undivided ownership, until the completion of the partition.  
The maintenance pension is taken from the estate. It is borne by all the heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all the particular legatees, in proportion to their emolument.  

However, if the deceased expressly declared that a particular legacy shall be paid in preference to the others, Article 1080 shall apply.

#### Chapter IV. Rights of the State

###### Article 877

In the absence of heirs, surviving spouse, universal legatees or donees, the estate is acquired by the State.  
The State is required to have seals affixed and, if the inventory of property has not already been carried out within the framework of the procedure provided for under the title of vacant estates, the domain authority has it carried out in the forms prescribed for the acceptance of estates under benefit of inventory.

###### Article 878

It must request the sending into possession from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the estate is opened.  
The State is exempted from using the services of a lawyer; the court rules on the request three months and forty days after publication and posting in the customary forms, and after hearing the public prosecutor.

###### Article 879

In the case where the vacancy had been regularly declared, and the domain administration appointed as curator, it may, before making its request, proceed by itself with the publicity formalities provided for.

###### Article 880

The domain administration that has not fulfilled the formalities prescribed to it may be ordered to pay damages to the heirs, if any appear.

#### Chapter V: Option of the heir

##### Section I: General provisions Article 881

Any successor, the heir with regard to the estate as the legatee with regard to the legacy that falls to him or her, may:	either accept it purely and simply,	either accept it under benefit of inventory, when he or she has a universal or universal title vocation,	or renounce it.

###### Article 882

The option is indivisible. However, the successor who combines more than one succession vocation has, for each of them, a separate right of option.

###### Article 883

This option cannot be exercised before the opening of the estate, nor by marriage contract nor with the consent of the person whose estate is in question.  
An option that is conditional or subject to a term is null and void.

###### Article 884

The heir of subsequent rank has the same rights as the heir when the latter renounces the estate or is struck by unworthiness and this, from the day he or she became aware of the renunciation or unworthiness. The same applies to the heirs of the person who dies without having opted, from the death of his or her predecessor; these heirs of the person who dies without having opted exercise the option separately, each for his or her share.

###### Article 885

The power to accept or renounce an estate is prescribed by ten years. At the end of this period, the successor is deemed to have renounced the estate. Anyone who claims to have accepted this estate before the expiration of this period must provide proof thereof.

###### Article 886

The subsequent heir of an heir whose acceptance is annulled shall have the ten-year period run against him only from the final decision establishing such nullity.  
The heir who has left the surviving spouse in enjoyment of the hereditary property shall have the period run against him only from the death of the latter.  

The period does not run either against one who legitimately was unaware of the arising of his right, in particular the opening of the succession.  

Moreover, as long as the prescription of the right to accept has not been acquired against the heirs who have renounced, they have the option to still accept the succession, if it has not already been accepted by other heirs; without prejudice nevertheless to rights that may be acquired by third parties over the property of the succession.

###### Article 887

The option exercised has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the succession.  

However, error, fraud as well as duress are a cause of nullity of the option exercised by the heir. The action for nullity is prescribed after five years from the day on which the error or fraud was discovered or the day on which the duress ceased.

###### Article 888

The heir who, knowingly and in bad faith, has concealed property or rights of a succession, or concealed the existence of a co-heir, or omitted to include in the inventory property or rights of the succession, is deprived of the benefit of inventory and the right of renunciation: he is an unconditional heir, without prejudice to damages that the victims of his actions may claim.  
The heir may not however claim any share in the property or rights misappropriated or concealed. Likewise, when the concealment related to a donation subject to hotchpot or reduction, the heir owes the hotchpot or reduction of that donation without being able to claim any share in it. The concealing heir is furthermore bound to return all fruits and revenues of the concealed property of which he has had enjoyment since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 889

The personal creditors of one who refrains from accepting a succession or who renounces a succession to the prejudice of their rights may be authorized by the court to accept the succession on behalf of their debtor, in his place and stead.  
The acceptance takes place only in favour of these creditors and up to the amount of their claims. It produces no other effect with regard to the heir.

###### Article 890

The acceptance of a succession that is found to be absorbed or diminished by more than half, by the discovery of a will unknown at the time of acceptance, is voidable for lesion.

##### Section II : De l'acceptation de la succession

###### Article 891

Successions devolving to minors and adults under guardianship may be validly accepted only in accordance with the provisions of the title On Minority, Guardianship and Emancipation.

###### Article 892

The acceptance of the succession may be express or tacit: it is express when the successor takes the title or quality of heir in an authentic or private instrument; it is tacit when the successor performs an act that necessarily presupposes his intention to accept and that he would have the right to perform only in his quality as heir.  
Purely conservatory acts, acts of supervision and provisional administration are not, by themselves, acts constituting acceptance on the part of the heir. If the successor wishes to perform another act without however taking the title or quality of heir, he must request authorization from the judge to perform it.

###### Article 893

The following are deemed purely conservatory:
1° The payment of funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other succession debts whose settlement is urgent;  
2° The collection of fruits and revenues of succession property or the sale of perishable property, subject to justifying that the funds were used to extinguish the debts referred to in 1° or were deposited with a notary or placed in escrow;  
3° Any act intended to prevent the aggravation of succession liabilities;  
4° Acts related to the termination of the employment contract of the employee of the deceased private employer, the payment of wages and compensation owed to the employee as well as the delivery of end-of-contract documents.

###### Article 894

The following are deemed provisional administration:
1° The renewal, as lessor or lessee, of leases which, in default, would give rise to payment of compensation;  
2° The implementation of administration or disposition decisions initiated by the deceased and necessary for the proper functioning of the business;  
3° Acts that are routine operations necessary for the continuation, in the short term, of the activity of the business forming part of the succession.

###### Article 895

The heir who, gratuitously or for consideration, transfers his rights in the succession, whether to a stranger, or to all his co-heirs, or to some of them, accepts by that fact alone the succession.  
The same applies when the heir has renounced the succession, gratuitously or not, in favour of one, several or all of his co-heirs, or in favour of one, several or all heirs of subsequent rank.

###### Article 896

When one to whom a succession has devolved has died before being able, expressly or tacitly, to express his choice, his heirs may accept it or renounce it on his behalf. In the absence of unanimity among them, the succession must be accepted subject to benefit of inventory.

###### Article 897

When the heir accepts the succession, the effect of acceptance goes back to the day of the opening of the succession.

##### Section III : De la renonciation aux successions Article 898

Renunciation of a succession is not presumed. It is enforceable against all from the day it is made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the succession opened, in a special register kept for that purpose.

###### Article 899

The heir who renounces is deemed never to have been an heir.

###### Article 900

The succession to which the heir renounces is distributed among his heirs in direct line; in the absence of heirs in direct line, it passes to the co-heirs and otherwise to the next degree.  
The heir who renounces the succession may however retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer expressly required hotchpot in case of renunciation. In that case, hotchpot is made in value; when the value brought into hotchpot exceeds the rights he should have had in the partition had he participated in it, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs up to the amount of that excess.

##### Section IV : Du bénéfice d'inventaire

###### § 1. Des formalités à respecter Article 901

The declaration of an heir, that he intends to take that quality only subject to benefit of inventory, must be made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the succession opened. It must be recorded in the register intended to receive acts of renunciation.

###### Article 902

The declaration mentions the surnames, given names, occupation of the heir and the capacity by virtue of which he is called to the succession.  
It also includes election of a single domicile located in Djibouti, which may be the domicile of one of the acceptors subject to benefit of inventory or that of the person in charge of settling the succession. It is to this address that creditors shall declare their claims.

###### Article 903

The declaration of the heir is registered by the registry, which gives him a receipt for it, and opens a file. The receipt informs the declarant of the necessity to comply with the publicity provided for by the following article.

###### Article 904

The declaration is published, within fifteen days, in a journal authorized to receive legal publications.  
When the law refers to the declaration as the starting point of a time limit, that time limit runs from the date of the publication made.

###### Article 905

The heir's declaration has effect only insofar as it is preceded or followed by a faithful and accurate inventory of the assets of the succession and within the time limits which will be determined hereinafter.

###### Article 906

The heir has, first, three months to make an inventory, from the day of the opening of the succession.  

However, he may request from the judge an additional time limit if he justifies serious and legitimate reasons which delay the filing of the inventory. In that case, the time limit is suspended from the date of the request for extension.  

The heir has, thereafter, forty days to deliberate on his acceptance or not of the succession. This second time limit begins to run from the day of the expiration of the time limit to which the heir is subject to make the inventory, or from the day of the closing of the inventory if it has been completed before the three months.

###### Article 907

The inventory is descriptive and estimative of the elements present, item by item, in the estate of the deceased.  
It is drawn up by a bailiff or a notary, according to the rules applicable to these professions.

###### Article 908

A copy of the inventory is delivered against receipt by the heir to the competent registry, which adds it to the file. The heir must carry out this formality within two months of the inventory being made. Failing this, he is deemed to have accepted the succession unconditionally.

###### Article 909

The inventory gives rise to the same publication as the initial declaration.  
Any person who justifies his status as creditor against the deceased may take cognizance of its content and obtain a copy at the registry.

###### § 2. Effects of acceptance subject to inventory Article 910

The declaration made by the heir to accept the succession subject to inventory entails:
1° Separation of estates: the personal assets of the heir are not merged with those of the succession;  
2° Preservation of all the rights that the heir had previously over the assets of the deceased; 3° Limitation of the acceptance of the succession to the succession assets: the heir is only required to pay the debts of the succession within the limit of the assets collected and not from his personal estate. The heir may only be held liable for his acts on his personal assets when provisions of this paragraph so provide;  
4° Framework for the management of the succession assets by the heir, who is required to administer the succession.

###### Article 911

During the duration of the time limits to make an inventory and to deliberate, the heir cannot be compelled to exercise his option. No judgment can be obtained against him.  
As long as the prescription of the right to accept has not been acquired against him, the heir may revoke his acceptance and accept the succession unconditionally. He is then deemed to have accepted it from the opening of the succession.  

Acceptance subject to inventory prevents any renunciation of the succession.

###### Article 912

If the heir does not file the inventory within the time limits provided for making it, or does not exercise his option within the time limit offered to deliberate, he retains the power to still make an inventory and to opt.  

It is otherwise if he has otherwise made an act manifesting his intention to accept the succession unconditionally or if there exists against him a judgment having acquired the force of res judicata which condemns him in the capacity of unconditional heir.

###### Article 913

However, upon the expiration of the time limits provided for making an inventory and for deliberating, the heir who has not opted may be summoned, by extrajudicial act, to take a position. The summons may emanate from a creditor of the succession, a co-heir, an heir of subsequent rank, or the State.  
Within two months following the summons, the heir must take a position or request an additional time limit from the judge when he has not been able to close the inventory begun or when he justifies other serious and legitimate reasons. This time limit is suspended from the date of the request for extension until the decision of the judge seized.  

Failing to have taken a position upon the expiration of the two-month time limit or the additional time limit granted, the heir is deemed to have accepted unconditionally.

###### Article 914

From the publication of the declaration of the heir who accepts the succession subject to inventory, the creditors of the succession have a time limit of twelve months to claim what is owed to them. They must declare their claim within this time limit, by notifying their title to the elected domicile of the succession.  
In case of late declaration or absence of declaration, claims not secured by security interests over the assets of the succession are extinguished with regard to the succession.  

This provision also benefits sureties and co-obligors, as well as persons having granted an independent guarantee relating to the claim thus extinguished.

###### Article 915

From the publication of the declaration of acceptance subject to inventory and for a period of twelve months, it stops or prohibits any means of execution and any new registration of security interest by the creditors of the succession, relating to both movables and immovables.  
However, seizing creditors are considered as holders of security interests over the assets and rights previously seized.

###### Article 916

When the succession has been accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by one or more others up to the net assets, the rules applicable to this latter option are imposed on all the heirs until the day of partition.  
The creditors of a succession accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by others up to the net assets may provoke the partition as soon as they justify difficulties in the recovery of the share of their claim incumbent upon the heirs accepting up to the net assets.

###### Article 917

The heir accepting up to the net assets has the obligation to administer the assets he collects in the succession, and must account for his management.  
He is liable for serious faults he would commit in this administration.  

He must present the account to any succession creditor who requests it and respond within a time limit of two months to the summons, served by extrajudicial act, to reveal to him where the assets and

rights collected in the succession that he has neither alienated nor retained are located. Failing this, he may be compelled on his personal assets.  

If he does not wish to personally administer the assets of the succession, or if he is in default, a representative may be appointed in court at the request of any interested party. The President of the Court of First Instance is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 918

The heir is the owner of the assets of the succession and has the power to dispose of the assets of the succession.  
If there exist in the succession objects liable to perish or too costly to preserve, the heir may proceed with the sale of these objects. If the heir has decided to retain such assets in kind, at the end of the acceptance procedure subject to inventory, he is only liable for the depreciation or deterioration caused by his negligence.

###### Article 919

For other property, within twelve months from the publication provided for in Article 904, the heir may declare:
1° that he intends to retain in kind certain property of the succession. He then owes the succession the value of such property as estimated in the inventory;  
2° that he is selling certain property, movable or immovable.  
Such property is excluded from the estate patrimony and removed from the security of estate creditors. On the other hand, its value is recorded in the assets of the succession. All without prejudice to the rights of creditors holding security interests.  
Other estate property that has not been the subject of such a declaration remains as security for the creditors of the succession.

###### Article 920

The declaration of alienation or retention of one or more items of property is made within fifteen days at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The heir ensures its publication in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices.  
Without prejudice to rights reserved to creditors holding security interests, any estate creditor may contest before the judge, within three months after the publication mentioned in the first paragraph, the value of the retained property or, when the sale was made amicably, the price of the alienation by proving that the value of the property is higher.  

When the creditor's application is granted, the heir is liable for the difference from his personal property, unless he restores the retained property to the succession.  
The creditor may also act in his own name to have acts done by his debtor in fraud of his rights declared unenforceable against him, provided he establishes, in the case of an act for valuable consideration, that the third party co-contractor had knowledge or should have had knowledge of the fraud.

###### Article 921

The declaration to retain property is not enforceable against creditors until it has been published.  

Failure to declare the alienation of property within the time limit provided for in the preceding article makes the heir liable on his personal property up to the amount of the price of the alienation.

###### Article 922

The heir settles the liabilities of the succession. He draws up for this purpose a draft settlement of liabilities.  

The costs of seals, if any have been affixed, of inventory and of account, are borne by the succession. The public officer or ministerial officer having settled the succession or enabled the preservation of estate property shall be paid before other creditors.  
Registered creditors are paid according to the rank of the security accompanying their claim.  

Other creditors who have declared their claim are satisfied in the order of declarations. Legacies of sums of money are delivered after payment of creditors.

###### Article 923

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed at the registry which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904. Creditors who are not fully satisfied in view of this draft may, within one month of publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in order to contest the settlement draft.

###### Article 924

In the absence of contestation at the end of the one-month period from the publication provided for in the preceding article, the heir must pay the creditors within the following two months, in accordance with the draft settlement of liabilities.  
When, conversely, the settlement draft is not validated due to a contestation concerning the order or nature of the claims, the heir deposits the available sums as long as the contestation persists.

###### Article 925

The personal creditors of the heir may not pursue recovery of their claims on the property of the succession until the end of the twelve-month period from the publication of the declaration of acceptance of the succession subject to inventory and after the full satisfaction of estate creditors and legatees.  
Creditors who have not declared their claim within the time limit referred to in the preceding article, and who appear only after exhaustion of the assets, have recourse only against legatees who have been satisfied in their rights.

##### Section V: Vacant successions Article 926

The succession is vacant when, after expiration of the time limits for making inventory and for deliberating: 1° No one appears who claims a succession and there is no known heir;  
2° All known heirs have renounced the succession;  
3° Known heirs have been summoned to take a position in accordance with the provisions of Article 913 and have renounced the succession or remained silent;  
4° In the absence of summons, known heirs have not opted, either expressly or tacitly, for ten years.  
When heirs come forward during the proceedings, their hereditary prerogatives take precedence. They may then exercise their legal right of option: if they accept the succession purely and simply, the vacancy automatically ends; if they renounce it, it continues; and if they accept subject to inventory, the procedure continues according to the rules set out in Section IV of this chapter.

###### Article 927

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the succession is opened, appoints a curator at the request of any interested person or at the requisition of the public prosecutor.  

His decision is, at the diligence of the curator, within fifteen days of its pronouncement, published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices.  

In the context of vacant successions, the curatorship is necessarily entrusted to the administrative authority responsible for the domain.

###### Article 928

The curator is required, before all else, to have its state established by an inventory: he exercises and pursues its rights; he responds to claims brought against the succession; he administers, under the obligation to have the sums of money found in the succession, as well as the amounts from the price of movables or immovables sold, paid into the National Treasury, for the preservation of rights and subject to rendering account to whom it may concern.  
The provisions of Section IV of this chapter, on the forms of inventory, on the mode of administration and on the accounts to be rendered by the beneficiary heir, as well as on the rights and obligations of creditors, are common to curators of vacant successions, subject to the following reservations.

###### Article 929

Creditors must declare their claim to the curator, by notifying him of their title, within nine months.  
The curator establishes a draft settlement of liabilities respecting the order provided for in Article 922, the costs related to the administration of the curatorship being paid before other claims. The curator may only provide for payment of the debts of the succession up to the amount of the assets.  

The curator may however pay, without waiting for the draft settlement of liabilities, the costs necessary for the preservation of the patrimony, funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other estate debts whose settlement is urgent.

###### Article 930

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed at the registry of the Court of First Instance which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904.

###### Article 931

Creditors who are not fully satisfied in view of this draft may, within one month of publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in order to contest the draft settlement.  
Those who have not declared their claim after submission of the draft may only claim against the remaining assets. In case of insufficiency of these assets, they have recourse only against the legatees who have been satisfied in their rights. This recourse is barred after one year from the realization of all the remaining assets.

###### Article 932

In the absence of recourse against the draft or after the president's decision has become final, the curator proceeds with the final realization of the remaining assets.  
Any surplus is remitted upon their request to heirs who come forward, if they are within the time limit to claim the succession.  

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the succession is opened, seized by the curator, sends the State into possession of the succession.

#### Chapter VI. Of partition

##### Section I: Of the legal regime of co-ownership

###### § 1. General provisions Article 933

Co-ownership arises when several persons have a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of property. This right may be ownership or another dismembered real right.  
Co-ownership does not have legal personality.  
Each co-owner has over the undivided property the same right shared with the others. The extent of each person's rights in the co-ownership is defined by the law or the agreement that gives rise to it. In the absence of other title, it results from a certificate of notoriety or an inventory heading established by the notary.

###### Article 934

Each co-owner holds title to his share. However, when a co-owner intends to transfer all or part of his undivided rights, for consideration and to a person outside the co-ownership, the other co-owners have a right of pre-emption.  
Any draft transfer must be notified beforehand to the other co-owners, with all useful information, such as the price, the conditions of the transfer and the identifying elements of the purchaser. This notification, made by extra-judicial act, opens a period of one month for the co-owners to bring to the knowledge of the transferring co-owner their decision to exercise their right of pre-emption under the conditions brought to their knowledge.  
The person who decides to pre-empt has two months to complete the transfer, from the sending of his decision to the transferring co-owner. After this period, he is formally notified to respond and, if he remains silent for fifteen days, his declaration of pre-emption is null and void by operation of law, without prejudice to damages that may be claimed by the transferor.  

When the transferor has granted payment terms and, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property that has fallen to him has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion, unless the parties exclude this variation.

###### Article 935

When a creditor seizes all or part of the rights of a co-owner in the co-ownership with a view to subjecting them to a forced sale, there is no right of pre-emption but a right of substitution for the successful bidder. The lawyer of the pursuing creditor or the notary notifies all the other co-owners one month before the scheduled date of the sale. The latter benefit from a period of one month from the adjudication, to substitute themselves for the purchaser.  
This right is exercised by declaration at the registry of the Court of First Instance or with the notary in charge of the sale. It is recorded in the schedule of conditions of sale established for the sale.

###### Article 936

For both amicable and forced transfers, compliance with the notification and time limit rules is prescribed on pain of nullity of the transaction. This nullity, of private interest, is available for five years to the persons

to whom the notifications should have been made or to their heirs.  

The notifications provided for by the two articles and the preceding paragraph must be addressed to every bare owner and to every usufructuary. But a usufructuary may only acquire a share in bare ownership if no bare owner comes forward as purchaser; a bare owner may only acquire a share in usufruct if no usufructuary comes forward as purchaser.

###### § 2. Of the rules of management of co-ownership Article 937

In co-ownership, decisions are made unanimously, subject to the following reservations.

###### Article 938

When they fall within the normal operation of undivided property, decisions concerning the following may be made by the holders of two-thirds of the undivided rights:
1° Acts of administration of undivided property;  
2° The designation of a co-owner or a third party as holder of a general administration mandate;
