3° The conclusion and renewal of leases other than those relating to property for agricultural, commercial, industrial or artisanal use;  
4° The decision to sell undivided movable property when this transaction is necessary for the payment of debts and charges of the co-ownership. The sale of undivided property outside this purpose requires unanimity, except by judicial authorization.

###### Article 939

Except in case of dismemberment of ownership of the property or if one of the co-owners is in one of the cases provided for in Article 863, the alienation of undivided property may be authorized by the Court of First Instance, at the request of one or more co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the undivided rights, according to the conditions and procedures defined in the following paragraphs.  
The co-owner or co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the undivided rights express before a notary, by this majority, their intention to proceed with the alienation of the undivided property. Within the month that follows, the notary has this intention served on the other co-owners.  
In the absence of opposition within three months of service, the decision to alienate the undivided property is confirmed, unless the service provided for in the second paragraph has not been made. In case of opposition, the Court of First Instance may authorize the alienation of the undivided property if it does not cause excessive harm to the rights of the other co-owners.  

This alienation is effected by licitation. The sums derived therefrom may not be reinvested except to pay the debts and charges of the co-ownership.

###### Article 940

Any co-owner may take the measures necessary for the preservation of undivided property, even if there is no urgency.  
These conservatory acts may be of a material nature, such as an act of occasional maintenance, or legal, such as formal notice to a debtor in default. They may be directed both against another co-owner and against a third party to the co-ownership.  

The co-owner may use for this purpose the co-ownership funds held by him and he is deemed to have free disposal thereof with regard to third parties.  

In the absence of co-ownership funds, he may oblige his co-owners to make the necessary expenditures with him.  

When undivided property is encumbered with a usufruct, these powers are enforceable against the usufructuary to the extent that the latter is liable for repairs.

###### Article 941

Co-owners may give a mandate to one or more of them or to a third party to perform a specific act, which constitutes a special mandate, or even to handle all the affairs of the undivided ownership, which is a general mandate. A general mandate only permits acts of administration.  
If one of the co-owners or a third party takes the initiative to manage the undivided property with the knowledge of the others and without opposition on their part, he is deemed to have received a tacit mandate. This mandate only permits acts of administration; it covers neither acts of disposition nor the conclusion or renewal of leases.  

The co-owner who manages one or more undivided properties is responsible for his management. He is entitled to remuneration for his activity under the conditions fixed amicably or, failing that, by judicial decision.  
If a co-owner or a third party performs an act useful to the undivided ownership without the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraphs being met, he is obliged to continue his management in accordance with the rules governing management of another's affairs.

###### Article 942

When the situation does not permit giving a mandate, a co-owner may seek judicial authorization:
1° When another co-owner is unable to express his will: the applicant co-owner may be authorized by the court to represent him, either generally or for certain particular acts. The court then determines the conditions and extent of the representation;  
2° In case of refusal by one of the co-owners to give his consent to an act deemed necessary by the applicant, when this refusal endangers the common interest. However, it is not within the power of the judge to authorize the sale in full ownership requested by a bare owner when the usufructuary opposes it;  
3° For all urgent measures required by the common interest.  
In cases 2° and 3°, authorization is sought before the President of the Court of First Instance who is seized and rules in summary proceedings. The President may, in particular, authorize a co-owner to collect from debtors of the undivided ownership or from depositaries of undivided funds a provision intended to meet urgent needs, prescribing, if necessary, the conditions of use. This authorization does not entail assumption of capacity for the surviving spouse or for the heir. He may also either appoint a co-owner as administrator requiring him if necessary to provide security, or appoint a sequestrator, or prohibit the displacement of movable property except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or another of the beneficiaries, on condition that they provide security if he deems it necessary.

###### Article 943

When an undivided immovable property for residential use or for mixed residential and professional use is vacant or has not been the subject of effective occupation for more than two calendar years, a co-owner may be authorized in court to carry out improvement, rehabilitation and restoration works on the property as well as to perform acts of administration and formalities of publication, having as sole purpose to lease it as a principal residence.

###### Article 944

For this purpose, a co-owner may seize the President of the Court of First Instance, so that he may appoint him as agent. The President fixes the duration of his mission as well as his remuneration. At the request of the appointed co-owner, the President may extend this mission for a period which he determines.  

The appointment decision is registered and published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 945

Within the limits of the powers conferred upon him, the appointed co-owner represents all the co-owners for the acts provided for in Article 943. He exercises his powers even when there is a minor or a protected adult among the other co-owners.  
The acts he performs within the framework of his mission have no effect on the hereditary option of the co-owner appointed as agent.

###### Article 946

At the request of any interested person or the public prosecutor, the President may remove the agent from his mission in case of characterized failure in the exercise thereof. The President then appoints another agent, for a period which he defines.

###### Article 947

Each heir may require the agent to allow consultation, at any time, of documents relating to the execution of his mission.  
Each year and at the end of his mission, the agent submits to the judge and to each heir upon his request a report on the execution of his mission.  
The mission ceases automatically by the effect of an undivided ownership agreement that would be signed between the heirs or by the signing of the partition deed. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the succession agent.

###### § 3. Rights and obligations of co-owners Article 948

Each co-owner has the same right of use and enjoyment over the undivided property as the others. The co-owners regulate the distribution of this right among themselves. It is possible for them to grant to a co-owner an exclusive right of use or enjoyment over the thing, in consideration of compensation.  

In the absence of agreement on the use of the undivided property, the President of the court settles the question on a provisional basis. He is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 949

Each person is entitled to the benefits of the undivided property and bears the losses in proportion to his rights in the undivided ownership. No claim relating to fruits and revenues shall, however, be admissible more than five years after the date on which they were collected or could have been.  
Any person who collects revenues or incurs expenses on behalf of the undivided ownership must keep a statement thereof which is available to the co-owners.  

The fruits and revenues benefit the entire undivided ownership; they may however, by express agreement, be attributed to one of the co-owners.  
Any co-owner may request his annual share in the benefits. In case of disagreement, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance rules taking into account the extent of each person's rights in the undivided ownership.

###### Article 950

Are automatically undivided, by the effect of real subrogation, the claims and indemnities that replace undivided property, as well as property acquired, with the consent of all the co-owners, in employment or re-employment of undivided property.

###### Article 951

When a co-owner has improved at his own expense the condition of an undivided property, it must be taken into account according to equity, having regard to the amount by which the value of the property is increased at the time of partition or alienation. He must likewise be credited for the necessary expenses he has made from his personal funds for the preservation of said property, even though they have not improved them.  
Conversely, the co-owner is liable for the degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of the undivided property by his act or by his fault.

###### § 4. Right of creditors to take action Article 952

The creditors of the undivided estate, who are those who could have taken action against the undivided property before the undivided ownership existed and those whose claim arose from the management of the undivided estate or from acts of preservation of which they were the authors, shall be paid from the assets of the undivided estate before any partition and, if the undivided estate should not be sufficient to satisfy them in their rights, they may take action against each of the co-owners. The latter are jointly and severally liable for the balance. The creditors of the undivided estate may also pursue the seizure and sale of the undivided property.

The personal creditors of a co-owner may not seize either the undivided property or their debtor's share. On the other hand, they may initiate partition in the name of their debtor or intervene in the partition that the debtor has initiated. The co-owners, however, have the power to stop the partition action by discharging the obligation owed by the debtor. Those who exercise this option shall reimburse themselves by deduction from the undivided property.

###### § 5. Applications for partition Article 953

No one may be compelled to remain in undivided ownership and partition may always be initiated, except by judgment or contrary agreement.

Co-owners who hold title to ownership, bare ownership or usufruct may agree to remain in undivided ownership for a limited time: this agreement may not be binding beyond five years; but it may be renewed. Conventional undivided ownership is subject to the rules of articles 2071 et seq.

###### Article 954

Where several undivided estates exist exclusively between the same persons, whether they relate to the same property or to different property, a single partition may take place.

###### Article 955

Partition may be requested even when one of the co-heirs has enjoyed separately all or part of the undivided property, if there has not been an act of partition, or sufficient possession to acquire prescription where it is permitted.

###### Article 956

If a minor, an adult under guardianship or curatorship, or a person presumed absent, is called to a partition, the partition may be made amicably.

In this case, the judge authorizes the partition, even partial, and appoints, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence as the case may be of the representative or curator of the person referred to in the preceding paragraph or, if that person is himself or herself interested in the partition, of his or her replacement appointed in accordance with article 143. The liquidation statement is submitted to the judge for approval.  
The partition may also be made in court in accordance with the provisions of articles 981 et seq. Failing compliance with these conditions, the amicable partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 957

One spouse may not, without the consent of the other, proceed with the partition of property devolving to the latter which falls into the community. Any partition which he or she carries out alone, with respect to such property, is valid only as a provisional partition.

###### Article 958

The co-owner in usufruct may request partition in kind of the undivided usufruct; if this partition in kind among the different usufructuaries is not possible, the usufruct may be sold.  
Where the sale of the usufruct alone cannot be envisaged under satisfactory conditions for the usufructuaries, the sale may relate to full ownership provided that it appears to be the only measure capable of preserving the interests of all holders of rights in the undivided property.

###### Article 959

The same option belongs to the co-owner in bare ownership for the undivided bare ownership. But in case of sale of full ownership, where the property is encumbered with usufruct, this may not operate against the will of the usufructuary.

###### Article 960

Where a person is in undivided ownership both of the usufruct and of the bare ownership, he or she has the options provided for in the two preceding articles. The contrary will of a usufructuary, if he or she requests the sale of the property in full ownership, may not be set against him or her.

###### Article 961

Where all parties agree on the partition, it is amicable; if one of the co-heirs refuses to consent to the partition, or if disputes arise either as to the manner of proceeding with it or as to the manner of completing it, the partition is judicial.

###### § 6. Preferential allocations Article 962

Except by decision or agreement to maintain undivided ownership, preferential allocation may be granted to the spouse or to any heir called to succeed by operation of law, whether he or she is a co-owner in full ownership or in bare ownership, under the conditions provided for by the following provisions.  
These provisions also benefit the heir having a universal or universal title vocation to the succession by virtue of a will or contractual institution.

###### Article 963

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation by way of partition, subject to an equalizing payment if applicable, of any enterprise, or part of an agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise or undivided share of such an enterprise, even formed in part from property of which he or she was already owner or co-owner before the death, in the operation of which he or she participates or has effectively participated. In the case of the heir, the condition

of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants.

If applicable, the application for preferential allocation may relate to company shares, without prejudice to the application of legal provisions or statutory clauses on the continuation of a company with the surviving spouse or one or more heirs.

###### Article 964

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may also request preferential allocation:
1° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises which effectively serve as his or her dwelling, if he or she had his or her residence there at the time of death, and of the furniture furnishing it, as well as of the deceased's vehicle provided that this vehicle is necessary for him or her for the needs of daily life. This preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;  
2° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises for professional use effectively serving for the exercise of his or her profession and of the movable objects for professional use furnishing these premises;  
3° Of the ownership of any agricultural holding whose size in area makes it a family holding. Preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;  
4° Of all the movable elements necessary for the operation of a rural property cultivated by the deceased in a professional capacity, where the lease continues for the benefit of the applicant, or where a new lease is granted to the latter.  
The rights resulting from preferential allocation do not prejudice the life rights of habitation and use, or enjoyment, which the spouse may exercise by virtue of law or contract.

###### Article 965

If maintenance in indivision has not been ordered and in the absence of preferential attribution in ownership, provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request the preferential attribution of all or part of the immovable property and rights with an agricultural purpose forming part of the succession with a view to constituting, with one or more co-heirs and, where applicable, one or more third parties, an agricultural land grouping.  
This attribution is of right if the surviving spouse or one or more of the co-heirs fulfilling the personal conditions provided for in articles 963 and 964, require that all or part of the property of the grouping be leased to them.  

In the event of multiple requests, the property of the grouping may, if its consistency permits, be the subject of several leases benefiting different co-heirs; otherwise, and in the absence of amicable agreement, the court designates the lessee taking into account the aptitude of the different applicants to manage the property concerned and to remain there. If the clauses and conditions of this lease or these leases have not been the subject of an agreement, they are fixed by the court.  
The immovable property and rights that the applicants do not envisage contributing to the agricultural land grouping, as well as the other property of the succession, are attributed by priority, within the limits of their respective succession rights, to the co-owners who have not consented to the formation of the grouping. If these co-owners are not satisfied with their rights by the attribution thus made, a balancing payment must be paid to them. Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the balancing payment possibly due is payable within the year following the partition. It may be the subject of a payment in kind in the form of shares of the agricultural land grouping, unless the interested parties, within the month following the proposal made to them, have made known their opposition to this method of settlement.  

The partition is only complete after the signature of the constitutive act of the agricultural land grouping and, if applicable, of the long-term lease or leases.

###### Article 966

If an agricultural holding constituting an economic unit and not operated in corporate form is not maintained in indivision and has not been the subject of a preferential attribution under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir who wishes to continue the holding in which he participates or has effectively participated may require, notwithstanding any request for sale by auction, that the partition be concluded on the condition that his co-partitioners grant him a long-term lease on the lands of the holding that fall to them. In the case of the heir, the condition of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his spouse or his descendants. Except by amicable agreement between the parties, the person who requests to benefit from these provisions receives by priority in his share the farm and residential buildings.  
The preceding provisions are applicable to a part of the agricultural holding that may constitute an economic unit. This economic unit may be formed, in part, of property of which the surviving spouse or the heir was already owner or co-owner before the death.  

Account is taken, if applicable, of the depreciation due to the existence of the lease in the valuation of the lands included in the different lots.  
If, by reason of the manifest inaptitude of the applicant or applicants to manage all or part of the holding, the interests of the co-heirs risk being compromised, the court may decide that there is no ground to apply the first three paragraphs of this article.

###### Article 967

In the absence of amicable agreement, the request for preferential attribution is brought before the court, which rules, except contrary provision, according to the interests involved.  
Preferential attribution may be requested jointly by several successors in order to preserve together the undivided property.  
In the event of multiple opposing requests concerning a holding or an enterprise, the court designates the attributee or joint attributees according to the interests involved and the aptitude of the different applicants to manage this holding or this enterprise and to remain there and in particular the duration of their personal participation in the activity of the holding or the enterprise.

###### Article 968

The property subject to the attribution is valued at its value on the day of partition.  

Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the balancing payment possibly due is payable in cash. However, when the attributee is the surviving spouse, he may require from his co-partitioners for the payment of a fraction of the balancing payment, equal at most to half, delays not exceeding ten years. Except contrary agreement, the sums remaining due bear interest at the legal rate.  

In the event of sale of the totality of the attributed property, the fraction of balancing payment remaining due becomes immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-partitioners and credited against the fraction of balancing payment still due.

###### Article 969

The beneficiary of the preferential attribution only becomes exclusive owner of the attributed property on the day of the final partition.  
Until that date, he may only renounce the attribution when the value of the property, as determined on the day of that attribution, has increased by more than one quarter on the day of partition independently of his personal act.

###### § 7. Of the constitution of shares and lots and of partition

A.	Common provisions

###### Article 970

The partitionable mass comprises the property existing at the opening of the succession, or those which have been subrogated to them, and of which the deceased has not disposed by reason of death, as well as the fruits relating thereto.  
It is increased by the values subject to return or to reduction, as well as by the debts of the co-partitioners towards the deceased or towards the indivision.

###### Article 971

The partition of undivided property is effected per capita. However, it is done per stirpes when there is ground for representation. Once the partition per stirpes is effected, within each stirpes, the partition is done, where applicable, per capita among the heirs of each stirpes.  
When a person dies, his heirs come to the succession of the person from whom he would have inherited if he had not died before him. The heirs come by representation of their author. Thus, grandchildren succeed to their grandparents by representation of their father or mother who predeceased. These heirs by representation constitute "a stirpes".

###### Article 972

When the debtor of a balancing payment has obtained payment delays, and when, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property placed in his lot has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion.  
The parties may however agree that the amount of the balancing payment will not vary.

###### Article 973

Any person, even related to the deceased, who is not his successor, and to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, may be excluded from the partition, either by all his co-heirs, or by one alone, by reimbursing him the price of the transfer.  
This faculty granted to the co-heirs or to one of them to exclude from the partition any non-successor person to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, also belongs to the undivided co-owner of an immovable, to the superficiary for the acquisition of the land, and to the owner of the land, for the acquisition of the superficies; any redemption without distinction must be exercised within a period of three months from the day when the sale was made public.

###### Article 974

In the formation and composition of lots for the purpose of partition, one must avoid fragmenting properties and dividing economic units and other sets of assets whose division would result in depreciation.

B.	Amicable partition

###### Article 975

Amicable partition may be total or partial. It is partial when it leaves co-ownership subsisting with respect to certain assets or certain persons.

###### Article 976

If all co-owners are present and capable, the partition may take place in the form and according to the procedures chosen by the parties.  
When the co-ownership relates to assets subject to land registration, the deed of partition is executed by notarial deed.

###### Article 977

If a co-owner is presumed absent or, due to distance, is unable to express his will, an amicable partition may take place under the conditions provided for in Article 146.  
Similarly, if a co-owner is subject to a protective regime, an amicable partition may take place in compliance with the provisions of the titles On Minority, Guardianship and Emancipation and On Majority and Adults Protected by Law.

###### Article 978

If a co-owner is in default, without nevertheless being in one of the cases provided for in the preceding article, he may, at the initiative of a co-partitioner, be formally notified, by extrajudicial act, to be represented at the amicable partition.  
If this co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, a co-partitioner may request the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to appoint any qualified person who will represent the defaulting party until the complete completion of the partition. This person may only consent to the partition with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 979

The co-owners compose the lots at their convenience, and agree on the distribution of the lots among themselves. Failing that, the lots once constituted shall be drawn by lot.  
Each lot must, as far as possible, be composed, either in whole or in part, of movables or immovables, rights or claims of equivalent value, subject to respect for the proportion of each person's rights in the co-ownership. In case of inequality of the lots constituted, this inequality is compensated, either by annuity or in money.  

Equality of all in the partition, understood as the rights that each holds proportionally in the co-ownership, is a rule of public policy.

###### Article 980

The co-owners freely proceed with valuations of the value of the undivided rights and assets.  

The assets are valued at their value on the date of divided enjoyment, taking into account, where applicable, the charges encumbering them. The determination of the day corresponding to the divided enjoyment of the assets by the co-owners is the subject of a special clause in the deed of partition.  

The date selected must be as close as possible to the partition. However, the judge may set the divided enjoyment at an earlier date if the choice of this date appears more favorable to the achievement of equality.  

C.	Judicial partition

###### Article 981

The partition is made in court when one of the co-owners refuses to consent to the amicable partition or if disputes arise over the manner of proceeding with it or completing it or when the amicable partition has not been authorized or approved in one of the cases provided for in Articles 977 and 978.  
In these cases, the affixing of seals on the effects of the estate carried out as soon as possible, either at the request of the heirs, or at the initiative of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance, or ex officio by the judge of the court within whose jurisdiction the estate is opened.

###### Article 982

Creditors may also request the affixing of seals, by virtue of an enforceable title or a permission from the judge.

###### Article 983

When the seal has been affixed, all creditors may form opposition to it, even if they have neither an enforceable title nor permission from the judge. The formalities for the removal of seals and the preparation of the inventory are governed by the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 984

The action for partition and the disputes that arise, either in connection with the maintenance of co-ownership or during partition operations, are submitted to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place where the estate is opened, which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear them. Any other judge must raise his lack of jurisdiction ex officio.  
It is before this court that sales by auction are conducted and that applications relating to the warranty of lots between co-partitioners and those for nullity of the partition or for additional share must be brought.

###### Article 985

If it considers that the settlement of the partition is simple, the court orders the partition; if it appears complex to it, it appoints, on the one hand, a notary to carry out the partition operations and, on the other hand and from within itself, a judge to supervise these operations.  
The notary certifies the property rights of each person, establishes the accounts of the co-ownership, forms the mass to be partitioned and constitutes the lots.  

If the appointed notary encounters the inertia of a co-owner, he formally notifies him, by extrajudicial act, to be represented. If the co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, the notary requests, without formality, the judge who appointed him to appoint any qualified person who will represent the defaulting party until the complete completion of the operations.

###### Article 986

A co-owner may request that certain assets be allocated to him preferentially. In case of opposition from another co-owner, the difficulty is resolved by the judge responsible for supervising the operations. This judge, for assets that cannot be easily partitioned or allocated, orders the sale by auction of said assets, under the conditions he determines.

###### Article 987

When the lots are constituted, each co-partitioner is admitted to submit his objections against their formation.  
When the objections are resolved or decided by the judge, the notary proposes to the co-partitioners to agree on the allocation of the lots. Failing that, a drawing by lot is conducted.

###### Article 988

At any time, the co-partitioners may abandon the judicial route to pursue the partition amicably if the conditions provided for a partition of this nature are met.

###### § 8. Judicial maintenance in co-ownership Article 989

At the request of a co-owner, the court may stay the partition for up to two years if its immediate completion risks harming the value of the undivided assets or if one of the co-owners cannot take over the agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise dependent on the

estate until the expiration of this period. This stay may apply to all of the undivided assets or to only some of them.  

If necessary, the request for stay of partition may relate to corporate rights.

###### Article 990

In the absence of amicable agreement, the judge may order the maintenance of co-ownership of any agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise, the operation of which was carried out by the deceased or by his spouse, as well as residential or professional premises actually used by the deceased or his spouse, and movable objects furnishing the residential premises or used in the exercise of the profession.  
If necessary, the request for maintenance of co-ownership may relate to corporate rights.

###### Article 991

In all these cases, where there are one or more minor descendants, the application may be made by the surviving spouse, by any heir or by the legal representative of the minor heirs; if there are no minor descendants, the action belongs to the surviving spouse alone.  
Two additional conditions then apply: the surviving spouse must have had the status of co-owner of the property in question, whether that status predated the death or was linked to it, and, in the case of residential premises, that surviving spouse must have been residing in the premises at the time of death.

###### Article 992

The court rules according to the interests at stake and the means of subsistence that the family can derive from the undivided property.  
It may order the maintenance of the undivided ownership for up to five years, renewable as the case may be until the death of the surviving spouse and until the youngest descendant reaches the age of majority.

###### Article 993

Where only one co-owner applies for partition, the court may, at the request of one or more of the co-owners who wish instead to remain in undivided ownership, according to the interests at stake and without prejudice to the application of articles 962 et seq. of this code, allocate after expert valuation his share to the person who applied for partition, either in kind if that share is easily detachable from the rest of the undivided property, or in value.  
If there is not a sufficient sum in the undivided estate, the balance is paid by those co-owners who joined in the application, without prejudice to the possibility for the other co-owners to participate, if they express their wish to do so. Each person's share in the undivided estate is increased in proportion to his payment.

##### Section II

Bringing into hotchpot, imputation and reduction of liberalities made to successors Article 994
Every heir, even having accepted the succession subject to an inventory, coming to a succession, must bring into hotchpot to his co-heirs everything he has received from the deceased, by inter vivos gifts, directly or indirectly; he may not retain gifts made to him by the deceased, unless they were expressly made to him in addition to his succession share.  

Legacies made to an heir are deemed to be made in addition to his succession share, unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, in which case the legatee may only claim his legacy by taking less.

###### Article 995

Gifts made in addition to the succession share may not be retained nor legacies claimed by the heir coming to partition except up to the amount of the disposable portion: the excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 996

The heir who renounces the succession may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer has expressly required bringing into hotchpot in case of renunciation.  
In that case, bringing into hotchpot is done in value. Where the value brought into hotchpot exceeds the rights he would have had in the partition had he participated in it, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs to the extent of that excess.

###### Article 997

The donee who was not a presumptive heir at the time of the gift, but who is found to be a successor on the day the succession opens, does not owe bringing into hotchpot, unless the donor has expressly required it.

###### Article 998

Gifts and legacies made to the son or daughter of a person who is found to be a successor at the time the succession opens are always deemed to be made with dispensation from bringing into hotchpot.  
The father or mother coming to the succession of the donor is not required to bring them into hotchpot.

###### Article 999

Similarly, the son or daughter coming in his own right to the succession of the donor is not required to bring into hotchpot the gift made to his father or mother, even if he has accepted the succession; but if that child comes only by representation, he must bring into hotchpot what had been given to his father or mother, even in the case where he has renounced his succession.

###### Article 1000

Gifts and legacies made to the spouse of a successor spouse are deemed to be made with dispensation from bringing into hotchpot.  

If the gifts and legacies are made jointly to two spouses, only one of whom is a successor, the latter brings into hotchpot half of them; if the gifts are made to the successor spouse, he brings them into hotchpot in their entirety.

###### Article 1001

Bringing into hotchpot is done only to the succession of the donor.

###### Article 1002

Bringing into hotchpot is owed for what has been used for the establishment of one of the co-heirs or for the payment of his debts.  
It is also owed in case of a gift of fruits or revenues, unless the liberality was made expressly in addition to the succession share.

###### Article 1003

Costs of food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary costs of equipment, wedding costs and customary presents, need not be brought into hotchpot, unless the disposer has expressed a contrary intention.  
The character of a customary present is assessed at the date it is granted and taking into account the fortune of the disposer.

###### Article 1004

The same applies to profits that the heir may have derived from agreements entered into with the deceased, if those agreements presented no indirect advantage when they were made.

###### Article 1005

Similarly, bringing into hotchpot is not owed for partnerships formed without fraud between the deceased and one of his heirs, where the conditions were settled by an authentic act.

###### Article 1006

Property that has perished by fortuitous event and without fault of the donee is not subject to bringing into hotchpot.  
However, if that property has been reconstituted by means of compensation received by reason of its loss, the donee must bring it into hotchpot in the proportion in which the compensation was used for its reconstitution.  

If the compensation has not been used for that purpose, it is itself subject to bringing into hotchpot.

###### Article 1007

The fruits of things subject to bringing into hotchpot are owed only from the day the succession opens. Interest is owed only from the day the amount to be brought into hotchpot is determined.

###### Article 1008

Bringing into hotchpot is owed only by a co-heir to his co-heir; it is not owed to legatees or to creditors of the succession.

###### Article 1009

Bringing into hotchpot is done by taking less, thus the donee retains the property received but takes, in return, less than the others in the mass to be partitioned in order to restore equality in figures, except in the case of the second paragraph of article 996.  
It may not be required in kind except by contrary stipulation in the deed of gift.  

In the case of such a stipulation, alienations and constitutions of real rights granted by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of bringing into hotchpot unless the donor has consented to them.

###### Article 1010

The heir also has the option of bringing into hotchpot in kind the gifted property that still belongs to him provided that that property is free of any charge or occupation with which it had not already been encumbered at the time of the gift.

###### Article 1011

Bringing into hotchpot is owed for the value of the gifted property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of the gift.  
If the property has been alienated before partition, account is taken of the value it had at the time of alienation. If new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, account is taken of the value of that new property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, no account is taken of the subrogation.  
All subject to contrary stipulation in the deed of gift.  

If it results from such a stipulation that the value subject to bringing into hotchpot is less than the determined value of the property, that difference forms an indirect advantage acquired by the donee in addition to his succession share.

###### Article 1012

The return of a sum of money is equal to its amount. However, if it has been used to acquire property, the return is due on the value of that property, under the conditions provided for in the preceding article.

###### Article 1013

When the return is made in kind and the condition of the donated objects has been improved by the act of the donee, account must be taken thereof, having regard to the amount by which their value is increased at the time of partition or alienation.  
Account must likewise be taken of the necessary expenses incurred by the donee for the preservation of the property, even though they have not improved it.

###### Article 1014

The co-heir who makes the return in kind may retain possession of the donated property until the effective reimbursement of the sums owed to him for expenses or improvements.

###### Article 1015

The donee, for his part, must, in the case of return in kind, account for the damage and deterioration which have diminished the value of the donated property by his act or by his fault.

##### Section III : Du paiement des dettes

###### § 1. Des dettes des copartageants Article 1016

When the divisible mass includes a claim against one of the co-partitioners, whether due or not, the latter is allotted it in the partition up to the amount of his rights in the mass.  

To the corresponding extent, the debt is extinguished by merger. If its amount exceeds the debtor's rights in that mass, he owes payment of the balance under the conditions and time limits which affected the obligation.

###### Article 1017

Except when it relates to undivided property, the claim is not due before the close of partition operations. However, the debtor heir may decide at any time to discharge it voluntarily.

###### Article 1018

Returnable sums bear interest at the legal rate, unless otherwise stipulated.  

Such interest runs from the opening of the succession when the heir was a debtor thereof to the deceased and from the day the debt becomes due, when it arose during the indivision.

###### Article 1019

When the co-partitioner himself has a claim to assert, he is allotted his debt only if, after balancing, the account shows a balance in favour of the undivided mass.

###### § 2. Des autres dettes Article 1020

The co-heirs contribute among themselves to the payment of the debts and charges of the succession, each in proportion to what he takes therein.

###### Article 1021

The legatee by general title contributes with the heirs, in proportion to his emolument; but the particular legatee is not liable for debts and charges, except however for the hypothecary action on the immovable bequeathed.

###### Article 1022

When immovables of a succession are encumbered with annuities by special hypothec, each of the co-heirs may require that the annuities be redeemed and the immovables rendered free before proceeding to the formation of lots.  
If the co-heirs divide the succession in the state in which it is found, the encumbered immovable must be valued at the same rate as the other immovables; deduction is made of the capital of the annuity from the total price; the heir in whose lot that immovable falls remains solely charged with the service of the annuity and he must guarantee his co-heirs therefor.

###### Article 1023

The heirs are liable for the debts and charges of the succession, personally for their successoral share, and hypothecarily for the whole; subject to their recourse either against their co-heirs or against the universal legatees, by reason of the share for which they must contribute thereto.

###### Article 1024

The particular legatee who has discharged the debt with which the bequeathed immovable was encumbered remains subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the heirs and successors by universal title.

###### Article 1025

The co-heir or successor by universal title who, by the effect of the hypothec, has paid beyond his share of the common debt, has recourse against the other co-heirs or successors by universal title only for the share which each of them must personally bear, even in the case where the co-heir who paid the debt has had himself subrogated to the rights of the creditors; without prejudice however to the rights of a co-heir who, by the effect of the benefit of inventory, has retained the power to claim payment of his personal claim, like any other creditor.

###### Article 1026

In case of insolvency of one of the co-heirs or successors by universal title, his share in the hypothecary debt is apportioned among all the others, proportionally.

###### Article 1027

Executory titles against the deceased are likewise executory against the heir personally, eight days after service of such titles has been made upon him.

###### Article 1028

The creditors of the deceased and the legatees of sums of money may demand to be preferred on the successoral assets over any personal creditor of the heir.  
Reciprocally, the personal creditors of the heir may demand to be preferred over any creditor of the deceased on the property of the heir not received by way of the succession.  

The right of preference gives rise to the privilege on immovables provided for in article 2354, and it is subject to registration.

###### Article 1029

This right of preference may be exercised by any act by which a creditor manifests to the competing creditor his intention to be preferred on a determined property.  
The right of preference may not be exercised when the claimant creditor has renounced it.

###### Article 1030

The right of preference is prescribed, in relation to movables, by the lapse of three years.  

With regard to immovables, the action may be exercised as long as they exist in the hands of the heir.

###### Article 1031

The creditors of a co-partitioner, to prevent the partition from being made in fraud of their rights, may oppose its being proceeded with outside their presence: they have the right to intervene therein at their expense; but they may not attack a completed partition, unless however it has been proceeded with without them and to the prejudice of an opposition which they have formed.

##### Section IV : Des effets du partage et de la garantie des lots Article 1032

Each co-indivisaire is deemed to have succeeded alone and immediately to all the effects included in his lot, or fallen to him on licitation, and never to have had ownership of the other effects of the succession.  
The same applies to property which has come to him by any other act having the effect of terminating the indivision. No distinction is made according to whether the act terminates the indivision in whole or in part, with regard to certain property or certain indivisaires only.  
However, acts validly performed either by virtue of a mandate from the co-indivisaires or by virtue of a judicial authorization retain their effects whatever may be, at the time of partition, the allocation of the property which was the subject thereof.

###### Article 1033

The co-indivisaires remain respectively guarantors, one towards the other, for disturbances and evictions only which proceed from a cause prior to the partition. They are also guarantors for the insolvency of the debtor of a debt placed in the lot of a co-partitioner, revealed before the partition.  
The guarantee does not apply if the kind of eviction suffered has been excepted by a particular and express clause of the partition deed; it ceases if it is by his fault that the co-indivisaire suffers the eviction.

###### Article 1034

Each of the co-indivisaires is personally obliged, in proportion to his emolument, to indemnify the evicted co-indivisaire for the loss he has suffered. This loss is valued at the day of eviction.  
If one of the co-indivisaires is found to be insolvent, the portion for which he is liable must be equally apportioned between the guaranteed party and all the solvent co-indivisaires.

###### Article 1035

The action for warranty is prescribed after two years from the eviction or the discovery of the disturbance.

##### Section V: Actions for nullity of partition or for additional share

###### § 1. Actions for nullity of partition Article 1036

Partition may be annulled on grounds of violence or fraud.  
It may also be annulled on grounds of error, if the error related to the existence or amount of the rights of the co-partitioners or to the ownership of property included in the partitionable mass.  

The action for nullity is prescribed after five years from the discovery of the defect or the cessation of the violence.  

However, if it appears that the consequences of the violence, fraud or error can be remedied otherwise than by annulment of the partition, the court may, at the request of one of the parties, order a supplementary or corrective partition.

###### Article 1037

Partition may also be annulled if one of the co-owners has been omitted.  

The omitted co-owner may however request to receive his share, either in kind or in value, without annulment of the partition.  
To determine this share, the property and rights that were the subject of the partition already carried out are revalued in the same manner as if it were a new partition.

###### Article 1038

The co-partitioner who has alienated his lot in whole or in part is no longer entitled to bring an action for nullity on grounds of error, fraud or violence, if the alienation he made is subsequent to the discovery of the error or fraud or to the cessation of the violence.

###### § 2. Action for additional share Article 1039

When one of the co-partitioners establishes, to his prejudice, a lesion of more than one quarter, the supplement to his share is provided to him, at the choice of the defendant, either in cash or in kind.  

To judge whether there has been lesion, the objects are valued according to their value at the time of partition, which corresponds to the date of divided enjoyment.  
The action for additional share is prescribed after two years from the partition.

###### Article 1040

The action for additional share is admitted against any act that has the purpose of terminating the co-ownership, regardless of the qualification that the parties may have given to that act.  
But after the partition, or the act that takes its place, the action for additional share is no longer admitted against the transaction made on the difficulties presented by that partition or that act.

###### Article 1041

The action is not admitted against a sale of succession rights made without fraud to a co-owner by his co-owners or by one of them, when the transfer includes a contingency defined in the act and expressly accepted by the transferee.

###### Article 1042

The simple omission of an object of the succession gives rise to a supplementary partition relating to that property.

### Title II: Inter vivos donations and wills

Chapter I: General provisions Article 1043
A liberality is an act by which a person disposes gratuitously of all or part of his property or his rights for the benefit of another person.  

A liberality may take the form only of these two categories of acts which are the inter vivos donation and the will.

###### Article 1044

The inter vivos donation is an act by which a person, the donor, transfers gratuitously to another person, the donee, who accepts it, the ownership of property.  
The donor may, without being deprived of his liberal intention, impose on the donee the obligation to perform a specified prestation; the act is then called a donation with charges.

###### Article 1045

The will is an act by which the testator disposes, for the time when he will no longer exist, of all or part of his property, in full ownership or in the form of any other real right. If it is not full ownership, the right transmitted is so only for the time provided in the act and in the absence of such provision, with regard to the legatee, the object of the legacy reverting, upon its extinction, to the succession of the testator.  
The will may be revoked by the testator, but the revocation is valid only insofar as it has been made by authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.  

The legacy may, after the death of the testator and at the latest two months after notification of the will to the legatee, be refused, totally or in part, by the latter or by his agent. The silence of the legatee during this period constitutes acceptance; if the legatee dies within this period, his heirs exercise the rights of their predecessor from the notification of the will made to them. The decision of the legatee is final, unless the heirs consent to his modifying it.

###### Article 1046

Any disposition by which a person is charged with preserving and returning to a third party produces effect only in the case where it is authorized by law.

###### Article 1047

The father and mother may impose on the child they gratify the charge of preserving and delivering the property received to his own children.  
A person without posterity may burden a liberality granted to his brothers or sisters with a charge requiring them to transmit the property received to their children and thus ensure the maintenance of the property in the family.  
However, clauses of inalienability affecting donated or bequeathed property are valid only if they are temporary and justified by a serious and legitimate interest. Even in this case, the donee or legatee may be judicially authorized to dispose of the property if the interest that had justified the clause has disappeared or if it happens that a more important interest requires it.  

The provisions of this article do not prejudice liberalities granted to legal persons or even to natural persons charged with constituting legal persons.  

Any clause by which the disposer deprives of the liberality the person who would challenge the validity of a clause of inalienability or request authorization to alienate is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1048

Any gratified person may request that the conditions and charges burdening the donations or legacies he has received be judicially revised, when, as a result of a change in circumstances, the execution thereof has become for him either extremely difficult or seriously harmful.  

The application for revision is made by principal action; it may also be made by counterclaim, in response to the action for performance or revocation that the heirs of the disposer have brought. It is made against the heirs and, at the same time, against the public prosecutor if there is doubt as to the existence or identity of some of them; if there is no known heir, it is made against the public prosecutor. The latter must, in all cases, have communication of the matter.  

The application is admissible only ten years after the death of the disposer or, in case of successive applications, ten years after the judgment that ordered the previous revision. The gratified person must justify the diligence he has made, in the interval, to perform his obligations.

###### Article 1049

The judge hearing the application for revision may, depending on the case and even of his own motion, either reduce in quantity or periodicity the prestations burdening the liberality, or modify the object thereof by drawing inspiration from the intention of the disposer, or even group them together with analogous prestations resulting from other liberalities.  

He may authorize the alienation of all or part of the property that is the object of the liberality by ordering that the price thereof be used for purposes related to the will of the disposer.  
He prescribes the measures appropriate to maintain, as far as possible, the designation that the disposer had intended to give to his liberality.

###### Article 1050

Third-party opposition to the judgment granting the application for revision is admissible only in case of fraud attributable to the donee or legatee.  
The retraction or reformation of the judgment challenged does not give rise to any action against a third-party purchaser in good faith.

###### Article 1051

If, subsequent to the revision, the performance of the conditions or charges, as originally provided, becomes possible again, it may be requested by the heirs.

###### Article 1052

The clause by which the grantor of a liberality designates a second-ranking beneficiary in the event that the beneficiary designated in the first instance has predeceased or, in case of survival, refuses the liberality, is authorized.  
The same applies to the inter vivos or testamentary disposition by which the usufruct will be given to one person and the bare ownership to another.

###### Article 1053

In any inter vivos or testamentary disposition, impossible conditions, those which are contrary to law or to morals, shall be deemed unwritten.  
If the thing bequeathed perishes before the death of the grantor, or if it is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, nothing is owed to the donee or legatee. If only part of the thing bequeathed perishes or is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, the donee or legatee receives the remainder.

#### Chapitre II

De la capacité de disposer ou de recevoir par donation entre vifs ou par testament Article 1054
Any person may dispose of and receive property, either by inter vivos donation or by will, except for persons whom the law declares incapable. The grantor of such a liberality must be of sound mind. If

the donation or will was made while consent was vitiated by error, fraud or duress, the act is null.  

A donation as well as a will made in favor of a foreigner is valid subject to the legal provisions in force.

###### Article 1055

A will made by a minor is valid, provided it is approved by the judge.

###### Article 1056

To be capable of receiving inter vivos, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the donation.  

To be capable of receiving by will, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the testator's death.  

Nevertheless, the donation or will shall have effect only insofar as the child is born viable.  

When the testator dies before the delivery of the child already conceived at the date of the will and in whose favor the will was made, from the death of the testator until the delivery, the fruits shall be subject to conservatory measures.

###### Article 1057

A minor may not, even by will, dispose of property in favor of his guardian.  

A minor, having reached majority or been emancipated, may not dispose of property, either by inter vivos donation or by will, in favor of the person who was his guardian, if the final account of the guardianship has not been previously rendered and settled.  
Excepted, in the two cases above, are the ascendants of minors, who are or who have been their guardians.

###### Article 1058

Members of the medical and pharmaceutical professions, as well as medical auxiliaries who have provided care to a person during the illness from which he dies, may not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that he may have made in their favor during the course of that illness.  
Judicial representatives for the protection of adults and the legal persons on whose behalf they exercise their functions may not similarly benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that the persons whose protection they ensure may have made in their favor regardless of the date of the liberality.  

Excepted are:
1° Remunerative dispositions made on a particular basis, having regard to the means of the grantor and the services rendered;  
2° Universal dispositions, in the case of relationship up to and including the fourth degree, provided however that the deceased has no heirs in the direct line; unless the person in whose favor the disposition was made is himself among those heirs.  
The same rules shall be observed with regard to the minister of religion.

###### Article 1059

Inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of health establishments, medical-social establishments, or public utility establishments shall have effect only insofar as they have been authorized by decree.  

However, inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of foundations, places dedicated to worship and legally constituted associations and associations, are freely accepted by them. If it concerns religious establishments, the liberality is valid even if the grantor and the person receiving the property are not of the same faith.

###### Article 1060

Any disposition in favor of a person, natural or legal, subject to an incapacity to receive gratuitously, whether it is disguised in the form of an onerous contract, or whether it is made in the name of interposed persons, is sanctioned by absolute nullity.  
Shall be deemed interposed persons, until proof to the contrary, the father and mother, the children and descendants, as well as the spouse of the incapable person.

#### Chapitre III

De la réserve héréditaire, de la quotité disponible, et de la réduction Section I: De la réserve héréditaire et de la quotité disponible

###### Article 1061

The hereditary reserve is the share of property and succession rights of which the law ensures the devolution free of charges to certain heirs called reserve heirs, if they are called to the succession and if they accept it.  
The beneficiaries of the reserve are:	the descendants of the deceased, that is: children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren;	in the absence of descendants, the ascendants of the deceased, that is: father and mother, grandparents, great-grandparents;	the surviving spouse, in the absence of descendants and ascendants.  

The disposable portion is the share of property and succession rights which is not reserved by law and of which the deceased was able to dispose freely by liberalities.

###### Article 1062

Liberalities, whether by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed one-half of the grantor's property, if he leaves at his death only one child; one-third, if he leaves two children; one-quarter, if he leaves three or a greater number;  
The child who renounces the succession is included in the number of children left by the deceased only if he is represented or if he is bound to account for a liberality in application of the provisions of article 900.

###### Article 1063

Included in article 1062, under the name of children, are descendants in whatever degree, even though they should be counted only for the child whose place they take in the succession of the grantor.

###### Article 1064

Liberalities, by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed three-quarters of the property if, in the absence of descendants, the deceased leaves a surviving spouse, not divorced.

###### Article 1065

In the absence of a surviving spouse and heirs, liberalities by inter vivos or testamentary acts may exhaust the entirety of the property.

###### Article 1066

If the liberality consists of a usufruct or a life annuity whose value exceeds the disposable portion, the heirs in whose favor the law makes a reserve shall have the option either to execute this disposition or to make the abandonment of the ownership of the disposable portion.

##### Section II: Reduction of Excessive Liberalities Article 1067

The value in full ownership of property alienated, whether subject to a life annuity, as a capital loss, or with reservation of usufruct to one of the successors in direct line, is charged against the available portion. Such acts are irrefutably requalified as liberalities outside the hereditary share.  
Any excess is brought back to the estate and therefore gives rise to reduction of the excessive liberality. This charging and this reduction may only be requested by those other successors in direct line who have not consented to these alienations.

###### Article 1068

The available portion may be given in whole or in part either by act inter vivos or by will, to the children or other successors of the donor, without being subject to collation by the donee or legatee coming to the succession, provided that with respect to donations the disposition has been expressly made outside the hereditary share.  
The declaration that the donation is outside the hereditary share may be made either by the act containing the disposition or subsequently, in the form of dispositions inter vivos or testamentary.

###### Article 1069

Liberalities made as an advancement on the hereditary share to a forced heir who accepts the succession are charged against his share of the reserve and, subsidiarily, against the available portion, unless otherwise agreed in the act providing for them. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1070

Liberalities made as an advancement on the hereditary share to a forced heir who renounces the succession are treated as a liberality made outside the hereditary share.  
However, when he is bound to collation pursuant to the provisions of Article 900, the heir who renounces is treated as an accepting heir for the notional reunion of all the property of the deceased, the charging and, where applicable, the reduction of the liberality granted to him. This principle is derogated from for: premiums of a life insurance policy taken out for the benefit of a specified third party, unless they prove to be manifestly excessive in relation to the means of the insured or the transaction was merely a pure investment; expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, which need not be brought into collation unless the disposer wills otherwise, in accordance with Article 1003; fruits and income accrued between the day of the donation and the death, in accordance with Article 1081.

###### Article 1071

The liberality made outside the hereditary share is charged against the available portion. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1072

The liberality made to a successor, or to successors jointly, which exceeds the available portion, may be retained in full by the beneficiaries, whatever the excess, subject to compensating the coheirs in money.  
When the reducible portion does not exceed the reserve share of the person concerned, he may always claim all the bequeathed objects and therefore execute the reduction in kind when the donated or bequeathed property still belongs to him and is free of any charge with which it had not already been encumbered at the date of the liberality, as well as any occupation to which it had not already been subject at that same date. This option expires if he does not express his choice for this method of reduction within three months from the date on which a forced heir served him with formal notice to take a position.

###### Article 1073

When the value of donations inter vivos exceeds or equals the available portion, all testamentary dispositions shall lapse.

###### Article 1074

The reduction compensation is calculated, in all cases, according to the value of the objects at the time of partition or alienation by the beneficiary and according to their condition on the day the liberality took effect. If there has been subrogation, the calculation of the reduction compensation takes into account the value of the new property at the time of partition, according to their condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the

new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.  

The reduction compensation is payable at the time of partition, subject to agreement between the coheirs. However, when the liberality has as its object one of the properties that may be the subject of a preferential allocation, time periods may be granted by the court, taking into account the interests involved, if they have not been granted by the disposer. The granting of these time periods may not, in any case, have the effect of deferring payment of the compensation beyond ten years from the opening of the succession. The provisions of Article 972 are then applicable to payment of the sums due.  
In the absence of a contrary agreement or stipulation, these sums bear interest at the legal rate in civil matters. The advantages resulting from the time periods and payment terms granted do not constitute a liberality.  

In case of sale of all of the donated or bequeathed property, the sums remaining due become immediately payable; in case of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the coheirs and charged against the sums still due.

###### Article 1075

Liberalities, direct or indirect, which exceed the available portion, are reducible to that portion upon the opening of the succession.

###### Article 1076

The reduction of dispositions inter vivos may only be requested by those for whose benefit the law makes the reserve, by their heirs or successors in title.  
Donees, legatees, and creditors of the deceased may not request this reduction or benefit from it.  
The limitation period for the action for reduction is set at five years from the opening of the succession, or two years from the day the heirs became aware of the infringement of their reserve, without ever being able to exceed ten years from the death.

###### Article 1077

The reduction is determined by forming an estate of all property existing at the death of the donor or testator.  
There are notionally reunited to it, after deducting debts, those of which disposition has been made by donation inter vivos according to their condition at the time of the donation and their value at the opening of the succession. If the property has been alienated, account is taken of its value at the time of alienation and, if there has been subrogation, of the value of the new property on the day of the opening of the succession according to their condition at the time of acquisition; however, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.  
There is calculated on all this property, having regard to the quality of heirs he leaves, what is the portion of which the deceased was able to dispose.

###### Article 1078

The reduction of donations inter vivos presupposes that the value of all property included in the testamentary dispositions has previously been determined. Once the reunion of property has been accomplished, the reduction is effected beginning with the last donation, and so on going back from the last to the earliest.

###### Article 1079

When the testamentary dispositions exceed either the available portion or the part of that portion which would remain after deducting the value of donations inter vivos, the reduction shall be made proportionally, without any distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies.

###### Article 1080

Nevertheless, in all cases where the testator has expressly declared that he intends a particular legacy to be satisfied in preference to others, this preference shall take effect; and the legacy which is the subject thereof shall be reduced only to the extent that the value of the others would not fulfill the legal reserve.

###### Article 1081

When reduction is carried out in kind, the donee shall restore the fruits of that which exceeds the available portion, from the day of the donor's death if the claim for reduction was made within the year; otherwise from the day of the claim.

###### Article 1082

Real rights created by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of the reduction. These rights shall nevertheless retain their effects when the donor has consented thereto in the very act of creation or in a subsequent act. The donee shall then be liable for the resulting depreciation.

###### Article 1083

The action for reduction or revendication may be exercised by the heirs against third-party holders of immovable property forming part of donations and alienated by the donees, in the same manner and in the same order as against the donees themselves, and after prior discussion of their property. This action must be exercised according to the order of dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent.  
When the donor has consented to the alienation with the agreement of all reserve heirs born and living at the time thereof, the action may no longer be exercised against third-party holders.

###### Article 1084

After prior discussion of the property of the debtor of the reduction indemnity and in case of insolvency of the latter, the reserve heirs may exercise the action for reduction or revendication against third-party holders of immovable property forming part of liberalities and alienated by the gratified party. The action is exercised in the same manner as against the gratified parties themselves and according to the order of dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. It may be exercised against third-party holders of movables when article 2276 (number to be added when file No. 15 is numbered) cannot be invoked.  
When, on the day of the donation or subsequently, the donor and all presumptive reserve heirs have consented to the alienation of the donated property, no reserve heir, even born after the consent of all interested heirs has been obtained, may exercise the action against third-party holders. With regard to bequeathed property, this action may no longer be exercised when the reserve heirs have consented to the alienation.

###### Article 1085

Any presumptive reserve heir may renounce, totally or partially, for example targeting only the reduction of a liberality relating to a specific property, the exercise of an action for reduction in an unopened succession, in favor of one or more specified persons. The renunciation binds the renouncer only from the day it has been accepted by the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit; but it cannot create obligations chargeable to the person from whom one has a vocation to inherit or be conditioned upon an act emanating from the latter.

###### Article 1086

The act of renunciation is, on pain of nullity, established by specific authentic act received by two notaries and precisely mentions its future legal consequences for the renouncer. The renunciation may be made in the same act by several reserve heirs, but they then sign separately before the notaries who receive the act.  

The capacity required of the renouncer is that required to consent to an inter vivos donation. However, the emancipated minor may not renounce in advance the action for reduction.  
The renunciation, whatever its modalities, does not constitute a liberality. It is opposable to the representatives of the renouncer.

###### Article 1087

The renunciation produces no effect if the hereditary reserve of the renouncer has not been infringed. If the infringement of the hereditary reserve has been exercised only partially, the renunciation produces effects only up to the amount of the infringement of the renouncer's reserve resulting from the liberality granted. If the infringement of the reserve relates to a fraction greater than that provided for in the renunciation, the excess is subject to reduction.  
The renunciation relating to the reduction of a liberality relating to a specific property lapses if the liberality infringing the reserve does not relate to that property. The same applies if the liberality has not been made in favor of the specified person or persons.

###### Article 1088

The renouncer has the possibility to revoke his renunciation, but only in the following cases: 1° When the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit does not fulfill his maintenance obligations toward him;  
2° When on the day of the opening of the succession, he is in a state of need which would disappear if he had not renounced his reserve rights;  
3° When the beneficiary of the renunciation has been guilty of a crime or offense against his person.

###### Article1089

In case of dispute, the renouncer seizes the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within one year from the day of the opening of the succession when the revocation is based on point 2° of the preceding article, and within one year from the act imputed by the renouncer or from the day when the act could have been known by his heirs, if it is based on point 2° or 3° of the preceding article.  
Revocation pursuant to 2° of the preceding article is pronounced only to the extent of the needs of the person who had renounced.

#### Chapter IV: Inter vivos donations

##### Section I: Conditions and effects of inter vivos donations Article 1090

To be valid, any donation must be executed by authentic act.  

In case of defect of form, an inter vivos donation cannot be the subject of confirmation: it must be remade in legal form.  
After the death of the donor, confirmation or voluntary execution of a donation by the heirs or successors in title of the donor entails their renunciation to oppose defects of form or any other cause of nullity.

###### Article 1091

An inter vivos donation shall not bind the donor, and shall produce no effect, except from the day it has been accepted in express terms.  

Acceptance may be made during the donor's lifetime by a subsequent and authentic act, of which a minute shall remain; but then the donation shall have effect, with regard to the donor, only from the day when the act evidencing this acceptance has been notified to him.

###### Article 1092

If the donee is of age, acceptance must be made by him or, in his name, by a representative endowed with express power to accept the donation made, or with general power to accept donations which have been or might be made.  
This power of attorney must be executed before a notary; and a copy must be annexed to the minute of the donation or to the minute of the acceptance which would be made by separate act.

###### Article 1093

A donation made to an unemancipated minor or to an adult under guardianship must be accepted by his guardian, in accordance with article 600, under the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.  
Nevertheless, the father and mother of the unemancipated minor, or other ascendants, even during the lifetime of the father and mother, although they are not guardians of the minor, may accept on his behalf.

###### Article 1094

A deaf-mute who can write may accept himself or through a representative.  

If he cannot write, acceptance must be made by a curator appointed for this purpose, according to the rules established under the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 1095
