Donations made for the benefit of the institutions referred to in Article 1059 shall be accepted by the administrators of those institutions, after having been duly authorized.  
A donation made by a terminally ill patient is deemed to be a legacy.

###### Article 1096

A donation duly accepted shall be perfected by the mere consent of the parties; and ownership of the donated objects shall be transferred to the donee, without any other delivery being necessary.  
If delivery of the donated thing has not taken place, the donee has the right to require it.

###### Article 1097

Where there is a donation of property capable of being mortgaged, publication of the instruments containing the donation and acceptance, as well as notification of acceptance that may have taken place by separate instrument, must be made at the mortgage registry of the place where the property is situated.  
Where the donation is made to minors, adults under guardianship, or public institutions, publication shall be carried out at the instance of the guardians, curators or administrators.

###### Article 1098

Failure to publish may be raised by all persons having an interest, except however those who are responsible for having publication made, or their successors in title, and the donor.

###### Article 1099

Minors and adults under guardianship may not request that the effects of failure to accept or publish donations not operate against them, even though the said guardians are found to be insolvent. Minors and adults under guardianship may however obtain compensation; against their guardians, at least if the latter's abstention has caused them prejudice.

###### Article 1100

A donation inter vivos may comprise only the present property of the donor; if it comprises future property, it is null and void in that respect.

###### Article 1101

Any donation inter vivos made subject to conditions the performance of which depends on the sole will of the donor is null and void.  
The same applies to a donation made subject to the condition of discharging debts or charges other than those existing at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1102

Where the donor has reserved the freedom to dispose of property included in the donation or of a fixed sum from the donated property, if he dies without having so disposed, the said property or the said sum belongs to the heirs of the donor, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary.

###### Article 1103

The three preceding articles do not apply to donations mentioned in Chapters VIII and IX of this Title.

###### Article 1104

Any instrument of donation of movable property shall be valid only for property of which an estimated statement, signed by the donor and the donee, or by those accepting on his behalf, has been annexed to the original of the donation.

###### Article 1105

The donor is permitted to reserve for his own benefit or to dispose of, for the benefit of another, the enjoyment or usufruct of the movable or immovable property donated.

###### Article 1106

Where the donation of movable property is made with reservation of usufruct, the donee shall be required, upon expiry of the usufruct, to take the donated property that is found in kind, in the state in which it is; and he shall have an action against the donor or his heirs, in respect of non-existent objects, up to the value assigned to them in the estimated statement.

###### Article 1107

The donor may stipulate the right of return of the donated objects either for the case of predeceasing of the donee alone, or for the case of predeceasing of the donee and his descendants.  
This right may be stipulated only for the benefit of the donor alone.

###### Article 1108

The effect of the right of return is to resolve all alienations of the donated property, and to cause that property to revert to the donor, free of all charges and mortgages, except however the mortgage of spouses, if the other property of the donee spouse is insufficient, and only in the case where the donation was made to him by the same marriage contract from which those charges and mortgages result.

###### Article 1109

The donor warrants eviction only if he has intentionally concealed the cause of eviction or if the donation was made with charges. In the first case, the donee shall be awarded fair compensation for the prejudice he has suffered; in the second case, the donor is liable only up to the value of the charges performed by the donee, all subject to any agreement to the contrary.  
In case of eviction, the donee is subrogated to the rights and actions of the donor.

###### Article 1110

The donor does not warrant defects in the donated thing.  
However, if the donor has intentionally concealed the defect or if he has warranted its non-existence, he shall owe the donee reparation for the damage thereby caused. He shall also be liable for damages if the donation is made with charges, provided that the amount of damages does not exceed, in that case, the value of the charges performed by the donee.

##### Section II

Exceptions to the rule of irrevocability of donations inter vivos Article 1111
A donation inter vivos may be revoked only for failure to perform the conditions under which it was made, for ingratitude, and for supervening birth of children.

###### Article 1112

In the case of revocation for failure to perform conditions, the property shall return to the hands of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on the part of the donee; and the donor shall have, against third party holders of the donated immovables, all the rights he would have against the donee himself.

###### Article 1113

A donation inter vivos may be revoked for ingratitude only in the following cases: 1° If the donee has made an attempt on the life of the donor;  
2° If he has been guilty towards him of abuse, offences or serious insults; 3° If he refuses him maintenance.

###### Article 1114

Revocation for failure to perform conditions, or for ingratitude, shall never take place by operation of law.

###### Article 1115

An application for revocation for ingratitude must be made within one year, from the day of the offence imputed by the donor to the donee or from the day the offence could have been known by the donor.  
This revocation may not be sought by the donor against the heirs of the donee, nor by the heirs of the donor against the donee, unless, in the latter case, the action was instituted by the donor, or he died within the year of the offence.

###### Article 1116

Revocation for ingratitude does not prejudice either the alienations made by the donee, or the mortgages and other real charges he may have imposed on the object of the donation, provided that all are prior to publication, at the mortgage registry of the location of the property, of the application for revocation.  
In the case of revocation, the donee is ordered to restore the value of the alienated objects, having regard to the time of the application, and the fruits, from the day of that application.

###### Article 1117

Donations in consideration of marriage are not revocable for ingratitude.

###### Article 1118

All donations inter vivos made by persons who had no children or descendants actually living at the time of the donation, of whatever value those donations may be, and under whatever title they were made, and even though they were mutual or remuneratory, even those made in consideration of marriage by persons other than the spouses to each other, may be revoked, if the instrument of donation so provides, by the supervening birth of a child born to the donor, even after his death, or adopted by him in the forms and conditions provided for in Chapter I of Title IX of Book I.

###### Article 1119

This revocation may take place even though the child of the donor, male or female, was conceived at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1120

The donation may likewise be revoked even if the donee has entered into possession of the donated property, and has been left therein by the donor since the birth of the child. However, the donee is not required to restore the fruits he has received, of whatever nature they may be, except from the day on which the birth of the child or his adoption in plenary form was notified to him by writ or other act in due form, even if the claim to recover the donated property was made after such notification.

###### Article 1121

The property included in the revoked donation returns to the patrimony of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on behalf of the donee, without being able to remain subject, even subsidiarily, to the mortgage of the spouses; this shall apply even when the donation was made in favor of the donee's marriage and inserted in the contract, and the donor bound himself as surety, by the donation, for the performance of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1122

The death of the donor's child has no effect on the revocation of donations provided for in Article 1118.

The donor may renounce the exercise of revocation for birth of a child, at any time, that is to say before or after the birth of the child.

###### Article 1123

The action for revocation is barred after five years from the birth or adoption of the last child.  
It may be exercised only by the donor.

#### Chapitre V

Testamentary dispositions Section I: General rules

###### Article 1124

Any person may dispose by will, whether under the title of institution of heir, or under the title of legacy, or under any other designation appropriate to manifest his will.

###### Article 1125

A will may not be made in the same act by two or more persons, whether for the benefit of a third party or as a reciprocal or mutual disposition.

###### Article 1126

To be valid, the will must be made by an authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

###### Article 1127

The will by authentic act is received either by two notaries, or by one notary assisted by two witnesses who may not be legatees, in whatever capacity, nor their relatives or in-laws up to and including the fourth degree, nor the clerks of the notaries by whom the acts are received.  
In both circumstances, the will is dictated by the testator and, as the case may be, one of the two notaries or the notary writes it himself or has it written by hand or mechanically.  
It is then obligatorily read to the testator.  
When the testator cannot express himself in French or Arabic, the dictation and reading may be accomplished by an interpreter whom the testator chooses from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The interpreter ensures the exact translation of the statements made. The notary is not required to use an interpreter when he himself as well as, as the case may be, the other notary or the witnesses understand the language in which the testator expresses himself.  

When the testator can write in French or Arabic but cannot speak, the notary writes the will himself or has it written by hand or mechanically from notes drafted before him by the testator, then reads it to the latter. When the testator cannot hear, he takes cognizance of the will by reading it himself, after reading by the notary. When the testator can neither speak or hear, nor read or write, the dictation or reading are accomplished, when possible, through a sign language interpreter and according to the same procedures.  

The act expressly mentions compliance with the above-mentioned requirements.

###### Article 1128

This will by authentic act must be signed by the testator in the presence, as the case may be, of the witnesses and the notary or the two notaries; if the testator declares that he does not know how or cannot sign, the act bears his fingerprint.  
It is also signed, as the case may be, by the witnesses and by the notary or the two notaries.

###### Article 1129

The mystic will is the will whose content remains hidden until the death of the person. When the testator wishes to make a mystic will, the paper containing the dispositions or the paper serving as an envelope, if there is one, is delivered closed, sealed and stamped, either to a notary before two witnesses, or to two notaries, or closed, sealed and stamped in their presence. The testator then declares that the content of this paper is his will, signed by him, and written by him or by another, affirming, in the latter case, that he has personally verified the wording. He indicates, in all cases, the mode of writing he has employed (by hand or mechanical).  
As the case may be, the notary or the notaries write or have written by hand or mechanically on this paper or on the sheet that will serve as an envelope intended to contain it, the date and indication of the place where the mystic will is executed, the description of the fold and the impression of the seal, and mention of all the above formalities; this act is signed both by the testator and by the notary and the witnesses, or by the two notaries. If the testator, either by an impediment arising since the signing of the will, or because he does not know how to sign, has not been able to sign this act, mention is made thereof as well as of the reason he has given for it.  

All of these operations must be carried out in one continuous process and without interruption.

###### Article 1130

Those who do not know how or cannot read may not make dispositions in the form of a mystic will.  
On the other hand, the testator who cannot speak but who knows how to write may make a mystic will, on the express condition that the will be signed by him and written by him or by another, that he present it to the notary and the witnesses, or to the two notaries, and that at the top of the act of superscription he write, in their presence, that the paper he presents is his will, this before signing the act. As the case may be, the notary or the notaries write on this act that the testator wrote and signed these words in his presence and that of the witnesses, or in their presence. The provisions of Article 1129, except those contrary to this article, are applicable.  

In all cases provided for in this article or in the preceding articles, the mystic will in which the legal formalities have not been observed, and which will be null as such, shall nevertheless be valid as a holographic will if all the conditions required for its validity as a holographic will are fulfilled, even if it has been qualified as a mystic will.

###### Article 1131

The witnesses called to be present at wills must be Djiboutian and of age, know how to sign and have the enjoyment of their civil rights. They may be of either sex, but husband and wife may not be witnesses in the same act.

###### Article 1132

The wills of military personnel, naval personnel of the State and persons employed with the armies may be received in the cases and conditions provided for in Article 125 in one of the following forms:
1° by a senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, in the presence of two witnesses;  
2° by two officials of the intendancy or commissariat officers or by one of these officials or officers in the presence of two witnesses;  
3° in the case of an isolated detachment and if there is no senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, intendancy official or commissariat officer in that detachment, by the officer commanding that detachment assisted by two witnesses;  
4° if the testator is sick or wounded and is staying in a military hospital or medical unit, by the chief medical officer, whatever his rank, assisted by the administrative management officer. In the absence of that administrative officer, the presence of two witnesses is necessary.  
The will of the officer commanding an isolated detachment may be received by the officer who comes after him in the order of service.  

The power to make a will under the conditions provided for in this article extends to prisoners with the enemy.  
In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus drawn up shall be made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will shall be drawn up to serve in place of the second original; this copy shall be signed by the witnesses and by the instrumentary officers. Mention shall be made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original.  

As soon as communication is possible, and within the shortest possible time, the two originals or the original and the copy of the will shall be sent, separately and by different couriers, under sealed and closed cover, to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of an indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.  

The will made in the form established above shall be null and void by operation of law six months after the testator has arrived in a place where he has the freedom to employ the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of that period, he has again been placed in one of the special situations provided for in Article 125. The will shall then be valid for the duration of that special situation and for a further period of six months after its expiration.  

All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1133

During a maritime voyage, both en route and during a stop in a port, when there is impossibility of communicating with land or when there is no Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent invested with the functions of notary in the port, if one is abroad, the wills of persons present on board shall be received, in the presence of two witnesses:
1° on State vessels, by the administrative officer or, in his absence, by the commander or the person performing his functions. The will of the administrative officer shall be received by the commander or by the person performing his functions, and, if there is no administrative officer, the will of the commander shall be received by the person who comes after him in the order of service;  
2° on other vessels, by the captain, master or skipper, assisted by the ship's mate, or, in their absence, by those who replace them. The will of the captain, master or skipper, or that of the mate, shall be received by the persons who come after them in the order of service.  
The instrument shall indicate which of the circumstances provided for above it is received in.  

In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus drawn up shall be made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will shall be drawn up to serve in place of the second original; this copy shall be signed by the witnesses and by the instrumentary officers. Mention shall be made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original.  

At the first stop in a foreign port where there is a Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent, one of the originals or the copy of the will shall be delivered, under sealed and closed cover, into the hands of that official, who shall send it to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of an indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.  
And, upon the arrival of the vessel in a port of Djibouti, the two originals of the will or the original and its copy, or the original that remains, in the event of transmission or delivery effected during the course of the voyage, shall be deposited, under sealed and closed cover, for State vessels, at the armaments office, and for other vessels at the maritime registration office. Each of these documents shall be sent, separately and by different couriers, to the Minister of Defence, who shall transmit them as stated in the preceding paragraph.  

The will made during a maritime voyage, in the form prescribed by Article 1132, shall be valid only insofar as the testator dies on board or within six months after he has disembarked in a place where he was able to remake it in the ordinary forms. However, if the testator undertakes a new maritime voyage before the expiration of that period, the will shall be valid for the duration of that voyage and for a further period of six months after the testator has again disembarked.  
All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1134

Provisions inserted in a will made, during a maritime voyage, for the benefit of officers of the vessel other than those who are relatives or relations by marriage of the testator, shall be null and void.

###### Article 1135

The testator, in the cases of Articles 1132 and 1133, shall be informed, in the presence of the witnesses, that his will shall be null and void by operation of law six months after he has arrived in a place where he has the freedom

to employ the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of that period, he is again placed in a situation that falls under the said articles.

###### Article 1136

On pain of nullity, wills must be signed by the testator, by those who have received them and by the witnesses.  
If the testator declares that he cannot or does not know how to sign, mention shall be made of his declaration, as well as of the cause which prevents him from signing.  
In the case where the presence of two witnesses is required, the will shall be signed by at least one of them, and mention shall be made of the reason why the other has not signed.

###### Article 1137

A Djiboutian who is in a foreign country may make his testamentary dispositions by private written instrument or by authentic instrument, with the forms customary in the place where that instrument is executed.  
Such wills made in a foreign country may be executed on property situated in Djibouti only after having been registered at the office of the domicile of the testator, if he has retained one, otherwise at the office of his last known domicile in Djibouti. In the case where the will contains dispositions of immovable property situated there, it must, in addition, be registered at the office of the location of that immovable property, without a double duty being able to be required.

##### Section II: Institutions of heirs and legacies in general Article 1138

Testamentary dispositions are either universal, or by universal title, or by particular title.  

Each of these dispositions shall produce its effect according to the rules established hereinafter for universal legacies, for legacies by universal title, and for particular legacies.

###### Article 1139

Unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, where the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law, the legatee may limit his emolument to a portion of the property disposed of in his favour. This limitation does not constitute a liberality made by the legatee to the other successors.  
Unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, any person gratified with a legacy may decide to receive only a portion of the property provided, on condition that the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law. This decision of the legatee is not considered as a liberality from the legatee to the other successors.

###### Sous-section 1 : Du legs universel Article 1140

A universal legacy is the testamentary disposition by which the testator gives to one or more persons the universality of the property he will leave at his death.

###### Article 1141

Where at the death of the testator there are heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, these heirs are seized by operation of law, upon his death, of all the property of the succession; and the universal legatee is required to request from them the delivery of the property included in the will.  

Nevertheless, in the same cases, the universal legatee shall have the enjoyment of the property included in the will, from the day of death, if the request for delivery was made within one year from that time; otherwise, such enjoyment shall commence only from the day of the request made in court, or from the day that delivery was voluntarily consented to.

###### Article 1142

Where at the death of the testator there are no heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, the universal legatee shall be seized by operation of law upon the death of the testator. If the will was executed by authentic act, he is not required to request delivery by an order of possession; in the contrary case, the legatee is required to obtain an order of possession, by an order of the president, placed at the bottom of a petition, to which is attached the act of deposit.

###### Article 1143

Every will under private signature is, before being executed, deposited with a notary. The will is opened if it is sealed. The notary immediately draws up a report of the opening and the state of the will, specifying the circumstances of the deposit. The will as well as the report are preserved among the minutes of the depositary.  
Within one month following the date of the report, the notary sends a copy thereof and a facsimile copy of the will to the clerk of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession, who acknowledges receipt of these documents and preserves them among his minutes.

###### Article 1144

The universal legatee, who is in concurrence with an heir to whom the law reserves a portion of the property, is liable for the debts and charges of the succession of the testator, personally for his share and portion and by mortgage for the whole; and he is required to discharge all legacies, except in case of reduction, as explained in articles 1079 and 1080.

###### Sous-section 2 : Du legs à titre universel Article 1145

A legacy by universal title is that by which the testator bequeaths a share of the property which the law permits him to dispose of, for example, one half, one third, or all his immovable property, or all his movable property, or a fixed portion of all his immovable property or of all his movable property.  

Any other legacy constitutes only a disposition by particular title.

###### Article 1146

Legatees by universal title must request delivery from the heirs to whom a portion of the property is reserved by law; in their absence, from the universal legatees and, in the absence of the latter, from the heirs called in the order established in the title On Successions.  
The delivery of legacies may be effected amicably; it may be evidenced by an act under private signature: a written, dated and signed document. However, an authentic act must be drawn up when immovable property is involved. Whether it is an act under private signature or an authentic act, the delivery of legacies specifies the property that is concerned.

###### Article 1147

The legatee by universal title is liable, like the universal legatee, for the debts and charges of the succession of the testator, personally for his share and portion, and by mortgage for the whole.  

Where the testator has disposed of only a portion of the disposable portion, and he has done so by universal title, this legatee is required to discharge particular legacies by contribution with the natural heirs.

###### Sous-section 3 : Des legs particuliers Article 1148

Every pure and simple legacy gives to the legatee, from the day of the death of the testator, a right to the thing bequeathed, a right transmissible to his heirs or successors in title.  
Nevertheless the particular legatee cannot take possession of the thing bequeathed, nor claim the fruits or interest thereof, except from the day of his request for delivery, made according to the order established in the title On Successions, or from the day on which such delivery was voluntarily consented to him.

###### Article 1149

The interest or fruits of the thing bequeathed accrue to the benefit of the legatee, from the day of death, and without his having made his request in court:
1° Where the testator has expressly declared his intention, in this regard, in the will; 2° Where a life annuity or a pension has been bequeathed as maintenance.

###### Article 1150

The costs of the request for delivery are chargeable to the succession, without however any reduction of the legal reserve resulting therefrom.  
Registration fees are payable by the legatee. All of the foregoing, except contrary stipulation in the will.  
Each legacy may be registered separately, without such registration being able to benefit anyone other than the legatee or his successors in title.

###### Article 1151

The heirs of the testator, or other debtors of a legacy, are personally bound to discharge the legacy, each in proportion to the share and portion in which they will benefit from the succession.  
They are bound, by mortgage for the whole, to deliver the thing bequeathed with the necessary accessories and in the state in which it will be found on the day of the death of the donor, up to the value of the immovable property of the succession of which they are holders. However, if the person who bequeathed the ownership of an immovable property subsequently increased it by acquisitions, these acquisitions, even if they are contiguous, shall not be deemed, without a new disposition, to form part of the legacy. On the other hand, embellishments, or new constructions made on the bequeathed land are necessarily included in the legacy.

###### Article 1152

If, before the will or since, the thing bequeathed has been the subject of a real right by the testator, the legatee receives the bequeathed property in the state in which it is at the death of the testator and the person who must deliver the legacy is not required to free this property before delivering it.

###### Article 1153

Where the testator has bequeathed the thing of another, the legacy is null, even if the testator did not know that it did not belong to him.

###### Article 1154

Where the legacy relates to an indeterminate thing, the heir is not obliged to give it of the best quality, and he cannot offer it of the worst.

###### Article 1155

A legacy made to a creditor is not deemed to be in compensation for his debt, nor is a legacy made to a servant in compensation for his wages.

###### Article 1156

The particular legatee is not liable for the debts of the succession, except for the reduction of the legacy as stated above, and except for the mortgage action of creditors.

##### Section III: Mandataries and Testamentary Executors Article 1157

The heirs may, by mutual agreement, entrust the administration of the estate to one of them or to a third party. The mandate is governed by the provisions of articles 2175 et seq.  
Where at least one heir has accepted the estate up to the net assets, the mandatary may not, even with the agreement of all the heirs, be appointed except by the judge.  
The judge may also be seized by any interested party or by the public prosecutor so that he may appoint a qualified person as estate mandatary, for the purpose of provisionally administering the estate by reason of the inertia, failure or fault of one or more heirs in such administration, their disagreement, a conflict of interests between them or the complexity of the estate situation.

###### Article 1158

In the preceding cases, the mandate or the judge, as the case may be, fixes the duration of the mission of the appointed mandatary, the limit of his powers and his remuneration.  
The appointment of a testamentary mandatary is the subject of publication at the mortgage registry.

###### Article 1159

At the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor, the judge may remove the estate mandatary, and appoint another, where the first has failed in his mission.  
The mission ceases by operation of law by the effect of an agreement of joint ownership between the heirs or by the signing of the deed of partition. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the estate mandatary.

###### Article 1160

As soon as the estate has been accepted by at least one heir, either purely and simply, or subject to inventory, the judge who appointed the estate mandatary may authorize him to perform all acts of administration of the estate.  

He may also authorize him, at any time, to carry out acts of disposition necessary for the proper administration of the estate and determine the prices and stipulations thereof.

###### Article 1161

The testator may appoint one or more testamentary executors, enjoying full civil capacity, to ensure or proceed with the execution of his wishes.  
The testamentary executor who has accepted his mission is bound to perform it in the same capacity as a mandatary acting gratuitously. He assumes responsibility for it. He ensures that the testament is executed; and, in case of dispute over its validity or execution, he must be made a party or intervene as the case may be to uphold the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.  

The testamentary executor exercises his mission gratuitously, except for a liberality made as a particular gift having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered.

###### Article 1162

The testator may authorize the testamentary executor to seize all or only part of the movable property of the estate, and to sell it if this is necessary to discharge the particular legacies within the limit of the available portion; this seizure may not last beyond one year and one day from the opening of the testament.  
The heir may cause the seizure to cease by offering to deliver to the testamentary executors a sufficient sum for the payment of the movable legacies or by proving such payment.

###### Article 1163

In the absence of an accepting reserved heir, the testator may authorize, for a period of two years from the opening of the testament, the testamentary executor to dispose of all or part of the immovable property of the estate, receive and invest capital, pay debts and charges and proceed with the attribution or partition of the remaining property between the heirs and the legatees.  
On pain of being unenforceable, the sale of an immovable property of the estate may only take place after information of the heirs by the testamentary executor.

###### Article 1164

The authorizations provided for in the two preceding articles may, by decision of the judge, be extended by one year at most.

###### Article 1165

If there are several testamentary executors who have accepted their mission, only one may act in the absence of the others, unless the testator has provided otherwise or has divided their functions. In case of joint acceptance, they are jointly and severally liable for the account of the property entrusted to them.

###### Article 1166

The testamentary executor takes any conservatory measure useful for the proper execution of the testament.  
He may make, in the presence of the presumptive heir, or he being duly summoned, the inventory of the property of the estate.  

He causes the sale of movable property in the absence of sufficient liquid assets to discharge the legacies and urgent debts of the estate.

###### Article 1167

In case of dispute over the validity or execution of the testament, the testamentary executor must be made a party or intervene as the case may be, to uphold the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

###### Article 1168

The mission of the testamentary executor ends:	upon completion of his mission;	by decision of the judge, who relieves him of his mission for serious reasons;	by his death, his powers not being transmissible to his heirs.  

The testamentary executor renders account within six months following the end of his mission; in case of death, this obligation is imposed on his heirs.

###### Article 1169

The expenses incurred by the testamentary executor in the exercise of his mission are chargeable to the estate. He is reimbursed before the delivery of the legacies.

##### Section IV: Revocation of Testaments and Their Lapse Article 1170

Testaments may be revoked, in whole or in part, only by a subsequent testament or by an act before a notary bearing declaration of the change of will.

###### Article 1171

In the absence of express revocation, the testator is deemed to have tacitly revoked his testament:

1° By a subsequent testament whose provisions prove incompatible with the preceding ones. In this case, the new provisions replace the former ones;  
2° By the voluntary alienation of the thing bequeathed when the legacy is as a particular gift and has as its object a specific thing, even if the alienation should subsequently be called into question, subject to the contrary will expressed by the testator in the act of alienation;  

3° By the destruction or voluntary alteration of the testament. In case of erasure or tearing of only part of the paper containing the testamentary provisions, there is no revocation of the provisions mentioned on the preserved part, at least if these fulfill the conditions of form provided by law.

###### Article 1172

The revocation made in a subsequent testament has full effect, even if this new act should remain without execution due to the incapacity of the instituted heir or the legatee, or by their refusal to take the succession or the legacy.  
The revocation of a testament does not revive the testament previously established in the absence of a will clearly manifested to that effect by the deceased.

###### Article 1173

Any testamentary provision lapses if the person in whose favor it is made does not survive the testator.  
It is the same when the testamentary provision had been made under a condition, and the instituted heir or the legatee dies before the fulfillment of this condition, except in the case of a

suspensive condition whose right was immediately acquired by the instituted heir, or the legatee and who, in this case, transmits this right to his heirs.

###### Article 1174

A testamentary disposition lapses:
1° If the bequeathed thing has totally perished during the testator's lifetime;  
2° If the bequeathed thing has perished since the testator's death, without the act or fault of the heir, even though the heir has been put in default to deliver it, when it would equally have had to perish in the hands of the legatee;  
3° When the instituted heir or the legatee repudiates it or is found incapable of receiving it.

###### Article 1175

In the absence of provision in the testamentary dispositions, the revocation, lapse or nullity of a legacy benefits the debtors of the revoked, lapsed or null legacy or legacies, that is to say, as the case may be, the heir, the universal legatee or the legatee by general title. Thus, the ineffectiveness of a universal legacy benefits the heirs; in the absence of a forced heir, the ineffectiveness of a particular legacy benefits the universal legatee.  
By way of exception, the property included in the legacy deprived of effect may be transmitted to the other legatees. There is thus accretion when the legacy has been made to several persons jointly. Two types of legacies are deemed joint within the meaning of this article, namely: the legacy made by one and the same provision of the will and without assignment of shares to each of the co-legatees; the legacy, to several persons, of a thing which can be divided without deterioration.

###### Article 1176

After the death of the testator, the legacies he had established may be revoked judicially if the legatee:
1° Has not performed the charges incumbent upon him; 2° Has made an attempt on the testator's life;  
3° Has been guilty towards the testator of acts of cruelty, offences or serious insults; 4° Has uttered a serious insult against the memory of the testator.  
The action for revocation belongs to all those who have an interest therein: the testator's heirs, the universal legatees, and by indirect action the creditors of the testator, of the heirs or of the legatees. The testamentary executor is also entitled to seek revocation for non-performance of the charges. On the other hand, the beneficiary of the legacy, as well as the beneficiary of the charge, may only bring the action for performance.  

In case 4°, the action must be brought within one year from the day of the offence.

#### Chapter VI

Gradual and residual liberalities Section I: Gradual liberalities

###### Article 1177

A liberality may be burdened with a charge entailing the obligation for the donee or legatee to preserve the property or rights which are the object thereof and to transmit them, upon his death, to a second beneficiary, designated in the instrument.

###### Article 1178

The liberality thus granted may only produce its effect on property or rights identifiable at the date of transmission and subsisting in kind at the death of the person burdened.  

When it relates to securities, the liberality also produces its effect, in case of alienation, on the securities which have been subrogated thereto.  

When it concerns immovable property, the charge burdening the liberality is subject to publication.

###### Article 1179

The rights of the second beneficiary open at the death of the person burdened.  

However, the person burdened may abandon, for the benefit of the second beneficiary, the enjoyment of the property or right which is the object of the liberality.  
This anticipated abandonment may not prejudice the creditors of the person burdened prior to the abandonment, nor third parties having acquired, from the latter, a right over the property or right abandoned.

###### Article 1180

The second beneficiary is deemed to hold his rights from the author of the liberality. The same applies to his heirs when they receive the liberality under the conditions provided for in Article 1066.

###### Article 1181

It is for the disposer to prescribe guarantees and securities for the proper performance of the charge.

###### Article 1182

The second beneficiary may not be subjected to the obligation to preserve and transmit.  

If the charge has been stipulated beyond the first degree, it remains valid but for the first degree only.

###### Article 1183

If the person burdened is a forced heir of the disposer, the charge may only be imposed on the disposable portion.  
The donee may however accept, in the deed of donation or subsequently in an instrument established by specific authentic act received by two notaries, that the charge burdens all or part of his forced share. The instrument is signed in the presence of the notaries alone and mentions precisely its future legal consequences for the donee, on pain of nullity.  
The legatee may, within one year from the day on which he became aware of the will, request that his share of the forced portion be, in whole or in part, freed from the charge. Failing this, he must assume its performance.  
The charge relating to the forced share of the person burdened, with his consent, benefits by operation of law, to that extent, all his children born and unborn.

###### Article 1184

The author of a gradual donation may revoke it with regard to the second beneficiary as long as the latter has not notified, in the forms required for donations, his acceptance to the donor.  
By way of derogation from Article 1091, the gradual donation may be accepted by the second beneficiary after the death of the donor.

###### Article 1185

When the second beneficiary dies before the person burdened or renounces the benefit of the gradual liberality, the property or rights which were the object thereof form part of the succession of the person burdened, unless the instrument expressly provides that his heirs may receive it or designates another second beneficiary.

##### Section II: Residual liberalities Article 1186

It may be provided in a liberality that a person will be called to receive what will remain of the gift or legacy made to a first beneficiary at the death of the latter.

###### Article 1187

The residual liberality does not oblige the first beneficiary to preserve the property received. It obliges him to transmit the subsisting property.  
When the property, objects of the residual liberality, have been alienated by the first beneficiary, the rights of the second beneficiary do not transfer either to the proceeds of these alienations or to the new property acquired.

###### Article 1188

The first beneficiary may not dispose by will of the property given or bequeathed on a residual basis.  

The residual liberality may prohibit the first beneficiary from disposing of the property by inter vivos donation.  

However, when he is a forced heir, the first beneficiary retains the possibility of disposing inter vivos or upon death of the property which has been given as an advancement on his succession share.

###### Article 1189

The first beneficiary is not required to account for his management to the disposer or to his heirs.

###### Article 1190

The provisions set out in Articles 1178, 1180, 1181, 1184 and 1185 are applicable to residual liberalities.

#### Chapter VII

Partition donations and partition wills Section I: General provisions

###### Article 1191

Any person may make, among his presumptive heirs, the distribution and partition of his property.  

This instrument may be made in the form of a partition donation or a partition will. It is subject to the formalities, conditions and rules prescribed for inter vivos donations in the first case and wills in the second, subject to the application of the provisions which follow.

###### Article 1192

Any person may also make the distribution and partition of his property and rights among descendants of different degrees, whether or not they are his presumptive heirs. The agreement of the forced heirs is then necessary.

###### Article 1193

The action for additional share on grounds of lesion may not be brought against partition donations and partition wills.  

The provisions of Article 972, first paragraph, are applicable to balancing payments charged to the donees, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

###### Article 1195

If all the property that the disposer leaves at the day of his death has not been included in the partition, those of his property that have not been included therein are allocated or partitioned in accordance with the law.

##### Section II: Gifts with partition

###### § 1. Gifts with partition made to presumptive heirs Article 1196

A gift with partition may only have as its object present property.

The gift and the partition may be made by separate instruments provided that the ascendant is a party to both instruments.

###### Article 1197

In the case of a gift with partition made jointly by two spouses, the non-common child may be allotted on behalf of his ancestor in separate property of the latter or in common property, without the spouse being able however to be co-donor of the common property.

###### Article 1198

Property received by way of advance partition by a presumptive forced heir is imputable to his share of the reserved portion, unless it has been given expressly in addition to his share.

###### Article 1199

The forced heir who has not participated in the gift with partition, or who has received an allotment less than his share of the reserved portion, may exercise the action for reduction, if there does not exist at the opening of the succession property not included in the partition and sufficient to compose or complete his reserved portion, taking into account liberalities from which he may have benefited.

###### Article 1200

Gifts with partition follow the rules of gifts inter vivos for everything concerning imputation, calculation of the reserved portion and reduction.
The action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the disposer who made the partition. In the case of a gift with partition made jointly by both spouses, the action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the survivor of the disposers, except for the non-common child who may act upon the death of his ancestor. The action is prescribed after five years from that death.

The child not yet conceived at the time of the gift with partition has a similar action to compose or complete his hereditary share.

###### Article 1201

Notwithstanding the rules applicable to gifts inter vivos, the property given shall, unless otherwise agreed, be valued at the day of the gift with partition for imputation and calculation of the reserved portion, provided that all forced heirs living or represented at the death of the ascendant have received an allotment in the advance partition and have expressly accepted it, and that no reservation of usufruct over a sum of money has been provided for.

The allotment of certain donees may be formed, in whole or in part, from gifts, whether subject to collation or in addition to their share, already received by them from the disposer, having regard where applicable to investments and reinvestments that they may have made in the interval.

The valuation date applicable to the advance partition shall also be applicable to prior gifts that have thus been incorporated into it. Any provision to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1203

The parties may also agree that a prior gift made in addition to a share shall be incorporated into the partition and imputed to the share of the reserved portion of the donee by way of advancement of succession share.

###### Article 1204

The agreements referred to in the two preceding articles may take place even in the absence of new gifts from the disposer. They are not regarded as liberalities between the presumptive heirs, but as a partition made by the disposer.

###### § 2

Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees Article 1205
When the ascendant proceeds with a gift with partition, his children may consent to their own descendants being allotted therein in their place and stead, in whole or in part.
Descendants of a subsequent degree may, in the advance partition, be allotted separately or jointly among themselves.

###### Article 1206

This liberality constitutes a gift with partition even though the donor ascendant has only one child, whether the partition is made between the latter and his descendants or between his descendants only.
It requires the consent, in the instrument, of the child who renounces all or part of his rights, as well as of his descendants who benefit therefrom. The liberality is null when the consent of the renouncing party has been vitiated by error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 1207

When descendants of different degrees participate in the same gift with partition, the partition is effected by stirpes.
Allocations may be made to descendants of different degrees in certain stirpes and not in others.

###### Article 1208

Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 to 1204.

###### Article 1209

In the succession of the donor ascendant, the property received by the children or their descendants by way of advance partition is imputed to the share of the reserved portion reverting to their stirps and subsidiarily to the disposable portion.
All gifts made to members of the same stirps are imputed together, whatever the degree of relationship with the deceased.

When all the children of the donor ascendant have given their consent to the advance partition and no reservation of usufruct over a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is valued according to the rule provided for in article 1201.

If the descendants of a stirps have not received an allotment in the gift with partition or have received therein only an allotment less than their share of the reserved portion, they are made whole in their rights according to the rules provided for in articles 1199 and 1200.

###### Article 1210

In the succession of the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead, the property received by them from the ascendant is treated as if they held it from their direct ancestor.
This property is subject to the rules governing gifts inter vivos for notional reunion, imputation, collation and, where applicable, reduction.
However, when all the descendants have received and accepted an allotment in the advance partition and no usufruct over a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is treated as if they had received it from their ancestor by gift with partition.

###### Article 1211

The rules laid down in article 1210 do not apply when the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead subsequently proceeds himself, with the latter, to a gift with partition into which is incorporated the property previously received under the conditions provided for in article 1205.
This new gift with partition may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 and 1203.

##### Section III: Wills with partition Article 1212

A will with partition produces the effects of a partition. Its beneficiaries may not renounce relying on the will to claim a new partition of the succession.

###### Article 1213

The beneficiary who has not received an allotment equal to his share of the reserved portion may exercise the action for reduction in accordance with article 1200.

#### Chapter VIII

Gifts made by marriage contract to the spouses, and to children to be born of the marriage

###### Article 1214

Any gift inter vivos of present property, although made by marriage contract to the spouses, or to one of them, shall be subject to the general rules prescribed for gifts made under that title.
It may not take place for the benefit of children to be born, except in the cases set out in chapter VI of this title.

###### Article 1215

Fathers and mothers, other ascendants, collateral relatives of the spouses, and even strangers, may, by marriage contract, dispose of all or part of the property they will leave at the day of their death, both for the benefit of said spouses and for the benefit of children to be born of their marriage, in the event that the donor survives the donee spouse.  

Such a donation, although made for the benefit only of the spouses or one of them, shall always, in said event of the donor's survival, be presumed made for the benefit of the children and descendants to be born of the marriage.

###### Article 1216

The donation in the form provided in the preceding article shall be irrevocable only in the sense that the donor may no longer dispose, by gratuitous title, of the objects included in the donation, except for modest sums, by way of reward or otherwise.

###### Article 1217

The donation by marriage contract may be made cumulatively of present and future property, in whole or in part, on condition that a statement of the donor's debts and charges existing at the day of the donation be annexed to the deed; in which case, it shall be open to the donee, upon the death of the donor, to confine himself to the present property, by renouncing the surplus of the donor's property.

###### Article 1218

If the statement mentioned in the preceding article has not been annexed to the deed containing the donation of present and future property, the donee shall be obliged to accept or repudiate this donation as a whole.  
In case of acceptance, he may claim only the property that will be found existing at the day of the donor's death, and he shall be subject to payment of all debts and charges of the succession.

###### Article 1219

The donation by marriage contract in favor of the spouses and children to be born of their marriage may also be made, on condition of paying indiscriminately all debts and charges of the donor's succession, or under other conditions the performance of which would depend on his will, by whatever person the donation is made: the donee shall be bound to fulfill these conditions, if he does not prefer to renounce the donation; and if the donor, by marriage contract, has reserved the liberty to dispose of an item included in the donation of his present property or of a fixed sum to be taken from this same property, the item or sum, if he dies without having disposed of it, shall be deemed included in the donation and shall belong to the donee or his heirs.

###### Article 1220

Donations made by marriage contract may not be challenged or declared null on the pretext of lack of acceptance.

###### Article 1221

Any donation made in favor of the marriage shall lapse if the marriage does not ensue.

###### Article 1222

Donations made to one of the spouses, in the terms of articles 1215, 1217 and 1219 above, shall lapse if the donor survives the donee spouse and his posterity.

###### Article 1223

All donations made to the spouses by their marriage contract shall, upon the opening of the donor's succession, be reducible to the portion which the law permitted him to dispose of.

#### Chapitre IX

Des dispositions entre époux, soit par contrat de mariage, soit pendant le mariage Article 1224
The spouses may, by marriage contract, make to each other reciprocally, or one of the two to the other, such donation as they deem appropriate, subject to the modifications hereinafter expressed.

###### Article 1225

Any inter vivos donation of present property, made between spouses by marriage contract, shall not be deemed made under the condition of survival of the donee, if this condition is not formally expressed; and it shall be subject to all the rules and forms prescribed above for such donations.

###### Article 1226

The donation of future property, or of present and future property, made between spouses by marriage contract, whether simple or reciprocal, shall be subject to the rules established by the preceding chapter, with regard to similar donations that will be made to them by a third party, except that it shall not be transmissible to the children born of the marriage, in case of death of the donee spouse before the donor spouse.

###### Article 1227

The spouse, whether by marriage contract or during the marriage, may, for the case where he would not leave children or descendants, dispose in favor of the other spouse in ownership, of all that he could dispose of in favor of a stranger.

###### Article 1228

For the case where the spouse would leave children or descendants, whether or not born of the marriage, he may dispose in favor of the other spouse, either of the ownership of that which he could dispose of in favor of a stranger, or of one quarter of his property in ownership and the three other quarters in usufruct, or again of the totality of his property in usufruct only.  
Unless otherwise stipulated by the disposer, the surviving spouse may limit his emolument, that is to say accept only certain of the property disposed of in his favor. This limitation may not be considered as a liberality made to the other successors.

###### Article 1229

The children or descendants may, notwithstanding any contrary stipulation of the disposer, require, as to the property subject to usufruct, that an inventory be drawn up of the movables as well as a statement of the immovables, that employment be made of the sums and that bearer securities be, at the choice of the usufructuary, converted into registered securities or deposited with an approved depositary.

###### Article 1230

The minor may not, by marriage contract, give to the other spouse, whether by simple donation or by reciprocal donation, except with the consent and assistance of those whose consent is required for the validity of his marriage; and, with this consent, he may give all that the law permits the adult spouse to give to the other spouse.

###### Article 1231

The donation of future property made between spouses during the marriage is always revocable.  

The donation of present property that takes effect during the marriage made between spouses is revocable only under the conditions provided for by articles 1111 to 1116.  
Donations made between spouses of present property or of future property are not revoked by the supervening of children.

###### Article 1232

If a spouse has made to his spouse, within the limits of article 1228, a liberality in ownership, each of the children who are not born of both spouses shall have, as concerns him, unless contrary and unequivocal will of the disposer, the faculty to substitute for the performance of this liberality the abandonment of the usufruct of the share of succession that he would have collected in the absence of a surviving spouse.  
Those who have exercised this faculty may require that the provisions of article 1229 be applied.

###### Article 1233

The spouses may not give each other indirectly beyond what is permitted to them by the provisions above.  
Any donation, whether disguised or made to interposed persons, shall be null.  

Shall be deemed made to interposed persons, donations from one of the spouses to the children or to one of the children of the other spouse born of another marriage, and those made by the donor to relatives of whom the other spouse will be presumptive heir on the day of the donation, even though the latter did not survive his donee relative.

###### Article 1234

When a spouse acquires property with money that has been given to him by the other for this purpose, the donation is only of the sums remitted and not of the property to which they are employed.  
In this case, the rights of the donor or his heirs have as their object only a sum of money according to the current value of the property. If the property has been alienated, the value it had on the day of alienation is considered, and if new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property.

### Title III: Obligations

###### Article 1235

Obligations arise from legal acts, legal facts or the authority of law alone.

They may arise from the promise to perform a natural obligation as well as from the voluntary performance of such an obligation. The promise to perform a natural obligation constitutes a contract; the completed performance of a natural obligation cannot give rise to restitution once the performance has been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1236

Legal acts are manifestations of will intended to produce legal effects. They may be a contract or a unilateral legal act.
Legal acts are subject, insofar as reasonable, for their validity and their effects, to the rules that govern contracts.

###### Article 1237

Legal facts are actions or events to which the law attaches legal effects.

Obligations arising from a legal fact are governed, as the case may be, by the sub-title relating to civil liability or the sub-title relating to quasi-contracts.

Sub-title I: The contract

Chapter I: Preliminary provisions Article 1238
A contract is an agreement of wills between two or more persons intended to create, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.

###### Article 1239

Everyone is free to contract or not to contract, to choose their contracting party and to determine the content and form of the contract, within the limits set by law.
Contractual freedom does not permit derogation from rules that concern public order and good morals.

###### Article 1240

Contracts legally formed have the force of law for those who have made them. Contracts are in principle consensual.
By way of exception, the validity of solemn contracts is subject to the observance of forms determined by law in the absence of which the contract is null and void, subject to possible regularisation.
Furthermore, the law makes the formation of certain contracts subject to the delivery of a thing.
On the other hand, forms required for the purposes of proof or enforceability have no effect on the validity of contracts.

###### Article 1241

Where a writing is required for the validity of a contract, whether under private signature or by authentic act, it may be established and preserved in electronic form, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions such as to guarantee not only its integrity but also the link between the electronic signature and the act to which it is attached.
The reliability of an electronic signature process is presumed until proven otherwise where that process implements a secure electronic signature, established by means of a secure electronic signature creation device and where the verification of that signature is based on the use of a qualified electronic certificate.
Where a handwritten mention by the person who binds himself is required, the latter may affix it in electronic form if the conditions of such affixing are such as to guarantee that it can only be done by himself.

###### Article 1242

Exception is made to the provisions of the preceding article for:
1° Acts under private signature relating to family law and succession law;
2° Acts under private signature relating to personal or real security interests, of a civil or commercial nature.

###### Article 1243

The requirement of sending in several copies is deemed satisfied electronically if the writing can be printed by the recipient.

###### Article 1244

The requirement of a detachable form is satisfied by an electronic process that allows access to the form and its return by the same means.

###### Article 1245

Contracts must be negotiated, formed and performed in good faith. This provision is a matter of public order.

###### Article 1246

Contracts, whether they have a specific designation or not, are subject to general rules, which are the subject of this title.
The particular rules for certain contracts are established in the provisions specific to each of them; the general rules apply subject to these particular rules.

###### Article 1247

A contract is synallagmatic or bilateral when the contracting parties mutually bind themselves to one another, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.
It is unilateral when one or more persons are bound to one or more others, without there being any reciprocal commitment from the latter.

###### Article 1248

A contract is commutative when each of the parties undertakes to provide the other with an advantage that is regarded as the equivalent of that which it receives.
It is aleatory when the equivalent consists in the chance of gain or loss for each of the parties, according to an uncertain event.

###### Article 1249

A contract is for valuable consideration when each of the parties receives from the other an advantage in return for that which it provides.
It is gratuitous or of beneficence when one of the parties provides the other with an advantage without expecting or receiving any consideration in return.

###### Article 1250

A contract is consensual when it is formed by the mere exchange of consents without the expression of will having to take a particular form.
A contract is solemn when it requires for its validity, in addition to the agreement of wills, compliance with forms determined by law.

A contract is real when its formation is subject to the delivery of a thing.

###### Article 1251

A contract by mutual agreement is one whose stipulations are freely negotiated between the parties.

A contract of adhesion is one whose general conditions, removed from negotiation, are determined in advance by one of the parties who proposes them to the other.

###### Article 1252

A framework contract is an agreement by which the parties agree on the general characteristics of their future contractual relations. It subsequently incorporates application contracts, which specify the terms of performance.

###### Article 1253

A contract with instantaneous performance is one whose obligations can be performed in a single performance.
A contract with successive performance is one whose obligations of at least one party are performed in several performances spread over time.

#### Chapter II: Formation of the contract

##### Section I: Contractual negotiation Article 1254

The initiation, conduct and termination of pre-contractual negotiations are free. They must imperatively satisfy the requirements of good faith.
It is always possible to break off pre-contractual negotiations, except for abrupt termination or termination without legitimate reason.
In the event of fault committed in the negotiations, the reparation of damage is of an extra-contractual nature. In the event of an agreement in principle, by which the parties undertake to continue a negotiation, to lead to the conclusion of a contract whose conditions remain to be defined, a contractual obligation to negotiate in good faith arises. Consequently, the termination of the negotiation must be justified. Failing this, damages may be awarded on the basis of contractual liability.

In all cases, the reparation awarded cannot have the purpose of compensating for the loss of benefits expected from the contract not concluded.

###### Article 1255

The party who knows information of decisive importance for the consent of the other party must inform the other party of it where the latter legitimately does not know this information or places trust in its co-contractor. Information of decisive importance is information that has a direct and necessary link with the content of the contract or the quality of the parties; however, the duty to inform does not extend to the estimation of the value of the performance.  
The parties may neither limit nor exclude this duty.  

The burden lies on the person who claims that information was owed to him to prove that the other party owed it to him, and it is for that other party to prove that it provided it.  
In addition to the liability of the person who was under the duty, breach of this duty to inform may result in annulment of the contract under the conditions provided for in Articles 1283 and following.

###### Article 1256

A person who uses or discloses without authorization confidential information obtained during negotiations incurs liability under the conditions of ordinary law.

##### Section II : La rencontre des consentements

###### § 1. L'offre et l'acceptation Article 1257

A contract is formed by the meeting of an offer and an acceptance by which the parties
express their intention to be bound.  

A declaration of intention, made expressly and without formality, is sufficient to create a binding commitment. The intention to be bound may also be expressed tacitly or implicitly, when it results from unequivocal conduct of its author.

###### Article 1258

A proposal to conclude a contract, addressed to one or more specified persons or to an unspecified person, constitutes an offer if it is sufficiently precise and if it indicates the intention of its author to be bound in the event of acceptance.  
A proposal is sufficiently precise when it contains the essential elements of the contemplated contract. Failing that, it is merely an invitation to enter into negotiations.

###### Article 1259

An offer takes effect as soon as it reaches its addressee. It is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.  
An offer may be freely revoked, provided that the revocation reaches the addressee before the addressee has dispatched his acceptance. However, an offer may not be revoked if it specifies that it is irrevocable or if it fixes a specified period for its acceptance. Revocation of the offer in breach of this prohibition prevents the conclusion of the contract. It engages the extra-contractual liability of its author under the conditions of ordinary law without obliging him to compensate for the loss of benefits expected from the contract.  

An offer, even if irrevocable, lapses when its rejection reaches the author of the offer.

###### Article 1260

An offer lapses upon expiry of the period fixed by its author or, failing that, after a reasonable period.  
It also lapses in the event of incapacity or death of its author.

###### Article 1261

A declaration or any other conduct of the addressee indicating that he intends to be bound by the terms of the offer made constitutes an acceptance.  
The silence or inaction of the person alleged to be bound cannot alone, in the absence of any other circumstance, constitute proof against him of the alleged obligation. It is otherwise when the law, usages, business relations or particular circumstances give the value of acceptance to silence maintained.

###### Article 1262

Where the author of the offer has fixed a period for acceptance in a letter, that period begins to run, unless otherwise indicated in the letter, from the day of dispatch of the offer, the postmark being conclusive evidence. The period for acceptance that the author of the offer fixes by telephone, telex, facsimile, email or any other means of instantaneous communication begins to run at the moment when the offer reaches the addressee.

###### Article 1263

The law or the contract may provide, on the one hand, for a period of reflection for the benefit of the addressee of the offer, which is the period before the expiry of which the addressee may not express his acceptance, or on the other hand, for a period of withdrawal, which is the period before the expiry of which its beneficiary may withdraw his consent.

###### Article 1264

Acceptance takes effect at the moment when the agreement expressed by the acceptor reaches the author of the offer. Acceptance does not take effect if that indication does not reach the author of the offer within the period he has stipulated or, failing stipulation, within a reasonable period, having regard to the circumstances surrounding the contemplated transaction and the means of communication used by the author of the offer.  

An acceptance is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.  
A verbal offer must be accepted immediately, unless the circumstances imply otherwise.

###### Article 1265

A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additional or different elements not substantially altering the terms of the offer, constitutes an acceptance.  
A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additions, limitations or other substantial modifications to the terms of the offer, must be considered as a rejection of the offer and constitutes a counter-offer.

###### Article 1266

Acceptance may be freely withdrawn, provided that the withdrawal reaches the author of the offer before the moment when the acceptance would have taken effect.

###### Article 1267

General conditions invoked by one party have effect in respect of the other party only if they have been brought to the knowledge of that party and if that party has accepted them.  
In the event of discrepancy between general conditions invoked by each of the parties, the incompatible clauses have no effect.  

In the event of discrepancy between general conditions and particular conditions, the latter prevail over the former.

###### Article 1268

A contract is concluded at the moment when acceptance of an offer takes effect in accordance with these provisions, thereby perfecting the meeting of intentions.

###### Article 1269

A contract is concluded at the place where the acceptance reached.

###### Article 1270

Where it is concluded by electronic means, a contract is valid only if the addressee of the offer has had the possibility of verifying the details of his order and its total price and of correcting any errors before confirming it to express his final acceptance.  
The author of the offer must acknowledge receipt without unjustified delay, by electronic means, of the order addressed to him.  
The order, the confirmation of acceptance of the offer and the acknowledgement of receipt are considered as received when the parties to whom they are addressed can have access to them.

###### § 2. La représentation Article 1271

Representation is the power recognized in a person, the representative, to act in the name and on behalf of another, the represented person. The representative does not become a party to the contract.  

This power is of legal, judicial or conventional origin. Conventional representation has its source in the contract of mandate.  

This power is either special and for one matter or certain matters only, or general and for all matters of the represented person. A mandate conceived in general terms embraces only acts of administration.

###### Article 1272

The legal, judicial or conventional representative is only entitled to act within the limits of the powers conferred upon them.

###### Article 1273

Representation is perfect when the representative acts within the limits of their powers and declares to act in the name and on behalf of the represented party. In this case, only the represented party is bound by the commitment entered into and the contract entered into by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.  
Representation is imperfect when the representative does not disclose to the third party the name of their principal. In this case, they alone are bound towards the contracting party.

###### Article 1274

The represented party is not bound by what has been done without authority or beyond the authority given to the representative. The same applies when the representative misuses their powers to the detriment of the represented party. A person who was unaware of the absence, excess or misuse of authority, or could not have been unaware of it, may bring an action for relative nullity of the contract, without prejudice to damages which may, where appropriate, be claimed from the representative.  
By way of exception, the represented party is bound by the act concluded when the contracting third party could legitimately believe in the reality of the representative's powers, in particular by reason of the conduct or statements of the represented party.  

These provisions do not exclude the application of the rules specific to management of another's affairs.  
The represented party may ratify the act concluded without authority or beyond the authority given, or confirm the act performed by misuse of authority. In these cases, the contract entered into by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.

###### Article 1275

The establishment of legal or judicial representation divests the represented party, for its duration, of the powers transferred to the representative.  
Conventional representation leaves the represented party with the exercise of their rights.

###### Article 1276

The powers of the representative cease if they become incapable or are struck by incapacity during the performance of the mandate. These powers also end with the death of the representative.

###### Article 1277

A representative may not act on behalf of both parties to the contract nor contract on their own account with the represented party.
