The act performed is null and void, by relative nullity, by the mere fact of breach of the rule provided for in the preceding paragraph, unless the law authorizes it or the represented party has authorized or ratified it.

##### Section III: The pact of preference and the unilateral promise of contract

###### Article 1278

The pact of preference is the promise made by one person to another, who accepts it, to offer them priority in concluding a contract of a specified nature, in the event that the promisor decides one day to conclude such a contract.

###### Article 1279

When a contract is concluded with a third party in violation of a pact of preference, the beneficiary of the pact may obtain compensation for the damage they suffer. If the third party knew of the existence of the pact and the beneficiary's intention to rely on it, the latter may, in addition, ask the judge to annul the contract entered into with the third party and to substitute themselves for the third party in the contract concluded; they must bring this action within six months of becoming aware of the violation of the pact of preference.  
The third party may request in writing that the beneficiary of the pact confirm within two months the existence of a pact of preference and whether they intend to rely on it. The writing mentions that in the absence of a response within this period, the beneficiary of the pact may no longer seek their substitution for the contract concluded with the third party.

###### Article 1280

The unilateral promise of contract is the act by which one person, the promisor, undertakes towards another, the beneficiary, who accepts it, to grant them, for a certain period, the right to opt for the conclusion of a contract whose essential elements are already determined, and for the formation of which only the consent of the beneficiary is lacking.  
The final contract is formed as soon as the option is exercised. The revocation of the promise during the time left to the beneficiary to opt does not prevent the formation of the promised contract.  

The contract concluded in violation of the unilateral promise with a third party who knew of its existence is null and void. The beneficiary of the promise may, in addition to all damages in compensation for the damage they suffer, ask the judge for their substitution for the third party in the contract concluded.

#### Chapter III: Conditions of validity of contracts Article 1281

Four conditions are essential for the validity of a contract: 1° A real, informed and free consent of the parties;  
2° Their capacity to contract; 3° A certain and lawful object;  
4° A lawful cause.

##### Section I: Consent Article 1282

There is no contract if there is no consent.

###### Article 1283

Error, fraud and duress vitiate consent when they are of such a nature that, without them, one of the parties would not have contracted or would have contracted on substantially different terms.  
Their decisive character as a defect of consent is assessed having regard to the persons and circumstances in which consent was given.

###### Article 1284

The absence of consent and defects of consent are a cause of relative nullity of the contract.

###### Article 1285

Error of law or fact, unless it is inexcusable, is a cause of nullity of the contract when it relates to the essential qualities of the performance due by one or other of the parties.  
Error is not a cause of nullity when it relates only to the person with whom one intends to contract, unless the consideration of that person is the principal cause of the agreement.  

Essential are the qualities in consideration of which both parties contracted, or, similarly, the qualities in consideration of which one of them contracted, to the knowledge of the other. These expected qualities are those which have been expressly or tacitly agreed upon by the parties to the act.  

The acceptance of a risk concerning a quality of the performance excludes error relating to that quality.

###### Article 1286

Error as to a simple motive, unrelated to the essential qualities of the performance due or of the contracting party, is not a cause of nullity, unless the parties, rather than making this motive a condition of their agreement, have expressly made it a decisive element of their consent.

###### Article 1287

Error as to value by which, without being mistaken as to the essential qualities of the performance, a contracting party merely makes an incorrect economic assessment of it, is not a cause of nullity.

###### Article 1288

Fraud is the act by which one party obtains the consent of the other by maneuvers or lies in order to obtain the conclusion of a legal act.  
Also constitutes fraud the concealment by one of the parties of information which they know to be decisive for the other. Nevertheless, the failure by one party to disclose to the other contracting party their assessment of the value of the performance does not constitute fraud.

###### Article 1289

Fraud is also constituted if it emanates from the representative, manager of another's affairs, agent or surety of a party.  
It is also constituted when it emanates from a third party in collusion.

###### Article 1290

Error resulting from fraud is always excusable; it is a cause of nullity even if it relates to the value of the performance or to a simple motive of the contract.

###### Article 1291

A person who is the victim of fraud may bring an action for nullity, seek only damages, or, where appropriate, both.

###### Article 1292

Violence is the act by which a party or a third party infringes upon the free consent of another, by inspiring in them the fear of exposing their person, their fortune or those of their relatives to considerable harm.

###### Article 1293

Mere reverential fear towards one's father, mother, or other ascendant, without any violence having been exercised, is not sufficient to annul the contract.

###### Article 1294

The threat of legal action does not constitute violence, except in case of abuse. Abuse is characterized when the legal action is diverted from its purpose or when it is invoked or exercised to obtain a manifestly excessive advantage.

###### Article 1295

There is also violence when a party, abusing the situation of weakness in which its co-contractor finds himself, obtains from him a commitment that he would not have entered into in the absence of such constraint and derives a manifestly excessive advantage therefrom.

###### Article 1296

The limitation period for the action for nullity runs, in case of error or fraud, only from the day on which they were discovered and, in case of violence, only from the day on which it ceased.  
A contract can no longer be challenged if, since the defect of error or fraud was discovered by the person who was the victim thereof or since the violence ceased, that contract has been approved by him, either expressly, or tacitly, or by allowing the time for restitution fixed by law to pass.

##### Section II : De la capacité des parties contractantes Article 1297

Any natural person may contract except in case of incapacity provided for by law.  

Legal persons contract through their representatives. In this regard, the capacity of legal persons is limited to acts useful for the realization of their object as defined by their statutes and to acts accessory thereto, in compliance with the rules applicable to each of them.

###### Article 1298

The following are incapable of contracting, to the extent defined by law:
1° Unemancipated minors;  
2° Protected adults within the meaning of article 565 of this code.

###### Article 1299

Any person incapable of contracting may nevertheless perform alone routine acts authorized by law or usage.

###### Article 1300

Routine acts performed by a minor may be annulled for simple lesion. But nullity is not incurred when the lesion results from an unforeseeable event.  

The simple declaration of majority made by the minor does not prevent annulment. Likewise, an incapable person cannot be reproached for having remained silent or for having made a false declaration about his status.  

A minor cannot escape the commitments he has made in the exercise of his profession.

###### Article 1301

Acts performed by protected adults are governed by articles 574, 602 and 621 without prejudice to articles 1299, 1304 and 1581.

###### Article 1302

Incapacity to contract is a ground for relative nullity that only the incapable co-contractor may invoke.

###### Article 1303

Except with judicial authorization, it is prohibited, on pain of nullity, for anyone exercising a function or occupying a position in an establishment housing elderly persons or providing psychiatric care to become the purchaser, directly or through an intermediary, of property or assignee of a right belonging to a person admitted to the establishment, nor to take a lease on the dwelling occupied by that person before his admission to the establishment.  
For the application of this article, the spouse, ascendants and descendants of the persons to whom the prohibitions set out above apply are deemed to be intermediaries.

###### Article 1304

The co-contractor of the incapable person may prevent the action for nullity brought against him by establishing that the act was useful to the protected person and free from lesion or that it benefited that person.  
He may also oppose to the action for nullity the confirmation of the act by his co-contractor who has become or become again capable.

###### Article 1305

The limitation period for the action runs:
1° With regard to acts done by a minor, from the day of majority or emancipation;  
2° With regard to acts done by a protected adult, from the day on which he became aware of them while he was in a position to validly redo them;  
3° With regard to the heirs of the person under guardianship or curatorship or of the person subject to family authorization, from the day of death if it had not begun to run previously.

##### Section III : De l'objet et de la matière des contrats Article 1306

The object of the contract is that to which the parties have bound themselves. It may be an obligation to do, not to do, or to give.

###### Article 1307

Only things that are in commerce may be the object of a legal act. A legal act may not derogate from public policy either by its stipulations or by its purpose, whether or not the latter was known to all the parties.

###### Article 1308

The obligation has as its object a present or future performance. One cannot however renounce a succession that has not been opened, nor make any stipulation concerning such a succession, even with the consent of the person whose succession is concerned.  

It must be possible and determined or determinable.  

The performance is determinable when it can be deduced from the contract or by reference to usages or to the prior relations of the parties, without a new agreement of the parties being necessary.

###### Article 1309

Lesion, economic imbalance between reciprocal performances, opens the way to an action for nullity only when the law so provides.

###### Article 1310

In framework contracts and contracts with successive performance, it may be agreed that the price will be fixed unilaterally by one of the parties, provided that it justifies the amount in case of dispute.  
In case of abuse in the fixing of the price, the judge may be seized with a request seeking to obtain damages and if necessary the termination of the contract. The seizure of the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1311

In service contracts, in the absence of agreement of the parties before their performance, the price may be fixed by the creditor, provided that he justifies the amount in case of dispute.  
In case of abuse in the fixing of the price, the judge may be seized with a request for damages. The seizure of the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1312

When the quality of the performance is not determined or determinable by virtue of the contract, the debtor must offer a performance of quality conforming to the legitimate expectations of the parties in consideration of its nature, usages and the amount of the consideration.

###### Article 1313

When the price or any other element of the contract must be determined by reference to an index that does not exist or has ceased to exist or to be accessible, it is replaced by the index that most closely approximates it.

##### Section IV : De la cause Article 1314

An obligation without cause, or based on a false cause, or based on an unlawful cause, can have no effect.

###### Article 1315

Any clause that deprives the debtor's essential obligation of its substance is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1316

A contract for valuable consideration is null when, at the time of its formation, the consideration agreed upon for the benefit of the person who commits himself is illusory or derisory.

###### Article 1317

In a contract of adhesion, any clause that creates a significant imbalance between the rights and obligations of the parties to the contract is deemed unwritten.  
The assessment of significant imbalance relates neither to the main object of the contract nor to the adequacy of the price to the performance.

###### Article 1318

The agreement is no less valid even though the cause is not expressed therein.

###### Article 1319

The cause is unlawful when it is prohibited by law, when it is contrary to public morals or to public order.

##### Section V

Sanctions for non-compliance with the conditions of validity of contracts Sub-section 1: Nullity

###### Article 1320

A contract that does not meet the conditions required for its validity is null and void. Nullity must be pronounced by the judge, unless the parties acknowledge it by mutual agreement.  
The annulled contract is deemed never to have existed.  
The performances executed give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in Articles 1577 to 1585.  

Independently of the annulment of the contract, the injured party may claim compensation for the damage suffered under the conditions of the general law of extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1321

Nullity is absolute when the violated rule has as its object the safeguarding of the general interest. It is relative when the violated rule has as its sole object the safeguarding of a private interest.  
When the rule that infringes a private interest derives from a fundamental value, such as the protection of the human body, the nullity is absolute.

###### Article 1322

Absolute nullity may be claimed by any person having an interest, as well as by the public prosecutor.  
It can never be cured by confirmation of the contract.

###### Article 1323

Relative nullity may only be claimed by the party whom the law intends to protect. It may be cured by confirmation.  
If the action for relative nullity has several holders, the waiver by one does not prevent the others from acting.

###### Article 1324

Confirmation is the act by which the person who could avail himself of the nullity waives it. This act mentions the object of the obligation and the defect affecting the contract.  
Confirmation may only take place after the conclusion of the contract.  

Voluntary performance of the contract, with knowledge of the cause of nullity, constitutes confirmation. In case of duress, confirmation may only take place after the duress has ceased.  

Confirmation entails waiver of the means and exceptions that could have been raised, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1325

A party may request in writing from the party who could avail himself of the nullity either to confirm the contract or to bring an action for nullity within six months on pain of forfeiture. The cause of the nullity must have ceased.  
The writing expressly mentions that in the absence of an action for nullity brought before the expiration of the six-month period, the contract shall be deemed confirmed.

###### Article 1326

When the cause of nullity affects only one or more clauses of the contract, it entails nullity of the entire act only if that clause or those clauses constituted a determining element of the commitment of the parties or of one of them.  
The contract is maintained when the law deems the clause unwritten, or when the purposes of the violated rule require its maintenance.  
Except for a provision of law that confers this power upon him, the judge may not modify a clause or an amount provided for by the contract.

###### Article 1327

The exception of nullity is not subject to prescription if it relates to a contract that has received no performance.

###### Sub-section 2: Lapse Article 1328

A validly formed contract lapses if one of its essential elements disappears.  

When the performance of several contracts is necessary for the realization of the same transaction and one of them disappears, those contracts whose performance is rendered impossible by this disappearance and those for which the performance of the disappeared contract was a determining condition of the consent of a party lapse.  

Lapse occurs, however, only if the contracting party against whom it is invoked knew of the existence of the overall transaction when he gave his consent.

###### Article 1329

Lapse terminates the contract.  

It may give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in Articles 1577 to 1585.

#### Chapter IV: Interpretation of legal acts Article 1330

When the will of the parties is expressed in a clear and precise manner, the judge may not, under cover of interpretation, modify the clauses thereof, on pain of misrepresentation.

###### Article 1331

The judge must in agreements seek what was the common intention of the contracting parties, rather than stopping at the literal meaning of the terms.  
When this intention cannot be discerned, the contract is interpreted according to the meaning that a reasonable person placed in the same situation would give it. But even when the terms in which an

agreement is drafted are general, it comprises only those things on which it appears that the parties intended to contract.

###### Article 1332

Terms susceptible of two meanings must be taken in the meaning that best suits the subject matter of the contract and the coherence of this act as a whole.  
When, in the common intention of the parties, several contracts contribute to the same transaction, they are interpreted in light thereof.

###### Article 1333

In case of doubt, the freely negotiated contract is interpreted against the creditor and in favor of the debtor, and the contract of adhesion against the party who proposed it.

###### Article 1334

When a clause is susceptible of two meanings, the one that confers an effect upon it prevails over the one that produces no effect.

#### Chapter V: The effects of the contract

##### Section I

The effects of the contract between the parties Sub-section 1: Binding force

###### Article 1335

Contracts may be modified or revoked only by the mutual consent of the parties, or for the causes authorized by law.

###### Article 1336

Contracts bind not only to what is expressed therein, but also to all the consequences given to them by equity, usage or law.

###### Article 1337

If an unforeseeable change of circumstances at the time of the conclusion of the contract renders performance excessively onerous for a party who had not agreed to assume the risk thereof, that party may request a renegotiation of the contract from its co-contracting party. It continues to perform its obligations during the renegotiation.  
In case of refusal or failure of the renegotiation, the parties may agree to the termination of the contract on the date and under the conditions they determine. Failing that, one of the parties may apply to the judge to terminate the contract, on the date and under the conditions he sets.

###### Article 1338

There is simulation when the parties conclude an apparent contract that contradicts a hidden contract. In this case, the latter, also called a counter-letter, produces effect between the contracting parties.  
However, any counter-letter having as its object an increase in the price stipulated in the deed of transfer of a ministerial office is null and void.  

Likewise, any contract having the purpose of concealing part of the price is null and void when it relates to a sale of immovable property, a transfer of a business or clientele, a transfer of a right to a lease, or the benefit of a promise of lease relating to all or part of an immovable property and all or part of the

balance of an exchange or partition comprising immovable property, a business or a clientele.

###### Sous-section 2 : Effet translatif Article 1339

In contracts whose purpose is the alienation of ownership or the transfer of another right, the transfer takes place upon the conclusion of the contract.  
This transfer may be deferred by the will of the parties, the nature of the things or by operation of law.  

The transfer of ownership entails transfer of the risks of the thing. However, the debtor of the obligation to deliver recovers the burden thereof from the time of his being placed in default, either by a summons or an act containing sufficient notice, or, if the contract so provides, by the mere enforceability of the obligation, all subject to the rules provided for in Article 1364, paragraph 3.

###### Article 1340

The obligation to deliver the thing entails an obligation to preserve it until delivery, by exercising all the care of a reasonable person.  
This obligation is more or less extensive in relation to certain contracts, whose effects, in this respect, are explained under the titles that concern them.

###### Article 1341

Where two successive purchasers of the same corporeal movable derive their right from the same person, the one who took possession of that movable first is preferred, even if his right is later, provided that he is in good faith.  
Where two successive purchasers of rights relating to the same immovable derive their right from the same person, the one who first published his title of acquisition executed in authentic form in the land registry is preferred, even if his right is later, provided that he is in good faith.

##### Section II

The effects of the contract with regard to third parties Sous-section 1: General provisions

###### Article 1342

The contract creates obligations only between the parties.  

Third parties may neither demand performance of the contract nor be compelled to perform it, subject to the provisions of this section and those of Articles 1526 to 1529.

###### Article 1343

Third parties must respect the legal situation created by the contract, which is enforceable against them. They may rely on it, in particular for evidentiary purposes.

###### Article 1344

In case of simulation, the counter-letter is not enforceable against third parties, who may nevertheless rely on it.

###### Article 1345

Where a person acts on behalf of another but without informing the person with whom he enters into the contract, the latter, upon learning of the existence of the nominee agreement, may rely on the act that had been concealed from him or on the act entered into with the nominee. On the other hand, if that third party contractor participated in the establishment of the simulation, he may rely only on the hidden contract.  
In such a case, in the presence of a contract transferring ownership, the nominee agreement operates a transfer directly from the patrimony of the nominee to that of the principal, without passing through the patrimony of the nominee.

###### Sous-section 2 : Le porte-fort et la stipulation pour autrui Article 1346

One may undertake in one's own name only for oneself.

###### Article 1347

One may act as guarantor by promising the act of a third party.  

The promisor is released from all obligation if the third party performs the promised act. Otherwise, he may be ordered to pay damages.  

Where the guarantee has as its object the ratification of an undertaking, the latter is retroactively validated by the ratification made by the third party, as of the date on which the guarantee was subscribed, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1348

One may stipulate for another.  

One of the contracting parties, the stipulator, may cause the other, the promisor, to promise to perform a benefit for the benefit of a third party, the beneficiary. The third party beneficiary may be a future person but must be precisely designated or capable of being determined at the time of performance of the promise. The stipulator may reserve the right to designate the third party beneficiary when the time comes.

###### Article 1349

The third party beneficiary is vested with a direct right to the benefit against the promisor from the time of the stipulation.  

Nevertheless the stipulator may freely revoke the stipulation as long as the third party beneficiary has not accepted it.  

The stipulation becomes irrevocable at the moment when the acceptance reaches the stipulator or the promisor.

###### Article 1350

The revocation may emanate only from the stipulator or, after his death, from his heirs. The latter may proceed thereto only upon the expiration of a period of three months from the day on which they placed the third party beneficiary in default to accept it.  
If it is not accompanied by the designation of a new beneficiary, the revocation benefits, as the case may be, the stipulator or his heirs.  

The revocation takes effect as soon as the third party beneficiary or the promisor has had knowledge of it. When it is made by will, it takes effect at the moment of death.  

The third party initially designated as beneficiary is then deemed never to have benefited from the stipulation made for his benefit.

###### Article 1351

The acceptance may emanate from the beneficiary or, after his death, from his heirs. It may occur even after the death of the stipulator or the promisor.  
The acceptance may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1352

The stipulator may himself require from the promisor the performance of his undertaking toward the beneficiary.

##### Section III : La durée du contrat Article 1353

Perpetual undertakings are prohibited.  

Each contracting party may put an end to them under the conditions provided for contracts of indefinite duration.

###### Article 1354

Where the contract is concluded for an indefinite duration, each party may put an end to it at any time, subject to respecting the contractually provided notice period or, failing that, a reasonable period.

###### Article 1355

Where the contract is concluded for a determinate duration, each party must perform it until its term.  
The contract may be extended if the contracting parties manifest their will before its expiration. The initial term of the contract is thus postponed to a later date. The extension may not, however, affect the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1356

No one may require the renewal of the contract, except by provision of law or agreement of the parties.  

In case of renewal, a new contract succeeds the previous one. Their content is identical but, except where the law provides otherwise, the duration of the new contract is indefinite.

###### Article 1357

Where upon the expiration of the term of a contract concluded for a determinate duration, the contracting parties continue to perform its obligations, there is tacit renewal.  
This produces the same effects as the renewal of the contract.

##### Section IV : La cession de contrat Article 1358

A contracting party, the assignor, may assign his capacity as party to the contract to a third party, the assignee, with the agreement of his co-contractor, the assigned party.  

This agreement may be given in advance, in particular in the contract concluded between the future assignor and assigned party, in which case the assignment takes effect with regard to the assigned party when the contract concluded between the assignor and the assignee is notified to him or when he acknowledges it.  
The assignment must be recorded in writing, on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1359

If the assigned party has expressly consented thereto, the assignment of contract releases the assignor for the future.  

In the absence of such express consent, the assignor is held jointly and severally liable for the performance of the contract. It is possible for the parties to exclude certain rights and obligations from the assignment.

###### Article 1360

By effect of the assignment carried out, the assignee becomes a party to the initial contract.

The assignee may raise against the party assigned to the defences inherent to the debt, such as payment, prescription, nullity that is not purely personal to the assignor, the defence of non-performance, termination or set-off of connected debts. The assignee may not raise against the party assigned to defences personal to the assignor, such as incapacity or a defect of consent affecting the latter's will.

The party assigned to may raise against the assignee all defences that could have been raised against the assignor.

###### Article 1361

If the assignor is not released by the party assigned to, the security interests that may have been granted subsist. In the contrary case, security interests granted by third parties subsist only with their consent.  
If the assignor is released, his joint and several co-debtors remain liable after deduction of his share in the debt.

##### Section V: Non-performance of the contract Article 1362

The debtor bound by an obligation of means has undertaken to implement all means necessary to perform his obligation, without undertaking to obtain that result. Non-performance of the contract requires that the creditor demonstrate fault of the debtor in the performance of his obligation.  
The debtor bound by an obligation of result has undertaken to obtain the result provided for contractually. He is at fault by the mere demonstration of the absence of the promised result, unless he proves that the non-performance is due to an event of force majeure.

###### Article 1363

The party towards whom the undertaking has not been performed, or has been imperfectly performed, may: refuse to perform or suspend performance of his own obligation; pursue specific performance of the obligation; request or, where the law so authorises, notify the other party of a reduction of the price; bring about termination of the contract; claim reparation for the consequences of non-performance.  
Remedies that are not incompatible may be cumulated; specific performance of the contract and termination are not compatible. Damages may always be added to the remedy pronounced.

In case of non-performance of a contractual obligation, neither the debtor nor the creditor may evade the application of provisions specific to contractual liability in order to opt in favour of rules specific to extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1364

In contractual matters the external cause may result from a fortuitous event, the act of a third party or the act of the co-contractor. The external cause constitutes a case of force majeure when it prevents

performance of his obligation by the debtor, results from an event which, escaping the control of the latter, could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time of conclusion of the contract and whose effects cannot be avoided by appropriate measures.

If the impediment is temporary, performance of the obligation is suspended, unless the resulting delay would justify termination of the contract.

If the impediment is definitive, as the case may be, the impossibility of performing the prestation either releases the debtor to the corresponding extent, or, if it constitutes a case of force majeure, entails termination of the contract by operation of law and releases the parties from their obligations. On the other hand, the debtor remains bound if he has agreed to assume the external cause or if he has been previously placed on notice. In the latter case, where the impossibility of performing results from the loss of the thing due, the debtor placed on notice is nevertheless released if he proves that the loss would similarly have occurred if the obligation had been performed. In all cases, the debtor is bound to assign to his creditor the rights and actions attached to the thing.

###### Sous-section 1: The defence of non-performance Article 1365

A party to a synallagmatic contract may refuse to perform his obligation, totally or partially, even though it is due, if the other does not perform his own.  
The refusal of performance must not be disproportionate in relation to the breach reproached to the other.

###### Article 1366

A party may, subject to the same reservation, suspend performance of his obligation where it is manifest that his co-contractor will not perform at the due date and that the consequences of such non-performance are sufficiently serious for him.  
This suspension must be notified as soon as possible.

###### Sous-section 2: Specific performance Article 1367

The creditor of an obligation may, after placing on notice, pursue its specific performance, unless such performance is impossible or there exists a manifest disproportion between its cost for the debtor and its interest for the creditor.

###### Article 1368

After placing on notice, the creditor may also, within a reasonable time and at a reasonable cost, have the obligation performed himself or, upon prior authorisation of the judge, destroy what has been done in violation thereof. He may claim from the debtor reimbursement of the sums committed for that purpose.  
He may also request in court that the debtor advance the sums necessary for such performance or such destruction.

###### Sous-section 3: Reduction of the price Article 1369

The creditor may, after placing on notice, accept imperfect performance of the contract and request a proportional reduction of the price.  
If he has not yet paid, the creditor notifies the debtor as soon as possible of his decision to reduce the price.

###### Sous-section 4: Termination

###### Article 1370

Termination results either from the application of a termination clause or, in case of sufficiently serious non-performance, from a notification by the creditor to the debtor or from a court decision.

###### Article 1371

The termination clause specifies the undertakings whose non-performance will entail termination of the contract.

Termination is subject to an unsuccessful placing on notice, if it has not been agreed that the latter would result from the mere fact of non-performance. The placing on notice produces effect only if it expressly mentions the termination clause.

The termination clause must be implemented in good faith by the creditor. On the other hand, in case of non-performance of his undertaking by the debtor, his good faith has no effect on the acquisition of the termination clause.

###### Article 1372

The creditor may, at his own risk, terminate the contract by way of notification. Except in case of urgency, he must first place the defaulting debtor on notice to satisfy his undertaking within a reasonable time.  
The placing on notice expressly mentions that in default of the debtor satisfying his obligation, the creditor will be entitled to terminate the contract.

Where non-performance persists, the creditor notifies the debtor of the termination of the contract and the reasons motivating it.

The debtor may at any time seize the judge to contest the termination. The creditor must then prove the seriousness of the non-performance.

###### Article 1373

Termination may, in any event, be requested in court.

It is however possible to renounce in advance the right to request judicial termination of the contract.

###### Article 1374

The judge may, according to the circumstances, declare or pronounce termination, or order performance of the contract possibly granting a time period to the debtor, or award only damages.

###### Article 1375

Termination brings the contract to an end.

Termination takes effect, as the case may be, either under the conditions provided for by the termination clause, or on the date of receipt by the debtor of the notification made by the creditor, or on the date fixed by the judge or, failing that, on the day of the summons to court.  
Where the exchanged performances could only find their utility through the complete performance of the terminated contract, the parties must restore the entirety of what they procured from one another. Where the exchanged performances found their utility progressively through the reciprocal performance of the contract, there is no need for restitution for the period prior to the last performance that did not receive its counterpart; in this case, the termination is qualified as rescission.  

Restitutions take place under the conditions provided for in articles 1577 to 1585.

###### Article 1376

Termination does not affect clauses relating to the settlement of disputes, nor those intended to produce effect even in the event of termination, such as confidentiality and non-competition clauses.

###### Sous-section 5

Reparation for loss resulting from non-performance of the contract Article 1377
Reparation for loss resulting from non-performance of the contract falls under the provisions of articles 1403 et seq.  

Sous-titre II: Civil liability

Chapitre Ier: Preliminary provisions Article 1378
Loss resulting from bodily injury is always repaired on the basis of the rules of extra-contractual liability, even where it is caused in connection with the performance of the contract.  
However, the victim may invoke the express stipulations of the contract where they are more favourable to him.

###### Article 1379

Where non-performance of the contract causes damage to a third party, the third party may only seek reparation for its consequences from the debtor on the basis of extra-contractual liability. He must then demonstrate the reality of one of the generative facts referred to in section II of chapter II.  
However, where the third party has a legitimate interest in the proper performance of a contract, he may invoke, on the basis of contractual liability, a contractual breach provided that it has caused him damage. The conditions and limits of liability that apply in relations between the contracting parties are then enforceable against him. On the other hand, any clause that limits the contractual liability of a contracting party towards third parties is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapitre II: The conditions of civil liability

##### Section I

Provisions common to contractual and extra-contractual liability Sous-section 1: The generative fact of liability

###### Article 1380

The generative fact of extra-contractual liability is defined by articles 1391 et seq. The generative fact of contractual liability is defined by articles 1403 et seq.

###### Article 1381

A person who performs an act is not civilly liable:	prescribed or authorised by legislative or regulatory provisions;  
	ordered by legitimate authority, except where that act is manifestly unlawful;	ordered by the necessity of legitimate defence of himself, others, or his property;	necessary for the safeguarding of the person or property in response to an actual or imminent danger that threatens himself, others or property.  
All subject to the limits placed on these acts by the criminal code.

###### Article 1382

Nor does a harmful act infringing a right or interest that the victim could dispose of give rise to liability, if the victim consented to it.

###### Sous-section 2: Recoverable loss Article 1383

Any certain loss resulting from damage and consisting in the infringement of a lawful interest, whether patrimonial or extra-patrimonial, is recoverable.  

Future loss is recoverable as soon as it is certain and direct.

###### Article 1384

Expenses incurred by the claimant to prevent the imminent occurrence of damage or to avoid its aggravation, as well as to reduce its consequences, constitute recoverable loss provided that they were reasonably incurred.

###### Article 1385

Only the present and certain disappearance of a favourable eventuality constitutes a recoverable loss of chance.  
The reparation corresponds to the lost chance and not to the advantage that this chance would have provided if it had materialised.

###### Sous-section 3: The causal link Article 1386

A causal link must exist between the act imputed to the defendant and the damage. Proof of the causal link is established by any means.

###### Article 1387

Where bodily injury is caused by an unidentified person among identified persons acting jointly or carrying on a similar activity, they are jointly and severally liable to answer for the whole. However, each of the co-responsible parties may demonstrate that he cannot have caused the damage.  
The responsible parties contribute among themselves in proportion to the probability that each caused the damage.

###### Sous-section 4: Clauses limiting or excluding liability Article 1388

Clauses having the object or effect of excluding or limiting liability are in principle valid, both in contractual and extra-contractual matters.  

However, liability may not be limited or excluded by contract in the event of bodily injury.

###### Article 1389

In contractual matters, clauses limiting or excluding liability have no effect in the event of gross or intentional fault.  
They are deemed unwritten where they deprive the debtor's essential obligation of its substance.

###### Article 1390

In extra-contractual matters, liability for fault may not be excluded or limited.

##### Section II: Provisions specific to extra-contractual liability

###### § 1. Liability for fault Article 1391

Any act whatsoever of man, which causes damage to another, obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to repair it.  

Each person is liable for the damage he has caused not only by his act, but also by his negligence or imprudence.

###### § 2. Liability for things Article 1392

Any harmful act of a thing automatically engages the liability of the person who has custody of it.  

The custodian is the person who has the use, control and direction of the thing at the time of the harmful act. The owner is presumed to be the custodian of the thing.  
The act of the thing and its causal role are presumed where the thing, in motion, came into contact with the seat of the damage. In other cases, it is for the victim to prove the act of the thing, by establishing either the defect of the thing, or the abnormality of its position, state or behaviour, and its role in the occurrence of the damage.

###### Article 1393

The owner of an animal, or the person who uses it, while it is in his use, is liable for the damage that the animal has caused, whether the animal was under his custody, or whether it had strayed or escaped.

###### Article 1394

The owner of a building is liable for the damage caused by its collapse, where it occurred as a result of lack of maintenance or a defect in its construction.  
A person who holds, under any title whatsoever, all or part of the immovable property or movable property in which a fire broke out shall only be liable, towards third parties, for damage caused by that fire if it is proved that it must be attributed to his fault or to the fault of persons for whom he is responsible.  

The preceding paragraph does not apply to relations between owners and tenants, which remain governed by the laws concerning them.

###### § 3. Liability for the acts of others

###### Article 1395

Liability for the acts of others requires proof of an act capable of engaging the personal liability of the direct author of the damage.

###### Article 1396

The following are liable by operation of law for the acts of a minor: his parents, insofar as they exercise parental authority; his guardian or guardians, insofar as they are responsible for the person of the minor; the natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis the minor's way of life. In this case, the liability of that minor's parents cannot be engaged.

###### Article 1397

The natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis the way of life of an adult placed under his supervision is liable by operation of law for the acts of that adult.

###### Article 1398

Other persons who, by contract, assume in a professional capacity, such as teachers and craftsmen with regard to their pupils and apprentices, a mission of supervision of others or of organization and control of the activity of others, are liable for the acts of the natural person supervised, during the time they are under their supervision.  
They may be exonerated from this liability by demonstrating that, in the exercise of their mission, they did not commit any fault of supervision or of organization and control.

###### Article 1399

The principal is liable by operation of law for damage caused by his agent. The relationship of agency presupposes the power of the principal to give the agent orders or instructions in relation to the performance of his functions.  
In case of transfer of the relationship of agency, this liability falls upon the beneficiary of the transfer.  

The principal or the beneficiary of the transfer is not liable if he proves that the agent acted outside the functions for which he was employed, without authorization and for purposes unrelated to his duties. Nor is he liable if he establishes collusion between the agent and the victim.  

The agent engages his personal liability in case of intentional fault, or when, without authorization, he acted for purposes unrelated to his duties. He engages it only in these cases.

###### § 4. Liability for abnormal neighborhood disturbances Article 1400

No one must cause another an abnormal neighborhood disturbance.

###### Article 1401

Neighborhood disturbance is sanctioned by the judge as soon as it is excessive.  

When it involves a fault committed in the performance of an obligation arising from a contract, the rules of contractual liability apply between the parties to the act. In other cases, the measure of liability is that of the excessive nature of the disturbance without any regard to the existence or not of a fault of the defendant.

###### Article 1402

When a damaging activity is carried out lawfully, the judge may nevertheless order reasonable measures to stop the disturbance and, failing the ability to do so without jeopardizing the activity, award damages to the victim of the disturbance.  
However, compensation for damage caused by nuisances resulting from an agricultural, industrial, artisanal, commercial or aeronautical activity that is carried out in compliance with legislation is excluded, as soon as the claimant settled in the location concerned after the activities started.

##### Section III: Provisions specific to contractual liability Article 1403

Any non-performance of the contract having caused damage to the creditor obliges the debtor to answer for it.

###### Article 1404

Unless the non-performance is definitive, damages are due only if the debtor has previously been given notice to perform within a reasonable time.

###### Article 1405

The debtor is condemned, if appropriate, to the payment of damages either by reason of non-performance of the obligation, or by reason of delay in performance, if he does not prove that performance was prevented by an external cause.

###### Article 1406

The damages due to the creditor are, in general, the loss he has suffered and the gain of which he has been deprived, subject to the exceptions and modifications below.

###### Article 1407

The debtor is liable only for damages that were foreseen or that could have been foreseen at the time of conclusion of the contract, except when the non-performance is due to gross or fraudulent fault.  
Fault is gross when its author adopts behavior of extreme gravity, bordering on fraud, and denoting his inability to fulfill his obligations.  

Fault is fraudulent when, deliberately, the debtor refuses to perform his contractual obligations, even if this refusal is not dictated by the intention to harm his contracting party.

###### Article 1408

Even when non-performance of the contract results from gross or fraudulent fault, damages include only what is an immediate and direct consequence of the non-performance.

###### Article 1409

A penalty clause is one by which a person, to ensure the performance of an agreement, undertakes to pay damages agreed upon as a lump sum in case of non-performance of his obligations.  
In the presence of a penalty clause, no greater or lesser penalty may be awarded to the other party. Nevertheless, the judge may, even of his own motion, moderate or increase the amount thus agreed upon, in cases where it is manifestly excessive or derisory.  

When the undertaking has been performed in part, the agreed penalty may be reduced by the judge, even of his own motion, in proportion to the benefit that the partial performance has provided to the creditor, without prejudice to the application of the preceding paragraph.  

Any stipulation contrary to the two preceding paragraphs is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1410

Whether or not the original obligation contains a term within which it must be performed, the penalty is incurred only when the person who is obliged is in default, except if the non-performance is definitive.

###### Article 1411

The creditor, instead of demanding the penalty stipulated against the debtor who is in default, may pursue the performance of the principal obligation. The creditor may not, however, demand at the same time, except on a subsidiary basis, the principal and the penalty, unless it was stipulated for simple delay.

###### Article 1412

The nullity of the principal obligation entails that of the penalty clause. The nullity of the latter does not entail that of the principal obligation.

###### Article 1413

Damages due by reason of delay in payment of an obligation of a sum of money consist of interest at the legal rate. They are due only from the day of notice, except in the case where the law makes them run by operation of law.  
Accrued income, such as rents, arrears of perpetual or life annuities, produces interest from the day of the demand or the agreement.  

These damages are due without the creditor being required to prove any loss.  
The creditor to whom his debtor in delay has caused harm independent of this delay, may obtain damages distinct from default interest.

###### Article 1414

In all matters, an award of damages bears interest at the legal rate even in the absence of a request or special provision in the judgment. Unless otherwise provided by law, such interest runs from the date the judgment is delivered, unless the judge decides otherwise.  
In the event of pure and simple confirmation by the court of appeal of a decision awarding damages in compensation for harm, the latter bears interest by operation of law at the legal rate from the first instance judgment. In other cases, damages awarded on appeal bear interest from the date of the appellate decision. The court of appeal may always derogate from the provisions of this paragraph.

#### Chapitre III : L'exonération de la responsabilité Article 1415

In non-contractual matters, external cause consists of fortuitous event, act of a third party or act of the victim. External cause is totally exonerating if it has the characteristics of force majeure. This is the case when the event is beyond the control of the defendant or the person for whom he must answer, and the occurrence or consequences of which they could not avoid by appropriate measures.  
In contractual matters, force majeure and its effects are defined in Article 1364.

###### Article 1416

The victim's breach of contractual obligations, fault or that of a person for whom the victim must answer are partially exonerating when they contributed to the occurrence of the harm.  
In case of bodily injury, only gross fault may result in partial exoneration.

###### Article 1417

Unless it has the characteristics of force majeure, fault committed by a victim deprived of discernment has no exonerating effect.

###### Article 1418

Fault or contractual non-performance that may be raised against the direct victim may also be raised against victims of consequential loss.

#### Chapitre IV

Les effets de la responsabilité civile Section I: Règles générales

###### Sous-section 1 : La sanction

###### § 1. La réparation Article 1419

The purpose of reparation is to erase the consequences of the harmful act and aims at complete restoration. The victim must derive neither loss nor profit from it.  
Reparation may take the form of reparation in kind or by monetary equivalent. These two forms of reparation may be combined in order to ensure full reparation of the victim's loss.

###### Article 1420

Reparation in kind must make it possible to eliminate, reduce or compensate for the harm. It may not be imposed on the victim.  
Nor may it be ordered in case of impossibility or manifest disproportion between its cost for the person liable and its benefit for the victim. Subject to the same reservations, the judge may authorize the victim to take reparation in kind measures himself at the expense of the person liable. The latter may be ordered to advance the necessary sums.

###### Article 1421

Damages are assessed at the date of the judgment, taking into account all circumstances that may have affected the nature and value of the loss since the date the harm became apparent, as well as its reasonably foreseeable evolution.  
In case of aggravation of the harm subsequent to the judgment, the victim may request additional compensation for the resulting loss.  
Each head of loss is assessed separately.

###### Article 1422

Except in case of bodily injury, damages are reduced whenever the victim has not taken useful and reasonable measures, particularly in light of his contributory capacity, to avoid aggravation of his loss.

###### § 2. La cessation de l'illicite

###### Article 1423

In non-contractual matters, independently of reparation for any loss suffered, the judge may always prescribe reasonable measures to prevent harm or stop the unlawful interference to which the plaintiff is exposed.

###### § 3. L'amende civile Article 1424

In non-contractual matters, when the author of the harm has deliberately committed a fault with a view to obtaining a gain or saving, the judge may order him, at the request of the victim or the public prosecutor and by a specially reasoned decision, to pay a civil fine.

###### Article 1425

This fine is proportionate to the seriousness of the fault committed, the contributory capacity of the author and the profits he will have derived from it.  
The civil fine may not exceed ten times the amount of the profit realized.  
If the person liable is a legal person, the fine may be increased to 5% of the amount of the highest turnover excluding taxes realized in Djibouti during one of the financial years closed since the financial year preceding that during which the fault was committed.

###### Article 1426

This civil fine is allocated to the Public Treasury. It is not insurable.

###### Sous-section 2 : L'incidence de la pluralité de responsables Article 1427

When several persons are liable for the same harm, they are jointly and severally liable to make reparation to the victim.

###### Article 1428

If all or some of the persons liable for the same harm have committed a fault, they contribute among themselves in proportion to the seriousness and causal role of the generating act attributable to them.  
If none of them has committed a fault, they contribute in proportion to the causal role of the generating act attributable to them and, failing that, in equal shares.

##### Section II : Règles particulières

###### Sous-section 1

Règles particulières à la réparation des préjudices résultant d'un dommage corporel

###### Article 1429

Any stipulation contrary to the provisions of this subsection is deemed unwritten, unless it is more favorable to the victim.

###### Article 1430

Losses must be assessed without taking into account any predispositions of the victim when the condition resulting therefrom was only caused or revealed by the harmful act.

###### Article 1431

Subject to special provisions, patrimonial and extra-patrimonial losses resulting from bodily injury give rise to full compensation.

###### Article 1432

Sums paid to the victim for compensatory purposes by third-party payers give rise to no action or subrogation recourse against the person liable or his insurer except in the cases and under the conditions provided by law.  
In the event that the insolvency of the person liable would prevent full compensation of the victim, the latter shall have priority over the third-party payer for what remains owed to him by the person liable.  

The victim's fault may only reduce his right to compensation on the portion of his loss that has not been repaired by the third-party payer's benefits. The latter is entitled to the balance of the debt charged to the person liable.

###### Sous-section 2

Règles particulières à la réparation des préjudices résultant d'un dommage matériel

###### Article 1433

In case of damage to a corporeal thing, the compensation is the lesser of the two sums representing the cost of restoration and that of replacement of the thing, without taking into account its wear and tear or any capital gain inherent in the repair.  
When the thing can be neither restored nor replaced, the compensation is the value that the thing would have had on the date of the decision, in its condition prior to the harm.  

If, at the request of the victim, the damaged thing is not returned to the person liable in its current condition, its residual value is deducted from the compensation.

###### Article 1434

Where applicable, the compensation also covers deprivation of enjoyment of the damaged thing, loss of profits or any other loss.

###### Sous-section 3

Special rules for the reparation of harm resulting from environmental damage

###### Article 1435

Any person responsible for ecological harm is required to repair it.

###### Article 1436

Reparable ecological harm is that which consists of a non-negligible injury to the elements or functions of ecosystems or to the collective benefits derived by humans from the environment.

###### Article 1437

The action for reparation of ecological harm is open to any person having standing and interest to act, such as the State or any public authority and public establishments as well as approved associations or associations created at least five years before the date of commencement of proceedings which have as their object the protection of nature and the defense of the environment.  
Independently of the action for reparation of harm possibly suffered or in parallel with it, the judge may always prescribe reasonable measures appropriate to prevent the damage or to stop the unlawful disturbance to which the environment is exposed.

###### Article 1438

Reparation of ecological harm is carried out as a priority in kind.  

In case of impossibility or insufficiency of reparation measures, the judge orders the person responsible to pay damages, allocated to the reparation of the environment, to the plaintiff or, if the plaintiff cannot take the measures useful for this purpose, to the State.  

The assessment of ecological harm takes into account the reparation measures which have, where applicable, already been able to take place.

###### Article 1439

In case of a penalty payment, it is liquidated by the judge for the benefit of the plaintiff, who allocates it to the reparation of the environment or, if the plaintiff cannot take the measures useful for this purpose, for the benefit of the State, which allocates it to this same purpose.  
The judge who orders a penalty payment with a view to the reparation of ecological harm has the power to liquidate it.

###### Sous-section 4

Special rules for liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury from traffic accidents

###### Article 1440

Liability for land motor vehicles is governed by the provisions of the Law on liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury from traffic accidents (Law No. 40/AN/99/4ème L of 8 June 1999).

###### Sous-section 5

Special rules for liability for defective products Article 1441
The provisions of this subsection apply to the reparation of damage which results from injury to a person or that, of an amount exceeding 100,000 FD, which results from injury to property other than the defective product itself.

###### Article 1442

A product within the meaning of this subsection is any movable property, even if it is incorporated into immovable property, including products of the soil, livestock, hunting and fishing. Electricity is considered a product.  
Such a product is considered defective within the meaning of this subsection when it does not offer the safety which one is legitimately entitled to expect having regard to the circumstances and in particular to the presentation of the product, the use which can reasonably be expected of it and the time when it was put into circulation. A product may not, however, be considered defective for the sole reason that another, more advanced product, was subsequently put into circulation.

###### Article 1443

The producer is liable for damage caused by a defect in a product which he has put into circulation, whether or not that producer is bound by a contract with the victim.  
A product is put into circulation when the producer has voluntarily parted with it. A product is put into circulation only once.

###### Article 1444

A producer within the meaning of these provisions is, when acting in a professional capacity, the manufacturer of a finished product, the producer of a raw material, the manufacturer of a component part. Any person acting in a professional capacity who presents himself as a producer by affixing to the product his name, trademark or other distinctive sign is treated as a producer for the application of this chapter;  
Persons whose liability may be sought on the basis of articles 1954 to 1962 and 1819 are not considered producers within the meaning of this chapter.  

If the producer cannot be identified, the seller, the lessor, with the exception of the lessor in a finance lease or a lessor similar to a lessor in a finance lease, or any other professional supplier, is liable for the lack of safety of the product, under the same conditions as the producer, unless he identifies his own supplier or the producer, within three months from the date on which the victim's claim was notified to him.  

The supplier may bring a warranty action against the producer, in which case his recourse against the producer follows the same rules as the claim from the direct victim of the defect. However, he must do so within one year following the date of his being summoned to court.

###### Article 1445

In case of damage caused by the defect of a product incorporated into another, the producer of the component part and the one who carried out the incorporation are jointly and severally liable.  
The producer of the component part is not, however, liable if he establishes that the defect is attributable to the design of the product into which that part was incorporated or to the instructions given by the producer of that product.

###### Article 1446

The plaintiff must prove the damage, the defect and the causal link between the defect and the damage.  

The producer is liable without fault unless he proves:
1° That he had not put the product into circulation;  
2° That, having regard to the circumstances, there is reason to believe that the defect which caused the damage did not exist at the time when the product was put into circulation by him or that this defect arose subsequently;  
3° That the product was not intended for sale or any other form of distribution;  
4° That the state of scientific and technical knowledge, at the time when he put the product into circulation, did not enable the existence of the defect to be detected; this ground of exoneration is excluded when the damage was caused by an element of the human body or by products derived from it;  
5° Or that the defect is due to the compliance of the product with mandatory rules of a legislative or regulatory nature.  

The producer cannot be exonerated on the pretext that the product was manufactured in compliance with the rules of the art or existing standards or that it was the subject of an administrative authorization.

###### Article 1447

The producer's liability may be reduced or eliminated, taking into account all the circumstances, when the damage is caused jointly by a defect in the product and by the fault of the victim or of a person for whom the victim is responsible.  

The producer's liability towards the victim is not reduced by the act of a third party who contributed to the occurrence of the damage.

###### Article 1448

Clauses which aim to exclude or limit liability for defective products are prohibited and deemed unwritten.  
However, for damage caused to property which is not used by the victim principally for his private use or consumption, clauses stipulated between professionals are valid.

###### Article 1449

Except in case of fault of the producer, the producer's liability, based on the provisions of this chapter, is extinguished ten years after the putting into circulation of the actual product which caused the damage unless, during this period, the victim has brought legal proceedings.

###### Article 1450

The action for damages based on the provisions of this subsection is time-barred after a period of three years from the date on which the claimant became aware or should have become aware of the damage, the defect and the identity of the producer.

###### Article 1451

The provisions of this chapter do not affect the rights which the victim of damage may invoke under the law of contractual or non-contractual liability or under a special liability regime.  
The producer remains liable for the consequences of his fault and that of the persons for whom he is responsible.  

Sous-titre III: Les quasi-contrats Article 1452
Quasi-contracts are purely voluntary acts which result in an obligation on the part of the person who benefits from them without being entitled to do so, and sometimes an obligation on the part of their author towards others.  
The quasi-contracts governed by this subtitle are: management of affairs, undue payment and unjust enrichment.  
Chapitre Ier: La gestion d'affaires

###### Article 1453

A person who, without being obliged to do so, knowingly and usefully manages the affairs of another, without the knowledge or opposition of the owner of those affairs, is subject, in the performance of the legal and material acts of his management, to all the obligations of a mandatary.  
The usefulness of the manager's act is assessed on the day it was performed.

###### Article 1454

This manager of affairs is required to bring to his management all the care of a reasonable person. He must continue the management begun, until the owner of the affairs or his successor is in a position to provide for it.  

The judge may, according to the circumstances, moderate the damages resulting from the faults or negligence of the manager.

###### Article 1455

The person whose affairs have been usefully managed must fulfil the commitments entered into in his interest by the manager.  
He shall reimburse the manager for useful or necessary expenses incurred in his interest, and compensate him for the damage he has suffered by reason of his management.  
The sums advanced by the manager bear interest from the day of payment.

###### Article 1456

Ratification of the management by the owner constitutes express mandate.

###### Article 1457

The fact that the manager has a personal interest in taking charge of the affairs of another does not exclude the application of the rules of management of affairs.  
In this case, the burden of commitments, expenses and damages is distributed in proportion to the interests of each in the common affair.

###### Article 1458

If the action of the manager does not meet the conditions of management of affairs but nevertheless benefits the owner of those affairs, the latter must compensate the manager according to the rules of unjust enrichment.

#### Chapitre II : Le paiement de l'indu Article 1459

Every payment presupposes a debt; what has been received without being due is subject to restitution.  
Restitution is not admitted in respect of natural obligations which have been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1460

A person who receives by error or knowingly what is not due to him must restore it to the person from whom he unduly received it.

###### Article 1461

A person who by error or under duress has discharged the debt of another may bring an action for restitution against the creditor.  
Nevertheless this right ceases in the case where the creditor, as a result of the payment, has destroyed his title or abandoned the securities which guaranteed his claim.  
Restitution may also be claimed from the person whose debt has been discharged by error.

###### Article 1462

Restitution is subject to the rules laid down in articles 1577 to 1585 It may be reduced if the payment proceeds from a fault.

#### Chapitre III : L'enrichissement sans cause

###### Article 1463

Apart from cases of management of affairs and undue payment, a person who benefits from unjust enrichment at the expense of another owes to the person who is thereby impoverished compensation equal to the lesser of the two values of the enrichment and the impoverishment.

###### Article 1464

Enrichment is without cause when it does not proceed either from the performance of an obligation by the impoverished person or from his gratuitous intention.

###### Article 1465

There is no ground for compensation if the impoverishment proceeds from an act performed by the impoverished person with a view to personal profit.  
Compensation may be moderated by the judge if the impoverishment proceeds from a fault of the impoverished person.

### Titre IV : Du régime général des obligations

Chapitre Ier: Les modalités de l'obligation

##### Section I : L'obligation conditionnelle Article 1466

An obligation is conditional when it depends on a future and uncertain event, or on an event which has already occurred but is still unknown to the parties.  
In the first case, the condition is either suspensive, when the coming into existence of the obligation depends on its fulfilment, or resolutory, when its fulfilment brings about the annulment of the legal act to which it relates.  
In the second case, the obligation has its effect from the day on which it was contracted.

###### Article 1467

Any condition of an impossible thing, or contrary to good morals, or prohibited by law is null, and renders null the agreement which depends on it. This nullity is absolute.  
The condition not to do an impossible thing does not render null the obligation contracted under this condition.

###### Article 1468

Any obligation is null when it has been contracted under a condition the realisation of which depends solely on the will of the debtor.  
This nullity, which is relative, cannot however be invoked when the obligation has been performed with full knowledge by the person who was bound by it.

###### Article 1469

Every condition must be fulfilled in the manner which the parties probably wished and intended it to be.  
The suspensive condition is deemed fulfilled when it is the debtor, obliged under this condition, who has prevented its fulfilment.  

The resolutory condition is deemed to have failed if its fulfilment has been brought about by the party who had an interest in it.

###### Article 1470

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will occur within a fixed time, this condition is deemed to have failed when the time has expired without the event having occurred. If there is no fixed time, the condition may always be fulfilled; and it is deemed to have failed only when it has become certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1471

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will not occur within a fixed time, this condition is fulfilled when that time has expired without the event having occurred: it is also fulfilled, if before the term it is certain that the event will not occur; and if there is no fixed time, it is fulfilled only when it is certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1472

A party is free to renounce the condition stipulated in his exclusive interest, as long as it is not fulfilled.

###### Article 1473

The fulfilled condition has a retroactive effect to the day on which the commitment was contracted. If the creditor died before the fulfilment of the condition, his rights pass to his heir.

###### Article 1474

Before the suspensive condition is fulfilled, the debtor must refrain from any act which would prevent the proper performance of the obligation.  
The creditor may, before the condition is fulfilled, exercise all acts preserving his right and challenge the acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.  
What has been paid may be recovered as long as the suspensive condition has not been fulfilled.

###### Article 1475

When the obligation has been contracted under a suspensive condition, the thing that is the subject matter of the agreement remains at the risk of the debtor of the obligation to deliver that thing until the fulfillment of the condition. The debtor retains the administration thereof and is entitled to the fruits until the fulfillment of the condition.  
If the thing has entirely perished without the fault of the debtor, the obligation is extinguished.  

If the thing has deteriorated without the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the choice either to terminate the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is found, without reduction of the price.  
If the thing has deteriorated through the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the right either to terminate the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is found, with damages.

###### Article 1476

The fulfillment of the suspensive condition gives rise to all the effects that were linked to its realization. However, the parties may provide that the fulfillment of the condition shall have retroactive effect to the day of the contract.

###### Article 1477

In case of failure of the suspensive condition, the obligation is deemed never to have existed; if the suspensive condition concerned all the effects of the contract, the latter becomes null and void.

###### Article 1478

In case of a resolutory condition, termination must be sought in court. The judge may grant the defendant a period of time according to the circumstances.  
The fulfillment of the resolutory condition extinguishes the obligation retroactively, without calling into question, where applicable, conservatory and administrative acts and the collection of fruits. If the thing has perished before the fulfillment of the condition, the risks realized are borne by the creditor of the obligation to deliver that thing.  

Retroactivity does not take place if such is the agreement of the parties or if the exchanged performances found their utility as the reciprocal performance of the contract progressed.

##### Section II : L'obligation à terme Article 1479

An obligation is subject to a term when its enforceability is deferred until the occurrence of a future and certain event, even though the date thereof is uncertain.

###### Article 1480

The term may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1481

What is due only at a term cannot be demanded before the expiry of the term; but what has been paid in advance cannot be recovered.  
The creditor of the obligation subject to a term may exercise all conservatory acts of his right and take action against acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.

###### Article 1482

The term benefits the debtor, unless it results from the law, the will of the parties or the circumstances that it was established in favor of the creditor or both parties.  
The party for whose exclusive benefit the term has been fixed may waive it without the consent of the other.

###### Article 1483

The debtor can no longer claim the benefit of the term when he has become bankrupt, or if he does not provide the securities promised to the creditor or diminishes those that guarantee the obligation.

###### Article 1484

The forfeiture of the term incurred by a debtor cannot be invoked against his co-obligors, even if solidary.

##### Section III : L'obligation plurale

###### Sous-section 1 : La pluralité d'objets Article 1485

An obligation is facultative when it has as its object a certain performance but the debtor has the option, in order to discharge himself, to provide another.  

A facultative obligation is extinguished if the performance of the initially agreed performance becomes impossible due to force majeure.

###### Article 1486

An obligation is alternative when it has as its object several performances and the performance of one of them discharges the debtor.  
The choice between the performances to be executed belongs to the debtor, if it has not been expressly granted to the creditor. The debtor may discharge himself by delivering one of the promised things; but he cannot force the creditor to receive part of one and part of another.  

If the choice is not exercised within the agreed time or within a reasonable period, the other party may, after formal notice, exercise that choice or terminate the contract.  
The choice, once exercised, is final and causes the obligation to lose its alternative character. The alternative obligation then becomes pure and simple.

###### Article 1487

When the obligation is alternative and the choice has been exercised, the impossibility of performing the chosen performance by reason of force majeure discharges the debtor.  
If the debtor has not made his choice known at the time the impossibility materializes, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible, perform one of the others. When the performances become impossible, the debtor is discharged only if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from force majeure.  

If the creditor has not made his choice known, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible to perform as a result of force majeure, be satisfied with one of the others.

###### Article 1488

When the performances become impossible, the debtor is discharged only if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from force majeure.

###### Sous-section 2 : La pluralité de sujets

###### Article 1489

An obligation that binds several creditors or debtors is divided by operation of law between them. The division also takes place between their successors, even if the obligation was solidary. If it is not otherwise regulated by law or by contract, the division takes place in equal shares.
