If the order prohibits disposing of corporeal movables, or moving them, it is served by the applicant on their spouse, and has the effect of making the latter a responsible custodian of the movables under the same conditions as a person whose property has been seized.  
When the spouse brings the order to the knowledge of a third party, that third party, if they nevertheless contract with the other spouse, is in bad faith.

###### Article 231

Subject to annulment, at the request of the applicant spouse, are all acts performed in violation of the order, if they were entered into with a third party in bad faith, or even with respect to property whose alienation is subject to publicity, if they are simply subsequent to the publication provided for by the preceding article.  
The action for nullity is open to the applicant spouse for two years from the day on which they became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought, if that act is subject to publicity, more than two years after its publication.

###### Article 232

Each of the spouses may open, without the consent of the other, any deposit account and any securities account in their personal name.  
The depositing spouse is deemed, with regard to the depositary, to have free disposal of the funds and securities on deposit.

###### Article 233

If one of the spouses appears alone to perform an act of administration, enjoyment or disposition over movable property that they hold individually, they are deemed, with regard to third parties in good faith, to have the power to perform that act alone.  
This provision is not applicable to furnishings referred to in Article 223, paragraph 3, nor to corporeal movables whose nature creates a presumption of ownership by the other spouse in accordance with Article 1651.

###### Article 234

Each of the spouses has the right to exercise a profession without the consent of their spouse, and may always, for the needs of that profession, alienate and encumber alone their personal property in full ownership.  

Each of the spouses administers, encumbers and alienates alone their personal property. The origin and composition of personal property are established both with regard to third parties and to the spouse, according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Article 235

Each of the spouses receives their earnings and salaries and may dispose of them freely after having discharged the charges of the marriage.

###### Article 236

Creditors to whom a spouse has become obligated may exercise their claims against their personal property, even when the obligation was not contracted by them in the exercise of their profession.

###### Article 237

The provisions of this chapter, in all points where they do not reserve the application of matrimonial agreements, are applicable, by the sole effect of marriage, whatever the matrimonial regime of the spouses.

#### Chapter VII. Dissolution of Marriage Article 238

Marriage is dissolved:

1° By the death of one of the spouses;  

2° By legally pronounced divorce.

#### Chapter VIII. On second marriages Article 239

A woman may not contract a new marriage until three hundred days have elapsed since the dissolution of the previous marriage. However, a woman may, before the expiration of this period of widowhood, contract marriage with her former spouse. The period is extended to four months and ten days elapsed from the death of the husband, for the widow, and from the judgment referred to in Article 158 of this code, for the wife of the missing person.  

This period ends in the event of childbirth after the dissolution of the marriage. It also ends if the woman produces a medical certificate attesting that she is not pregnant.  
The President of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the marriage is to be celebrated may, by order rendered upon simple application, shorten the period provided for in this article when it is evident from the circumstances that, for three hundred days, the previous husband has not cohabited with his wife. The application is communicated to the public prosecutor. In the event of rejection of the application, an appeal may be lodged.

### Title VII: On divorce

#### Chapter I. On grounds for divorce Article 240

Divorce may be pronounced in the event of:	either mutual consent;	or definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond;	or fault.

##### Section I: On divorce by mutual consent

###### § 1. On divorce upon joint application of the spouses Article 241

When the spouses jointly apply for divorce, they do not have to disclose the cause thereof; they must only submit for the judge's approval a draft agreement that settles the consequences thereof.  
The application may be presented either by the parties themselves, or by their respective lawyers, or by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.  
Divorce by mutual consent may not be applied for during the first six months of marriage.

###### Article 242

The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers, if one or both spouses have made such a choice.  
If the spouses persist in their intention to divorce, the judge informs them that their application must be renewed after a reflection period of one month.  
In the absence of renewal within three months following the expiration of this reflection period, the joint application shall lapse.

###### Article 243

The judge approves the agreement and pronounces the divorce if he has acquired the conviction that the will of each of the spouses is genuine and that their consent is free and informed.  
The judge may refuse approval and not pronounce the divorce if he finds that the agreement insufficiently protects the interests of the children or of one of the spouses.

###### § 2. On accepted divorce Article 244

Divorce may be applied for by either spouse or by both when they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage without consideration of the facts at the origin thereof.  

This acceptance is not subject to retraction. Once it has been validly given, it can no longer be called into question, even by the exercise of a remedy.

###### Article 245

If he has acquired the conviction that each of the spouses has given his or her agreement freely, the judge pronounces the divorce and rules on its consequences.

##### Section II: On divorce for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond Article 246

Divorce may be applied for by one of the spouses when the conjugal bond is definitively broken down.

###### Article 247

The definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond results from the cessation of the community of life between the spouses, when they have been living separately for two years at the time of the divorce summons.  
Notwithstanding these provisions, divorce is pronounced for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond in the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 251, as soon as the application presented on this ground is made by way of counterclaim.

##### Section III: On divorce for fault Article 248

Divorce may be applied for by one of the spouses when facts constituting a serious or repeated violation of the duties and obligations of marriage are imputable to his or her spouse and make the continuation of the common life intolerable.

###### Article 249

In the event of reconciliation of the spouses that has occurred since the alleged facts, these facts can no longer be invoked as grounds for divorce. If this were nevertheless to be the case, the judge would have the obligation to declare the application inadmissible.  
A new application may however be made by reason of facts that have occurred or been discovered since the reconciliation, the old facts being able then to be recalled in support of this new application.  
The maintenance or temporary resumption of the common life are not considered as a reconciliation if they result only from necessity, from an effort at conciliation, or from the needs of the children's education.

###### Article 250

The faults of the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce do not prevent examination of his or her application; they may, however, remove from the facts that he or she reproaches his or her spouse the character of seriousness that would have made them grounds for divorce.  
These faults may also be invoked by the other spouse in support of a counterclaim for divorce. If both applications are granted, the divorce is pronounced on shared fault.  

Even in the absence of a counterclaim, the divorce may be pronounced on the shared fault of both spouses if the proceedings reveal faults chargeable to both.

###### Article 251

If an application for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond and an application for fault are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the application for fault.  
In this case, if he rejects the application for divorce for fault, the judge rules without delay on the application for divorce for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond.

##### Section IV: On modifications of the ground of an application for divorce

###### Article 252

The spouses may, at any time during the proceedings, ask the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced by mutual consent by presenting him with an agreement settling the consequences thereof.

###### Article 253

The spouses may also, at any time during the proceedings, when the divorce has been applied for on grounds of definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, ask the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage.

###### Article 254

If, in the context of proceedings instituted for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the defendant applies by way of counterclaim for divorce for fault, the plaintiff may invoke the faults of his or her spouse to modify the ground of his or her application.

#### Chapter II

On divorce proceedings Section I: General provisions

###### Article 255

The proceedings on the grounds, the consequences of the divorce and the provisional measures are not public.

###### Article 256

In the event of divorce for fault, and at the request of the spouses, the court may limit itself to noting in the grounds of the judgment that there exist facts constituting grounds for divorce, without having to state the faults and grievances of the parties.

###### Article 257

If an application for divorce must be made in the name of an adult under guardianship, it is presented by the guardian with the authorization of the family council, after the opinion of the attending physician.  
The adult under curatorship exercises the action himself with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 258

If the spouse against whom the application is made is under guardianship, the action is exercised against the guardian; if he is under curatorship, he defends himself, with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 259

A special guardian or curator is appointed when the guardianship or curatorship had been entrusted to the spouse of the incapacitated person.

###### Article 260

If one of the spouses is placed under safeguard of justice, the application for divorce may not be examined until after the organization of guardianship or the appointment of a special curator.

###### Article 261

When one of the spouses is placed under one of the protection regimes provided for in Chapter II Legal protection measures for adults of Title XII Majority and adults protected by law(

###### art. 565

and following), no application for divorce by mutual consent may be submitted.

##### Section II: Procedure applicable to divorce by mutual consent

###### Article 262

The application for divorce is submitted by the parties themselves or their lawyers. The spouses may be represented by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.  
This application takes the form of an initial petition to which is annexed an agreement containing the provisional measures that the spouses will observe during the course of the proceedings, as well as a draft final agreement intended to settle the consequences of the divorce.  
The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers if they have made that choice.

###### Article 263

When the conditions provided for in Article 243 are met, the judge approves the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce and, by the same decision, pronounces it.

###### Article 264

In case of refusal to approve the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce, the judge may nevertheless approve the provisional measures envisaged by the parties under Article 262, paragraph 2, and take any measure provided for in Articles 272 and 273, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes res judicata, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.  
A new agreement settling the consequences of the divorce may then be submitted by the spouses within a maximum period of three months.

###### Article 265

In the absence of submission of a new agreement within the time limit set in the preceding article or if the judge refuses approval again, the application for divorce lapses.

##### Section III: Procedure applicable to other cases of divorce

###### § 1. Initial petition Article 266

The spouse who files an application for divorce submits, himself or herself or through a lawyer, a petition to the judge, without indicating the grounds for divorce.

###### § 2. Conciliation Article 267

The judge must organize a conciliation hearing. In case of failure, the conciliation attempt may be renewed and attempted at any time during the divorce proceedings which may be initiated by a spouse in accordance with Article 276.  

The judge invites the spouses to consider renouncing the divorce and, if he notes their intention to continue the proceedings, the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses both on the principle of the divorce and on its consequences.

###### Article 268

When the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses, he must meet personally with each of them separately before bringing them together in his presence.  
The lawyers are then called to attend and participate in the meeting.  

In the case where the spouse who did not file the application does not appear at the hearing or is unable to express his or her will, the judge meets with the other spouse and invites him or her to reflect.

###### Article 269

The conciliation attempt may be suspended and resumed without formality, allowing the spouses time for reflection within a limit of eight days.  
If a longer period seems useful, the judge may decide to suspend the proceedings and resort to a new conciliation attempt within six months at most. He orders, if necessary, the necessary provisional measures.

###### Article 270

When the judge notes that the applicant maintains his or her application, he encourages the spouses to settle the consequences of the divorce amicably.  
He asks them to submit for the trial hearing a draft settlement of the effects of the divorce.  

To this end, he may take any provisional measure within the meaning of Articles 272 and 273 of this code, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes res judicata, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.

###### Article 271

What has been said or written on the occasion of a conciliation attempt, in whatever form it took place, may never be invoked for or against a spouse or a third party in the continuation of the proceedings.

###### § 3. Provisional measures Article 272

At the appearance of the spouses in the case referred to in Article 244, or at the order of non-conciliation in other cases, the judge prescribes the measures that are necessary to ensure the existence of the spouses and children until the date on which the judgment becomes res judicata.

###### Article 273

The judge may in particular:
1° Propose to the spouses a mediation measure and, after obtaining their agreement, appoint a mediator to proceed with it;  
2° Enjoin the spouses to meet with a mediator who will inform them about the purpose and conduct of mediation;  
3° Rule on the terms of the separate residence of the spouses;  
4° Allocate to one of them the enjoyment of the dwelling and furniture of the household, or share this enjoyment between them, specifying whether it is free of charge or not and, where applicable, recording the spouses' agreement on the amount of an occupancy indemnity; failing that, set this amount;  
5° Order the return of clothing and personal objects and, in case of dispute over the ownership of these goods, decide provisionally on their allocation;  
6° Set the alimony and the provision for costs of proceedings that one of the spouses must pay to his or her spouse, designate which spouse or spouses must ensure the provisional settlement of all or part of the debts;  
7° Grant to one of the spouses advances to be credited against his or her rights in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime if the situation makes it necessary;  
8° Rule on the allocation of the enjoyment or management of common or undivided property other than those referred to in 4°, subject to the rights of each of the spouses in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime;  

9° Appoint any qualified professional to draw up an estimated inventory or to make proposals regarding the settlement of the pecuniary interests of the spouses;  
10° Appoint a notary to prepare a draft liquidation of the matrimonial regime and formation of lots to be divided.

###### Article 274

If there are minor children, the judge rules on their custody, as well as on the right of visitation and accommodation. He sets the contribution due, for their maintenance and education, by the spouse who does not have custody.  
Parental authority is exercised by the spouse to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other.

###### Article 275

The judge may take, from the initial petition, emergency measures.  

He may, in this capacity, authorize the applicant spouse to reside separately, if necessary with his or her minor children; the judge may then and where applicable, determine, with the agreement of the spouses and failing that by decision, the financial arrangements between spouses in order to facilitate this separate residence.  

The judge may also, for the guarantee of the rights of a spouse, order all conservatory measures such as the affixing of seals on common property. The provisions of Article 240 and the other safeguards established by the matrimonial regime remain applicable, however.

###### § 4. Commencement of divorce proceedings Article 276

After the non-reconciliation order, a spouse may commence proceedings or file a counterclaim for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for final breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault.  
However, when at the reconciliation hearing the spouses have declared that they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage and the granting of divorce on the basis of Article 244, proceedings may only be commenced on that same basis.

###### Article 277

On pain of inadmissibility, the application commencing proceedings must include a proposal for settlement of the pecuniary and patrimonial interests of the spouses.

###### Article 278

When the court definitively dismisses the application for divorce, it may rule on the contribution to the charges of the marriage, the family residence and the terms of exercise of parental authority.

###### § 5. Evidence Article 279

The facts invoked as grounds for divorce or as defences to an application may be established by any mode of proof, including admission. However, descendants may never be heard on the grievances invoked by the spouses.

###### Article 280

A spouse may not submit to the proceedings any evidence that he or she obtained by violence or fraud.

###### Article 281

Reports drawn up at the request of a spouse outside judicial proceedings shall be excluded from the proceedings if there has been a violation of domicile or unlawful interference with the privacy of private life.

###### Article 282

The spouses must communicate to each other and communicate to the court and to the experts appointed by it, all information and documents useful for fixing benefits and pensions and liquidating the matrimonial regime.  
The court may have all useful investigations carried out with debtors or those who hold assets on behalf of the spouses without professional secrecy being invoked. Any contravention of the court's order shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance, and punished by a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 FD.

#### Chapter III: Consequences of divorce

##### Section I: Date on which the effects of divorce occur Article 283

The decision granting the divorce dissolves the marriage on the date on which it acquires the force of res judicata.

###### Article 284

To contract a new marriage, the woman must observe the period of three hundred days as provided for in Article 250.  
If the spouses have been authorised to reside separately during the proceedings, this period begins to run from the day of the decision authorising separate residence or approving, in the case of a joint application, the temporary agreement entered into for that purpose.  
The woman may remarry without delay when the divorce has been granted in the cases provided for in Articles 246 and 247.

###### Article 285

The period referred to in the preceding article ends if a birth takes place after the decision authorising or approving separate residence or, failing that, after the date on which the divorce judgment acquired the force of res judicata.  
If the husband dies before the divorce judgment has acquired the force of res judicata, the period runs from the day after the day on which the death is officially recorded.

###### Article 286

The divorce judgment is enforceable against third parties, with regard to the property of the spouses, from the day on which the formalities of marginal notation prescribed by the rules of civil status have been completed.

###### Article 287

The agreement or divorce judgment takes effect in relations between the spouses, with regard to their property: when it is granted by mutual consent in accordance with Article 263, on the date of approval of the agreement settling all the consequences of the divorce, unless the agreement provides otherwise; when it is granted for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for final breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, on the date of the non-reconciliation order.  

One of the spouses may request that the effect of the judgment be brought forward to the date when, through the fault of the other, their cohabitation and collaboration ceased.

###### Article 288

Any obligation contracted by one of the spouses to be charged to the community, any alienation of common property made by one of them within the limits of his or her powers, subsequent to the initial application, shall be declared null and void if it is proved that there has been fraud on the rights of the other spouse.

##### Section II: Consequences of divorce for the spouses

###### § 1. General provisions Article 289

If the divorced spouses wish to contract another union between themselves, a new celebration of the marriage is necessary.

###### Article 290

Following the divorce, each of the spouses loses the use of the name of his or her spouse.  

One of the spouses may nevertheless retain the use of the name of the other, either with the latter's agreement, or with the authorisation of the court, if he or she justifies a particular interest for himself or herself or for the children.

###### Article 291

Divorce has no effect on matrimonial benefits that take effect during the marriage and on gifts of present property whatever their form.  
Divorce entails automatic revocation of matrimonial benefits that only take effect upon dissolution of the matrimonial regime or upon the death of one of the spouses and of dispositions upon death, granted by one spouse to his or her spouse by marriage contract or during the union, unless the spouse who granted them expresses a contrary intention. This intention is recorded in the agreement signed by the spouses and approved by the court, or by the court at the time of granting the divorce; in these cases, the benefit or disposition maintained is irrevocable.  

However, if the marriage contract so provides, the spouses may always take back the property that they brought to the community.

###### Article 292

Divorce has no effect on the rights that either spouse derives from the law or from agreements entered into with third parties.

###### Article 293

The spouses may, during divorce proceedings, enter into any agreements for the liquidation and partition of their matrimonial regime.  
When the liquidation relates to property subject to land registration formalities, the agreement must be made by notarial deed.

###### § 2

Consequences specific to divorces other than by mutual consent Article 294

Without prejudice to the application of Article 297, damages may be awarded to a spouse in compensation for consequences of particular gravity that he or she suffers as a result of the dissolution of the marriage:
1° either when he or she was a defendant in a divorce granted for final breakdown of the conjugal bond and had not himself or herself filed any application for divorce;  
2° either when the divorce is granted on the exclusive fault of his or her spouse. This application may only be made in connection with the divorce action.

###### Article 295

In the absence of a conventional settlement by the spouses, the court shall rule on their applications for maintenance in joint ownership, preferential allocation and advance on share of community property or jointly owned property.  
The court shall rule on applications for liquidation and partition of patrimonial interests, under the conditions set out in Articles L.624-5 to L.624-11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, if the disagreements remaining between the parties are established by any means, in particular by producing: a joint declaration of acceptance of a judicial partition, indicating the points of disagreement between the spouses; the draft prepared by the notary appointed on the basis of paragraph 10° of Article 273.  

It may, even of its own motion, rule on the determination of the matrimonial regime applicable to the spouses.

###### Article 296

The spouses may, during the proceedings, submit to the judge for approval conventions settling all or part of the consequences of the divorce.  
The judge, after having verified that the interests of each of the spouses and of the children are preserved, shall approve the conventions by pronouncing the divorce.

###### § 3. Compensatory Allowances Article 297

Divorce terminates the duty of support between spouses.  

One of the spouses may be required to pay the other an allowance intended to compensate, as far as possible, for the disparity that the dissolution of the marriage creates in the respective living conditions.  
However, the judge may refuse to grant such an allowance if equity so requires, either in consideration of the criteria provided for in Article 298, or when the divorce is pronounced on the exclusive fault of the spouse who requests the benefit of this allowance, having regard to the particular circumstances of the dissolution.

###### Article 298

The compensatory allowance is fixed according to the needs of the spouse to whom it is paid and the resources of the other, taking into account the situation at the time of the divorce and the evolution thereof in the foreseeable future.  
For this purpose, the judge takes into consideration, in particular:	the duration of the marriage;	the age and state of health of the spouses;	their qualifications and their professional situations;	the consequences of the professional choices made by one of the spouses during the common life for the education of the children and the time that will still have to be devoted thereto or to promote the career of his or her spouse to the detriment of his or her own;  
	the estimated or foreseeable patrimony of the spouses, both in capital and in income, after the liquidation of the matrimonial regime;	their existing and foreseeable rights;	their respective situation with regard to retirement pensions, having estimated, as far as possible, the reduction in retirement rights that may have been caused, for the spouse who is creditor of the compensatory allowance, by the circumstances referred to in the sixth paragraph.

###### Article 299

In the context of fixing a compensatory allowance, by the judge or by the parties, or on the occasion of a request for revision, the parties provide the judge with a declaration certifying on their honour the accuracy of their resources, income, patrimony and living conditions.

###### Article 300

The compensatory allowance has a lump-sum character. It may not be revised even in the event of an unforeseen change in the resources or needs of the parties, unless the absence of revision would have consequences of exceptional gravity for one of the spouses.

###### Article 301

When the composition of the assets of the spouse who is debtor of the compensatory allowance permits, it shall take the form of a capital sum the amount of which is fixed by the judge.

###### Article 302

The judge decides on the terms according to which the attribution or allocation of property in capital shall be executed:
1° Payment of a sum of money;  
2° Abandonment of property in kind, movable or immovable, but for the usufruct only, the judgment operating forced transfer in favour of the creditor;  

3° Deposit of income-producing securities with a third party charged with paying the income to the spouse who is creditor of the allowance until the fixed term.  
The divorce judgment may be made subject to the actual payment of the capital or to the constitution of the guarantees provided for in Article 306.

###### Article 303

If the spouse who is debtor of the compensatory allowance does not have immediate liquid assets, he or she may be authorised, under the guarantees provided for in Article 306, to constitute the capital in three annual instalments.  
In the absence of capital or if it is not sufficient, the compensatory allowance shall take the form of an annuity.

###### Article 304

When the compensatory allowance takes the form of an annuity, this annuity is granted for a period equal to or less than the life of the spouse who is creditor.  
The annuity is indexed; the index is determined as in matters of maintenance.  
The amount of the annuity before indexation is fixed uniformly for its entire duration or may vary by successive periods according to the probable evolution of resources and needs.

###### Article 305

Upon the death of the spouse who is debtor, the burden of the annuity passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 306

Independently of the legal or judicial mortgage, the judge may require the spouse who is debtor to constitute a personal or real security to guarantee the annuity.

###### Article 307

In the event of a joint request, the spouses fix the amount and terms of the compensatory allowance in the convention that they submit to the judge for approval.  
The judge, however, refuses to approve the convention if it inequitably fixes the rights and obligations of the spouses.

###### Article 308

The approved convention has the same executory force as a judicial decision.  

It may be modified only by a new convention between the spouses, also subject to approval.  
The spouses nevertheless have the option of providing in their convention that each of them may, in the event of an unforeseen change in his or her resources and needs, request the judge to revise the compensatory allowance.

###### Article 309

The transfers and abandonments provided for in this paragraph are considered as participating in the matrimonial regime. They are not assimilated to donations.

###### Article 310

The spouse on whose exclusive fault the divorce is pronounced is not entitled to any compensatory allowance.  

However, he or she may obtain compensation on an exceptional basis, if, taking into account the duration of the common life and the collaboration provided to the profession of the other spouse, it appears manifestly contrary to equity to refuse him or her any pecuniary compensation following the divorce.

###### § 4. The Duty of Support After Divorce Article 311

When the divorce is pronounced for breakdown of common life, the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce remains fully bound by the duty of support.  

In the case of Article 247, the duty of support covers everything necessary for the medical treatment of the sick spouse.

###### Article 312

The performance of the duty of support takes the form of maintenance. It may always be revised according to the resources and needs of each of the spouses.

###### Article 313

Maintenance ceases by operation of law to be due if the spouse who is creditor thereof contracts a new marriage.  
It is terminated if the creditor lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.

###### Article 314

Upon the death of the spouse who is debtor, the burden of the maintenance passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 315

When the composition of the assets of the spouse who is debtor lends itself thereto, the maintenance is replaced, in whole or in part, by the constitution of a capital sum, according to the rules of Articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309.  
If this capital becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the spouse who is creditor, the latter may request a supplement in the form of maintenance.

###### § 5. Housing Article 316

If the dwelling serving as housing for the family belongs in ownership or personally to one of the spouses, the judge may grant a lease on it to the other spouse:
1° When custody of one or more children has been entrusted to the latter;  
2° When the divorce has been pronounced at the request of the spouse who is the owner, for breakdown of common life.  

In the case provided for in 1° above, the judge sets the duration of the lease and may renew it until the youngest of the children reaches the age of majority.  
In the case provided for in 2°, the lease may not be granted for a duration exceeding nine years, but may be extended by a new decision. It terminates, by operation of law, in the event of remarriage of the person to whom it was granted. It is terminated if the latter lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.  
In all cases, the judge may terminate the lease if new circumstances justify it.

##### Section III: Consequences of divorce for children Article 317

Divorce leaves intact the rights and duties of the father and mother with regard to their children, subject to the rules that follow.

###### Article 318

According to the interest of minor children, their custody is entrusted to one or the other of the spouses.  
On an exceptional basis and if the interest of the children so requires, this custody may be entrusted: 1° either to another person chosen preferably from among their relatives;  
2° or, if this proves impossible, to an educational establishment or to a recognized association in this field.

###### Article 319

Before ruling on the custody of children, provisional or final, and on visiting rights, the judge may give a mission to any qualified person to conduct a social investigation. The purpose of this investigation is to gather information on the material and moral situation of the family, on the conditions in which the children live and are educated and on the measures that should be taken in their interest.  
If one of the spouses contests the conclusions of the social investigation, he or she may request a counter-investigation. The social investigation may not be used in the debate on the cause of the divorce.

###### Article 320

The spouse to whom custody of the children has not been entrusted retains the right to supervise their maintenance and education. He or she contributes to it in proportion to his or her resources.  

A right of visit and accommodation may be refused to him or her only for serious reasons.  
He or she may be charged with administering, under judicial supervision, all or part of the children's patrimony, by way of derogation from articles 480 and 518 paragraph 2, if the interest of proper administration of this patrimony so requires.

###### Article 321

The judge rules on the attribution of custody and on the modalities of the exercise of parental authority, at the request of one of the spouses, a member of the family or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 322

The judge takes into account:
1° Agreements entered into between the spouses;  
2° Information that has been gathered in the investigation and counter-investigation provided for in article 319;  
3° Feelings expressed by minor children when their hearing has appeared necessary and when it does not entail disadvantages for them.

###### Article 323

Decisions relating to the exercise of parental authority may be modified or supplemented at any time by the judge, at the request of a spouse, a member of the family or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 324

In the case of divorce by joint application, the provisions of the agreement approved by the judge relating to the exercise of parental authority may be revised, for serious reasons, at the request of one of the spouses or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 325

The contribution to the maintenance and education of children provided for in article 320 takes the form of maintenance payments paid to the person who has custody of them.  
The modalities and guarantees of this maintenance payment are fixed by the judgment or, in the case of divorce by joint application, by the agreement of the spouses approved by the judge.

###### Article 326

When the consistency of the debtor's assets so permits, the maintenance payment may be replaced, in whole or in part, according to the rules of articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309, by the payment of a sum of money into the hands of an accredited body charged with granting in return to the child an indexed annuity, the abandonment of property in usufruct or the allocation of income-producing property.

###### Article 327

If the capital thus constituted becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the children, the person who has custody may request the attribution of a supplement in the form of maintenance payments.

###### Article 328

The parent who assumes primary responsibility for adult children who cannot themselves provide for their needs may request his or her spouse to pay him or her a contribution to their maintenance and education.

#### Chapter IV: Judicial separation

##### Section I: Cases and procedure for judicial separation

###### Article 329

Judicial separation may be pronounced at the request of one of the spouses in the same cases and under the same conditions as divorce.

###### Article 330

The spouse against whom an application for divorce is presented may file a counterclaim for judicial separation. However, when the main application for divorce is based on the definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the counterclaim may only seek divorce.  
The spouse against whom an application for judicial separation is presented may file a counterclaim for divorce.

###### Article 331

When an application for divorce and an application for judicial separation are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the application for divorce. He pronounces it as soon as the conditions are met. Failing that, he rules on the application for judicial separation.  
However, when these applications are based on fault, the judge examines them simultaneously and, if he grants them, pronounces divorce on shared fault with regard to both spouses.

###### Article 332

The rules contained in article 250 as well as in chapter II above are applicable to the procedure for judicial separation.

##### Section II: Consequences of judicial separation Article 333

Judicial separation does not dissolve the marriage but it terminates the duty of cohabitation.

###### Article 334

Judicial separation allows each of the spouses who was using the name of the other to retain this use for the future. However, the judgment of judicial separation, or a subsequent judgment, may prohibit a spouse from retaining the use of his or her spouse's name.

###### Article 335

In the event of death of one of the spouses judicially separated, the other spouse retains the rights that the law grants to the surviving spouse. When judicial separation is pronounced by mutual consent, the spouses may include in their agreement a renunciation of the succession rights conferred on them by articles 858 et seq. and 872 et seq. of this code.

###### Article 336

Judicial separation always entails separation of property.  

With regard to property, the date on which judicial separation produces its effects is determined in accordance with the provisions of articles 286 to 288.

###### Article 337

Judicial separation leaves intact the duty of support; the judgment that pronounces it or a subsequent judgment fixes the maintenance payment that is owed to the spouse in need.  

This payment is awarded without consideration of fault. The debtor spouse may nevertheless invoke, if applicable, the provisions of article 215, paragraph 2.  

This payment is subject to the rules of maintenance obligations; the provisions of article 315 are however applicable to it.

###### Article 338

Subject to the provisions of this section, the consequences of legal separation are governed by the same rules as the consequences of divorce set out in Chapter III above.

##### Section III: On the termination of legal separation Article 339

The voluntary resumption of cohabitation terminates the legal separation.

To be enforceable against third parties, this must either be recorded by notarial deed or be the subject of a declaration to the registrar of civil status. Mention thereof is made in the margin of the marriage certificate.
The separation of property subsists unless the spouses adopt a new matrimonial regime in accordance with the rules of Article 1642.

###### Article 340

At the request of one of the spouses, the judgment of legal separation is converted by operation of law into a judgment of divorce when the legal separation has lasted three years.

###### Article 341

In all cases of legal separation, it may be converted into divorce by joint application.
When legal separation has been pronounced on joint application, it may be converted into divorce only by a new joint application.

###### Article 342

As a result of the conversion, the ground for legal separation becomes the ground for divorce; the attribution of fault is not modified.
The judge determines the consequences of the divorce. Benefits and allowances between spouses are determined according to the rules specific to divorce.

###### Article 343

The wife may contract a new marriage as soon as the conversion decision has become final.

#### Chapter V

On the conflict of laws relating to divorce and legal separation Article 344
Divorce and legal separation are governed by Djiboutian law: when both spouses are of Djiboutian nationality; when the spouses both have their domicile on Djiboutian territory; when no foreign law recognizes itself as having jurisdiction, while the Djiboutian courts have jurisdiction to hear the divorce or legal separation.

### Title VIII: On filiation

Chapter I: Provisions common to legitimate filiation and natural filiation Section I: On presumptions relating to filiation

###### Article 345

The law presumes that the child was conceived during the period extending from the three hundredth to the one hundred and eightieth day, inclusive, before the date of birth.
Conception is presumed to have occurred at any time during this period, according to what is required in the interest of the child.

Proof to the contrary is admissible to rebut these presumptions.

###### Article 346

Possession of status is established by a sufficient combination of facts indicating the relationship of filiation and kinship between an individual and the family to which he is said to belong.
Possession of status must be continuous.

###### Article 347

The principal of these facts are: that the individual has always borne the name of those from whom he is said to be descended; that they have treated him as their child, and that he has treated them as his father and mother; that they have, in that capacity, provided for his education, maintenance and establishment; that he is recognized as such in society and by the family; that the public authority considers him as such.

###### Article 348

The parents or the child may request from the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or from the judge designated for that purpose that there be issued to them, under the conditions provided for in Articles 106 and 107 of this code, a certificate of notoriety establishing the possession of status until proof to the contrary; this without prejudice to all other means of proof to which they could resort to establish its existence in court, if it were to be contested.

##### Section II: On actions relating to filiation Article 349

No action is received as to the filiation of a child who was not born viable.

###### Article 350

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction to hear actions relating to filiation under the Civil Code. The Personal Status Court of First Instance has jurisdiction to hear disputes relating to personal status matters of persons governed by the Family Code.

###### Article 351

In the case of an offence affecting the filiation of an individual, the criminal action may be decided only after the judgment on the question of filiation has become final.

###### Article 352

Whenever they are not confined by law to shorter periods, actions relating to filiation are prescribed after thirty years from the day on which the individual was deprived of the status he claims, or began to enjoy the status which is contested.

###### Article 353

The action which belonged to an individual as to his filiation may be exercised by his heirs only in cases where that individual died a minor or within five years after his majority or emancipation.
His heirs may also pursue the action which he had already commenced, unless there has been a withdrawal or lapse of proceedings.

###### Article 354

Actions relating to filiation may not be the subject of waiver.

###### Article 355

Judgments rendered in matters of filiation are enforceable against any person, even those who were not parties to the proceedings; but persons who were not parties to the proceedings have the right to file third-party opposition against said judgments.
Judges may of their own motion order that all interested parties to whom they consider the judgment should be made common be joined in the case.

###### Article 356

Similarly, when, in one of the actions opened by Articles 418 and 436 below, a plea of inadmissibility or a defence is raised on the ground that the mother had, during the legal period of conception, relations with a third party, the judge may order that the latter be called into the case.

###### Article 357

The courts settle conflicts of filiation for which the law has not established any other principle, by determining by all means of proof the most probable filiation.
In the absence of sufficient elements of conviction, they have regard to possession of status.

###### Article 358

In the case where they are led to dismiss the claim of the party who was, in fact, taking care of the education of the minor child, the courts may, nevertheless, taking into account the interest of the child, grant that party a right of visitation.

##### Section III

On the conflict of laws relating to the establishment of filiation Article 359
Filiation is governed by the personal law of the mother on the day of the child's birth; if the mother is not known, by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 360

However, if the legitimate child and his father and mother, the natural child and one of his father or mother have their habitual residence in Djibouti, common or separate, possession of status produces all the consequences which flow from it according to Djiboutian law, this even in the case where the other elements of filiation could have depended on a foreign law.

###### Article 361

Marriage entails legitimation when, on the day the union was celebrated, this consequence is admitted, either by the law governing the effects of marriage, or by the personal law of one of the spouses, or by the personal law of the child.

Legitimation by judicial authority is governed, at the choice of the applicant, either by the personal law of the latter, or by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 362

Voluntary recognition of paternity or maternity is valid if it was made in accordance with either the personal law of its author or the personal law of the child.


This excerpt sits under: REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI > BOOK I: ON PERSONS > Title VII: On divorce > Chapter IV: On legal separation > Section II: On the consequences of legal separation Article 333

###### Article 363

The action for maintenance is governed, at the choice of the child, either by the law of his or her habitual residence, or by the law of the habitual residence of the debtor.

#### Chapter II: Legitimate Filiation

##### Section I: Presumption of Paternity Article 364

A child conceived or born during marriage has the husband as father.

Nevertheless, the latter may disavow the child in court, if he provides facts capable of demonstrating that he cannot be the father.

###### Article 365

In case of judgment or even application, either for divorce or for legal separation, the presumption of paternity does not apply to a child born more than three hundred days after the order authorizing the spouses to reside separately, and less than one hundred and eighty days since the final rejection of the application or since the reconciliation.  
The presumption of paternity nevertheless recovers, by operation of law, its force:
1° If the child, with regard to the spouses, has the possession of status of legitimate child and if he or she does not have paternal filiation already established with regard to a third party.  
2° If, upon application brought by either spouse before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance during the minority of the child, proof is provided that the husband is indeed the father of the child. This action is also open to the child during the ten years following his or her majority.

###### Article 366

The presumption of paternity is set aside when the child, registered without indication of the husband's name, has possession of status only with regard to the mother.

###### Article 367

When the presumption of paternity is set aside under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the filiation of the child is established with regard to the mother as if there had been disavowal admitted in court.  
Either spouse may request that the effects of the presumption of paternity be restored, by proving that, during the legal period of conception, a factual reunion took place between them, which makes the husband's paternity plausible.

###### Article 368

A child born before the one hundred and eightieth day of marriage is legitimate and deemed to have been so from his or her conception.

The husband, however, may disavow him or her according to the rules of article 312.

He may even disavow him or her on the sole proof of the date of delivery, unless he knew of the pregnancy before the marriage, or unless he behaved as the father after the birth.

###### Article 369

The presumption of paternity is not applicable to a child born more than three hundred days after the dissolution of the marriage, nor, in case of declared absence of the husband, to one who is born to a married woman more than one year after the absence or death of her husband or the date of divorce.

###### Article 370

The husband must bring the action for disavowal within six months of the birth, when he is present at the place.  
If he was not at the place, within six months of his return.

And within six months following the discovery of the fraud, if the birth of the child had been concealed from him.

###### Article 371

If the husband died before bringing the action, but while still within the time limit to do so, his heirs shall have standing to contest the legitimacy of the child.  
Their action, nevertheless, shall cease to be admissible when six months have elapsed from the time when the child took possession of the alleged paternal property, or from the time when they were disturbed by him or her in their own possession.

###### Article 372

Any extrajudicial act containing disavowal on the part of the husband or contestation of legitimacy on the part of the heirs, shall be deemed null and void, if it is not followed by a court action within six months.

###### Article 373

The action for disavowal is directed, in the presence of the mother, against a guardian ad hoc, appointed to the child by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or by the judge designated for that purpose.

###### Article 374

Even in the absence of disavowal, the mother may contest the paternity of the husband, but only for the purposes of legitimation, when she has, after dissolution of the marriage, remarried the true father of the child.

###### Article 375

On pain of inadmissibility, the action, directed against the husband or his heirs, is joined to an application for legitimation made in the terms of article 390 below.  
It must be brought by the mother and her new spouse within six months of their marriage and before the child has reached the age of seven years.

###### Article 376

Both applications are decided by one and the same judgment, which may grant the contestation of paternity only if legitimation is admitted.

##### Section II: Proof of Legitimate Filiation Article 377

The filiation of legitimate children is proved by birth certificates registered in the civil status registers.

###### Article 378

In the absence of such title, possession of the status of legitimate child is sufficient.

###### Article 379

There is possession of status of legitimate child only insofar as it connects the child indivisibly to his or her father and mother.

###### Article 380

No one may claim a status contrary to that given to him or her by his or her birth certificate and possession consistent with that title.  
And reciprocally, no one may contest the status of one who has possession consistent with his or her birth certificate.

###### Article 381

However, if it is alleged that there has been substitution of a child, or substitution, even involuntary, either before or after the drafting of the birth certificate, proof thereof shall be admissible and may be made by any means.

###### Article 382

In the absence of title and possession of status, or if the child was registered, either under false names, or without indication of the mother's name, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses.  
Proof by witnesses may, nevertheless, be admitted only when there exists either a beginning of proof in writing, or presumptions or indications serious enough to determine its admission.

###### Article 383

The beginning of proof in writing results from family documents, registers and domestic papers, as well as from all other public or private writings emanating from a party engaged in the dispute or who would have an interest therein if he or she were alive.

###### Article 384

Counter-proof may be made by all means capable of establishing that the claimant is not the child of the mother he or she claims to have, or even, maternity being proved, that he or she is not the child of the mother's husband.  
If the husband was not made a party to the proceedings for claim of status, he may contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the judgment having acquired the force of res judicata granting the child's application.

###### Article 385

Without waiting for a claim of status to be brought by the child, the husband may, by any means, contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the birth.

###### Article 386

After the death of the husband, his heirs shall likewise have the right to contest his paternity either preventively if the husband was still within the time limit to do so, or in defense to an action for claim of status.

###### Article 387

The spouses, separately or jointly, may, by providing the proof provided for in article 382 above, claim a child as being theirs; but if the child already has another established filiation, they must first demonstrate its inaccuracy, assuming that one is in one of the cases where the law authorizes such demonstration.

##### Section III: On Legitimation Article 388

Legitimation is the act by which a lawfully married couple confers upon a natural child the status of a legitimate child.

Legitimation may benefit all natural children, as soon as their filiation has been legally established, either by voluntary recognition or by judgment.

Legitimation takes place either by marriage of the parents or by authority of justice.

###### § 1. On Legitimation by Marriage Article 389

All children born out of wedlock are legitimated by operation of law by the subsequent marriage of their father and mother.

If their filiation was not already established, these children are the subject of recognition at the time of the celebration of the marriage. In this case, the civil registrar who performs the celebration records the recognition and legitimation in a separate act.

###### Article 390

When the filiation of a natural child has been established with respect to his father and mother or one of them only after their marriage, legitimation can only take place by virtue of a judgment.
This judgment must establish that the child has had, since the celebration of the marriage, the possession of status as a common child.

###### Article 391

Every legitimation is noted in the margin of the birth certificate of the legitimated child.
This notation may be requested by any interested party. In the case of Article 389, the civil registrar provides for it himself, if he has had knowledge of the existence of the children.

###### Article 392

Legitimation may take place after the death of the child, if he has left descendants; it then benefits them.

###### Article 393

Legitimation confers upon the legitimated child the rights and duties of a legitimate child. It takes effect on the date of the marriage.

###### § 2. On Legitimation by Authority of Justice

###### Article 394

If it appears that marriage is impossible between the two parents, the benefit of legitimation may still be conferred upon the child by authority of justice provided that he has, with respect to the parent who requests it, the possession of status as a natural child.

###### Article 395

The application for legitimation is made by one of the two parents or by both jointly before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 396

If one of the parents of the child was, at the time of conception, in the bonds of a marriage that is not dissolved, his application is admissible only with the consent of his spouse.

###### Article 397

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and, after having received or solicited, as the case may be, the observations of the child himself, of the other parent when he is not a party to the application, as well as of the spouse of the applicant, it pronounces, if it deems it justified, the legitimation.

###### Article 398

Legitimation by authority of justice takes effect on the date of the decision that pronounces it definitively.

If it took place at the request of only one of the parents, it has no effect with respect to the other; it does not entail modification of the child's name, except by contrary decision of the Civil Chamber.

###### Article 399

If legitimation by authority of justice has been pronounced with respect to both parents, the child takes the name of the father; if he is a minor, his custody is decided upon by the Civil Chamber, as in matters of divorce.

###### Article 400

The provisions of Articles 391 to 393, first paragraph are applicable to legitimation by authority of justice.

#### Chapter III: On Natural Filiation

##### Section I

On the Effects of Natural Filiation and Its Modes of Establishment in General Article 401
Every natural child falls under the regime of the civil code whenever his parents have expressed their will to subject this child to this regime at the time of the declaration of his birth to the civil registrar.
The one of the parents who, alone, makes the declaration, is deemed to act in agreement with the other for this purpose. The one who has not made the declaration has one month, from the declaration made to the civil registrar to contest its meaning. In case of disagreement between the two parents, the regime of the family code shall then be applicable to the child.
If the parents of this child give birth to one or more other common children, they shall be subject to the choice retained for the first common child.

###### Article 402

The natural child has in principle the same rights and the same duties as the legitimate child in his relations with his father and mother.

He enters into the family of his author.

###### Article 403

The natural child acquires the name of that one of his two parents with respect to whom his filiation is established first; the name of his father, if the filiation is established simultaneously with respect to one and the other.

###### Article 404

Even in the case where his filiation was established only second with respect to the father, the natural child may take the name of the latter by substitution, if, during his minority, his two parents make the joint declaration before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose.

If the child is more than fifteen years old, his personal consent is necessary.

###### Article 405

In all other cases, the change of name of the natural child must be requested from the Court of First Instance.
The action is open during the minority of the child and in the two years that will follow, either his majority, or a modification made to his status.

###### Article 406

The substitution of name extends by operation of law to the minor children of the interested party. It extends to adult children only with their consent.

###### Article 407

In the absence of established paternal filiation, the husband of the mother may confer, by substitution, his own name to the child by a declaration that he will make jointly with the mother, under the conditions provided for in Article 404 above.
The child may however request to resume the name he bore previously by a request that he will submit to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within two years following his majority.

###### Article 408

The rules of attribution of name provided for in the preceding articles do not prejudice the effects of possession of status.

###### Article 409

In the case provided for in the third paragraph of Article 401 above, the natural child may be raised at the conjugal domicile only with the consent of the spouse of his author.

###### Article 410

Natural filiation is legally established, either by voluntary recognition or by judicial declaration, following an action in search of paternity or maternity.
Natural filiation may also be legally established by the necessary effect of a judgment, notably following an action in disavowal or in contestation of legitimacy.

###### Article 411

Every recognition is null, every claim in search is inadmissible, when the child has a legitimate filiation already established by possession of status.

###### Article 412

If there exists between the father and mother of the natural child one of the impediments to marriage provided for by Articles 173 and 174 by reason of kinship, the filiation being already established with respect to one, it is forbidden to establish the filiation with respect to the other.

##### Section II: On the Recognition of Natural Children Article 413

The recognition of a natural child shall be made by authentic act, when it has not been made in the birth certificate.

###### Article 414

The recognition of the father, without the indication and avowal of the mother, has effect only with respect to the father.

###### Article 415

The birth certificate bearing the indication of the mother is valid as recognition, when it is corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 416

As long as it has not been contested in court, an acknowledgment renders inadmissible the establishment of another natural filiation that would contradict it.

###### Article 417

The acknowledgment may be contested by all persons who have an interest therein, even by its author.  
The action is also open to the public prosecutor, if indications drawn from the acts themselves render the declared filiation implausible.  

When there exists a possession of status consistent with the acknowledgment and which has lasted at least ten years since such acknowledgment, no contestation is admissible any longer, except by the other parent, the child himself or those who claim to be the true parents.

##### Section III : Des actions en recherche de paternité et de maternité Article 418

In the absence of title and possession of status, the search for maternity is admitted. The mother may however, at the time of childbirth, request that the secrecy of her admission and her identity be preserved.  
The child who brings the action is required to prove that he is the one whom the alleged mother gave birth to.  

He may prove it by establishing that he has, with respect to her, the possession of status of natural child. In the absence thereof, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses, if there exist either serious presumptions or indications, or a commencement of proof in writing, within the meaning of Article 383.

###### Article 419

Paternity outside marriage may be judicially declared in the presence of established facts that render the filiation plausible.

###### Article 420

The action belongs only to the child.  
The parent, even if a minor, with respect to whom filiation is established has, during the minority of the child, sole capacity to exercise the action for search of maternity or paternity.  

If no filiation link is established or if that parent is deceased or unable to express his will, the action is brought by the guardian in accordance with the provisions of Article 542, paragraph 2.

###### Article 421

The action for search of paternity is brought against the alleged parent or against his heirs. In the absence of heirs or if they have renounced the succession, it is directed against the State. The renouncing heirs are called to the proceedings to assert their rights therein.

###### Article 422

The action must, on pain of forfeiture, be brought within two years following the birth.  

However, when the alleged father and the mother lived during the legal period of conception in a state of cohabitation, implying, in the absence of a common life, stable and continuous relations, or when the alleged father has provided for or participated in the maintenance, education or establishment of the child in the capacity of father, the action may be brought until the expiration of two years following the cessation, either of the cohabitation, or of the acts of participation in the maintenance and education of the child.  

If it has not been brought during the minority of the child, the child may still bring it during the two years following his majority.

###### Article 423

When it grants the action, the court may, at the request of the mother, order the father to reimburse her for all or part of her maternity and maintenance expenses during the three months preceding and the three months following the birth, without prejudice to the damages to which she could claim by application of Article 1391.

###### Article 424

The court rules, if appropriate, on the attribution of the name and on the exercise of parental authority, in accordance with Articles 405 and 486.

###### Article 425

In rejecting the claim, the judges may, nevertheless, award subsistence to the child, if the relations between the mother and the defendant have been demonstrated under the conditions provided for in Articles 426 and following.

##### Section IV : De l'action à fins de subsides Article 426

Any natural child whose paternal filiation is not legally established, may claim subsistence from the one who had relations with his mother during the legal period of conception.  

The action is admissible even if the father or the mother was at the time of conception, bound in the bonds of marriage with another person, or if there existed between them one of the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 173 to 176 of this code.

###### Article 427

The action for subsistence may also be brought by the child of a married woman, if his title of legitimate child is not corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 428

Subsistence is determined, in the form of a pension, according to the needs of the child, the resources of the debtor, the family situation of the latter.  

The pension may be due beyond the majority of the child, if he is still in need, unless that state is attributable to his fault.

###### Article 429

When there is occasion for the application of Article 356 above, the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, in the absence of other elements of decision, has the power to place an indemnity intended to ensure the maintenance and education of the child at the charge of the defendants, if faults are established against them, or if commitments have been made previously by them.  
The president determines the period within which the indemnity must be paid to the legal representative of the child; in case of default of payment within the indicated period, the creditor may seize that judge by simple petition with a view to accompanying the condemnation with a penalty which shall be, here, immediately final.  

The provisions governing subsistence are, for the remainder, applicable to this indemnity.

###### Article 430

The defendant may dismiss the claim, by providing proof that he could not be the father of the child.

###### Article 431

The burden of subsistence is transmitted to the succession of the debtor within the limits of Articles 216 to 219.

###### Article 432

Articles 420 to 423 above are applicable to the action for subsistence.

###### Article 433

The judgment that awards subsistence creates between the debtor and the beneficiary, as well as, where applicable, between each of them and the parents or the spouse of the other, the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 161 to 164 of this code.

###### Article 434

The res judicata on the action for subsistence raises no bar to a subsequent action for search of paternity.  
The award of subsistence shall cease to have effect if the paternal filiation of the child comes to be established subsequently with respect to another than the debtor.

### Titre IX : De la filiation adoptive

Chapitre Ier: De l'adoption plénière

##### Section I : Des conditions requises pour l'adoption plénière Article 435

Adoption, according to the regime established by the civil code, may be requested after five years of marriage by two spouses not legally separated.

###### Article 436

If the adopter is married and not legally separated, the consent of his spouse is necessary unless that spouse is unable to express his will.

###### Article 437

The adopters must be fifteen years older than the children they propose to adopt. If the latter are the children of their spouse, the required age difference is only ten years.  

However, the court may, if there are just grounds, pronounce the adoption when the age difference is less than those provided for in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 438

Adoption is permitted only in favour of children under fifteen years of age, received into the home of the adoptive parent or parents for at least six months.  
However, if the child is over fifteen years of age and was received before reaching that age by persons who did not meet the legal conditions for adoption or if the child was the subject of a simple adoption before reaching that age, full adoption may be requested, if the conditions are met, throughout the child's minority.  

If the child is over thirteen years of age, the adoptee must personally consent to his or her full adoption.

###### Article 439

No person may be adopted by several persons except by two spouses.  

However, a new adoption may be pronounced either after the death of the adoptive parent, or of both adoptive parents, or after the death of one of the two adoptive parents, if the application is submitted by the new spouse of the survivor.

###### Article 440

May be adopted:
1° Children for whom the father and mother or the family council have validly consented to the adoption;  
2° Children who have been legally entrusted to a duly registered association for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defence or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognised by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.  
3° Children declared abandoned under the conditions provided for in Article 448.

###### Article 441

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to his or her father and mother, both must consent to the adoption.  
If one of them is deceased or unable to express his or her will, if he or she has lost parental authority rights, the consent of the other is sufficient.

###### Article 442

When the filiation of a child is established only with respect to one of his or her parents, that parent gives consent to the adoption.

###### Article 443

When the father and mother of the child are deceased, unable to express their will or if they have lost their parental authority rights, consent is given by the family council, after obtaining the opinion of the person who, in fact, takes care of the child.  

The same applies when the filiation of the child is not established.

###### Article 444

Consent to adoption is given before the president of the Civil Chamber of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose of the domicile or residence of the person who consents, or before a Djiboutian or foreign notary, or before Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. It may also be received by a duly registered association for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defence or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognised by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.  
Consent to adoption may be retracted within three months. The retraction must be made by any means allowing confirmation of its receipt by the person or service that had received the consent to adoption. The return of the child to his or her parents upon request, even verbal, also constitutes proof of retraction.  

If at the expiration of the three-month period, the consent has not been retracted, the parents may still request the return of the child provided that the child has not been placed with a view to adoption. If the person who received the child refuses to return him or her, the parents may apply to the court which assesses, taking into account the interest of the child, whether it is appropriate to order the return. The return renders the consent to adoption null and void.

###### Article 445

The father and mother or the family council may consent to the adoption of the child leaving the choice of the adoptive parent to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorised adoption agency which would provisionally receive the child.

###### Article 446

Except in the case where there is a relationship of kinship or affinity up to and including the sixth degree between the adoptive parent and the adoptee, consent to the adoption of children under two years of age is valid only if the child has been effectively handed over to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorised adoption agency.

###### Article 447

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may pronounce the adoption if it considers abusive the refusal of consent opposed by the legitimate and natural parents or by one of them only, when they have lost interest in the child at the risk of compromising his or her health or morality.  
The same applies in case of abusive refusal of consent by the family council.

###### Article 448

A child received by a private individual, a private agency or an association as designated in Article 444, whose parents have manifestly lost interest during the year preceding the filing of the application for declaration of abandonment, may be declared abandoned by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.  
Parents who have not maintained with the child the relations necessary for the maintenance of emotional ties are considered to have manifestly lost interest in their child.  
The simple retraction of consent to adoption, the request for news or the intention expressed but not followed by effect to take back the child, is not a sufficient mark of interest to automatically justify the rejection of an application for declaration of abandonment.  

Abandonment is not declared if, during the period provided for in the first paragraph of this article, a member of the family has requested to assume responsibility for the child and if this request is deemed to be in the interest of the child.  

When it declares the child abandoned, the court delegates by the same decision the parental authority rights over the child to an association as designated in Article 444 or to the private individual guardian of the child.  

Third-party opposition is admissible only in case of fraud, deceit or error as to the identity of the child.

##### Section II

Placement with a view to full adoption and judgment of full adoption Article 449
Placement with a view to adoption is carried out by the effective delivery to the prospective adoptive parents of a child for whom consent to adoption has been validly and definitively given, or of a child declared abandoned by judicial decision.
