When the filiation of the child is not established, there can be no placement with a view to adoption during a period of three months from the receipt of the child.  
Placement cannot take place when the parents have requested the return of the child until a decision has been made on the merits of this request at the application of the most diligent party.

###### Article 450

Placement with a view to adoption prevents any return of the child to his or her family of origin. It precludes any declaration of filiation and any acknowledgment.  
If the placement with a view to adoption ceases or if the court has refused to pronounce the adoption, the effects of this placement are retroactively resolved.

###### Article 451

Adoption is pronounced upon the application of the adopter by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, which verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and whether the adoption is in the best interest of the child.  
In the case where the adopter has descendants, the court further verifies whether the adoption is not likely to compromise family life.  

If the adopter dies after having lawfully taken in the child with a view to adoption, the application may be presented in his or her name by the surviving spouse or one of the adopter's heirs.  

The judgment pronouncing the adoption is not reasoned.

###### Article 452

Third-party opposition to the adoption judgment is admissible only in case of fraud or deceit attributable to the adopters.

###### Article 453

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes final, the decision pronouncing full adoption is transcribed in the civil status registers of the place of birth of the adopted person, at the request of the Public Prosecutor.  

The transcription states the day, time and place of birth, the sex of the child as well as his or her given names, as they result from the adoption judgment, the given names, surnames, date and place of birth, occupation and domicile of the adopter or adopters. It contains no indication relating to the actual filiation of the child.  

The transcription serves as birth certificate for the adopted person.  

The original birth certificate and, where applicable, the birth certificate drawn up pursuant to Article 89 are, at the initiative of the Public Prosecutor, marked with the mention adoption and considered null and void.

##### Section III : Des effets de l'adoption plénière Article 454

Adoption produces its effects from the day of filing of the application for adoption.

###### Article 455

Adoption confers upon the child a filiation which replaces his or her original filiation: the adopted person ceases to belong to his or her family by blood, subject to the prohibitions on marriage referred to in Articles 161 to 164.  
However, the adoption of the child of the spouse allows his or her original filiation to subsist with respect to that spouse and his or her family. It produces, for the remainder, the effects of an adoption by two spouses.

###### Article 456

Adoption confers upon the child the name of the adopter and, in case of adoption by two spouses, the name of the husband.  

Upon the request of the adopter or adopters, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may modify the given names of the child.  

If the adopter is a married woman, the Civil Chamber may, in the adoption judgment, deduce from the consent of the adopter's husband that the latter's name will be conferred upon the adopted person; if the husband is deceased or unable to express his will, the court has sovereign discretion after consulting the husband's heirs or his closest successors.

###### Article 457

The adopted person has, in the family of the adopter, the same rights and the same obligations as a legitimate child.

###### Article 458

Adoption is irrevocable.

#### Chapitre II : De l'adoption simple

##### Section I : Des conditions requises et du jugement Article 459

Simple adoption is permitted regardless of the age of the adopted person.  

If the adopted person is over fifteen years of age, he or she must personally consent to the adoption.

###### Article 460

The provisions of Articles 435 to 437, 439 to 448, 451, 452, 454 and 456, last paragraph, are applicable to simple adoption.

###### Article 461

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes final, the decision pronouncing simple adoption is noted or transcribed in the civil status registers at the request of the Public Prosecutor.

##### Section II : Des effets de l'adoption simple Article 462

Simple adoption confers the name of the adopter upon the adopted person by adding it to the latter's name. The court may however decide that the adopted person shall bear only the name of the adopter.

###### Article 463

The adopted person remains in his or her family of origin and retains all his or her rights therein, in particular his or her inheritance rights.  

The prohibitions on marriage provided for in Articles 173 to 176 of this code apply between the adopted person and his or her family of origin.

###### Article 464

The adopter alone is vested with respect to the adopted person with all the rights of parental authority, including that of consenting to the marriage of the adopted person, unless he or she is the spouse of the father or mother of the adopted person; in that case, the adopter has parental authority concurrently with his or her spouse, but the latter retains the exercise thereof.  
The rights of parental authority are exercised by the adopter or adopters under the same conditions as with respect to the legitimate child.  
The rules of legal administration and guardianship of the legitimate child apply to the adopted person.

###### Article 465

The relationship of kinship resulting from adoption extends to the legitimate children of the adopted person.  

Marriage is prohibited:
1° Between the adopter, the adopted person and his or her descendants;  
2° Between the adopted person and the spouse of the adopter; reciprocally between the adopter and the spouse of the adopted person; 3° Between the adoptive children of the same individual;  
4° Between the adopted person and the children of the adopter.  

Nevertheless, the prohibitions on marriage set out in 3° and 4° above may be lifted by dispensation of the President of the Republic, if there are serious causes.  

The prohibition on marriage set out in 2° above may be lifted under the same conditions when the person who created the affinity is deceased.

###### Article 466

The adopted person owes maintenance to the adopter if he or she is in need and, reciprocally, the adopter owes maintenance to the adopted person.  
The obligation to provide maintenance continues to exist between the adopted person and his or her father and mother. However, the father and mother of the adopted person are required to provide him or her with maintenance only if he or she cannot obtain it from the adopter.

###### Article 467

The adopted person and his or her legitimate descendants have in the family of the adopter the same succession rights as a legitimate child without however acquiring the status of forced heir with respect to the ascendants of the adopter.

###### Article 468

If the adopted person dies without descendants, the property given by the adopter or received in his or her succession returns to the adopter or to his or her descendants, if they still exist in kind at the time of the death of the adopted person, subject to contribution to debts and subject to rights acquired by third parties. The property that the adopted person had received gratuitously from his or her father and mother likewise returns to the latter or to their descendants.  
The remainder of the property of the adopted person is divided in half between the family of origin and the family of the adopter, without prejudice to the rights of the spouse over the entire succession.

###### Article 469

Adoption retains all its effects, notwithstanding the subsequent establishment of a filiation link.

###### Article 470

If serious grounds are established, adoption may be revoked, at the request of the adopter or of the adopted person.  
The application for revocation made by the adopter is admissible only if the adopted person is over fifteen years of age.  
When the adopted person is a minor, the father and mother by blood or, failing them, a member of the family of origin up to and including the fourth degree, may also apply for revocation.

###### Article 471

The judgment revoking adoption must be reasoned.  
The operative part of the judgment is noted in the margin of the birth certificate or of the transcription of the adoption judgment, under the conditions provided for in Article 461.

###### Article 472

Revocation terminates for the future all the effects of adoption.

### Titre X : De l'autorité parentale

Chapitre Ier: De l'autorité parentale relativement à la personne de l'enfant

###### Article 473

The child, at any age, owes honor and respect to his or her father and mother.

###### Article 474

He or she remains under their authority until his or her majority or emancipation.

###### Article 475

Authority belongs to the father and mother to protect the child in his safety, health and morality. They have the right and duty towards him of custody, supervision and education.

###### Article 476

The child may not, without permission of the father and mother, leave the family home and he may not be removed from it except in cases of necessity as determined by law.

###### Article 477

The father and mother may not, except for serious reasons, obstruct the personal relations of the child with his grandparents. In the absence of agreement between the parties, the modalities of these relations are settled by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.  
In consideration of exceptional situations, the Civil Chamber may grant a right of correspondence or visitation to other persons, whether related or not.

##### Section I: On the exercise of parental authority Article 478

During marriage, the father and mother exercise their authority jointly.

###### Article 479

If the father and mother cannot agree on what the interest of the child requires, the practice they may have previously followed on similar occasions shall serve as their rule.  
In the absence of such practice or in case of dispute as to its existence or validity, the more diligent spouse may refer the matter to the president of the Court of First Instance or the judge he delegates for this purpose, who shall rule after having attempted to reconcile the parties.

###### Article 480

With regard to third parties in good faith, each spouse is deemed to act with the agreement of the other when he alone performs a usual act of parental authority relating to the person of the child.

###### Article 481

Loses the exercise of parental authority or is temporarily deprived of it that one of the father and mother who is in one of the following cases:
1° If he is unable to express his will, by reason of his incapacity, his absence, his remoteness or any other cause;  
2° If he has consented to a delegation of his rights according to the rules established in section III of this chapter; 3° If he has been convicted under one of the various counts of family abandonment, as long as he has not resumed his obligations for a period of at least six months;  
4° If a judgment of forfeiture or withdrawal has been pronounced against him, for those of his rights which have been withdrawn from him.

###### Article 482

If one of the father and mother dies or is in one of the cases enumerated by the preceding article, the exercise of parental authority is devolved in its entirety to the other.

###### Article 483

If the father and mother are divorced or legally separated, parental authority is exercised by the one of them to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other.  
When custody has been entrusted to a third party, the other attributes of parental authority continue to be exercised by the father and mother. But the court, in designating a third party as provisional guardian, may decide that he must request the opening of a guardianship.  

When ruling, the judge always does so taking into consideration the best interest of the child.

###### Article 484

Divorce or legal separation does not prevent the devolution provided for in article 482, even if the one of the father and mother who remains able to exercise parental authority had been deprived of custody by the effect of the judgment pronounced against him.  
Nevertheless, the Civil Chamber which had last ruled on custody may always be referred to by the family or by the public prosecutor, in order to designate a third party as guardian of the child, with or without opening of a guardianship, as stated in the preceding article.  
In exceptional circumstances, the Civil Chamber ruling on custody of the child after divorce or legal separation may decide, even during the lifetime of the spouses, that it shall not pass to the survivor in case of death of the custodial spouse. It may, in this case, designate the person to whom custody shall be provisionally devolved.

###### Article 485

If there remains neither father nor mother able to exercise parental authority, there shall be grounds for opening a guardianship.

###### Article 486

Concerning the natural child, parental authority is exercised by the one of the father and mother who has voluntarily recognized him, if he has been recognized by only one of them.  
If both have recognized him, parental authority is exercised in its entirety by the mother. The court may, nevertheless, at the request of either one or the other, or of the public prosecutor, decide that it shall be exercised either by the father alone, or by the father and mother jointly, to whom articles 478 to 480 shall then be applicable, as if the child were a legitimate child.

##### Section II: On educational assistance Article 487

If the health, safety or morality of an unemancipated minor is in danger, or if the conditions of his education are seriously compromised, educational assistance measures may be ordered by the court at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor. The judge may take up the matter on his own initiative in exceptional circumstances.  

These educational assistance measures may be ordered at the same time for several children subject to the same parental authority.  

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, or the judge he delegates for this purpose, has jurisdiction, subject to appeal, for all matters concerning educational assistance.  

The president or the delegated judge must always endeavor to obtain the family's consent to the measure envisaged.

###### Article 489

Whenever possible, the minor must be maintained in his current environment. In this case, the judge designates either a qualified person or an association as designated in article 444, giving the designated person or association the mission of providing aid and advice to the family, in order to overcome the material or moral difficulties it encounters. This person or association is responsible for monitoring the child's development and reporting to the judge periodically.  
The president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may also make the child's maintenance in his environment subject to particular obligations, such as that of regularly attending an educational establishment, or of engaging in a professional activity.

###### Article 490

If it is necessary to remove the child from his current environment, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may decide to entrust him:
1° To the one of the father and mother who did not have custody;  
2° To another member of the family or to a trustworthy third party; 3° To an association as designated in article 444.  
However, when a petition for divorce has been filed or a divorce judgment rendered between the father and mother, these measures may be taken only if a new fact likely to cause danger to the minor has been revealed subsequent to the decision ruling on custody of the child. They may not prevent the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge from deciding, by application of article 302, to whom the child must be entrusted. The same rules are applicable to legal separation.

###### Article 491

In the cases specified in 1° and 2° of the preceding article, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may entrust a qualified person, an association as designated in Article 444, or an observation, education or re-education service in an open environment, to provide assistance and advice to the guardian as well as to the family and to monitor the development of the child.  
In all cases, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may attach to the return of the child the same conditions as under Article 489, paragraph 2. He may also decide that he shall be given periodic reports on the situation of the child.

###### Article 492

On a provisional basis but subject to appeal, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may, during the proceedings, take one of the measures provided for in Articles 490 and 491.  
In case of urgency, the public prosecutor of the place where the minor was found has the same power, subject to referring the matter within eight days to the president of the Civil Chamber, who shall maintain, modify or withdraw the measure.

###### Article 493

Decisions taken in matters of educational assistance may be, at any time, modified or withdrawn by the judge who rendered them either on his own motion, or at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor.  

The father and mother whose child has given rise to an educational assistance measure retain their parental authority over him and exercise all the attributes thereof that are not incompatible with the application of the measure. They may not emancipate the child without authorization from the children's judge, as long as the educational assistance measure is being applied.  
If it has been necessary to place the child outside his parents' home, the parents retain a right of correspondence and a right of visit. The judge shall determine the conditions thereof and may, if the interest of the child so requires, decide that the exercise of these rights, or of one of them, shall be provisionally suspended.

###### Article 495

The costs of maintenance and education of the child who has been the subject of an educational assistance measure continue to be borne by his father and mother as well as by the ascendants from whom maintenance may be claimed, except for the power of the judge to discharge them therefrom in whole or in part.

##### Section III: On the delegation of parental authority Article 496

No renunciation, no assignment relating to parental authority, may have effect, except by virtue of a judgment and in the cases determined below.

###### Article 497

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, when called upon to rule on the custody or education of a minor child, have regard to the agreements that the father and mother may have freely concluded between themselves on this subject, unless one of them justifies serious grounds that would authorize him to revoke his consent.

###### Article 498

The father and mother, together or separately, or the tutor authorized by the family council, may, when they have entrusted the minor child of sixteen years to a trustworthy individual or to an establishment approved for this purpose, or an association as designated in Article 444, renounce in whole or in part the exercise of their authority.  
In this case, delegation, total or partial, of parental authority shall result from the judgment that shall be rendered by the Civil Chamber on the joint application of the delegators and the delegatee.  

The same delegation may be decided, at the sole request of the delegatee, when the parents have lost interest in the child for more than one year.

###### Article 499

The delegation of parental authority may also take place when the minor of sixteen years has been taken in without the intervention of the father and mother or of the tutor. But it is necessary, in this case, that the individual, establishment or association, after having taken in the child, has made a declaration thereof to the administrative authority of the place.  
This declaration is made within one week. The administrative authority, within the month that follows, gives notice thereof to the father and mother or to the tutor. The notification thus made to them opens a new period of three months at the expiration of which, failing by them to claim the child, they are presumed to renounce exercising their authority over him.  

The individual, establishment or association that has taken in the child may then present an application to the Civil Chamber for the purpose of having parental authority delegated to it totally or partially.

###### Article 500

The delegation may, in all cases, come to an end or be transferred by a new judgment, if new circumstances are justified.  

In the case where the restitution of the child is granted to the father and mother, the Civil Chamber shall charge them, if they are not indigent, with the reimbursement of all or part of the maintenance costs.  
When the application for restitution has been rejected, it may not be renewed until after six months from the day on which the decision of rejection became final.

###### Article 501

The right to consent to the adoption of the minor is never delegated.

##### Section IV

On the forfeiture and partial withdrawal of parental authority Article 502
May be deprived of parental authority by an express provision of the criminal judgment the father and mother who are convicted, either as perpetrators, co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offence committed against the person of their child, or as co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offence committed by their child.  

This forfeiture is applicable to ascendants other than the father and mother for the share of parental authority that may fall to them over their descendants.

###### Article 503

May be deprived of parental authority, outside of any criminal conviction, the father and mother who, either by ill-treatment, or by harmful examples of habitual drunkenness, notorious misconduct or delinquency, or by a lack of care or a lack of direction, manifestly endanger the safety, health or morality of the child.  
May likewise be deprived thereof, when an educational assistance measure had been taken with regard to the child, the father and mother who, for more than two years, have voluntarily abstained from exercising the rights and fulfilling the duties that Article 494 left to them.  
The action for forfeiture is brought before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, either by the public prosecutor, or by a member of the family or the tutor of the child.

###### Article 504

The forfeiture pronounced by virtue of one of the two preceding articles applies by operation of law to all the attributes, both patrimonial and personal, relating to parental authority; in the absence of other determination, it extends to all minor children already born at the time of the judgment.  
It entails, for the child, exemption from the maintenance obligation, by way of derogation from Articles 212 to 214, except for a contrary provision in the judgment of forfeiture.

###### Article 505

The judgment may, instead of total forfeiture, limit itself to pronouncing a partial withdrawal of rights, limited to the attributes that it specifies. It may also decide that the forfeiture or withdrawal shall have effect only with regard to certain of the children already born.

###### Article 506

In pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal of the right of custody, the court seized must, if the other parent is deceased or if he has lost the exercise of parental authority, either designate a third party who shall provisionally assume the custody of the child subject to his requesting the organization of guardianship, or entrust the child to an association as designated in Article 444.  

The court seized may take the same measures when parental authority is devolved to one of the parents by the effect of the forfeiture pronounced against the other.

###### Article 507

Fathers and mothers who have been subject to forfeiture or withdrawal of rights for one of the causes provided for in Articles 502 and 503, may, by petition, obtain from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, upon proof of new circumstances, that all or part of the rights of which they had been deprived be restored to them.  
The application for restoration may not be made until six months from the day on which the judgment pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal became final; in case of rejection, this application may not be renewed until after a new period of one year. No application shall be admissible when, before the filing of the petition, the child has been placed with a view to adoption.  

If restoration is granted, the public prosecutor shall request, where appropriate, educational assistance measures.

#### Chapter II: Parental authority in relation to the child's property Article 508

Fathers and mothers have, subject to the distinctions that follow, the administration and enjoyment of their child's property.

###### Article 509

Legal administration is exercised in accordance with the provisions of Articles 518 et seq. of this Code.

###### Article 510

The right of enjoyment ceases:
1° As soon as the child has reached sixteen years of age, or even earlier when he or she contracts marriage;  
2° By the causes that terminate parental authority, or even more specifically by those that terminate legal administration;  
3° By the causes that bring about the extinction of any usufruct.

###### Article 511

The charges of this enjoyment are:
1° Those to which usufructuaries are generally bound;  
2° The food, maintenance and education of the child, according to his or her fortune;  
3° The debts encumbering the succession received by the child insofar as they should have been paid from the income.

###### Article 512

This enjoyment shall not take place for the benefit of the surviving spouse who has failed to make an inventory, authentic or under private signature, of the property accruing to the minor.

###### Article 513

Legal enjoyment does not extend to property that the child may acquire through his or her work, nor to property given or bequeathed to him or her on the express condition that the father and mother shall not enjoy it.

### Title XI: Minority, guardianship and emancipation

###### Article 514

In this title, whenever mention is made of the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he or she has designated.  

Chapter I: Minority Article 515
The minor is the individual of either sex who has not yet reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 516

In any proceedings concerning him or her, the minor capable of discernment may, without prejudice to the provisions providing for his or her intervention or consent, be heard by the judge or, when his or her interest so requires, by the person designated by the judge for that purpose.  
This hearing is a matter of right when the minor so requests. When the minor refuses to be heard, the judge assesses the merits of this refusal. He or she may be heard alone, with a lawyer or a person of his or her choice.

###### Article 517

The legal administrator represents the minor in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes minors to act themselves.

#### Chapter II: Legal administration Article 518

Legal administration belongs to the parents.  
If parental authority is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is a legal administrator. In other cases, legal administration belongs to the parent who exercises parental authority.

###### Article 519

When legal administration is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is deemed, with respect to third parties, to have received from the other the power to perform alone acts of administration relating to the minor's property.  
The list of acts that are regarded as acts of administration is defined by presidential decree.

###### Article 520

When the interests of the sole legal administrator or, as the case may be, of both legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the latter request the appointment of an ad hoc administrator by the judge. In the absence of diligence by the legal administrators, the judge may proceed with this appointment at the request of the public prosecutor, the minor himself or herself or of his or her own motion.  
When the interests of one of the two legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the judge may authorize the other legal administrator to represent the child for one or more specified acts.

###### Article 521

Property given or bequeathed to the minor on condition that it be administered by a third party is not subject to legal administration.  

The third-party administrator has the powers conferred upon him or her by the gift, the will or, failing that, those of a legal administrator.  

When the third-party administrator refuses this function or is legally unable to exercise it, the judge designates an ad hoc administrator to replace him or her.

###### Article 522

The legal administrator is required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in the management of the minor's property, in the sole interest of the minor.

###### Article 523

The legal administrator is liable for any damage resulting from any fault he or she commits in the management of the minor's property.  
If legal administration is exercised jointly, both parents are jointly and severally liable.  

The action for liability is barred after five years from the majority of the person concerned or his or her emancipation.

#### Chapter III: Guardianship

##### Section I: Cases of opening and termination of guardianship Article 524

Guardianship opens when the father and mother are both deceased or are deprived of the exercise of parental authority.  
It also opens with respect to a child whose filiation is not legally established.

###### Article 525

In case of legal administration, the judge may, at any time and for serious cause, either of his or her own motion or at the request of relatives or in-laws or the public prosecutor, decide to open guardianship after having heard or summoned, except in urgent cases, the legal administrator. The latter may not perform any act of disposition from the day he or she is informed of the application and until the final judgment except in case of urgency.  
If guardianship is opened, the judge convenes the family council, which may either appoint the legal administrator as guardian or designate another guardian.

###### Article 526

If a child comes to be recognized by one of his or her two parents after the opening of guardianship, the judge may, at the request of that parent, decide to substitute legal administration for guardianship.

###### Article 527

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 526, guardianship ends upon the emancipation of the minor or upon his or her majority. It also ends in case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata or in case of death of the person concerned.

##### Section II: Organization and operation of guardianship

###### § 1. Guardianship duties

###### Article 528

Guardianship, protection owed to the child, is a public duty. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 529

The following may not exercise the various duties of guardianship:
1° Unemancipated minors, except if they are the father or mother of the minor under guardianship
2° Adults who benefit from a legal protection measure provided for by this Code; 3° Persons from whom parental authority has been withdrawn;  
4° Persons who have been prohibited from exercising guardianship duties by court decision.

###### Article 530

Any tutorship duty may be withdrawn by reason of the unfitness, negligence, misconduct or fraud of the person to whom it has been entrusted. The same applies when a dispute or conflict of interest prevents the holder of the duty from exercising it in the interest of the minor.  
Any person to whom a tutorship duty has been entrusted may be replaced in the event of a significant change in their situation or in that of the minor.

###### Article 531

The family council rules on impediments, withdrawals and replacements concerning the tutor.  
The judge rules on those concerning the other members of the family council.  

A tutorship duty may only be withdrawn, by the person who entrusted it, after its holder has been heard or summoned.  
The judge may, if they consider that there is urgency, prescribe provisional measures in the interest of the minor.

###### § 2. Du conseil de famille Article 532

Even in the presence of a testamentary tutor and except in case of vacancy, the tutorship is organized with a family council.

###### Article 533

The judge appoints the members of the family council for the duration of the tutorship.  

The family council is composed of at least four members, including the tutor. The judge is not included in this number.  
Relatives and in-laws of the minor's father and mother as well as any person, residing in Djibouti or abroad, who shows an interest in the minor may be members of the family council.  

The members of the family council are chosen in consideration of the interest of the minor and according to their aptitude, the habitual relations they maintained with the minor's father or mother, the emotional ties they have with the minor as well as their availability.  

The judge must avoid, insofar as possible, leaving either of the two branches, paternal or maternal, without representation.

###### Article 534

The family council is presided over by the judge. Its deliberations are adopted by vote of its members.  

However, the tutor does not vote.  

In the event of a tie, the judge's vote is decisive.

###### Article 535

The family council determines the general conditions of the minor's maintenance and education having regard to the wishes that the father and mother may have expressed.  
It assesses the allowances that may be granted to the tutor.  

It makes the decisions and gives the tutor the necessary authorizations for the management of the minor's property in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII of this code.

###### Article 536

The deliberations of the family council are null and void when they have been obtained by deceit or fraud or when substantial formalities have been omitted.  
The action for nullity may be brought by the tutor, the other members of the family council and the public prosecutor within two years of the deliberation as well as by the minor who has become of age or emancipated within two years of their majority or emancipation. The limitation period does not run if there has been deceit or fraud as long as the fact which is at its origin is not discovered.  

Acts performed pursuant to an annulled deliberation are annulled upon simple request by one of the persons entitled to act pursuant to the preceding paragraph. However, the time limit runs from the act and not from the deliberation.

###### § 3. Du tuteur Article 537

The individual right to choose a tutor, whether or not related to the minor, belongs only to the last surviving of the father and mother if they retained, on the day of their death, the exercise of parental authority.  
This designation may only be made in the form of a will or a special declaration before a notary.  
It is binding on the family council unless the interest of the minor requires that it be set aside. In this case, the family council decides to refer the matter to the judge, who will assess.  

The tutor designated by the father or mother is not required to accept the tutorship.

###### Article 538

If there is no testamentary tutor, or if the person designated in that capacity ceases their functions, or refuses the tutorship, the family council appoints a tutor to the minor.

###### Article 539

The family council may, in consideration of the minor's situation, the aptitudes of the interested parties and the composition of the estate to be administered, appoint several tutors to exercise the protective measure jointly. Each tutor is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a tutor would not need any authorization.  
The family council may decide that the exercise of the tutorship will be divided between a tutor responsible for the person of the minor and a tutor responsible for the management of their property. Unless otherwise decided by the family council, these tutors are independent of each other, and are not responsible to each other. However, they inform each other of the decisions they make

###### Article 540

The tutor is appointed for the duration of the tutorship.

###### Article 541

Tutorship is a personal duty.  

It is not transmitted to the tutor's heirs.

###### Article 542

The tutor takes care of the person of the minor and represents them in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes the minor to act themselves.  
The tutor represents the minor in legal proceedings. However, they may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert extra-patrimonial rights except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council. The family council may also enjoin the tutor to withdraw from the proceedings or action, or to settle.  

The tutor manages the minor's property and accounts for their management in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### § 4. De la vacance de la tutelle Article 543

The President of the Court of First Instance and the public prosecutor exercise general supervision over the tutorships within their jurisdiction.  

Tutors and other tutorship bodies are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.  
The judge may issue injunctions against them and impose a civil fine of 50,000 to 200,000 FD on those who have not complied.

###### § 5. De la responsabilité Article 544

All tutorship bodies are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.  

When the fault at the origin of the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the tutorship by the judges or the court clerk, the action for liability is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 545

The action for liability is barred after five years from the majority of the interested party, even if the management continued beyond, or from the end of the measure if it ceases before.

#### Chapitre IV : De l'émancipation Article 546

The minor is emancipated by operation of law by marriage.

###### Article 547

The minor, even if not married, may be emancipated when they have reached the age of sixteen years.  

After hearing the minor, this emancipation shall be pronounced, if there are just grounds, by the judge, at the request of the father and mother or one of them.  
When the request is submitted by only one of the parents, the judge decides, after having heard the other parent unless the latter is unable to express their will.

###### Article 548

The minor left without father or mother may be emancipated at the request of the family council, convened by the tutor or by the court at the request of a member of the family council or the minor themselves. Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 547 are then applicable.

###### Article 549

The account of the administration, if applicable, or of the tutorship is rendered to the emancipated minor in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### Article 550

The emancipated minor is capable, like an adult, of all acts of civil life.

However, in order to marry or consent to adoption, he must observe the same rules as if he were not emancipated.

###### Article 551

The emancipated minor ceases to be under the authority of his father and mother.  
They are not liable by operation of law, in their sole capacity as father or mother, for damage he may cause to others subsequent to his emancipation.

###### Article 552

The emancipated minor may not be a trader.

### Titre XII : Majority and adults protected by law

Chapitre Ier: General provisions Article 553
The age of majority is fixed at eighteen years completed; at that age, everyone is capable of exercising the rights which he enjoys.

##### Section I : Provisions independent of protective measures Article 554

To make a valid act, one must be of sound mind. It is for those who bring an action for nullity on this ground to prove the existence of a mental disorder at the time of the act.

###### Article 555

During his lifetime, the action for nullity belongs only to the person concerned.

After his death, acts done by him, other than inter vivos gifts and wills, may be challenged by his heirs, for unsoundness of mind, only in the following cases:

1° If the act bears in itself proof of a mental disorder;  
2° If it was done while the person concerned was placed under judicial protection;  
3° If an action was brought before his death for the purpose of opening a curatorship or tutorship or for the purpose of family empowerment.  
The action for nullity is available within a period of five years, to the person concerned from the cessation of his condition and, after his death, to the heirs, from the day of death.

###### Article 556

A person who has caused damage to another while under the influence of a mental disorder is nonetheless obliged to make reparation.

##### Section II : Provisions common to protected adults Article 557

Adult persons receive protection of their person and their property that their condition or situation makes necessary according to the procedures provided for in this title.  
This protection is established and ensured with respect for individual freedoms, fundamental rights and the dignity of the person.  
Its purpose is the interest of the protected person. It promotes, as far as possible, the autonomy of that person. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 558

The President of the Court of First Instance and the Public Prosecutor exercise general supervision of protective measures in their jurisdiction. They may visit or have visited the protected persons and those who are the subject of an application for protection, whatever the measure pronounced or sought.  
Persons responsible for protection are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.

###### Article 559

The President of the Court of First Instance may issue injunctions against persons responsible for protection and impose a civil fine of 10,000 FD to 100,000 FD on those who have not complied.  
He may also remove them from their mission in the event of a clear failure in the exercise thereof, after having heard them or summoned them.

###### Article 560

Without prejudice to the application of the rules of management of affairs, the death of the protected person terminates the mission of the person responsible for protection.

###### Article 561

Persons exercise judicial protective measures without remuneration.  
However, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may authorize, according to the importance of the property managed or the difficulty of exercising the measure, the payment of an allowance to the person responsible for protection. He fixes the amount thereof. This allowance is borne by the protected person.

###### Article 562

All organs of the judicial protective measure are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.

However, when the person designated as an organ of judicial protection exercises his mission without remuneration, he incurs liability, for acts performed with his assistance, only in the event of fraud or gross negligence.

###### Article 563

When the fault causing the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the protective measure by the judge or the clerk, the action for liability brought by the protected person or person who has been protected or by his heirs is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 564

The action for liability is barred after five years from the end of the protective measure even though the management may have continued beyond.  
However, when the curatorship has ceased by the opening of a tutorship measure, the period runs only from the expiration of the latter.

#### Chapitre II

Judicial protective measures for adults Section I: General provisions

###### Article 565

Any person unable to provide for his interests alone by reason of a medically established impairment, either of his mental faculties or of his bodily faculties such as to prevent the expression of his will, may benefit from a judicial protective measure provided for in this chapter.  
Unless otherwise provided, the measure is intended for the protection of both the person and the property interests of that person. It may, however, be expressly limited to one of these two missions.

###### Article 566

The dwelling of the protected person and the furniture with which it is furnished, whether it is a principal or secondary residence, are kept at the disposal of that person as long as possible.  
The power to administer the property mentioned in the first paragraph permits only precarious enjoyment agreements which cease, notwithstanding any provisions or stipulations to the contrary, upon the return of the protected person to his dwelling.

If it becomes necessary or if it is in the interest of the protected person that the rights relating to his dwelling or his furniture be disposed of by alienation, termination or conclusion of a lease, the act is authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, by the President of the Court of First Instance, without prejudice to the formalities that the nature of the property may require. If the purpose of the act is the admission of the person concerned to an establishment, the prior opinion of a doctor, not exercising a function or occupying a position in that establishment, is required. In all cases, souvenirs, objects of a personal nature, those essential for disabled persons or intended for the care of sick persons are kept at the disposal of the person concerned, where appropriate by the care of the establishment in which he is accommodated.

###### Article 567

The person responsible for the protective measure may not proceed with the modification of accounts or passbooks opened in the name of the protected person, nor with the opening of another account or passbook with a bank or any other organization legally authorized to receive funds from the public. The family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance may however authorize it if the interest of the protected person so requires.

A special account is opened in the name of the protected person with a local bank by the person responsible for the protection if the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance deems it necessary.
When the protected person holds no account or passbook, the person responsible for the protective measure opens one for them.

Banking operations for collection, payment and asset management carried out in the name and on behalf of the protected person are conducted exclusively by means of accounts opened in the name of the latter; the fruits, products and capital gains generated by the funds and securities belonging to the protected person accrue exclusively to them.
If the protected person has been subject to a prohibition on issuing checks, the person responsible for the protective measure may nevertheless, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, operate under their signature the accounts of which the protected person is the holder and have access to all usual means of payment.

##### Section II: Provisions common to judicial measures Article 568

The protective measure may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application either of the rules of common law of representation, or of those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protective measure.

The measure is proportionate and individualized according to the degree of impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned.

###### Article 569

The judicial protective measure may be opened for an emancipated minor as well as for an adult.

For a non-emancipated minor, the application may be filed and adjudicated in the last year of their minority. The judicial protective measure takes effect, however, only from the day of their majority.

###### Article 570

The application for opening of the measure may be presented to the judge by the person who needs to be protected or, as the case may be, by their spouse, or by a relative or a person related by marriage, a person maintaining close and stable ties with the adult, or the person exercising legal protective measures over them.
It may also be presented by the public prosecutor either of their own motion or at the request of a third party.

###### Article 571

The application is accompanied, on pain of inadmissibility, by a detailed certificate drafted by a doctor chosen from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This doctor may request the opinion of the treating physician of the person who needs to be protected.

###### Article 572

The judge rules after the person has been heard or summoned. The person concerned may be accompanied by a lawyer or, subject to the agreement of the judge, by any other person of their choice.
The judge may however, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with the hearing of the person concerned if it is likely to harm their health or if they are unable to express their will.

##### Section III: Safeguard of justice Article 573

The judge may place under safeguard of justice the person who, for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, needs temporary legal protection or to be represented for the accomplishment of certain specified acts.

This measure may also be pronounced by the judge, seized of curatorship or guardianship proceedings, for the duration of the proceedings.

###### Article 574

The person placed under safeguard of justice retains the exercise of their rights. However, they may not, on pain of nullity, perform an act for which a special agent has been designated pursuant to Article 576.
The acts they have performed and the commitments they have entered into during the duration of the measure may be annulled for simple lesion or reduced in case of excess. The courts take into consideration in particular the utility or inutility of the transaction, the importance or consistency of the estate of the protected person and the good or bad faith of those with whom they have contracted.

The action for nullity or reduction belongs only to the protected person and, after their death, to their heirs. It is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it.

###### Article 575

The mandate by which the protected person has entrusted another person with the administration of their property continues to produce its effects during the safeguard of justice unless it is revoked or suspended by the president of the Court of First Instance; the agent being heard or summoned.
In the absence of a mandate, the rules of management of affairs are applicable.

Those who have standing to request the opening of a curatorship or guardianship are required to perform the conservatory acts essential to the preservation of the estate of the protected person as soon as they have knowledge both of their urgency and of the opening of the measure of safeguard. The same provisions are applicable to the person or establishment that accommodates the person placed under safeguard.

###### Article 576

If there is need to act outside the cases defined in Article 570, any interested person may give notice thereof to the judge.

The judge may designate a special agent, for the purpose of performing one or more specified acts, even acts of disposition, made necessary by the management of the estate of the protected person
The special agent is required to account for the execution of their mandate to the protected person and to the judge under the conditions provided for in Articles 639 to 644.

###### Article 577

The special agent may also be entrusted with a mission of protection of the person in compliance with Articles 595 to 600.

###### Article 578

On pain of lapse, the measure of safeguard of justice may not exceed one year, renewable once under the conditions set forth in the fourth paragraph of Article 581.
The judge may, at any time, order its lifting if the need for temporary protection ceases.

In the absence of lifting, the safeguard of justice ends upon expiration of the period or after the accomplishment of the acts for which it was ordered. It also ends by the opening of a measure of curatorship or guardianship from the day on which the new legal protective measure takes effect.

##### Section IV: On curatorship and guardianship Article 579

A person who, without being incapable of acting themselves, needs, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, to be assisted or supervised in a continuous manner in important acts of civil life may be placed under curatorship.  
Curatorship shall only be ordered if it is established that safeguard of justice cannot provide sufficient protection.  

A person who, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, must be represented in a continuous manner in acts of civil life, may be placed under guardianship.  
Guardianship shall only be ordered if it is established that neither safeguard of justice nor curatorship can provide sufficient protection.

###### Subsection 1: On the duration of the measure Article 580

The President of the Court of First Instance shall set the duration of the measure, which may not exceed five years.  

The judge who orders a guardianship measure may, by specially reasoned decision and upon the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list of judicial experts in accordance with Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure finding that the impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to improve according to acquired scientific knowledge, set a longer duration, not exceeding ten years.

###### Article 581

The judge may renew the measure for the same duration.  

However, when the impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to improve according to acquired scientific knowledge, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and upon the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, renew the measure for a longer duration that they determine, not exceeding twenty years.  
The judge may, at any time, terminate the measure, modify it or substitute another measure provided for in this title, after obtaining the opinion of the person responsible for the protection measure.  
They shall rule of their own motion or at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 570, upon review of a medical certificate and under the conditions provided for in Article 572. However, they may only strengthen the protection regime of the person concerned if they are seized with a request to that effect satisfying Articles 570 and 571.

###### Article 582

The measure shall terminate, in the absence of renewal, upon expiration of the set period, in the event of a judgment lifting it having become res judicata or in the event of the death of the person concerned.  
The judge may also terminate it when the protected person resides outside the national territory, if such distance prevents the monitoring and supervision of the measure.

###### Subsection 2: On publication of the measure Article 583

Judgments ordering the opening, modification or lifting of curatorship or guardianship shall only be enforceable against third parties two months after the notation thereof has been made in the margin of the birth certificate of the protected person according to the procedures provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure.  

However, even in the absence of such notation, they shall be enforceable against third parties who have personal knowledge thereof.

###### Subsection 3: On protection bodies Article 584

Curatorship and guardianship duties are subject to the conditions provided for curatorship duties of minors by Articles 529 to 531. However, the powers conferred by Article 531 on the family council shall be exercised by the judge in the absence of establishment of that body.  

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries, may not exercise curatorship or guardianship duties with regard to their patients.  
The fiduciary designated by the fiduciary contract may not exercise curatorship or guardianship duties with regard to the settlor.

###### § 1. On the curator and the guardian Article 585

A curator or a guardian shall be designated for the protected person under the conditions provided for in this paragraph and subject to the powers conferred on the family council if it has been established.

###### Article 586

The curator or the guardian shall be designated by the judge.  

The judge may, in consideration of the situation of the protected person, the aptitudes of the persons concerned and the composition of the estate to be administered, designate several curators or several guardians to exercise the protection measure jointly. Each curator or guardian shall be deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone in acts for which a guardian would not need any authorization.  
The judge may divide the protection measure between a curator or a guardian responsible for the protection of the person and a curator or a guardian responsible for estate management.  
Unless the judge has decided otherwise, the persons designated pursuant to the preceding paragraph shall be independent of one another, and shall not be responsible to one another. However, they shall inform each other of the decisions they make.

###### Article 587

The designation by a person of one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian in the event that they are placed under curatorship or guardianship shall be binding on the judge, unless the designated person refuses the mission or is unable to exercise it, or unless the interest of the protected person requires their exclusion. In case of difficulty, the judge shall rule.  
The same shall apply when the parents or the last surviving of the father and mother, not subject to a curatorship or guardianship measure, who exercise parental authority over their minor child or assume the material and emotional care of their adult child designate one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian from the day when they themselves die or can no longer continue to care for the person concerned.

###### Article 588

In the absence of designation made pursuant to Article 587, the judge shall appoint, as curator or guardian, the spouse of the protected person, unless common life has ceased between them or another cause prevents entrusting them with the measure.  
In the absence of appointment made pursuant to the preceding paragraph and subject to the last reservation mentioned therein, the judge shall designate a relative, a person related by marriage or a person residing with the protected adult or maintaining close and stable ties with them.  

The judge shall take into consideration the feelings expressed by the person concerned, their usual relationships, the interest shown in them and any recommendations of their relatives and persons related by marriage as well as their entourage.

###### Article 589

When no family member or close person can assume the curatorship or guardianship, the judge shall designate a judicial representative for the protection of adults. This representative may not refuse to perform urgent acts required by the interest of the protected person, in particular conservatory acts essential to the preservation of their estate.

###### Article 590

If the interest of the person accommodated or cared for in a health establishment so justifies, the judge may designate, as curator or guardian, a person or service officer of the establishment registered on the list of judicial representatives for the protection of adults.  
The mission entrusted to the representative shall extend to the protection of the person, unless the judge decides otherwise.

###### Article 591

No one shall be required to retain the curatorship or guardianship of a person beyond five years, with the exception of the spouse, the children of the person concerned as well as judicial representatives for the protection of adults.

###### § 2. Of the ad hoc curator and the ad hoc guardian

###### Article 592

The curator or guardian whose interests are, on the occasion of an act or a series of acts, in opposition with those of the protected person or who cannot provide assistance or act on their behalf due to the limitations of their mission, shall have appointed by the judge or by the family council if one has been constituted an ad hoc curator or guardian, that is to say a curator or guardian for the act or series of acts concerned.  
This appointment may also be made at the request of the Public Prosecutor, any interested party or of the court's own motion.

###### § 3. Of the family council of adults under guardianship Article 593

The judge may organize the guardianship with a family council if the necessities of protecting the person or the extent of their patrimony justify it and if the composition of their family and entourage permits it.  
The judge appoints the members of the family council in consideration of the sentiments expressed by the protected person, their habitual relationships, the interest shown in them and any recommendations of their relatives and in-laws as well as their entourage.  

The family council appoints the guardian, and, where applicable, the ad hoc guardian in accordance with articles 584 to 591.  
The rules prescribed for the family council of minors apply, excluding those provided for in article 532, in the fourth paragraph of article 533 and in the first paragraph of article 535. For the application of the third paragraph of article 536, the time limit runs, when the action is brought by the protected adult, from the day the protection measure ends.

###### Article 594

The judge may authorize the family council to meet and deliberate outside their presence, when the latter has appointed a judicial representative for the protection of adults as guardian. The family council then appoints a president and a secretary from among its members, excluding the guardian.  
The president of the family council transmits to the judge in advance the agenda of each meeting.  

The decisions taken by the family council only take effect in the absence of opposition filed by the judge, under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.  
The president exercises the missions devolved to the judge for the convocation, meeting and deliberation of the family council. The judge may however, at any time, convene a meeting of the family council under their presidency.

###### Sous-section 4

Effects of curatorship and guardianship with regard to the protection of the person Article 595
The protected person receives from the person responsible for their protection, according to methods adapted to their condition and without prejudice to the information that third parties are required to provide them by virtue of the law, all

information about their personal situation, about the acts that the person responsible for their protection wishes to carry out, their usefulness, their degree of urgency, their effects and the consequences of a refusal on their part.

###### Article 596

Subject to the special provisions provided for by law, the performance of acts whose nature implies a strictly personal consent can never give rise to assistance or representation of the protected person.  

The declaration of birth of a child, their recognition, acts of parental authority relating to the person of a child, the declaration of the choice or change of name of a child and the consent given to their own adoption or to that of their child are deemed strictly personal.

###### Article 597

Outside the cases provided for in article 596, the protected person alone makes decisions relating to their person to the extent that their condition permits.  
When the condition of the protected person does not permit them to make an informed personal decision alone, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance may provide that they will benefit, for all acts relating to their person or those among them that it enumerates, from the assistance of the person responsible for their protection. In the event that this assistance would not suffice, that same person may, where applicable after the opening of a guardianship measure, authorize the guardian to represent the interested party.  

However, except in an emergency, the person responsible for the protection of the adult may not, without the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, make a decision having the effect of seriously affecting the bodily integrity of the protected person or the privacy of their private life.  

The person responsible for the protection of the adult may take with regard to them the protection measures strictly necessary to put an end to the danger that their own behavior would cause to the interested party.  
They inform the family council without delay and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 598

The protected person chooses the place of their residence.  

They freely maintain personal relationships with any third party, relative or not. They have the right to be visited and, where applicable, accommodated by them.  

In case of difficulty, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance rules.

###### Article 599

The marriage of a person under curatorship is permitted only with the authorization of the curator or, failing that, that of the judge.  
The marriage of a person under guardianship is permitted only with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, and after hearing of the future spouses by the judge.  

The opinion of the parents and the entourage is possibly obtained by the judge.

###### Article 600

At the opening of the measure or, failing that, subsequently, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance decides on the conditions under which the curator or guardian responsible for a mission of protection of the person accounts for the steps they take in this capacity.

###### Sous-section 5: Of the regularity of acts Article 601

The obligations resulting from acts performed by the protected person less than two years before the publication of the judgment opening the protection measure may be reduced on the sole proof that their inability to defend their interests, as a result of the alteration of their personal faculties, was notorious or known to the contracting party at the time the acts were entered into.  

These acts may, under the same conditions, be annulled if harm suffered by the protected person is established.  
By way of derogation from article 2387, the action must be brought within five years from the date of the judgment opening the measure.


This excerpt sits under: REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI > BOOK I: OF PERSONS > Title XII: Of majority and adults protected by law > Chapter II > Section IV: Of curatorship and guardianship Article 579

###### Article 602

From the publication of the opening judgment, the irregularity of acts performed by the protected person or by the person responsible for the protection is sanctioned under the following conditions:
1° If the protected person has performed alone an act that they could do without the assistance or representation of the person responsible for their protection, the act remains subject to the actions for nullity or reduction provided for in Article 574 as if it had been performed by a person placed under safeguard of justice, unless it has been expressly authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance.  
2° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which they should have been assisted, the act may only be annulled if it is established that the protected person has suffered harm;  
3° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which they should have been represented, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm;  
4° If the guardian or curator has performed alone an act that should have been done by the protected person either alone or with their assistance or that could only be performed with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm.  
The curator or guardian may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction of the acts provided for in 1°, 2° and 3°.  
In all cases, the action is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it.  
During this period and as long as the protection measure is open, the act provided for in 4° may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge or the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 603

Articles 601 and 602 do not preclude the application of Articles 554 and 555.

###### Sous-section 6 : Des actes faits dans la curatelle Article 604

The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, perform any act which, in case of guardianship, would have required authorization from the judge or the family council.  

When concluding a written act, the assistance of the curator is manifested by the affixing of their signature next to that of the protected person. If the latter does not know how to sign, the act is marked with their fingerprint.  
On pain of nullity, any service of process made on the protected person must also be made on the curator.

###### Article 605

Capital sums due to the person under curatorship are paid directly into an account opened in their name alone and indicating their protection regime, with an establishment authorized to receive funds from the public.  
The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, use their capital. This assistance is also required to bring legal action or defend in it.

###### Article 606

The curator may not substitute themselves for the person under curatorship to act in their name.  

However, the curator may, if they find that the person under curatorship is seriously compromising their interests, refer the matter to the judge to be authorized to perform alone a specific act or to initiate the opening of guardianship.  
If the curator refuses their assistance for an act for which their cooperation is required, the person under curatorship may ask the judge for authorization to perform it alone.

###### Article 607

The person under curatorship may freely make a will subject to the provisions of Article 554. They may only make a donation with the assistance of the curator.  
The curator is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person when they are the beneficiary of the donation.

###### Article 608

At any time, the judge may, by way of derogation from Article 604, list certain acts that the person under curatorship has the capacity to perform alone or, conversely, add other acts to those for which the assistance of the curator is required.

###### Article 609

The judge may also, at any time, order a reinforced curatorship. In this case, the curator alone receives the income of the person under curatorship in an account opened in the name of the latter. They themselves ensure the settlement of expenses with third parties and deposit the surplus in an account left at the disposal of the person concerned or pay it into their hands.  
Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 598, the judge may authorize the curator to conclude alone a residential lease or an accommodation agreement ensuring the housing of the protected person.  
Reinforced curatorship is subject to the provisions of Articles 630 and 639 to 644.

###### Sous-section 7 : Des actes faits dans la tutelle Article 610

Subject to cases where the law or custom authorizes the person under guardianship to act themselves, the guardian represents them in all acts of civil life.  

However, the judge may, in the opening judgment or subsequently, list certain acts that the person under guardianship will have the capacity to perform alone or with the assistance of the guardian.

###### Article 611

The person under guardianship is represented in acts necessary for the management of their patrimony under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in Title XIII.

###### Article 612

The person under guardianship is represented in court by the guardian.  

The guardian may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert the extra-patrimonial rights of the protected person except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance.  
The judge or the family council may also enjoin the guardian to withdraw from the proceedings or action or to settle.

###### Article 613

The person under guardianship may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance, be assisted or if necessary represented by the guardian to make donations.  
They may only make their will alone after the opening of the guardianship with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance, this on pain of nullity of the act. The guardian may neither assist nor represent them on this occasion.  
However, they may alone revoke the will made before or after the opening of the guardianship.  

The will made prior to the opening of the guardianship remains valid unless it is established that, since this opening, the cause that had determined the testator to dispose has disappeared.

##### Section V : De l'habilitation familiale Article 614

When a person is unable to express their will for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, the judge may authorize one or more persons chosen from among their ascendants or descendants, brothers and sisters or, unless the community of life has ceased between them, the spouse or cohabitant to represent them or to perform one or more acts in their name under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in this section and those of Title XV of Book III of this code.  
The authorized person must meet the conditions for exercising guardianship duties. They exercise their mission free of charge.

###### Article 615

Family authorization may only be ordered by the judge in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application, either of the rules of common law of representation, or of those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or again by another less restrictive judicial protection measure.

###### Article 616

The application for the appointment of an authorized person may be submitted to the judge by one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or by the public prosecutor at the request of one of them.

The application is filed, examined and adjudicated in accordance with the rules of the code of civil procedure and in compliance with the provisions of Articles 569 and 571.

###### Article 617

The person in respect of whom authorization is sought is heard or summoned according to the procedures provided for in the first paragraph of Article 572. However, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of the doctor mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with their hearing if it is likely to harm their health or if the person is unable to express themselves.
The judge ensures the consent or, failing that, the absence of legitimate opposition to the authorization measure and to the choice of the authorized person from the relatives mentioned in Article 614 who maintain close and stable ties with the person or who show interest in them and whose existence is known to the judge at the time of ruling.

###### Article 618

The judge rules on the choice of the authorized person and the scope of the authorization by ensuring that the proposed arrangement is in accordance with the property interests and, where applicable, personal interests of the person concerned.

###### Article 619

The authorization may cover:
1° one or more of the acts that the guardian has the power to perform, alone or with authorization, on the property of the person concerned;
2° one or more acts relating to the person to be protected. In this case, the authorization is exercised in compliance with the provisions of Articles 595 to 598 of this code.

The authorized person may perform an act of gratuitous disposition only with the authorization of the judge.
