If the interest of the person to be protected so requires, the judge may issue a general authorization covering all acts or one of the two categories of acts mentioned in points 1° and 2° of this article.

###### Article 620

The authorized person may, unless the judge decides otherwise, proceed without authorization with the acts mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 567.

###### Article 621

If the person in respect of whom authorization has been issued performs alone an act whose performance has been entrusted to the authorized person, it is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.
The obligations resulting from acts performed by a person in respect of whom a family authorization measure was pronounced less than two years before the judgment issuing the authorization may be reduced or annulled under the conditions provided for in Article 601.
The authorized person may, with the authorization of the judge, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction provided for in the above paragraphs.
If the authorized person performs alone, in that capacity, an act not falling within the scope of the authorization issued to them or which could only be performed with the authorization of the judge, the act is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.

In all cases, the action for nullity or reduction is brought within five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to bring it. During

this period and as long as the authorization measure is in effect, the contested act may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 622

The judge rules at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor on any difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the arrangement.
Seized for this purpose under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 616, the judge may, at any time, modify the scope of the authorization or terminate it, after having heard or summoned, on the one hand, the person in respect of whom the authorization has been issued, under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 617 and, on the other hand, the authorized person.

###### Article 623

In addition to the death of the person in respect of whom the family authorization has been issued, this family authorization terminates:
1° By the placement of the person concerned under safeguard of justice, under curatorship or under guardianship;
2° In the event of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata pronounced by the judge at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor, when it appears that the conditions provided for in that article are no longer met or when the execution of the family authorization is likely to harm the interests of the protected person;
3° By operation of law in the absence of renewal upon expiration of the fixed period;
4° After the performance of the acts for which the authorization had been issued.

### Titre XIII

Management of the property of minors and adults under guardianship Chapter I: Procedures for management

###### Article 624

The guardian represents the protected person in the acts necessary for the management of their property.
They are required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in such management, solely in the interest of the protected person.

The list of acts that are regarded, for the application of this title, as acts of administration relating to the current management of property and as acts of disposition that commit it in a lasting and substantial manner is fixed by decree.

###### Article 625

Capital accruing to the protected person is paid directly into an account opened in their name alone and mentioning the guardianship measure, with a bank or any other organization legally authorized to receive funds from the public.

###### Article 626

Third parties may inform the judge of acts or omissions by the guardian that appear to them likely to harm the interests of the protected person. In this title, each time the judge is mentioned, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate they have designated.
These third parties are not guarantors of the use of capital. However, if in connection with such use they become aware of acts or omissions that manifestly compromise the interest of the protected person, they notify the judge.

Third-party opposition against authorizations of the family council or the judge may only be exercised by creditors of the protected person and in case of fraud against their rights.

##### Section unique: Decisions of the family council or the judge Article 627

The guardian establishes the guardianship budget by determining, according to the importance of the protected person's property and the operations involved in their management, the sums annually necessary for the maintenance of that person and the reimbursement of the costs of administering their property. The guardian informs the family council or, failing that, the judge. In case of difficulties, the budget is established by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to include in the management costs the remuneration of particular administrators whose assistance they request under their own responsibility.
The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to conclude a contract for the management of the securities and financial instruments of the protected person. They choose the contracting third party in consideration of their professional experience and solvency. The contract may, at any time and notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, be terminated on behalf of the protected person.

###### Article 628

The family council or, failing that, the judge determines the amount from which the obligation to invest liquid capital and surplus income begins for the guardian.  
The family council or, failing that, the judge prescribes all measures it deems useful regarding the investment or reinvestment of funds either in advance or on the occasion of each transaction. The investment or reinvestment is carried out by the guardian within the time limit set by the decision ordering it and in the manner it prescribes. After this time limit, the guardian may be declared debtor of the interest.  

The family council or, failing that, the judge may order that certain funds be deposited in an unavailable account.

###### Article 629

The family council or, failing that, the judge rules on the authorizations that the guardian requests for acts that he cannot perform alone.

###### § 1. Des actes que le tuteur accomplit sans autorisation Article 630

Within three months of the opening of the guardianship, the guardian has an inventory of the property of the protected person prepared and transmits it to the judge. He ensures its updating during the measure.  

He may obtain communication of all information and documents necessary for the establishment of the inventory from any public or private person, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being invoked against him.  
If the inventory has not been established or proves to be incomplete or inaccurate, the protected person and, after his death, his heirs may prove the value and initial composition of his property by any means.

###### Article 631

The guardian performs alone conservatory acts and, subject to the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 608, acts of administration necessary for the management of the protected person's patrimony.  

He acts alone in court to assert the patrimonial rights of the protected person.  
Leases granted by the guardian confer on the lessee, against the protected person who has become capable, no right of renewal and no right to remain in the premises at the expiration of the lease, even if there exist contrary legal provisions. These provisions are not, however, applicable to leases granted before the opening of the guardianship and renewed by the guardian.

###### § 2. Des actes que le tuteur accomplit avec une autorisation Article 632

The guardian may not, without being authorized by the family council or, failing that, the judge, make acts of disposition in the name of the protected person.  
The authorization that may be given to him by the family council or, failing that, the judge, determines the stipulations and, where applicable, the price or reserve price for which the act may be executed. Authorization is not required in case of forced sale by judicial decision or in case of amicable sale upon authorization of the judge.

###### Article 633

The guardian may not settle or compromise in the name of the protected person except after having had the clauses of the settlement or compromise and, where applicable, the arbitration clause approved by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

###### Article 634

Partition with respect to a protected person may be made amicably upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, of the judge, who designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it. It may be only partial.  
The liquidation statement is submitted for approval to the family council or, failing that, the judge.  

Partition may also be made in court in accordance with Articles 981 and 998. Any other partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 635

By way of derogation from Article 881, the guardian may accept a succession that has fallen to the protected person only subject to inventory. However, the family council or, failing that, the judge may, by a deliberation or a decision, authorize him to accept purely and simply if the assets manifestly exceed the liabilities.  
The guardian may not renounce a succession that has fallen to the protected person without authorization from the family council or, failing that, the judge.

###### Article 636

In the case where the succession that was renounced in the name of the protected person has not been accepted by another heir and as long as the State has not been sent into possession, the renunciation may be revoked, either by the guardian authorized for this purpose by a new deliberation of the family council or, failing that, a new decision of the judge, or by the protected person who has become capable.  
This revocation, like the renunciation, has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the succession, without however calling into question the rights that may be acquired by third parties over the property of the succession by prescription or by acts validly made with the curator of the vacant succession.

###### Article 637

On an exceptional basis and in the interest of the protected person, the guardian may, upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, the judge, purchase the property of the latter or take it on lease.  
For the conclusion of the act, the guardian is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person.

###### § 3. Des actes que le tuteur ne peut accomplir Article 638

The guardian may not, even with authorization:
1° Perform acts that entail a gratuitous alienation of the property or rights of the protected person except as stated regarding donations, such as the remission of debt, the gratuitous renunciation of an acquired right, the advance renunciation of the action for reduction referred to in Articles 1085 and 1086, the release of mortgage or security without payment or the gratuitous constitution of an easement or security to guarantee the debt of a third party;  
2° Acquire from a third party a right or claim that the latter holds against the protected person; 3° Carry on trade or a liberal profession in the name of the protected person;  
4° Purchase the property of the protected person as well as take it on lease, subject to the provisions of Article 637;  
5° Transfer into a fiduciary patrimony the property or rights of a protected adult.

#### Chapitre II

De l'établissement, de la vérification et de l'approbation des comptes Article 639
The guardian establishes each year an account of his management to which are annexed all useful supporting documents.  

For this purpose, he requests from the institutions with which one or more accounts are opened in the name of the protected person an annual statement thereof, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being invoked against him.  
The guardian is required to ensure the confidentiality of the management account. However, a copy of the account and supporting documents is given each year by the guardian to the protected person when he is at least sixteen years of age and, if the guardian deems it useful, to other persons responsible for the protection of the interested party.  

In addition, the judge may, after having heard the protected person and obtained his agreement, if he has reached the aforementioned age and if his condition permits, authorize the spouse, a relative, a relative by marriage of the latter or one of his close relations, if they justify a legitimate interest, to have the guardian communicate to them at their expense a copy of the account and supporting documents or a part of these documents.

###### Article 640

The guardian submits each year the management account, accompanied by supporting documents, for verification to the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance.  
For the verification of the account, the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance may make use of the right of communication provided for in the second paragraph of Article 639. He may be assisted in his mission of auditing the accounts under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.  

If he refuses to approve the account, the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance draws up a report of the difficulties encountered which he transmits to the judge. The latter rules on the conformity of the account.  

The judge may decide that the mission of verification and approval of accounts devolved to the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance shall be exercised by a certified public accountant registered on the list of judicial experts.  

When Article 594 is applied, the judge may decide that the family council shall verify and approve the accounts in place of the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 641

The judge may, by way of derogation from Articles 639 and 640 and in consideration of the modest nature of the income and assets of the protected person, exempt the guardian from preparing the management account and from submitting it for approval to the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance director of judicial registry services.

###### Article 642

If the resources of the protected person permit and if the importance and composition of his assets justify it, the judge may decide, in consideration of the patrimonial interest at stake, that the mission of verification and approval of the management account shall be exercised, at the expense of the person concerned and according to the procedures he sets, by a technician.

###### Article 643

When his mission ends for any reason whatsoever, the guardian prepares a management account of the operations that have taken place since the preparation of the last annual account and submits it for verification and approval as provided for in Articles 640 and 642.  
In addition, within three months following the end of his mission, the guardian or his heirs if he has died deliver a copy of the last five management accounts and of the account mentioned in the first paragraph of this article, as the case may be, to the person who has become capable if he has not already been a recipient thereof, to the person newly charged with the management measure or to the heirs of the protected person.  

The preceding paragraphs are not applicable in the case provided for in Article 641.  

In all cases, the guardian delivers to the persons mentioned in the second paragraph of this article the documents necessary to continue the management or ensure the liquidation of the estate, as well as the initial inventory and the updates to which it has given rise.

#### Chapter III: On Prescription Article 644

The action for rendering of accounts, for revendication or for payment brought by the protected person or person who has been protected or by his heirs relating to the facts of the guardianship is prescribed after five years from the end of the measure, even though the management may have continued beyond.

### Title XIV: On Measures for the Protection of Victims of Violence

###### Article 645

When violence exercised within the couple or by a former spouse, or a former cohabitant endangers the person who is the victim thereof, one or more children, the judge may issue urgently to the latter a protection order.  
In this title, each time mention is made of the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he has designated.

###### Article 646

The protection order is issued by the judge, seized by the person in danger, if necessary assisted, or, with the consent of the latter, by the public prosecutor.  
Upon receipt of the application for a protection order, the judge summons, by all appropriate means, for a hearing, the applicant party and the respondent party, assisted, where appropriate, by a lawyer, as well as the public prosecutor. These hearings may take place separately. They must be held in chambers.

###### Article 647

The protection order is issued, as soon as possible, by the judge, if he considers, in view of the elements produced before him and debated adversarially, that there are serious reasons to consider as plausible the commission of the alleged acts of violence and the danger to which the victim or one or more children are exposed. On the occasion of its issuance, the judge is competent to:
1° Prohibit the respondent party from receiving or meeting certain persons as well as from entering into contact with them, in any manner whatsoever;  
2° Prohibit the respondent party from holding or carrying a weapon and, where appropriate, order him to surrender to the police or gendarmerie service he designates the weapons of which he is the holder with a view to their deposit at the registry;  
3° Rule on the separate residence of the spouses by specifying which of the two will continue to reside in the matrimonial home and on the procedures for covering the costs relating to this home. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this home is attributed to the spouse who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if he has benefited from emergency accommodation;  
4° Specify which of the cohabitants will continue to reside in the common home and rule on the procedures for covering the costs relating to this home. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this home is attributed to the cohabitant who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if he has benefited from emergency accommodation;  
5° Rule on the procedures for exercising parental authority and, where appropriate, on the contribution to the charges of the marriage and on the contribution to the maintenance and education of the children;  
6° Authorize the applicant party to conceal his domicile or residence and to elect domicile with the lawyer who assists or represents him or with the public prosecutor for all civil proceedings in which he is also a party. If, for the purposes of executing a court decision, the bailiff charged with this execution must have knowledge of the address of this person, it is communicated to him, without his being able to reveal it to his principal;  

When the judge issues a protection order by reason of violence likely to endanger one or more children, he informs the public prosecutor without delay.

###### Article 648

The measures mentioned in Article 647 are ordered for a maximum duration of six months from the notification of the order. They may be extended beyond if, during this period, a petition for divorce or for legal separation has been filed or if the judge has been seized with a petition relating to the exercise of parental authority.  
The judge may, at any time, at the request of the public prosecutor or of either party, or after having caused any useful investigative measure to be carried out, and after having invited each of them to express themselves, remove or modify all or part of the measures set out in the protection order, decide on new ones, grant the respondent party a temporary dispensation from observing certain of the obligations that have been imposed on him or revoke the protection order.

###### Article 649

A protection order may also be issued urgently by the judge to the adult person threatened with forced marriage, under the conditions set in Article 646.  

The judge is competent to take the measures mentioned in 1°, 2° and 6° of Article 647.

## BOOK II. - ON PROPERTY, AND THE DIFFERENT MODIFICATIONS OF OWNERSHIP

###### Article 650

The property of public persons is governed by the codes and laws that concern them and, in the absence of specific provisions, by the common law of property as established by this Book.

### Title I: On patrimony and the property that composes it

Subtitle I: Patrimony Article 651
Patrimony is the legal universality comprising all the property of a person, both movable and immovable, present and future, the entirety of the assets answering for the entirety of the liabilities.  
Every natural or legal person holds a patrimony. Unless otherwise provided by law, a person may have only one patrimony.

###### Article 652

Property within the meaning of the preceding article means corporeal or incorporeal things that are the object of appropriation by the holder of the patrimony in question, as well as real and personal rights that are his.

###### Article 653

A real right is one that confers on its holder a direct power over property.  

The holder of a real right may exercise his power over the thing in whatever hands it may be found. When it is accessory to a claim whose payment it guarantees, it confers, in addition to the right of pursuit, a right of preference over the property.

###### Article 654

A personal right is one held by the creditor of an obligation against his debtor.  
Subtitle II. On the distinction of property Article 655
All property is either movable or immovable.

###### Article 656

Subject to the laws that protect them, animals are subject to the legal regime of corporeal things.

###### Article 657

Except where the law provides otherwise:
	a consumable thing is a thing that is consumed when used. It cannot be used without being destroyed at first use or without leaving the patrimony of its owner;  
	a non-fungible thing or specific thing consists of a determined and individualized thing; a fungible thing or generic thing is determined only by its species and quantity;  
	when a thing gives or produces fruits periodically, it is fruit-bearing. Fruits are what a property generates, periodically or not, spontaneously or through its development, without its substance being altered in any way. They may be natural, when they come spontaneously from the land or from animals; industrial, when they are obtained through cultivation or breeding; or civil, such as rents from leases, interest on sums due, and arrears of annuities. Civil fruits are also called income. Products affect the very matter of the property, which is diminished when it is exploited.  

Chapter I: On immovables Article 658
Corporeal property is immovable, either by its nature or by its destination. Incorporeal property is immovable by the object to which it applies.

###### Article 659

Immovable by nature are land, buildings and vegetation found thereon, as well as all other things incorporated therein, as long as the connection with the soil is thus maintained.  
Pipes used to conduct water in a house or any other immovable by nature to which they are attached are immovable and form part of the land to which they are joined.  

Condominium units are also immovable.  
Houses known as plank houses are movable property, except when the State sells to its owner the land on which it is built. In that case, a land title may be established and the whole consisting of the land and the house then becomes immovable property subject to registration.

###### Article 660

Immovables by destination are a legal fiction by which the law treats movable property as immovable. A movable is immovable by destination when two cumulative conditions are met: 1° Both properties must be owned by the same person;  
2° A relationship of destination must exist between the movable and the immovable to which it is attached. This relationship of destination results either from the assignment of the movable to the operation of an immovable by nature, or from the attachment of the movable property to the immovable property by nature in perpetuity.

###### Article 661

The assignment of the movable to the operation of an immovable by nature may result from the agricultural operation of land, such as animals attached to cultivation as long as they remain attached to the land by the effect of an agreement; from the industrial operation of land, such as equipment in an industrial building used for the activity; from the commercial operation of land, such as furniture used for the operation of an immovable for hotel purposes; or from the civil operation of an immovable, such as equipment elements that allow the use of an apartment rented by its owner.

###### Article 662

The attachment of a movable to an immovable by nature in perpetuity resides in the material attachment process implemented by the owner. This process externalizes the owner's intention to attach the movable to the immovable.  
Irrefutably presumed to be attached to the immovable are movables that have been fixed thereto by means of plaster, lime or cement, or any other mode of attachment that would prevent the movables from being

detached without being broken or damaged, or without breaking or damaging the part of the land to which they are attached.  

Presumed, unless proven otherwise, to be attached to the immovable are movables that have been specially designed or adapted to be integrated into the immovable by nature, or for which the owner has made a modification to the immovable in order to receive them, such as a niche made expressly to receive a statue, even if it can be removed without breakage or damage.  

In other cases, the owner must establish that he intended to attach the movable in perpetuity to the immovable by nature.

###### Article 663

The owner of an immovable by destination may always terminate the relationship of destination, by his sole will, subject to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 664

Immovable by the object to which they apply are:
1° Real immovable rights:
a)	ownership of immovable property;  
b)	usufruct of the same property;  
c)	rights of use and habitation;  
d)	emphyteusis;  
e)	right of superficies;  
f)	servitudes and land services;  
g)	antichresis;  
h)	privileges and mortgages.  
2° Actions that tend to claim an immovable.

###### Article 665

The real rights enumerated in the preceding article are preserved and produce effect with respect to third parties only insofar as they have been made public in the forms, conditions and limits regulated in this code, without prejudice to the rights of the parties for the performance of their agreements.  
By way of derogation from the rule of the preceding paragraph, creditors and legatees who request the separation of the patrimony of a deceased person retain, with respect to his heirs and representatives, for the exercise of their privilege over hereditary immovables, the benefit of the period of six months from the opening of the succession, notwithstanding any alienation by said heirs or representatives.

#### Chapter II: On movables Article 666

Property is movable by its nature or by determination of law.  
Movable by nature are all corporeal things other than those referred to in articles 659 and 660.  

Movable by determination of law are all rights other than those referred to in article 664.

###### Article 667

The word movable property, used alone in the provisions of the law or in a legal act, without any other addition or designation, does not include cash, precious stones, receivables, books, medals, instruments of the sciences, arts and crafts, body linen, weapons, grains, wines, hay and other commodities; it also does not include what is the object of a trade.

###### Article 668

The words movable furnishings include only movable property intended for the use and decoration of apartments, such as beds, seats, mirrors, clocks, tables, porcelain and other objects of this nature.  
The sale or gift of a furnished house includes only movable furnishings. Similarly, the sale or gift of a house, with everything found therein, does not include cash, nor receivables and other rights whose titles may be deposited in the house; all other movable effects are included therein.

###### Article 669

Subject to the rights of third parties, property that is currently immovable but which is intended, by the effect of the will of the contracting parties, to become movable property shortly and in the perspective of performance of the agreement, is considered as movable property. Thus: crops sold standing, products to be extracted from quarries or mines, materials to come from the demolition of a building.

### Titre II : De la propriété, de la possession et de la détention

###### Article 670

Real rights not subject to publicity, subject to the provisions relating to legal acts, are proved by all means.  
In case of conflict, when no sufficiently probative title is produced, it is for the judge of the revendication action to identify the best and most characteristic presumptions of ownership, and he retains the most likely right after having analyzed all the circumstances to decide between the litigants. If he does not succeed in doing so, the possessor in place is awarded ownership.  

For immovable property, the conflict between several persons invoking titles emanating from a common author is resolved according to the rules of land registration.  

Chapitre Ier: La propriété Article 671
Ownership is the exclusive right to enjoy and dispose of things and rights.  

It confers upon its holder an absolute power, subject to the laws and regulations that govern it. This power may not be used for the purpose of harming others, except to constitute an abuse of right.

###### Article 672

No one may be compelled to transfer his ownership, except for reasons of public utility, and in return for fair and prior compensation.

###### Article 673

Ownership of a thing, whether movable or immovable, extends to the fruits and products of the thing.  

The fruits produced by the thing, however, belong to the owner of the thing only subject to reimbursement of the costs of plowing, work and seeds done by third parties and whose value is estimated at the date of reimbursement.  

Ownership of the thing also extends to everything that is united to it accessorily either naturally or artificially. This right is called the right of accession.

###### Article 674

Ownership is not lost by non-use.  

The revendication action, subject to contrary provision of the law, is perpetual.

###### Article 675

By way of derogation from the preceding articles, when the owner victim of a minor encroachment on his land does not bring a revendication action within two years after having had knowledge of the encroachment, or within the limit of 10 years from the completion of the works, the author of the constructions and other works may request, if he is in good faith and if the circumstances permit, that the encroachment be attributed to him as a real right against payment of fair compensation.  
The owner victim of the encroachment may, within the time limits stated above, request at his choice, either the demolition of what has been done in violation of his right, or the payment of fair compensation.  

The encroachment is minor when it is less than 0.20 meters.  
The compensation is fixed amicably by the owners concerned who establish an authentic act of their agreement and, failing that, determined by the judge who takes into account the value of the land occupied, the added value brought to the land of the author of the encroachment, and the damage he has caused to the owner of the land victim of the encroachment.

###### Article 676

Ownership of a treasure belongs to the person who finds it in his own land, by virtue of the right of accession; if the treasure is found in the land of another, it belongs for half to the person who discovered it, by occupation, and for the other half to the owner of the land, by accession.  
A treasure is any hidden or buried thing over which no one can justify his ownership, and which is discovered by pure chance.

###### Article 677

The rights over effects thrown into the sea, over objects that the sea casts up, of whatever nature they may be, over plants and herbage that grow on the shores of the sea, are regulated by special laws.  
The same applies to lost things whose owner does not come forward.

###### Article 678

The public domain includes all property of all kinds, immovable or movable, classified or delimited in the public domain, whether or not allocated to public use. The public domain of the State is determined by a special law.  
The public domain of the State comprises, on the one hand, natural sites determined by law, such as: the seashore, up to the limit of the highest tides, as well as a zone of 50 meters from this limit; islands and islets; springs as well as non-navigable and non-floatable watercourses within the limits determined by the height of the highest waters flowing at full bank before overflowing, as well as a passage zone of 25 meters wide from these limits on each bank; lakes, ponds and lagoons within the limits determined by the level of the highest waters before overflow, with a passage zone of 25 meters wide from these limits on each outer bank; underground water tables, whatever their origin, nature and depth and, on the other hand, developments and works carried out for reasons of general interest or public utility, as well as the land that supports them, determined by law or having been the subject of a classification procedure, such as: irrigation or drainage canals, aqueducts, boreholes, dams and hillside reservoirs, cemented wells, as well as the appurtenances of these works, when they are executed for a purpose of public utility; railways, roads and communication routes of all kinds, ports and roadsteads, maritime dikes, semaphores, lighting or beaconing works, as well as their appurtenances; telegraph and telephone lines, radio stations and other telecommunications installations, as well as their appurtenances; works declared of public utility for the use of hydraulic forces and the transport of electrical energy.  
More generally, the public domain of the State comprises property of all kinds that Djiboutian laws declare not susceptible to private ownership.  

Property that does not belong to private individuals is administered and may only be alienated in the forms and according to the rules that are particular to them.

###### Article 679

All immovable property that has no owner, and that of persons who die without heirs or whose estates are abandoned, belongs to the State.  
Movable property without an owner belongs to the first person who appropriates it, subject to special provisions.

###### Article 680

There are things that belong to no one and whose use is common to all. Police laws regulate the manner of enjoying them.  
The right to hunt or fish is also regulated by special laws.

#### Chapitre II

Of possession and detention Section I: Possession

###### Article 681

Possession is the fact of exercising, with the intention of being the holder thereof, a right over a thing. It is immaterial whether the possessor is or is not the true holder of the right exercised. Possession exists only if it is public, unequivocal and peaceful. In case of violence, useful possession begins only from the day the violence ceased. It is protected, without regard to the merits of the right, against disturbance that affects or threatens it.  
However, there is no immovable possession except in the presence of a title duly published according to the laws governing immovable property.  

Possession of incorporeal movables is governed by the special laws that govern them.  

Payment made in good faith to the person who is in possession of the claim is valid, even if the possessor is subsequently evicted.

###### Article 682

Acts of mere faculty and those of mere tolerance cannot establish either possession or prescription.

###### Article 683

The possessor is in good faith when he possesses as would the holder of the right he exercises, by virtue of a title transferring ownership whose defects he is unaware of.  
Good faith is always presumed, and it is for the person alleging bad faith to prove it. It is assessed on the day of entry into possession, unless otherwise provided.  

He ceases to be in good faith from the moment these defects become known to him.

###### Article 684

One may possess by oneself or through another.

###### Article 685

Possession is proved by all means.  

One is always presumed to possess for oneself, and as owner, unless it is proved that one began to possess for another.  
When one has begun to possess for another, one is always presumed to possess under the same title, unless there is proof to the contrary.

###### Article 686

With respect to movables, possession in good faith instantly confers title.  

It is otherwise when the person who lost or from whom the thing was stolen intends to claim it: that person has three years, from the day of the loss or theft, to take action against the possessor. If the possessor purchased the claimed thing in a normal circuit of commercialization of goods and services, the claimant must pay the possessor the price the thing cost him; otherwise, he shall obtain the property without having to reimburse the price to the possessor. The claimant who had to pay a price to the possessor, or the possessor who had to return the thing without obtaining reimbursement of its price, may take action for that amount against the person from whom the possessor obtained the thing, up to the finder or thief thereof.  
When the possessor is in bad faith, the claimed right is acquired only after thirty years. When the period is reached, the right arises from the day possession began.  

In case of an action for recovery concerning the property he possesses, the possessor shall be defendant in the action brought. The plaintiff may rebut the presumptions favorable to the possessor, by all means.

###### Article 687

The current possessor of a movable who proves having possessed it formerly is presumed to have possessed it in the intervening time, unless proof to the contrary.

###### Article 688

One may always join to one's possession that of one's predecessor.

###### Article 689

The possessor in bad faith, in addition to the obligation to return the thing, owes to the owner who claims it, the interest, the fruits he has received in kind or their value estimated at the date of payment. The possessor in good faith owes them only from the day of the demand.  
Every possessor is however entitled to reimbursement of necessary and useful expenses for the preservation of the property within the limit of the added value provided.

###### Article 690

Articles 2401 and following are applicable during possession.

##### Section II : Detention

###### Article 691

When the person who holds a property knows that this property is subject to a real right of which he is not the holder, he is a mere detainer. Such is the case of the contractor to whom an object has been entrusted for repair, or of the usufructuary who holds the thing of the bare owner.  
Detention is precarious and entails the obligation to return the thing to the holder of the real right that relates to it under the conditions of the juridical act that gave rise to it.

###### Article 692

Article 685 paragraph three is applicable to the detainer.  

Possessory protection is granted to the detainer against anyone other than the person from whom he holds his rights.

##### Section III : The protection of possession and detention Article 693

Possession is protected against disturbance that affects or threatens it.  

Likewise, the detainer is protected from disturbance he suffers in the exercise of his right, by any person other than the one from whom he holds his rights.

#### Chapitre III : Of the right of accession

##### Section I : Of the right of accession in relation to immovable things Article 694

Ownership of the soil carries with it ownership of what is above and below.  
Everything that is united and incorporated into the thing belongs to the owner thereof.

###### Article 695

The owner may make above all plantations and constructions, within the limits imposed by laws, regulations and juridical acts, and below, all constructions and excavations he deems appropriate, and draw from these excavations all the products they can provide, subject to modifications resulting from laws and regulations relating to mines, and police laws and regulations.

###### Article 696

All constructions, plantations and works on land or in the interior are presumed made by the owner at his expense and to belong to him, unless the contrary is proved.  
The owner of the soil who has made constructions, plantations and works with materials that did not belong to him must pay their value estimated at the date of payment; he may also be ordered to pay damages, if appropriate. But the owner of the materials does not have the right to remove them.

###### Article 697

Where plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in good faith and with materials belonging to him, the owner of the land must compensate the latter for the lower value of the two sums represented, at the date of payment, by the increase in value provided to the land or the cost of materials and labour, taking into account the state in which the said constructions,

plantations and works are found. The possessor then benefits from a right of retention until complete payment of the sum due.

Where plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in bad faith and with materials belonging to the latter, the owner of the land has the right either to retain ownership thereof under the conditions of the preceding paragraph, or to oblige the third party to remove them.  
If the owner of the land requires the removal of the constructions, plantations and works, it shall be carried out at the expense of the third party, without any compensation for him; the third party may, in addition, be ordered to pay damages for any loss suffered by the owner of the land.

Where plantations, constructions and works have been made by a holder, their fate is governed by the title which is at the origin of the possession. In the absence thereof, only plantations, constructions and works made in the sight and knowledge of the owner fall within the application of the first paragraph above.

###### Article 698

The movement of rivers or wadis which modifies riparian land benefits riparian lands. The riparian owner on the opposite side cannot complain where he has, on his side, lost land as a result, except where a sudden force has carried away a considerable and recognisable part of riparian land, and it remains identified at the place where it has been carried; in that case, the owner of the removed part may claim his property, provided he acts within one year of the event.

##### Section II: Of the right of accession in relation to movable property Article 699

The right of accession, when it relates to two movable things belonging to two different owners, is entirely subject to the principles of natural equity.

The following rules shall serve as an example to the judge in determining, according to the particular circumstances.

###### Article 700

There are three kinds of movable incorporation.

Adjunction, which is the act of uniting one movable object to another movable object for a purpose of use, ornament or completion of the first. Such is the case of property used to personalise cars or motorcycles.  
Specification, which is the act of a person using material which does not belong to him and creating a new object from it. Such is the case of a person who takes pieces of wood and makes a table from them.

Mixture, which is the act of forming a thing by the union of several materials such that the resulting material can no longer be separated. Such is the case where two metals are mixed.

###### Article 701

In the case of adjunction, the newly created property reverts in its entirety to the person whose thing was the most important in value and, failing that, in volume, regardless of whether the two things would be separable from each other. In return, the other person shall receive compensation.  
It is otherwise if the thing united to the other is much more valuable than the principal thing and the operation was carried out without the knowledge of its owner, the latter may request that the united thing be separated to be returned to him, even where some deterioration of the thing to which it has been joined might result.

###### Article 702

In the case of specification, ownership of the new property reverts to the owner of the materials against remuneration for the work accomplished, except where the work clearly exceeds the value of the material used.

###### Article 703

In the case of mixture, division of separable materials may be requested by the owner without whose knowledge the mixture was made. Failing that, ownership shall be common to the persons concerned, in proportion to the quantities. But where there is a manifest disproportion in the quantities mixed, the accessory shall again follow the principal.

###### Article 704

In all cases where property has been used without the knowledge of its owner, the latter has the choice of requesting the restitution of his material in the same nature, quantity, weight, measure and quality, or its value estimated at the date of restitution.

#### Chapter IV: Of collective ownership

##### Section I: Ordinary co-ownership Article 705

Co-ownership is the situation in which several persons hold a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of property. None of these persons may then claim an exclusive right over the property.

This right may be one of ownership or another real right.

###### Article 706

Co-ownership is governed by articles 933 and following (legal co-ownership) and 2071 and following (conventional co-ownership).

##### Section II: Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots Article 707

Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots is a combination of private ownership, on the one hand, and co-ownership, on the other hand. Ownership of the immovable property is divided into lots each comprising a private part, such as an apartment, and a share of the common parts of the immovable property.

Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots is governed by the texts which govern it.

### Title III

Of usufruct, use and habitation, special real rights, emphyteusis and the right of superficies

Chapter I: Of usufruct

##### Section I: General provisions Article 708

Usufruct is the real right to use and enjoy things of which another has ownership, as the owner himself, but subject to preserving their substance.

###### Article 709

Usufruct is established by law, or by the will of man.

###### Article 710

The will of the parties expressed in the constitutive act determines the starting point of the right of usufruct.

Usufruct is temporary and is extinguished in accordance with the provisions of Section IV below, which govern its duration.

###### Article 711

Usufruct may be established over any kind of property or set of properties, movable or immovable, corporeal or incorporeal.

##### Section II

Of the mutual obligations of the bare owner and the usufructuary Article 712
An inventory of the property subject to usufruct and of its condition is drawn up at the latest at the time the usufructuary enters into enjoyment. The latter may not enter into enjoyment until after having had the inventory drawn up, in the presence of the owner, or the owner having been duly summoned.  
In the event of disagreement between them, the inventory is carried out by an independent professional chosen by mutual agreement and, failing that, designated by the president of the civil chamber of the court of first instance, ruling by order on the merits.  
The usufructuary takes the things in the state in which they are.

###### Article 713

The owner may not, by his act, nor in any manner whatsoever, harm the rights of the usufructuary.

###### Article 714

Unless otherwise agreed, the owner is liable for all major works and repairs, namely works relating to the structure and general solidity of the immovable property such as the repair of load-bearing walls, dikes, retaining walls and enclosures in their entirety, or again, the restoration of beams or roofs, also in their entirety.  
All other repairs are maintenance repairs.

###### Article 715

Maintenance and conservation works, like other periodic expenses, are the responsibility of the usufructuary.  
If major repairs are the responsibility of the owner, it is otherwise when they have been caused by the lack of maintenance repairs since the opening of the usufruct. In this case, the usufructuary is liable for them. He is also liable for expenses made necessary by his abuse of enjoyment.  
In case of judicial proceedings, the usufructuary is only liable for the costs of proceedings concerning the enjoyment, and other condemnations to which these proceedings might give rise.

###### Article 716

The usufructuary cannot, upon cessation of the usufruct, claim any compensation for improvements that he may have made, even though the value of the thing was increased thereby. In this case, he may however, or

his heirs, remove the improvements that he has made to the property, but subject to restoring the premises to their original state.

###### Article 717

When the obligations provided for by the preceding articles are not respected, the other party may seize the judge so that he may enjoin the person who is bound to carry out the necessary works and, failing that, authorize him to have them carried out, at the expense of the person who has responsibility for them.  
He may also request from the judge authorization to create a security interest over the property, in order to guarantee, as the case may be, the financing of the works by the other, or the reimbursement of the sums expended.

###### Article 718

In case of usufruct of simply determinable duration, the contract may provide that upon its extinction, the owner may request from the usufructuary a contribution to the expenses that he has covered for major works. This contribution is calculated according to the value of the usufruct in relation to what its actual duration has been.

###### Article 719

Neither the owner nor the usufructuary is required to rebuild what has fallen from age, or what has been destroyed by fortuitous event.

###### Article 720

With regard to charges that may be imposed on the property during the duration of the usufruct, the usufructuary and the owner contribute to them as follows:
The owner is obliged to pay them, and the usufructuary must account to him for the interest; If they are advanced by the usufructuary, he has recovery of the capital at the end of the usufruct.

##### Section III: Rights and obligations of the usufructuary

###### § 1. Rights of the usufructuary Article 721

The usufructuary has the right to use and enjoy the property of which he has the usufruct.  

The right of enjoyment covers every kind of fruits that the property concerned may produce.

###### Article 722

The usufructuary exercises his right, either by himself or by granting the use and enjoyment to another.  

He may transfer his right, for consideration as well as gratuitously, or encumber it with real securities. In this case, the right thus created is extinguished, at the latest, on the date provided for the transferred usufruct.  

The usufructuary may not create any real right over the property other than use and habitation.  

The creation or renewal of leases subject to the statutes of commercial or rural leases, as well as those constituting a real right, may only be carried out with the agreement of the owner. Other leases may be concluded by the usufructuary alone, but if they subsist upon the extinction of the usufruct, the owner is only bound for the current period and, except for his written agreement, for a maximum duration of six years for immovable leases and three years for movable leases.

###### Article 723

The usufructuary uses and enjoys all the rights that the owner may use and enjoy, and he uses and enjoys them as the owner himself.

###### Article 724

He also uses and enjoys, in the same manner as the owner, the products of the exploitation of the property subject to the usufruct; such is the case with mines and quarries that are in operation at the opening of the usufruct. Nevertheless, if it is an operation that cannot be carried out without a concession, the usufructuary may only use and enjoy it after having obtained permission from the President of the Republic.  
He has no right to mines and quarries not yet opened, nor to treasure that might be discovered during the duration of the usufruct.

###### Article 725

Unless otherwise agreed, natural and industrial fruits, hanging by branches or by roots at the time when the usufruct is opened, belong to the usufructuary.  
Those that are ripe at the time when the usufruct ends belong to the owner, without compensation on either side for plowing and seeds.

###### Article 726

Unless otherwise agreed, income provided by the property, such as rents, interest and dividends whose distribution has been voted, is acquired day by day.

###### § 2. Obligations of the usufructuary Article 727

The usufructuary uses and enjoys the property subject to the usufruct in a manner consistent with the destination of the property.  

If, during the duration of the usufruct, a third party commits some usurpation on the land, or otherwise infringes the rights of the owner, the usufructuary is required to report it to him; failing which, he is liable for all damage that may result therefrom for the owner, as he would be for damage committed by himself.  
Upon extinction of the usufruct, he returns the property to its owner, subject to the provisions specific to special usufructs.

###### Article 728

If the usufruct is established only over an animal that perishes without the fault of the usufructuary, the latter is not required to return another, nor to pay its valuation.  
If the herd over which a usufruct has been established perishes entirely by accident or by disease and without the fault of the usufructuary, the latter is only required towards the owner to account to him for the hides, or their value estimated at the date of restitution. On the other hand, if the herd does not perish entirely, the usufructuary is required to replace, up to the amount of the increase, the heads of animals that have perished.

###### Article 729

The usufructuary must provide sufficient security for compliance with the obligations mentioned in the preceding article, unless he is exempted therefrom by law, the instrument creating the usufruct, or by the owner.  
However, the following are exempted: the father and mother having the legal usufruct of the property of their children, as well as the seller or donor with reservation of usufruct.

###### Article 730

If the usufructuary does not find security, the immovables are leased or placed under sequestration;  

The sums included in the usufruct are invested;  

The commodities are sold and the price resulting therefrom is similarly invested;  
The interest on these sums and prices belongs, in this case, to the usufructuary.

###### Article 731

In the absence of security on the part of the usufructuary, the owner may require that movables that deteriorate through use be sold, so that the price thereof be invested like that of commodities.

###### Article 732

Delay in the provision of security does not deprive the usufructuary of the fruits to which he may be entitled; they are due to him from the moment when the usufruct was opened.

###### Article 733

The universal or general title usufructuary and the owner are obliged to the estate liabilities in proportion to their respective value of the usufruct and the bare ownership. They contribute to them in the same proportions, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 734

The usufructuary by particular title is not liable for debts that burden the land.

###### Article 735

If the usufructuary fails to comply with his obligations, either by committing waste on the property or by allowing it to deteriorate for lack of maintenance, the owner may apply to the court to have the right of usufruct forfeited.  
The creditors of the usufructuary may intervene in the proceedings for the preservation of their rights; they may offer to substitute themselves for him in the performance of his obligations and by providing all guarantees.  
The judges may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, either pronounce the absolute extinction of the usufruct, or order the return of the owner into the enjoyment of the object subject to it, only subject to the obligation to pay annually to the usufructuary, or to his successors in title, a specified sum, until the time when the usufruct should have ceased.

##### Section IV: The duration of usufruct Article 736

Usufruct is constituted for the life of its holder.  

It may also be constituted for a fixed or determinable period. In that case, whether the duration of the usufruct is fixed or determinable, it may not exceed thirty years.

###### Article 737

Life usufruct is extinguished by the death of the usufructuary, a natural person, or the dissolution of the legal person when such a person holds the right. When the usufruct is constituted for the benefit of a legal person, it may never exceed thirty years.  
Usufruct constituted for a fixed period or for a determinable period is extinguished by the expiration of the time for which it was granted. When the usufruct has been granted until a third party has reached a fixed age, it lasts until that time, even if the third party dies before the fixed age.  

All usufruct is extinguished by the union in the same person of the two capacities of usufructuary and owner.

###### Article 738

In case of transfer of the right of usufruct, the right is extinguished: by the death or dissolution of the first holder and not by that of the transferee; by non-use of the right for thirty years; by the total loss of the thing on which the usufruct is established, subject to the agreement of the usufructuary and the owner to transfer it to the thing representing that which has perished.

##### Section V: Special usufructs

###### § 1. Quasi-usufruct Article 739

If the usufruct includes consumable things, such as money, grain, the usufructuary has the right to
use them, but subject to the obligation to return to the owner, at the end of the usufruct, either things of the same quantity and quality, or their value estimated at the date of restitution.

###### Article 740

If the usufruct includes things which, without being consumed immediately, deteriorate gradually through use, such as linen, household furniture, the usufructuary has the right to use them for the purpose for which they are intended, and is only obliged to return them at the end of the usufruct in the state in which they are found, not deteriorated by his fault.

###### Article 741

If the instrument creating the usufruct so provides, the usufructuary may dispose of any non-consumable movable property. The instrument creating it then specifies the conditions under which restitution will take place.  
The usufructuary may reinvest the funds arising from the alienation. The instrument creating it may even make this an obligation on the usufructuary. The judge may also, at the request of the owner, be seized for this purpose for the preservation of his rights. The reinvestment made may be proved by any means.  

At the end of the usufruct, in the absence of contractual provision, the usufructuary returns to the owner either things of the same quantity and quality, or their value estimated at the date of restitution. If there has been reinvestment, he returns the property resulting from it or their value estimated at the same date. When the reinvestment has been carried out freely and spontaneously by the usufructuary, the latter returns the greater of the sums represented by the current value of the property acquired in reinvestment or that of the property on which the quasi-usufruct was initially constituted.

###### § 2. Usufruct of claims Article 742

Usufruct of a claim for a sum of money gives the usufructuary the right to interest, as fruits. In case of repayment of the capital during his usufruct, the usufructuary exercises, unless otherwise agreed, his right over this capital in accordance with Article 739.  

Usufruct of a life annuity gives the usufructuary, during the duration of his usufruct, the right to receive the arrears, without being required to make any restitution.

###### § 3. Usufruct of corporate rights Article 743

Dividends distributed as income belong to the usufructuary.  

Unless otherwise agreed, the usufructuary exercises his right over other sums in accordance with Article 744, during the duration of his usufruct.

###### § 4. Usufruct of property forming a whole Article 744

Unless otherwise agreed, when the usufruct relates to property forming a whole, the usufructuary may dispose of each of its elements, but he shall do so by replacing them and in accordance with the purpose of that whole.  

If compliance with the purpose of the whole puts his right in jeopardy, the usufructuary may ask the judge to adapt and modify that purpose.

#### Chapter II: Of use and habitation Article 745

The right of use, like the right of use and habitation, is that which confers on its beneficiary, within the limits of his needs and those of his family, present and future, the personal use of a property and the collection of fruits.  
These rights are established and lost in the same manner as usufruct. They may be neither transferred nor leased.

###### Article 746

One may not enjoy them, as in the case of usufruct, without first giving security and without making statements and inventories.

###### Article 747

The user, and the person who has a right of habitation, must exercise their right reasonably and in compliance with the normal purpose of the property.

###### Article 748

When the user uses the whole of the property or receives all the fruits thereof, he is liable for maintenance expenses and, more generally, for periodic expenses which Article 715 places on the usufructuary.  
If he takes only part of the fruits or if he occupies only part of the property, he contributes in proportion to what he enjoys.

#### Chapter III: Special real rights

##### Section I: Real rights conferred by leases Article 749

Certain contracts, such as emphyteutic leases or building leases, confer on the lessee a real property right.  

Such rights are transferable and susceptible to real property securities. They confer on their holder, during the duration of the contract, ownership of the constructions, plantations, or installations, the realization of which they authorize.  

These contracts are governed by the laws that establish them.

##### Section II: The special real right of enjoyment Article 750

The owner may grant, subject to rules of public policy, one or more real rights conferring the benefit of special enjoyment of one or more of his properties.

###### Article 751

The special real right of enjoyment is established and lost in the same manner as usufruct.  

It may not be established in perpetuity, but may be granted for the duration of existence of the person who benefits from it.

###### Article 752

The special real right of enjoyment, subject to the instrument creating it, gives its holder the right to all the rights that benefit the usufructuary and imposes, likewise, all the obligations.  
It is always exercised in compliance with the normal purpose of the property concerned.

###### Article 753

Subject to contractual provisions, the real right of special enjoyment is extinguished: by the expiration of the time for which it was granted; by non-use of the right for a period established by the constitutive act and, failing that, for a reasonable period fixed by the judge; by the merger in the same person of the two capacities of holder of the real right of special enjoyment and owner; by the total loss of the thing on which the real right of special enjoyment relates.

#### Chapter IV: On Emphyteusis Article 754

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property confers on the lessee a real right susceptible to mortgage; this right may be assigned and seized in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

This lease must be granted for more than eighteen years and cannot exceed ninety-nine years; it cannot be extended by tacit renewal.

###### Article 755

The emphyteutic lease can only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as in the same forms.
Immovable property belonging to minors or to adults under guardianship may be given on emphyteutic lease by virtue of a resolution of the family council.
When spouses are subject to the dotal regime, the husband may give dotal immovable property on emphyteutic lease with the consent of the wife and judicial authorization.

Concerning premises for residential use, lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with tenants continue automatically with the owner of the immovable property until the end of each of the lease contracts as signed with the tenants.

###### Article 756

Proof of the emphyteusis contract is established in accordance with the rules of this code regarding leases.

###### Article 757

In the absence of contrary agreements, it is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 758

The lessee cannot request a reduction of the rent on grounds of partial loss of the land, nor on grounds of sterility or deprivation of any harvest following fortuitous events.

###### Article 759

In the absence of payment for two consecutive years, the lessor is authorized, after a summons that has remained without effect, to have the resolution of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.
Resolution may also be requested by the lessor in case of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deteriorations on the land.
Nevertheless, the courts may grant a period of time according to the circumstances.

###### Article 760

The lessee cannot free himself from the rent, nor evade the performance of the conditions of the emphyteutic lease by abandoning the land.

###### Article 761

The lessee cannot make any change in the land that diminishes its value.

If the lessee has made improvements or constructions that increase the value of the land, he cannot destroy them, nor claim any compensation in this regard.

###### Article 762

The lessee is liable for all contributions and charges on the property.

With regard to constructions existing at the time of the lease and those that will have been erected in performance of the agreement, he is liable for repairs of all kinds; but he is not obliged to rebuild the buildings, if he proves that they were destroyed by fortuitous event, by force majeure, or that they perished by defect of construction prior to the lease.

He is liable for fire, in accordance with Article 1394, paragraphs 2 and 3, of this code.

###### Article 763

The emphyteuta may acquire active easements for the benefit of the land, and burden it, by title, with passive easements for a time that will not exceed the duration of the lease and subject to notifying the owner.

###### Article 764

The emphyteuta benefits from the right of accession during the duration of the emphyteusis.

###### Article 765

In case of expropriation for reasons of public utility, the lessor must make known the right of the emphyteuta, in accordance with the legal provisions in force. Separate compensation is granted to the lessor and to the lessee.

###### Article 766

The lessee alone has the rights of hunting and fishing and exercises with regard to mines, mineral deposits, quarries and peat bogs all the rights of the usufructuary.

###### Article 767

The constitutive act of emphyteusis is subject only to the registration and transcription fees established for leases for a limited duration.
Transfers of any kind having as their object either the right of the lessor or the right of the lessee are subject to the legal provisions concerning transfers of ownership of immovable property. The fee is assessed on the market value determined by an estimated declaration of the parties.

#### Chapter V: On the Right of Superficies Article 768

A land may be the subject of a division aimed at conferring on a third party the ownership of a part of this land situated above or below a conventionally fixed limit. The ownership of the upper part is called superficiary ownership or right of superficies, that of the lower part subsoil ownership.

Thus, the right of superficies consists, for the holder of this right, in the fact of possessing constructions, works or plantations on land belonging to another. For the holder of the right of ownership on the soil, the right of superficies is a renunciation of accession.

The holder of the right of superficies may burden with easements the property that is the subject of his right, but only within the limit imposed for the exercise of this right.

###### Article 769

A land may also be the subject of a spatial division creating volumes. To each volume corresponds a full right of ownership.
A descriptive statement of division must obligatorily be executed by notarial act.

### Title IV: On Easements or Land Services

###### Article 770

An easement is a charge that burdens a land for the use and utility of a land belonging to another owner.
It establishes neither preeminence of one land over the other nor personal obligations for the benefit or at the charge of the owners, but only relations between servient land and dominant land and services attached to them.

It derives either from the natural situation of the places, or from obligations imposed by law, or from agreements between the owners.
Chapter I: On Easements that Derive from the Situation of the Places Article 771
Lower lands are subject towards those that are more elevated to receive the waters that flow from them naturally without the hand of man having contributed thereto.

The lower owner cannot raise a dike that prevents this flow.

The upper owner cannot do anything that aggravates the easement of the lower land.

###### Article 772

Every owner has the right to use and dispose of rainwater that falls on his land.

If the use of this water or the direction given to it aggravates the natural servitude of drainage established by Article 771, compensation is owed to the owner of the lower land.
The same provision applies to spring water arising on a land.

When, through drilling or underground works, an owner causes water to emerge on his land, the owners of lower lands must receive it; but they are entitled to compensation in case of damage resulting from its flow.

Houses, courtyards, gardens, parks and enclosures adjoining dwellings cannot be subjected to any aggravation of the servitude of drainage in the cases provided for by the preceding paragraphs.
Disputes to which the establishment and exercise of the servitudes provided for by these paragraphs may give rise and the settlement, if applicable, of compensation owed to the owners of lower lands are brought, in first instance, before the judge of the district court of the canton who, in ruling, must reconcile the interests of agriculture and industry with the respect due to property.

If an expert assessment is required, only one expert may be appointed.

###### Article 773

He who has a spring on his land may always use the water at his will within the limits and for the needs of his land.
The owner of a spring may no longer use it to the detriment of the owners of lower lands who, for more than thirty years, have made and completed, on the land where the spring arises, apparent and permanent works intended to use the water or to facilitate its passage into their property.
Nor may he use it in such a way as to deprive the inhabitants of a commune, village or hamlet of the water necessary to them; but if the inhabitants have not acquired or prescribed the use thereof, the owner may claim compensation, which is determined by experts.

If, from the point where they emerge from the land where they arise, the spring waters form a watercourse having the character of public and running waters, the owner cannot divert them from their natural course to the detriment of downstream users.

###### Article 774

Every owner may compel his neighbour to mark the boundaries of their contiguous properties.

Boundary marking is the operation that makes it possible to recognize and fix, in an adversarial and definitive manner, the dividing lines of private properties belonging or intended to belong to different owners.
Boundary marking is carried out by mutual agreement of the parties and, failing that, by a decision of the judge seized by one of them or, within the framework of the registration procedure for the immovable property, by the sworn surveyor of the Cadastre section who has been designated by the Registrar to proceed with the boundary marking of the immovable property to be registered.

Boundary marking is done at common expense.

###### Article 775

The action for boundary marking is perpetual

###### Article 776

Every owner may enclose his land, subject to the exception relating to the right of passage set forth in Articles 794 and following.

#### Chapitre II : Des servitudes établies par la loi Article 777

Servitudes established by law are governed by the rules that institute them.

##### Section I : De la mitoyenneté Article 778

Party wall ownership is a right of undivided ownership over a wall, fence or ditch.

###### Article 779

A wall, fence or ditch may only be constructed straddling the dividing line of two contiguous lands by mutual agreement of the owners of said lands.
The one of the two who has not consented to this construction cannot, in urbanized areas of the country, require the demolition of the wall. He acquires by operation of law and free of charge the party wall ownership thereof.

###### Article 780

Existing walls, fences or ditches, constructed at the dividing boundary or on the line separating two lands, are presumed to be party walls, unless there is title or factual element to the contrary.

###### Article 781

Unless there is title to the contrary: a wall is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the land towards which its top is inclined in whole or on the side of which there are architectural elements attesting to the initial intention of the builders of the wall; a ditch is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the land on the side of which the earth spoil is located; a fence is deemed to belong solely to the owner of the enclosed land if only one of the lands is enclosed.

###### Article 782

The costs of repair and reconstruction of a party wall, fence or ditch are divided between the owners in proportion to the rights of each, unless the costs were made necessary by the act of one of them. The latter must then bear the entire cost.
However, any owner of a party wall, fence or ditch may avoid these costs by abandoning his right of party wall ownership, unless the wall supports a building belonging to him or the ditch serves for the drainage of water from his land.

###### Article 783

Each of the owners may support his construction on the party wall.

###### Article 784

Any co-owner may raise the party wall; but he must pay alone the expense related both to the raising and to future maintenance repairs above the current height of the common enclosure.

If the party wall is not in a condition to support the raising, the one who nevertheless intends to raise it must have the wall entirely rebuilt at his expense, and any excess thickness that may be necessary must be taken from his side.
The neighbour who has not contributed to the raising may acquire party wall ownership thereof by paying half of the expense it cost and the value of half of the land provided for the excess thickness, if there is
any. The expense that the raising cost is estimated at the date of acquisition, taking into account the condition in which the raised part of the wall is found.

###### Article 785

Any owner adjoining a wall has the option of making it a party wall in whole or in part, by reimbursing to the owner of the wall half of the current value of the wall and half of the value of the land supporting the wall or the part of the wall.

This option does not apply to other modes of enclosure nor to ditches.

###### Article 786

No owner may carry out works affecting or potentially affecting the structure of the party wall, fence or ditch without the consent of the other or, failing that, the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 787

The fruits and products of a party hedge belong to the owners by half.

The co-owner of a party hedge may destroy it up to the limit of his property, provided he constructs a wall on that limit. The same rule applies to the co-owner of a party ditch that serves only as an enclosure.

Trees that are found in the party hedge are party trees like the hedge. Each owner may require the uprooting or pruning of a party tree as soon as it is isolated and does not participate in the enclosure.

##### Section II : Des distances à respecter entre fonds voisins Article 788

He who builds on his land is obliged to respect the distance prescribed by particular regulations and usages according to the works in question.

###### Article 789

Likewise, the planting of vegetation is governed by administrative regulations or by constant and recognized usages. In the absence thereof and subject to special provisions on urban planning, it is only permitted to have trees, shrubs and bushes near the boundary of the neighbouring property at a distance of two metres from the dividing line of the two lands for plantings whose height exceeds two metres, and at a distance of half a metre for other plantings.

###### Article 790

The neighbor may require that trees, shrubs and bushes planted at a lesser distance or whose branches extend over his land be uprooted or reduced to the legal height or distance.
