He may also cut himself what overhangs his land, provided that this does not result in the death of the plant in question, failing which he shall be liable.  
If it is the roots, brambles or twigs that extend over his land, he has the right to cut them himself at the boundary line. This right is imprescriptible.  

The fruits that fall naturally from these branches belong to him.

###### Article 791

Openings are apertures or arrangements that allow a view towards the neighbor's land, such as a window, a balcony or a platform.  
Lights are apertures or arrangements that allow air or light to pass through, but do not allow a view towards the neighbor's land, such as a translucent brick.  
Openings and lights constitute external arrangements within the meaning of the provisions relating to easements. Consequently:	no opening, neither opening nor light, is authorized when the wall is party, unless all the owners agree;	only openings are authorized when the wall is private and it is established at the boundary line of the neighboring land;	when the wall built by the owner of a land at a distance from the boundary between the lands, any direct view must be 1.90 meters from this boundary; and any oblique view must be 0.60 meters from this same boundary. This distance is calculated from the center of the opening to the boundary line between the lands.

###### Article 792

The distance rules provided for in the preceding article do not apply to openings that give onto a space belonging to the public domain, nor when specific urban planning provisions provide for other rules.  
They do not apply either when the contemplated opening gives onto a land burdened with an easement preventing construction, such as a right of way easement, established in favor of the person who wishes to open the view, provided that the distance between the contemplated opening and the limit of exercise of the easement in the neighboring land is located at least three meters away.

##### Section III: Roof drainage Article 793

Every owner must construct his roofs so that rainwater flows onto his land or onto the public road; he may not cause it to flow onto his neighbor's land.

##### Section IV: Right of way Article 794

The owner whose lands are landlocked may claim a sufficient passage over the lands of his neighbors, subject to compensation proportionate to the damage he may cause, unless the state of being landlocked was voluntarily created.  
A land is landlocked when it has no access to the public road, or only insufficient access, to allow its normal use or agricultural, industrial or commercial exploitation.

###### Article 795

The passage must normally be taken from the side where the route is shortest from the landlocked land to the public road, unless another route is less damaging in which case that route must be preferred.

###### Article 796

If the landlocked state results from the division of a land following a sale, an exchange, a partition or any other contract, the passage may only be requested over the lands that were the subject of these acts.  

However, in the case where a sufficient passage could not be established over the divided lands, Article 794 would be applicable.

###### Article 797

The action for compensation, in the case provided for by Article 794, is subject to prescription, and the passage may be continued, even though the action for compensation is no longer admissible.  
The maintenance of the passage is the responsibility of the owner of the dominant land, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 798

In case of cessation of the landlocked state and regardless of the manner in which the location and mode of the easement were determined, the owner of the servient land may, at any time, invoke the extinction of the easement.  
Failing an amicable agreement, this disappearance is established by a court decision.

#### Chapter III: Easements established by act of man

##### Section I

The various types of easements that may be established on property Article 799
Easements are either continuous or discontinuous.  

Continuous easements are those whose use is or may be continual without requiring the actual act of man: such are water conduits, drains, views and others of this kind.  
Discontinuous easements are those that require the actual act of man to be exercised: such are rights of passage, drawing water, grazing and other similar rights.

###### Article 800

Easements are apparent or non-apparent.  

Apparent easements are those that are announced by external works, such as a door, a window, an aqueduct.  
Non-apparent easements are those that have no external sign of their existence, such as, for example, the prohibition to build on a land, or to build only to a determined height.

##### Section II: How easements are established Article 801

Easements that do not result from the configuration of the places or that are imposed by law can only be acquired by title.  
By exception, continuous and apparent easements may be established by destination of the father of the family:

There is destination of the father of the family when, in the absence of a stipulation to the contrary in the deed of division, it is proved that the two lands currently divided belonged to the same owner, and that the external works or arrangements from which the easement results were made by him before the division of the land and maintained since.

###### Article 802

If the owner of two lands between which there exists an apparent sign of easement, disposes of one of the lands without the contract containing any agreement relating to the easement, it continues to exist actively or passively in favor of the alienated land or on the alienated land.

###### Article 803

When an easement is established, one is deemed to grant everything necessary to use it.  

Thus the easement of drawing water from another's fountain necessarily carries the right of passage.

##### Section III

Rights of the owner of the land to which the easement is due Article 804
The person to whom an easement is due has the right to make all works necessary to use it and to preserve it.

###### Article 805

These works are at his expense, and not at the expense of the owner of the servient land, unless the title establishing the easement states otherwise.

###### Article 806

Even in the case where the owner of the servient land is charged by the title to make at his expense the works necessary for the use or preservation of the easement, he may always free himself from the charge, by abandoning the servient land to the owner of the land to which the easement is due.

###### Article 807

If the land for which the easement was established comes to be divided, the easement remains due for each portion, without however the condition of the servient land being aggravated.  
Thus, for example, if it is a right of way, all the co-owners shall be obliged to exercise it by the same place.

###### Article 808

The owner of the servient estate may do nothing that tends to diminish the use of the servitude or to make it more inconvenient.  
Thus, he may not change the state of the premises, nor transfer the exercise of the servitude to a place different from that where it was originally assigned.  

However, if this original assignment has become more onerous to the owner of the burdened estate, or if it prevents him from making advantageous repairs thereto, he may offer to the owner of the other estate a place equally convenient for the exercise of his rights, and the latter may not refuse it.

###### Article 809

For his part, he who has a right of servitude may only use it according to his title, without being able to make, either in the estate which owes the servitude or in the estate to which it is due, any change which aggravates the condition of the former.

##### Section IV: How servitudes are extinguished Article 810

Servitudes cease when things are in such a state that they can no longer be used.  

They revive if things are restored in such a manner that they can be used.

###### Article 811

Any servitude is extinguished when the estate to which it is due and the estate which owes it are united in the same hand.

###### Article 812

A servitude is extinguished by non-use for thirty years, unless it is registered in the Land Register.  

The period begins to run from the day on which the holder of the dominant estate ceased to enjoy it, in the case of discontinuous servitudes, and from the day on which an act contrary to the servitude was done, in the case of continuous servitudes.

###### Article 813

If the estate in favour of which the servitude is established belongs to several persons in undivided ownership, the enjoyment by one prevents extinctive prescription with regard to all.  
If, among the co-owners, there is one against whom prescription could not run, such as a minor, he shall have preserved the right of all the others.

## BOOK III. OF THE DIFFERENT WAYS IN WHICH PROPERTY IS ACQUIRED

General provisions

###### Article 814

Ownership of property is acquired and transferred by succession, by gift inter vivos or by will, by the effect of obligations, by accession or incorporation, by occupation, by delivery, by prescription, or any other mode of acquisition provided by law.  

Title I: Of successions
Chapter I: Of the opening of successions and of the seisin of heirs Article 815
Successions open, upon death, at the last domicile of the deceased.  

They devolve, when the deceased has not disposed of his property by gifts or will, according to the present provisions of the civil code whenever the spouses have opted for the regime of the civil code at the time of their marriage or an unmarried person has expressed his or her wish to that effect to the civil registrar. Gifts and wills are authorized to the extent compatible with the reserved portion.  

The provisions of this title apply to the succession of a person subject to bankruptcy proceedings, subject to the special provisions provided in this area.

###### Article 816

Agreements which have the object of creating rights or renouncing rights over all or part of a succession not yet opened or of property dependent thereon produce effect only in cases where they are authorized by law.

###### Article 817

The law regulates the order of succession among the different heirs and the surviving spouse.  

Universal legatees and donees are seised under the conditions provided in Title II, Of gifts inter vivos and wills, of this book.  
In their absence, the succession passes to the State.

###### Article 818

Heirs and the surviving spouse are seised by operation of law of the property, rights and actions of the deceased, under the obligation to discharge all the charges of the succession.  
The State must have itself sent into possession.

###### Article 819

The provisions of this title, in particular those concerning undivided ownership and partition, apply as appropriate to universal or residuary legatees and donees, when not derogated from by a particular rule.

#### Chapter II

Of the qualities required to succeed - Of proof of the quality of heir

##### Section I: Of the qualities required to succeed Article 820

To succeed, it is necessary to exist at the instant of the opening of the succession or, having already been conceived, to be born viable.  
A person whose absence is presumed within the meaning of articles 142 and following may succeed.

###### Article 821

When several persons who had a vocation to succeed one another perish in the same event, the order of deaths is established by all means.  
Persons who die without it being possible to establish which survived the other are deemed to have died at the same instant, if at least one of them is called to the succession of the other.  
The succession of each of them is then devolved to the persons who would have been called to receive it in their absence.

###### Article 822

Unworthy to succeed, and, as such, excluded from successions, are:
1° He who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily caused or attempted to cause the death of the deceased;  
2° He who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily inflicted blows or violence having caused the death of the deceased, without intention to cause it;  
3° He who is convicted of having voluntarily abstained from preventing the commission of an offence against the bodily integrity of the deceased from which death resulted, when he could have done so without risk to himself or to third parties;  
4° He who, in criminal proceedings, has brought against the deceased an accusation or testimony found to be false or defamatory;  

5° The heir of full age who, informed of the murder of the deceased, did not report it to the authorities. However, failure to report may not be raised against the ascendants and descendants of the murderer, nor against his relatives in the same degree, nor against his husband or wife, nor against his brothers or sisters, nor against his uncles and aunts, nor against nephews and nieces.

###### Article 823

When by reason of their death, the public prosecution could not be pursued to its conclusion against the persons who committed the acts mentioned in 1° and 2°, they may nevertheless be declared unworthy by the court upon application of any heir and, failing that, of the public prosecutor. The application must be made within six months of the death.

###### Article 824

When the deceased, subsequent to the facts which constitute the cause of unworthiness, became aware of them and expressly stated, in testamentary form, that he intended to maintain the heir in his rights or made him a universal or residuary gift, this successor affected by a cause of unworthiness is not excluded from the succession.

###### Article 825

The heir excluded from the succession on grounds of unworthiness is bound to return all the fruits and all the revenues of which he has had enjoyment since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 826

The children of the unworthy person are not excluded by the fault of their ancestor, whether they come to the succession in their own right or by the effect of representation; but the unworthy person may not, in any case, claim, over the property of this succession, the usufruct which the law grants to fathers and mothers over the property of their children.

##### Section II: Of proof of the quality of heir Article 827

Proof of the quality of heir is established by all means.  
There is no derogation from the practices concerning the issuance of certificates of ownership or inheritance by judicial or administrative authorities.

###### Article 828

Proof of the status of heir may result from a certificate of notoriety drawn up by a notary, at the request of one or more beneficiaries.  
The certificate of notoriety must refer to the death certificate of the person whose succession is open and mention the supporting documents that could be produced, such as civil status certificates and, where applicable, documents concerning the existence of gifts causa mortis that may have an impact on succession devolution.  

It contains the affirmation, signed by the beneficiary or beneficiaries who are the authors of the request, that they have entitlement, alone or with others whom they designate, to collect all or part of the succession of the deceased.  

Any person whose statements would appear useful may be called to the certificate.  
Mention is made of the existence of the certificate of notoriety in the margin of the death certificate.

###### Article 829

The certificate of notoriety thus established is valid until proof to the contrary.  

The person who relies on it is presumed to have inheritance rights in the proportion indicated therein, and the heirs designated in the certificate of notoriety or their common agent are deemed, with regard to third parties holding property of the succession, to have free disposal of such property and, if it concerns funds, free disposal thereof in the proportion indicated in the certificate.  
The certificate of notoriety does not, by itself, entail acceptance of the succession.

###### Article 830

Any person who, knowingly and in bad faith, relies on an inaccurate certificate of notoriety, incurs the sanctions provided for in Article 888, without prejudice to damages.

#### Chapitre III : De l'ordre des successions Article 831

Successions devolve to the relatives and to the successible spouse of the deceased, in the order and according to the rules determined hereinafter.  
The successible spouse is the surviving spouse who is not divorced.

##### Section I : Des droits des parents en l'absence de conjoint successible

###### § 1. Dispositions générales Article 832

The law does not distinguish according to the modes of establishment of filiation in regulating succession.  

The rights resulting from adoptive filiation are regulated in Title IX of this code, relating to adoption according to the Civil Code.

###### Article 833

In the absence of a successible spouse, relatives are called to succeed as follows: 1° Children and their descendants;  
2° Father and mother; brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter; 3° Ascendants other than father and mother;  
4° Collaterals other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter. Each of these four categories constitutes an order of heirs which excludes the following ones.

###### Article 834

Children or their descendants succeed to their father and mother or other ascendants, without distinction of sex or primogeniture, even if they are born of different unions.

###### Article 835

When the deceased leaves neither issue, nor brother, nor sister, nor descendants of the latter, his father and mother succeed him, each for one half.

###### Article 836

When the father and mother died before the deceased and the latter leaves no issue, the brothers and sisters of the deceased or their descendants succeed him, to the exclusion of other relatives, ascendants or collaterals.

###### Article 837

When the father and mother survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, but has brothers and sisters or descendants of the latter, the succession devolves, for one quarter, to each of the father and mother and, for the remaining half, to the brothers and sisters or their descendants.  

When only one of the father and mother survives, the succession devolves for one quarter to that person and for three quarters to the brothers and sisters or their descendants.

###### Article 838

When only the father or the mother survives and the deceased has neither issue nor brother nor sister nor descendant of the latter, but leaves one or more ascendants of the other branch than that of his surviving father or mother, the succession devolves for one half to the father or mother and for one half to the ascendants of the other branch.

###### Article 839

When the father and mother or one of them survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, they may in all cases exercise a right of return, up to the shares fixed in the first paragraph of Article 837, over the property that the deceased had received from them by gift.  
The value of the portion of property subject to the right of return is credited as a priority against the succession rights of the father and mother.  

When the right of return cannot be exercised in kind, it is executed in value, within the limit of the succession assets.

###### Article 840

In the absence of heirs of the first two orders, the succession devolves to ascendants other than the father and mother.

###### Article 841

In the absence of heirs of the first three orders, the succession devolves to the collateral relatives of the deceased other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter.

###### § 2. Des degrés et des branches Article 842

Proximity of relationship is established by the number of generations; each generation is called a degree.

###### Article 843

The sequence of degrees forms the line. The direct line is called the sequence of degrees between persons who descend from one another, and the collateral line, the sequence of degrees between persons who do not descend from one another but who descend from a common ancestor.  
The direct line is distinguished into direct descendant line and direct ascendant line. The first is that which links the head with those who descend from him; the second is that which links a person with those from whom he descends.

###### Article 844

In the direct line, there are as many degrees as there are generations between the persons. Thus, the child is, with regard to the father and mother, in the first degree; the grandson or granddaughter in the second; and reciprocally from the father and mother with regard to the child and from the grandparents with regard to the grandson or granddaughter; and so on.  
In the collateral line, degrees are counted by generation, from one of the relatives up to but not including the common ancestor, and from the latter to the other relative. Thus, brothers and sisters are in the

second degree; the uncle or aunt and the nephew or niece are in the third degree; first cousins in the fourth; and so on.

###### Article 845

In each order, the closest heir excludes the more remote heir in degree. At equal degree, heirs succeed in equal portions and per capita.  
All subject to what will be said hereinafter concerning division by branches and representation.

###### Article 846

Collateral relatives belonging to the order of heirs mentioned in 4° of Article 833 do not succeed beyond the sixth degree.

###### Article 847

Relationship is divided into two branches, according to whether it proceeds from the father or the mother.  
When the succession devolves to ascendants, it is divided by half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 848

In each branch succeeds, to the exclusion of all others, the ascendant who is in the closest degree.  
Ascendants in the same degree succeed per capita.  

In the absence of an ascendant in one branch, the ascendants of the other branch take the entire succession.

###### Article 849

When the succession devolves to collaterals other than brothers and sisters or their descendants, it is divided by half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 850

In each branch succeeds, to the exclusion of all others, the collateral who is in the closest degree.  
Collaterals in the same degree succeed per capita.  
In the absence of a collateral in one branch, the collaterals of the other branch take the entire succession.

###### § 3. De la représentation Article 851

Representation is a legal fiction, the effect of which is to call the representatives to the succession in the place, degree and rights of the person represented.

###### Article 852

Representation takes place indefinitely in the direct descending line.

It is admitted in all cases, whether the children of the deceased compete with the descendants of a predeceased child, or whether all the children of the deceased having died before him, the descendants of said children find themselves among themselves in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 853

Representation does not take place in favor of ascendants; the closest, in each of the two lines, always excludes the more remote.

###### Article 854

In the collateral line, representation is admitted in favor of the children and descendants of brothers or sisters of the deceased, whether they come to his succession concurrently with uncles or aunts, or whether all the brothers and sisters of the deceased having predeceased, the succession is devolved to their descendants in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 855

In all cases where representation is admitted, the partition is carried out by root, as if the person represented were coming to the succession: if the same root has produced several branches, the subdivision is also made by root in each branch. Within a root or a subdivision of a root, the partition is made per capita.

###### Article 856

One does not represent living persons, but only those who are dead; one may represent a person whose succession one has renounced.

One represents renunciants only in successions devolved in the direct or collateral line.

The children of the renunciant conceived before the opening of the succession from which the renunciant was excluded bring back to the succession of the latter the property which they inherited in his place and stead, if they come in competition with other children conceived after the opening of the succession. The bringing back is made according to the provisions set out in articles 994 et seq. of this code.

Unless the disposer wills otherwise, in case of representation of a renunciant, the donations made to the latter are imputed, where applicable, on the reserved portion that should have gone to him if he had not renounced.

The law does not distinguish, for the exercise of representation, between legitimate filiation and natural filiation.

###### Article 857

Representation is admitted in favor of the children and descendants of the unworthy person, even though the latter is alive at the opening of the succession.

The provisions set out in the second paragraph of article 856 are applicable to the children of the unworthy person during his lifetime.

##### Section II : Des droits du conjoint survivant

###### § 1. De la nature des droits, de leur montant et de leur exercice Article 858

The successor spouse is called to the succession, either alone or in competition with the relatives of the deceased.

###### Article 859

If the predeceased spouse leaves children or descendants, the surviving spouse receives, at his choice, the usufruct of all the existing property or the ownership of one quarter of the property when all the children are issue of both spouses and the ownership of one quarter in the presence of one or more children who are not issue of both spouses.

###### Article 860

If, in the absence of children or descendants, the deceased leaves his father and mother, the surviving spouse receives half of the property. The other half is devolved for one quarter to the father and for one quarter to the mother.

When the father or the mother has predeceased, the share that would have gone to him or her passes to the surviving spouse.

###### Article 861

In the absence of children or descendants of the deceased and of his father and mother, the surviving spouse receives the entire succession.

###### Article 862

By way of derogation from article 861, in case of predecease of the father and mother, the property that the deceased had received from his ascendants by succession or donation and which is found in kind in the succession is, in the absence of descendants, devolved for half to the brothers and sisters of the deceased or to their descendants, themselves descendants of the predeceased parent or parents at the origin of the transmission.

###### Article 863

When the surviving spouse receives all or three quarters of the property, the ascendants of the deceased, other than the father and mother, who are in need benefit from a claim for maintenance against the succession of the predeceased.

The time limit for claiming it is one year from the death or from the moment when the heirs cease to provide the benefits they previously furnished to the ascendants. The time limit is extended, in case of joint ownership, until the completion of the partition.

The pension is taken from the succession. It is borne by all the heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all the particular legatees, proportionally to their emolument.

However, if the deceased expressly declared that a certain legacy shall be paid in preference to the others, article 1080 shall apply.

###### Article 864

When the spouse has the choice of ownership or usufruct, his rights are inalienable as long as he has not exercised his option.

###### Article 865

The spouse's option between usufruct and ownership is proved by any means.

Any heir may invite the spouse in writing to exercise his option. Failing to have taken a position in writing within three months, the spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct.

The spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct if he dies without having taken a position.

###### Article 866

The calculation of the right in full ownership of the spouse provided for in articles 859 and 860 shall be carried out on a mass made up of all the property existing at the death of his spouse to which shall be fictitiously reunited those of which he would have disposed, either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, in favor of successors, without dispensation from bringing back.

The spouse may exercise his right only on the property of which the predeceased shall not have disposed either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, and without prejudice to the rights of reserve or to the rights of return.

###### Article 867

The liberalities received from the deceased by the surviving spouse are imputed on the rights of the latter in the succession. When the liberalities thus received are less than the rights defined in articles 859 and 860,

the surviving spouse may claim the complement, without ever receiving a portion of the property greater than the available portion defined in article 1228.

###### § 2. De la conversion de l'usufruit Article 868

Any usufruct belonging to the spouse on the property of the predeceased, whether it results from the law, a will or a donation of property to come, gives rise to a faculty of conversion into a life annuity, at the request of one of the bare owner heirs or of the successor spouse himself.

The faculty of conversion is not susceptible to renunciation. The coheirs cannot be deprived of it by the will of the predeceased.

###### Article 869

In the absence of agreement between the parties, the request for conversion is submitted to the judge. The request for conversion may be introduced until the final partition.

If he grants the request for conversion, the judge determines the amount of the annuity, the securities that the debtor coheirs must provide, as well as the type of indexation appropriate to maintain the initial equivalence of the annuity to the usufruct.

However, the judge cannot order against the will of the spouse the conversion of the usufruct relating to the dwelling he occupies as his principal residence, as well as the furniture furnishing it.

###### Article 870

By agreement between the heirs and the spouse, the conversion of the spouse's usufruct into capital may be carried out.

###### Article 871

The conversion of the usufruct is included in the partition operations. It does not produce retroactive effect, unless otherwise stipulated by the parties.

###### § 3

Of the right to temporary housing and the life right to housing Article 872
If, at the time of death, the surviving spouse actually occupies, as a principal residence, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or forming part of the estate entirely, he or she has by operation of law, for one year, the free enjoyment of that dwelling, as well as of the furniture, included in the estate, that furnishes it.

If his or her housing was secured by means of a lease or a dwelling belonging in undivided part to the deceased, the rent or occupancy indemnity shall be reimbursed to him or her by the estate during the year, as and when paid.
The rights provided for in this article are deemed direct effects of marriage and not succession rights. This article is a matter of public policy.

###### Article 873

In addition, unless the deceased expressed a contrary intention under the conditions of Article 1127, the surviving spouse who actually occupied, at the time of death, as a principal residence, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or forming part of the estate entirely, has over that dwelling and over the furniture included in the estate that furnishes it, until his or her death, a right of habitation and a right of use.

When the dwelling is subject to a lease, the surviving spouse, if he or she actually occupied the premises as a principal residence at the time of death, benefits from the right of use over the furniture included in the estate furnishing it.
The deprivation of these rights of habitation and use expressed by the deceased under the conditions mentioned in the first paragraph has no effect on the usufruct rights that the spouse receives by virtue of law or a liberality, which continue to be governed by their own rules.

These rights of habitation and use are exercised under the conditions provided for in Articles 745 paragraph 3, 747 and 748.

The spouse, the other heirs or one of them may require that an inventory of the movables and a statement of the immovable subject to the rights of use and habitation be drawn up.
By way of derogation from Article 745, paragraph 3, when the situation of the spouse is such that the dwelling burdened with the right of habitation is no longer adapted to his or her needs, the spouse or his or her representative may lease it for use other than commercial or agricultural in order to generate the resources necessary for new accommodation conditions.

###### Article 874

The value of the rights of habitation and use is imputed to the value of the succession rights received by the spouse.
If the value of the rights of habitation and use is less than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse may take the balance from the existing property.

If the value of the rights of habitation and use is greater than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse is not required to compensate the estate for the excess.

###### Article 875

The spouse has one year from the death to express his or her intention to benefit from these rights of habitation and use.
The surviving spouse and the heirs may, by agreement, convert the rights of habitation and use into a life annuity or into capital.

If among the successors who are parties to the agreement there is a minor or a protected adult, the agreement must be authorized by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### § 4. Of the right to pension Article 876

The estate of the predeceased spouse owes a pension to the surviving spouse who is in need. The time limit to claim it is one year from the death or from the moment when the heirs cease to pay the benefits they previously provided to the spouse. The time limit is extended, in case of undivided ownership, until the completion of the partition.
The maintenance pension is taken from the estate. It is borne by all the heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all the particular legatees, in proportion to their emolument.

However, if the deceased expressly declared that a particular legacy shall be paid in preference to the others, Article 1080 shall apply.

#### Chapter IV. Of the rights of the State

###### Article 877

In the absence of heirs, surviving spouse, universal legatees or donees, the estate is acquired by the State.
The State is required to have seals affixed and, if the inventory of the property has not already been carried out within the framework of the procedure provided for under the title of vacant estates, the domain authority has it carried out in the forms prescribed for the acceptance of estates under benefit of inventory.

###### Article 878

It must request the sending into possession from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the estate is opened.
The State is dispensed from resorting to the ministry of a lawyer; the court rules on the application three months and forty days after publication and posting in the customary forms, and after having heard the public prosecutor.

###### Article 879

In the case where the vacancy had been regularly declared, and the domain administration appointed curator, it may, before filing its application, proceed by itself with the publicity formalities provided for.

###### Article 880

The domain administration that has not fulfilled the formalities prescribed to it may be ordered to pay damages to the heirs, if any appear.

#### Chapter V: Of the option of the heir

##### Section I: General provisions Article 881

Every successor, the heir with regard to the estate as the legatee with regard to the legacy that falls to him or her, may:	either accept it purely and simply,	either accept it under benefit of inventory, when he or she has a universal or universal title vocation,	or renounce it.

###### Article 882

The option is indivisible. However, the successor who combines more than one succession vocation has, for each of them, a separate right of option.

###### Article 883

This option cannot be exercised before the opening of the estate, neither by marriage contract nor with the consent of the person whose estate is at issue.
Any conditional or term option is null and void.

###### Article 884

The heir of subsequent rank has the same rights as the heir when the latter renounces the estate or is struck by unworthiness and this, from the day he or she became aware of the renunciation or unworthiness. The same applies to the heirs of the person who dies without having opted, from the death of his or her predecessor; these heirs of the person who dies without having opted exercise the option separately, each for his or her share.

###### Article 885

The power to accept or renounce an estate is prescribed by ten years. At the end of this period, the successor is deemed to have renounced the estate. The person who claims to have accepted this estate before the expiration of this period must provide proof thereof.

###### Article 886

The subsequent heir of an heir whose acceptance is annulled sees the ten-year period run against him or her only from the final decision finding this nullity.
The heir who has left the surviving spouse in enjoyment of the hereditary property sees the period run against him or her only from the death of the latter.

The period does not run either against the person who, legitimately, was unaware of the birth of his or her right, in particular the opening of the estate.

Moreover, as long as the prescription of the right to accept is not acquired against the heirs who have renounced, they have the power to still accept the estate, if it has not already been accepted by other heirs; without prejudice however to the rights that may be acquired by third parties over the property of the estate.

###### Article 887

The option exercised has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the succession.

However, error, fraud as well as duress are grounds for nullity of the option exercised by the heir. The action for nullity is barred after five years from the day on which the error or fraud was discovered or from the day on which the duress ceased.

###### Article 888

The heir who, knowingly and in bad faith, has concealed assets or rights of a succession, or concealed the existence of a co-heir, or failed to include in the inventory assets or rights of the succession, is deprived of the benefit of inventory and the right of renunciation: he is an unconditional heir, without prejudice to damages that the victims of his actions may claim.  
The heir may not, however, claim any share in the assets or rights misappropriated or concealed. Likewise, when the concealment related to a donation subject to hotchpot or reduction, the heir owes the hotchpot or reduction of that donation without being able to claim any share in it. The concealing heir is furthermore required to return all fruits and income from the concealed assets which he has enjoyed since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 889

Personal creditors of a person who refrains from accepting a succession or who renounces a succession to the prejudice of their rights may be authorized by the court to accept the succession on behalf of their debtor, in his place and stead.  
The acceptance takes place only in favor of these creditors and up to the amount of their claims. It produces no other effect with regard to the heir.

###### Article 890

The acceptance of a succession which is found to be absorbed or diminished by more than half, by the discovery of a will unknown at the time of acceptance, is voidable for lesion.

##### Section II: Of the acceptance of the succession

###### Article 891

Successions devolving to minors and adults under guardianship may only be validly accepted in accordance with the provisions of the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 892

The acceptance of the succession may be express or tacit: it is express when the successor takes the title or quality of heir in an authentic or private instrument; it is tacit when the successor performs an act which necessarily presumes his intention to accept and which he would only have the right to perform in his quality as heir.  
Purely conservatory acts, acts of supervision and provisional administration are not, in themselves, acts constituting acceptance on the part of the heir. If the successor wishes to perform another act without taking the title or quality of heir, he must request authorization from the judge to perform it.

###### Article 893

The following are deemed purely conservatory:
1° The payment of funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other succession debts whose settlement is urgent;  
2° The collection of fruits and income from succession assets or the sale of perishable goods, provided that it is shown that the funds were used to extinguish the debts referred to in 1° or were deposited with a notary or placed in escrow;  
3° Any act intended to prevent the aggravation of succession liabilities;  
4° Acts related to the termination of the employment contract of the employee of the deceased private employer, the payment of wages and compensation owed to the employee as well as the delivery of end-of-contract documents.

###### Article 894

The following are deemed provisional administration:
1° The renewal, as lessor or lessee, of leases which, failing which, would give rise to the payment of compensation;  
2° The implementation of administrative or disposition decisions initiated by the deceased and necessary for the proper functioning of the business;  
3° Acts which are routine operations necessary for the short-term continuation of the activity of the business forming part of the succession.

###### Article 895

The heir who, gratuitously or for consideration, transfers his rights in the succession, whether to a third party, or to all his co-heirs, or to some of them, accepts the succession by that fact alone.  
The same applies when the heir has renounced the succession, gratuitously or not, in favor of one, several or all of his co-heirs, or in favor of one, several or all heirs of subsequent rank.

###### Article 896

When a person to whom a succession has devolved has died before being able, expressly or tacitly, to express his choice, his heirs may accept it or renounce it on his behalf. In the absence of unanimity among them, the succession must be accepted subject to benefit of inventory.

###### Article 897

When the heir accepts the succession, the effect of the acceptance relates back to the day of the opening of the succession.

##### Section III: Of the renunciation of successions Article 898

The renunciation of a succession is not presumed. It is enforceable against all from the day on which it is made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the succession opened, in a special register kept for that purpose.

###### Article 899

The heir who renounces is deemed never to have been an heir.

###### Article 900

The succession to which the heir renounces is distributed among his heirs in direct line; in the absence of heirs in direct line, it passes to the co-heirs and otherwise to the next degree.  
The heir who renounces the succession may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer expressly required hotchpot in case of renunciation. In that case, the hotchpot is made in value; when the value brought into hotchpot exceeds the rights he should have had in the partition had he participated in it, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs up to the amount of that excess.

##### Section IV: Of the benefit of inventory

###### § 1. Formalities to be observed Article 901

The declaration of an heir that he intends to take that quality only subject to benefit of inventory must be made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the succession opened. It must be recorded in the register intended to receive acts of renunciation.

###### Article 902

The declaration states the surnames, given names, occupation of the heir and the capacity by virtue of which he is called to the succession.  
It also includes the election of a single domicile located in Djibouti, which may be the domicile of one of the acceptors subject to benefit of inventory or that of the person in charge of settling the succession. It is to this address that creditors shall declare their claims.

###### Article 903

The declaration of the heir is registered by the registry, which gives him a receipt for it, and opens a file. The receipt informs the declarant of the need to comply with the publication provided for by the following article.

###### Article 904

The declaration is published, within fifteen days, in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.  
When the law refers to the declaration as the starting point of a time limit, that limit runs from the date of the publication made.

###### Article 905

The declaration of the heir has effect only insofar as it is preceded or followed by a faithful and accurate inventory of the assets of the succession and within the time limits to be determined hereinafter.

###### Article 906

The heir has, first, three months to make an inventory, from the day of the opening of the succession.

However, he may request from the judge an additional period if he justifies serious and legitimate reasons that delay the filing of the inventory. In that case, the period is suspended from the date of the request for extension.

The heir then has forty days to deliberate on whether or not to accept the succession. This second period begins to run from the day of expiration of the period to which the heir is subject to make the inventory, or from the day of closure of the inventory if it was completed before the three months.

###### Article 907

The inventory is descriptive and estimative of the elements present, item by item, in the estate of the deceased.  
It is established by a bailiff or a notary, according to the rules applicable to these professions.

###### Article 908

A copy of the inventory is delivered against receipt by the heir to the competent registry, which adds it to the file. The heir must carry out this formality within two months of the inventory being made. Failing this, he is deemed to have accepted the succession unconditionally.

###### Article 909

The inventory gives rise to the same publicity as the initial declaration.  
Any person who justifies his status as creditor against the deceased may take cognizance of its content and obtain a copy at the registry.

###### § 2. Effects of acceptance subject to inventory Article 910

The declaration made by the heir to accept the succession subject to inventory entails:
1° Separation of estates: the personal property of the heir is not merged with that of the succession;  
2° Preservation of all the rights that the heir had previously over the property of the deceased; 3° Limitation of the acceptance of the succession to the succession assets: the heir is only required to pay the debts of the succession within the limit of the assets collected and not from his personal estate. The heir may only be held liable for his acts on his personal property when provisions of this paragraph so provide;  
4° Framework for the management of the succession assets by the heir, who is required to administer the succession.

###### Article 911

During the duration of the periods to make an inventory and to deliberate, the heir cannot be compelled to exercise his option. No judgment can be obtained against him.  
As long as the prescription of the right to accept has not been acquired against him, the heir may revoke his acceptance and accept the succession unconditionally. He is then deemed to have accepted it from the opening of the succession.  

Acceptance subject to inventory prevents any renunciation of the succession.

###### Article 912

If the heir does not file the inventory within the periods provided for making it, or does not exercise his option within the period offered to deliberate, he retains the power to still make an inventory and to opt.

It is otherwise if he has otherwise made an act manifesting his intention to accept the succession unconditionally or if there exists against him a judgment having acquired the force of res judicata that condemns him in the capacity of unconditional heir.

###### Article 913

However, upon expiration of the periods provided for making an inventory and for deliberating, the heir who has not opted may be summoned, by extrajudicial act, to take a position. The summons may emanate from a creditor of the succession, a co-heir, an heir of subsequent rank, or the State.  
Within two months following the summons, the heir must take a position or request an additional period from the judge when he has not been able to close the inventory begun or when he justifies other serious and legitimate reasons. This period is suspended from the date of the request for extension until the decision of the judge seized.  

Failing to have taken a position upon expiration of the two-month period or the additional period granted, the heir is deemed to have accepted unconditionally.

###### Article 914

From the publicity of the declaration of the heir who accepts the succession subject to inventory, the creditors of the succession have a period of twelve months to claim what is owed to them. They must declare their claim within this period, by notifying their title to the elected domicile of the succession.  
In case of late declaration or absence of declaration, claims not secured by security interests over the property of the succession are extinguished with regard to the succession.  

This provision also benefits sureties and co-obligors, as well as persons having granted an independent guarantee relating to the claim thus extinguished.

###### Article 915

From the publicity of the declaration of acceptance subject to inventory and for a period of twelve months, it stops or prohibits any means of execution and any new registration of security interest by the creditors of the succession, relating to both movables and immovables.  
However, seizing creditors are considered as holders of security interests over the property and rights previously seized.

###### Article 916

When the succession has been accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by one or more others up to the net assets, the rules applicable to this latter option are imposed on all heirs until the day of partition.  
The creditors of a succession accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by others up to the net assets may provoke the partition as soon as they justify difficulties in the recovery of the share of their claim incumbent upon the heirs accepting up to the net assets.

###### Article 917

The heir accepting up to the net assets has the obligation to administer the property he collects in the succession, and must account for his management.  
He is liable for serious faults he would commit in this administration.  

He must present the account to any succession creditor who requests it and respond within two months to the summons, served by extrajudicial act, to reveal to him where the property and

rights collected in the succession that he has neither alienated nor retained are located. Failing this, he may be compelled on his personal property.  

If he does not wish to personally administer the property of the succession, or if he is in default, a representative may be appointed in court at the request of any interested party. The President of the Court of First Instance is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 918

The heir is the owner of the assets of the succession and has the power to dispose of the property of the succession.  
If there exist in the succession objects liable to perish or too costly to preserve, the heir may proceed with the sale of these objects. If the heir has decided to retain such property in kind, at the end of the acceptance procedure subject to inventory, he is only liable for the depreciation or deterioration caused by his negligence.

###### Article 919

For other property, within twelve months from the publicity provided for in Article 904, the heir may declare:
1° that he intends to retain in kind certain property of the succession. He then owes to the succession the value of this property as it was estimated in the inventory;  
2° that he sells certain property, movable or immovable.  
This property is excluded from the succession estate and withdrawn from the pledge of succession creditors. On the other hand, their value is recorded in the assets of the succession. All without prejudice to the rights of creditors holding security interests.  
Other succession property that has not been the subject of such a declaration remains in the pledge of the creditors of the succession.

###### Article 920

The declaration of the alienation or retention of one or more assets is made within fifteen days to the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The heir ensures its publication in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices.  
Without prejudice to the rights reserved to creditors holding security interests, any estate creditor may challenge before the judge, within three months after the publication mentioned in the first paragraph, the value of the retained asset or, when the sale was made amicably, the price of the alienation by proving that the value of the asset is higher.  

When the creditor's claim is granted, the heir is liable for the difference from his personal assets, unless he returns the retained asset to the estate.  
The creditor may also act in his own name to have acts performed by his debtor in fraud of his rights declared unenforceable against him, provided he establishes, in the case of an act for valuable consideration, that the third-party co-contractor had knowledge or should have had knowledge of the fraud.

###### Article 921

The declaration to retain an asset is not enforceable against creditors as long as it has not been published.  

Failure to declare the alienation of an asset within the time limit provided in the preceding article makes the heir liable on his personal assets up to the amount of the alienation price.

###### Article 922

The heir settles the liabilities of the estate. For this purpose, he draws up a draft settlement of liabilities.  

The costs of seals, if any have been affixed, of inventory and of account, are borne by the estate. The public officer or ministerial officer who settled the estate or enabled the preservation of estate assets shall be paid before the other creditors.  
Registered creditors are paid according to the rank of the security interest accompanying their claim.  

Other creditors who have declared their claim are satisfied in the order of declarations. Legacies of sums of money are delivered after payment of creditors.

###### Article 923

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed with the registry which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904. Creditors who are not fully satisfied in view of this draft may, within one month of publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in order to challenge the settlement draft.

###### Article 924

In the absence of challenge at the end of the one-month period from the publication provided for in the preceding article, the heir must pay the creditors within the following two months, in accordance with the draft settlement of liabilities.  
When, conversely, the settlement draft is not validated due to a challenge concerning the order or nature of claims, the heir deposits the available sums as long as the challenge persists.

###### Article 925

The personal creditors of the heir may not pursue recovery of their claims against the assets of the estate until the end of the twelve-month period from the publication of the declaration of acceptance of the estate subject to inventory and after the full satisfaction of estate creditors and legatees.  
Creditors who have not declared their claim within the time limit referred to in the preceding article, and who appear only after exhaustion of the assets, have recourse only against legatees who have been satisfied in their rights.

##### Section V: Vacant estates Article 926

An estate is vacant when, after expiration of the time limits for making inventory and for deliberating: 1° No one appears who claims an estate and there is no known heir;  
2° All known heirs have renounced the estate;  
3° Known heirs have been summoned to take a position in accordance with the provisions of Article 913 and have renounced the estate or remained silent;  
4° In the absence of summons, known heirs have not opted, either expressly or tacitly, for ten years.  
When heirs come forward during the proceedings, their hereditary prerogatives take precedence. They may then exercise their legal right of option: if they accept the estate purely and simply, the vacancy automatically ends; if they renounce it, it continues; and if they accept subject to inventory, the procedure continues according to the rules set out in Section IV of this chapter.

###### Article 927

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the estate is opened, appoints a curator upon the request of any interested person or upon the requisition of the public prosecutor.  

His decision is, at the initiative of the curator, within fifteen days of its pronouncement, published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices.  

In the context of vacant estates, the curatorship is necessarily entrusted to the administrative authority responsible for the domain.

###### Article 928

The curator is required, first of all, to have its condition recorded by an inventory: he exercises and pursues its rights; he responds to claims made against the estate; he administers, under the obligation to have the sums of money found in the estate, as well as the amounts from the sale price of movables or immovables sold, paid into the National Treasury, for the preservation of rights and under the obligation to account to whom it may concern.  
The provisions of Section IV of this chapter, on the forms of inventory, on the mode of administration and on the accounts to be rendered by the beneficiary heir, as well as on the rights and obligations of creditors, are common to curators of vacant estates, subject to the following reservations.

###### Article 929

Creditors must declare their claim to the curator, by notifying him of their title, within nine months.  
The curator establishes a draft settlement of liabilities respecting the order provided for in Article 922, with costs related to the administration of the curatorship being paid before other claims. The curator may only provide for payment of estate debts up to the amount of the assets.  

The curator may however pay, without waiting for the draft settlement of liabilities, costs necessary for the preservation of the patrimony, funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other estate debts whose settlement is urgent.

###### Article 930

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed with the registry of the Court of First Instance which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904.

###### Article 931

Creditors who are not fully satisfied in view of this draft may, within one month of publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in order to challenge the settlement draft.  
Those who have not declared their claim after submission of the draft may only claim the remaining assets. In case of insufficiency of these assets, they have recourse only against legatees who have been satisfied in their rights. This recourse is prescribed after one year from the realization of all remaining assets.

###### Article 932

In the absence of recourse against the draft or after the president's decision has become final, the curator proceeds with the final realization of the remaining assets.  
Any surplus is remitted upon their request to heirs who would come forward, if they are within the useful time limit to claim the estate.  

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the estate is opened, seized by the curator, sends the State into possession of the estate.

#### Chapter VI. On Partition

##### Section I: On the Legal Regime of Co-ownership

###### § 1. General Provisions Article 933

Co-ownership arises when several persons have a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of property. This right may be ownership or another dismembered real right.  
Co-ownership does not have legal personality.  
Each co-owner has a right over the undivided property shared with the others. The extent of each person's rights in the co-ownership is defined by the law or the agreement that gives rise to it. In the absence of another title, it results from a certificate of notoriety or an inventory heading established by the notary.

###### Article 934

Each co-owner holds title to his share. However, when a co-owner intends to transfer all or part of his undivided rights, for consideration and to a person outside the co-ownership, the other co-owners have a right of pre-emption.  
Any proposed transfer must be notified in advance to the other co-owners, with all useful information, such as the price, the conditions of the transfer and the identifying elements of the purchaser. This notification, made by extra-judicial act, opens a period of one month for the co-owners to bring to the knowledge of the transferring co-owner their decision to exercise their right of pre-emption under the conditions brought to their knowledge.  
The person who decides to pre-empt has two months to complete the transfer, from the sending of his decision to the transferring co-owner. After this period, he is given formal notice to respond and, if he remains silent for fifteen days, his declaration of pre-emption is null and void by operation of law, without prejudice to damages that may be claimed by the transferor.  

When the transferor has granted payment terms and, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property that has fallen to him has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion, unless the parties exclude this variation.

###### Article 935

When a creditor seizes all or part of the rights of a co-owner in the co-ownership with a view to subjecting them to a forced sale, there is no right of pre-emption but a right of substitution for the successful bidder. The lawyer of the pursuing creditor or the notary notifies all the other co-owners one month before the scheduled date of the sale. The latter have a period of one month from the adjudication to substitute themselves for the purchaser.  
This right is exercised by declaration at the registry of the Court of First Instance or with the notary in charge of the sale. It is recorded in the schedule of conditions of sale established for the sale.

###### Article 936

For both amicable and forced transfers, compliance with the notification and time limit rules is prescribed on pain of nullity of the transaction. This nullity, of private interest, is available for five years to the persons

to whom the notifications should have been made or to their heirs.  

The notifications provided for by the two articles and the preceding paragraph must be addressed to every bare owner and to every usufructuary. But a usufructuary may acquire a share in bare ownership only if no bare owner comes forward as purchaser; a bare owner may acquire a share in usufruct only if no usufructuary comes forward as purchaser.

###### § 2. On the Management Rules of Co-ownership Article 937

In co-ownership, decisions are made unanimously, subject to the following reservations.

###### Article 938

When they fall within the normal operation of undivided property, decisions concerning the following may be made by the holders of two-thirds of the undivided rights:
1° Acts of administration of undivided property;  
2° The designation of a co-owner or a third party as holder of a general administration mandate;  
3° The conclusion and renewal of leases other than those relating to property for agricultural, commercial, industrial or artisanal use;  
4° The decision to sell movable undivided property when this transaction is necessary for the payment of debts and charges of the co-ownership. The sale of undivided property outside this purpose requires unanimity, except by judicial authorization.

###### Article 939

Except in the case of dismemberment of ownership of the property or if one of the co-owners is in one of the cases provided for in Article 863, the alienation of undivided property may be authorized by the Court of First Instance, at the request of one or more co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the undivided rights, according to the conditions and procedures defined in the following paragraphs.  
The co-owner or co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the undivided rights express before a notary, by this majority, their intention to proceed with the alienation of the undivided property. Within the month that follows, the notary has this intention served on the other co-owners.  
In the absence of opposition within three months of service, the decision to alienate the undivided property is confirmed, unless the service provided for in the second paragraph has not been made. In the event of opposition, the Court of First Instance may authorize the alienation of the undivided property if it does not cause excessive harm to the rights of the other co-owners.  

This alienation is carried out by licitation. The sums derived therefrom may not be reinvested except to pay the debts and charges of the co-ownership.

###### Article 940

Any co-owner may take the measures necessary for the preservation of undivided property, even if there is no urgency.  
These conservatory acts may be of a material nature, such as an occasional maintenance act, or legal, such as formal notice to a debtor in default. They may be directed both against another co-owner and against a third party to the co-ownership.  

The co-owner may use for this purpose the funds of the co-ownership held by him and he is deemed to have free disposal thereof with regard to third parties.  

In the absence of funds of the co-ownership, he may oblige his co-owners to make the necessary expenditures with him.  

When undivided property is encumbered with a usufruct, these powers are enforceable against the usufructuary to the extent that the latter is liable for repairs.

###### Article 941

Co-owners may give a mandate to one or more of them or to a third party to perform a specific act, which forms a special mandate, or even to take care of all the affairs of the co-ownership, which is a general mandate. The general mandate permits only acts of administration.  
If one of the co-owners or a third party takes the initiative to manage the undivided property with the knowledge of the others and without opposition on their part, he is deemed to have received a tacit mandate. This mandate permits only acts of administration; it covers neither acts of disposition nor the conclusion or renewal of leases.  

The co-owner who manages one or more undivided properties is responsible for his management. He is entitled to remuneration for his activity under the conditions fixed amicably or, failing that, by judicial decision.  
If a co-owner or a third party performs an act useful to the co-ownership without the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraphs being met, he undertakes to continue his management in accordance with the rules governing management of affairs.

###### Article 942

When the situation does not allow for the granting of a mandate, a co-owner may seek judicial authorization:
1° When another co-owner is unable to express his or her will: the applicant co-owner may be authorized by the court to represent him or her, both generally and for certain particular acts. The court shall then determine the conditions and extent of the representation;  
2° In case of refusal by one of the co-owners to give consent to an act deemed necessary by the applicant, when such refusal jeopardizes the common interest. However, it is not within the power of the judge to authorize the sale in full ownership requested by a bare owner when the usufructuary opposes it;  
3° For all urgent measures required by the common interest.  
In cases 2° and 3°, authorization is sought before the President of the Court of First Instance who is seized and rules in summary proceedings. The President may, in particular, authorize a co-owner to collect from debtors of the undivided estate or from depositaries of undivided funds a provision intended to meet urgent needs, prescribing, if necessary, the conditions of use. This authorization does not entail assumption of capacity for the surviving spouse or for the heir. He may also either appoint a co-owner as administrator, requiring him if necessary to provide security, or appoint a sequestrator, or prohibit the removal of movable property except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or another of the beneficiaries, on condition that they provide security if he deems it necessary.

###### Article 943

When an undivided immovable property for residential use or for mixed residential and professional use is vacant or has not been effectively occupied for more than two calendar years, a co-owner may be authorized in court to carry out improvement, rehabilitation and restoration works on the property as well as to perform acts of administration and publicity formalities, having as sole purpose to lease it as a principal residence.

###### Article 944

To this end, a co-owner may seize the President of the Court of First Instance, so that he may appoint him as mandatary. The President sets the duration of his mission as well as his remuneration. At the request of the appointed co-owner, the President may extend this mission for a period he determines.  

The appointment decision is registered and published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 945

Within the limits of the powers conferred upon him, the appointed co-owner represents all co-owners for the acts provided for in Article 943. He exercises his powers even when there is a minor or a protected adult among the other co-owners.  
The acts he performs within the framework of his mission have no effect on the hereditary option of the co-owner appointed as mandatary.

###### Article 946

At the request of any interested person or the public prosecutor, the President may remove the mandatary from his mission in case of characterized breach in the exercise thereof. The President then appoints another mandatary, for a period he defines.

###### Article 947

Each heir may require the mandatary to consult, at any time, documents relating to the performance of his mission.  
Each year and at the end of his mission, the mandatary submits to the judge and to each heir upon request a report on the performance of his mission.  
The mission ceases automatically by the effect of an undivided ownership agreement that would be signed between the heirs or by the signing of the partition deed. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the succession mandatary.

###### § 3. Rights and obligations of co-owners Article 948

Each co-owner has the same right of use and enjoyment over undivided property as the others. The co-owners regulate the distribution of this right among themselves. It is possible for them to grant to a co-owner an exclusive right of use or enjoyment over the property, in exchange for compensation.  

In the absence of agreement on the use of undivided property, the President of the court settles the matter on a provisional basis. He is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 949

Each person is entitled to the benefits of undivided property and bears the losses in proportion to his or her rights in the undivided estate. However, no claim relating to fruits and revenues shall be admissible more than five years after the date on which they were received or could have been received.  
Any person who receives revenues or incurs expenses on behalf of the undivided estate must keep a record thereof which is available to the co-owners.  

The fruits and revenues benefit the entire undivided estate; however, they may, by express agreement, be attributed to one of the co-owners.  
Any co-owner may request his or her annual share in the benefits. In case of disagreement, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance rules taking into account the extent of each person's rights in the undivided estate.

###### Article 950

Are automatically undivided, by the effect of real subrogation, claims and indemnities that replace undivided property, as well as property acquired, with the consent of all co-owners, in employment or re-employment of undivided property.

###### Article 951

When a co-owner has improved at his or her own expense the condition of undivided property, it must be taken into account according to equity, having regard to the amount by which the value of the property is increased at the time of partition or alienation. He or she must likewise be credited for necessary expenses incurred from his or her personal funds for the preservation of said property, even though they did not improve them.  
Conversely, the co-owner is liable for degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of undivided property by his or her act or fault.

###### § 4. Right of pursuit of creditors Article 952

Creditors of the undivided estate, who are those who could have acted on the undivided property before there was an undivided estate and those whose claim arose from the fact of management of the undivided estate or acts of preservation of which they were the authors, shall be paid from the assets of the undivided estate before any partition and, if the undivided estate should not suffice to satisfy them in their rights, they may act against each of the co-owners. The latter are jointly and severally liable for the balance. Creditors of the undivided estate may also pursue the seizure and sale of undivided property.  

Personal creditors of a co-owner may not seize either the undivided property or their debtor's share. On the other hand, they may provoke partition in the name of their debtor or intervene in the partition that the latter would have provoked. The co-owners, however, have the power to stop the course of the partition action by discharging the obligation owed by the debtor. Those who exercise this option shall reimburse themselves by deduction from the undivided property.

###### § 5. Petitions for partition Article 953

No one may be compelled to remain in undivided ownership and partition may always be provoked, except by judgment or contrary agreement.  

Co-owners who hold a title of ownership, bare ownership or usufruct may agree to remain in undivided ownership for a limited time: this agreement cannot be binding beyond five years; but it may be renewed. Conventional undivided ownership is subject to the rules of Articles 2071 and following.

###### Article 954

When several undivided estates exist exclusively between the same persons, whether they relate to the same property or to different property, a single partition may take place.

###### Article 955

Partition may be requested even when one of the co-heirs has separately enjoyed all or part of the undivided property, if there has been no act of partition, or sufficient possession to acquire prescription when it is permitted.

###### Article 956

If a minor, an adult under guardianship or curatorship, or a presumed absentee, is called to a partition, the latter may be done amicably.

In this case, the judge authorizes the partition, even partial, and designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence as the case may be of the representative or curator of the person referred to in the preceding paragraph or, if that person is themselves interested in the partition, of their replacement designated in accordance with Article 143. The liquidation statement is submitted to the approval of the judge.
The partition may also be done in court in accordance with the provisions of Articles 981 and following. Failing to meet these conditions, the amicable partition is considered as provisional.

###### Article 957

A spouse may not, without the consent of the other, proceed with the partition of property devolved to the latter which falls into the community. Any partition which he or she proceeds with alone, as to such property, is valid only as a provisional partition.

###### Article 958

The co-owner in usufruct may request the partition in kind of the undivided usufruct; if this partition in kind among the different usufructuaries is not possible, the usufruct may be sold.
When the sale of the usufruct alone cannot be envisaged under satisfactory conditions for the usufructuaries, the sale may relate to the full ownership provided that it appears to be the only measure that can preserve the interests of all holders of rights over the undivided property.

###### Article 959

The same power belongs to the co-owner in bare ownership for the undivided bare ownership. But in case of sale of the full ownership, when the property is encumbered with a usufruct, this may not operate against the will of the usufructuary.

###### Article 960

When a person is in co-ownership both over the usufruct and over the bare ownership, he or she has the powers provided for in the two preceding articles. The contrary will of a usufructuary, if he or she requests the sale of the property in full ownership, may not be opposed to him or her.

###### Article 961

When all parties agree on the partition, it is amicable; if one of the co-heirs refuses to consent to the partition, or if disputes arise either on the manner of proceeding with it, or on the manner of completing it, the partition is judicial.

###### § 6. Preferential Allocations Article 962
