Except for a decision or agreement to maintain the co-ownership, preferential allocation may be granted to the spouse or to any heir called to succeed by virtue of the law, whether he or she is a co-owner in full ownership or in bare ownership, under the conditions provided for by the following provisions.
These provisions also benefit the heir having a universal or universal title vocation to the succession by virtue of a will or a contractual institution.

###### Article 963

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation by way of partition, subject to an equalizing payment if applicable, of any enterprise, or part of an agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise or undivided share of such an enterprise, even formed in part from property of which he or she was already owner or co-owner before the death, in the operation of which he or she participates or has effectively participated. In the case of the heir, the condition

of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants.

If applicable, the request for preferential allocation may relate to company shares, without prejudice to the application of legal provisions or statutory clauses on the continuation of a company with the surviving spouse or one or more heirs.

###### Article 964

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may also request preferential allocation:
1° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises which effectively serve as his or her dwelling, if he or she had his or her residence there at the time of death, and of the furniture furnishing it, as well as of the deceased's vehicle provided that this vehicle is necessary for him or her for the needs of daily life. This preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
2° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises for professional use effectively serving for the exercise of his or her profession and of the movable objects for professional use furnishing these premises;
3° Of the ownership of any agricultural holding whose size in surface area makes it a family holding. Preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
4° Of all the movable elements necessary for the operation of a rural property cultivated by the deceased in a professional capacity, when the lease continues for the benefit of the applicant, or when a new lease is granted to the latter.
The rights resulting from preferential allocation do not prejudice the life rights of habitation and use, or enjoyment, which the spouse may exercise by virtue of the law or a contract.

###### Article 965

If maintenance in co-ownership has not been ordered and in the absence of preferential allocation in ownership, provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request the preferential allocation of all or part of the immovable property and rights with an agricultural purpose dependent on the succession with a view to constituting, with one or more co-heirs and, where applicable, one or more third parties, an agricultural land grouping.
This allocation is by right if the surviving spouse or one or more of the co-heirs meeting the personal conditions provided for in Articles 963 and 964, require that all or part of the property of the grouping be leased to them.

In case of multiple requests, the property of the grouping may, if its consistency permits, be the subject of several leases benefiting different co-heirs; otherwise, and in the absence of amicable agreement, the court designates the lessee taking into account the aptitude of the different applicants to manage the property concerned and to remain there. If the clauses and conditions of this lease or these leases have not been the subject of an agreement, they are fixed by the court.
The immovable property and rights that the applicants do not envisage contributing to the agricultural land grouping, as well as the other property of the succession, are allocated by priority, within the limits of their respective succession rights, to the co-owners who have not consented to the formation of the grouping. If these co-owners are not satisfied with their rights by the allocation thus made, an equalizing payment must be paid to them. Except for amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the equalizing payment if any due is payable within the year following the partition. It may be the subject of a payment in kind in the form of shares of the agricultural land grouping, unless the interested parties, within the month following the proposal made to them, have made known their opposition to this method of settlement.

The partition is perfect only after the signature of the constitutive act of the agricultural land grouping and, if applicable, of the long-term lease or leases.

###### Article 966

If an agricultural holding constituting an economic unit and not operated in corporate form is not maintained in indivision and has not been the subject of a preferential allocation under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir who wishes to continue the operation in which he participates or has effectively participated may require, notwithstanding any application for sale by auction, that the partition be concluded on the condition that his co-partitioners grant him a long-term lease on the lands of the holding that fall to them. In the case of the heir, the condition of participation may be or may have been fulfilled by his spouse or his descendants. Except by amicable agreement between the parties, the person who requests to benefit from these provisions receives as a priority in his share the farm and residential buildings.  
The foregoing provisions are applicable to a part of the agricultural holding that may constitute an economic unit. This economic unit may be formed, in part, from property of which the surviving spouse or the heir was already owner or co-owner before the death.  

Account shall be taken, if applicable, of the depreciation due to the existence of the lease in the valuation of the lands included in the different lots.  
If, by reason of the manifest unfitness of the applicant or applicants to manage all or part of the holding, the interests of the co-heirs are likely to be compromised, the court may decide that there is no ground to apply the first three paragraphs of this article.

###### Article 967

In the absence of amicable agreement, the application for preferential allocation is brought before the court, which rules, unless otherwise provided, according to the interests involved.  
Preferential allocation may be requested jointly by several successors in order to preserve the undivided property together.  
In the event of a plurality of conflicting applications concerning a holding or an enterprise, the court designates the attributee or joint attributees according to the interests involved and the aptitude of the different applicants to manage this holding or this enterprise and to maintain themselves therein and in particular the duration of their personal participation in the activity of the holding or the enterprise.

###### Article 968

The property subject to the allocation is valued at its value on the day of partition.  

Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, any balance due is payable in cash. However, when the attributee is the surviving spouse, he may require from his co-partitioners for the payment of a fraction of the balance, equal at most to one-half, time periods not exceeding ten years. Unless otherwise agreed, the sums remaining due bear interest at the legal rate.  

In the event of sale of the whole of the allocated property, the fraction of the balance remaining due becomes immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-partitioners and credited against the fraction of the balance still due.

###### Article 969

The beneficiary of the preferential allocation becomes exclusive owner of the allocated property only on the day of the final partition.  
Until that date, he may renounce the allocation only when the value of the property, as determined on the day of that allocation, has increased by more than one quarter on the day of partition independently of his personal act.

###### § 7. Of the constitution of shares and lots and of partition

A.	Common provisions

###### Article 970

The partitionable mass comprises the property existing at the opening of the succession, or that which has been subrogated thereto, and of which the deceased has not disposed by reason of death, as well as the fruits relating thereto.  
It is increased by the values subject to collation or reduction, as well as by the debts of the co-partitioners towards the deceased or towards the indivision.

###### Article 971

The partition of undivided property is effected per capita. However, it is done per stirpes when there is ground for representation. Once the partition per stirpes has been effected, within each stirps, the partition is done, where applicable, per capita among the heirs of each stirps.  
When a person dies, his heirs come to the succession of the person from whom he would have inherited if he had not died before him. The heirs come by representation of their author. Thus, grandchildren succeed to their grandparents by representation of their predeceased father or mother. These heirs by representation constitute "a stirps".

###### Article 972

When the debtor of a balance has obtained time periods for payment, and when, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property placed in his lot has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion.  
The parties may however agree that the amount of the balance shall not vary.

###### Article 973

Any person, even related to the deceased, who is not his successor, and to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, may be excluded from the partition, either by all his co-heirs, or by one alone, by reimbursing him the price of the transfer.  
This power granted to the co-heirs or to one of them to exclude from the partition any person not a successor to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, also belongs to the undivided co-owner of an immovable, to the superficiary for the acquisition of the land, and to the owner of the land, for the acquisition of the superficies; any redemption without distinction must be exercised within a period of three months from the day the sale was made public.

###### Article 974

In the formation and composition of lots with a view to partition, one must avoid fragmenting the lands and dividing the economic units and other sets of property whose division would entail depreciation.  

B.	Amicable partition

###### Article 975

Amicable partition may be total or partial. It is partial when it leaves the indivision subsisting with regard to certain property or certain persons.

###### Article 976

If all the co-owners are present and capable, the partition may take place in the form and according to the modalities chosen by the parties.  
When the indivision relates to property subject to land registration, the deed of partition is executed by notarial deed.

###### Article 977

If a co-owner is presumed absent or, as a result of remoteness, is unable to manifest his will, an amicable partition may take place under the conditions provided for in article 146.  
Likewise, if a co-owner is subject to a protective regime, an amicable partition may take place in compliance with the provisions of the titles Of minority, guardianship and emancipation and Of majority and adults protected by law.

###### Article 978

If a co-owner is in default, without however being in one of the cases provided for in the preceding article, he may, at the instance of a co-partitioner, be formally notified, by extrajudicial act, to be represented at the amicable partition.  
Should this co-owner fail to have appointed a representative within three months of the formal notice, a co-partitioner may request the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to designate any qualified person who shall represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the partition. This person may consent to the partition only with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 979

The co-owners compose the lots at their convenience, and agree on the distribution of the lots among themselves. Failing that, once the lots are constituted they shall be drawn by lot.  
Each lot must, as far as possible, be composed, either in whole or in part, of movables or immovables, rights or claims of equivalent value, subject to respect for the proportion of each person's rights in the undivided ownership. In case of inequality of the constituted lots, this inequality is compensated, either by annuity or in money.  

The equality of all in the partition, understood as the rights that each holds proportionally in the undivided ownership, is a rule of public policy.

###### Article 980

The co-owners freely proceed with the valuations of the value of the undivided rights and property.  

The property is valued at its value on the date of divided enjoyment, taking into account, where applicable, the charges encumbering it. The determination of the day corresponding to the divided enjoyment of the property by the co-owners is the subject of a special clause in the deed of partition.  

The date selected must be as close as possible to the partition. However, the judge may set the divided enjoyment at an earlier date if the choice of that date appears more favorable to the achievement of equality.  

C.	Judicial partition

###### Article 981

The partition is made in court when one of the co-owners refuses to consent to the amicable partition or if disputes arise over the manner of proceeding with it or completing it or when the amicable partition has not been authorized or approved in one of the cases provided for in articles 977 and 978.  
In these cases, the affixing of seals on the effects of the succession carried out as soon as possible, either at the request of the heirs, or at the initiative of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance, or ex officio by the judge of the court within whose jurisdiction the succession is opened.

###### Article 982

Creditors may also request the affixing of seals, by virtue of an enforceable title or a permission from the judge.

###### Article 983

When the seal has been affixed, all creditors may form opposition to it, even if they have neither an enforceable title nor permission from the judge. The formalities for the removal of seals and the preparation of the inventory are governed by the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 984

The action for partition and the disputes that arise, either in connection with the maintenance of undivided ownership, or during partition operations, are submitted to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear them. Any other judge must raise ex officio his lack of jurisdiction.  
It is before this court that sales by auction are carried out and that applications relating to the warranty of lots between co-partitioners and those for nullity of the partition or for supplement of share must be brought.

###### Article 985

If it considers that the settlement of the partition is simple, the court orders the partition; if it appears complex to it, it appoints, on the one hand, a notary to carry out the partition operations and, on the other hand and from within itself, a judge to supervise these operations.  
The notary certifies the property rights of each, establishes the accounts of the undivided ownership, forms the mass to be partitioned and constitutes the lots.  

If the appointed notary encounters the inertia of a co-owner, he serves formal notice on him, by extrajudicial act, to be represented. Failing the co-owner to have appointed an agent within three months of the formal notice, the notary requests, without formality, the judge who appointed him to appoint any qualified person who will represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the operations.

###### Article 986

A co-owner may request that certain property be attributed to him preferentially. In case of opposition from another co-owner, the difficulty is settled by the judge responsible for supervising the operations. This judge, for property that cannot be easily partitioned or attributed, orders the sale by auction of said property, under the conditions he determines.

###### Article 987

When the lots are constituted, each co-partitioner is admitted to propose his claims against their formation.  
When the claims are removed or settled by the judge, the notary proposes to the co-partitioners to agree on the allocation of the lots. Failing that, a drawing by lot is carried out.

###### Article 988

At any time, the co-partitioners may abandon the judicial route to pursue the partition amicably if the conditions provided for a partition of this nature are met.

###### § 8. Judicial maintenance in undivided ownership Article 989

At the request of a co-owner, the court may stay the partition for up to two years if its immediate completion risks harming the value of the undivided property or if one of the co-owners cannot take over the agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or liberal enterprise dependent on the

succession until the expiration of this period. This stay may apply to all of the undivided property or to only some of it.  

If necessary, the request for stay of partition may relate to company shares.

###### Article 990

In the absence of amicable agreement, the judge may order the maintenance of undivided ownership of any agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or liberal enterprise, the operation of which was ensured by the deceased or by his spouse, as well as residential or professional premises actually used by the deceased or his spouse, and movable objects furnishing the residential premises or used in the exercise of the profession.  
If necessary, the request for maintenance of undivided ownership may relate to company shares.

###### Article 991

In all these cases, when there is one or more minor descendants, the request may be presented by the surviving spouse, by any heir or by the legal representative of the minor heirs; if there are no minor descendants, the action belongs to the surviving spouse alone.  
Two conditions are then added: the surviving spouse must have had the status of co-owner of the property in question, whether this status was prior to the death or linked to it, and, in the case of residential premises, this surviving spouse must have resided in the premises at the time of death.

###### Article 992

The court rules according to the interests at stake and the means of subsistence that the family can derive from the undivided property.  
It may order the maintenance of undivided ownership for up to five years, renewable as the case may be until the death of the surviving spouse and until the majority of the youngest of the descendants.

###### Article 993

When only one co-owner requests the partition, the court may, at the request of one or more of the co-owners who intend on the contrary to remain in undivided ownership, according to the interests at stake and without prejudice to the application of articles 962 and following of this code, attribute after expert appraisal his share to the one who requested the partition, either in kind if this share is easily detachable from the rest of the undivided property, or in value.  
If there is not a sufficient sum in the undivided ownership, the balance is paid by those of the co-owners who concurred in the request, without prejudice to the possibility for the other co-owners to participate in it, if they express the wish. The share of each in the undivided ownership is increased in proportion to his payment.

##### Section II

On collation, imputation and reduction of gifts made to successors Article 994
Every heir, even having accepted the succession subject to inventory, coming to a succession, must bring into hotchpot to his coheirs everything he has received from the deceased, by inter vivos gifts, directly or indirectly; he may not retain gifts made to him by the deceased, unless they were expressly made to him in addition to his share of the succession.

Legacies made to an heir are deemed made in addition to his share of the succession, unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, in which case the legatee may only claim his legacy by taking less.

###### Article 995

Gifts made in addition to the share of the succession may not be retained nor legacies claimed by the heir coming to partition except up to the amount of the disposable portion: the excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 996

The heir who renounces the succession may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer has expressly required collation in case of renunciation.
In this case, collation is made in value. When the value brought into hotchpot exceeds the rights he should have had in the partition had he participated, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs up to the amount of this excess.

###### Article 997

The donee who was not a presumptive heir at the time of the gift, but who is found to be a successor on the day of the opening of the succession, does not owe collation, unless the donor has expressly required it.

###### Article 998

Gifts and legacies made to the son or daughter of one who is found to be a successor at the time of the opening of the succession are always deemed made with dispensation from collation.
The father or mother coming to the succession of the donor is not required to bring them into hotchpot.

###### Article 999

Similarly, the son or daughter coming in his own right to the succession of the donor is not required to bring into hotchpot the gift made to his father or mother, even when he has accepted the succession; but if this child comes only by representation, he must bring into hotchpot what had been given to his father or mother, even in the case where he has renounced his succession.

###### Article 1000

Gifts and legacies made to the spouse of a successor spouse are deemed made with dispensation from collation.

If gifts and legacies are made jointly to two spouses, of whom only one is a successor, the latter brings into hotchpot half; if the gifts are made to the successor spouse, he brings them into hotchpot in full.

###### Article 1001

Collation is made only to the succession of the donor.

###### Article 1002

Collation is owed for what has been used for the establishment of one of the coheirs or for the payment of his debts.
It is also owed in case of gift of fruits or revenues, unless the gift was made expressly in addition to the share of the succession.

###### Article 1003

Expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, need not be brought into hotchpot, unless the disposer has expressed a contrary intention.
The character of a customary gift is assessed at the date when it is granted and taking into account the fortune of the disposer.

###### Article 1004

The same applies to profits that the heir may have derived from agreements entered into with the deceased, if these agreements presented no indirect advantage when they were made.

###### Article 1005

Similarly, no collation is owed for partnerships formed without fraud between the deceased and one of his heirs, when the conditions thereof were settled by an authentic act.

###### Article 1006

Property that has perished by fortuitous event and without fault of the donee is not subject to collation.
However, if this property has been reconstituted by means of compensation received by reason of its loss, the donee must bring it into hotchpot in the proportion in which the compensation was used for its reconstitution.

If the compensation has not been used for this purpose, it is itself subject to collation.

###### Article 1007

The fruits of things subject to collation are owed only from the day of the opening of the succession. Interest is owed only from the day when the amount of collation is determined.

###### Article 1008

Collation is owed only by the coheir to his coheir; it is not owed to legatees or to creditors of the succession.

###### Article 1009

Collation is made by taking less, thus the donee retains the property received but takes, in return, less than the others in the mass to be partitioned in order to restore equality in figures, except in the case of the second paragraph of Article 996.
It may not be required in kind except by contrary stipulation in the deed of gift.

In the case of such a stipulation, alienations and constitutions of real rights granted by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of collation unless the donor has consented thereto.

###### Article 1010

The heir also has the option of bringing into hotchpot in kind the donated property that still belongs to him provided that this property is free of any charge or occupation with which it had not already been encumbered at the time of the gift.

###### Article 1011

Collation is owed for the value of the donated property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of the gift.
If the property has been alienated before partition, account is taken of the value it had at the time of alienation. If new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, account is taken of the value of this new property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, no account is taken of the subrogation.
All subject to contrary stipulation in the deed of gift.

If it results from such a stipulation that the value subject to collation is less than the determined value of the property, this difference forms an indirect advantage acquired by the donee in addition to his share of the succession.

###### Article 1012

Collation of a sum of money is equal to its amount. However, if it has been used to acquire property, collation is owed for the value of this property, under the conditions provided in the preceding article.

###### Article 1013

When collation is made in kind and the condition of the donated objects has been improved by the act of the donee, account must be taken thereof, having regard to the amount by which their value is increased at the time of partition or alienation.
Account must likewise be taken to the donee of necessary expenses he has incurred for the preservation of the property, even though they have not improved it.

###### Article 1014

The coheir who makes collation in kind may retain possession of the donated property until actual reimbursement of the sums owed to him for expenses or improvements.

###### Article 1015

The donee, for his part, must, in case of collation in kind, account for degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of the donated property by his act or by his fault.

##### Section III: On payment of debts

###### § 1. On debts of copartitioners Article 1016

When the mass to be partitioned includes a claim against one of the copartitioners, whether due or
not, the latter is allotted it in the partition up to the amount of his rights in the mass.

Up to that amount, the debt is extinguished by merger. If its amount exceeds the debtor's rights in this mass, he owes payment of the balance under the conditions and time limits that affected the obligation.

###### Article 1017

Except when it relates to undivided property, the claim is not due before the closing of partition operations. However, the debtor heir may decide at any time to discharge it voluntarily.

###### Article 1018

Amounts subject to collation bear interest at the legal rate, unless otherwise stipulated.

Such interest runs from the opening of the succession when the heir was a debtor thereof to the deceased and from the day the debt becomes due, when it arose during the indivision.

###### Article 1019

When the co-sharer himself has a claim to assert, he is only allotted his debt if, after balancing, the account shows a balance in favour of the undivided estate.

###### § 2. Des autres dettes Article 1020

Co-heirs contribute among themselves to the payment of debts and charges of the succession, each in proportion to what he takes therein.

###### Article 1021

The legatee by general title contributes with the heirs, in proportion to his emolument; but the particular legatee is not liable for debts and charges, except however for the hypothecary action on the immovable bequeathed.

###### Article 1022

When immovables of a succession are encumbered with annuities by special hypothec, each of the co-heirs may require that the annuities be redeemed and the immovables rendered free before proceeding to the formation of lots.
If the co-heirs divide the succession in the state in which it is found, the encumbered immovable must be valued at the same rate as the other immovables; deduction is made of the capital of the annuity from the total price; the heir in whose lot this immovable falls remains solely charged with the service of the annuity and he must guarantee his co-heirs therefor.

###### Article 1023

Heirs are liable for the debts and charges of the succession, personally for their successoral share, and hypothecarily for the whole; subject to their recourse either against their co-heirs or against the universal legatees, by reason of the share for which they must contribute thereto.

###### Article 1024

The particular legatee who has discharged the debt with which the bequeathed immovable was encumbered remains subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the heirs and successors by general title.

###### Article 1025

The co-heir or successor by general title who, by the effect of the hypothec, has paid beyond his share of the common debt, has recourse against the other co-heirs or successors by general title only for the share that each of them must personally bear, even in the case where the co-heir who paid the debt has been subrogated to the rights of the creditors; without prejudice nevertheless to the rights of a co-heir who, by the effect of the benefit of inventory, has retained the faculty to claim payment of his personal claim, like any other creditor.

###### Article 1026

In case of insolvency of one of the co-heirs or successors by general title, his share in the hypothecary debt is apportioned among all the others, proportionally.

###### Article 1027

Executory titles against the deceased are likewise executory against the heir personally, eight days after service of such titles has been made upon him.

###### Article 1028

Creditors of the deceased and legatees of sums of money may demand to be preferred on the successoral assets over any personal creditor of the heir.
Reciprocally, personal creditors of the heir may demand to be preferred over any creditor of the deceased on the property of the heir not received by way of the succession.

The right of preference gives rise to the privilege on immovables provided for in article 2354, and it is subject to registration.

###### Article 1029

This right of preference may be exercised by any act by which a creditor manifests to the competing creditor his intention to be preferred on a determined property.
The right of preference may not be exercised when the claimant creditor has renounced it.

###### Article 1030

The right of preference is prescribed, with respect to movables, by the lapse of three years.

With respect to immovables, the action may be exercised as long as they exist in the hands of the heir.

###### Article 1031

Creditors of a co-sharer, to prevent the partition from being made in fraud of their rights, may oppose its being proceeded with outside their presence: they have the right to intervene therein at their expense; but they may not attack a completed partition, unless however it has been proceeded with without them and to the prejudice of an opposition they have filed.

##### Section IV : Des effets du partage et de la garantie des lots Article 1032

Each co-undivided owner is deemed to have succeeded alone and immediately to all the effects included in his lot, or fallen to him by licitation, and never to have had ownership of the other effects of the succession.
The same applies to property that has come to him by any other act having the effect of terminating the indivision. No distinction is made according to whether the act terminates the indivision in whole or in part, with respect to certain property or certain undivided co-owners only.
However, acts validly performed either by virtue of a mandate from the co-undivided owners or by virtue of a judicial authorization retain their effects whatever may be, upon partition, the allocation of the property that was the subject thereof.

###### Article 1033

Co-undivided owners remain respectively guarantors, one towards the other, for disturbances and evictions only that proceed from a cause prior to the partition. They are also guarantors for the insolvency of the debtor of a debt placed in the lot of a co-sharer, revealed before the partition.
The guarantee does not apply if the kind of eviction suffered has been excepted by a particular and express clause of the partition deed; it ceases if it is by his fault that the co-undivided owner suffers the eviction.

###### Article 1034

Each of the co-undivided owners is personally obliged, in proportion to his emolument, to indemnify the evicted co-undivided owner for the loss he has suffered. This loss is valued at the day of the eviction.
If one of the co-undivided owners is found to be insolvent, the portion for which he is liable must be equally apportioned between the guaranteed party and all the solvent co-undivided owners.

###### Article 1035

The action in guarantee is prescribed by two years from the eviction or the discovery of the disturbance.

##### Section V : Des actions en nullité du partage ou en complément de part

###### § 1. Des actions en nullité du partage Article 1036

Partition may be annulled for cause of violence or fraud.
It may also be annulled for cause of error, if the latter related to the existence or quotity of the rights of the co-sharers or to the ownership of property included in the divisible mass.

The action for nullity is prescribed by five years from the discovery of the defect or the cessation of the violence.

However, if it appears that the consequences of the violence, fraud or error can be remedied otherwise than by annulment of the partition, the court may, at the request of one of the parties, order a supplementary or corrective partition.

###### Article 1037

Partition may also be annulled if one of the co-undivided owners has been omitted therefrom.

The omitted co-undivided owner may however demand to receive his share, either in kind or in value, without annulment of the partition.
To determine this share, the property and rights over which the partition already carried out related are revalued in the same manner as if it were a new partition.

###### Article 1038

The co-sharer who has alienated his lot in whole or in part is no longer entitled to bring the action for nullity for error, fraud or violence, if the alienation he has made is subsequent to the discovery of the error or fraud or to the cessation of the violence.

###### § 2. Of the action for additional share Article 1039

Where one of the co-partitioners establishes, to his prejudice, a lesion of more than one quarter, the additional share is provided to him, at the choice of the defendant, either in cash or in kind.  

To determine whether there has been a lesion, the objects are valued according to their value at the time of the partition, which corresponds to the date of divided enjoyment.  
The action for additional share is prescribed after two years from the partition.

###### Article 1040

The action for additional share is admitted against any act which has as its object to terminate the indivision, independently of the qualification that the parties may have given to that act.  
But after the partition, or the act which takes its place, the action for additional share is no longer admitted against the transaction made on the difficulties presented by that partition or that act.

###### Article 1041

The action is not admitted against a sale of succession rights made without fraud to a co-owner by his co-owners or by one of them, where the assignment includes a contingency defined in the act and expressly accepted by the assignee.

###### Article 1042

The simple omission of an object of the succession gives rise to a supplementary partition relating to that property.

### Title II: Of gifts inter vivos and wills

Chapter I: General provisions Article 1043
A liberality is an act by which a person disposes gratuitously of all or part of his property or his rights for the benefit of another person.  

A liberality may take only the form of these two categories of acts which are the gift inter vivos and the will.

###### Article 1044

The gift inter vivos is an act by which a person, the donor, transfers gratuitously to another person, the donee, who accepts it, the ownership of a property.  
The donor may, without being deprived of his liberal intention, impose on the donee the obligation to perform a specified prestation; the act is then called a gift with charges.

###### Article 1045

The will is an act by which the testator disposes, for the time when he will no longer exist, of all or part of his property, in full ownership or in the form of any other real right. If it is not full ownership, the right transmitted is so only for the time provided in the act and in the absence of such provision, with regard to the legatee, the object of the legacy reverting, upon its extinction, to the succession of the testator.  
The will may be revoked by the testator, but the revocation is valid only insofar as it has been made by authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.  

The legacy may, after the death of the testator and at the latest two months after notification of the will to the legatee, be refused, totally or in part, by the latter or by his agent. The silence of the legatee during this period constitutes acceptance; if the legatee dies within this period, his heirs exercise the rights of their predecessor from the notification of the will made to them. The decision of the legatee is final, unless the heirs consent to his modifying it.

###### Article 1046

Any disposition by which a person is charged with preserving and returning to a third party produces effect only in the case where it is authorized by law.

###### Article 1047

The father and mother may impose on the child whom they gratify the charge of preserving and delivering the property received to his own children.  
A person without posterity may burden a liberality granted to his brothers or sisters with a charge imposing on them the transmission of the property received to their children and thus ensure the maintenance of the property in the family.  
However, clauses of inalienability affecting a property given or bequeathed are valid only if they are temporary and justified by a serious and legitimate interest. Even in this case, the donee or legatee may be judicially authorized to dispose of the property if the interest which had justified the clause has disappeared or if it happens that a more important interest requires it.  

The provisions of this article do not prejudice liberalities granted to legal persons or even to natural persons charged with constituting legal persons.  

Any clause by which the disposer deprives of the liberality the one who would challenge the validity of a clause of inalienability or request authorization to alienate is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1048

Any gratified person may request that the conditions and charges burdening the donations or legacies he has received be judicially revised, when, as a result of a change of circumstances, the execution thereof has become for him either extremely difficult or seriously harmful.  

The application for revision is made by principal action; it may also be made by counterclaim, in response to the action for execution or revocation that the heirs of the disposer have brought. It is made against the heirs and, at the same time, against the public prosecutor if there is doubt as to the existence or identity of some of them; if there is no known heir, it is made against the public prosecutor. The latter must, in all cases, have communication of the matter.  

The application is admissible only ten years after the death of the disposer or, in case of successive applications, ten years after the judgment which ordered the previous revision. The gratified person must justify the diligence he has made, in the interval, to execute his obligations.

###### Article 1049

The judge seized of the application for revision may, according to the cases and even of his own motion, either reduce in quantity or periodicity the prestations burdening the liberality, or modify the object thereof by drawing inspiration from the intention of the disposer, or even group them together with analogous prestations resulting from other liberalities.  

He may authorize the alienation of all or part of the property which is the object of the liberality by ordering that the price thereof be employed for purposes in relation to the will of the disposer.  
He prescribes the measures appropriate to maintain, as far as possible, the appellation that the disposer had intended to give to his liberality.

###### Article 1050

Third-party opposition to the judgment granting the application for revision is admissible only in case of fraud attributable to the donee or legatee.  
The retraction or reformation of the judgment challenged does not give rise to any action against the third-party acquirer in good faith.

###### Article 1051

If, subsequent to the revision, the execution of the conditions or charges, as it was originally provided, becomes possible again, it may be requested by the heirs.

###### Article 1052

The clause by which the author of a liberality designates a beneficiary of second rank for the case where the beneficiary designated in the first place would have predeceased or, in case of survival, would refuse the liberality, is authorized.  
The same applies to the disposition inter vivos or testamentary by which the usufruct will be given to one and the bare ownership to the other.

###### Article 1053

In any disposition inter vivos or testamentary, impossible conditions, those which are contrary to laws or morals, shall be deemed unwritten.  
If the thing bequeathed perishes before the death of the disposer, or if it is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, nothing is owed to the donee or to the legatee. If only part of the thing bequeathed perishes or is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, the donee or the legatee receives the remainder.

#### Chapter II

On the capacity to dispose or receive by inter vivos gift or by will Article 1054
Any person may dispose and receive, either by inter vivos gift or by will, except for persons whom the law declares incapable. The author of such a liberality must be of sound mind. If

the gift or the will was made while consent was vitiated by error, fraud or duress, the act is null.  

A gift as well as a will made in favor of a foreigner is valid subject to the legal provisions in force.

###### Article 1055

A will made by a minor is valid, provided it is approved by the judge.

###### Article 1056

To be capable of receiving inter vivos, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the gift.  

To be capable of receiving by will, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the testator's death.  

Nevertheless, the gift or the will shall only take effect insofar as the child is born viable.  

When the testator dies before the delivery of the child already conceived at the date of the will and in whose favor the will was made, from the death of the testator until the delivery, the fruits shall be subject to conservatory measures.

###### Article 1057

A minor may not, even by will, dispose in favor of his guardian.  

A minor, having become of age or emancipated, may not dispose, either by inter vivos gift or by will, in favor of the person who was his guardian, if the final account of the guardianship has not been previously rendered and settled.  
Excepted, in the two cases above, are the ascendants of minors, who are or who have been their guardians.

###### Article 1058

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries who have provided care to a person during the illness from which he dies, may not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that he would have made in their favor during the course of that illness.  
Judicial representatives for the protection of adults and the legal persons on whose behalf they exercise their functions may not similarly benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that the persons whose protection they ensure would have made in their favor regardless of the date of the liberality.  

Excepted are:
1° Remunerative dispositions made on a particular basis, having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered;  
2° Universal dispositions, in the case of relationship up to and including the fourth degree, provided however that the deceased has no heirs in the direct line; unless the person in whose favor the disposition was made is himself among those heirs.  
The same rules shall be observed with regard to the minister of religion.

###### Article 1059

Inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of health establishments, medical-social establishments, or public utility establishments shall only take effect insofar as they have been authorized by decree.  

However, inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of foundations, places dedicated to worship and legally constituted associations and associations, are freely accepted by them. If it concerns religious establishments, the liberality is valid even if the disposer and the person receiving the property are not of the same faith.

###### Article 1060

Any disposition in favor of a person, natural or legal, subject to an incapacity to receive gratuitously, whether it is disguised in the form of an onerous contract, or whether it is made in the name of interposed persons is sanctioned by absolute nullity.  
Shall be deemed interposed persons, until proof to the contrary, the father and mother, the children and descendants, as well as the spouse of the incapable person.

#### Chapter III

On the hereditary reserve, the disposable portion, and reduction Section I: On the hereditary reserve and the disposable portion

###### Article 1061

The hereditary reserve is the share of property and succession rights of which the law ensures the devolution free of charges to certain heirs called reserve heirs, if they are called to the succession and if they accept it.  
The beneficiaries of the reserve are:	the descendants of the deceased, that is to say: the children, the grandchildren, the great-grandchildren;	in the absence of descendants, the ascendants of the deceased, that is to say: the father and mother, the grandparents, the great-grandparents;	the surviving spouse, in the absence of descendants and ascendants.  

The disposable portion is the share of property and succession rights that is not reserved by law and which the deceased was able to dispose of freely by liberalities.

###### Article 1062

Liberalities, whether by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed half of the disposer's property, if he leaves at his death only one child; one-third, if he leaves two children; one-quarter, if he leaves three or a greater number;  
A child who renounces the succession is included in the number of children left by the deceased only if he is represented or if he is bound to account for a liberality in application of the provisions of article 900.

###### Article 1063

Included in article 1062, under the name of children, are descendants in whatever degree, even though they should only be counted for the child whose place they take in the succession of the disposer.

###### Article 1064

Liberalities, by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed three-quarters of the property if, in the absence of descendants, the deceased leaves a surviving spouse, not divorced.

###### Article 1065

In the absence of a surviving spouse and heirs, liberalities by inter vivos or testamentary acts may exhaust the totality of the property.

###### Article 1066

If the liberality consists of a usufruct or a life annuity whose value exceeds the disposable portion, the heirs for whose benefit the law makes a reserve shall have the option either to execute this disposition or to make the abandonment of the ownership of the disposable portion.

##### Section II: On the reduction of excessive liberalities Article 1067

The value in full ownership of property alienated, either subject to a life annuity, or as a lost fund, or with reservation of usufruct to one of the successors in the direct line, is charged against the disposable portion. Such acts are requalified, irrefutably, as liberalities outside the succession share.  
Any excess is brought back to the mass and therefore gives rise to reduction of the excessive liberality. This charging and this reduction may only be requested by those of the other successors in the direct line who have not consented to these alienations.

###### Article 1068

The disposable portion may be given in whole or in part either by inter vivos act or by will, to the children or other successors of the donor, without being subject to accounting by the donee or the legatee coming to the succession, provided that with regard to gifts the disposition was made expressly outside the succession share.  
The declaration that the gift is outside the succession share may be made either by the act that will contain the disposition, or subsequently, in the form of inter vivos or testamentary dispositions.

###### Article 1069

Liberalities made as an advancement of succession share to a reserve heir who accepts the succession are charged against his reserve share and, subsidiarily, against the disposable portion, if it has not been otherwise agreed in the act that provides for them. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1070

Liberalities made as an advancement on succession share to a forced heir who renounces the succession are treated as a liberality made outside the succession share.  
However, when he is bound to bring into hotchpot pursuant to the provisions of Article 900, the heir who renounces is treated as an accepting heir for the notional reunion of all the property of the deceased, the imputation and, where applicable, the reduction of the liberality granted to him. This principle is derogated from for: life insurance premiums taken out for the benefit of a specified third party, unless they prove to be manifestly excessive having regard to the means of the insured or the transaction was purely an investment; expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, which need not be brought into hotchpot unless the disposer wills otherwise, in accordance with Article 1003; fruits and income accrued between the day of the donation and the death, in accordance with Article 1081.

###### Article 1071

A liberality made outside the succession share is imputed to the disposable portion. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1072

A liberality made to a successor, or to successors jointly, which exceeds the disposable portion, may be retained in full by the beneficiaries, whatever the excess, subject to compensating the co-heirs in money.  
Where the reducible portion does not exceed the reserve share of the person concerned, he may always claim all the bequeathed objects and thus execute the reduction in kind when the donated or bequeathed property still belongs to him and is free of any charge with which it was not already encumbered at the date of the liberality, as well as any occupation to which it was not already subject at that same date. This option expires if he does not express his choice for this method of reduction within three months from the date on which a forced heir gave him formal notice to take a position.

###### Article 1073

Where the value of inter vivos donations exceeds or equals the disposable portion, all testamentary dispositions shall lapse.

###### Article 1074

The reduction compensation is calculated, in all cases, according to the value of the objects at the time of partition or alienation by the beneficiary and according to their condition on the day the liberality took effect. If there has been subrogation, the calculation of the reduction compensation takes into account the value of the new property at the time of partition, according to their condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the

new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.  

The reduction compensation is payable at the time of partition, subject to agreement between the co-heirs. However, when the liberality has as its object one of the properties that may be the subject of a preferential attribution, time periods may be granted by the court, taking into account the interests involved, if they have not been granted by the disposer. The granting of these time periods may not, in any case, have the effect of deferring payment of the compensation beyond ten years from the opening of the succession. The provisions of Article 972 are then applicable to the payment of sums due.  
In the absence of agreement or stipulation to the contrary, these sums bear interest at the legal rate in civil matters. The advantages resulting from the time periods and payment terms granted do not constitute a liberality.  

In the event of sale of all of the donated or bequeathed property, the sums remaining due become immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-heirs and imputed to the sums still due.

###### Article 1075

Liberalities, direct or indirect, which exceed the disposable portion, are reducible to that portion upon the opening of the succession.

###### Article 1076

The reduction of inter vivos dispositions may only be requested by those for whose benefit the law makes the reserve, by their heirs or successors in title.  
Donees, legatees, and creditors of the deceased may not request this reduction, nor benefit from it.  
The limitation period for the action for reduction is set at five years from the opening of the succession, or two years from the day the heirs became aware of the infringement of their reserve, without ever being able to exceed ten years from the death.

###### Article 1077

The reduction is determined by forming a mass of all property existing at the death of the donor or testator.  
There are notionally reunited to it, after deducting debts, those of which he disposed by inter vivos donation according to their condition at the time of the donation and their value at the opening of the succession. If the property has been alienated, account is taken of its value at the time of alienation and, if there has been subrogation, of the value of the new property on the day of the opening of the succession according to their condition at the time of acquisition; however, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.  
There is calculated on all this property, having regard to the quality of heirs he leaves, what is the portion of which the deceased was able to dispose.

###### Article 1078

The reduction of inter vivos donations presupposes that the value of all property included in testamentary dispositions has previously been determined. Once the reunion of property has been carried out, the reduction is effected beginning with the last donation, and so on going back from the most recent to the oldest.

###### Article 1079

Where testamentary dispositions exceed either the disposable portion, or the portion of that portion which would remain after deducting the value of inter vivos donations, the reduction shall be made proportionally, without any distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies.

###### Article 1080

Nevertheless in all cases where the testator has expressly declared that he intends that a particular legacy be discharged in preference to others, this preference shall take place; and the legacy which is the object thereof shall only be reduced to the extent that the value of the others would not fill the legal reserve.

###### Article 1081

When the reduction is executed in kind, the donee restores the fruits of what exceeds the disposable portion, from the day of the death of the donor if the demand for reduction was made within the year; otherwise from the day of the demand.

###### Article 1082

Real rights created by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of the reduction. These rights shall nevertheless retain their effects when the donor consented thereto in the very act of creation or in a subsequent act. The donee shall then be liable for the resulting depreciation.

###### Article 1083

The action for reduction or revendication may be exercised by the heirs against third party holders of immovables forming part of the donations and alienated by the donees, in the same manner and in the same order as against the donees themselves, and after prior discussion of their property. This action must be exercised according to the order of dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent.  
Where the donor consented to the alienation with the agreement of all forced heirs born and living at the time thereof, the action may no longer be exercised against third party holders.

###### Article 1084

After prior discussion of the assets of the debtor of the reduction compensation and in case of insolvency of the latter, the forced heirs may exercise the action for reduction or revendication against third-party holders of immovable property forming part of the liberalities and alienated by the donee. The action is exercised in the same manner as against the donees themselves and according to the order of the dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. It may be exercised against third-party holders of movable property when article 2276 (number to be added when file no. 15 is numbered) cannot be invoked.  
When, on the day of the donation or subsequently, the donor and all the presumptive forced heirs have consented to the alienation of the donated property, no forced heir, even born after the consent of all the interested heirs has been obtained, may exercise the action against third-party holders. With regard to bequeathed property, this action may no longer be exercised when the forced heirs have consented to the alienation.

###### Article 1085

Any presumptive forced heir may renounce, totally or partially, for example targeting only the reduction of a liberality relating to a specific property, the exercise of an action for reduction in an unopened succession, in favour of one or more specified persons. The renunciation binds the renouncer only from the day it has been accepted by the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit; but it cannot create obligations chargeable to the person from whom one has a vocation to inherit or be conditioned on an act emanating from the latter.

###### Article 1086

The act of renunciation is, on pain of nullity, established by specific authentic act received by two notaries and precisely mentions its future legal consequences for the renouncer. The renunciation may be made in the same act by several forced heirs, but they then sign separately before the notaries who receive the act.  

The capacity required of the renouncer is that required to consent to an inter vivos donation. However, the emancipated minor may not renounce in advance the action for reduction.  
The renunciation, whatever its modalities, does not constitute a liberality. It is enforceable against the representatives of the renouncer.

###### Article 1087

The renunciation produces no effect if the hereditary reserve of the renouncer has not been infringed. If the infringement of the hereditary reserve has been exercised only partially, the renunciation produces effects only up to the amount of the infringement of the renouncer's reserve resulting from the liberality granted. If the infringement of the reserve relates to a fraction greater than that provided for in the renunciation, the excess is subject to reduction.  
The renunciation relating to the reduction of a liberality relating to a specific property lapses if the liberality infringing the reserve does not relate to that property. The same applies if the liberality has not been made in favour of the specified person or persons.

###### Article 1088

The renouncer has the possibility to revoke his renunciation, but only in the following cases: 1° When the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit does not fulfil his maintenance obligations towards him;  
2° When on the day of the opening of the succession, he is in a state of need that would disappear if he had not renounced his rights as forced heir;  
3° When the beneficiary of the renunciation has been guilty of a crime or offence against his person.

###### Article1089

In case of dispute, the renouncer seizes the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within one year from the day of the opening of the succession when the revocation is based on point 2° of the preceding article, and within one year from the act imputed by the renouncer or from the day when the act could have been known by his heirs, if it is based on point 2° or 3° of the preceding article.  
Revocation pursuant to 2° of the preceding article is pronounced only to the extent of the needs of the person who had renounced.

#### Chapter IV: Inter vivos donations

##### Section I: Conditions and effects of inter vivos donations Article 1090

To be valid, any donation must be executed by authentic act.  

In case of defect of form, an inter vivos donation cannot be the subject of confirmation: it must be remade in the legal form.  
After the death of the donor, the confirmation or voluntary execution of a donation by the heirs or successors in title of the donor entails their renunciation to oppose defects of form or any other cause of nullity.

###### Article 1091

The inter vivos donation shall not bind the donor, and shall produce no effect, except from the day it has been accepted in express terms.  

The acceptance may be made during the lifetime of the donor by a subsequent and authentic act, of which a minute shall remain; but then the donation shall have effect, with regard to the donor, only from the day when the act establishing this acceptance has been notified to him.

###### Article 1092

If the donee is of full age, the acceptance must be made by him or, in his name, by a representative endowed with the express power to accept the donation made, or with a general power to accept donations that have been or might be made.  
This power of attorney must be executed before a notary; and a copy must be annexed to the minute of the donation or to the minute of the acceptance that would be made by separate act.

###### Article 1093

The donation made to an unemancipated minor or to an adult under guardianship must be accepted by his guardian, in accordance with article 600, under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation.  
Nevertheless, the father and mother of the unemancipated minor, or other ascendants, even during the lifetime of the father and mother, although they are not guardians of the minor, may accept on his behalf.

###### Article 1094

The deaf-mute who can write may accept himself or through a representative.  

If he cannot write, the acceptance must be made by a curator appointed for this purpose, according to the rules established under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 1095

Donations made for the benefit of the establishments referred to in article 1059 shall be accepted by the administrators of these establishments, after having been duly authorized.  
The donation made by a terminally ill patient is deemed a legacy.

###### Article 1096

The donation duly accepted shall be perfected by the mere consent of the parties; and the ownership of the donated objects shall be transferred to the donee, without any other delivery being necessary.  
If delivery of the donated thing has not taken place, the donee has the right to require it.

###### Article 1097

When there is a donation of property susceptible to mortgages, the publication of the acts containing the donation and the acceptance, as well as the notification of the acceptance that would have taken place by separate act, must be made at the mortgage office of the place where the property is situated.  
When the donation is made to minors, adults under guardianship, or public establishments, the publication is made at the instance of the guardians, curators or administrators.

###### Article 1098

The lack of publication may be opposed by all persons having an interest, except however those who are charged with having the publication made, or their successors in title, and the donor.

###### Article 1099

Minors and adults under guardianship cannot request that the effects of the lack of acceptance or publication of donations not operate against them, even if said guardians are found to be insolvent. Minors and adults under guardianship may however obtain compensation; against their guardians, at least if the abstention of the latter has caused them prejudice.

###### Article 1100

A gift inter vivos may comprise only the present property of the donor; if it comprises future property, it is null and void in that respect.

###### Article 1101

Any gift inter vivos made subject to conditions the performance of which depends solely on the will of the donor is null and void.  
The same applies to a gift made subject to the condition of discharging debts or charges other than those existing at the time of the gift.

###### Article 1102

Where the donor has reserved the freedom to dispose of property included in the gift or of a fixed sum on the property given, if he dies without having so disposed, the said property or the said sum belongs to the heirs of the donor, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary.

###### Article 1103

The three preceding articles do not apply to gifts mentioned in chapters VIII and IX of this title.

###### Article 1104

Any deed of gift of movable property shall be valid only for property of which an estimated statement, signed by the donor and the donee, or by those accepting on his behalf, has been annexed to the original of the gift.

###### Article 1105

The donor is permitted to reserve for his own benefit or to dispose of, for the benefit of another, the enjoyment or usufruct of the movable or immovable property given.

###### Article 1106

Where the gift of movable property is made with reservation of usufruct, the donee shall be required, upon expiry of the usufruct, to take the property given which is found in kind, in the state in which it is; and he shall have an action against the donor or his heirs, in respect of non-existent objects, up to the value given to them in the estimated statement.

###### Article 1107

The donor may stipulate the right of return of the objects given either for the case of predeceasing of the donee alone, or for the case of predeceasing of the donee and his descendants.  
This right may be stipulated only for the benefit of the donor alone.

###### Article 1108

The effect of the right of return is to resolve all alienations of the property given, and to cause such property to revert to the donor, free of all charges and mortgages, except however the mortgage of the spouses, if the other property of the donee spouse is insufficient, and only in the case where the gift was made to him by the same marriage contract from which these charges and mortgages result.

###### Article 1109

The donor warrants eviction only if he has intentionally concealed the cause of eviction or if the gift was made with charges. In the first case, the donee shall be awarded fair compensation for the loss he has suffered; in the second case, the donor is liable only up to the value of the charges performed by the donee, all subject to agreement to the contrary.  
In case of eviction, the donee is subrogated to the rights and actions of the donor.

###### Article 1110

The donor does not warrant the defect of the thing given.  
However, if the donor has intentionally concealed the defect or if he has warranted its non-existence, he shall owe the donee compensation for the damage caused thereby. He shall also be liable for damages if the gift is made with charges, provided that the amount of damages does not exceed, in that case, the value of the charges performed by the donee.

##### Section II

Exceptions to the rule of irrevocability of gifts inter vivos Article 1111
A gift inter vivos may be revoked only for failure to perform the conditions under which it was made, for ingratitude, and for supervening birth of children.

###### Article 1112

In the case of revocation for failure to perform conditions, the property shall return to the hands of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on behalf of the donee; and the donor shall have, against third party holders of the immovable property given, all the rights he would have against the donee himself.

###### Article 1113

A gift inter vivos may be revoked for ingratitude only in the following cases: 1° If the donee has made an attempt on the life of the donor;  
2° If he has been guilty towards him of cruelty, offences or serious insults; 3° If he refuses him maintenance.

###### Article 1114

Revocation for failure to perform conditions, or for ingratitude, shall never take place by operation of law.

###### Article 1115

The application for revocation for ingratitude must be made within one year from the day of the offence imputed by the donor to the donee or from the day the offence could have been known by the donor.  
This revocation may not be sought by the donor against the heirs of the donee, nor by the heirs of the donor against the donee, unless, in the latter case, the action was brought by the donor, or he died within the year of the offence.

###### Article 1116

Revocation for ingratitude does not prejudice either the alienations made by the donee, or the mortgages and other real charges he may have imposed on the object of the gift, provided that all is prior to the publication, at the mortgage registry of the location of the property, of the application for revocation.  
In case of revocation, the donee is ordered to restore the value of the alienated objects, having regard to the time of the application, and the fruits, from the day of that application.

###### Article 1117

Gifts in consideration of marriage are not revocable for ingratitude.

###### Article 1118

All gifts inter vivos made by persons who had no children or descendants actually living at the time of the gift, of whatever value such gifts may be, and under whatever title they were made, and even if they were mutual or remuneratory, even those made in consideration of marriage by persons other than the spouses to each other, may be revoked, if the deed of gift so provides, by the supervening birth of a child born to the donor, even after his death, or adopted by him in the forms and conditions provided for in chapter I of title IX of book I.

###### Article 1119

This revocation may take place even if the child of the donor or the female donor was conceived at the time of the gift.

###### Article 1120

The gift may likewise be revoked even if the donee has entered into possession of the property given, and has been left there by the donor since the supervening birth of the child. However, the donee is not required to restore the fruits he has received, of whatever nature they may be, except from the day on which the birth of the child or his adoption in full form was notified to him by writ or other act in due form, even if the application to recover the property given was made after that notification.

###### Article 1121

The property included in the revoked gift returns to the patrimony of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on behalf of the donee, without being able to remain subject, even subsidiarily, to the mortgage of the spouses; which shall take place even if the gift was made in consideration of the marriage of the donee and inserted in the contract, and the donor bound himself as surety, by the gift, for the performance of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1122

The death of the child of the donor has no effect on the revocation of gifts provided for in article 1118.  

The donor may renounce exercising the revocation for supervening birth of a child, at any time, that is to say before or after the birth of the child.

###### Article 1123

The action for revocation is prescribed after five years from the birth or adoption of the last child.  
It may be exercised only by the donor.

#### Chapitre V

Testamentary dispositions Section I: General rules

###### Article 1124

Any person may dispose by will, whether under the title of institution of heir, or under the title of legacy, or under any other designation appropriate to manifest their will.

###### Article 1125

A will cannot be made in the same instrument by two or more persons, whether for the benefit of a third party or as a reciprocal or mutual disposition.

###### Article 1126

To be valid, a will must be made by an authentic instrument or by an instrument entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

###### Article 1127

A will by authentic instrument is received either by two notaries or by one notary assisted by two witnesses who cannot be either the legatees, in whatever capacity, or their relatives or in-laws up to and including the fourth degree, or the clerks of the notaries by whom the instruments will be received.  
In both circumstances, the will is dictated by the testator and, as the case may be, one of the two notaries or the notary writes it himself or has it written by hand or mechanically.  
It must then be read to the testator.  
When the testator cannot express himself in French or Arabic, the dictation and reading may be accomplished by an interpreter whom the testator chooses from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The interpreter ensures the exact translation of the statements made. The notary is not required to use an interpreter when he himself as well as, as the case may be, the other notary or the witnesses understand the language in which the testator expresses himself.  

When the testator can write in French or Arabic but cannot speak, the notary writes the will himself or has it written by hand or mechanically from notes drafted before him by the testator, then reads it to the latter. When the testator cannot hear, he takes cognizance of the will by reading it himself, after it has been read by the notary. When the testator can neither speak or hear, nor read or write, the dictation or reading are accomplished, when possible, through the intermediary of a sign language interpreter and according to the same procedures.  

The instrument expressly mentions compliance with the above-mentioned requirements.

###### Article 1128

This will by authentic instrument must be signed by the testator in the presence, as the case may be, of the witnesses and the notary or of the two notaries; if the testator declares that he does not know how or cannot sign, the instrument bears his fingerprint.  
It is also signed, as the case may be, by the witnesses and by the notary or by the two notaries.

###### Article 1129

A mystic will is a will whose content remains hidden until the death of the person. When the testator wishes to make a mystic will, the paper containing the dispositions or the paper serving as an envelope, if there is one, is delivered closed, sealed and stamped, either to a notary before two witnesses or to two notaries, or closed, sealed and stamped in their presence. The testator then declares that the content of this paper is his will, signed by him, and written by him or by another, affirming, in the latter case, that he has personally verified the wording. He indicates, in all cases, the mode of writing he has employed (by hand or mechanical).  
As the case may be, the notary or the notaries write or have written by hand or mechanically on this paper or on the sheet that will serve as an envelope intended to contain it, the date and indication of the place where the mystic will is executed, the description of the fold and the impression of the seal, and mention of all the above formalities; this instrument is signed both by the testator and by the notary and the witnesses, or by the two notaries. If the testator, either by an impediment arising since the signing of the will or because he does not know how to sign, has not been able to sign this instrument, mention is made of it as well as of the reason he has given for it.  

All of these operations must be carried out in one continuous process and without interruption.

###### Article 1130

Those who do not know how or cannot read cannot make dispositions in the form of a mystic will.  
On the other hand, a testator who cannot speak but who knows how to write may make a mystic will, on the express condition that the will be signed by him and written by him or by another, that he present it to the notary and the witnesses, or to the two notaries, and that at the top of the superscription instrument he write, in their presence, that the paper he presents is his will, this before signing the instrument. As the case may be, the notary or the notaries write on this instrument that the testator wrote and signed these words in his presence and that of the witnesses, or in their presence. The provisions of Article 1129, except those contrary to this article, are applicable.
