In all cases provided for in this article or in the preceding articles, a mystic will in which the legal formalities have not been observed, and which will be null as such, shall nevertheless be valid as a holographic will if all the conditions required for its validity as a holographic will are fulfilled, even if it has been designated as a mystic will.

###### Article 1131

Witnesses called to be present at wills must be Djiboutian and of age, know how to sign and have the enjoyment of their civil rights. They may be of either sex, but husband and wife cannot be witnesses in the same instrument.

###### Article 1132

The wills of military personnel, naval personnel of the State and persons employed in the service of the armies may be received in the cases and conditions provided for in Article 125 in one of the following forms:
1° by a senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, in the presence of two witnesses;  
2° by two officials of the intendancy or commissariat officers or by one of these officials or officers in the presence of two witnesses;  
3° in case of an isolated detachment and if there is no senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, intendancy official or commissariat officer in this detachment, by the officer commanding this detachment assisted by two witnesses;  
4° if the testator is sick or wounded and is staying in a military hospital or medical unit, by the chief medical officer, whatever his rank, assisted by the administrative officer in charge. In the absence of this administrative officer, the presence of two witnesses is necessary.  
The will of the officer commanding an isolated detachment may be received by the officer who comes after him in the order of service.  

The power to make a will under the conditions provided for in this article extends to prisoners with the enemy.  
In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus drawn up shall be made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will shall be drawn up to take the place of the second original; this copy shall be signed by the witnesses and by the instrumentary officers. Mention shall be made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original.  

As soon as communication is possible, and within the shortest possible time, the two originals or the original and the copy of the will shall be sent, separately and by different couriers, under sealed and closed cover, to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of an indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.  

The will made in the form established above shall be null and void by operation of law six months after the testator has arrived in a place where he has the freedom to use the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he has again been placed in one of the special situations provided for in Article 125. The will is then valid for the duration of this special situation and for a new period of six months after its expiration.  

All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1133

During a maritime voyage, both en route and during a stop in a port, when there is impossibility of communicating with land or when there is no Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent invested with the functions of notary in the port, if one is abroad, the wills of persons present on board shall be received, in the presence of two witnesses:
1° on State vessels, by the administrative officer or, in his absence, by the commander or the person performing his functions. The will of the administrative officer is received by the commander or by the person performing his functions, and, if there is no administrative officer, the will of the commander is received by the person who comes after him in the order of service;  
2° on other vessels, by the captain, master or skipper, assisted by the ship's mate, or, in their absence, by those who replace them. The will of the captain, master or skipper, or that of the mate, is received by the persons who come after them in the order of service.  
The act indicates which of the circumstances provided for above it is received in.  

In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus drawn up shall be made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will shall be drawn up to take the place of the second original; this copy shall be signed by the witnesses and by the instrumentary officers. Mention shall be made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original.  

At the first stop in a foreign port where there is a Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent, one of the originals or the copy of the will shall be delivered, under sealed and closed cover, into the hands of this official, who shall send it to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of an indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.  
And, upon the arrival of the vessel in a port of Djibouti, the two originals of the will or the original and its copy, or the original that remains, in case of transmission or delivery made during the course of the voyage, shall be deposited, under sealed and closed cover, for State vessels, at the armaments office, and for other vessels at the maritime registration office. Each of these documents shall be sent, separately and by different couriers, to the Minister of Defence, who shall transmit them as stated in the preceding paragraph.  

The will made during a maritime voyage, in the form prescribed by Article 1132, shall be valid only insofar as the testator dies on board or within six months after he has disembarked in a place where he could remake it in the ordinary forms. However, if the testator undertakes a new maritime voyage before the expiration of this period, the will is valid for the duration of this voyage and for a new period of six months after the testator has again disembarked.  
All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1134

The dispositions inserted in a will made, during a maritime voyage, in favour of the officers of the vessel other than those who are relatives or relations by marriage of the testator, are null and void.

###### Article 1135

The testator, in the cases of Articles 1132 and 1133, is informed, in the presence of the witnesses, that his will shall be null and void by operation of law six months after he has arrived in a place where he will have the freedom

to use the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he is again placed in a situation which falls under the said articles.

###### Article 1136

On pain of nullity, wills must be signed by the testator, by those who have received them and by the witnesses.  
If the testator declares that he cannot or does not know how to sign, mention shall be made of his declaration, as well as of the cause which prevents him from signing.  
In the case where the presence of two witnesses is required, the will shall be signed by at least one of them, and mention shall be made of the reason why the other has not signed.

###### Article 1137

A Djiboutian who is in a foreign country may make his testamentary dispositions by private deed or by authentic act, with the forms customary in the place where this act is executed.  
Such wills made in a foreign country can be executed on property located in Djibouti only after having been registered at the office of the domicile of the testator, if he has retained one, otherwise at the office of his last known domicile in Djibouti. In the case where the will contains dispositions of immovable property located there, it must, in addition, be registered at the office of the location of this immovable property, without a double duty being able to be required.

##### Section II: Institutions of heirs and legacies in general Article 1138

Testamentary dispositions are either universal, or by universal title, or by particular title.  

Each of these dispositions shall produce its effect according to the rules established hereinafter for universal legacies, for legacies by universal title, and for particular legacies.

###### Article 1139

Unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, where the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law, the legatee may limit his emolument to a portion of the property disposed of in his favour. This limitation does not constitute a liberality made by the legatee to the other successors.  
Unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, any person gratified with a legacy may decide to receive only a portion of the property provided, on condition that the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law. This decision of the legatee is not considered as a liberality from the legatee to the other successors.

###### Sous-section 1 : Du legs universel Article 1140

A universal legacy is a testamentary disposition by which the testator gives to one or more persons the universality of the property he will leave at his death.

###### Article 1141

Where at the death of the testator there are heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, those heirs are seised by operation of law, upon his death, of all the property of the succession; and the universal legatee is required to request from them delivery of the property included in the will.  

Nevertheless, in the same cases, the universal legatee shall have enjoyment of the property included in the will from the day of death, if the request for delivery was made within one year from that time; otherwise, such enjoyment shall commence only from the day the application was made in court, or from the day that delivery was voluntarily consented to.

###### Article 1142

Where at the death of the testator there are no heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, the universal legatee shall be seised by operation of law upon the death of the testator. If the will was executed by authentic instrument, he is not required to request delivery by sending into possession; in the contrary case, the legatee is required to have himself sent into possession by an order of the president, placed at the foot of a petition to which the instrument of deposit is attached.

###### Article 1143

Every will under private signature is, before being executed, deposited in the hands of a notary. The will is opened if it is sealed. The notary immediately draws up a record of the opening and condition of the will, specifying the circumstances of the deposit. The will together with the record are preserved among the minutes of the depositary.  
Within one month following the date of the record, the notary sends an authenticated copy thereof and a facsimile copy of the will to the registrar of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession, who acknowledges receipt of these documents and preserves them among his minutes.

###### Article 1144

The universal legatee who is in concurrence with an heir to whom the law reserves a portion of the property is liable for the debts and charges of the testator's succession, personally for his share and portion and by mortgage for the whole; and he is required to discharge all legacies, except in case of reduction, as explained in Articles 1079 and 1080.

###### Sous-section 2 : Du legs à titre universel Article 1145

A legacy by general title is one by which the testator bequeaths a share of the property which the law permits him to dispose of, for example, one half, one third, or all his immovable property, or all his movable property, or a fixed portion of all his immovable property or of all his movable property.  

Any other legacy constitutes only a disposition by particular title.

###### Article 1146

Legatees by general title must request delivery from the heirs to whom a portion of the property is reserved by law; in their absence, from the universal legatees and, in the absence of the latter, from the heirs called in the order established in the title On Successions.  
Delivery of legacies may be effected amicably; it may be recorded by instrument under private signature: a written, dated and signed document. However, an authentic instrument must be drawn up when immovable property is involved. Whether it be an instrument under private signature or an authentic instrument, the delivery of legacies specifies the property that is concerned.

###### Article 1147

The legatee by general title is liable, like the universal legatee, for the debts and charges of the testator's succession, personally for his share and portion, and by mortgage for the whole.  

Where the testator has disposed of only a portion of the disposable portion, and he has done so by general title, that legatee is required to discharge particular legacies by contribution with the natural heirs.

###### Sous-section 3 : Des legs particuliers Article 1148

Every pure and simple legacy gives the legatee, from the day of the testator's death, a right to the thing bequeathed, a right transmissible to his heirs or successors in title.  
Nevertheless the particular legatee may not take possession of the thing bequeathed, nor claim the fruits or interest thereof, except from the day of his request for delivery, made according to the order established in the title On Successions, or from the day on which such delivery was voluntarily consented to him.

###### Article 1149

The interest or fruits of the thing bequeathed accrue to the benefit of the legatee from the day of death, and without his having made his application in court:
1° Where the testator has expressly declared his intention in this regard in the will; 2° Where a life annuity or pension has been bequeathed as maintenance.

###### Article 1150

The costs of the application for delivery are chargeable to the succession, without however any reduction of the legal reserve resulting therefrom.  
Registration fees are payable by the legatee. All of the foregoing, except contrary stipulation in the will.  
Each legacy may be registered separately, without such registration being able to benefit anyone other than the legatee or his successors in title.

###### Article 1151

The heirs of the testator, or other debtors of a legacy, are personally liable to discharge the legacy, each in proportion to the share and portion in which they will benefit from the succession.  
They are liable by mortgage for the whole to deliver the thing bequeathed with the necessary accessories and in the condition in which it will be found on the day of the donor's death, up to the value of the immovable property of the succession of which they are holders. However, if the person who bequeathed ownership of an immovable property subsequently increased it by acquisitions, those acquisitions, even if contiguous, shall not be deemed, without a new disposition, to form part of the legacy. On the other hand, embellishments or new constructions made on the bequeathed land are necessarily included in the legacy.

###### Article 1152

If, before the will or since, the thing bequeathed has been the subject of a real right by the testator, the legatee receives the bequeathed property in the condition in which it is at the death of the testator and the person who must deliver the legacy is not required to free that property before delivering it.

###### Article 1153

Where the testator has bequeathed the property of another, the legacy is null, even if the testator did not know that it did not belong to him.

###### Article 1154

Where the legacy relates to an indeterminate thing, the heir is not obliged to give it of the best quality, and he may not offer it of the worst.

###### Article 1155

A legacy made to a creditor is not deemed to be in compensation for his debt, nor is a legacy made to a servant in compensation for his wages.

###### Article 1156

The particular legatee is not liable for the debts of the succession, except for reduction of the legacy as stated above, and except for the mortgage action of creditors.

##### Section III: Mandataries and Testamentary Executors Article 1157

The heirs may, by mutual agreement, entrust the administration of the estate to one of them or to a third party. The mandate is governed by the provisions of articles 2175 and following.  
When at least one heir has accepted the estate up to the net assets, the mandatary cannot, even with the agreement of all the heirs, be designated except by the judge.  
The judge may also be seized by any interested party or by the public prosecutor so that he may designate a qualified person as estate mandatary, for the purpose of provisionally administering the estate by reason of the inertia, failure or fault of one or more heirs in this administration, their disagreement, a conflict of interests between them or the complexity of the estate situation.

###### Article 1158

In the preceding cases, the mandate or the judge, as the case may be, fixes the duration of the mission of the appointed mandatary, the limit of his powers and his remuneration.  
The appointment of a testamentary mandatary is subject to publication at the mortgage registry.

###### Article 1159

At the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor, the judge may remove the estate mandatary, and designate another, when the first has failed in his mission.  
The mission ceases by operation of law by the effect of an agreement of joint ownership between the heirs or by the signing of the deed of partition. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the estate mandatary.

###### Article 1160

As soon as the estate has been accepted by at least one heir, either purely and simply, or subject to inventory, the judge who designated the estate mandatary may authorize him to carry out all acts of administration of the estate.  

He may also authorize him, at any time, to carry out acts of disposition necessary for the proper administration of the estate and determine the prices and stipulations thereof.

###### Article 1161

The testator may appoint one or more testamentary executors, enjoying full civil capacity, to ensure or proceed with the execution of his wishes.  
The testamentary executor who has accepted his mission is bound to fulfill it in the same capacity as a gratuitous mandatary. He assumes responsibility for it. He ensures that the will is executed; and, in case of dispute over its validity or execution, he must be made a party or intervene as the case may be to uphold the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.  

The testamentary executor exercises his mission gratuitously, except for a liberality made as a particular gift having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered.

###### Article 1162

The testator may authorize the testamentary executor to seize all or only part of the movable property of the estate, and to sell it if necessary to discharge the particular legacies within the limit of the available portion; this seizure may not last beyond one year and one day from the opening of the will.  
The heir may terminate the seizure by offering to deliver to the testamentary executors a sufficient sum for the payment of the movable legacies or by proving such payment.

###### Article 1163

In the absence of an accepting forced heir, the testator may authorize, for a period of two years from the opening of the will, the testamentary executor to dispose of all or part of the immovable property of the estate, receive and invest capital, pay debts and charges and proceed with the allocation or partition of the remaining property between the heirs and legatees.  
On pain of being unenforceable, the sale of an immovable property of the estate may only take place after information of the heirs by the testamentary executor.

###### Article 1164

The authorizations provided for in the two preceding articles may, by decision of the judge, be extended by one year at most.

###### Article 1165

If there are several testamentary executors who have accepted their mission, only one may act in the absence of the others, unless the testator has provided otherwise or has divided their functions. In case of joint acceptance, they are jointly and severally liable for the account of the property entrusted to them.

###### Article 1166

The testamentary executor takes any conservatory measure useful for the proper execution of the will.  
He may make, in the presence of the presumptive heir, or he being duly summoned, the inventory of the property of the estate.  

He causes the sale of movable property in the absence of sufficient liquid assets to discharge the legacies and urgent debts of the estate.

###### Article 1167

In case of dispute over the validity or execution of the will, the testamentary executor must be made a party or intervene as the case may be, to uphold the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

###### Article 1168

The mission of the testamentary executor ends:	upon completion of his mission;	by decision of the judge, who relieves him of his mission for serious reasons;	by his death, his powers not being transmissible to his heirs.  

The testamentary executor renders account within six months following the end of his mission; in case of death, this obligation is imposed on his heirs.

###### Article 1169

The expenses incurred by the testamentary executor in the exercise of his mission are borne by the estate. He is reimbursed before the delivery of legacies.

##### Section IV: Revocation of Wills and Their Lapse Article 1170

Wills may be revoked, in whole or in part, only by a subsequent will or by an act before a notary bearing declaration of change of will.

###### Article 1171

In the absence of express revocation, the testator is deemed to have tacitly revoked his will:

1° By a subsequent will whose provisions prove incompatible with the previous ones. In this case, the new provisions replace the old ones;  
2° By the voluntary alienation of the thing bequeathed when the legacy is as a particular gift and has as its object a specific thing, even if the alienation should subsequently be called into question, subject to the contrary will expressed by the testator in the act of alienation;  

3° By the destruction or voluntary alteration of the will. In case of erasure or tearing of only part of the paper containing the testamentary provisions, there is no revocation of the provisions mentioned on the preserved part, at least if these fulfill the conditions of form provided by law.

###### Article 1172

The revocation made in a subsequent will has full effect, even if this new act should remain without execution due to the incapacity of the instituted heir or the legatee, or by their refusal to take the succession or the legacy.  
The revocation of a will does not revive the previously established will in the absence of a will clearly manifested to that effect by the deceased.

###### Article 1173

Any testamentary provision lapses if the person in whose favor it is made does not survive the testator.  
The same applies when the testamentary provision had been made under a condition, and the instituted heir or the legatee dies before the fulfillment of this condition, except in the case of a

suspensive condition whose right was immediately acquired by the instituted heir, or the legatee and who, in this case, transmits this right to his heirs.

###### Article 1174

A testamentary disposition lapses:
1° If the bequeathed thing has totally perished during the testator's lifetime;  
2° If the bequeathed thing has perished since the testator's death, without the act or fault of the heir, even though the heir has been placed in default of delivering it, when it would equally have had to perish in the hands of the legatee;  
3° When the instituted heir or the legatee repudiates it or is found incapable of receiving it.

###### Article 1175

In the absence of provision in the testamentary dispositions, the revocation, lapse or nullity of a legacy benefits the debtors of the revoked, lapsed or null legacy or legacies, that is to say, as the case may be, the heir, the universal legatee or the legatee by general title. Thus, the ineffectiveness of a universal legacy benefits the heirs; in the absence of a forced heir, the ineffectiveness of a particular legacy benefits the universal legatee.  
By way of exception, the property included in the legacy deprived of effect may be transmitted to the other legatees. There is thus accretion when the legacy has been made to several persons jointly. Two types of legacies are deemed joint within the meaning of this article, namely: the legacy made by one and the same provision of the will and without assignment of shares to each of the co-legatees; the legacy, to several persons, of a thing which can be divided without deterioration.

###### Article 1176

After the death of the testator, the legacies which he had established may be revoked judicially if the legatee:
1° Has not performed the charges incumbent upon him; 2° Has made an attempt on the testator's life;  
3° Has been guilty towards the testator of acts of cruelty, offences or serious injuries; 4° Has uttered a serious insult against the memory of the testator.  
The action for revocation belongs to all those who have an interest therein: the testator's heirs, the universal legatees, and by indirect action the creditors of the testator, of the heirs or of the legatees. The testamentary executor is also entitled to seek revocation for non-performance of charges. On the other hand, the beneficiary of the legacy, as well as the beneficiary of the charge, may only bring the action for performance.  

In case 4°, the action must be brought within one year from the day of the offence.

#### Chapter VI

Gradual and residual liberalities Section I: Gradual liberalities

###### Article 1177

A liberality may be burdened with a charge comprising the obligation for the donee or legatee to preserve the property or rights which are the object thereof and to transmit them, upon his death, to a second beneficiary, designated in the instrument.

###### Article 1178

The liberality thus granted may only produce its effect on property or rights identifiable at the date of transmission and subsisting in kind at the death of the person burdened.  

When it relates to securities, the liberality also produces its effect, in case of alienation, on the securities which have been subrogated thereto.  

When it concerns immovable property, the charge burdening the liberality is subject to publication.

###### Article 1179

The rights of the second beneficiary open at the death of the person burdened.  

However, the person burdened may abandon, for the benefit of the second beneficiary, the enjoyment of the property or right which is the object of the liberality.  
This anticipated abandonment may not prejudice the creditors of the person burdened prior to the abandonment, nor third parties having acquired, from the latter, a right over the property or right abandoned.

###### Article 1180

The second beneficiary is deemed to hold his rights from the author of the liberality. The same applies to his heirs when they receive the liberality under the conditions provided for in Article 1066.

###### Article 1181

It is for the disposer to prescribe guarantees and securities for the proper performance of the charge.

###### Article 1182

The second beneficiary may not be subjected to the obligation to preserve and transmit.  

If the charge has been stipulated beyond the first degree, it remains valid but for the first degree only.

###### Article 1183

If the person burdened is a forced heir of the disposer, the charge may only be imposed on the disposable portion.  
The donee may however accept, in the deed of donation or subsequently in an instrument established by specific authentic act received by two notaries, that the charge burdens all or part of his forced share. The instrument is signed in the presence of the notaries alone and mentions precisely its future legal consequences for the donee, on pain of nullity.  
The legatee may, within a period of one year from the day on which he became aware of the will, request that his share of the forced portion be, in whole or in part, freed from the charge. Failing this, he must assume its performance.  
The charge relating to the forced share of the person burdened, with his consent, benefits by operation of law, to that extent, all his children born and unborn.

###### Article 1184

The author of a gradual donation may revoke it with regard to the second beneficiary as long as the latter has not notified, in the forms required for donations, his acceptance to the donor.  
By way of derogation from Article 1091, the gradual donation may be accepted by the second beneficiary after the death of the donor.

###### Article 1185

When the second beneficiary dies before the person burdened or renounces the benefit of the gradual liberality, the property or rights which were the object thereof form part of the succession of the person burdened, unless the instrument expressly provides that his heirs may receive it or designates another second beneficiary.

##### Section II: Residual liberalities Article 1186

It may be provided in a liberality that a person will be called to receive what will remain of the gift or legacy made to a first beneficiary at the death of the latter.

###### Article 1187

The residual liberality does not oblige the first beneficiary to preserve the property received. It obliges him to transmit the subsisting property.  
When the property, objects of the residual liberality, have been alienated by the first beneficiary, the rights of the second beneficiary do not transfer either to the proceeds of these alienations or to the new property acquired.

###### Article 1188

The first beneficiary may not dispose by will of the property given or bequeathed on a residual basis.  

The residual liberality may prohibit the first beneficiary from disposing of the property by inter vivos donation.  

However, when he is a forced heir, the first beneficiary retains the possibility of disposing inter vivos or upon death of the property which has been given as an advancement on succession.

###### Article 1189

The first beneficiary is not required to account for his management to the disposer or to his heirs.

###### Article 1190

The provisions set out in Articles 1178, 1180, 1181, 1184 and 1185 are applicable to residual liberalities.

#### Chapter VII

Partition donations and partition wills Section I: General provisions

###### Article 1191

Any person may make, among his presumptive heirs, the distribution and partition of his property.  

This instrument may be made in the form of a partition donation or a partition will. It is subject to the formalities, conditions and rules prescribed for inter vivos donations in the first case and wills in the second, subject to the application of the provisions which follow.

###### Article 1192

Any person may also make the distribution and partition of his property and his rights among descendants of different degrees, whether or not they are his presumptive heirs. The agreement of the forced heirs is then necessary.

###### Article 1193

The action for additional share on grounds of lesion may not be exercised against partition donations and partition wills.  

The provisions of Article 972, first paragraph, are applicable to balancing payments charged to the donees, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

###### Article 1195

If all the property that the disposer leaves on the day of his death has not been included in the partition, those of his property that have not been included therein are allocated or partitioned in accordance with the law.

##### Section II: Gifts with partition

###### § 1. Gifts with partition made to presumptive heirs Article 1196

A gift with partition may only have as its object present property.

The gift and the partition may be made by separate instruments provided that the ascendant is a party to both instruments.

###### Article 1197

In the case of a gift with partition made jointly by two spouses, the non-common child may be allotted on behalf of his ancestor in separate property of the latter or in common property, without the spouse being able, however, to be co-donor of the common property.

###### Article 1198

Property received by way of advance partition by a presumptive forced heir is imputable to his share of the reserved portion, unless it has been expressly given outside his share.

###### Article 1199

The forced heir who has not participated in the gift with partition, or who has received a lot less than his share of the reserved portion, may exercise the action for reduction, if there does not exist at the opening of the succession property not included in the partition and sufficient to compose or complete his reserved portion, taking into account liberalities from which he may have benefited.

###### Article 1200

Gifts with partition follow the rules of gifts inter vivos for everything concerning imputation, calculation of the reserved portion and reduction.
The action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the disposer who made the partition. In the case of a gift with partition made jointly by both spouses, the action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the survivor of the disposers, except for the non-common child who may act upon the death of his ancestor. The action is barred by limitation after five years from that death.

The child not yet conceived at the time of the gift with partition has a similar action to compose or complete his hereditary share.

###### Article 1201

Notwithstanding the rules applicable to gifts inter vivos, the property given shall, unless otherwise agreed, be valued on the day of the gift with partition for imputation and calculation of the reserved portion, provided that all forced heirs living or represented at the death of the ascendant have received a lot in the advance partition and have expressly accepted it, and that no reservation of usufruct relating to a sum of money has been provided for.

The lot of certain donees may be formed, in whole or in part, from gifts, whether subject to collation or outside the share, already received by them from the disposer, having regard where appropriate to investments and reinvestments that they may have made in the meantime.

The valuation date applicable to the advance partition shall also be applicable to prior gifts that have thus been incorporated into it. Any provision to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1203

The parties may also agree that a prior gift made outside the share shall be incorporated into the partition and imputed to the share of the reserved portion of the donee by way of advancement of succession share.

###### Article 1204

The agreements referred to in the two preceding articles may take place even in the absence of new gifts from the disposer. They are not regarded as liberalities between the presumptive heirs, but as a partition made by the disposer.

###### § 2

Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees Article 1205
When the ascendant proceeds with a gift with partition, his children may consent to their own descendants being allotted therein in their place and stead, in whole or in part.
Descendants of a subsequent degree may, in the advance partition, be allotted separately or jointly among themselves.

###### Article 1206

This liberality constitutes a gift with partition even though the donor ascendant has only one child, whether the partition is made between the latter and his descendants or between his descendants only.
It requires the consent, in the instrument, of the child who renounces all or part of his rights, as well as of his descendants who benefit therefrom. The liberality is void when the consent of the renouncing party has been vitiated by error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 1207

When descendants of different degrees participate in the same gift with partition, the partition is effected by stirpes.
Allocations may be made to descendants of different degrees in certain stirpes and not in others.

###### Article 1208

Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 to 1204.

###### Article 1209

In the succession of the donor ascendant, the property received by the children or their descendants by way of advance partition is imputed to the share of the reserved portion reverting to their stirps and subsidiarily to the disposable portion.
All gifts made to members of the same stirps are imputed together, whatever the degree of relationship with the deceased.

When all the children of the donor ascendant have given their consent to the advance partition and no reservation of usufruct relating to a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is valued according to the rule provided for in article 1201.

If the descendants of a stirps have not received a lot in the gift with partition or have received therein only a lot less than their share of the reserved portion, they are filled in their rights according to the rules provided for in articles 1199 and 1200.

###### Article 1210

In the succession of the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead, the property received by them from the ascendant is treated as if they held it from their direct ancestor.
This property is subject to the rules governing gifts inter vivos for notional reunion, imputation, collation and, where appropriate, reduction.
However, when all the descendants have received and accepted a lot in the advance partition and no usufruct relating to a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is treated as if they had received it from their ancestor by gift with partition.

###### Article 1211

The rules laid down in article 1210 do not apply when the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead subsequently proceeds himself, with the latter, to a gift with partition into which is incorporated the property previously received under the conditions provided for in article 1205.
This new gift with partition may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 and 1203.

##### Section III: Testamentary partitions Article 1212

A testamentary partition produces the effects of a partition. Its beneficiaries may not renounce relying on the testament to claim a new partition of the succession.

###### Article 1213

The beneficiary who has not received a lot equal to his share of the reserved portion may exercise the action for reduction in accordance with article 1200.

#### Chapter VIII

Gifts made by marriage contract to the spouses, and to children to be born of the marriage

###### Article 1214

Any gift inter vivos of present property, although made by marriage contract to the spouses, or to one of them, shall be subject to the general rules prescribed for gifts made under that title.
It may not take place for the benefit of children to be born, except in the cases set out in chapter VI of this title.

###### Article 1215

Fathers and mothers, other ascendants, collateral relatives of the spouses, and even strangers, may, by marriage contract, dispose of all or part of the property they will leave at the day of their death, both in favor of said spouses and in favor of the children to be born of their marriage, in the event that the donor survives the donee spouse.

Such a donation, although made in favor only of the spouses or one of them, shall always, in said case of survival of the donor, be presumed made in favor of the children and descendants to be born of the marriage.

###### Article 1216

The donation in the form provided in the preceding article shall be irrevocable only in the sense that the donor may no longer dispose, by gratuitous title, of the objects included in the donation, except for modest sums, by way of reward or otherwise.

###### Article 1217

The donation by marriage contract may be made cumulatively of present and future property, in whole or in part, on condition that a statement of the debts and charges of the donor existing at the day of the donation be annexed to the deed; in which case, it shall be open to the donee, upon the death of the donor, to confine himself to the present property, by renouncing the surplus of the donor's property.

###### Article 1218

If the statement mentioned in the preceding article has not been annexed to the deed containing the donation of present and future property, the donee shall be obliged to accept or renounce this donation for the whole.  
In case of acceptance, he may claim only the property that will be found existing at the day of the donor's death, and he shall be subject to payment of all the debts and charges of the succession.

###### Article 1219

The donation by marriage contract in favor of the spouses and the children to be born of their marriage may also be made, on condition of paying indiscriminately all the debts and charges of the donor's succession, or under other conditions the performance of which would depend on his will, by whatever person the donation is made: the donee shall be bound to fulfill these conditions, if he does not prefer to renounce the donation; and if the donor, by marriage contract, has reserved the liberty to dispose of an item included in the donation of his present property or of a fixed sum to be taken from this same property, the item or sum, if he dies without having disposed of it, shall be deemed included in the donation and shall belong to the donee or his heirs.

###### Article 1220

Donations made by marriage contract may not be attacked or declared null on the pretext of lack of acceptance.

###### Article 1221

Any donation made in favor of the marriage shall lapse if the marriage does not follow.

###### Article 1222

Donations made to one of the spouses, in the terms of articles 1215, 1217 and 1219 above, shall lapse if the donor survives the donee spouse and his posterity.

###### Article 1223

All donations made to the spouses by their marriage contract shall, upon the opening of the donor's succession, be reducible to the portion which the law permitted him to dispose of.

#### Chapter IX

Dispositions between spouses, either by marriage contract or during marriage Article 1224
The spouses may, by marriage contract, make to each other reciprocally, or one of the two to the other, such donation as they see fit, subject to the modifications hereinafter expressed.

###### Article 1225

Any inter vivos donation of present property, made between spouses by marriage contract, shall not be deemed made under the condition of survival of the donee, if this condition is not formally expressed; and it shall be subject to all the rules and forms prescribed above for such donations.

###### Article 1226

The donation of future property, or of present and future property, made between spouses by marriage contract, whether simple or reciprocal, shall be subject to the rules established by the preceding chapter, with regard to similar donations that will be made to them by a third party, except that it shall not be transmissible to the children born of the marriage, in case of death of the donee spouse before the donor spouse.

###### Article 1227

The spouse, either by marriage contract or during the marriage, may, for the case where he would not leave children or descendants, dispose in favor of the other spouse in ownership, of all that he could dispose of in favor of a stranger.

###### Article 1228

For the case where the spouse would leave children or descendants, whether or not born of the marriage, he may dispose in favor of the other spouse, either of the ownership of what he could dispose of in favor of a stranger, or of one quarter of his property in ownership and the three other quarters in usufruct, or again of the totality of his property in usufruct only.  
Unless otherwise stipulated by the disposer, the surviving spouse may limit his emolument, that is to say accept only certain of the property disposed of in his favor. This limitation may not be considered as a liberality made to the other successors.

###### Article 1229

The children or descendants may, notwithstanding any stipulation to the contrary by the disposer, require, as to the property subject to usufruct, that an inventory be drawn up of the movables as well as a statement of the immovables, that employment be made of the sums and that bearer securities be, at the choice of the usufructuary, converted into registered securities or deposited with an approved depositary.

###### Article 1230

The minor may not, by marriage contract, give to the other spouse, either by simple donation or by reciprocal donation, except with the consent and assistance of those whose consent is required for the validity of his marriage; and, with this consent, he may give all that the law permits the adult spouse to give to the other spouse.

###### Article 1231

The donation of future property made between spouses during the marriage is always revocable.  

The donation of present property that takes effect during the marriage made between spouses is revocable only under the conditions provided by articles 1111 to 1116.  
Donations made between spouses of present property or of future property are not revoked by the supervening of children.

###### Article 1232

If a spouse has made to his spouse, within the limits of article 1228, a liberality in ownership, each of the children who are not born of both spouses shall have, as concerns him, unless contrary and unequivocal will of the disposer, the faculty to substitute for the performance of this liberality the abandonment of the usufruct of the share of succession that he would have collected in the absence of a surviving spouse.  
Those who have exercised this faculty may require that the provisions of article 1229 be applied.

###### Article 1233

The spouses may not give each other indirectly beyond what is permitted to them by the provisions above.  
Any donation, either disguised or made to interposed persons, shall be null.  

Shall be deemed made to interposed persons, donations by one of the spouses to the children or to one of the children of the other spouse born of another marriage, and those made by the donor to relatives of whom the other spouse will be presumptive heir on the day of the donation, even though the latter did not survive his donee relative.

###### Article 1234

When a spouse acquires property with money that has been given to him by the other for this purpose, the donation is only of the sums remitted and not of the property to which they are employed.  
In this case, the rights of the donor or his heirs have as their object only a sum of money according to the current value of the property. If the property has been alienated, the value it had on the day of alienation is considered, and if new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property.

### Title III: Obligations

###### Article 1235

Obligations arise from juridical acts, juridical facts or the authority of law alone.

They may arise from the promise to perform a natural obligation as well as from the voluntary performance of such an obligation. The promise to perform a natural obligation constitutes a contract; the completed performance of a natural obligation cannot give rise to restitution once the performance has been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1236

Juridical acts are manifestations of will intended to produce legal effects. They may be a contract or a unilateral juridical act.
Juridical acts are subject, insofar as applicable, for their validity and their effects, to the rules governing contracts.

###### Article 1237

Juridical facts are acts or events to which the law attaches legal effects.

Obligations arising from a juridical fact are governed, as the case may be, by the sub-title relating to civil liability or the sub-title relating to quasi-contracts.

Sub-title I: The Contract

Chapter I: Preliminary Provisions Article 1238
A contract is an agreement of wills between two or more persons intended to create, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.

###### Article 1239

Everyone is free to contract or not to contract, to choose their contracting party and to determine the content and form of the contract, within the limits set by law.
Contractual freedom does not permit derogation from rules concerning public order and good morals.

###### Article 1240

Contracts legally formed have the force of law for those who have made them. Contracts are in principle consensual.
By way of exception, the validity of solemn contracts is subject to the observance of forms determined by law in the absence of which the contract is null and void, subject to possible regularisation.
Furthermore, the law makes the formation of certain contracts subject to the delivery of a thing.
On the other hand, forms required for the purposes of proof or enforceability have no effect on the validity of contracts.

###### Article 1241

Where a writing is required for the validity of a contract, whether under private signature or by authentic act, it may be established and preserved in electronic form, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions such as to guarantee not only its integrity but also the link between the electronic signature and the act to which it is attached.
The reliability of an electronic signature process is presumed until proven otherwise where that process implements a secure electronic signature, established by means of a secure electronic signature creation device and the verification of that signature is based on the use of a qualified electronic certificate.
Where a handwritten mention by the person who binds himself is required, the latter may affix it in electronic form if the conditions of such affixing are such as to guarantee that it can only be done by himself.

###### Article 1242

Exception is made to the provisions of the preceding article for:
1° Acts under private signature relating to family law and succession law;
2° Acts under private signature relating to personal or real security interests, of a civil or commercial nature.

###### Article 1243

The requirement of sending in several copies is deemed satisfied electronically if the writing can be printed by the recipient.

###### Article 1244

The requirement of a detachable form is satisfied by an electronic process which allows access to the form and its return by the same means.

###### Article 1245

Contracts must be negotiated, formed and performed in good faith. This provision is a matter of public order.

###### Article 1246

Contracts, whether they have a specific designation or not, are subject to general rules, which are the subject of this title.
The particular rules for certain contracts are established in the provisions specific to each of them; the general rules apply subject to these particular rules.

###### Article 1247

A contract is synallagmatic or bilateral when the contracting parties mutually bind themselves to one another, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.
It is unilateral when one or more persons are bound to one or more others, without there being any reciprocal commitment on the part of the latter.

###### Article 1248

A contract is commutative when each of the parties undertakes to provide the other with an advantage which is regarded as the equivalent of that which it receives.
It is aleatory when the equivalent consists in the chance of gain or loss for each of the parties, according to an uncertain event.

###### Article 1249

A contract is for valuable consideration when each of the parties receives from the other an advantage in return for that which it provides.
It is gratuitous or of beneficence when one of the parties provides the other with an advantage without expecting or receiving any consideration in return.

###### Article 1250

A contract is consensual when it is formed by the mere exchange of consents without the expression of will having to take a particular form.
A contract is solemn when it requires for its validity, in addition to the agreement of wills, compliance with forms determined by law.

A contract is real when its formation is subject to the delivery of a thing.

###### Article 1251

A contract by mutual agreement is one whose stipulations are freely negotiated between the parties.

A contract of adhesion is one whose general conditions, removed from negotiation, are determined in advance by one of the parties who proposes them to the other.

###### Article 1252

A framework contract is an agreement by which the parties agree on the general characteristics of their future contractual relations. It subsequently incorporates application contracts, which specify the terms of performance.

###### Article 1253

A contract with instantaneous performance is one whose obligations can be performed in a single performance.
A contract with successive performance is one whose obligations of at least one party are performed in several performances spread over time.

#### Chapter II: Formation of the Contract

##### Section I: Contractual Negotiation Article 1254

The initiation, conduct and termination of pre-contractual negotiations are free. They must imperatively satisfy the requirements of good faith.
It is always possible to break off pre-contractual negotiations, except in the case of abrupt termination or termination without legitimate reason.
In the event of fault committed in the negotiations, the reparation of the damage is of an extra-contractual nature. In the event of an agreement in principle, by which the parties undertake to continue a negotiation, in order to reach the conclusion of a contract whose conditions remain to be defined, a contractual obligation to negotiate in good faith arises. Consequently, the termination of the negotiation must be justified. Failing this, damages may be awarded on the basis of contractual liability.

In all cases, the reparation awarded cannot have the purpose of compensating for the loss of the advantages expected from the contract not concluded.

###### Article 1255

The party who knows information of decisive importance for the consent of the other party must inform the other party of it where the latter legitimately does not know this information or places trust in its co-contractor. Information of decisive importance is information that has a direct and necessary link with the content of the contract or the quality of the parties; however, the duty to inform does not extend to the estimation of the value of the performance.  
The parties may neither limit nor exclude this duty.  

It is incumbent upon the person who claims that information was owed to him to prove that the other party owed it to him, and it is for that other party to prove that it provided it.  
In addition to the liability of the person who was bound by it, breach of this duty to inform may result in annulment of the contract under the conditions provided for in Articles 1283 and following.

###### Article 1256

A person who uses or discloses without authorization confidential information obtained during negotiations incurs liability under the conditions of ordinary law.

##### Section II: The Meeting of Consents

###### § 1. Offer and Acceptance Article 1257

A contract is formed by the meeting of an offer and an acceptance by which the parties
express their will to be bound.  

A declaration of will, made expressly and without formality, is sufficient to be bound. The will to be bound may also be expressed tacitly or implicitly, when it results from unequivocal conduct of its author.

###### Article 1258

A proposal to conclude a contract, addressed to one or more determinate persons or to an indeterminate person, constitutes an offer if it is sufficiently precise and if it indicates the will of its author to be bound in the event of acceptance.  
A proposal is sufficiently precise when it contains the essential elements of the contemplated contract. Failing that, there is only an invitation to enter into negotiations.

###### Article 1259

An offer takes effect as soon as it reaches its addressee. It is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made to him verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.  
An offer may be freely revoked, provided that the revocation reaches the addressee before the latter has dispatched his acceptance. However, an offer may not be revoked if it specifies that it is irrevocable or if it fixes a determinate period for its acceptance. Revocation of the offer in violation of this prohibition prevents the conclusion of the contract. It engages the extra-contractual liability of its author under the conditions of ordinary law without obliging him to compensate for the loss of the advantages expected from the contract.  

An offer, even if irrevocable, comes to an end when its rejection reaches the author of the offer.

###### Article 1260

An offer lapses upon expiry of the period fixed by its author or, failing that, at the end of a reasonable period.  
It also lapses in the event of incapacity or death of its author.

###### Article 1261

A declaration or any other conduct of the addressee indicating that he intends to be bound by the terms of the offer made, constitutes an acceptance.  
The silence or inaction of the person alleged to be bound cannot alone, in the absence of any other circumstance, serve as proof against him of the alleged obligation. It is otherwise when the law, usages, business relations or particular circumstances give the value of acceptance to silence maintained.

###### Article 1262

When the author of the offer has fixed a period for acceptance in a letter, that period begins to run, unless otherwise indicated in the letter, from the day of dispatch of the offer, the postmark serving as proof. The period for acceptance that the author of the offer fixes by telephone, by telex, by facsimile, by email or by any other means of instantaneous communication begins to run at the moment when the offer reaches the addressee.

###### Article 1263

The law or the contract may provide, on the one hand, for a period of reflection for the benefit of the addressee of the offer, which is the period before the expiry of which the latter may not express his acceptance, or on the other hand, for a period of withdrawal, which is the period before the expiry of which its beneficiary may withdraw his consent.

###### Article 1264

Acceptance takes effect at the moment when the agreement issued by the acceptor reaches the author of the offer. Acceptance does not take effect if that indication does not reach the author of the offer within the period he has stipulated or, failing stipulation, within a reasonable period, having regard to the circumstances surrounding the contemplated transaction and the means of communication used by the author of the offer.  

An acceptance is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made to him verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.  
A verbal offer must be accepted immediately, unless the circumstances imply the contrary.

###### Article 1265

A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additional or different elements not substantially altering the terms of the offer, constitutes an acceptance.  
A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additions, limitations or other substantial modifications to the terms of the offer, must be considered as a rejection of the offer and constitutes a counter-offer.

###### Article 1266

Acceptance may be freely withdrawn, provided that the withdrawal reaches the author of the offer before the moment when the acceptance would have taken effect.

###### Article 1267

General conditions invoked by one party have effect with regard to the other only if they have been brought to the knowledge of the latter and if the latter has accepted them.  
In the event of discordance between general conditions invoked by one and the other of the parties, the incompatible clauses have no effect.  

In the event of discordance between general conditions and particular conditions, the latter prevail over the former.

###### Article 1268

A contract is concluded at the moment when acceptance of an offer takes effect in accordance with these provisions, thus perfecting the meeting of wills.

###### Article 1269

A contract is concluded at the place where the acceptance reached.

###### Article 1270

When it is concluded by electronic means, a contract is valid only if the addressee of the offer has had the possibility of verifying the details of his order and its total price and of correcting any errors before confirming it to express his final acceptance.  
The author of the offer must acknowledge receipt without unjustified delay, by electronic means, of the order that has been addressed to him.  
The order, the confirmation of acceptance of the offer and the acknowledgment of receipt are considered received when the parties to whom they are addressed can have access to them.

###### § 2. Representation Article 1271

Representation is the power recognized in a person, the representative, to act in the name and on behalf of another, the represented person. The representative does not become a party to the contract.  

This power is of legal, judicial or conventional origin. Conventional representation has its source in the contract of mandate.  

This power is either special and for one matter or certain matters only, or general and for all the matters of the represented person. A mandate conceived in general terms embraces only acts of administration.

###### Article 1272

The legal, judicial or conventional representative is entitled to act only within the limits of the powers conferred upon them.

###### Article 1273

Representation is perfect when the representative acts within the limits of their powers and declares to act in the name and on behalf of the represented party. In such case, only the represented party is bound by the commitment entered into and the contract concluded by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.  
Representation is imperfect when the representative does not disclose to the third party the name of their principal. In such case, they alone are bound towards the contracting party.

###### Article 1274

The represented party is not bound by what has been done without authority or beyond the authority given to the representative. The same applies when the representative misuses their powers to the detriment of the represented party. A person who was unaware of the absence, excess or misuse of authority, or could not have been unaware of it, may bring an action for relative nullity of the contract, without prejudice to damages which may where appropriate be claimed from the representative.  
By way of exception, the represented party is bound by the act concluded when the contracting third party could legitimately believe in the reality of the representative's powers, particularly by reason of the conduct or statements of the represented party.  

These provisions do not exclude the application of the rules specific to management of another's affairs.  
The represented party may ratify the act concluded without authority or beyond the authority given, or confirm the act accomplished by misuse of authority. In such cases, the contract concluded by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.

###### Article 1275

The establishment of legal or judicial representation divests the represented party, for its duration, of the powers transferred to the representative.  
Conventional representation leaves the represented party with the exercise of their rights.

###### Article 1276

The powers of the representative cease if they become incapable or are struck by incapacity during the performance of the mandate. These powers also end with the death of the representative.

###### Article 1277

A representative may not act on behalf of both parties to the contract nor contract on their own account with the represented party.  
The act accomplished is null and void, by relative nullity, by the mere fact of breach of the rule provided for in the preceding paragraph, unless the law authorizes it or the represented party has authorized or ratified it.

##### Section III : Le pacte de préférence et la promesse unilatérale de contrat

###### Article 1278

A pact of preference is a promise made by one person to another, who accepts it, to offer them priority in concluding a contract of a specified nature, in the event that the promisor decides one day to conclude such a contract.

###### Article 1279

When a contract is concluded with a third party in violation of a pact of preference, the beneficiary of the pact may obtain compensation for the prejudice suffered. If the third party knew of the existence of the pact and the beneficiary's intention to rely on it, the latter may, in addition, ask the judge to annul the contract concluded with the third party and to substitute themselves for the third party in the contract concluded; they must bring this action within six months of becoming aware of the violation of the pact of preference.  
The third party may request in writing that the beneficiary of the pact confirm within two months the existence of a pact of preference and whether they intend to rely on it. The writing mentions that in the absence of a response within this period, the beneficiary of the pact may no longer seek their substitution in the contract concluded with the third party.

###### Article 1280

A unilateral promise of contract is the act by which one person, the promisor, undertakes towards another, the beneficiary, who accepts it, to grant them, for a certain period, the right to opt for the conclusion of a contract whose essential elements are already determined, and for the formation of which only the consent of the beneficiary is lacking.  
The definitive contract is formed as soon as the option is exercised. The revocation of the promise during the time left to the beneficiary to opt does not prevent the formation of the promised contract.  

A contract concluded in violation of the unilateral promise with a third party who knew of its existence is null and void. The beneficiary of the promise may, in addition to all damages in compensation for the prejudice suffered, ask the judge for their substitution for the third party in the contract concluded.

#### Chapitre III : Des conditions de validité des contrats Article 1281

Four conditions are essential for the validity of a contract: 1° Real, informed and free consent of the parties;  
2° Their capacity to contract; 3° A certain and lawful object;  
4° A lawful cause.

##### Section I : Du consentement Article 1282

There is no contract if there is no consent.

###### Article 1283

Error, fraud and duress vitiate consent when they are of such a nature that, without them, one of the parties would not have contracted or would have contracted on substantially different terms.  
Their decisive character as a defect of consent is assessed having regard to the persons and the circumstances in which consent was given.

###### Article 1284

Absence of consent and defects of consent are a cause of relative nullity of the contract.

###### Article 1285

Error of law or fact, unless it is inexcusable, is a cause of nullity of the contract when it relates to the essential qualities of the performance due by one or other of the parties.  
Error is not a cause of nullity when it relates only to the person with whom one intends to contract, unless the consideration of that person is the principal cause of the agreement.  

Essential are the qualities in consideration of which both parties contracted, or, similarly, the qualities in consideration of which one of them contracted, to the knowledge of the other. These expected qualities are those which have been expressly or tacitly agreed upon by the parties to the act.  

The acceptance of a risk concerning a quality of the performance excludes error relating to that quality.

###### Article 1286

Error as to a simple motive, unrelated to the essential qualities of the performance due or of the contracting party, is not a cause of nullity, unless the parties, rather than making this motive a condition of their agreement, have expressly made it a decisive element of their consent.

###### Article 1287

Error as to value by which, without being mistaken as to the essential qualities of the performance, a contracting party merely makes an incorrect economic assessment of it, is not a cause of nullity.

###### Article 1288

Fraud is the act by one party of obtaining the consent of the other by maneuvers or lies in order to obtain the conclusion of a legal act.  
Also constitutes fraud the concealment by one of the parties of information which they know to be decisive for the other. Nevertheless, the failure by a party to disclose to their contracting party their estimation of the value of the performance does not constitute fraud.

###### Article 1289

Fraud is also constituted if it emanates from the representative, manager of another's affairs, agent or surety of a party.  
It is also constituted when it emanates from a third party in collusion.

###### Article 1290

Error resulting from fraud is always excusable; it is a cause of nullity even if it relates to the value of the performance or to a simple motive of the contract.

###### Article 1291

A person who is the victim of fraud may bring an action for nullity, seek only damages, or, where appropriate, both.

###### Article 1292

Violence is the act by which a party or a third party infringes upon the free consent of another, by inspiring in them the fear of exposing their person, their fortune or those of their relatives to considerable harm.

###### Article 1293

Mere reverential fear towards one's father, mother, or other ascendant, without any violence having been exercised, is not sufficient to annul the contract.

###### Article 1294

The threat of legal action does not constitute violence, except in case of abuse. Abuse is characterized when the legal action is diverted from its purpose or when it is invoked or exercised to obtain a manifestly excessive advantage.

###### Article 1295

There is also violence when a party, abusing the situation of weakness in which its co-contractor finds themselves, obtains from them a commitment that they would not have entered into in the absence of such constraint and derives a manifestly excessive advantage therefrom.

###### Article 1296

The limitation period for the action for nullity runs, in case of error or fraud, only from the day on which they were discovered and, in case of violence, only from the day on which it ceased.  
A contract can no longer be challenged if, since the defect of error or fraud was discovered by the person who was the victim thereof or since the violence ceased, that contract has been approved by them, either expressly, or tacitly, or by allowing the time for restitution fixed by law to pass.

##### Section II : De la capacité des parties contractantes Article 1297

Any natural person may contract except in case of incapacity provided for by law.  

Legal persons contract through their representatives. In this regard, the capacity of legal persons is limited to acts useful for the realization of their object as defined by their statutes and to acts accessory thereto, in compliance with the rules applicable to each of them.

###### Article 1298

The following are incapable of contracting, to the extent defined by law:
1° Unemancipated minors;  
2° Protected adults within the meaning of article 565 of this code.

###### Article 1299

Any person incapable of contracting may nevertheless accomplish alone the ordinary acts authorized by law or usage.

###### Article 1300

Ordinary acts accomplished by a minor may be annulled for simple lesion. But nullity is not incurred when the lesion results from an unforeseeable event.  

The simple declaration of majority made by the minor does not prevent annulment. Likewise, an incapable person cannot be reproached for having remained silent or for having made a false declaration about their status.  

A minor cannot escape the commitments they have made in the exercise of their profession.

###### Article 1301

Acts accomplished by protected adults are governed by articles 574, 602 and 621 without prejudice to articles 1299, 1304 and 1581.

###### Article 1302

Incapacity to contract is a ground for relative nullity that only the incapable co-contractor may invoke.

###### Article 1303

Except with judicial authorization, it is prohibited, on pain of nullity, for anyone exercising a function or occupying a position in an establishment housing elderly persons or dispensing psychiatric care to become the purchaser, directly or through an intermediary, of property or assignee of a right belonging to a person admitted to the establishment, nor to take a lease on the dwelling occupied by that person before their admission to the establishment.  
For the application of this article, the spouse, ascendants and descendants of the persons to whom the prohibitions set out above apply are deemed to be intermediaries.

###### Article 1304

The co-contractor of the incapable person may prevent the action for nullity brought against them by establishing that the act was useful to the protected person and free from lesion or that it benefited them.  
They may also oppose to the action for nullity the confirmation of the act by their co-contractor who has become or become again capable.

###### Article 1305

The limitation period for the action runs:
1° With regard to acts done by a minor, from the day of majority or emancipation;  
2° With regard to acts done by a protected adult, from the day on which they became aware of them while in a position to validly redo them;  
3° With regard to the heirs of the person under guardianship or curatorship or of the person subject to family authorization, from the day of death if it had not begun to run previously.

##### Section III : De l'objet et de la matière des contrats Article 1306

The object of the contract is that to which the parties have obligated themselves. It may be an obligation to do, not to do, or to give.

###### Article 1307

Only things that are in commerce may be the object of a legal act. A legal act may not derogate from public policy either by its stipulations or by its purpose, whether or not the latter was known by all the parties.

###### Article 1308

The obligation has as its object a present or future performance. However, one cannot renounce a succession that has not been opened, nor make any stipulation concerning such a succession, even with the consent of the person whose succession is concerned.  

It must be possible and determined or determinable.  

The performance is determinable when it can be deduced from the contract or by reference to usages or to the prior relations of the parties, without a new agreement of the parties being necessary.

###### Article 1309

Lesion, economic imbalance between reciprocal performances, opens the way to an action for nullity only when the law so provides.

###### Article 1310

In framework contracts and contracts with successive performance, it may be agreed that the price will be fixed unilaterally by one of the parties, provided that they justify the amount in case of dispute.  
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request seeking damages and if appropriate the termination of the contract. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1311

In service contracts, in the absence of agreement of the parties before their performance, the price may be fixed by the creditor, provided that they justify the amount in case of dispute.  
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request for damages. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1312

When the quality of the performance is not determined or determinable under the contract, the debtor must offer a performance of quality conforming to the legitimate expectations of the parties in consideration of its nature, usages and the amount of the consideration.

###### Article 1313

When the price or any other element of the contract must be determined by reference to an index that does not exist or has ceased to exist or to be accessible, it is replaced by the index that most closely approximates it.

##### Section IV : De la cause Article 1314

An obligation without cause, or based on a false cause, or on an unlawful cause, can have no effect.

###### Article 1315

Any clause that deprives the debtor's essential obligation of its substance is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1316

A contract for valuable consideration is null when, at the time of its formation, the consideration agreed upon for the benefit of the person who commits themselves is illusory or derisory.

###### Article 1317

In a contract of adhesion, any clause that creates a significant imbalance between the rights and obligations of the parties to the contract is deemed unwritten.  
The assessment of significant imbalance relates neither to the principal object of the contract nor to the adequacy of the price to the performance.

###### Article 1318

The agreement is no less valid even though the cause is not expressed therein.

###### Article 1319

The cause is unlawful when it is prohibited by law, when it is contrary to public morals or to public order.

##### Section V

Sanctions for non-compliance with the conditions of validity of contracts Sub-section 1: Nullity

###### Article 1320

A contract that does not meet the conditions required for its validity is null and void. Nullity must be pronounced by the judge, unless the parties acknowledge it by mutual agreement.  
The annulled contract is deemed never to have existed.  
The performances executed give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in articles 1577 to 1585.  

Independently of the annulment of the contract, the injured party may claim compensation for the damage suffered under the conditions of the general law of extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1321

Nullity is absolute when the violated rule has as its object the safeguarding of the general interest. It is relative when the violated rule has as its sole object the safeguarding of a private interest.
