The creditor may also act in his own name, by way of the Paulian action, to have acts performed by his debtor in fraud of his rights declared unenforceable against him, provided he establishes, if it concerns an act for valuable consideration, that the third-party co-contractor had knowledge of the fraud.  
The action is available when the debtor has performed an act of impoverishment aimed at organizing his insolvency or making the creditor's enforcement more difficult. It is also available when the creditor has a special right over property of the debtor and the latter performs an act that has the effect of impairing that special right.  

The claim must be certain on the day the action is brought. The enforceability and liquidity of the claim are not a condition of the Paulian action.

###### Article 1529

In cases determined by law, the creditor may act directly for payment of his claim against a debtor of his debtor.

#### Chapter IV

The Extinction of the Obligation Section I: Payment

###### Subsection 1: General Provisions

###### Article 1530

Payment is the voluntary performance of the due obligation.  

It must be made as soon as the debt becomes enforceable; it may be made even by a person not bound thereto, except in case of legitimate refusal by the creditor.  
Payment releases the debtor towards the creditor and extinguishes the debt, except where the law or the contract provides for subrogation to the rights of the creditor.

###### Article 1531

Payment must be made to the creditor or to the person designated to receive it.  

Payment made to a person who did not have authority to receive it is nevertheless valid if the creditor ratifies it or has benefited therefrom.  
Payment made to a creditor incapable of contracting is not valid, unless he has benefited therefrom.

###### Article 1532

Payment made in good faith to an apparent creditor is valid.

###### Article 1533

The creditor may refuse partial payment even if the obligation is divisible. He may accept to receive in payment something other than what is owed to him.

###### Article 1534

The debtor of an obligation to deliver a specific thing is released by its delivery to the creditor in its condition, except to prove, in case of deterioration, that it is not due to his act or to that of persons for whom he must answer.  

If the debt is of a thing determined only by its kind, the debtor shall not be required, to be released, to give it of the best kind; but he may not offer it of the worst kind.

###### Article 1535

In the absence of another designation by law, contract or judge, payment must be made at the domicile of the debtor.

###### Article 1536

The costs of payment are, unless otherwise provided by law or clause, borne by the debtor.

###### Article 1537

Payment is proved by any means.

###### Article 1538

The voluntary delivery by the creditor to the debtor of the original under private signature or of the enforceable copy of the title of his claim constitutes a simple presumption of release.  
The same delivery to one of the joint and several co-debtors produces the same effect towards all.

###### Article 1539

The debtor of several debts may indicate, when he pays, which one he intends to discharge.  

In the absence of indication by the debtor, imputation takes place as follows: first on debts that have fallen due; among these, on debts which the debtor had the greatest interest in discharging. Where interests are equal, imputation is made on the oldest; all things being equal, it is made proportionally.

###### Sous-section 2 : Special provisions for monetary obligations

###### Article 1540

The debtor of a monetary obligation is discharged by payment of its nominal amount. The amount of the sum due may however vary through indexation or debts of value.  
A debt of value is an obligation which has as its object, not a determined sum of money, but a value which may give rise, according to the time, to different assessments, such as a debt of reparation which is determined on the day of judgment and not on the day of the harmful act. The debtor of a debt of value is discharged by payment of the sum of money resulting from its liquidation.

###### Article 1541

When the monetary obligation bears interest, the debtor is discharged by paying the principal and the interest. Partial payment is imputed first to the interest, unless otherwise agreed.  
Interest is granted by law or stipulated in the contract. The rate of contractual interest must be fixed in writing. It is deemed annual by default.

###### Article 1542

Accrued interest, due for at least one full year, bears interest if the contract so provides or if a court decision so specifies.

###### Article 1543

Payment, in Djibouti, of a monetary obligation is made in Djibouti Francs. However, payment may be made in another currency if the obligation so denominated arises from an international contract or a foreign judgment.

###### Article 1544

In the absence of another designation by law, contract or judge, the place of payment of the monetary obligation is the domicile of the creditor.

###### Article 1545

The judge may, taking into account the situation of the debtor and in consideration of the needs of the creditor, defer or schedule, within the limit of two years, the payment of sums due.  
By special and reasoned decision, he may order that the sums corresponding to deferred instalments shall bear interest at a reduced rate at least equal to the legal rate, or that payments shall be imputed first to the capital.  

He may make these measures conditional upon the debtor's performance of acts designed to facilitate or guarantee payment of the debt.  
The judge's decision suspends enforcement proceedings that may have been initiated by the creditor. Interest increases or penalties provided for in case of delay are not incurred during the period fixed by the judge.  

Any stipulation to the contrary is deemed unwritten.  
The provisions of this article do not apply to maintenance debts.

###### Sous-section 3 : Notice to perform

###### Article 1546

Notice to perform is the act by which either the creditor clearly indicates to his debtor that he does not intend to allow contractual non-performance to continue, or the debtor enjoins his creditor not to obstruct performance of the contract.

###### § 1. Notice to perform served on the debtor Article 1547

The debtor is given notice to pay either by a summons or an act containing sufficient demand, or, if the contract so provides, by the mere enforceability of the obligation.

###### Article 1548

Notice to perform to pay a monetary obligation causes default interest to run, at the legal rate. The creditor need not prove any loss.

###### Article 1549

Notice to perform to deliver a thing places the risks on the debtor, if they are not already there.

###### § 2

Notice to perform served on the creditor or "tender of payment" Article 1550
When the creditor, at maturity and without legitimate reason, refuses to receive the payment due to him or prevents it by his act, the debtor may give him notice to accept it or to permit its performance. This notice to perform constitutes a tender of payment.  
Notice to perform served on the creditor stops the running of interest due by the debtor and places the risks of the thing on the creditor, if they are not already there. It is otherwise in case of gross or fraudulent fault of the debtor.  

Notice to perform does not interrupt prescription.

###### Article 1551

If the obstruction has not ended within two months of the notice to perform, the debtor may, when the obligation relates to a sum of money, deposit it with the registry of the Court of First Instance or, when the obligation relates to the delivery of a thing, sequester it with a professional custodian.  
If sequestration of the thing is impossible or too costly, the judge may authorize its private sale or sale by public auction. After deduction of the costs of sale, the price is deposited with the registry of the Court of First Instance.  

Deposit or sequestration discharges the debtor from the time of their notification to the creditor.

###### Article 1552

When the obligation relates to another object, for example an obligation to do, the debtor is discharged if the obstruction has not ceased within two months of the notice to perform.

###### Article 1553

The costs of notice to perform and of deposit or sequestration are borne by the creditor.

###### Sous-section 4 : Payment with subrogation

###### Article 1554

Subrogation occurs by operation of law alone in favor of one who, having a legitimate interest, pays insofar as his payment discharges, towards the creditor, the person who is liable for the final burden of all or part of the debt.

###### Article 1555

Conventional subrogation is effected at the initiative of the creditor when the latter, receiving his payment from a third person, subrogates him to his rights against the debtor.  
This subrogation must be express.  

It must be granted at the same time as the payment, unless, in a prior act, the subrogor has manifested the intention that his contracting party be subrogated to him upon payment. The concomitance of the subrogation and the payment may be proved by any means.

###### Article 1556

Subrogation also occurs when the debtor, borrowing a sum for the purpose of paying his debt, subrogates the lender to the rights of the creditor with the latter's concurrence. In this case, the subrogation must be express and the receipt given by the creditor must indicate the origin of the funds.  
Subrogation may be granted without the concurrence of the creditor, but on condition that the debt is due or that the term is in favor of the debtor. It is then necessary that the loan agreement and the receipt be executed before a notary, that in the loan agreement it be declared that the sum has been borrowed to make the payment, and that in the receipt it be declared that the payment has been made from the sums paid for that purpose by the new creditor.

###### Article 1557

Subrogation cannot harm the creditor when he has been paid only in part; in this case, he may exercise his rights, for what remains due to him, in preference to the person from whom he has received only partial payment.  
Subrogation transfers to its beneficiary, within the limit of what he has paid, the claim and its accessories, with the exception of rights exclusively attached to the person of the creditor.  

However, the subrogee is entitled only to legal interest from the time of notice to perform, if he has not agreed with the debtor on a new interest. This interest is guaranteed by the security interests attached to the claim, within the limits, when they have been created by third parties, of their initial commitments if they do not consent to be bound beyond.

###### Article 1558

The debtor may invoke subrogation as soon as he becomes aware of it, but it may only be enforced against him if it has been notified to him or if he has acknowledged it.  
Subrogation is enforceable against third parties from the time of payment.  
The debtor may raise against the subrogated creditor defenses inherent to the debt, such as nullity, the defense of non-performance, termination or set-off of related debts. He may also raise against him defenses arising from his relations with the subrogor before the subrogation became enforceable against him, such as the granting of a term, remission of debt or set-off of unrelated debts.

##### Section II : Set-off

###### Sous-section 1 : General Rules Article 1559

Set-off is the simultaneous extinction of reciprocal obligations between two persons.  

It operates, subject to being invoked, to the extent applicable, on the date when its conditions are met.

###### Article 1560

Subject to the provisions set out in the following subsection, set-off only occurs between two fungible, certain, liquidated and due obligations.  
Fungible are obligations of sums of money, even in different currencies, provided they are convertible, or those having as their object a quantity of things of the same kind.

###### Article 1561

Unseizable claims and obligations to restore a deposit, a loan for use or a thing of which the owner has been unjustly deprived may only be set off if the creditor consents thereto.

###### Article 1562

A grace period does not prevent set-off.

###### Article 1563

If there are several debts that may be set off, the rules for imputation of payments in articles 1392, 1394 and 1398 are transposable.

###### Article 1564

The debtor who has acknowledged without reservation the assignment of the claim may not raise against the assignee the set-off that he could have raised against the assignor.

###### Article 1565

The surety may raise against the creditor the set-off that occurred between the latter and the principal debtor.  

The joint and several co-debtor may rely on the set-off that occurred between the creditor and one of his co-obligors to have the divisible share of the latter deducted from the total debt.

###### Article 1566

Set-off does not prejudice rights acquired by third parties.

###### Sous-section 2 : Special Rules Article 1567

Set-off may be ordered by the court even if one of the obligations, although certain, is not yet liquidated or due. Unless otherwise decided, set-off then produces its effects on the date of the decision.

###### Article 1568

The judge may not refuse set-off of related debts on the sole ground that one of the obligations is not liquidated or due.  
In that case, set-off is deemed to have occurred on the day when the first of them became due.  
In the same case, the acquisition of rights by a third party over one of the obligations does not prevent its debtor from raising set-off.

###### Article 1569

The parties may freely agree to extinguish all reciprocal obligations, present or future, by set-off; this takes effect on the date of their agreement or, in the case of future obligations, on the date of their coexistence.

##### Section III : Merger Article 1570

Merger results from the union of the capacities of creditor and debtor of the same obligation in the same person. It extinguishes the claim and its accessories, subject to rights acquired by or against third parties.

###### Article 1571

Where there is joint and several liability among several debtors or among several creditors, and the merger concerns only one of them, extinction occurs, with respect to the others, only for his share.  
Where the merger concerns a secured obligation, the surety, even if joint and several, is released. Where the merger concerns the obligation of one of the sureties, the principal debtor is not released. The other joint and several sureties are released to the extent of that surety's share.

##### Section IV : Remission of Debt Article 1572

Remission of debt is the contract by which the creditor releases the debtor from his obligation.

###### Article 1573

Remission of debt granted to one of the joint and several co-debtors releases the others to the extent of his share.  

Remission of debt made by only one of the joint and several creditors releases the debtor only for the share of that creditor.

###### Article 1574

Remission of debt granted to the principal debtor releases the sureties, even if joint and several.  

Remission granted to one of the joint and several sureties does not release the principal debtor, but releases the others to the extent of his share.  

What the creditor has received from a surety for the discharge of his suretyship must be imputed to the debt and discharge the principal debtor proportionally. The other sureties remain liable only after deduction of the share of the released surety or of the value provided if it exceeds that share.

##### Section V : Impossibility of Performance Article 1575

Impossibility of performing the obligation releases the debtor to the extent applicable when it proceeds from a case of force majeure and is definitive, unless he has agreed to assume it or has been previously placed in default.

###### Article 1576

Where the impossibility of performance results from the loss of the thing due, the debtor placed in default is nevertheless released if he proves that the loss would likewise have occurred if the obligation had been performed. He is however bound to assign to his creditor the rights and actions attached to the thing.

#### Chapter V : Restitutions

###### Article 1577

Restitution of a thing other than a sum of money takes place in kind or, where that is impossible, in value, estimated on the day of restitution.

###### Article 1578

The person who restores the thing is liable for damage and deterioration that have diminished its value, unless he is in good faith and they are not due to his fault.

###### Article 1579

The person who, having received the thing in good faith, has sold it, need only restore the sale price.  

If he received it in bad faith, he owes its value on the day of restitution when it is greater than the price.

###### Article 1580

Restitution includes the fruits and the value of the enjoyment that the thing has provided. The value of the enjoyment is assessed by the judge on the day he rules.  
Unless otherwise stipulated, restitution of fruits, if they are not found in kind, takes place according to a value estimated on the date of reimbursement, according to the state of the thing on the day of payment of the obligation.

###### Article 1581

Restitutions due to an unemancipated minor or to a protected adult are reduced in proportion to the benefit he has derived from the annulled act.

###### Article 1582

To determine the amount of restitutions, account is taken for the person who must restore, even if he is in bad faith, of necessary and useful expenses for the preservation of the thing, within the limit of the increased value estimated on the day of restitution.

###### Article 1583

Restitution of a sum of money includes interest at the legal rate and taxes paid into the hands of the person who received it.

###### Article 1584

The person who received in bad faith owes interest, the fruits he has received or the value of the enjoyment from the time of payment. The person who received in good faith owes them only from the day of the demand.

###### Article 1585

Restitution of a service takes place in value. This is assessed on the date on which it was provided.  
Securities constituted for payment of the obligation are transferred by operation of law to the obligation to restore without however depriving the surety of the benefit of the term.

### Title V: Civil Proof

###### Article 1586

The burden of proof lies with the person who claims recognition of a right or the performance of an obligation.  
Conversely, the person who claims to be released must justify the fact that produced the extinction of the right asserted against him.  

The judicial administration of evidence and disputes relating thereto are governed by the code of civil procedure.  

Chapter I: The Admissibility of Modes of Proof Article 1587
Except in cases where the law provides otherwise, proof may be adduced by any means.

###### Article 1588

A juridical act relating to a sum or value exceeding the sum or value of 100,000 FD must be proved by writing under private signature or authentic instrument.  
Proof may not be adduced beyond or against a writing establishing a juridical act, even if the sum or value does not exceed that amount, except by another writing under private signature or authentic instrument.  
A person whose claim exceeds the threshold mentioned in the first paragraph may not be dispensed from proof in writing by restricting his demand.  

The same applies to a person whose demand, even if less than that amount, relates to the balance or part of a claim exceeding that amount.

###### Article 1589

The rules provided for in Article 1588 are subject to exception:	in case of material or moral impossibility of obtaining a writing,	if it is customary not to establish a writing,	or when the writing has been lost as a result of an external cause.

###### Article 1590

Writing may also be substituted by judicial admission, the decisive oath or a commencement of proof in writing corroborated by another means of proof.

###### Article 1591

Any written act emanating from the person against whom the claim is made, or from the person he represents, and which makes the alleged fact plausible, constitutes a commencement of proof in writing.  
Statements made by a party during his personal appearance, his refusal to answer or his absence from the appearance may be considered by the judge as equivalent to a commencement of proof in writing.  

The mention of an authentic or privately signed writing in a public register is equivalent to a commencement of proof in writing.

#### Chapter II: Proof in Writing

##### Section I: General Provisions

###### Article 1592

No one may constitute title for himself.

###### Article 1593

Proof of a juridical act may be preconstituted by a writing in authentic form or under private signature.  
When a party does not know how to read, write or sign, if it concerns an authentic act, the public officer shall have the fingerprints of that person affixed to the act after having read it to him and asked whether he consents thereto. If it concerns an act under private signature, the person who does not know how to read, write or sign first chooses a person of his choice who reads the act to him, then affixes his fingerprint on the said act, and finally the chosen person signs the act as a witness.

###### Article 1594

Writing consists of a sequence of letters, characters, numbers or any other signs or symbols endowed with intelligible meaning, whatever their medium.

###### Article 1595

Electronic writing has the same probative force as writing on paper medium, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions likely to guarantee its integrity.

###### Article 1596

The signature necessary for the perfection of a juridical act identifies its author. It manifests his consent to the obligations arising from that act. When it is affixed by a public officer, it confers authenticity on the act.  
When it is electronic, it consists in the use of a reliable identification process guaranteeing its connection with the act to which it is attached.

###### Article 1597

In the absence of contrary provisions or agreements, the judge resolves conflicts of proof in writing by determining by any means the most plausible title.

##### Section II: The Authentic Act Article 1598

An authentic act is one that has been received, with the required solemnities, by a public officer having the right to execute instruments in the place where the act was drawn up.

###### Article 1599

An act that is not authentic due to the incompetence or incapacity of the officer, or due to a defect of form, is valid as a writing under private signature if it has been signed by the parties.

###### Article 1600

An authentic act is evidence until impugnment for forgery of what the public officer states he personally accomplished or observed.  
Nevertheless, in case of complaints for principal forgery, the execution of the act alleged to be forged shall be suspended by the indictment; and, in case of impugnment for forgery made incidentally, the courts may, according to the circumstances, provisionally suspend the execution of the act.

##### Section III: The Act Under Private Signature

###### Article 1601

An act under private signature, acknowledged by the party against whom it is invoked or legally held to be acknowledged with regard to him, is evidence between those who subscribed to it and with regard to their heirs and successors in title.

###### Article 1602

The person against whom an act under private signature is invoked is obliged to formally acknowledge or disavow his handwriting or signature.  
His heirs or successors in title may similarly disavow the handwriting or signature of their predecessor, or may content themselves with declaring that they do not know the handwriting or signature of their predecessor. In these cases, verification of handwriting is ordered in court.

###### Article 1603

An act under private signature that records a synallagmatic contract is proof only if it has been made in as many originals as there are parties having a distinct interest, unless the parties have agreed to deliver to a third party the single copy drawn up.  
One original suffices for all persons having the same interest.  

Each original must contain mention of the number of originals that have been made.  

A person who has performed the contract, even partially, may not invoke the lack of plurality of originals or of mention of their number.  
The requirement of a plurality of originals is deemed satisfied for contracts in electronic form when the act is established and preserved in accordance with Articles 1595 and 1596 second paragraph, and the process allows each party to have a copy on a durable medium or to have access to it.

###### Article 1604

An act under private signature by which a single party undertakes towards another to pay him a sum of money or to deliver a fungible good to him must include the signature of the person who subscribes to this undertaking as well as the mention, written by himself, of the sum or quantity in words and figures.  
If the party declares that he does not know how or cannot sign, express mention is made in the act of his declaration, as well as of the cause that prevents him from signing. The act bears his fingerprint.

###### Article 1605

When the sum expressed in the body of the act differs from that expressed by the handwritten mention, the act under private signature is proof for the sum written in words.

###### Article 1606

An act under private signature acquires certain date with regard to third parties only from the day it was registered, from the day of death of a signatory, or from the day its substance is recorded in an authentic act.

##### Section IV: Other Writings Article 1607

Registers and documents that professionals must keep or establish have, against their author, the same probative force as writings under private signature; but the person who relies on them may not divide the entries to retain only those that are favorable to him.

###### Article 1608

Personal registers and papers do not constitute proof in favour of the person who wrote them. They constitute proof against that person:
1° In all cases where they formally state a payment received;  
2° When they contain an express mention that the writing was made to make up for the absence of a title in favour of the person for whom they state an obligation.

###### Article 1609

The mention of a payment or other cause of discharge entered by the creditor on an original title which has always remained in his possession constitutes a simple presumption of discharge of the debtor.  
The same applies to a mention entered on the duplicate of a title or receipt, provided that this duplicate is in the hands of the debtor.

##### Section V : Les copies des titres Article 1610

Copies, when the original title exists, only constitute proof of what is contained in the title, the presentation of which may always be required.  
When the original title no longer exists, the reliable copy has the same probative force as the original. Reliability is left to the assessment of the judge. Nevertheless, the enforceable or authentic copy of an authentic writing is deemed reliable; the same applies to copies that were made by the authority of the magistrate, with the parties present or duly summoned, or to those that were made in the presence of the parties and with their mutual consent.  

Copies that the judge does not consider reliable may only serve as a commencement of proof in writing.  
Copies of copies may, depending on the circumstances, be considered as mere information.

###### Article 1611

The transcription of an act in public registers may only serve as a commencement of proof in writing; for this it will even be necessary:
1° That it be established that all the minutes of the notary, for the year in which the act appears to have been made, are lost, or that it be proved that the loss of the minute of this act was caused by a particular accident;  
2° That there exist a proper repertory of the notary, which establishes that the act was made on the same date.  
When, by means of the concurrence of these two circumstances, proof by witnesses is admitted, it will be necessary that those who were witnesses to the act, if they still exist, be heard.

##### Section VI : Les actes récognitifs Article 1612

The recognitive act is the juridical act which establishes the existence of a prior act without modifying its substance. It constitutes acknowledgment of the pre-existing obligation. The recognitive act does not dispense with the presentation of the original title, unless its content is specifically recited therein.  

What it contains that is additional or different from the original title has, in the absence of express intention to novate, no effect.  

Nevertheless, if there were several conforming acknowledgments, supported by possession, and one of which was dated thirty years ago, the creditor could be dispensed from producing the original title.

#### Chapitre III : La preuve par témoins Article 1613

The probative value of statements made by a third party under the conditions of the code of civil procedure is left to the assessment of the judge.

#### Chapitre IV : Les présomptions Article 1614

Presumptions are consequences that the law or the magistrate draws from a known fact to an unknown fact.

##### Section I : Les présomptions légales Article 1615

A legal presumption is one which is attached by law to certain acts or certain facts, and which holds them to be certain.  

It dispenses the person in whose favour it exists from providing proof thereof or shifts the object of proof.  

The presumption is said to be simple when the law reserves proof to the contrary; it is said to be irrefutable when it cannot be overturned.

###### Article 1616

The authority of res judicata only applies with respect to what was the subject of the judgment. It is necessary that the thing claimed be the same; that the claim be founded on the same cause; that the claim be between the same parties, and brought by them and against them in the same capacity.

###### Article 1617

Agreements on proof are valid when they relate to rights over which the parties have free disposal.  
Nevertheless, they cannot contradict irrefutable presumptions established by law, nor modify the faith attached to admission or oath. They cannot further establish an irrefutable presumption in favour of one of the parties.

##### Section II : Les présomptions judiciaires Article 1618

Judicial presumptions are not established by law, but are left to the assessment of the judge, who must only admit them if they are serious, precise and concordant, and only in cases where the law admits proof by any means.

#### Chapitre V : L'aveu de la partie

###### Article 1619

Admission is the declaration by which a person acknowledges as true a fact capable of producing legal consequences against that person.  
The admission that is opposed to a party is either extrajudicial or judicial.

###### Article 1620

A purely verbal extrajudicial admission is only received in cases where the law permits proof by any means.  
Its probative value is left to the assessment of the judge.

###### Article 1621

Judicial admission is the declaration made in court by the party or its representative specially mandated. It constitutes full proof against the person who made it.  
It cannot be divided against its author.  
It cannot be revoked, unless it is proved that it was the result of an error of fact; it could not be revoked on the pretext of an error of law.

#### Chapitre VI : Le serment Article 1622

The judicial oath is of two kinds:
1° That which one party refers to the other to make the judgment of the case depend on it: it is called decisory.  
2° That which is referred ex officio by the judge to one or the other of the parties.

##### Section I : Le serment décisoire Article 1623

The decisory oath may be referred in any kind of dispute whatsoever.

###### Article 1624

It may only be referred to a fact personal to the party to whom it is referred.

###### Article 1625

It may be referred at any stage of the case, and even when there exists no commencement of proof of the claim or exception on which it is invoked.

###### Article 1626

The oath may be referred back to the person who refers it, except when the fact which is its object is not that of both parties, but is purely personal to the person to whom the oath had been referred.

###### Article 1627

The person to whom the oath is referred, who refuses it or does not consent to refer it back to his adversary, or the adversary to whom it has been referred back and who refuses it, must fail in his claim or in his exception.

###### Article 1628

The oath only constitutes proof in favour of the person who referred it and of his heirs and successors in title, or against them.  

The oath referred by one of the joint and several creditors to the debtor only discharges the latter for the share of that creditor.  
The oath referred to the principal debtor also discharges the sureties. That referred to one of the joint and several debtors benefits the co-debtors.  
That referred to the surety benefits the principal debtor.  
In these last two cases, the oath of the joint and several co-debtor or of the surety only benefits the other co-debtors or the principal debtor when it has been referred to the debt, and not to the fact of joint and several liability or suretyship.

##### Section II : Le serment déféré d'office Article 1629

The judge may refer to one of the parties the oath, either to make the decision of the case depend on it, or only to determine the amount of the condemnation.

###### Article 1630

The judge may not defer the oath ex officio, either on the claim or on the defence raised against it, except under the following two conditions:
1. That the claim or defence is not fully proven;  
2. That it is not totally devoid of evidence.  
Outside these two cases, the judge must either grant or reject the claim purely and simply.

###### Article 1631

The oath deferred ex officio by the judge to one of the parties may not be referred by that party to the other.

###### Article 1632

The oath on the value of the thing claimed may be deferred by the judge to the claimant only when it is otherwise impossible to establish that value.  
The judge must even, in that case, determine the sum up to which the claimant will be believed on his oath.

### Titre VI : Du contrat de mariage et des régimes matrimoniaux

Chapitre Ier. Dispositions générales Article 1633
The law governs the conjugal partnership, as regards property, only in the absence of special agreements, which the spouses may make as they see fit, provided that they are not contrary either to public morals or to the provisions that follow.

###### Article 1634

The spouses, in the marriage certificate, indicate whether or not they have entered into a marriage contract.  

They declare whether they opt for the matrimonial regime of the civil code. Mention thereof is made in the marriage certificate.  

When they opt for the regime of the civil code, they indicate the matrimonial regime they choose. In the absence of stipulations in this regard, the spouses shall be subject to the regime of legal community (

###### article 1647

et suivants); and, with regard to third parties, the spouses shall be deemed married under this common law regime whenever they have seized the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or accept its jurisdiction when they are in defence, unless in the acts entered into with those third parties, they have declared having made a marriage contract falling under such regime as they have indicated to them.

###### Article 1635

The spouses may not derogate from the duties or rights that result for them from marriage or that are provided by law under the heading of parental authority and guardianship.

###### Article 1636

The spouses may not make any agreement or waiver the object of which would be to change the legal order of succession, without prejudice to inter vivos or testamentary gifts that may take place according to the forms and in the cases determined by this code.

###### Article 1637

The spouses may no longer stipulate in a general manner that their partnership will be governed by one of the customs, laws or local statutes that could govern the various parts of Djiboutian territory, and which are repealed by this code.

###### Article 1638

All matrimonial agreements shall be drawn up, before the marriage, by notarial deed, in the presence and with the simultaneous consent of the future spouses and all persons who are parties thereto or their agents. Matrimonial agreements take effect on the day of the celebration of the marriage and may not receive any change after that celebration.  
Changes or counter-letters that could be made to these agreements before the celebration of the marriage must be recorded by deed executed before a notary and in the presence and simultaneous consent of all persons who were parties thereto.

###### Article 1639

The notary delivers to the parties, at the time of signing the contract, a certificate on plain paper and without charge, stating his names and place of residence, the names, first names, capacities and residences of the future spouses, as well as the date of the contract. This certificate indicates that it must be delivered to the civil registrar before the celebration of the marriage, which the notary also recalls orally to the future spouses.  
In case of changes made to the initial deed, the notary drafts them following the original of the marriage contract; the notary may not issue either engrossments or copies of the marriage contract without transcribing following them the changes or counter-letters that may have been made thereto. In the absence of compliance with these formalities, the changes or counter-letters shall have no effect with regard to third parties.

###### Article 1640

The minor capable of contracting marriage may consent to all agreements of which this contract is susceptible; and the agreements and gifts he has made therein are valid, provided that he has been assisted, in the contract, by the persons whose consent is necessary for the validity of the marriage.  
The adult under guardianship or curatorship may enter into matrimonial agreements if he is assisted, in the contract, by his guardian or curator.  
If matrimonial agreements have been entered into without this assistance, annulment thereof may be requested by the incapable person or by the persons whose consent was required, but only for one year from the marriage.

###### Article 1641

Once the marriage has been celebrated, no change may be made to the matrimonial regime except by effect of a judgment:

1° When one of the spouses requests judicial separation of property by reason of disorder in the affairs or misconduct of the spouse jeopardizing his interests;  
2° When partial and temporary modifications to the rules setting the powers of the spouses are granted by the judge, such as when the other spouse is unable to manifest his will and judicial authorization to act without the consent of the other spouse is granted (

###### article 225

du présent code), or when judicial authorization to represent the other spouse has been decided (

###### article 227

du présent code), or in the case of transfer of powers over ordinary or reserved common property (

###### article 1671

du présent code), or transfer of powers over separate property (

###### article 1674 du présent code)

3° By effect of a notarial deed, if necessary approved by the judge, in the case of article 1642.

###### Article 1642

After two years of application of the matrimonial regime, the spouses may agree, in the interest of the family, to modify it, or even to change it entirely, by notarial deed. Mention of the modification is made on the original of the modified marriage contract and, on pain of nullity, the notarial deed contains the liquidation of the modified matrimonial regime if it is necessary.  
The persons who were parties to the modified contract and the adult children of each spouse are personally informed of the proposed modification; the creditors of the spouses are informed thereof by publication of a notice in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices. Each of them may oppose the modification within a period of three months.  

In case of opposition, the notarial deed is submitted for approval to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the domicile of the spouses. It is so submitted mandatorily when one or the other of the spouses has minor children. The application and the decision of approval are published.  

Non-opposing creditors, if their rights have been defrauded, may challenge the change of matrimonial regime to have this deed declared unenforceable against them, provided they establish, if it is an act for valuable consideration, that the third party co-contractor had knowledge of the fraud. They must specify how the contested fraudulent acts are related to the change of matrimonial regime, which is not in itself indicative of fraud

###### Article 1643

The change of matrimonial regime takes effect between the parties on the date of the deed or judgment providing for it and, with regard to third parties, three months after a notation thereof has been made in the margin of the marriage certificate. However, even in the absence of such notation, the change is nonetheless enforceable against third parties if, in deeds executed with them, the spouses have declared that they have modified their matrimonial regime.  
When either spouse is subject to a legal protection measure under the conditions provided for in Title XII of Book I of this Code, the change or modification of the matrimonial regime is subject to prior authorization from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or from the family council if one has been constituted.  

By way of exception, agreements entered into by spouses in divorce proceedings with a view to liquidating their matrimonial regime are governed by the provisions of this Code specific to the divorce proceedings initiated.

###### Article 1644

When a change to the matrimonial regime occurs by application of a foreign law governing the effects of the union, the spouses inform the persons who were parties to the marriage contract and each of their adult children and proceed, where applicable, with land registration publicity. They have a notation thereof made in the margin of the marriage certificate.

###### Article 1645

The change of matrimonial regime takes effect between the parties from the date of the decision or deed providing for it and, with regard to third parties, three months after the publicity formalities provided for in Article 1644 have been completed.  

However, in the absence of completion of these formalities, the change of matrimonial regime is enforceable against third parties if, in deeds executed with them, the spouses have declared that they have modified their matrimonial regime.

#### Chapitre II : Du régime en communauté Article 1646

The community, whether legal or conventional, begins on the day of the marriage contracted before the civil status officer: it cannot be stipulated that it will begin at another time.

##### Section I : De la communauté légale Article 1647

The community that is established in the absence of a contract, or by the simple declaration that one is marrying under the community regime, is subject to the rules explained in the following subsections.

###### Sous-section 1 : De ce qui compose la communauté activement et passivement

###### § 1. De l'actif de la communauté Article 1648

The community is composed on the asset side of acquisitions made by the spouses together or separately during the marriage, and arising both from their personal industry and from savings made from the fruits and income of their separate property.

###### Article 1649

Any property, movable or immovable, is presumed to be a community acquisition unless it is proved that it is separate property of one of the spouses by application of a provision of law. If the property is of a kind that does not bear in itself proof or mark of its origin, the personal ownership of the spouse, if contested, must be established in writing. In the absence of an inventory or other pre-constituted proof, the judge may take into consideration all writings, including family documents, registers and domestic papers, as well as bank documents and invoices. He may even admit proof by testimony or presumption, if he finds that a spouse was in a material or moral impossibility of obtaining a writing.

###### Article 1650

Each spouse retains full ownership of his or her separate property. The community is entitled only to fruits collected and not consumed. But compensation may be due to it, upon dissolution of the community, for fruits that the spouse has neglected to collect or has fraudulently consumed, without any inquiry, however, being admissible beyond the last five years.

###### Article 1651

Constitute separate property by their nature, even if they were acquired during the marriage, clothing and linens for the personal use of one of the spouses, actions for compensation for bodily or moral injury, inalienable claims and pensions, and, more generally, all property that has a personal character and all rights exclusively attached to the person. Also constitute separate property by their nature, but subject to compensation if applicable, work instruments necessary for the profession of one of the spouses, unless they are an accessory to a business or operation forming part of the community.

###### Article 1652

Property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of the celebration of the marriage, or which they acquire during the marriage by succession, donation or legacy, remains separate property. The liberality may stipulate that the property that is the subject thereof will belong to the community. Property falls into the community, unless otherwise stipulated, when the liberality is made to both spouses jointly. Property abandoned or transferred by father, mother or other ascendant to one of the spouses, either to fulfill what is owed to him or her, or subject to paying the donor's debts to strangers, remains separate property, subject to compensation.

###### Article 1653

Constitute separate property, subject to compensation if applicable, property acquired as accessories to separate property as well as new securities and other accretions relating to separate movable securities. Also constitute separate property, by the effect of real subrogation, claims and indemnities that replace separate property, as well as property acquired by employment or reinvestment, in accordance with Articles 1678 and 1679.

###### Article 1654

Property acquired in exchange for property that belonged as separate property to one of the spouses is itself separate property, subject to compensation due to or by the community, if there is a balancing payment. However, if the balancing payment charged to the community exceeds the value of the property transferred, the property acquired in exchange falls into the common mass, subject to compensation for the benefit of the transferor.

###### Article 1655

The acquisition made, by way of auction or otherwise, of a portion of property of which one of the spouses was an undivided owner, does not constitute an acquisition, subject to compensation due to the community for the sum it may have provided.

###### § 2.Du passif de la communauté Article 1656

The community is composed on the liability side:	on a final basis, of maintenance owed by the spouses and debts contracted by them for the upkeep of the household and the education of the children, in accordance with Article 228;	on a final basis or subject to compensation, depending on the case, of other debts arising during the community.

###### Article 1657

Debts with which the spouses were charged on the day of the celebration of their marriage, or with which the successions and liberalities that fall to them during the marriage are burdened, remain their personal debts, both in principal and in arrears or interest.

###### Article 1658

The creditors of either spouse, in the case of Article 1657, may pursue their payment only against the separate property and income of their debtor.  
They may, nevertheless, also seize the community property when the movable property that belongs to their debtor on the day of marriage or that has fallen to him or her by succession or liberality has been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Article 1659

Compensation is due to the community that has discharged the personal debt of a spouse.

###### Article 1660

Payment of debts with which each spouse is charged, for whatever cause, during the community, may always be pursued against the common property, unless there has been fraud by the debtor spouse and bad faith of the creditor, subject to compensation due to the community if applicable.

###### Article 1661

The earnings and salaries of one spouse may be seized by the creditors of the other spouse only if the obligation was contracted for the maintenance of the household or the education of the children, in accordance with Article 228.

###### Article 1662

Each spouse may only bind their separate property and income by a suretyship or loan, unless these have been contracted with the express consent of the other spouse who, in that case, does not bind their separate property.

###### Article 1663

The community which has paid a debt for which it could be pursued under the preceding articles is nevertheless entitled to compensation, whenever that obligation had been contracted in the personal interest of one of the spouses, such as for the acquisition, preservation or improvement of separate property.

###### Article 1664

The community is entitled to compensation, after deduction, where applicable, of the profit it derived, when it has paid fines incurred by a spouse by reason of criminal offences, or the damages and costs to which the spouse had been condemned for civil delicts or quasi-delicts. It is likewise entitled to compensation if the debt it paid had been contracted by one of the spouses in disregard of the duties imposed upon them by marriage.

###### Article 1665

When a debt has entered the community on account of only one of the spouses, it may not be pursued against the separate property of the other. If there is joint and several liability, the debt is deemed to enter the community on account of both spouses.

###### Sous-section 2 : De l'administration de la communauté et des biens propres Article 1666

Each spouse has the power to administer the common property alone and to dispose of it, subject to being liable for faults committed in their management. Acts performed without fraud by one spouse are binding on the other. The spouse who exercises a separate profession alone has the power to perform the acts of administration and disposition necessary for it. All subject to Articles 1667 to 1670.

###### Article 1667

The spouses may not, one without the other, dispose inter vivos, by gratuitous title, of community property. Nor may they, one without the other, assign any such property as security for the debt of a third party.

###### Article 1668

A legacy made by one spouse may not exceed their share in the community. If a spouse has bequeathed an asset of the community, the legatee may only claim it in kind insofar as the asset, by the outcome of the

partition, falls into the lot of the testator's heirs; if the asset does not fall into the lot of those heirs, the legatee has compensation for the total value of the bequeathed asset, against the share, in the community, of the heirs of the testator spouse and against the personal property of the latter.

###### Article 1669

The spouses may not, one without the other, alienate or encumber with real rights the immovable property, business goodwill and enterprises forming part of the community, nor non-negotiable partnership rights and corporeal movables whose alienation is subject to publicity. They may not, without their spouse, collect the capital proceeds from such transactions. Likewise, they may not, one without the other, transfer community property into a fiduciary estate.

###### Article 1670

The spouses may not, one without the other, lease a rural property or immovable property for commercial, industrial or artisanal use forming part of the community. Other leases on common property may be entered into by one spouse alone and are subject to the rules provided for leases entered into by the usufructuary.

###### Article 1671

If one of the spouses is, in a lasting manner, unable to manifest their will, or if their management of the community evidences unfitness or fraud, the other spouse may apply to the court to be substituted in the exercise of their powers. The provisions of Articles 1689 to 1692 are applicable to this application.  
The spouse thus authorized by the court has the same powers as the spouse they replace would have had; they perform with judicial authorization the acts for which their consent would have been required had there been no substitution. The spouse deprived of their powers may subsequently apply to the court for their restoration, by establishing that their transfer to the other spouse is no longer justified.

###### Article 1672

If one of the spouses has exceeded their powers over common property, the other, unless they have ratified the act, may apply for its annulment. The action for nullity is open to the spouse for two years from the day on which they became aware of the act, but may never be brought more than two years after the dissolution of the community.

###### Article 1673

Each spouse has the administration and enjoyment of their separate property and may dispose of it freely.

###### Article 1674

If one of the spouses is, in a lasting manner, unable to manifest their will, or if they endanger the interests of the family, either by allowing their separate property to fall into disrepair or by dissipating or misappropriating the income derived from it, they may, at the request of their spouse, be divested of the rights of administration and enjoyment recognized by Article 1673. The provisions of Articles 1689 to 1691 are applicable to this application.  
Unless the appointment of a judicial administrator appears necessary, the judgment confers upon the applicant spouse the power to administer the separate property of the divested spouse, as well as to collect the fruits, which must be applied by them to the charges of the marriage and the surplus used for the benefit of the community. From the date of the application, the divested spouse may only dispose alone of the bare ownership of their property. They may subsequently apply to the court to be restored to their rights, if they establish that the causes which had justified the divestment no longer exist.

###### Article 1675

If, during the marriage, one of the spouses entrusts the other with the administration of their separate property, the rules of mandate are applicable. The mandatary spouse is, however, dispensed from accounting for the fruits, when the power of attorney does not expressly require it.

###### Article 1676

When one of the spouses takes over the management of the separate property of the other, with the latter's knowledge and nevertheless without opposition on their part, they are deemed to have received a tacit mandate, covering acts of administration and enjoyment, but not acts of disposition. That spouse is liable to the other for their management as a mandatary. They are, however, only accountable for existing fruits; for those which they neglected to collect or fraudulently consumed, they may only be pursued within the limit of the last five years.  
If it is in disregard of a recorded opposition that one of the spouses has interfered in the management of the separate property of the other, they are liable for all the consequences of their interference and accountable without limitation for all the fruits they have collected, neglected to collect or consumed.

###### Article 1677

The community owes compensation to the owner spouse whenever it has derived profit from separate property. This is the case, in particular, when it has collected separate monies or proceeds from the sale of separate property, without employment or reinvestment having been made.  
If a dispute is raised, proof that the community has derived profit from separate property may be adduced by all means, even by testimony and presumptions.

###### Article 1678

Employment or reinvestment is deemed made with respect to a spouse whenever, at the time of an acquisition, they declared that it was made with separate monies or proceeds from the alienation of separate property, and to serve as employment or reinvestment for them. In the absence of this declaration in the instrument, employment or reinvestment only takes place by agreement of the spouses, and it produces its effects only in their mutual relations.

###### Article 1679

If the employment or re-employment is made in anticipation, the property acquired is separate property, subject to the condition that the sums expected from the separate estate are paid to the community within five years from the date of the deed.

###### Article 1680

When the price and costs of the acquisition exceed the sum for which employment or re-employment was made, the community is entitled to compensation for the excess.  
If, however, the contribution of the community is greater than that of the acquiring spouse, the property acquired falls into the community, subject to the compensation due to the spouse.

###### Article 1681

Whenever a sum is taken from the community, either to pay debts or charges personal to one of the spouses, such as the price or part of the price of property belonging to him or her separately or the redemption of land services, or for the recovery, preservation or improvement of his or her personal property, and generally whenever one of the two spouses has derived a personal benefit from the property of the community, he or she owes compensation for it.

###### Article 1682

If the father and mother have jointly endowed the common child without expressing the portion in which they intended to contribute, they are deemed to have endowed each for one half, whether the dowry was provided or promised in property of the community, or whether it was provided in property personal to one of the two spouses. In the second case, the spouse whose personal property was constituted as dowry has, against the property of the other, an

action for indemnity for half of said dowry, having regard to the value of the property given at the time of the endowment.

###### Article 1683

The dowry constituted to the common child, in property of the community, is chargeable to the community. It must be borne for one half by each spouse, upon dissolution of the community, unless one of them, in constituting it, has expressly declared that he or she would bear it in full or for a share greater than one half.

###### Article 1684

The guarantee of the dowry is owed by every person who constituted it; and its interest runs from the day of the marriage, even if there is a term for payment, unless there is a stipulation to the contrary.

###### Sous-section 3 : De la dissolution de la communauté

###### § 1. Des causes de dissolution et de la séparation de biens Article 1685

The community is dissolved:
1° by the death of one of the spouses; 2° by declared absence;  
3° by divorce;  
4° by legal separation; 5° by separation of property;  
6° by change of matrimonial regime.

###### Article 1686

There can be no continuation of the community, notwithstanding any provisions to the contrary.  

Either spouse may request, if appropriate, that, in their mutual relations, the effect of the dissolution be carried back to the date when they ceased to cohabit and collaborate.

###### Article 1687

If, by reason of the disorder of the affairs of a spouse, his or her mismanagement or misconduct, it appears that the maintenance of the community endangers the interests of the other spouse, the latter may seek separation of property in court. Any separation, without the intervention of the judge, is null and void by operation of law.

###### Article 1688

Separation of property, although pronounced by a court, is null if proceedings to liquidate the rights of the parties have not been commenced within three months of the judgment becoming res judicata and if the final settlement has not occurred within one year of the opening of liquidation operations.  
This period of one year may be extended by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance ruling in summary proceedings.

###### Article 1689

The application for and judgment of separation of property must be published under the conditions and subject to the sanctions provided for by the code of civil procedure.  
The judgment pronouncing separation of property takes effect, as to its effects, from the day of the application.  

Mention of the judgment shall be made in the margin of the marriage certificate as well as on the original of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1690

The creditors of a spouse may not request separation of property on his or her behalf.

###### Article 1691

When an action for separation of property has been brought, creditors may summon the spouses by writ from lawyer to lawyer to communicate to them the application and supporting documents. They may even intervene in the proceedings for the preservation of their rights.  
If the separation was pronounced in fraud of their rights, they may challenge it by third-party opposition, under the conditions provided for in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 1692

The spouse who has obtained separation of property must contribute, in proportion to his or her means and those of his or her spouse, both to household expenses and to the costs of educating the children. He or she must bear these costs entirely, if nothing remains to the other.

###### Article 1693

Separation of property pronounced by a court has the effect of placing the spouses under the regime of articles 1739 and following. The court, in pronouncing the separation, may order that one spouse pay his or her contribution to his or her spouse, who shall henceforth assume alone with respect to third parties the settlement of all the charges of the marriage.

###### Article 1694

Agreements entered into pursuant to article 293 are suspended, as to their effects, until the divorce is pronounced; they may not be executed, even in relations between spouses, until the judgment has become res judicata. Either spouse may request that the divorce judgment modify the agreement if the consequences of the divorce fixed by that judgment call into question the basis of the liquidation and partition.

###### § 2. De la liquidation et du partage de la communauté Article 1695

Once the community is dissolved, each of the spouses takes back those of the properties that had not entered the community, if they exist in kind, or the properties that have been subrogated thereto. There is then occasion for the liquidation of the common mass, assets and liabilities.

###### Article 1696

There is established, in the name of each spouse, an account of the compensation that the community owes him or her and of the compensation that he or she owes to the community, according to the rules prescribed in the preceding sections.

###### Article 1697

Compensation is, in general, equal to the lesser of the two sums represented by the expenditure made and the profit subsisting. It may not, however, be less than the expenditure made when the latter was necessary. It may not be less than the profit subsisting, when the borrowed value was used to acquire, preserve or improve a property that is found, on the day of liquidation of the community, in the borrowing estate. If the property acquired, preserved or improved was alienated before liquidation, the profit is valued on the day of alienation; if a new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the profit is valued on that new property.

###### Article 1698

If, on balance, the account shows a balance in favor of the community, the spouse returns the amount to the common mass. If it shows a balance in favor of the spouse, the latter has the choice either to demand payment or to take common property up to the corresponding amount.

###### Article 1699

Withdrawals are made first from cash, then from movables, and subsidiarily from immovables of the community. The spouse who makes the withdrawal has the right to choose the movables and immovables that he or she will withdraw. He or she may not, however, prejudice by his or her choice the rights that his or her spouse may have to request the maintenance of indivision or the preferential allocation of certain property. If the spouses wish to withdraw the same property, it is proceeded, except demonstration of an abuse by the one who opposes the withdrawal of a property determined by the other, by drawing lots.

###### Article 1700

In the event of insufficiency of the community, the withdrawals of each spouse are proportional to the amount of compensation owed to them. However, if the insufficiency of the community is attributable to the fault of one of the spouses, the other spouse may exercise their withdrawals before them on all the common property; they may exercise them subsidiarily on the separate property of the responsible spouse.

###### Article 1701

Compensation owed by the community or to the community bears interest by operation of law from the day of dissolution. However, when the compensation is equal to the subsisting profit, interest runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1702

Withdrawals from common property constitute a partition operation. They do not confer on the spouse exercising them any right to be preferred over the creditors of the community.

###### Article 1703

After all withdrawals have been executed from the mass, the surplus is divided in half between the spouses. If an immovable of the community is an annex to another immovable belonging separately to one of the spouses, or if it is contiguous to that immovable, the spouse owner has the option to have it attributed to them by imputation on their share or by means of an equalizing payment, according to the value of the property on the day the attribution is requested.

###### Article 1704

The partition of the community, with respect to all matters concerning its forms, the maintenance of joint ownership and preferential attribution, the sale by auction of property, the effects of partition, the warranty and equalizing payments, is subject to all the rules that are established in the title On Successions for partitions among co-heirs.  
However, for communities dissolved by divorce, legal separation or separation of property, preferential attribution is never by right, and it may always be decided that the totality of any equalizing payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1705

The spouse who has misappropriated or concealed any effects of the community is deprived of their portion in said effects. Likewise, the spouse who has knowingly concealed the existence of a common debt must assume it definitively.

###### Article 1706

After the partition is completed, if one of the two spouses is a personal creditor of the other, as when the price of their property was used to pay a personal debt of their spouse, or for any other cause, they exercise their claim on the share that has fallen to the latter in the community or on their personal property.

###### Article 1707

Personal claims that the spouses have to exercise against each other do not give rise to withdrawal and bear interest only from the day of formal demand.  

Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, these personal claims that the spouses have to exercise against each other are valued according to the rules of Article 1697, in the cases provided for therein; interest then runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1708

Gifts that one of the spouses may have made to the other are executed only on the donor's share in the community and on their personal property.

###### § 3

On the obligation and contribution to liabilities after dissolution Article 1709
Each of the spouses may be sued for the totality of debts existing, on the day of dissolution, that had entered the community on their account.

###### Article 1710

Each of the spouses may be sued only for half of the debts that had entered the community on account of their spouse.  
After partition and except in case of concealment, the spouse who is not personally obligated is liable only up to the amount of their emolument, that is to say up to the amount of the active share of the community that they receive, provided that there has been an inventory, and subject to accounting for both the contents of that inventory and what has fallen to them by partition as well as the common liabilities already discharged.

###### Article 1711

The inventory provided for in Article 1710 must take place in the forms regulated by the code of civil procedure, adversarially with the other spouse or with them duly summoned. It must be closed within nine months from the day the community was dissolved, except for an extension granted by the judge in summary proceedings. It must be affirmed sincere and true before the public officer who received it.

###### Article 1712

Each of the spouses contributes half to the community debts for which no compensation was owed, as well as to the costs of sealing, inventory, sale of movables, liquidation, sale by auction and partition.  
When the debt was definitively incumbent only on one of the spouses and the other spouse nevertheless contributed, the latter has a right to corresponding compensation.

###### Article 1713

The spouse who may avail themselves of the benefit of Article 1710, second paragraph, does not contribute more than the active share of the community that they receive, to debts that had entered the community on account of the other spouse, unless these are debts for which they would have owed compensation.

###### Article 1714

The spouse who has paid beyond the portion for which they were liable by application of the preceding articles has, against the other, recourse for the excess.

###### Article 1715

They do not have, for that excess, a claim for restitution against the creditor, unless the receipt expresses that they intend to pay only within the limit of their obligation.

###### Article 1716

The one of the two spouses who, by the effect of a mortgage exercised on the immovable that has fallen to them in partition, is sued for the totality of a community debt, has by right their recourse against the other for half of that debt.

###### Article 1717

The provisions of the preceding articles do not prevent a clause of the partition from obligating one or the other of the spouses to pay a quota of debts other than that which is fixed above, or even to discharge the liabilities entirely, without prejudice to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1718

The heirs of the spouses exercise, in case of dissolution of the community, the same rights as the spouse they represent and are subject to the same obligations.

##### Section II: On the conventional community Article 1719

The spouses may, in their marriage contract, modify the legal community by any kind of agreements not contrary to Articles 1633, 1635 and 1636.  
They may, in particular, agree:
1° That the community shall include movables and acquisitions; 2° That the rules concerning administration shall be derogated from;  
3° That one of the spouses shall have the option to withdraw certain property by means of compensation; 4° That one of the spouses shall have received sums or property outside the succession share;  
5° That the spouses shall have unequal shares;  
6° That there shall be universal community between them.  

The rules of the legal community remain applicable in all points that have not been the subject of the parties' agreement.

###### Sous-section 1: On the community of movables and acquisitions Article 1720

When the spouses agree that there shall be between them community of movables and acquisitions, the common assets include, in addition to the property that would form part of it under the legal community regime, the movable property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of marriage or which has fallen to them since by succession or liberality, unless the donor or testator has stipulated otherwise.  

Nevertheless, those of these movable properties that would have formed separate property by their nature under Article 1651, under the legal regime, if they had been acquired during the community, remain separate.  
If one of the spouses had acquired an immovable since the marriage contract, containing a stipulation of community of movables and acquisitions, and before the celebration of the marriage, the immovable acquired in that interval shall enter the community, unless the acquisition was made in execution of some clause of the marriage contract, in which case it would be regulated according to the agreement.

###### Article 1721

Under this regime, the common liabilities include, in addition to the debts that would form part of it under the legal regime, a fraction of those with which the spouses were already burdened when they married, or with which successions and liberalities that fall to them during the marriage are charged.  
The fraction of liabilities that the community must bear is proportional to the fraction of assets that it receives according to the rules of Article 1720, either in the spouse's patrimony on the day of marriage, or in all the property that is the subject of the succession or liberality.  

For the establishment of this proportion, the composition and value of the assets are proved in accordance with Article 1649.

###### Article 1722

The debts for which the community is liable in consideration of the property it receives are its definitive charge.

###### Article 1723

The distribution of liabilities prior to the marriage or encumbering successions and liberalities may not prejudice creditors. They retain, in all cases, the right to seize the property that formerly constituted their security. They may even pursue their payment against the entire community when the movable property of their debtor has been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Sous-section 2 :De la clause d'administration conjointe Article 1724

The spouses may agree that they will jointly administer the community.  
In that case, acts of administration and disposition of common property are made under the joint signature of both spouses. This dual signature entails by operation of law joint and several liability for the obligations undertaken. Conservatory acts may be made separately by each spouse.

###### Sous-section 3 : De la clause de prélèvement moyennant indemnité Article 1725

The spouses may stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, or even one of them in all cases of dissolution of the community, shall have the option to withdraw certain common property, subject to accounting for it to the community according to the value they will have on the day of partition, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1726

The marriage contract may fix bases of valuation and terms of payment of any balancing payment. Taking into account these clauses and in the absence of agreement between the parties, the value of the property shall be fixed by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 1727

The option to withdraw lapses if the beneficiary spouse has not exercised it by notification made to the other spouse or to his or her heirs within one month from the day on which they have given him or her formal notice to make a decision. This formal notice may not itself take place before the expiration of the time limits provided for in Article 906 for making an inventory and deliberating.

###### Article 1728

The withdrawal is a partition operation: the property withdrawn is charged against the share of the beneficiary spouse; if their value exceeds that share, a balancing payment is due.  
The spouses may agree that the compensation owed by the person making the withdrawal shall be charged subsidiarily against his or her rights in the succession of the predeceased spouse.

###### Sous-section 4

L'attribution, au conjoint, de somme ou biens hors part successorale Article 1729
It may be agreed, in the marriage contract, that the survivor of the spouses, or one of them if he or she survives, shall be authorized to withdraw from the community, before any partition, either a certain sum, or certain property in kind, or a certain quantity of a specified type of property.

###### Article 1730

This attribution outside the succession share is not regarded as a donation, either as to substance or as to form, but as a marriage contract and between partners.

###### Article 1731

When the community is dissolved during the lifetime of both spouses, there is no occasion for the delivery of the sums and property whose attribution is provided for outside the succession share; but the spouse in whose favor it has been stipulated retains his or her rights in the event of survival, subject to Article 291.  
He or she may require security from his or her spouse as guarantee of his or her rights.

###### Article 1732

The creditors of the community always have the right to have the property included outside the succession share sold, subject to the spouse's recourse against the remainder of the community.

###### Sous-section 5 : De la stipulation de parts inégales Article 1733

The spouses may derogate from the equal partition established by law.

###### Article 1734

When it has been stipulated that the spouse or his or her heirs shall have only a certain share in the community, such as one-third or one-quarter, the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs bear the debts of the community only in proportion to the share they take in the assets.  
The agreement is null if it obliges the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs to bear a greater share, or if it exempts them from bearing a share in the debts equal to that which they take in the assets.

###### Article 1735

The attribution of the entire community may be agreed only for the event of survival, either in favor of a designated spouse, or in favor of whichever one survives. The spouse who thus retains the totality of the community is obliged to pay all its debts.
