5° However, to be enforceable against the owner, the sub-lease of a premises or the assignment of a lease must have had his express or tacit consent. For this purpose, and except for special provisions in this regard in the lease contract, the proposed sub-lease or assignment of lease must be served on the owner by extra-judicial act two months before the sub-tenant or assignee enters the premises. Within one month following service, the owner must make known whether he intends to participate in the act. After this period, he is deemed to have given his tacit agreement;  
6° The benefit of the right to remain in the premises for the premises referred to in Article 1903 belongs, in case of abandonment of domicile or death of the occupant, to his relatives or in-laws in the first degree who habitually lived with him for more than six months;  
7° In case of divorce or legal separation proceedings, the court seized shall award to one of the spouses the possible right to remain in the premises in consideration of the social or family interests at stake.  

If the spouse who is the beneficiary is not the one in whose name the receipts were issued, notification of the decision must be made to the lessor within three months of its pronouncement by extra-judicial means;  
8° However, the right to remain in the premises may not benefit the persons referred to in the two preceding paragraphs for premises used exclusively for professional purposes, unless one of these persons continues to practice there the profession for which these premises were allocated;  
9° The right to remain in the premises is granted to legal persons occupying premises for professional use as well as to legal persons carrying out a non-profit activity, in particular to registered associations and professional unions if these persons meet the conditions provided for in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this article. However, the right to remain in the premises thus recognized for legal persons is not enforceable against the owner who wants to occupy the premises himself or have it occupied by his spouse, his ascendants or descendants, or by those of his spouse.

###### Article1917

Natural or legal persons do not have the right to remain in the premises:
1° Who have been or will be the subject of a final judicial decision, having pronounced their eviction by application of common law, or who will be the subject of a similar decision for one of the causes and under the conditions admitted by this resolution;  
2° Who have several dwellings, except for those constituting their principal establishment, unless they justify that their functions or profession require them to do so;  
3° Who have not effectively occupied the leased premises themselves or have not had them occupied by relatives or in-laws in the first degree who habitually lived with them;  
4° Who occupy premises subject to an administrative injunction for reasons of hygiene or public utility requiring their evacuation;  
5° Who cease or have ceased the functions of which the title of occupation was an accessory;  
6° Who have at their disposal or can recover, by exercising their right of repossession, another premises meeting their needs and those of their relatives or in-laws in the first degree in their care;  
7° Installed in the premises by the principal tenant or any other beneficiary of the right to remain in the premises, without the consent of the lessor given under the conditions specified in point 5° of Article 1916;  
8° Who occupy premises located in buildings acquired or expropriated following a public declaration, subject to the administration ensuring the rehousing of evicted tenants or occupants.  

C.	Right of repossession

###### Article1918

The right of repossession may be exercised by the owner who has obtained authorization to rebuild or raise the building, or to make modifications to it requiring its evacuation. The exercise of this right of repossession is however subject to the following conditions.  
The owner:
1° Must give the occupants, by extra-judicial act, three months' notice which shall indicate precisely the reason or reasons justifying the exercise of the right of repossession and shall refer to the administrative decision authorizing the works, all on pain of nullity;  
2° Shall be required to begin the works within a maximum period of three months from the evacuation of the premises by the last occupant;  
3° Must, to the extent of his means, proceed with the rehousing of the evicted occupants if he owns other premises;  
4° May not re-let, occupy or have occupied the premises before the completion of the works;  
5° Must, upon completion of the works, grant to the evicted occupant a priority right over any applicants.

###### Article1919

The owner who has not satisfied the obligations prescribed by the provisions of paragraphs 2, 3, 4 and 5 of Article 1918 above shall be liable, towards the evicted occupants, for payment for

unjustified deprivation of enjoyment, of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1920

The right of repossession also belongs to the owner who wants to take back the building to occupy it himself or have it occupied by his spouse or by his relatives or in-laws in the first degree.  
The owner who wants to benefit from the above provisions must, by extra-judicial act, give three months' notice to the occupant whose premises he proposes to take back.  
The owner must, within a maximum period of two months from the evacuation of the premises, occupy them himself or have them occupied by the beneficiary of the right of repossession for a minimum period of one year.  

The owner who has not occupied or had occupied the premises under the conditions defined in the preceding paragraphs of this article, shall be liable for payment towards the evicted occupant, of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1921

The owner may not exercise the right of repossession provided for in Article 1920:
1° If he is the owner of another vacant premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of repossession;  
2° If he is the owner of another premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of repossession, of which he can regain possession from occupants who do not benefit from the right to remain in the premises.  

D.	Miscellaneous provisions

###### Article1922

Any demand by the lessor or their agents, any agreement, tending to impose on the lessee, in an indirect form (remittance of money, taking back of furniture, provision of service, etc.) a rental price higher than that which has been stipulated in the lease contract or than that which will result from the application of the provisions of point B. of this section, shall be null and void.

###### Article1923

A presidential decree may, in all or part of the territory of the Republic, subject to prior authorization the conversion of premises for residential use into premises for any other use.  
Offenders shall be punished by a civil fine which may not be less than 100,000 FD nor more than three times the annual rent provided for prior to the offence. In all cases, the court shall order the reallocation and restoration of the premises at the expense of the offender within the time limit it shall set. In the event of failure to execute within the time limits set, the fine provided for may be doubled.

###### Article1924

Any lessor of premises for residential use rented unfurnished, convicted of having refused to rent a vacant premises to a prospective tenant, on the grounds of the existence or number of children in the latter's care, shall be punished by a civil fine equal to at least one quarter and at most three times the rent payable at the time of the refusal.  
The perpetrator of the offence shall, in addition, be required to grant to the evicted family, for a minimum period of two years, a lease on the refused property, unless the premises have already been rented, in which case the said perpetrator of the offence shall be condemned, towards the injured party, to all damages and interest.

###### Article 1925

The maintenance repairs or minor upkeep for which the tenant is liable, if there is no clause to the contrary, are those designated as such by the usage of the premises and, in the absence thereof, by the general provisions of the first section of this chapter.

###### Article 1926

The lease of furniture provided to furnish the rented premises is deemed made for the ordinary duration of leases, according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1927

The lease of a furnished apartment is deemed subscribed for the year, when it has been made at so much per year; For the month, when it has been made at so much per month;  
For the day, when it has been made at so much per day.  
If nothing establishes that the lease is made at so much per year, per month or per day, the lease is deemed made according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1928

If the tenant of a house or an apartment continues their enjoyment after the expiration of the written lease, without opposition from the lessor, there is tacit renewal of the original contract.

###### § 2. Le bail emphytéotique et le bail à construction

A.	Du bail emphytéotique

###### Article 1929

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property is a contract by which the lessor confers on the lessee, called emphyteuta, a real immovable right called emphyteusis.  
The lease is granted for a duration which is between eighteen and ninety-nine years. It may not be extended by tacit renewal; in case of express renewal, the total duration of the lease may not exceed 99 years.  

The right thus conferred is susceptible to mortgage, transferable and seizable in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

###### Article 1930

The emphyteutic lease may only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as in the same forms. It is enforceable against third parties from the publication at the mortgage registry.  
Immovable property belonging to minors or to adults under guardianship may be given on emphyteutic lease by virtue of a deliberation of the family council.  

Concerning premises for residential use, the lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with the tenants continue automatically with the owner of the property until the end of each of the lease contracts signed with the tenants and under the same conditions.  
In the absence of contrary agreements, the emphyteutic lease is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 1931

The lessee is liable for a periodic rent, called redevance, in the form of a sum of money or in a portion of fruits and products.  

The lessee may not request the reduction of this redevance on grounds of partial loss of the property.  
In the absence of payment for six consecutive months, the lessor is authorized, after a summons that has remained without effect, to have the resolution of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.

###### Article 1932

The lessee may not make any change in the property that diminishes its value. Conversely, if they make improvements or constructions that increase the value of the property, they may not destroy them, nor claim in this regard any compensation from the lessor.  
The resolution may also be requested by the lessor in case of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deteriorations on the property.  
Nevertheless, the courts may grant a time limit according to the circumstances.

###### Article 1933

The lessee is liable for all contributions and charges weighing on the property.  

They are liable for the maintenance and repairs of all kinds on the constructions that exist at the time of the lease and those that will have been erected in execution of the agreement, but they are not obliged to rebuild the buildings, if they prove that they were destroyed by fortuitous event, by force majeure or that they perished by the defect of construction prior to the lease.  

They are liable for fire, in accordance with Article 1394, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Code.

###### Article 1934

The lessee may acquire for the benefit of the property active easements, and encumber them, by title, with passive easements, for a time that will not exceed the duration of the lease, subject to notifying the owner.  
If the lessee has concluded agreements with third parties, they end with the extinction of the emphyteusis, without possibility for the contracting parties of the lessee to claim extension, nor compensation.

###### Article 1935

The lessee benefits from the right of accession during the duration of the emphyteusis.  

B.	Du bail à construction

###### Article 1936

The construction lease is the lease contract by which the lessee undertakes, as principal obligation, to erect constructions on the lessor's land and to keep them in good state of maintenance throughout the duration of the lease.  
The construction lease is subject, subject to the provisions below, to the rules provided for the emphyteutic lease.  

When the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option, the lease ends on the date of the sale.

###### Article 1937

The parties agree on their respective ownership rights over existing constructions and over erected constructions. In the absence of such an agreement, the lessor becomes the owner at the end of the lease and benefits from the improvements.

###### Article 1938

The construction lease confers on the lessee a real immovable right.  

This right may be mortgaged, as well as the constructions erected on the leased land; it may be seized in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.  

The lessee may transfer all or part of their rights or contribute them to a company. The transferees or the company are bound by the same obligations as the transferor who remains guarantor thereof until the completion of all the constructions that the lessee has undertaken to erect in application of Article 1936.  

The lessee may grant the passive easements indispensable to the realization of the constructions provided for in the lease.  

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are of public policy.

###### Article 1939

The lessee is liable for all charges, taxes and duties relating to both the constructions and the land. Unless otherwise stipulated in the lease, he may demolish, with a view to rebuilding them, the existing buildings.

###### Article 1940

The rent of the lease may consist, in whole or in part, in the transfer to the lessor, at agreed dates and under agreed conditions, of immovable property or fractions of immovable property or securities conferring entitlement to ownership or enjoyment of such immovable property.  
If a periodic rent payable in cash is stipulated, this rent is affected by a coefficient revisable by three-year periods counted from the completion of the works. However, the first revision takes place at the latest upon expiry of the first six years of the lease.  
The variation of the coefficient is proportional to that of the gross income from the immovable property. The income taken as the basis for the variation of the coefficient is that of the first calendar year following that of the completion of the works.  

Disputes relating to the application of the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are brought before the President of the Court of First Instance.  

In the event of loss of the buildings, the rent is maintained at the rate it had reached on the date of such loss until possible reconstruction of the destroyed buildings.

###### Article 1941

Passive easements, other than those mentioned in the fourth paragraph of Article 1938, privileges, mortgages or other charges arising from the lessee and, in particular, leases and occupancy titles of any kind relating to the constructions, are extinguished upon expiry of the lease except for residential lease contracts.  
However, when the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 1936, the privileges and mortgages from the lessee registered before the exercise of the option are not extinguished upon expiry of the lease but retain their effects, until their date of extinction, on the immovable property that has become the property of the grantor. They extend by operation of law to the land and may secure loans granted for the acquisition of said land.  

Furthermore, if the lease ends by judicial or amicable termination, the privileges and mortgages mentioned in the first paragraph and registered, as the case may be, before the publication of the legal claim seeking to obtain such termination or before the publication of the deed or agreement recording it, are only extinguished on the date originally agreed for the expiry of the lease.

###### Article 1942

If during the term of the lease the constructions are destroyed by fortuitous event or force majeure, termination may, at the request of either party, be ordered by judicial decision, which shall also rule on any compensation that may be due.

#### Chapter III. Of the hiring of work and industry Article 1943

There are three main types of hiring of work and industry:
1° The hiring of service;  
2° That of carriers, both by land and by water, who undertake the transport of persons or goods;  
3° That of architects, contractors of works and technicians pursuant to studies, estimates or contracts.

##### Section I: Of the hiring of service Article 1944

One may engage one's services only for a time, or for a specified undertaking.  
In the case of a contract concluded for an indefinite period, the hiring of service may always cease by the will of one of the contracting parties.  

Nevertheless, this right of unilateral termination may give rise to damages when, by the conditions under which it occurs, the termination has caused prejudice to the other party.  

For the determination of the compensation to be awarded, if applicable, account is taken of customs, the nature of the services engaged, the time elapsed, deductions made and payments made with a view to a retirement pension, and, in general, all circumstances that may justify the existence and determine the extent of the prejudice caused.  

The parties may not renounce in advance the potential right to claim damages under the above provisions.  

Disputes to which the application of the preceding paragraphs may give rise, when they are brought before the civil courts and before the courts of appeal, shall be heard and judged urgently.

##### Section II: Of the hiring of carriers by land and by water

###### Article 1945

Carriers by land and by water are subject, for the custody and preservation of things entrusted to them, to the same obligations as innkeepers, of whom mention is made in the title Of deposit and sequestration.  
With regard to their liability, carriers are subject to the regime provided for in Articles L.2223-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code (

##### Section 3 Of the liability of the carrier of the Commercial Code)

###### Article 1946

They are liable not only for what they have already received in their vessel or vehicle, but also for what has been delivered to them at the port or in the warehouse, to be placed in their vessel or vehicle.

###### Article 1947

They are liable for the loss and damage of things entrusted to them, unless they prove that they were lost and damaged by fortuitous event or force majeure.

###### Article 1948

Operators of public vehicles by land and by water, and those of public haulage, must keep a register of money, effects and packages of which they take charge.

###### Article 1949

Operators and directors of public vehicles and haulage, masters of barges and ships, are further subject to particular regulations.

##### Section III: Of estimates and contracts Article 1950

When one engages someone to make a work, one may agree that he will provide only his labour or his industry, or else that he will also provide the material.

###### Article 1951

When the contractor provides the material and the thing perishes, in whatever manner, before being delivered, the loss falls on the contractor, unless the master of the work was in default in receiving the thing.

###### Article 1952

When the contractor provides only his labour or his industry and the thing perishes, the risks of the thing fall on its owner, except in case of fault of the contractor who, in that case, is liable for the loss.  
The contractor who undertakes to manufacture an object with material provided by the master of the work is not entitled to remuneration if the object perishes, even in the absence of fault on his part, before he has delivered it.

###### Article 1953

If the building perishes in whole or in part due to a defect in construction, even due to a defect in the ground, the architects, contractors and other persons bound to the master of the work by a contract for the hiring of work are liable for it for ten years.

###### Article 1954

Is deemed to be a constructor of the work:
1° Any architect, contractor, technician or other person bound to the master of the work by a contract for the hiring of work;  
2° Any person who sells, after completion, a work that he has built or had built;  
3° Any person who, although acting in the capacity of agent of the owner of the work, performs a mission comparable to that of a lessor of work.


This excerpt sits under: REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI > BOOK III. OF THE DIFFERENT WAYS IN WHICH PROPERTY IS ACQUIRED > Title IX: Of the contract of lease > Chapter II. Of the lease of things Article 1874 > Section II: Of particular rules

###### Article 1955

The presumption of liability established by Article 1953 also extends to damage affecting the solidity of equipment elements of a structure, but only when these form an inseparable part of the works of access, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing.

An equipment element is considered to form an inseparable part of one of the works of access, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing when its removal, dismantling or replacement cannot be carried out without deterioration or removal of material from that work.

###### Article 1956

The other equipment elements of the structure are subject to a guarantee of proper functioning for a minimum period of two years from its acceptance.

###### Article 1957

The manufacturer of a structure, part of a structure or equipment element designed and produced to satisfy, in service condition, specific requirements determined in advance, is jointly and severally liable for the obligations placed by Articles 1953, 1955 and 1956 on the contractor who has implemented, without modification and in accordance with the rules laid down by the manufacturer, the structure, part of structure or equipment element in question.  
The following are treated as manufacturers for the application of this article:	the person who has imported a structure, part of a structure or equipment element manufactured abroad
;	the person who has presented it as his own work by placing on it his name, trademark or any other distinctive sign.

###### Article 1958

Any natural or legal person whose liability may be engaged pursuant to Articles 1953 to 1957 of this code is discharged from the liabilities and guarantees weighing upon them, under Articles 1953 to 1955, after ten years from the acceptance of the works or, under Article 1956, upon expiry of the period referred to in that article.

###### Article 1959

Actions in liability brought against a subcontractor by reason of damage affecting a structure or equipment elements of a structure mentioned in Articles 1953 and 1955 are time-barred after ten years from the acceptance of the works and, for damage affecting those equipment elements of the structure mentioned in Article 1956, after two years from that same acceptance.

###### Article 1960

Apart from actions governed by Articles 1956, 1958 and 1959, actions in liability brought against the constructors designated in Articles 1953 and 1954 and their subcontractors are time-barred after ten years from the acceptance of the works.

###### Article 1961

Any clause in a contract which has the purpose either of excluding or limiting the liability provided for in Articles 1953, 1954 and 1955, or of excluding the guarantees provided for in Articles 1956 and 1962 or limiting their scope, or of excluding or limiting the joint and several liability provided for in Article 1957, is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1962

Acceptance is the act by which the client declares that he accepts the structure with or without reservations. It takes place at the request of the most diligent party, either amicably or, failing that, judicially. It is, in any event, pronounced after adversarial proceedings.  
The guarantee of perfect completion, for which the contractor is liable for a period of one year from acceptance, extends to the repair of all defects notified by the client, either by means of reservations mentioned in the acceptance report, or by written notification for those revealed after acceptance.  

The time periods necessary for the execution of repair works are fixed by mutual agreement between the client and the contractor concerned.  

In the absence of such agreement or in case of non-performance within the fixed period, the works may, after formal notice remaining without effect, be executed at the expense and risk of the defaulting contractor.  
The execution of works required under the guarantee of perfect completion is established by mutual agreement, or, failing that, judicially.  

The guarantee does not extend to works necessary to remedy the effects of normal wear and tear or use.

###### Article 1963

Equipment elements whose exclusive function is to permit the exercise of a professional activity in the structure are not considered to be equipment elements of a structure within the meaning of Articles 1953, 1955, 1956 and 1957, including their accessories.

###### Article 1964

When an architect or contractor has undertaken the construction at a fixed price of a building, according to a plan settled and agreed with the owner of the land, he may not request any increase in price, either on the pretext of an increase in labour or materials, or on the ground of changes or additions made to that plan, if those changes or additions have not been authorised in writing, and the price agreed with the owner.

###### Article 1965

The client may terminate, by his sole will, the fixed-price contract, even though the work has already begun, by compensating the contractor for all his expenses, all his work, and all that he could have earned in that undertaking.

###### Article 1966

The contract for work is dissolved by the death of the architect or contractor.  

The death of the client only results in termination of the contract if his person was a determining element in the conclusion of the contract.  
The dissolution of the contract by death does not, however, allow the client to retain without consideration the unfinished work, in the state in which it is: the client is bound to pay in proportion to the price stated in the agreement, to the estate of the architect or contractor, the value of works completed and that of materials prepared, but only when those works or materials may be useful to him. In the case of paragraph 2, the same effect applies to the heirs of the client.

###### Article 1967

The contractor is liable for the acts of the persons he employs.

###### Article 1968

Employees and subcontractors who have been employed in the construction of a building or other works done under contract have no action against the person for whom the works were done, except up to the amount of which he is found to be debtor to the contractor, at the time when their action is brought.

### Titre X : De la société

Chapitre Ier. Dispositions générales Article 1969

A company is established by two or more persons who agree by contract to allocate to a common enterprise property or their industry with a view to sharing the profit or benefiting from the economy which may result therefrom.  

A company may also be established, in cases provided for by law, by the act of will of a single person.  

The partners undertake to contribute to losses.  

Even if they use only community property for contributions to a company or for the acquisition of shares, two spouses alone or with other persons may be partners in the same company and participate together or not in the management of the company.

###### Article 1970

Every company must have a lawful object, and be contracted for the common interest of the partners.

###### Article 1971

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all companies unless otherwise provided by law by reason of their form or object.

###### Article 1972

The articles of association must be established in writing. They determine, in addition to the contributions of each partner, the form, object, name, registered office, share capital, duration of the company and the procedures for its operation.

###### Article 1973

The articles of association may not be amended, in the absence of a provision to the contrary, except by unanimous agreement of the members.  

In no case may the commitments of a member be increased without his consent.

###### Article 1974

Any company whose registered office is located on the territory of the Republic of Djibouti is subject to the provisions of Djiboutian law.  
Third parties may rely on the registered office stated in the articles of association, but the company may not invoke it against them if the actual registered office is located elsewhere.

###### Article 1975

The duration of the company may not exceed ninety-nine years.

###### Article 1976

If the articles of association do not contain all the particulars required by legislation or if a formality prescribed by it has been omitted or irregularly performed, any interested party may apply to the court for an order, subject to penalty, for the regularization of the incorporation. The public prosecutor may act for the same purposes.  
The same rules apply in the event of an amendment to the articles of association.  

The action for regularization provided for in the first paragraph is barred after three years from the registration of the company or the publication of the deed amending the articles of association.

###### Article 1977

The founders, as well as the first members of the management, executive or administrative bodies are jointly and severally liable for the damage caused either by the absence of a mandatory mention in the articles of association, or by the omission or irregular performance of a formality prescribed for the incorporation of the company.  
In the event of an amendment to the articles of association, the provisions of the preceding paragraph apply to the members of the management, executive or administrative bodies then in office.  

The action is barred after three years from the day of performance of the omitted or irregularly performed formality. The disappearance of the omission or irregularity does not prevent the exercise of the action for damages seeking compensation for the damage caused thereby. This action is barred after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

###### Article 1978

Companies other than the partnerships referred to in Chapter III have legal personality from the time of their registration.  
Until registration, relations between the members are governed by the company contract and by the general principles of law applicable to contracts and obligations.

###### Article 1979

Persons who have acted in the name of a company in formation before registration are bound by the obligations arising from the acts thus performed, jointly and severally if the company is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.  
The company duly registered may assume the commitments entered into, which are then deemed to have been contracted by it from the outset.

###### Article1980

The contribution of property or a right subject to publication for its enforceability against third parties may be published even before registration and subject to the condition that it takes place.  
From the registration of the company, the effects of the formality are retroactive to the date of performance of said formality.

###### Article 1981

The rights of each member in the share capital are proportional to his contributions at the time of incorporation of the company or during its existence.  
Contributions in industry do not contribute to the formation of the share capital but give rise to the allocation of shares entitling the holder to share in the profits and net assets, subject to contributing to losses.

###### Article 1982

Each member is a debtor to the company for everything he has promised to contribute to it in kind, in cash or in industry.  
Contributions in kind are made by the transfer of the corresponding rights and by the effective placing at disposal of the property.  
When the contribution is in ownership, the contributor is guarantor to the company as a seller to his buyer.  
When it is in enjoyment, the contributor is guarantor to the company as a lessor to his lessee. However, when the contribution in enjoyment relates to fungible things or to any other property

normally intended to be renewed during the life of the company, the contract transfers to it the ownership of the contributed property, subject to returning a similar quantity, quality and value; in this case, the contributor is guarantor under the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraph.  

The member who was to contribute a sum to the company and who has not done so becomes by operation of law and without demand, debtor of the interest on this sum from the day on which it was to be paid, without prejudice to further damages, if applicable. Furthermore, when calls for funds have not been made to achieve the full payment of the capital, any interested party may request the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings either to order under penalty the directors, managers and officers to make these calls for funds, or to appoint an agent responsible for carrying out this formality.  

The member who has undertaken to contribute his industry to the company owes it an account of all the gains he has made through the activity that is the subject of his contribution.

###### Article 1983

I.	In cases where the law refers to this article to set the conditions of price for a transfer of the company rights of a member, or the repurchase thereof by the company, the value of these rights is determined, in the event of dispute, by an expert appointed either by the parties or, failing agreement between them, by order of the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings and without possible recourse.  
II.	In cases where the articles of association provide for the transfer of the company rights of a member or the repurchase of these rights by the company without their value being either determined or determinable, it is determined, in the event of dispute, by an expert appointed under the conditions of the first paragraph.  

III.	In the cases provided for in points I. and II., the expert thus appointed is required to apply, where they exist, the rules and methods for determining the value provided for by the articles of association of the company or by any agreement binding the parties.

###### Article 1984

In addition to the action for compensation for damage suffered personally, one or more members may bring the corporate action for liability against the managers. The plaintiffs are authorized to seek compensation for the damage suffered by the company; in the event of conviction, the damages are awarded to the company.  
Any clause in the articles of association having the effect of making the exercise of the corporate action subject to the prior opinion or authorization of the general meeting or which would involve advance waiver of the exercise of this action is deemed unwritten.  
No decision of the general meeting of members may have the effect of extinguishing an action for liability against the managers for fault committed in the performance of their mandate.

###### Article 1985

Every member has the right to participate in collective decisions.  

The co-owners of an undivided company share are represented by a single agent, chosen from among the co-owners or from outside them. In the event of disagreement, the agent is appointed by court order at the request of the most diligent.  
If a share is encumbered with a usufruct, the voting right belongs to the bare owner, except for decisions concerning the allocation of profits, where it is reserved to the usufructuary.  

The articles of association may derogate from the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs.

###### Article 1986

The share of each partner in the profits and their contribution to losses shall be determined in proportion to their share in the share capital, and the share of the partner who has contributed only their industry shall be equal to that of the partner who has contributed the least, all subject to any clause to the contrary.

However, the stipulation attributing to a partner the entirety of the profit generated by the company or exempting them from all losses, as well as that excluding a partner entirely from the profit or placing upon them the entirety of the losses, shall be deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1987

A mortgage or any other real security interest may be granted over the assets of the company by virtue of powers resulting from resolutions or delegations established by private signature even where the creation of the mortgage or security interest must be by authentic instrument.

###### Article 1988

The regular transformation of a company into a company of another form does not result in the creation of a new legal person. The same applies to the extension or any other amendment to the articles of association.

###### Article 1989

A company, even in liquidation, may be absorbed by another company or participate in the formation of a new company, by way of merger. It may also transfer its assets by way of division to existing companies or to new companies.  
These transactions may take place between companies of different forms.  

They shall be decided by each of the companies concerned, under the conditions required for the amendment of its articles of association.  
If the transaction involves the creation of new companies, each of them shall be formed according to the rules specific to the form of company adopted.

###### Article 1990

The combination of all the shares in a single hand does not result in the dissolution by operation of law of the company. Any interested party may request this dissolution if the situation has not been regularised within a period of one year. The court may grant the company a maximum period of six months to regularise the situation. It may not order dissolution if, on the day it rules on the merits, this regularisation has taken place.  
The ownership of the usufruct of all the shares by the same person has no consequence on the existence of the company.  

In the event of dissolution, it results in the universal transfer of the assets of the company to the sole partner, without there being any need for liquidation.  

Creditors may oppose the dissolution within a period of thirty days from the publication thereof. A judicial decision shall reject the opposition or order either the repayment of the debts or the provision of guarantees if the company offers them and if they are deemed sufficient. The transfer of assets is only effected and the legal person only ceases to exist at the end of the opposition period or, where applicable, when the opposition has been rejected at first instance or when the repayment of debts has been made or the guarantees provided.  

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs shall not apply to companies whose sole partner is a natural person.

###### Article 1991

The extension of the company shall be decided unanimously by the partners or, if the articles of association so provide, by the majority required for the amendment thereof.  

At least one year before the expiry date of the company, the partners must be consulted in order to decide whether the company should be extended.  

In default thereof, any partner may request the president of the court of first instance, ruling on application, to appoint a judicial representative responsible for initiating the consultation provided for above.

###### Article 1992

The company comes to an end:
1° By the expiry of the time for which it was formed, subject to extension carried out in accordance with Article 1991;  
2° By the achievement or extinction of its object; 3° By the annulment of the company contract;  
4° By early dissolution decided by the partners;  
5° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance at the request of a partner for just cause, in particular in the event of failure by a partner to perform their obligations, or disagreement between partners paralysing the operation of the company;  
6° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance in the case provided for in Article 1990;  
7° By the effect of a judgment ordering the closure of judicial liquidation for insufficiency of assets; 8° For any other cause provided for in the articles of association.

###### Article 1993

The dissolution of the company results in its liquidation, except in the cases provided for in Article 1989 and in the third paragraph of Article 1990. It has effect with regard to third parties only after its publication.  
The liquidator shall be appointed in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association. In the absence thereof, they shall be appointed by the partners or, if the partners have been unable to make this appointment, by judicial decision. The liquidator may be removed under the same conditions. The appointment and removal are only enforceable against third parties from their publication. Neither the company nor third parties may, in order to evade their commitments, rely on an irregularity in the appointment or removal of the liquidator, provided that it has been duly published.  

The legal personality of the company subsists for the purposes of the liquidation until the publication of the closure thereof.  
If the closure of the liquidation has not occurred within a period of three years from the dissolution, the public prosecutor or any interested party may refer the matter to the court of first instance, which shall have the liquidation carried out or, if it has been commenced, its completion.

###### Article 1994

After payment of debts and repayment of the share capital, the division of the assets shall be carried out among the partners in the same proportions as their participation in the profits, subject to any clause or agreement to the contrary.  
The rules concerning the division of estates, including preferential allocation, shall apply to divisions among partners.  
However, the partners may validly decide, either in the articles of association or by a separate decision or instrument, that certain assets shall be allocated to certain partners. In default thereof, any contributed asset which is found in kind in the mass to be divided shall be allocated, upon their request, and subject to an equalisation payment if applicable, to the partner who had made the contribution. This option shall be exercised before any other right to a preferential allocation.  

All the partners, or only some of them, may also remain in joint ownership for all or part of the company assets. Their relations are then governed, at the closure of the liquidation, with regard to these assets, by the provisions relating to joint ownership.

###### Article 1995

The nullity of the company may only result from the violation of the provisions of Articles 1969 and 1970, or from one of the grounds for nullity of contracts in general.  
Any clause in the articles of association contrary to a mandatory provision of this title the violation of which is not sanctioned by the nullity of the company, shall be deemed unwritten.  
The nullity of acts or resolutions of the organs of the company may only result from the violation of a mandatory provision of this title or from one of the grounds for nullity of contracts in general.

###### Article 1996

The action for nullity is extinguished when the ground for nullity has ceased to exist on the day the court rules on the merits at first instance, unless this nullity is based on the unlawfulness of the corporate object.

###### Article 1997

In the event of nullity of a company or of acts or resolutions subsequent to its formation, based on a defect of consent or the incapacity of a partner, and where rectification may occur, any person having an interest therein may give formal notice to the person who is able to effect it, either to rectify or to bring an action for nullity within a period of six months on pain of forfeiture. This formal notice is notified to the company.  
The company or a partner may submit to the court seized within the period provided for in the preceding paragraph, any measure likely to eliminate the interest of the claimant, in particular by the purchase of his company rights. In this case, the court may either pronounce the nullity or make the proposed measures mandatory if they have been previously adopted by the company under the conditions provided for statutory amendments. The vote of the partner whose purchase of rights is requested has no influence on the decision of the company.  

In the event of dispute, the value of the company rights to be reimbursed to the partner is determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983.

###### Article 1998

The court, seized of an application for nullity, may, even of its own motion, fix a period to allow the nullities to be cured. It may not pronounce nullity less than two months after the date of the writ initiating proceedings.  
If, to cure a nullity, a meeting must be convened, or a consultation of the partners must be carried out, and if proof is provided of a regular convening of this meeting or of the sending to the partners of the text of the draft decisions accompanied by the documents which must be communicated to them, the president of the court of first instance seized by way of summary proceedings, grants the time necessary for the partners to make a decision.

###### Article 1999

Actions for nullity of the company or of acts and resolutions subsequent to its formation are barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the nullity was incurred.

###### Article 2000

When the nullity of the company is pronounced, it terminates, without retroactive effect, the performance of the company contract.  

With regard to the legal person which may have come into existence, the nullity of the company produces the effects of a dissolution pronounced by court order.

###### Article 2001

Neither the company nor the partners may rely on a nullity against third parties in good faith.  

However, nullity resulting from incapacity or from one of the defects of consent may be invoked even against third parties in good faith by the incapable person and his legal representatives, or by the partner whose consent was obtained by error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 2002

The action for liability based on the annulment of the company or of acts and resolutions subsequent to formation is barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the decision of annulment became res judicata.  
The disappearance of the cause of nullity does not prevent the exercise of the action for damages seeking reparation for the harm caused by the defect with which the company, the act or the resolution was tainted. This action is barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

#### Chapitre II. De la société civile

##### Section I : Dispositions générales Article 2003

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all civil companies, unless derogated from by the particular legal status to which some of them are subject.  

All companies to which the law does not attribute another character by reason of their form, their nature, or their object have civil character.

###### Article 2004

The capital is divided into equal shares.  

The provisions of Chapter I of Title II of Book III of the Commercial Code relating to the variable capital of companies are applicable to civil companies.

##### Section II : De la gérance Article 2005

The company is managed by one or more persons, whether partners or not, appointed either by the articles of association, or by a separate instrument, or by a decision of the partners.  
The articles of association fix the rules for designation of the manager or managers and the method of organization of the management.  

Unless otherwise provided by the articles of association, the manager is appointed by a decision of the partners representing more than half of the company shares.  
In the silence of the articles of association, and if the partners have not decided otherwise at the time of designation, the managers are deemed appointed for the duration of the company.  

If, for any reason whatsoever, the company finds itself without a manager, any partner may request the president of the court of first instance ruling on application the designation of a representative charged with bringing the partners together with a view to appointing one or more managers.

###### Article 2006

Apart from the cases referred to in Article 1992, the company is terminated by early dissolution which may be pronounced by the court of first instance at the request of any interested party, when it has been without a manager for more than one year.

###### Article 2007

The appointment and cessation of function of managers must be published.  

Neither the company nor third parties may, to avoid their commitments, rely on an irregularity in the appointment of managers or in the cessation of their function, when these decisions have been regularly published.

###### Article 2008

If a legal person exercises the management, its directors are subject to the same conditions and obligations and incur the same civil and criminal liabilities as if they were managers in their own name, without prejudice to the joint and several liability of the legal person which they direct.

###### Article 2009

In relations between partners, the manager may perform all management acts required by the interest of the company.  
If there are several managers, they exercise these powers separately, except for the right which belongs to each to oppose an operation before it is concluded.  
All this, in the absence of provisions in the articles of association on the method of administration.

###### Article 2010

In relations with third parties, the manager binds the company by acts falling within the corporate object.  

In the event of a plurality of managers, they hold separately the powers provided for in the preceding paragraph. Opposition made by one manager to the acts of another manager has no effect with regard to third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of it.  

Statutory clauses limiting the powers of managers may not be invoked against third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of them.

###### Article 2011

Each manager is individually liable to the company and to third parties, either for infringements of laws and regulations, or for violation of the articles of association, or for faults committed in his management.  
If several managers have participated in the same acts, their liability is joint and several with regard to third parties and partners. However, in their relations among themselves, the court determines the contributory share of each in the reparation of the damage.

###### Article 2012

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, the manager may be removed by a decision of the partners representing more than half of the shares. If the removal is decided without just cause, it may give rise to damages.  
The manager may also be removed by the courts for legitimate cause, at the request of any partner.  

Unless otherwise stipulated, the removal of a manager, whether a partner or not, does not result in the dissolution of the company. If the removed manager is a partner, he may, unless otherwise agreed in the articles of association, or unless the other partners decide on the early dissolution of the company, withdraw from it and claim reimbursement of the value of his partnership rights determined, in the absence of amicable agreement, by expert opinion, in accordance with Article 1983.

##### Section III: Collective decisions Article 2013

Decisions that exceed the powers granted to the managers are made according to the provisions of the articles of association or, in the absence of such provisions, by unanimous consent of the partners.

###### Article 2014

Decisions are made by the partners meeting in assembly. The articles of association may also provide that they result from a written consultation or by electronic means.

###### Article 2015

Decisions may also result from the consent of all the partners expressed in a deed.

##### Section IV: Information of partners Article 2016

Partners have the right to obtain, at least once a year, access to the company's books and documents, and to ask written questions about the company's management to which answers must be provided in writing within one month.

###### Article 2017

Managers must, at least once a year, account for their management to the partners. This account must include a comprehensive written report on the company's activity during the year or past financial period, indicating the profits made or foreseeable and the losses incurred or anticipated.

##### Section V: Obligations of partners towards third parties

###### Article 2018

Towards third parties, partners are indefinitely liable for company debts in proportion to their share in the share capital on the date of maturity or on the day of cessation of payments.  
The partner who has only contributed his industry is liable as the one whose participation in the share capital is the smallest.

###### Article 2019

Creditors may not pursue payment of company debts against a partner except after having previously and unsuccessfully pursued the legal entity.

###### Article 2020

All actions against non-liquidating partners or their heirs and successors are barred by limitation after three years from the publication of the dissolution of the company.

###### Article 2021

If there is insolvency, personal bankruptcy, liquidation of assets or judicial settlement affecting one of the partners, unless the others unanimously decide to dissolve the company early or unless such dissolution is provided for in the articles of association, the reimbursement of the partnership rights of the person concerned shall be carried out under the conditions set out in Article 1983, and he shall then lose the status of partner.

##### Section VI: Transfer of shares Article 2022

Shares may only be transferred with the approval of all partners.  

The articles of association may however agree that this approval will be either obtained by a majority they determine, or granted by the managers. They may also waive the approval requirement for transfers made to partners or to the spouse of one of them. Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, transfers made to ascendants or descendants of the transferor are not subject to approval.  

The proposed transfer is notified, with a request for approval, to the company and to each of the partners. It is notified only to the company when the articles of association provide that approval may be granted by the managers.  
When two spouses are simultaneously members of a company, transfers made by one of them to the other must, to be valid, result from a notarial deed or from a deed under private signature having acquired certain date otherwise than by the death of the transferor.

###### Article 2023

When several partners express their intention to acquire, they are, unless otherwise stipulated or agreed, deemed to be purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held.  
If no partner comes forward as purchaser, the company may have the shares acquired by a third party designated by unanimous consent of the other partners or according to the procedures provided for in the articles of association. In case of deadlock, Article 2024, paragraph 1 applies. The company may also proceed with the repurchase of the shares with a view to their cancellation.  

The name of the proposed purchaser(s), partners or third parties, or the company's repurchase offer, as well as the price offered are notified to the transferor. In case of dispute over the price, it is determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983, all without prejudice to the transferor's right to retain his shares.

###### Article 2024

If no purchase offer is made to the transferor within six months from the last of the notifications provided for in the third paragraph of Article 2022, approval of the transfer is deemed to have been obtained, unless the other partners decide, within the same period, on the early dissolution of the company.  
In the latter case, the transferor may render this decision null and void by making known that he renounces the transfer within one month from said decision.

###### Article 2025

The provisions of the two preceding articles may only be derogated from to modify the six-month period provided for in the first paragraph of Article 2024, and provided that the period stipulated in the articles of association does not exceed one year nor be less than one month.

###### Article 2026

The transfer of shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company by service of the transfer made or, if the articles of association so stipulate, by transfer in the company's registers.  
It is only enforceable against third parties after completion of these formalities and after publication.

###### Article 2027

Shares may be the subject of a pledge recorded either by authentic deed or by deed under private signatures served on the company or accepted by it in an authentic deed, and giving rise to publication the date of which determines the rank of pledgee creditors. Those whose titles are published on the same day rank equally.  
The privilege of the pledgee creditor subsists on the pledged partnership rights by the mere fact of publication of the pledge.

###### Article 2028

Any partner may obtain from the other partners their consent to a proposed pledge under the same conditions as their approval for a transfer of shares.  
Consent given to the proposed pledge implies approval of the transferee in case of forced realization of the shares on condition that this realization is notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company.  

Each partner may substitute himself for the purchaser within five clear days from the sale. If several partners exercise this option, they are, unless otherwise stipulated or agreed, deemed to be purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held. If no partner exercises this option, the company may repurchase the shares itself, with a view to their cancellation.

###### Article 2029

Forced realisation that does not proceed from a pledge to which the other partners have given their consent must likewise be notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company.  
The partners may, within this period, decide to dissolve the company or to acquire the shares under the conditions provided for in Articles 2023 and 2024.  
If the sale has taken place, the partners or the company may exercise the right of substitution recognised to them by Article 2028. Failure to exercise this right entails approval of the purchaser.

##### Section VII: Withdrawal or death of a partner

###### Article 2030

Without prejudice to the rights of third parties, a partner may withdraw totally or partially from the company, under the conditions provided for in the articles of association or, failing that, after authorisation given by a unanimous decision of the other partners. This withdrawal may also be authorised for just cause by a court decision.  
Unless certain assets of the company of equivalent value are allocated to him, the partner who withdraws is entitled to reimbursement of the value of his partnership rights, fixed, in the absence of amicable agreement, by expert determination, in accordance with Article 1983.

###### Article 2031

The company is not dissolved by the death of a partner, but continues with his heirs or legatees, subject to providing in the articles of association that they must be approved by the partners.  
It may however be agreed that this death will result in the dissolution of the company or that it will continue with the surviving partners only.  

It may also be agreed that the company will continue either with the surviving spouse, or with one or more of the heirs, or with any other person designated by the articles of association or, if they so authorise, by testamentary disposition.  

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, where the succession devolves to a legal person, the latter may become a partner only with the approval of the other partners, given according to the conditions in the articles of association or, failing that, by unanimous agreement of the partners.

###### Article 2032

The heirs or legatees who do not become partners are entitled only to the value of the partnership shares of their predecessor. This value must be paid to them by the new holders of the shares or by the company itself if it has repurchased them with a view to their cancellation.  
The value of these partnership rights is determined at the date of death by expert determination, except by amicable agreement, under the conditions provided for in Article 1983.

#### Chapter III: Undisclosed partnership Article 2033

The partners may agree that the company will not be registered. The company is then called an "undisclosed partnership". Such a company is not a legal person and is not subject to publicity. Its existence may be proved by any means.  

The partners freely agree on the object, operation and conditions of the undisclosed partnership, subject to the mandatory rules of the general law of companies.

###### Article 2034

Unless a different organisation has been provided for, the relations between partners are governed, as appropriate, either by the provisions applicable to civil companies, if the company has a civil character, or, if it has a commercial character, by those applicable to general partnerships.

###### Article 2035

In relation to third parties, each partner remains the owner of the assets that he makes available to the company.  

Assets acquired by use or reinvestment of undivided funds during the life of the company and those which were undivided before being made available to the company are deemed to be undivided between the partners.  

The same applies to those which the partners have agreed to place in undivided ownership.  

It may further be agreed that one of the partners is, in relation to third parties, the owner of all or part of the assets that he acquires with a view to achieving the corporate object.

###### Article 2036

Each partner contracts in his own name and is alone bound in relation to third parties.  

However, if the participants act in the capacity of partners in the sight and knowledge of third parties, each of them is liable in relation to the latter for obligations arising from acts performed in that capacity by one of the others, with joint and several liability, if the company is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.  

The same applies to the partner who, by his interference, has led the contracting party to believe that he intended to bind himself towards him, or whose engagement is proved to have benefited him.  
In all cases, with regard to assets deemed undivided pursuant to Article 2035 (paragraphs 2 and 3), the provisions of Chapter VI of Title I of Book III of this Code (Articles 933 et seq.) are applicable in relations with third parties, or, if the formalities provided for in Article 2037 have been completed, those of Title XI of this Book (

###### article 2071

et seq.), all partners then being, unless otherwise agreed, deemed managers of the undivided ownership.

###### Article 2037

Where the undisclosed partnership is of indefinite duration, its dissolution may result at any time from a notification addressed by one of them to all the partners provided that this notification is in good faith and not made at an inopportune time.  
Unless otherwise agreed, no partner may request the partition of undivided assets pursuant to the rules applicable to undivided ownership under Article 2035 so long as the company is not dissolved.

###### Article 2038

The provisions of this Chapter are applicable to companies created de facto.

#### Chapter IV

Professional civil company Section I: General provisions

###### Article 2039

Professional civil companies may be formed between natural persons practising the same liberal profession subject to a legislative or regulatory status or whose title is protected, and in particular between public officers and ministerial officers, which enjoy legal personality and are subject to the provisions of this Chapter III.  
These professional civil companies have as their object the joint practice of the profession of their members, notwithstanding any legislative or regulatory provision reserving the practice of that profession to natural persons.  

Registration of the company may take place only after approval thereof by the competent authority or its registration on the list or roll of the professional order.  

The conditions for application of this Chapter III to each profession are determined by the laws and regulations applicable to each of the professions concerned.

###### Article 2040

A decree may authorise, under the conditions it determines, natural persons practising a liberal profession referred to in the preceding article, to form companies governed by this Chapter III with natural persons practising other liberal professions with a view to the joint practice of their respective professions.  
Members of the professions referred to in Article 2039 may enter a professional civil company grouping persons belonging to liberal professions not referred to in Article 2039 only on condition that they have been authorised to do so by the body exercising disciplinary jurisdiction over them. In the event of refusal of authorisation, an appeal may be made to the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal.  

The companies referred to in this article may perform the acts of a particular profession only through one of their members qualified to practise that profession.

###### Article 2041

Only persons who, prior to the formation of the company, regularly practiced the profession, as well as those who, meeting all the conditions required by the laws and regulations in force, are entitled to practice it, may be partners, subject to the provisions of Article 2062.

###### Article 2042

Except where otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, any partner may be a member of only one professional civil company and may not practice the same profession individually.

###### Article 2043

Natural persons holding a public or ministerial office and practicing the same profession may also form professional civil companies among themselves for the joint practice of their profession, without such companies themselves being appointed holders of an office.  
The application of the preceding paragraph is subject to the provisions of Article 2039, paragraph 3.  

The provisions of Article 2040 are applicable to companies formed pursuant to this article.

##### Section II : Constitution de la société Article 2044

Professional civil companies are freely formed under the conditions provided by the regulations specific to each profession, which shall determine the approval or registration procedure and the role of professional bodies.  
With regard to public and ministerial offices, the company must be approved or appointed to the office under the conditions to be provided by decree.

###### Article 2045

The articles of association of the company must be drawn up in writing. The regulations specific to each profession determine the information that must be included in the articles of association.  

The corporate name of the company must be immediately preceded or followed by the words:
"société civile professionnelle" or the initials: "SCP", themselves followed by an indication of the profession practiced.  
The name of one or more partners may be included in the corporate name.

###### Article 2047

The share capital is divided into equal shares which may not be represented by negotiable instruments. The regulations specific to each profession may limit the number of partners.

###### Article 2048

The shares must be subscribed in full by the partners. Those representing contributions in kind must be fully paid up upon formation of the company.  
The distribution of shares is stated in the articles of association. It takes into account contributions in cash and, according to the valuation made thereof, contributions in kind and in particular contributions of intangible rights.  
The articles of association may, by unanimous decision of the partners, establish the principles and methods applicable to determining the value of the shares.  

Except where otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, the value of the shares takes into consideration a value representing the civil clientele. However, by unanimous decision of the partners, the articles of association may exclude this value representing the civil clientele from the valuation of the shares.

##### Section III : Fonctionnement de la société Article 2049

All partners are managers unless otherwise stipulated in the articles of association, which may designate one or more managers from among the partners or provide for their designation by a subsequent act.  
The conditions for appointment and removal of managers, their powers and the duration of their term of office are determined by the articles of association. The powers of managers may in no case have the effect of creating subordination of the partners to the company for the performance of their professional acts.

###### Article 2050

Managers are liable, individually or jointly and severally as the case may be, towards the company or towards third parties, either for infringements of laws and regulations, or for violation of the articles of association, or for faults committed in their management. If several managers have cooperated in the same acts, the court shall determine the contributory share of each in the apportionment of the damage.

###### Article 2051

Decisions that exceed the powers of the managers are taken by the partners.  

Each partner has, except for special provisions of the decree specific to each profession or, failing that, of the articles of association, one vote only, regardless of the number of shares he holds.  
The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association determine the method of consulting the partners, the quorum and majority rules required for the validity of their decisions and the conditions under which they are informed of the state of company affairs.  

Remuneration of any kind, paid in consideration of the professional activity of the partners, constitutes receipts of the company and is collected by it.  

The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association may determine methods of distributing profits that are not proportional to capital contributions.  

In the absence of a regulatory provision or statutory clause, each partner is entitled to the same share in the profits.

###### Article 2053

Partners are indefinitely liable for company debts towards third parties. This provision does not prevent two spouses from being partners in the same professional civil company.  
Creditors of the company may not pursue payment of company debts against a partner except after having unsuccessfully served formal notice on the company and on condition of joining it as a party.  
The articles of association may stipulate that, in relations between partners, each of them is liable for company debts in the proportion they determine.

###### Article 2054

Each partner is liable on his entire patrimony for the professional acts he performs. The company is jointly and severally liable with him for the harmful consequences of such acts.  
The company or the partners must take out professional liability insurance, under the conditions provided by the regulations specific to each profession.

###### Article 2055

The regulations specific to each profession determine the powers and authority of each partner and of the company for the practice of the profession, and make, where appropriate, adaptations to the rules of professional ethics and discipline applicable to them.

###### Article 2056

A partner may withdraw from the company, either by transferring his shares or by having the company reimburse him the value of his shares.  
Upon the withdrawal of a partner, the professional civil company is subject to the registration modifications and the transferee of the shares to the approval procedure, provided by the regulations specific to each profession.  

With regard to public and ministerial offices, the regulations specific to each profession determine the conditions under which the transferee of the shares must be approved by the appointing authority and the withdrawal of the partner to whom the value of his shares is reimbursed must be approved.

###### Article 2057

Company shares may be transferred or assigned to third parties with the consent of the partners representing at least three-quarters of the votes. However, the articles of association may require a larger majority or the unanimity of the partners.  
The transfer or proposed assignment is notified to the company and to each of the partners. If the company has not made its decision known within two months from the last of the notifications provided for in this paragraph, consent is implicitly given.  

If the company has refused to give its consent, the partners are required, within six months from such refusal, to acquire or have acquired the company shares at a price representing their value

determined in application of the third and fourth paragraphs of Article 2048 or, where the articles of association do not provide for the methods of determining the price, a price fixed under the conditions provided for by Article 1983 of the Civil Code.

###### Article 2058

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, company shares are freely transferable between partners.  

If the articles of association contain a clause limiting freedom of transfer, the provisions of Article 2057, paragraphs 2 and 3, are applicable in the absence of statutory provisions.

###### Article 2059

When a partner so requests, the company is required either to have his shares acquired by other partners or third parties, or to acquire them itself, under the conditions determined by the regulations specific to each profession. In the latter case, the company is required to reduce its capital by the amount of the nominal value of those shares.

###### Article 2060

The assignment of company shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company in the forms provided for in Article 1994.  
The assignment of company shares is enforceable against third parties only after completion of these formalities and, in addition, after publication inserted in the Official Journal or in a legal notices newspaper.

###### Article 2061

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, the articles of association freely determine the duration of the company.

###### Article 2062

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession or, failing that, by the articles of association, the professional civil company is not dissolved by the death, incapacity or withdrawal from the company of a partner for any other cause. Nor is it dissolved when one of the partners is subject to a permanent prohibition from practising his profession.  
In the event of death, the successors in title of the deceased partner do not acquire the status of partner. However, they have the option of assigning the company shares of the deceased partner, within the time limits and conditions provided for in Articles 2057 and 2060; furthermore, if one or more of them meet the conditions required by Article 2041, they may request the consent of the company under the conditions provided for in Article 2057. If consent is given, the company shares of the deceased partner may be the subject of a preferential allocation to the approved successor in title, subject to an equalisation payment if applicable. In the event of refusal, the above time limit is extended by the time elapsed between the request for consent and the refusal thereof. If no assignment or consent has occurred upon expiry of the time limit, the company or the partners reimburse the value of the company shares to the successors in title under the conditions provided for in Article 2059.  
The partner subject to a permanent prohibition from practising the profession loses, on the day of such prohibition, the status of partner. The provisions of the preceding paragraph are applicable, with the exception of those concerning the successors in title of the person concerned.  

During the time limit provided for in paragraph 2 above, the partner, his heirs or successors in title, as the case may be, may not exercise any right in the company. However, and unless they are deprived thereof, they retain entitlement to the distribution of profits, under the conditions provided for by the articles of association.

###### Article 2063

The regulations specific to each profession determine the effects of the temporary prohibition from practising the profession with which a partner or the company may be subject.

###### Article 2064

The dissolution or extension of the company is decided by the partners voting by the majority that will be determined by the regulations specific to the profession.  
When the company formed between partners practising different professions no longer includes, at least, one partner practising each of the professions concerned, the partners may, within one year, regularise the situation or decide to modify the corporate purpose. Failing that, the company is dissolved.

###### Article 2065
