The professional civil company may not, unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to the profession, be transformed into a company of another form.  
A company of another form may be transformed into a professional civil company without such transformation resulting in the creation of a new legal person.

###### Article 2066

The nullity of the professional civil company may only be pronounced for lack of a constitutive instrument or in the cases provided for by the provisions governing nullities of contracts.  
Neither the company nor the partners may rely on the nullity against third parties.

###### Article 2067

The designation "professional civil company" may only be used by companies subject to the provisions of this Chapter III.  
The unlawful use of this designation or of any expression likely to cause confusion therewith is punishable by imprisonment of one year and a fine of 1,000,000 FD, or by one of these two penalties only.  
The court may, in addition, order the publication of the judgment, at the expense of the convicted person, and its posting.

###### Article 2068

Articles 1969 to 2037 are applicable to professional civil companies, in their provisions that are not contrary to those of this chapter.

###### Article 2069

The partners of professional civil companies formed and operating in accordance with the provisions of this chapter are personally subject to income tax on natural persons for the share of company profits allocated to them.

##### Section IV: Civil companies for means Article 2070

Notwithstanding any contrary legislative or regulatory provisions, natural or legal persons practising liberal professions and in particular public officers and ministerial officers, may form among themselves civil companies having as their exclusive purpose to facilitate for each of their members the exercise of his activity.  

For this purpose, the partners pool the means useful for the exercise of their professions, without the company itself being able to practise it.

### Titre XI: Conventional regime of joint ownership

Chapitre Ier: Agreements relating to the exercise of undivided rights in the absence of a usufructuary Article 2071
Joint owners, if they all consent thereto, may agree to remain in joint ownership.  

On pain of nullity, the agreement must be established in writing containing the designation of the jointly owned property and the indication of the shares belonging to each joint owner. If the jointly owned property includes claims, the agreement is enforceable against the debtors concerned only from the service upon them thereof, or from its acceptance by the debtor in an authentic instrument; if it includes immovable property, the formalities of land registration are required.

###### Article 2072

The agreement may be concluded for a fixed term, less than or equal to five years. It is renewable by an express decision of the parties. Partition may not be brought about before the agreed term unless there are just grounds for it.  
It may also be decided that this fixed-term agreement shall be renewed by tacit renewal, for a fixed or indefinite term. In the absence of such an agreement, the co-ownership shall be governed by articles 933 et seq. upon expiry of the fixed-term agreement.  
The agreement may also be concluded for an indefinite term. Partition may, in this case, be brought about at any time, provided that it is not done in bad faith or at an inopportune time.

###### Article 2073

The agreement for the maintenance of co-ownership requires the capacity or power to dispose of the co-owned property.  
It may, however, be concluded on behalf of a minor by his legal representative alone; but, in this case, the minor who has reached the age of majority may terminate it, whatever its duration, within one year following his majority.

###### Article 2074

The co-owners may appoint one or more managers, chosen from among themselves or not.  
The terms of appointment and revocation of the manager may be determined by a unanimous decision of the co-owners.  
In the absence of such an agreement, the manager chosen from among the co-owners may only be removed from his functions by a unanimous decision of the other co-owners.  

The manager, who is not a co-owner, may be revoked under the conditions agreed between his principals or, failing that, by a decision taken by a majority of the co-owners in number and in shares. In all cases, revocation may be pronounced by the court at the request of a co-owner when the manager, through his management faults, jeopardizes the interests of the co-ownership.  

If the revoked manager is a co-owner, the agreement shall be deemed to be concluded for an indefinite term from the date of his revocation.

###### Article 2075

The manager represents the co-owners within the scope of his powers, either for acts of civil life or in legal proceedings, both as plaintiff and as defendant. He is required to indicate, purely for information purposes, the names of all the co-owners in the first procedural document.  

The manager administers the co-ownership and exercises, for this purpose, the powers attributed to each spouse over community property. He may not, however, dispose of corporeal movables except for the needs of normal operation of the co-owned property, or if they are things difficult to preserve or subject to deterioration. Any clause extending the manager's powers is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2076

The manager exercises the powers conferred upon him by the preceding article even when there is an incapacitated person among the co-owners.

###### Article 2077

Decisions that exceed the manager's powers are taken unanimously, except for the manager, if he is himself a co-owner, to use the procedures provided for in article 942.  
If there are incapacitated minors or adults among the co-owners, the decisions referred to in the preceding paragraph give rise to the application of the protection rules provided in their favor.  

It may be agreed between the co-owners that in the absence of incapacitated persons, certain categories of decisions shall be taken otherwise than unanimously. However, no co-owned immovable may be alienated without the agreement of all the co-owners, except pursuant to article 942 or the rules of management of another's affairs.

###### Article 2078

The co-ownership agreement may regulate the mode of administration in case of a plurality of managers. In the absence of special stipulations, they hold separately the powers provided for in article 2075, except the right for each to oppose any operation before it is concluded.

###### Article 2079

The manager is entitled, unless otherwise agreed, to remuneration for his work. The conditions thereof are fixed by the co-owners, excluding the person concerned, or, failing that, by the President of the Court of First Instance ruling provisionally.  
The manager is liable, as a mandatary, for faults he commits in his management.

###### Article 2080

Each co-owner may require the communication of all documents relating to the management. The manager must, once a year, account for his management to the co-owners. On this occasion, he shall indicate in writing the profits realized and the losses incurred or foreseeable.  
Each co-owner is required to participate in the expenses of preservation of the co-owned property. In the absence of a particular agreement, the texts governing legal co-ownership are applicable to the exercise of the right of use and enjoyment, as well as to the distribution of profits and losses.

###### Article 2081

Similarly, in case of alienation of all or part of the rights of a co-owner in the co-owned property, or in one or more of these properties, the co-owners benefit from the rights of pre-emption and substitution provided for by this legal regime. However, as soon as an undivided share devolves to a person outside the co-ownership, for whatever reason, the agreement is deemed to be concluded for an indefinite term.

###### Article 2082

The co-owners may agree that upon the death of one of them, each of the survivors may acquire the share of the deceased, or that the surviving spouse, or any other designated heir, may have it attributed to him on condition of accounting for it to the estate according to its value at the time of acquisition or attribution.  
If several co-owners or several heirs simultaneously exercise their right of acquisition or attribution, they are deemed, unless otherwise agreed, to acquire together the share of the deceased in proportion to their respective rights in the co-ownership or the estate.  

The provisions of this article may not prejudice the application of the provisions relating to preferential attributions.

###### Article 2083

The right of acquisition or attribution lapses if its beneficiary has not exercised it by notification made to the surviving co-owners and to the heirs of the predeceased within one month from the day on which he was given formal notice to take a position. This formal notice may not itself take place before the expiry of the period provided for in the title On Successions for making an inventory and deliberating.  
When no right of acquisition or attribution has been provided for, or when it has lapsed, the share of the deceased passes to his heirs or legatees. In such a case, the co-ownership agreement shall be deemed to be concluded for an indefinite term from the opening of the succession.

###### Article 2084

Article 952 is applicable to creditors of the co-ownership, as well as to personal creditors of the co-owners.  
However, the latter may only bring about partition in cases where their debtor could himself bring it about. In other cases, they may pursue the seizure and sale of their debtor's share in the co-ownership by following the forms provided for by the code of civil procedure. The provisions of article 2081 are then applicable.

#### Chapitre II

Agreements relating to the exercise of undivided rights in the presence of a usufructuary Article 2085
When the co-owned property is encumbered with a usufruct, agreements, subject in principle to the provisions of the preceding chapter, may be concluded, either between the bare owners, or between the usufructuaries, or between both.  

There may likewise be an agreement between those who are in co-ownership for the enjoyment and the person who is bare owner of all the property, as well as between the universal usufructuary and the bare owners.

###### Article 2086

Where the usufructuaries have not been party to the agreement, third parties who have dealt with the manager of the undivided ownership may not rely, to the prejudice of the usufructuary rights, on the powers that would have been conferred upon him by the bare owners.

###### Article 2087

Where the agreement entered into between usufructuaries and bare owners provides that decisions shall be taken by a majority in number and in shares, the voting right attached to the shares is divided in half between the usufruct and the bare ownership, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Any expenditure exceeding the obligations of the usufructuary, as defined by the provisions of Section III of Chapter One (articles 721 et seq.), binds him only with his consent given in the agreement itself or by a subsequent act.

The alienation of the full ownership of the undivided property may not be made without the agreement of the usufructuary, except where it is brought about by creditors entitled to pursue the sale.

### Titre XII : Du prêt

###### Article 2088

There are two kinds of loan:

That of things which can be used without destroying them;

And that of things which are consumed by the use made of them. The first kind is called loan for use.
The second is called loan for consumption.

Chapitre Ier. Du prêt à usage

##### Section I : De la nature du prêt à usage Article 2089

The loan for use is a contract by which one of the parties delivers a thing to the other to use it, on condition that the borrower returns it after having used it. The lender remains owner of the thing lent.

###### Article 2090

In the absence of contrary provision by the parties, the loan for use is gratuitous.

###### Article 2091

Anything that is in commerce and which is not consumed by use may be the object of such a loan.

###### Article 2092

The obligations which are formed by the loan for use pass to the heirs of the lender, and to the heirs of the borrower.
But if the loan was made only in consideration of the person of the borrower, the heirs must immediately return the thing lent.

##### Section II : Des engagements de l'emprunteur Article 2093

The borrower is bound to watch over, as a normally diligent person, the custody and preservation of the thing lent. He may use it only for the use determined by its nature or by the agreement; all on pain of nullity of the agreement, without prejudice to damages, if any.

###### Article 2094

If, in order to use the thing, the borrower has incurred any expense, he may not obtain restitution against the lender.

It is otherwise if, during the duration of the loan, the borrower has been obliged, for the preservation of the thing, to incur some extraordinary expense, necessary and so urgent that he could not inform the lender, the latter is then bound to reimburse him.

###### Article 2095

He is not liable for fortuitous events or force majeure when the destruction of the thing, occurring during its normal use, results from such an event or from the proper functioning of the thing lent.
The borrower is however liable for the loss of the thing lent occurring by fortuitous event or force majeure:
1° If he makes use of the thing for another purpose or for a longer time than he should;
2° If the thing lent perishes by a fortuitous event that the borrower could have counteracted by using a thing belonging to him, or if, being compelled to preserve only one of the two things, he preferred to save his own;
3° If the borrower had estimated the value of the thing in lending it, unless otherwise agreed; 4° If by express or tacit agreement the borrower has taken the fortuitous events upon himself.

The liability resting on the borrower provided for in the preceding paragraph does not apply when the thing is the object of common use by the lender and the borrower or when the lender has reserved the possibility of using the thing lent.

###### Article 2096

The borrower may not retain the thing by set-off of what the lender owes him.

###### Article 2097

If several persons have jointly borrowed the same thing, they are jointly and severally liable towards the lender.

##### Section III : Des engagements de celui qui prête à usage Article 2098

The lender may not take back the thing lent until after the agreed term, or, in the absence of such provision, until after it has served the use for which it was borrowed.

He is bound to reimburse the sums engaged by the borrower under the conditions of article 2094, second paragraph.

###### Article 2099

Nevertheless, if, during the agreed period or before the borrower's need has ceased, there arises for the lender a pressing and unforeseen need for his thing, the judge may, according to the circumstances, oblige the borrower to return it to him without waiting.

###### Article 2100

Where the thing lent has defects such that it risks causing prejudice to the person using it, the lender is liable as soon as he knew of the defects and did not warn the borrower.

#### Chapitre II : Du prêt de consommation

##### Section I : De la nature du prêt de consommation

###### Article 2101

The loan for consumption is a contract by which one of the parties delivers to the other a certain quantity of things which are consumed by use, on condition that the latter returns as much of the same kind and quality.

###### Article 2102

By the effect of this loan, the borrower becomes the owner of the thing lent.

If it perishes, it is he who, independently of the cause of this event, suffers the loss, except for his recourse against the person by whose fault it occurred

###### Article 2103

One may not give by way of loan for consumption things which, although of the same kind, differ in the individual, such as animals: then it is a loan for use.

###### Article 2104

The obligation which results from a loan in money is always only of the sum stated in the contract.

If there has been an increase or decrease in currency before the time of payment, the debtor must return the sum lent, and must return only that sum in the currency having legal tender at the time of payment.

This rule does not apply if the loan was made in bullion or commodities, in which cases the debtor must always return the same quantity and quality, and must return only that independently of the variation in value by which the property may have been affected.

##### Section II : Des obligations du prêteur Article 2105

In the loan for consumption, the lender is subject to the liability established by article 2100 for the loan for use.

###### Article 2106

The lender may not demand back the things lent before the agreed term.

###### Article 2107

If no term has been fixed for restitution, the judge may grant the borrower a period according to the circumstances.

###### Article 2108

If it has only been agreed that the borrower would pay when he could, or when he had the means, the judge shall fix a term of payment for him according to the circumstances.

##### Section III : Des engagements de l'emprunteur Article 2109

The borrower is bound to return the things lent, in the same quantity and quality, and at the agreed term.
If he is unable to satisfy this on that date, he must pay the value:	on the day and at the place of repayment when the contract has provided the time and place of restitution;	on the day and at the place where the loan was made.

If the borrower does not return the things lent or their value at the agreed term and in default, from the formal demand addressed to him, he owes interest thereon from the day of the summons or of the legal claim.

#### Chapitre III : Du prêt à intérêt Article 2111

The stipulation of interest is authorized both for the loan of money, commodities, and other movable things.

###### Article 2112

If the borrower has paid interest when it was not stipulated, he cannot obtain reimbursement. Nor can he impute it to the principal.

###### Article 2113

Interest is legal or conventional. Legal interest is fixed by law. Conventional interest may exceed that of the law, whenever the law does not prohibit it.  
The rate of conventional interest must be fixed in writing. In the absence thereof, the loan is granted gratuitously and interest at the legal rate runs only from the formal demand to return the principal.

###### Article 2114

The receipt for the principal given without reservation of interest creates a presumption of payment thereof and operates as a discharge.

###### Article 2115

It may also be provided that, in consideration for making capital available, which the lender undertakes not to demand, the borrower undertakes to pay him periodically an annuity.  
In this case, the loan takes the name of constitution of annuity.  
It may also be constituted, on a purely gratuitous basis, by gift inter vivos or by will. It must then be clothed in the forms required by law.

###### Article 2116

This annuity may be constituted in two ways, in perpetuity or for life.

###### Article 2117

An annuity constituted in perpetuity is redeemable. This possibility of redemption is imprescriptible and implied in these kinds of contracts.  
The parties may only agree that redemption shall not be made before a certain period. This period takes the form: either of a waiting period, which shall be fixed by the parties for a maximum duration of ten years, from the loan; or of a notice period, which the debtor must give to the creditor when he notifies him of his intention to redeem.

###### Article 2118

The debtor of an annuity constituted in perpetuity may be compelled to redeem: 1° If he ceases to fulfill his obligations for two years;  
2° If he fails to provide the lender with the securities promised by the contract.  

The capital of the annuity constituted in perpetuity also becomes due in the event of bankruptcy of the debtor.

###### Article 2120

The rules concerning life annuities are established in the title On Aleatory Contracts.

### Titre XIII : Du dépôt

Chapitre Ier: Des deux espèces de dépôts Article 2121
Deposit is an act by which a person receives the thing of another, with the obligation to keep it and to return it in kind.

###### Article 2122

There are two kinds of deposit: deposit properly so called and sequestration.

#### Chapitre II : Du dépôt proprement dit

##### Section I : De la nature et de l'essence du contrat de dépôt Article 2123

Deposit properly so called is an essentially gratuitous contract.

###### Article 2124

It can only have movable things as its object.

###### Article 2125

It is perfected only by the real or fictitious delivery of the thing deposited.  
Fictitious delivery suffices when the depositary is already in possession, under some other title, of the thing which one consents to leave with him as a deposit.

###### Article 2126

Deposit is voluntary or necessary.

##### Section II : Du dépôt volontaire Article 2127

Voluntary deposit is formed by the reciprocal consent of the person who makes the deposit and the person who receives it.  
Voluntary deposit presupposes persons capable of contracting. Nevertheless, if a person capable of contracting accepts a deposit made by an incapable person, he is bound by all the obligations of a true depositary; he may be sued by the tutor or administrator of the person who made the deposit.  

Conversely, if the deposit was made by a capable person to an incapable person, the person who made the deposit has only the action for revendication of the thing deposited, as long as it exists in the hands of the depositary, or the action for restitution up to the amount that has turned to the profit of the latter.

###### Article 2128

Voluntary deposit can only be validly made by the owner of the thing deposited, or with his express or tacit consent.

###### Article 2129

Voluntary deposit must be proved in writing. Proof by witness is not admitted when the value of the thing deposited exceeds 20,000 FD.

###### Article 2130

When the deposit, being above the amount provided for in the preceding article, is not proved in writing, the person who is sued as depositary is believed on his declaration, whether for the fact of the deposit itself, or for the thing which was its object, or for the fact of its restitution.

##### Section III : Des obligations du dépositaire Article 2131

The depositary must exercise, in the custody of the thing deposited, the same care that he exercises in the custody of things belonging to him.  

This obligation must be applied with greater rigor:
1° If the depositary offered himself to receive the deposit; 2° If he stipulated a salary for the custody of the deposit;  
3° If the deposit was made solely for the interest of the depositary;  
4° If it was expressly agreed that the depositary would be liable for any kind of fault.

###### Article 2132

The depositary is not liable, in any case, for accidents of force majeure, unless he has been formally demanded to return the thing deposited.

###### Article 2133

He may not use the thing deposited without the express or presumed permission of the depositor.

###### Article 2134

He must not seek to know what things have been deposited with him if they were entrusted to him in a closed container or under a sealed envelope.

###### Article 2135

When the thing deposited is a specific thing, the depositary must return the very thing he received. Otherwise, he must return a thing of the same kind, and identical in quantity and quality.

###### Article 2136

The depositary returns the thing deposited in the state in which it is at the moment of restitution. Deteriorations that have not occurred through his act are at the expense of the depositor.

###### Article 2137

If the thing deposited comes to disappear as a result of a case of force majeure, the depositary who has received a price or something in its place must return what he has received in exchange.

###### Article 2138

The heir of the depositary, who has sold in good faith the thing of whose deposit he was unaware, is only bound to return the price he has received, or to assign his action against the buyer, if he has not received the price.

###### Article 2139

If the thing deposited has produced fruits that have been collected by the depositary, he is obliged to return them. He owes no interest on the money deposited, except from the day on which he was formally demanded to make restitution.

###### Article 2140

The depositary must return the thing deposited only to the person who entrusted it to him, or to the person in whose name the deposit was made, or to the person who was designated to receive it.

###### Article 2141

He cannot require of the person who made the deposit, proof that he was the owner of the thing deposited.  

Nevertheless, if he discovers that the thing was stolen, and who is the true owner, he must notify the latter of the deposit that was made with him with summons to claim it within a fixed and sufficient period. If the person to whom the notification was made neglects to claim the deposit, the depositary is validly discharged by returning it to the person from whom he received it.

###### Article 2142

In the event of death of the person who made the deposit, the thing deposited can only be returned to his heir. If there are several heirs, it must be returned to each of them for their share and portion.  
If the thing deposited is indivisible, the heirs must agree among themselves to receive it.

###### Article 2143

If the person who made the deposit has been divested of their powers of administration, for example when an adult depositor becomes subject to incapacity, the deposit may only be returned to the person who has the administration of the depositor's property.

###### Article 2144

If the deposit was made by a guardian or an administrator, in one of these capacities, it may only be returned to the person whom that guardian or administrator represented, if their guardianship or administration has ended.

###### Article 2145

If the deposit contract designates the place in which the return must be made, the depositary is required to take the deposited thing there. If there are transportation costs, they are borne by the depositor.  
If the contract does not designate the place of return, it must be made in the very place of the deposit.

###### Article 2146

The deposit must be returned to the depositor as soon as he claims it, even if the contract had fixed a specific time limit for the return; unless there exists, in the hands of the depositary, a seizure or an opposition to the return and removal of the deposited thing.

###### Article 2147

The depositary who misappropriates the thing entrusted to him or who, through his fault, cannot return the deposited thing must pay its value, at the depositor's choice, either on the day of the deposit or on the day the judge rules, without prejudice to damages that may be awarded.

###### Article 2148

All obligations of the depositary cease if he comes to discover and prove that he is himself the owner of the deposited thing.

##### Section IV : Des obligations du déposant Article 2149

The depositor must reimburse the depositary for the expenses he incurred for the preservation of the deposited thing, and indemnify him for all losses that the deposit may have caused him.

###### Article 2150

The depositary may retain the deposited thing until full payment of what is owed to him by reason of the deposit.

##### Section V : Du dépôt nécessaire Article 2151

Necessary deposit results from the constraint suffered by a person, by reason of an unforeseen event, for example, a fire, a collapse, a pillage, or a shipwreck, to deposit their effects in the hands of a third party to ensure their safekeeping.  

Except for special provisions, necessary deposit is governed by all the rules previously stated.

###### Article 2152

Proof by witnesses may be received for necessary deposit, even when it concerns a value exceeding the amount provided for in Article 2129.

###### Article 2153

Hotel deposit is assimilated to necessary deposit: innkeepers or hoteliers are responsible, as depositaries, for the clothing, luggage and various objects brought into their establishment by the traveler who lodges with them.  
They are responsible for the theft or damage of the traveler's effects, whether the theft was committed or the damage was caused by their employees, or by third parties coming and going in the hotel or any establishment assimilated to a hotel.  

When an object, whatever its nature or value, has been deposited in their hands or they have refused to receive it without legitimate reason, their liability in case of theft or deterioration is complete, notwithstanding any contrary clause. In all other cases, the damages owed to the traveler are, to the exclusion of any lower contractual limitation, limited to the equivalent of twenty times the rental price of the accommodation per day, except when the traveler demonstrates that the harm he suffered results from a fault of the person who accommodates him or of the persons for whom the latter must answer.  

They are not, however, responsible for thefts committed with armed force or other cases of force majeure.

#### Chapitre III : Du séquestre Article 2154

Sequestration is conventional or judicial.

##### Section I : Du séquestre conventionnel

###### Article 2155

Conventional sequestration is the deposit made by one or more persons, of a contentious thing, in the hands of a third party who undertakes to return it, after the dispute is ended, to the person who is judged to be entitled to obtain it.

###### Article 2156

Sequestration need not be gratuitous.  
When it is gratuitous, it is subject to the rules of deposit properly so called, provided that:
1° Sequestration may have as its object, not only movable effects, but also immovables. 2° The depositary charged with sequestration may not be discharged before the dispute is ended, except with the consent of all interested parties, or for a cause judged legitimate such as a long absence or a failing state of health, and obtain, if applicable, the designation of a replacement.

##### Section II : Du séquestre ou « dépôt judiciaire » Article 2157

Justice may order sequestration:
1° Of movables seized from a debtor;  

2° Of an immovable or a movable thing whose ownership or possession is disputed between two or more persons;  
3° Of things, according to what he owes, that a debtor offers for his release.

###### Article 2158

The establishment of a judicial keeper produces, between the seizing party and the keeper, reciprocal obligations:
1° The keeper must:	exercise, for the preservation of the seized effects, the care of a good father of a family;	produce said effects, either to the discharge of the seizing party for the sale, or to the party against whom the executions were made, in case of release of the seizure.  
2° The seizing party must pay the keeper the salary determined by the judge.

###### Article 2159

Judicial sequestration is given, either to a person whom the interested parties have agreed upon among themselves, or to a person appointed ex officio by the judge.  
In both cases, the person to whom the thing has been entrusted is subject to all the obligations that conventional sequestration entails.

### Titre XIV : Des contrats aléatoires

Chapitre Ier: Du jeu et du pari Article 2160
The law grants no action for a gambling debt or for the payment of a wager.

###### Article 2161

However, the loser may never recover what he has voluntarily paid, unless there has been, on the part of the winner, fraud, trickery or swindling.

#### Chapitre II : Du contrat de rente viagère

##### Section I : Des conditions requises pour la validité du contrat Article 2162

An annuity is a claim whose object is a periodic income obtained by a person, called the annuitant, from another person, the debtor of the annuity; when it is life annuity, the annuity is paid throughout the life of its beneficiary.

###### Article 2163

The annuity may be constituted for valuable consideration, by means of a sum of money, or for an appreciable movable thing, or for an immovable.

###### Article 2164

It may also be constituted, on a purely gratuitous basis, by donation inter vivos or by will. It must then be clothed with the forms required by law. Such is especially the case for annuities constituted by way of partition-donation.  
When it is constituted on a purely gratuitous basis, the annuity is reducible if it exceeds that which one is permitted to dispose of; it is null if it is in favor of a person incapable of receiving.

###### Article 2165

The annuity may be constituted either on the head of the person who furnishes the price, or on the head of a third party, although the price of the annuity is furnished in that case by another person.  
It may also be constituted on one or more heads.

###### Article 2166

When an annuity is constituted on the life of a third party, although it has the characteristics of a liberality, it is not subject to the forms required for donations; except that it may be reduced if it exceeds what one is permitted to dispose of or be annulled if it is made in favour of a person incapable of receiving.  
In life annuity constitution contracts, the clause by which the purchaser stipulates that after his death, the annuity shall be continued to a third party during the latter's life, is valid, even though that third party has not been a party to the contract.  

When, constituted by spouses or one of them, the annuity is stipulated reversionary in favour of the surviving spouse, the reversionary clause may have the characteristics of a liberality or those of an act for valuable consideration. In the latter case, the compensation or indemnity owed by the beneficiary of the reversion to the community or to the estate of the predeceased is equal to the value of the reversion of the annuity. Unless the spouses express a contrary intention, the reversion is presumed to have been granted gratuitously.

###### Article 2167

Any life annuity contract, created on the life of a person who was dead on the day of the contract, produces no effect.  
The same applies to a contract by which the annuity was created on the life of a person suffering from the illness from which he died within twenty days of the date of the contract.

###### Article 2168

A life annuity may be constituted at the rate which the contracting parties are pleased to fix.

##### Section II : Des effets du contrat entre les parties contractantes Article 2169

The person for whose benefit the life annuity has been constituted for a price may demand the rescission of the contract, if the annuity debtor does not give him the security which may have been stipulated for its performance.

###### Article 2170

The mere failure to pay the arrears of the annuity does not authorise the person in whose favour it is constituted to demand the reimbursement of the capital, or to re-enter the property alienated by him: he has only the right to seize and cause to be sold the property of his debtor and to have ordered or agreed, from the proceeds of the sale, the employment of a sum sufficient for the service of the arrears.

###### Article 2171

The annuity debtor cannot discharge himself from payment of the annuity, by offering to reimburse the capital and renouncing the recovery of arrears paid: he is bound to serve the annuity during the whole life of the person or persons on whose life the annuity was constituted, whatever the duration of the life of those persons, and however onerous the service of the annuity may have become.

###### Article 2172

The life annuity is acquired by the owner only in proportion to the number of days he has lived.  

Nevertheless, if it has been agreed that it shall be paid in advance, the term which was to be paid is acquired from the day on which payment was to be made.

###### Article 2173

A life annuity may be stipulated unseizable only when it has been constituted gratuitously.

###### Article 2174

The holder of a life annuity may demand its arrears only by proving his existence, or that of the person on whose life it was constituted.

### Titre XV : Du mandat

Chapitre Ier: De la nature et de la forme du mandat Article 2175
Mandate, or power of attorney, is an act by which one person called the principal, gives to another, the mandatary, the power to do something for the principal and in his name.  
The contract is formed only by the acceptance of the mandatary.

###### Article 2176

Mandate may be given by authentic act or by private written instrument, even by letter. It may also be given verbally; but testimonial proof thereof is admissible only in accordance with the title On Obligations.  
Acceptance of the mandate may be only tacit, and result from the performance given to it by the mandatary.

###### Article 2177

Mandate is gratuitous, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 2178

It is special when it is given for one matter or certain matters only; it is general when it is given for all the affairs of the principal.  
When it is general, the mandate permits only acts of administration.  

If it concerns alienating or mortgaging, or any other act of ownership, the mandate must be express.

###### Article 2179

The mandatary may do nothing beyond what is contained in his mandate. The power to compromise does not include that to submit to arbitration.

###### Article 2180

In case of absence, exceeding or misuse of power by the mandatary, the rules of article 1274 are applicable.

###### Article 2181

An unemancipated minor may be chosen as mandatary; but the principal shall have no action against him except according to the general rules relating to the obligations of minors.

#### Chapitre II : Des obligations du mandataire Article 2182

The mandatary is bound to accomplish the mandate so long as he remains charged with it, and is liable for damages which might result from his non-performance.  
He is likewise bound to complete the thing begun at the death of the principal, if there is danger in delay.

###### Article 2183

The mandatary is liable not only for fraud, but also for faults he commits in his management.  

Nevertheless, liability relating to faults is applied less rigorously to one whose mandate is gratuitous than to one who receives a salary.

###### Article 2184

Every mandatary is bound to render account of his management, and to account to the principal for everything he has received by virtue of his power of attorney, even in the case where what he has received is not due to the principal.

###### Article 2185

The mandatary is liable for the person he has substituted in the management:
1° when he has not received the power to substitute someone;  
2° when that power has been conferred on him without designation of a person, but the one he has chosen was notoriously incapable or insolvent.  
In all cases, the principal may act directly against the person whom the mandatary has substituted.

###### Article 2186

When there are several attorneys in fact or mandataries established by the same act, there is solidarity between them only insofar as it is expressed.

###### Article 2187

The mandatary owes interest on sums he has used for his own purposes from the date of that use; and on those of which he is debtor by reason of his mission, from the day he is placed in default.

###### Article 2188

The mandatary who has given to the party with whom he contracts in that capacity sufficient knowledge of his powers is bound by no warranty for what has been done beyond, unless he has personally submitted thereto.

#### Chapitre III : Des obligations du mandant Article 2189

The principal is bound to perform the engagements contracted by the mandatary, in accordance with the power given to him.  

He is bound by what may have been done beyond, only insofar as he has ratified it expressly or tacitly.

###### Article 2190

The principal must reimburse to the mandatary the advances and expenses which the latter has made for the performance of the mandate, and pay him his salary when it has been promised.  
If there is no fault attributable to the mandatary, the principal cannot dispense with making these reimbursements and payment, even in the case where the matter he hoped to conclude has not succeeded, nor have the amount of expenses and advances reduced on the pretext that they could have been less.

###### Article 2191

Unless otherwise agreed, the principal must also indemnify the mandatary for losses which the latter has suffered on the occasion of his management, without imprudence attributable to him.

###### Article 2192

Advances made by the agent bear interest against the principal, from the date of the recorded advances.  
Such interest is owed by the principal from the day the advances were made, and not from the day they were recorded by court decision or from the day of the demand for payment.

###### Article 2193

When the agent has been appointed by several persons for a common matter, each of them is jointly and severally liable to him for all the effects of the mandate.

#### Chapitre IV : Des différentes manières dont le mandat finit Article 2194

The mandate terminates in particular:
1° By revocation of the agent;  
2° By renunciation by the latter of the mandate;  
3° By death, guardianship of adults or bankruptcy, either of the principal or of the agent.

###### Article 2195

The principal may revoke his power of attorney whenever he sees fit and compel, if necessary, the agent to return to him the instrument containing the power of attorney. Such return must take place without delay, as soon as the agent is so required by the principal.  

The appointment of a new agent for the same matter constitutes revocation of the first, from the day it was notified to the latter.  

In all cases, from the time of revocation, the rendering of accounts becomes immediately due.

###### Article 2196

Revocation notified to the agent alone is presumed unknown to third parties who have dealt in ignorance of such revocation, except for the principal to prove that, taking into account the circumstances, the third party should have been aware of it.

###### Article 2197

The agent may renounce the mandate, by notifying the principal of his renunciation.  

Nevertheless, if such renunciation prejudices the principal, he must be compensated by the agent, unless the latter finds himself unable to continue the mandate without himself suffering considerable prejudice.

###### Article 2198

If the agent is unaware of the death of the principal or of one of the other causes which terminate the mandate, what he has done in such ignorance is valid.

###### Article 2199

In the above cases, the commitments of the agent are performed with respect to third parties who are in good faith.

###### Article 2200

In case of death of the agent, his heirs must give notice thereof to the principal, and provide, in the meantime, for what the circumstances require for the interest of the latter.

### Titre XVI : De certains patrimoines d'affectation

Chapitre Ier: De la fondation Article 2201
A foundation results from an act by which a person allocates, in an irrevocable manner, all or part of his property to a purpose of social utility having a lasting character.  

The foundation may not have as its essential object the realization of a profit or the operation of an enterprise.

###### Article 2202

The property of the foundation constitutes either an autonomous patrimony distinct from that of the disposer and of any other person, or the patrimony of a legal person.  
In the first case, the foundation is governed by the provisions of this title relating to the trust of social utility, subject to the provisions of the law; in the second case, it is governed by the laws applicable to legal persons of its kind.

###### Article 2203

The foundation created by trust is established by donation or by will, according to the rules governing such acts.

###### Article 2204

Unless otherwise stipulated in the constitutive act of the foundation, the property which forms the initial patrimony of the foundation created by trust, or the property which is subrogated or added thereto, must be preserved and allow the intended purpose to be achieved either by the distribution of the revenues alone which derive therefrom, or by a use which does not substantially modify the composition of the patrimony.

#### Chapitre II : De la fiducie

##### Section I : De la nature de la fiducie et de sa constitution

###### § 1. De la nature de la fiducie Article 2205

A trust results from an act by which one or more persons, called the settlor, transfer from their patrimony property, rights or security interests, or a set of property, rights or security interests, present or future, to one or more patrimonies which they constitute for a determined purpose for the benefit of one or more beneficiaries, and which a trustee undertakes, by the fact of his acceptance, to hold and administer.

###### Article 2206

The trust patrimony, formed of the property referred to in the preceding article and transferred in trust, constitutes an autonomous patrimony of allocation distinct from that of the settlor, the trustee or the beneficiary, over which none of them has a real right. In particular, the opening of a judicial reorganization or liquidation proceeding, personal bankruptcy and fraudulent bankruptcy, or an equivalent proceeding abroad concerning the trustee does not affect the trust patrimony.  
Without prejudice to the rights of creditors of the settlor holding a right of pursuit attached to a security interest published prior to the trust contract and except in cases of fraud against the rights of creditors of the settlor, the trust patrimony may be seized only by holders of claims arising from the preservation or management of such patrimony.  
In case of insufficiency of the trust patrimony, the obligation for trust liabilities is limited to the trust patrimony alone.

###### Article 2207

A trust is established by contract, for consideration or gratuitously, by will or by law. It may also, when the law so authorizes, be established by judgment.

###### Article 2208

A trust is constituted upon acceptance by the trustee or, if there are several, by one of them. The settlor may revoke the trust contract as long as it has not been accepted by the beneficiary; after acceptance by the beneficiary, the contract may be modified or revoked only with his consent or by court decision.  
When the trust is established by will, the effects of acceptance relate back to the day of death.

###### Article 2209

Acceptance of the trust divests the settlor of the property, charges the trustee with ensuring their allocation and the administration of the trust patrimony, and makes certain the right of the beneficiary.

###### § 2. Du contrat de fiducie

###### Article 2210

The trust contract determines, on pain of nullity:
1° The property, rights or security interests transferred. If they are future, they must be determinable;  
2° The duration of the transfer, which may not exceed ninety-nine years from the signing of the contract;  
3° The identity of the settlor or settlors; 4° The identity of the trustee or trustees;  
5° The identity of the beneficiary or beneficiaries or, failing that, the principles or rules allowing their designation; 6° The mission of the trustee or trustees and the extent of their powers of administration and disposition.  
The trust contract also defines the conditions under which the trustee accounts for his mission to the settlor. However, when during the performance of the contract the settlor becomes subject to a guardianship measure, the trustee, as soon as he is informed thereof, accounts for his mission to the guardian at the request of the latter at least once a year, without prejudice to the periodicity fixed by the contract. When during the performance of the contract the settlor becomes subject to a curatorship measure, the trustee accounts for his mission, under the same conditions, to the settlor and to his curator.

###### Article 2211

When the trust contract provides that the settlor retains the use or enjoyment of a business or professional real property transferred into the trust patrimony, the agreement concluded for this purpose is not subject to chapters 2 and 4 of title I of book II of the commercial code, unless otherwise stipulated.

###### Article 2212

The assignment of receivables carried out within the framework of a fiducie is enforceable against third parties as of the date of the fiducie contract or of the amendment recording it. It becomes enforceable against the debtor of the assigned receivable only through notification given to the debtor by the assignor or the fiduciary.

###### Article 2213

On pain of nullity, the fiducie contract and its amendments are registered in a public register, within one month from their date, with the register of immovable securities.  
Where they relate to immovable property or real property rights, they are also published in the Land Register. The fiduciary is, in case of default by the settlor, subject to the rules relating to the exercise of mortgage rights as set out in this code.  

The transfer of rights resulting from the fiducie contract and, if the beneficiary is not designated in the fiducie contract, his subsequent designation must, on pain of nullity, give rise to a written instrument registered under the same conditions.

###### Article 2214

A national register of fiducies is established and maintained by the Central Bank of Djibouti.

##### Section II : Des diverses espèces de fiducie Article 2215

Fiducies are established for personal purposes, or for purposes of private or social utility.  
They may, insofar as a mention indicates that it is a fiducie, be identified under the name of the settlor, the fiduciary or the beneficiary or, if they are established for purposes of private or social utility, under a name designating their object.

###### Article 2216

A personal fiducie is established gratuitously, with the aim of procuring an advantage for a specified person or one who may be specified.

###### Article 2217

A fiducie of private utility is one whose object is the construction, maintenance or preservation of corporeal property, or the use of property allocated to a specified use, either for the indirect advantage of a person or in his memory, or for another purpose of a private nature.

###### Article 2218

Also of private utility is a fiducie established for consideration with the aim, in particular, of enabling the realization of a profit by means of placements or investments, of providing for retirement or of procuring another advantage to the settlor or to the persons he designates, to members of a company or association, to employees or to security holders.

###### Article 2219

A fiducie established by contract for consideration may also have as its object to guarantee the performance of an obligation.

###### Article 2220

A fiducie of social utility is one that is established for a purpose of general interest, in particular of a cultural, educational, philanthropic, religious or scientific character.  
Its essential object is not to realize a profit or to operate an enterprise.

###### Article 2221

A personal fiducie established for the benefit of several persons successively may not comprise more than two orders of beneficiaries of the fruits and income, in addition to that of the beneficiary of the capital.  
Accretions operate between co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the same order.

###### Article 2222

The right of the beneficiary of the first order opens at the latest upon the expiration of ninety-nine years following the establishment of the fiducie, even if a longer term has been stipulated. That of the beneficiaries of subsequent orders may open subsequently, but only for the benefit of beneficiaries who have the required qualification to receive upon the expiration of ninety-nine years following the establishment of the fiducie.  
Legal persons may never be beneficiaries for a period exceeding ninety-nine years, even if a longer term has been stipulated.

###### Article 2223

A fiducie of private or social utility may be perpetual.

##### Section III : De l'administration de la fiducie

###### § 1. De la désignation et de la charge du fiduciaire Article 2224

Only banking or financial institutions, investment firms, and insurance companies may have the capacity of fiduciaries. Members of the legal profession may also have the capacity of fiduciary.  

The settlor or the beneficiary may be a fiduciary, but he must act jointly with a fiduciary who is neither settlor nor beneficiary.

###### Article 2225

The settlor may designate one or more fiduciaries or provide for the manner of their designation or replacement.  
In the absence of contractual stipulations providing for the conditions of his replacement or if it is impossible to provide for the replacement of a fiduciary, the court may, at the request of an interested person and after notice given to the persons it indicates, proceed with the replacement. It may also, when the conditions of administration so require, designate one or more other fiduciaries.  
Where the fiduciary fails in his duties or jeopardizes the interests entrusted to him, or if he is subject to safeguard or judicial reorganization proceedings, the settlor, the beneficiary or the third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 may apply to the court for the appointment of a provisional fiduciary or request the replacement of the fiduciary. The judicial decision granting the application entails by operation of law the divesting of the original fiduciary and the vesting of his replacement.

###### Article 2226

The fiduciary has complete and exclusive control and administration of the fiduciary patrimony and the titles relating to the property composing it are established in his name; he exercises all rights pertaining to the patrimony and may take any measure appropriate to ensure its allocation.  
When the fiduciary acts on behalf of the fiducie, he must expressly mention it.  

In his relations with third parties, the fiduciary is deemed to have the most extensive powers over the fiduciary patrimony, unless it is demonstrated that the third parties had knowledge of any limitations affecting his powers.

###### § 2. Du bénéficiaire et de ses droits Article 2227

The settlor or the fiduciary may be the beneficiary or one of the beneficiaries of the fiducie contract.

###### Article 2228

The beneficiary of a fiducie established gratuitously must have the qualifications required to receive by donation or by will at the opening of his right.  
The beneficiary of a fiducie must, in order to receive, fulfill the conditions required by the constitutive instrument.

###### Article 2229

The settlor may reserve the right to receive the fruits and income or, as the case may be, the capital of a fiducie, even established gratuitously, or to participate in the advantages it procures.

###### Article 2230

The settlor may reserve or confer upon the fiduciary or a third party the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share.  
In the case of a fiducie of social utility, the power of the fiduciary to elect the beneficiaries and to determine their share is presumed. In the case of a personal fiducie or one of private utility, the power to elect may be exercised by the fiduciary or the third party only if the category of persons from among whom they must choose the beneficiary is clearly determined in the constitutive instrument.  

The person who has the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share exercises it as he sees fit; he may modify or revoke his decision for the needs of the fiducie. The person who exercises the power may not do so for his own advantage.

###### Article 2231

During the term of the trust, the beneficiary has the right to require:
1° According to the periodicity fixed by the contract, an account by the trustee of his mission. The third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 has the same power.  
2° According to the constitutive instrument, either the provision of a benefit granted to him, or the payment of fruits and income and capital or only one of them.

###### Article 2232

The beneficiary of a trust constituted gratuitously is presumed to have accepted the right granted to him and he may dispose of it.  
He may also renounce it at any time. The renunciation must be made by notarial act if he is the beneficiary of a personal trust or a trust for private purposes.

###### Article 2233

In case of plurality of beneficiaries, when one of them renounces his right or when the latter becomes without effect, that right passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income or of the capital, according to whether he himself is a beneficiary of the fruits and income or of the capital.  
If he is the sole beneficiary of the fruits and income in his order, the right of the renouncing party passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the second order or, failing that, to the beneficiaries of the capital.

###### § 3. Measures of supervision and control Article 2234

Unless otherwise stipulated in the trust contract, the settlor may, at any time, designate a third party responsible for ensuring the preservation of his interests in the context of the performance of the contract and who may exercise the powers that the law grants to the settlor.  

When the settlor is a natural person, he may not waive this power.

###### Article 2235

The administration of the trust is subject to the supervision of the settlor or his heirs, if he is deceased, and of the beneficiary, even contingent. It is also subject to the supervision of the third party designated by the settlor pursuant to Article 2234.  
In addition, in the cases provided by law, the administration of trusts for private or social purposes is subject, according to their object and purpose, to the supervision of the persons and bodies designated by law.

###### Article 2236

Upon the constitution of the trust for private or social purposes subject to the supervision of a person or body designated by law, the trustee must file with the person or body a declaration indicating, in particular, the nature and object of the trust, its duration, as well as the name and address of the trustee.  
He must, at the request of the person or body, permit the examination of the trust files and provide any account, report or information requested of him.

###### Article 2237

The rights of the beneficiary of a personal trust are exercised, if he is not yet conceived, by the person who, having been designated by the settlor to act as curator, accepts that charge or, failing that, by the person appointed by the court at the request of the trustee or any interested person.  

In case of a trust for private purposes of which no person, even determinable or contingent, may be a beneficiary, the rights that this paragraph grants to the beneficiary may be exercised by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2238

The settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person may, notwithstanding any stipulation to the contrary, bring action against the trustee to compel him to perform his obligations or to do an act necessary for the trust, to enjoin him from any act detrimental to the trust or to obtain his removal.  
He may also challenge acts done by the trustee in fraud of the trust patrimony or of the rights of the beneficiary.

###### Article 2239

The court may authorize the settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person to bring legal action in place of the trustee, when the latter, without sufficient reason, refuses to act, neglects to do so or is prevented from doing so.

###### Article 2240

The trustee, the settlor and the beneficiary are, if they participate therein, solidarily liable for acts performed in fraud of the rights of the creditors of the settlor or of the trust patrimony.

##### Section IV: Modification and termination of the trust

###### § 1. Modification of the trust Article 2241

Any person may increase the trust patrimony by transferring property to it by contract or by
will and by following, for such increases, the rules specific to the constitution of a trust. He does not thereby acquire the rights of a settlor.  
The transferred property merges into the trust patrimony and is administered in accordance with the provisions of the constitutive instrument and those of this chapter.

###### Article 2242

When a trust has ceased to correspond to the original intention of the settlor, in particular when the court finds the occurrence of unforeseeable circumstances that make the pursuit of the purpose of the trust too onerous or the impossibility of achieving that purpose, that court may, at the request of an interested person, terminate the trust.  
If the trust still corresponds to the intention of the settlor, but new measures would better respect his intention or would facilitate the accomplishment of the trust, the court may modify the provisions of the constitutive instrument.  

In all the situations referred to in the preceding paragraphs, notice of the application must be given to the settlor and to the trustee and, as the case may be, to the beneficiary, to the liquidator of the succession of the settlor or to the heirs, and to any other person or body designated by law whenever the trust is subject to their supervision. These persons must be heard by the court if they so request.

###### § 2. Termination of the trust

###### Article 2243

The trust terminates by:
1° the lapse of the right of all beneficiaries, both of capital and of fruits and income;  
2° the renunciation by all of the beneficiaries of the trust, unless stipulations of the contract provide the conditions under which it continues;  
3° the arrival of the term or the occurrence of the condition if one is provided;  
4° the fact that the purpose of the trust has been achieved or by the impossibility found by the court of achieving it.

###### Article 2244

The trustee must, at the termination of the trust, deliver the property to those who are entitled to it.  

In the absence of a beneficiary, the property remaining at the termination of the trust devolves by operation of law to the settlor or his heirs.

###### Article 2245

The property of the trust for social purposes that terminates by reason of the impossibility of accomplishing it returns to the settlor. If he is deceased, that property devolves to a trust, to a legal person or to any other group of persons having a purpose as close as possible to that of the trust. The designation is made by the court, on the recommendation of the trustee. The court also takes the opinion of the person or body designated by law, if the trust was subject to their supervision.

### Title XVII: Transactions

###### Article 2246

A transaction is a contract by which the parties, by reciprocal concessions, terminate a dispute that has arisen, or prevent a dispute that may arise.  
This contract must be drawn up in writing.

###### Article 2247

To enter into a transaction, one must have the capacity to dispose of the objects included in the transaction.  

The tutor may enter into a transaction for the minor or the major under tutorship only in accordance with Article 604 of the title On Minority, Tutorship and Emancipation; and he may enter into a transaction with the minor who has become of age, on the tutorship account, only in accordance with Article 609 of the same title.  

Municipalities and public establishments may enter into transactions only with the express authorization of the President of the Republic.

###### Article 2248

One may settle the civil interest arising from an offence.  
The settlement does not prevent prosecution by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2249

A penalty clause may be added to a settlement against the party who fails to perform it.

###### Article 2250

Settlements are confined to their subject matter: the waiver made therein of all rights, actions and claims applies only to matters relating to the dispute which gave rise to it.

###### Article 2251

Settlements govern only the disputes comprised therein, whether the parties have manifested their intention by specific or general expressions, or whether that intention is recognised as a necessary consequence of what is expressed.

###### Article 2252

If a person who has settled a right which he held in his own capacity, and has thus abandoned it in part, subsequently acquires a similar right through another person, he is not, as regards the newly acquired right, bound by the prior settlement.

###### Article 2253

A settlement made by one of the interested parties does not bind the other interested parties and cannot be invoked by them.

###### Article 2254

A settlement prevents the commencement or continuation between the parties of legal proceedings having the same subject matter. The judge may raise of his own motion this bar to proceedings arising from the existence of a settlement.  
A settlement may not be challenged on grounds of error of law or on grounds of lesion.

###### Article 2255

Nevertheless, a settlement may be annulled where there is an error as to the person or as to the subject matter of the dispute.  
It may be annulled in all cases where there is fraud or duress.

###### Article 2256

An action for annulment also lies against a settlement where it has been made in performance of a void instrument, unless the parties, where they have the power to do so, have expressly confirmed the ground of nullity.

###### Article 2257

A settlement made on the basis of documents which have since been found to be false is entirely void.

###### Article 2258

A settlement concerning proceedings terminated by a judgment which has become res judicata, of which the parties or one of them had no knowledge, is void.  
If the judgment unknown to the parties was subject to appeal, the settlement is valid.

###### Article 2259

Where the parties have settled generally all matters which they might have between them, instruments which were then unknown to them and which were subsequently discovered do not constitute a ground for annulment, unless they were withheld by the act of one of the parties.  
But the settlement would be void if it related only to a subject matter in respect of which it was established, by newly discovered instruments, that one of the parties had no right whatsoever.

###### Article 2260

An error of calculation in a settlement must be rectified.

### Titre XVIII : Du compromis

###### Article 2261

Arbitration is governed by the provisions of articles L.710-1 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.

### Titre XIX : Les sûretés

###### Article 2262

Whoever has undertaken a personal obligation is bound to fulfil his undertaking upon all his movable and immovable property, present and future.

###### Article 2263

The debtor's property may be seized even where it is held by third parties. Seizure is effected according to the rules specific to the nature of each item.

###### Article 2264

Property referred to in articles L.511-4 to L.511-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure may not be seized.  

Furthermore, any individual entrepreneur who is a natural person may render unseizable the rights he holds over the immovable property forming his principal residence, in order to protect his family home from a failure of his business. Unseiability is effected by a declaration before a notary which, to be enforceable against third parties, must be published in a journal authorised to receive legal publications.

###### Article 2265

Seized property is unavailable.  

Leases granted by the person whose property is seized are, whatever their duration, unenforceable against pursuing creditors. The same rules apply to property seized, mortgaged or pledged on a conservatory basis.

###### Article 2266

The debtor's property is the common security of his creditors; and the proceeds are distributed among them proportionately, unless there are legitimate grounds of preference among the creditors.

###### Article 2267

As regards real security interests, the legitimate grounds of preference are privileges and mortgages.  
Sous-Titre I: Les sûretés personnelles Chapitre I: Du cautionnement

##### Section I : De la nature et de l'étendue du cautionnement

###### Article 2268

Civil suretyship is a contract by which the surety undertakes towards the creditor to perform the debtor's obligation if the debtor does not satisfy it himself.

###### Article 2269

Suretyship may exist only in respect of a valid obligation.  

However, it is possible to stand surety, with full knowledge of the facts, for an obligation even though it might be annulled by an exception purely personal to the obligor; for example, the undertakings of a person lacking capacity. The confirmation by the debtor of an obligation tainted by relative nullity does not, however, bind the surety, unless the surety expressly waives that nullity.  
The lack of authority of the representative to bind the legal person who is the principal debtor may be invoked by the surety of that legal person under the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 2270

The surety's undertaking may not be contracted on more onerous terms than the principal obligation, nor exceed what is owed by the debtor at the time of proceedings.  
The principal debtor may not aggravate the surety's undertaking by an agreement subsequent to the suretyship.  
Suretyship which exceeds the debt, or which is contracted on more onerous terms, is not void; it is reduced to the extent of the principal obligation.  
The surety's undertaking may be contracted for only part of the debt, and on less onerous terms.

###### Article 2271

Suretyship may be contracted without the debtor's instruction and even without his knowledge.  

One may also stand surety not only for the principal debtor, but also for the person who has stood surety for him.

###### Article 2272

Suretyship is not presumed, whatever the nature of the guaranteed obligation.  

It must be express, and it may not be extended beyond the limits within which it was contracted.  
Suretyship must be recorded in an instrument bearing the surety's signature and the mention of the maximum sum guaranteed in words and figures. In case of discrepancy, the suretyship is valid for the sum expressed in words.  

A surety who does not know how or is unable to write affixes his fingerprint in the presence of a witness who attests in the suretyship instrument his identity, his presence and that the nature and effects of the instrument have been explained to the surety.  

The provisions of this article also apply to suretyship required by law.

###### Article 2273

Suretyship for an obligation may extend, in addition to the principal and within the limit of the maximum sum guaranteed, to the accessories of the debt and to the costs of recovering the claim, including those subsequent to the notice given to the surety, provided that this undertaking results from a manuscript mention by the surety in accordance with the provisions of the preceding article.  
The instrument constituting the principal obligation must be annexed to the suretyship agreement.

###### Art.2274

General suretyship for the debts of the principal debtor, in the form of a suretyship for all commitments, for the debit balance of a current account, or in any other form, shall be understood, unless expressly provided otherwise, only as a guarantee of direct contractual debts.

It must be concluded, on pain of relative nullity, for a maximum amount freely determined between the parties, including the principal and all accessories.

General suretyship may be renewed when the maximum amount is reached. The renewal must be express; any clause to the contrary shall be deemed unwritten.

It may be revoked, at any time, by the surety before the maximum guaranteed amount has been reached. All commitments of the guaranteed debtor arising before the revocation remain guaranteed by the surety.  
Unless otherwise stipulated, general suretyship does not guarantee the debts of the principal debtor prior to the date of the suretyship.

###### Article 2275

The debts incumbent upon the deceased in the capacity of surety remain, like all other debts, the responsibility of his successors.  
However, only debts arising prior to the death of the surety are transmitted to his successors. On the other hand, debts arising before the death or universal transmission remain their responsibility, regardless of the time of their enforceability.

###### Article 2276

The debtor required to provide a surety must present one who has the capacity to contract, who has sufficient property to answer for the object of the obligation, and whose domicile is within the jurisdiction where it must be given, unless dispensed by the creditor or the competent court.  
The debtor who cannot find a surety may replace it with any real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.

###### Article 2277

The solvency of a civil surety is estimated only with regard to his landed properties, except in commercial matters, or when the debt is modest.  
No regard is had to litigious immovables, or those whose discussion would become too difficult due to the remoteness of their location.

###### Article 2278

When the surety received by the creditor, voluntarily or in court, subsequently becomes insolvent, the debtor must provide another or provide a real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.  
This rule is excepted only in the case where the surety was given by virtue of an agreement by which the creditor required a particular person as surety.

##### Section II : De l'effet du cautionnement

###### § 1

De l'effet du cautionnement entre le créancier et la caution Article 2279
The creditor must notify the surety of any default by the debtor, forfeiture or extension of the term, indicating the amount remaining owed by him in principal, interest and costs at the date of the default, forfeiture or extension of the term.

In case of extension of the term granted to the principal debtor, the surety is entitled to refuse the benefit of this extension and to pursue the debtor to compel payment or obtain a guarantee or a conservatory measure.

In case of forfeiture of the term affecting the principal debtor, this does not automatically extend to the surety who may only be required to pay at the maturity date fixed at the time when the surety was provided. Any clause to the contrary is unwritten. However, the surety incurs forfeiture of the term if, after formal notice, it does not satisfy its own obligations at the fixed maturity date.

###### Article 2280

Civil suretyship is simple, unless otherwise provided by law or conventional stipulation of solidarity.

The joint and several surety is bound to perform the principal obligation under the same conditions as a joint and several debtor subject to the special provisions of this code.  
Unless otherwise provided by law or stipulation, the simple surety, unlike the judicial surety and the joint and several surety, has the benefit of discussion and division.  
However, the creditor may only pursue the surety, whether simple, joint and several or judicial, by joining the principal debtor as a party.

###### Article 2281

The creditor may not bring legal action against the surety except after a formal notice to pay addressed to the debtor and remaining without effect.  
The surety is only bound to pay the creditor if the principal debtor does not perform his obligation. It is bound in the same manner as the principal debtor.

###### Article 2282

Any surety may raise against the creditor all exceptions belonging to the principal debtor, which are inherent to the debt and tend to reduce, extinguish or defer the debt, subject to contrary legislative provisions. But the surety may not raise against the creditor exceptions that are purely personal to the debtor.  
The simple or joint and several surety is discharged when subrogation to the rights and guarantees of the creditor can no longer operate in its favor, by act of the creditor. Any clause to the contrary shall be deemed unwritten.

If the act imputed to the creditor only limits this subrogation, the surety is discharged to the extent of the insufficiency of the preserved guarantee.

###### Article 2283

The surety who, upon first proceedings brought against it, requests the benefit of discussion must indicate to the creditor the property of the principal debtor capable of being immediately seized on the national territory and, if the creditor so requests, advance sufficient sums to conduct the discussion.

###### Article 2284

Whenever the surety has made the indication of property authorized by the preceding article, and has provided sufficient sums for the discussion, the creditor is, up to the value of the property indicated, liable to the surety for the insolvency of the principal debtor arising from failure to pursue.

###### Article 2285

If there are several sureties for the same debtor and the same debt, unless there is a stipulation of solidarity between them or renunciation by them of this benefit, each of them may, upon first proceedings by the

creditor, request the division of the debt among the solvent sureties on the day the exception is invoked.

The surety is not liable for the insolvencies of other sureties arising after the division.  
The creditor who voluntarily divides his action when he could have avoided it, may not reverse this division and bears the insolvency of the sureties pursued without being able to transfer it to the other sureties.

###### § 2. De l'effet du cautionnement entre le débiteur et la caution Article 2286

As soon as it is pursued, the surety must notify the principal debtor or join him as a party before paying the debt to the pursuing creditor.  
If the surety has paid without having notified or joined the principal debtor as a party, it loses its recourse against him if, at the time of payment by it or subsequent to that payment, the debtor had the means to have the debt declared extinguished or if he had paid in ignorance of the surety's payment. Nevertheless, the surety retains its action for restitution against the pursuing creditor.

###### Article 2287

The surety who has paid has recourse against the principal debtor, even if the suretyship was given without the debtor's knowledge.  
This recourse applies both to the principal and to interest and costs; nevertheless the surety has recourse only for costs incurred by it since it notified the principal debtor of the proceedings brought against it.  
It also has recourse for damages and interest, if applicable in case of prejudice it may have suffered from the creditor's proceedings.

###### Article 2288
