The surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all the rights and guarantees of the pursuing creditor against the debtor.  
If there are several principal debtors jointly and severally liable for the same debt, the surety is subrogated against each of them for all that it has paid, even if it has only stood surety for one. If the debtors are joint, it must divide its recourse.

###### Article 2289

The surety, even before having paid, may act against the debtor to be indemnified by him, or request the preservation of its rights in the debtor's patrimony:
1° As soon as it is sued in court for payment; 2° When the debtor has ceased payments;  
3° When the debtor has not discharged it within the agreed period;  
4° When the debt has become due by the expiry of the term under which it was contracted.

###### § 3. De l'effet du cautionnement entre les diverses cautions Article 2290

When several persons have stood surety for the same debtor for the same debt, the surety who has discharged the debt has recourse against the other sureties, each for its share and portion;  

But this recourse only applies when the surety has paid in one of the cases set out in the preceding article.

##### Section III : De l'extinction du cautionnement Article 2291

The obligation resulting from suretyship is extinguished by the same causes as under the general law of contracts.  
Payment in kind definitively releases the surety, even if the creditor is subsequently evicted from the thing accepted by him. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.  
Novation of the principal obligation by change of object or cause releases the surety unless it agrees to transfer its guarantee to the new debt. Any clause to the contrary stipulated before the novation is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2292

The surety's undertaking is extinguished independently of the principal obligation:	when in proceedings brought against it, the surety pleads set-off for a personal claim against the pursuing creditor;	when the creditor has granted a release of debt to the surety alone;	when confusion occurs between the person of the creditor and the surety;	when the creditor has voluntarily accepted immovable property or any effect in payment of the principal debt, even if the creditor is subsequently evicted therefrom;	for debts arising after the death of the surety;	in the case of article 2282.

###### Article 2293

The simple extension of time granted by the creditor to the principal debtor, or the modification of the security interests accompanying the principal obligation into new equivalent security interests, does not discharge the surety, who may, in this case, pursue the debtor to compel payment.

#### Chapitre II : De la lettre de garantie ou « garantie autonome » Article 2294

A letter of guarantee or independent guarantee is the necessarily written undertaking by which the guarantor binds itself, in consideration of an obligation subscribed by a third party principal, to pay a sum either on first demand or according to agreed terms.  
Such a contract may not be entered into, on pain of nullity, by natural persons; and may not, for legal persons, be stipulated for a purpose unrelated to the commercial or professional activity of the borrower. In this case, the letter of guarantee is governed by articles L.2281-201 et seq. of the commercial code.

#### Chapitre III : De la lettre d'intention

###### Article 2295

The letter of intent is an undertaking to do or not to do having as its object the support provided to a debtor in the performance of its obligation towards its creditor.  

Sous-Titre II: Les sûretés réelles Chapitre I: Dispositions générales

###### Article 2296

Any real security interest may be created, registered, managed and enforced on behalf of the creditors of the guaranteed obligation by a person they designate for this purpose in the instrument recording that obligation.

###### Article 2297

Privilege is a right that the quality of the claim gives to a creditor to be preferred over other creditors, even mortgage creditors. It may be over movables or over immovables.  
As between privileged creditors, preference is determined by the different qualities of the privileges. When they are of the same rank, privileged creditors are paid proportionately.

###### Article 2298

Privilege by reason of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised are governed by the laws concerning them.  
The Public Treasury may not, however, obtain privilege to the prejudice of rights previously acquired by third parties.

###### Article 2299

Privileges, like security interests, may be over movables or over immovables.

#### Chapitre II : Des sûretés sur les meubles Article 2300

Real security interests over movables comprise: the right of retention, pledge, privileges and ownership retained or transferred by way of security.

##### Section I : Du droit de rétention Article 2301

The creditor who lawfully holds property of the debtor may retain it until complete payment of what is owed to him, independently of any other security interest.  
When the same property is the subject of several successive pledges without dispossession, the rank of creditors is determined by the order of their registration. When property given in pledge without dispossession is subsequently the subject of a pledge with dispossession, the preference right of the prior pledgee is enforceable against the subsequent pledgee when it is duly published notwithstanding the latter's right of retention.

###### Article 2302

The right of retention may only be exercised:	before any seizure;	if the claim is certain, liquidated and due;	if there is a connection between the arising of the claim and the thing retained.

##### Section II : Du nantissement Article 2303

Pledge is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing to its creditor as security for the debt.  

Pledges without dispossession relating to: rights of partners and securities; business goodwill; professional equipment; stocks of raw materials and goods, are governed by the provisions of the commercial code.  
The pledge of a movable thing is called gage. That of an immovable thing is called gage immobilier.

###### Article 2304

Heavy equipment purchased by a private individual may be the subject of a pledge for the benefit of the seller, the third party having guaranteed the purchaser's undertakings towards the seller, or any person having lent the sums necessary for the purchase.  
Such a security interest is only enforceable against third parties if it is registered in the Movable Security Interests register.

###### Article 2305

Gage is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing or set of things of a movable nature to its creditor as security for the debt.  
The guaranteed claims may be present, future or contingent; in the latter two cases, they must be determinable and not be tainted with nullity.  

Gage confers on the creditor the right to be paid from the thing that is its object, by privilege and preference over other creditors.

###### Article 2306

Gage may be granted by the debtor or by a third party; in the latter case, the creditor has recourse only against the property assigned as security.  
Except for gage granted by a third party, gage of another's thing is null and may give rise to damages when the creditor was unaware that the thing belonged to another. If the thing does not belong to the grantor, the pledgee in good faith may oppose the owner's claim for recovery under the conditions provided for the possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2307

Any movable property, corporeal or incorporeal, may be given as a pledge.

Security interests in movable property subject to publicity are registered, at the initiative of the creditor, in the Register of Security Interests in Movable Property.

###### Article 2308

The parties may agree to the substitution during the performance of the contract of the pledged thing by another thing.  
The pledge may also relate to sums or securities deposited as security by civil servants, ministerial officers or any other person to guarantee abuses for which they could be held responsible and loans granted for the constitution of this security.

###### Article 2309

The pledge contract provided with dispossession only takes effect if the pledged thing is actually delivered to the creditor or to a third party agreed upon between the parties.  

The promise of pledge, in particular of future things, obliges the promisor to deliver the thing under the agreed conditions.

###### Article 2310

When it is without dispossession of the debtor, the pledge is enforceable against third parties by the publicity given to it. This is carried out at the initiative of the creditor in the Register of Security Interests in Movable Property.

###### Article 2311

The pledge contract is only enforceable against third parties if it is evidenced by a writing, authentic or under private signature, duly registered, and containing an indication of the sum due as well as the kind, nature and quantity of the movable property given as a pledge, unless otherwise provided by law.  
The drafting of the deed in writing and its registration are nevertheless only required for matters exceeding the value of 100,000 FD.  
The pledge is also enforceable against third parties by the dispossession into the hands of the creditor or of an agreed third party of the property which is the object thereof.  
If the pledge is constituted over incorporeal movable property, such as a movable debt, the deed, once registered, is notified to the debtor of the debt given as a pledge.

###### Article 2312

The debtor who pledges his debt against a named third party must deliver to the pledgee creditor his debt instrument and notify his own debtor of the transfer of his debt in this capacity; failing this, the pledgee creditor may proceed with this notification.  
This pledge is realized by the demand for payment that the pledgee creditor addresses to the transferred debtor. The latter may raise against the pledgee creditor the defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor as well as the defenses which he may assert against the pledgee creditor. It is otherwise if the transferred debtor has made a written commitment to pay the pledgee creditor directly, in which case he may not raise against the pledgee creditor the defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor.  

The creditor of the transferred debtor remains liable, jointly and severally with the latter, for payment of the pledged debt.  
The pledgee creditor who has obtained payment must account for it to his own debtor.

###### Article 2313

In other areas, if there are no specific legal provisions or contractual stipulations defining the methods of pledging the incorporeal property given as security, the delivery to the creditor of the instrument evidencing the existence of the right operates dispossession of the grantor.

###### Article 2314

The deposit or consignment of sums, instruments or securities, judicially ordered as security or as a conservatory measure, entails special allocation and privilege under Article 2305 paragraph 3.

###### Article 2315

The pledgee creditor retains or causes the agreed third party to retain the pledged thing until full payment, in principal, interest and costs, of the debt for which the pledge was constituted.  
If there arises on the part of the same debtor towards the same creditor, one or more other debts contracted subsequent to the pledging, and becoming due before payment of the first debt, the creditor may retain or cause the pledged thing to be retained until complete payment of all the debts, even in the absence of any stipulation to that effect.

###### Article 2316

The privilege subsists over the pledge only insofar as this pledge has been placed and has remained in the possession of the creditor, or of a third party agreed upon between the parties.  
But if he has been dispossessed against his will, the creditor may claim the pledged thing as a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2317

Until the expropriation of the debtor, if applicable, the grantor remains owner of the pledge, which is, in the hand of the creditor, only a deposit ensuring the latter's privilege.

###### Article 2318

The creditor or the agreed third party must watch over the thing and ensure its preservation, as must a remunerated depositary. He is liable for the loss or deterioration of the pledge which would have occurred through his negligence.  
He may not, unless otherwise stipulated, use the pledged thing or collect the fruits thereof. If he is authorized to collect the fruits, he must impute them, unless otherwise agreed, to what is owed to him in interest and capital. When the pledged thing is a debt, the provisions of Article 2320 apply.  

If the thing threatens to perish, the creditor or the agreed third party may, upon authorization, as the case may be, from the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance, sell it and the effects of the pledge are then transferred to the price.  
The agreed third party and, if applicable, the purchaser in bad faith of the pledged thing are jointly and severally liable with the pledgee creditor for the non-performance of these obligations.  
The pledging of a consumable thing authorizes the creditor or the agreed third party to return an equivalent thing.  

When the pledge has as its object fungible things, the creditor or the agreed third party may only alienate them if the agreement so provides, subject to replacing them with the same quantity of equivalent things. In the absence of a stipulation to that effect, he must keep them separate from things of the same nature belonging to him. If the creditor or the agreed third party fails to do so, the grantor may claim the restitution of the pledged property, without prejudice to damages, if the creditor or the agreed third party does not satisfy his obligation to preserve the pledge. When the agreement exempts the creditor from the obligation to separate the pledged property from his things of the same nature, he acquires ownership thereof subject to returning the same quantity of equivalent things.

###### Article 2319

For his part, when he has fully paid him the capital, interest and costs, the debtor must account to the creditor for the useful and necessary expenses that the latter has incurred for the preservation of the pledge.

###### Article 2320

When the thing given as a pledge is a debt: if the maturity of the debt given as a pledge is prior to the maturity of the secured debt, the pledgee creditor is entitled to collect the amount thereof in capital and interest, unless otherwise agreed; if the maturity of the secured debt is prior to the maturity of the debt given as a pledge, the pledgee creditor is required to wait for the maturity of the latter to collect the amount thereof.  
In both cases, the pledgee creditor collects the amount of the pledged debt subject to accounting, in the capacity of agent, for the surplus collected in favor of the grantor of the pledge.  
In addition, unless otherwise agreed, if this debt bears interest, the creditor imputes this interest to that which may be owed to him in interest and capital.  
If the debt for the security of which the debt was given as a pledge does not itself bear interest, the imputation is made to the capital of the debt.

###### Article 2321

In the absence of payment at maturity, the pledgee creditor may, eight days after simple service on the debtor and on the third party holding the pledged thing, if there is one, proceed with the public sale of the pledged thing.  
The sale is conducted by a bailiff at least eight days after publication of a notice in a newspaper authorised to receive legal announcements mentioning the date, time and place of the sale, the place where the objects may be viewed, the reserve price or prices, the description of the object and the costs.  

The creditor may also seize, as the case may be, the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance to request that the pledge be attributed to him or sold to a third party up to the amount of his claim and according to an estimate based on market prices or expert opinion.  
Any clause that would authorise the creditor to appropriate the pledge or dispose of it without the above formalities is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2322

In case of sale or loss or destruction of the pledged thing, the pledgee creditor has priority over the price of the thing sold or over the insurance indemnity for the amount of the guaranteed claim in principal, interest and costs.  
He exercises his right of preference in accordance with Article 2331 of this code. If there are several pledgee creditors, they are ranked in the order of registration of successive pledges or, in the absence of registration, in the order of creation.

###### Article 2323

The pledge is indivisible notwithstanding the divisibility of the debt towards the heirs of the debtor or those of the creditor.  
The heir of the debtor who has paid his portion of the debt may not request the return of his portion in the pledge, even if it is divisible by nature, as long as the debt is not entirely discharged.  

Reciprocally, the heir of the creditor who has received his share of the claim may not release the pledge, even if it is divisible, to the prejudice of those of his co-heirs who are not paid.

###### Article 2324

The commercial pledge is governed by the provisions of the commercial code.

###### Article 2325

The pledge over a registered motor land vehicle or trailer is governed by this article and Articles 2326 to 2329 below.  
This pledge is enforceable against third parties by the declaration made to the Mining Service. This declaration is entered in a special counterfoil register and mentions the creation of the pledge over the vehicle or trailer, the name of the owner of the property and that of the creditor, and the date of registration of the contract.  

A receipt for this declaration is issued to the pledgee creditor, repeating verbatim the entries appearing on the counterfoil. By possession of this receipt, the pledgee creditor is deemed to have retained the vehicle or trailer in his possession.

###### Article 2326

In case of a pledge over a new vehicle or trailer, the registration of the pledge by the seller, assignee of the claim, discounter or lender of money for the purchase made, must be done within three months from the issue of the receipt for the declaration of putting the vehicle into circulation.

###### Article 2327

The cancellation of the pledge entry may be requested either by the creditor or by the debtor.  

When it is done by the creditor, indication of the cancellation is entered on the receipt issued to him. In this case, the debtor may request to obtain a certificate of cancellation.  
When it is done by the debtor, the latter must justify the extinction of the guaranteed debt or produce the deed giving release of the registration. A certificate of cancellation is then issued to him.

###### Article 2328

In the absence of payment of the guaranteed debt, the creditor may have the sale of the pledged property ordered by the court. This sale takes place according to the procedures provided for enforcement methods without the pledge agreement being able to derogate therefrom.  
The creditor may also have it ordered by the court that the property shall remain with him in payment. When the value of the property exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

###### Article 2329

It may be agreed, at the time of creation of the pledge or subsequently, that in the absence of performance of the guaranteed obligation the creditor shall become owner of the pledged property.  
The value of the property is determined on the day of transfer by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.  
When this value exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

##### Section III: Privileges over movables

###### Article 2330

Privileges are either general, or special over certain movables.

###### § 1. General privileges over movables Article 2331

Claims with privilege over all movables are those expressed below, and are exercised in the following order, without formality of publicity:
1° Court costs; 2° Funeral expenses;  
3° Any costs of the last illness preceding the seizure of property, whatever its outcome, concurrently among those to whom they are owed;  
4° Without prejudice to the possible application of the provisions of Articles 152 to 155 of the labour code, the privileges of wages, which cover:	sums owed to workers and apprentices for performance and termination of their contract during the last six months preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;	indemnities owed for paid leave;	redundancy indemnities owed;  

5° Supplies of subsistence provided to the debtor and his family during the last year

6° Sums owed to authors of intellectual, literary and artistic works for the last three years preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;  

7° Up to a limit of one million Djibouti Francs, sums for which the debtor is liable in respect of tax and customs claims and towards the National Social Security Fund.

###### Article 2332

It is recalled that, in accordance with Article 2298, the privilege by reason of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised are governed by the laws concerning them. The same applies to claims for contributions to the National Social Security Fund.  
Special texts creating general privileges must specify their rank by determining it in relation to the provisions of this article. Failing this, the rank of these privileges is the last of that established by this article.

###### § 2. Privileges over certain movables Article 2333

Creditors holding special privileges have, over the movables assigned to them as a basis by law, a right of preference.  

This right of preference is also exercised, by subrogation, over the insurance indemnity for the movable that has perished or disappeared, as long as it is not paid.

###### Article 2334

Privileged claims on certain movables are, without prejudice to special provisions establishing others, those:
1° Of the lessor of immovable property, who has a privilege on the fruits and revenues of the year, and on the price of everything that furnishes the leased property.  
This privilege guarantees, in addition to the damages that may be awarded to him, the claims of the lessor against the lessee for the twelve months elapsed preceding the seizure and for the twelve months to fall due after it.  
The lessee or any person who, by fraudulent maneuvers, deprives the lessor of his privilege totally or partially, commits a criminal offense punished by the penalties for breach of trust.  
The owner may seize the movables that furnish his house or his farm, when they have been moved without his consent, and he retains his privilege over them, provided that he has made the claim in the act of seizure; however, the lessor who thus claims the movables moved without his consent must reimburse the purchaser the price they cost him.  
2° Of the pledgee, on the pledge that he realizes;  

3° Of the person who has incurred expenses or provided services for the preservation of the thing;  

4° Of the seller, who has, on the movable sold, a privilege to guarantee payment of the unpaid price, if it is still in the possession of the debtor or on the price still owed by the sub-purchaser.  
5° The hotelier for his supplies, on the effects of the traveler that have been transported to his hotel; 6° The carrier, for the costs of carriage and accessory expenses, on the thing transported;  
7° The holders of claims resulting from abuses and malfeasance committed by public officials in the exercise of their functions, on the funds of their security deposit and on the interest that may be owed thereon;  
8° The holders of claims arising from an accident for the benefit of third parties injured by that accident or their successors in title, on the indemnity of which the civil liability insurer acknowledges itself or has been judicially recognized as debtor by reason of the insurance agreement.  

No payment made to the insured shall be liberating as long as the privileged creditors have not been satisfied.

##### Section V: Property Retained or Transferred as Security

###### § 1. Property Retained as Security Article 2335

The ownership of property may be retained as security by the effect of a retention of title clause. The effect of a retention of title clause is to suspend the transfer effect of a contract until the complete payment of the obligation that constitutes its consideration.  

The property thus reserved is the accessory of the claim whose payment it guarantees.

###### Article 2336

The retention of title must be agreed in writing.

###### Article 2337

The reserved ownership of a fungible property may be exercised, up to the amount of the claim remaining due, on property of the same nature and same quality held by the debtor or on his behalf.

###### Article 2338

The incorporation of a movable subject to a retention of title into another property does not prevent the rights of the creditor when these properties can be separated without suffering damage.

###### Article 2339

In the absence of complete payment at maturity, the creditor may request the restitution of the property in order to recover the right to dispose of it.  
The value of the property repossessed is imputed, as payment, on the balance of the guaranteed claim.  

When the value of the property repossessed exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt still due, the creditor owes the debtor a sum equal to the difference.

###### Article 2340

The right of ownership transfers to the claim of the debtor against the sub-purchaser or to the insurance indemnity subrogated to the property.

###### § 2. Property Transferred as Security Article 2341

The ownership of movable property or of a right may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiduciary contract concluded in application of articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2342

In case of fiducie concluded as security, the contract mentions on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in article 2210, the guaranteed debt and the estimated value of the property or right transferred into the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 2343

In the absence of payment of the guaranteed debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiduciary contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires the free disposal of the property or right transferred as security.  
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the fiduciary contract so provides, the sale of the property or right transferred and the delivery of all or part of the price.  

The value of the property or right transferred is determined by an expert designated amicably or judicially, unless the property is a sum of money. Any contrary clause is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2344

If the beneficiary of the fiducie has acquired the free disposal of the property or right transferred in application of article 2343, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to the prior payment of debts arising from the preservation or management of the fiduciary patrimony.  
Under the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the property or right transferred in application of the fiduciary contract, he restores to the settlor the part of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, as the case may be, the value of the guaranteed debt.

###### Article 2345

The property transferred in application of article 2341 may be subsequently allocated to the guarantee of debts other than those mentioned by the constitutive act provided that it expressly so provides.  
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary patrimony may then be allocated as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.  

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of article 2342 is registered in the form provided for in article 2213. The date of registration determines, among them, the rank of the creditors.  

The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary to them is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapter III: Securities on Immovable Property Article 2346

Securities on immovable property are: privileges, immovable pledge (or antichresis), and mortgages.  
The ownership of the immovable property may also be retained or transferred as security.

##### Section I: Immovable Pledge or "Antichresis" Article 2347

The immovable pledge, or antichresis, is the allocation, by the debtor or by a third party for the debtor, of an immovable property as security for an obligation; it entails dispossession of the person who constitutes it.  
The immovable pledge is established only in writing.  

The creditor acquires by this contract only the faculty to collect the fruits of the immovable property, with the obligation to impute them annually on the interest, if any is owed to him, and then on the principal of his claim. He may for this purpose, without losing possession of the property, lease the immovable property, either to a third party or to the debtor himself.

###### Article 2348

The creditor is required, unless otherwise agreed, to pay the contributions and annual charges on the immovable property that he holds as immovable pledge.  
He must also, under penalty of damages, provide for the maintenance and useful and necessary repairs of the immovable property, and may deduct for this purpose, from the fruits, all expenses relating to these various matters. He may, at any time, free himself from this obligation by returning the property to its owner.

###### Article 2349

The debtor may not claim enjoyment of the immovable property that he has given as immovable pledge before the full discharge of his debt.

###### Article 2350

The creditor does not become owner of the immovable property by mere default of payment at the agreed term; any clause to the contrary is null and void.  

The creditor, in case of default of payment at the agreed term, may on the other hand pursue the expropriation of his debtor by legal means.

###### Article 2351

The provisions of Article 2323 apply to immovable pledge.

###### Article 2352

Nothing provided in this chapter shall prejudice the rights that third parties might have over the land of the immovable property given as immovable pledge. Indeed, the immovable pledge being only a delegation of fruits as and when they fall due or are collected, third parties may acquire and exercise their rights over the pledged immovable property.  
If the creditor, holding such title, has privileges or mortgages legally established and preserved over the land, he exercises them in his rank and like any other creditor.

###### Article 2353

The rights of the creditor holding a right of immovable pledge are extinguished in particular: 1° By the extinction of the principal obligation;  
2° By the early return of the immovable property to its owner.

##### Section II: Immovable privileges

###### § 1. Special privileges over immovable property Article 2354

Privileged creditors over immovable property are:

1° The seller, over the immovable property sold, for payment of the price;  

If there are several successive sales of which the price is owed in whole or in part, the first seller is preferred to the second, the second to the third, and so on;  
2° Those who have provided funds for the acquisition of an immovable property, provided that it is authentically established, by the loan agreement, that the sum was intended for this use and, by the seller's receipt, that this payment was made from the borrowed funds;  

3° Co-heirs, over the immovable property of the succession, for the guarantee of partitions made between them, and of balancing payments or returns of lots;  

4° Architects, contractors and artisans who have built, reconstructed or repaired buildings, canals or any other works whatsoever, provided however that, by an expert appointed ex officio by the court of first instance within whose jurisdiction the buildings are located, a report has been drawn up beforehand, for the purpose of establishing the state of the premises in relation to the works that the owner will declare his intention to have done, and that the works have been, within six months at most of their completion, received by an expert also appointed ex officio. But the amount of the privilege cannot exceed the values established by the second report, and it is reduced to the added value existing at the time of alienation of the immovable property and resulting from the works that have been done there;  

5° Those who have lent the funds to pay or reimburse the workers, enjoy the same privilege, provided that this use is authentically established by the loan agreement, and by the workers' receipt, as stated above for those who have lent the funds for the acquisition of an immovable property;  

6° The creditors of the deceased and the legatees of sums of money over the immovable property of the succession, as well as the personal creditors of the heir over the immovable property of the latter, for the guarantee of the rights they hold from Article 1028.

###### Article 2355

The privileges enumerated in Articles 2331 and 2354 of the Civil Code, with the exception however of the privilege for costs of justice, incurred for the realization of the immovable property and the distribution of the price, only grant a right of preference to the beneficiaries called to exercise them over the immovable mass over unsecured creditors.

###### § 2. General privileges over immovable property Article 2356

The privileges that extend over movable property and immovable property are those set out in Article 2331.

###### Article 2357

When, for lack of movable property, the privileged creditors set out in the preceding article present themselves to be paid from the price of an immovable property in competition with other privileged creditors over the immovable property, payments are made in the following order:
1° Costs of justice and others set out in Article 2331; 2° Claims designated in Article 2354.

###### § 3. How immovable privileges are preserved Article 2358

Between creditors, privileges only produce effect with regard to immovable property insofar as they are made public by registration in the registers of the mortgage registrar, in the manner determined by law, and from the date of this registration, subject only to the following exceptions.

###### Article 2359

The claims enumerated in Article 2331 are excepted from the formality of registration.

###### Article 2360

If their privilege is established by a notarial deed to be published in the land register:
1° The privileged seller preserves his privilege by the transcription of the title that transferred ownership to the purchaser, and which establishes that all or part of the price is owed to him; for which purpose, the transcription of the contract made by the purchaser shall be valid as registration for the seller and for the lender who has provided him with the sums paid, and who will be subrogated to the rights of the seller by the same contract. In this case, the mortgage registrar shall nevertheless be required, under penalty of all damages towards third parties, to make ex officio the registration in his register, of the claims resulting from the deed transferring ownership, both in favor of the seller and in favor of the lenders, who may also have made, if it has not been done, the transcription of the sale contract, for the purpose of acquiring the registration of what is owed to them on the price.  

2° The co-heir or co-partitioner preserves his privilege over the property of each lot or over the property sold by licitation for the balancing payments and returns of lots or for the price of the licitation, by registration made at his initiative, within sixty days, from the date of the partition deed or the adjudication by licitation; during which time no mortgage may take place over the property charged with balancing payment or adjudicated by licitation, to the prejudice of the creditor of the balancing payment or the price.

###### Article 2361

Architects, contractors, masons and other workers employed to build, reconstruct or repair buildings, canals, or other works, and those who have, to pay and reimburse them, lent the sums whose use has been established, preserve by the double registration made:

1° Of the report establishing the state of the premises;  

2° Of the report of receipt, their privilege at the date of registration of the first report.

###### Article 2362

Creditors and legatees who request the separation of the patrimony of the deceased, in accordance with Article 665 under the title Of Successions, preserve, with regard to the creditors of the heirs or representatives of the deceased, their privilege over the immovable property of the succession, by registrations made on each of these properties, within six months from the opening of the succession.  
Before the expiration of this period, no mortgage may be established with effect on these properties by the heirs or representatives to the prejudice of these creditors or legatees.

###### Article 2363

The assignees of these various privileged claims exercise all the same rights as the assignors in their place and stead.

###### Article 2364

All privileged claims subject to the formality of registration, with respect to which the conditions prescribed above for preserving the privilege have not been fulfilled, do not cease to be hypothecary, but the hypothec dates, with respect to third parties, only from the time of the registrations which must be made as will be explained hereinafter.

##### Section III : Les hypothèques Article 2365

The provisions of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership are applicable, in a general manner and subject to the provisions that follow, to registered immovables and to the real rights relating thereto.

###### Article 2366

A hypothec is a real right over immovables assigned to the discharge of an obligation.  

It is, by its nature, indivisible, and subsists in its entirety over all the immovables assigned, over each and over each portion of these immovables.  

It follows them into whatever hands they pass.

###### Article 2367

A hypothec takes place only in the cases and according to the forms authorized by law.

###### Article 2368

Only the following are susceptible of hypothecs:
1° Lands whether built upon or not which are in commerce and with them, their accessories deemed immovable;  
2° The usufruct of the same property, during the time of its duration;  
3° The rights of emphyteusis, during the time of its duration, and of superficies, established over the same property. Movables have no right of suite by hypothec.  

Ships and seagoing vessels are governed by the provisions specific to them.

###### Article 2369

A hypothec is either legal, or judicial, or conventional. A legal hypothec is one which results from the law.  
A judicial hypothec is one which results from judgments or judicial acts. A hypothec may likewise result from judgments rendered in foreign countries, if they have been declared enforceable by a Djiboutian court, subject to special laws or treaties. Similarly, arbitral awards give rise to a hypothec only insofar as they are vested with the exequatur.  
A conventional hypothec is one which results from contracts and other juridical acts. It is granted by notarial act; the transfer and release of the hypothec take place in the same forms.

###### Article 2370

A conventional hypothec may be granted only by those who have the capacity to alienate the immovables which they subject thereto. The property of minors, of adults under tutorship, and that of absentees as long as possession thereof is granted only provisionally, may be hypothecated only for the causes and in the forms established by law, or by virtue of judgments; those who have over the immovable only a right suspended by a condition, or resolvable in certain cases, or subject to rescission, may grant only a hypothec subject to the same conditions or to the same rescission.  
The authentic instrument specifically declares the nature and location of each of the immovables presently belonging to the debtor, over which he grants the hypothec of the claim.

###### Article 2371

Future property cannot be hypothecated.  

Nevertheless, if the present and unencumbered property of the debtor is insufficient for the security of the claim, he may, by acknowledging this insufficiency, consent that each of the properties which he shall acquire thereafter be specially assigned thereto as acquisitions are made.

###### Article 2372

If the immovable or immovables presently subject to the hypothec perish or suffer deterioration in such a manner that they become insufficient for the security of the creditor, the creditor may obtain a supplement of hypothec or, failing that, pursue his reimbursement forthwith.

###### Article 2373

A conventional hypothec is valid only insofar as the sum for which it is granted is certain and determined by the act: if the claim resulting from the obligation is conditional as to its existence, or indeterminate in its value, the creditor may require the registration of which mention will be made hereinafter, only up to an estimated value expressly declared by him, and which the debtor shall have the right to have reduced, if appropriate.

###### Article 2374

Hypothecs and privileges which have given rise to registration are extinguished: 1° By the extinction of the obligation of which they constitute the guarantee;  
2° By the renunciation by the creditor of his right;  
3° By the completion of the procedure for purging hypothecs by the third party holder upon forced expropriation or upon expropriation for reasons of public utility, in accordance with the requirements of Article 51 of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership.

##### Section IV : De la propriété immobilière cédée en garantie

###### Article 2375

The provisions of this chapter are not applicable to fiducies constituted as security by legal persons.

###### Article 2376

The ownership of immovable property may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiducie contract concluded in application of Articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2377

In the case of a fiducie concluded as security, the contract mentions on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in Article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the immovable transferred into the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 2378

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiducie contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires the free disposal of the property transferred as security.  
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the agreement so provides, the sale of the property and the delivery of all or part of the price.  

The value of the property is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2379

If the beneficiary of the fiducie has acquired the free disposal of the property in application of Article 2378, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to the prior payment of debts arising from the preservation or management of the fiduciary patrimony.  
Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the property in application of the fiducie contract, he restores to the settlor the portion of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, as the case may be, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2380

The ownership transferred in application of Article 2376 may be subsequently assigned as security for debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive act provided that the latter expressly so provides.  
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary patrimony may then be assigned as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.  

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of Article 2377 is published in the form provided for in Article 2213. The date of publication determines, among them, the rank of the creditors.  
The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary thereto is deemed unwritten.

### TITLE XX: Real Property Revendication and Forced Sale of Immovable Property

###### Article 2381

The action for revendication of immovable property and the forced sale of immovable property is pursued in compliance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure and those of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership.

### Title XXI: On Prescription

Chapter I: General Provisions Article 2382
Prescription is a means of acquiring or being released by a certain lapse of time, and under the conditions determined by law.  

Time limits for forfeiture are not, except where contrary provisions are provided by law, governed by this title.  

The provisions of this title do not prevent the application of special rules provided by other texts or special laws.

###### Article 2383

Extinctive prescription is a mode of extinction of a right resulting from the inaction of its holder for a time defined by law.  
It is subject to the law governing the right which it affects.

###### Article 2384

Acquisitive prescription is a means of acquiring property or a right by the effect of possession, when the law authorizes such an effect.

###### Article 2385

Prescription can in no case constitute a mode of acquisition of real rights over immovable property or of release from charges encumbering the same immovable property.

###### Article 2386

In movable matters, possession may produce an acquisitive effect of right under the conditions set out in article 686 and following.

###### Article 2387

One cannot renounce prescription in advance; one may renounce prescription once acquired.  

Renunciation of prescription is express or tacit; tacit renunciation results from an act which presupposes the abandonment of the acquired right.  

One who cannot exercise his rights by himself cannot renounce acquired prescription alone.

###### Article 2388

Except for renunciation, prescription may be raised at any stage of proceedings, even before the court of appeal.  

Creditors, or any other person having an interest in the prescription being acquired, may raise it, even if the debtor or owner has said he renounces it.  
Judges cannot supply of their own motion the ground resulting from prescription.

###### Article 2389

Payment made to extinguish a debt cannot be recovered on the sole ground that the prescription period had expired.

###### Article 2390

The State, public establishments and communes are subject to the same prescriptions as private individuals, and may also raise them.

###### Article 2391

However, the following are imprescriptible, subject to the texts which regulate them:
1° Property belonging to the public domain within the meaning of the law (specifically referred to here are Law No. 171/AN/91/2ème L on the determination and organization of the public domain and Law No. 173/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of the private domain of the State);  
2° Things which are not in commerce;  
3° In accordance with article 674, the right of ownership as well as the rights and actions which are attributes of the right of ownership, such as for example the right to acquire joint ownership of a wall, the right to use running water of which one is a riparian owner, the right to claim passage for the owner of an enclosed land, the right to enclose oneself, or the right to request partition.

#### Chapter II: On Causes Which Prevent Movable Prescription Article 2392

One cannot change for oneself the cause and principle of one's possession, so that one prescribes according to the obligation one has contracted. Thus, those who possess for others never prescribe by any lapse of time whatsoever. Such is the case, for example, of the depositary or the usufructuary, and of all others who hold the thing of the owner precariously, cannot prescribe it.  

The heirs of those who held the thing under some such precarious titles cannot prescribe either.

###### Article 2393

It is otherwise in case of interversion of title, namely when the person whom the owner designates as precarious holder considers that his holding has been changed into possession or ownership.

###### Article 2394

Those to whom the thing has been transmitted by a precarious holder by a title transferring ownership may nevertheless prescribe it when the conditions of possession are fulfilled.

#### Chapter III

On the Running of Prescription Section I: General Provisions

###### Article 2395

Prescription runs against all persons, unless they are within some exception established by law.

###### Article 2396

Prescription is counted by days, and not by hours.  

It is acquired when the last day of the term is completed.

###### Article 2397

When a new law lengthens the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, it has no effect on a prescription or forfeiture already acquired. Subject to the transitional provisions it may provide, such a law applies immediately to the situation when the prescription period or forfeiture period had not expired on the date of its entry into force; the time already elapsed is then taken into account.  

If the new law reduces the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, this new period runs from the day of entry into force of this new law, without the total duration being able to exceed the duration provided by the former law.

###### Article 2398

The prescription period may be interrupted or suspended according to the causes indicated by law.  

Interruption of prescription erases the period already acquired and starts a new period running. This new period is of the same duration as the old one.  
Suspension of prescription temporarily stops its running without erasing the period already elapsed.

##### Section II: On the ordinary limitation period and certain special limitation periods Article 2399

Unless otherwise provided by law:

1° Personal or movable actions are time-barred after three years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it;

2° Real actions relating to immovable property are time-barred after thirty years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it.

3° The limitation period is:
a.	10 years in case of bodily injury for the victim, from the date of consolidation of the damage;
b.	10 years for ecological damage;
c.	20 years in case of harm related to an act of torture or barbarity, or violence or sexual assault against minors.
d.	Architects, contractors and other persons bound to the principal by a contract for work are discharged from the warranty for works they have made or directed after ten years if they are major works, after two years for minor works.
e.	The action of bailiffs, for the remuneration of acts they serve and commissions they execute; the action of notaries for payment of their acts; the action of doctors, surgeons, dental surgeons, midwives and pharmacists, for their visits, operations and medicines, are time-barred after two years.
f.	The action of lawyers, for payment of their costs and fees, is time-barred after two years, from the judgment of proceedings or the settlement of the parties, or from the revocation of said lawyers. With regard to unfinished matters, they may not make claims for their costs and fees going back more than five years.
g.	The limitation period, in the above cases, runs even though there has been a continuation of supplies, deliveries, services and works.
It ceases to run only when there has been a settled account, note or obligation, or a legal summons that has not lapsed.
h.	Nevertheless, those against whom these limitation periods are invoked may defer the oath to those who invoke them, on the question of whether the thing has actually been paid.
The oath may be deferred to the widows and heirs, or to the guardians of the latter, if they are minors, so that they may declare whether they do not know that the thing is due.

i.	Judges, bailiffs as well as persons who have represented or assisted the parties are discharged from documents five years after the judgment or the cessation of their involvement.
j.	The action of workers for payment of wages, wage accessories, bonuses and allowances of any kind as well as, more generally, any sum due by the employer to the worker, and that for the provision of benefits in kind and possibly their reimbursement, are time-barred after one year. The limitation period runs from the date from which the wage is payable. It is suspended or interrupted under the conditions provided for in Section III below.

###### Article 2400

All actions, both real and personal, are time-barred after thirty years, without the person alleging this limitation period being required to produce a title or being able to have the exception derived from bad faith raised against him.
The thirty-year extinctive limitation period established by the preceding paragraph is not applicable to cases where the law provides for a shorter period to run, when it starts from the day of knowledge of the fact, act or event.

##### Section III: On causes that interrupt or suspend the limitation period

###### § 1. On causes that interrupt the running of the limitation period Article 2401

The limitation period is interrupted:
1° When the possessor is deprived for more than one year of the enjoyment of the thing, either by the purported owner, or even by a third party;
2° By the acknowledgment that the debtor or possessor makes of the right of the person against whom he was acquiring by prescription.

###### Article 2402

A legal claim, even in summary proceedings, a demand or a seizure, served on the person whom one wishes to prevent from acquiring by prescription, also interrupts the limitation period as well as the foreclosure period.
The same applies when the legal claim is brought before an incompetent court, or when the summons is void by reason of a defect in form.
The interruption resulting from the legal claim produces its effects until the extinction of the proceedings.

###### Article 2403

The interruption is regarded as void: if the claimant withdraws his claim; if he allows the proceedings to lapse; or if his claim is definitively rejected.

###### Article 2404

The demand made to one of the joint and several debtors by a legal claim, or by an act of forced execution, or the acknowledgment by the debtor of the right of the person against whom he was acquiring by prescription, interrupts the limitation period against all the others, even against their heirs.
On the other hand, the demand made to one of the heirs of a joint and several debtor, or the acknowledgment of that heir, does not interrupt the limitation period with regard to the other co-heirs, even in case of a mortgage debt, if the obligation is divisible. This demand or this acknowledgment interrupts the limitation period, with regard to the other co-debtors, only for the share for which that heir is liable.
To interrupt the limitation period for the whole, with regard to the other co-debtors, the demand must be made to all the heirs of the deceased debtor, or the acknowledgment of all these heirs.

###### Article 2405

The demand made to the principal debtor, or his acknowledgment, interrupts the limitation period against the surety.

###### § 2. On causes that suspend the running of the limitation period Article 2406

By way of exception to Article 2395, the limitation period does not run against a person who cannot validly act, by reason of an impediment resulting from the law, from an agreement, or from force majeure.

###### Article 2407

The limitation period does not run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, except in cases determined by law.
Thus and by way of exception, limitation periods run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, subject to their recourse against their guardians: limitation periods aimed at payment or recovery of wages, arrears of annuities, maintenance payments, rents, rental charges, interest on sums lent and, generally, actions for payment of everything that is payable by years or at shorter periodic terms.

###### Article 2408

The limitation period does not run between spouses, one against the other.

###### Article 2409

The limitation period does not run: with regard to a claim that depends on a condition, until the condition occurs; with regard to an action in warranty, until the eviction has taken place; with regard to a claim at a fixed date, until that date has arrived.

###### Article 2410

The limitation period does not run against the beneficiary heir, with regard to claims he has against the estate.
On the other hand, it runs against a vacant estate, even in the case where it is not provided with a curator.

###### Article 2411

When the law grants a person a grace period, the prescription of the property and rights concerned is suspended during this legally granted time.

Article final General Transitional Provisions

All texts contrary to the provisions of this code are repealed, except where they create texts derogating from common law, in consideration of their domain.  
References to provisions repealed, amended or relocated by this code and contained in provisions of any nature, legislative as well as regulatory, are replaced by references to provisions having the same subject matter.  

Contracts and other legal acts that were entered into under the previous code are valid if they complied with the conditions then required.  

Prescriptions commenced at the time of publication of this code are governed in accordance with the former texts. Nevertheless, prescriptions then commenced, and for which more than thirty years would still be required, following the former laws, from the same time, shall be completed by this period of thirty years, all subject to Article 2400, paragraph 2.  

This law shall be executed upon its promulgation.
